BEN.summary: On 22 April 2026 the Council of Ministers authorised a specialist firm's mission to start a digital, geolocated, participatory addressing system. It is to start first in Abomey-Calavi, Cotonou, Ouidah, Porto-Novo, Sèmè-Podji and Parakou. The Ministry of Cadre de Vie says a 21 May 2026 meeting of ANAT, EDENMAP and others agreed a shared vision and guidelines for the national strategy. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

BFA.short: Digital address platforms served Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso in 2023; no source found reports national coverage.
BFA.summary: A pilot of the urban information project, financed by the European Union, addressed more than 93,000 doors and 16,000 streets in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso. It built two digital address platforms, presented on 24 October 2023. On 2 April 2025 the commune of Ouagadougou extended street naming and door numbering to arrondissements 5 and 12. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

BWA.short: An addressing system was under way in 2024; none in service is on record.
BWA.summary: A June 2024 journal article says Botswana has adopted LAPCAS. Its authors built a prototype location addressing system for Tlokweng. The article says addressing at village level remains unresolved. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

CAF.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national addressing system, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: No stage is set. No source found since October 2023 says whether the Central African Republic has a national addressing system, or whether one is under way or in service. Nothing has been found in the last twelve months that says addressing is absent. No dated source from the past three years has been found for the country. Preparing would need a national addressing policy adopted, or street naming, numbering or digital addressing under way in some cities.

CIV.short: Digital addressing was in effect in two Abidjan zones in 2025; no source found reports national coverage.
CIV.summary: The Direction Générale de l'Économie says addressing through Google Maps is in effect in Abidjan's zones 1 and 2, on a page with figures to July 2025. By March 2026 the Abidjan project had named 14,276 streets and fitted 290,805 door plates. In September 2025 Abidjan's addressing was due to finish on 31 December 2025. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

CMR.short: An address register or digital addressing system was in service in 2025; no source found reports national coverage.
CMR.summary: Launch Base Africa reports that around 15,000 Cameroonians had generated geolocated addresses on FindMe's platform by June 2025. Campost signed a partnership with FindMe on 1 November 2024 in Yaounde to enhance the national address system. The addresses are certified through national postal partnerships. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

COD.short: Nothing found names a national addressing system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COD.summary: Not found. Nothing found names an addressing system, or says there is none.

COG.short: An addressing system was under way in 2024; none in service is on record.
COG.summary: ARPCE's postal regulation director reported progress on the national digital addressing platform, provisionally named Système de localisation mixte. It was demonstrated at a steering committee on 9 October 2024. In the last twelve months, on 15 October 2026 ARPCE presented its digital postal addressing project, run with town halls since April 2022. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

COM.short: A 2024 source says there is no national addressing system.
COM.summary: In August 2024 Comores Infos reported that the Comoros has no postcodes and no precise way to locate places. The telecoms minister has pledged to introduce postcodes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an addressing system is under way. Preparing would need a national addressing policy adopted, or street naming, numbering or digital addressing under way in some cities.

CPV.short: An address register or digital addressing system was in service in 2026; no source found reports national coverage.
CPV.summary: The Câmara Municipal da Praia launched its Plataforma Municipal de Toponímia in October 2025. In April 2026 it said the platform lets residents find street names and official building numbers across the Praia municipality. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 São Filipe's council was matching inventoried names to its streets and squares. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

DJI.short: Streets were being addressed in a few parts of Djibouti city in 2023; no source found reports an address register in service.
DJI.summary: Terms of reference for the PROGOUV programme, dated November 2023, say street addressing in Djibouti city exists only in a few central streets and in Ras Dika commune. Those streets have plates but no door numbers, and a pilot ran in Cité Nassib in Balbala. The city council was recruiting an expert to define a city addressing strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

DZA.short: Official geolocated addresses covered 12 of 69 wilayas in 2026; all are due by 2030, so national coverage is not yet reached.
DZA.summary: On 12 October 2026 the interior ministry's director general Amal Djouama said 1.5 million official, geolocated addresses had been counted under the national address reference, with the rollout in 12 wilayas. The ministry's plan extends the unified addressing system to all 69 wilayas by 2030. El Khabar names five users of the system at a study day in Oran on 12 October 2026, among them civil protection, Sonelgaz and the tax services. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

EGY.short: Real estate ID numbers were being issued in 2025 while their system was built; no source found reports an address register in service.
EGY.summary: In June 2025 the communications ministry said about 19 million national real estate identification numbers had been issued across several governorates. The ministry said the digital system to manage them was still being developed ahead of its launch. In March 2020 Egypt Post's chairperson said a new seven-digit postcode had been applied across the country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the digital system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a national addressing system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names an addressing system, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Digital addresses were in service in 73 cities in 2025; no source found reports national coverage.
ETH.summary: In December 2025 SSGI said eDAS was in use in 73 cities. In January 2026 SSGI's Director General said the system was being rolled out in stages across several cities. In December 2025 SSGI's Deputy Director General said eDAS integrates the Fayda digital ID, and it also integrates postal and parcel delivery services. In October 2026 the Minister of Innovation and Technology said the system should be expanded nationwide. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

GAB.short: An addressing system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
GAB.summary: Street naming and door numbering in Libreville stopped at the end of 2021. By March 2025 the work had resumed, with 5,000 of 60,000 door numbers placed. AIMF and the EU fund the work, which is Libreville's municipal programme. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

GHA.short: The addressing system covered the whole country in 2026; no source found reports its use by services.
GHA.summary: Ghana Post's site says GhanaPostGPS is Ghana's official digital property addressing system, giving every location a unique digital address. It says the system covers every inch of the country and all locations are addressed. An academic evaluation says the system had been in implementation nearly six years, and that it might be a partial failure. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says other services use the address system. Mature would need the post, emergency services, utilities or other registers to use the address system.

GIN.short: An addressing system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
GIN.summary: On 3 October 2024 the urbanism minister Mory Condé said the national addressing programme was complete in Kaloum. He said it would extend to Dixinn, Matam, the other Conakry communes, Coyah, Dubréka and regional and prefecture towns. An order of 25 August 2025 created a management unit for the National Addressing Programme under the urbanism minister. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

GMB.short: Kanifing's digital addresses were in service in 2026; no source found reports national coverage.
GMB.summary: In June 2026 Kanifing Municipal Council was bringing in sequential street numbers, beside its Plus Codes shown on compound gates. LoGRI says Kanifing gave Plus Code addresses to 500,000 residents, georeferencing 36,000 properties. In November 2026 the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy held a West Coast Region forum on the National Digital Addressing Initiative. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says the addressing system covers the whole country. Operating would need the addressing system to cover the whole country, rural areas included.

GNB.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national addressing system, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: No stage is set. No source found since October 2023 says whether Guinea-Bissau has a national addressing system, or whether one is under way or in service. Nothing has been found in the last twelve months that says addressing is absent. No dated source from the past three years has been found for the country. Preparing would need a national addressing policy adopted, or street naming, numbering or digital addressing under way in some cities.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names a national addressing system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names an addressing system, or says there is none.

KEN.short: An addressing system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
KEN.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya has led the draft National Addressing System Bill, 2025. It wrote national addressing standards with the Kenya Bureau of Standards. In Parliament the Bill's sponsor said Kenya relies on informal dropped-pin location sharing. In September 2026 the National Addressing System Bill was still a draft. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

LBR.short: An addressing system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
LBR.summary: In February 2026 the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications published Digital Liberia, its Strategic Plan 2025-2029. It makes a national digital addressing system one of eight priority areas. On 6 July 2026 the ministry announced that deployment had begun in Montserrado County. It is to expand to all 15 counties. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

LBY.short: An addressing system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
LBY.summary: At the start of 2025 Libya Post began installing address plates in several municipalities. Its first phase numbers 42,000 buildings, with more than 23 municipalities to follow. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 an experts forum in Tripoli urged faster work on the Digital Addressing Platform, which the Libya Herald reports as already being implemented. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

LSO.short: A 2026 source says there is no national addressing system.
LSO.summary: In October 2026 the Government of Lesotho said a standard digital address was still missing. A World Bank urban team has expressed interest in supporting a nationwide Digital Address system. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says an addressing system is under way. Preparing would need a national addressing policy adopted, or street naming, numbering or digital addressing under way in some cities.

MAR.short: One commune, Beni Ansar, began an addressing project in 2023; no address register in service has been found.
MAR.summary: On 22 December 2023 the commune of Beni Ansar met Barid Al-Maghrib on its project for a street-naming and house-numbering system. The meeting was the first in a series of workshops to complete the system across the commune. Article 85 of the organic law and decree 2.17.307 of July 2017 provide for such a system. The project covers one commune. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

MDG.short: Addressing was under way in Antsiranana in 2024; nothing found says an addressing system is in service.
MDG.summary: In July 2024 L'Express reported that the tax directorate DGI was training staff of Antsiranana commune to set up addressing and tax census operations. Drones were to survey the town before the address database was built. The work concerns one commune. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says an address register or digital addressing system is in service in Madagascar, or how far the Antsiranana work went. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

MLI.short: An addressing system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
MLI.summary: In March 2025 the permanent secretary for land reform said Ninacad-Adresse gives each plot a six-digit code in a secure database, reaching about 1,500,000 plots in Bamako and parts of Kati and Ségou. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the DGI said the application was at its design phase. No source found says it is in service. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

MOZ.short: An addressing system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
MOZ.summary: On 3 October 2025 the Ministry of State Administration and Public Service launched postal addressing in Marracuene, Maputo province, under Decree 74/2024. The work names and numbers streets and buildings, puts up street signs and builds a geographic database. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the Council of Ministers approved 1,444 geographic names. On 21 October 2026 INCM presented the new eight-digit postal code in Pemba. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

MRT.short: An addressing system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
MRT.summary: On 29 September 2026 the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Administrative Modernization presented a national digital addressing system. Ecofin Agency reports that a pilot is expected by the end of 2026. In November 2026 the country still had no general postal addressing system, which makes deliveries harder. No earlier dated position has been found, so no change in the last twelve months is shown. No source found since October 2023 says an address register or digital addressing system is in service. Establishing would need an address register or digital addressing system in service.

MUS.summary: No stage is set. No source found since October 2023 says whether Mauritius has a national addressing system, or whether one is under way or in service. In the last twelve months this is the only draft found, and it is not a law on AI itself. No source found says it has gone to cabinet or parliament, or that a rule on AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

GIN.short: A ministry official said in October 2025 that Guinea has no AI law or framework; no source found says whether a draft is under way.
GIN.summary: On 14 October 2025 a senior official of Guinea's Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy opened a diagnostic workshop. The secretary-general said Guinea lacks a legislative and regulatory framework on AI. He added that Guinea has not yet adopted a specific AI law. In the last twelve months this is the only statement found on the legal position, and it names no law. No source found says whether any draft is under way. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

GMB.short: An assessment of June 2026 says The Gambia has no legislation on AI and none proposed.
GMB.summary: An assessment by the Oxford Institute of Technology and Justice covers the position as at June 2026. It states that there is no dedicated legislation regulating the use of AI in The Gambia and no proposed legislation on AI. In the last twelve months, a security practitioner wrote in November 2026 that The Gambia still has no law written for AI. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

GNB.short: Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one. Nothing found says there is none.

GNQ.short: A ministry was revising a preliminary draft of an AI law in 2025; no rule on AI is in force.
GNQ.summary: In August 2025 the ministry responsible for transport, telecommunications and AI systems was writing a preliminary draft of an AI law in Equatorial Guinea. A working session went through the observations and amendments made to its first version. The report is dated 27 August 2025. In the last twelve months no source found says the draft has been approved by the Council of Ministers or sent to parliament. No rule on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

KEN.short: An AI bill has been before the Senate since early 2026, its committee advising against it in October; no rule on AI is in force.
KEN.summary: The Artificial Intelligence Bill was introduced in the Senate on 19 February 2026. A memorandum of May 2026 describes the bill as creating an AI Commissioner's office and an advisory committee. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Senate ICT Committee recommended that the Senate not proceed with it. A November 2026 analysis says the bill formally remains before the Senate. No Senate vote has been found, and no law on AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

LBR.short: In 2026 Liberia had no guardrails on AI in law; no draft is named.
LBR.summary: A memorandum by Abdullah Kamara, reported in March 2026, says Liberia lacks clear guardrails on how AI should be used or governed. It recommends legislation to regulate high-risk AI applications. It says the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, the telecoms regulator and the National Security Agency have yet to set AI-specific frameworks. In the last twelve months this memorandum is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

LBY.short: In 2025 Libya had a legislative vacuum on AI; no draft is named.
LBY.summary: An article in the Journal of the Academic Forum, published in November 2025, says Libya has a legislative vacuum on AI-related crimes, including deepfakes. It says the country's legislation needs updating to cover them. The national AI strategy and ethics charter the country has published are policy documents, not law. In the last twelve months this article is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

MAR.short: The electoral law revised for the 2026 elections makes AI-made falsehoods a crime; a general AI bill of 2025 has not passed.
MAR.summary: The broadcasting regulator's decision 50-26 binds licensed radio and television not to broadcast misleading AI-generated or AI-altered election content. It does not reach online platforms. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the digital transition minister said her ministry was preparing a digital administration bill with provisions specific to AI. In November 2026 an analyst wrote that no text governs AI as a whole. No law on AI itself, applying across sectors, has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

MDG.short: Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.

MOZ.short: In August 2026 an official said Mozambique has no AI legislation; an education AI law was still being written in September.
MOZ.summary: In August 2026 the chairman of the national institute for information and communication technologies said that Mozambique does not yet have specific legislation governing AI. UNESCO's profile of December 2025 also says Mozambique has no specific AI legislation. In the last twelve months, on 16 September 2026, the education and culture minister said that a law to regulate the use of AI in education is almost ready. She said the text was still being written. No draft of it has been found published, out for consultation or before the Council of Ministers. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

MUS.short: Regulations in force since March 2026 govern AI in higher education; there is no law on AI itself.
MUS.summary: The Higher Education (Use of Artificial Intelligence) Regulations 2026 are Government Notice 39 of 2026, made under the Higher Education Act 2017. They came into operation on 31 March 2026. They oblige higher education institutions to adopt policies on AI and require the use of AI tools to be disclosed. The Financial Services Commission's rules of 2021 cover AI-enabled advisory services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

MWI.short: In 2025 Malawi had passed no dedicated AI law; an AI bill is announced but no draft is known.
MWI.summary: The Minister of Higher Education, Jessie Kabwila, said in June 2025 that Malawi has not yet passed a dedicated AI law. An AI bill has been announced alongside the national AI strategy. In the last twelve months no draft text of it has been found. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded for the country. No published bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

NAM.short: The minister said in August 2026 that no AI legislation has been introduced; a strategy comes first.
NAM.summary: The minister for information and communication technology spoke at a meeting on 3 August 2026. The minister said the government has put a national AI strategy before legislation, so no AI legislation has yet been introduced. In the last twelve months a second report of the meeting says the same. In October 2026 a commentator wrote of the absence of explicit, standalone national AI laws. No draft of a law on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

NER.short: The data protection law in force obliges AI developers and providers to declare to the regulator; no law on AI itself has been found.
NER.summary: Article 57 of Law 2022-59, in the authority's consolidated text of April 2026, defines artificial intelligence. It requires AI developers, makers and service providers to comply with the law. Those operating from Niger must declare to the data protection authority, the HAPDP. In July 2025 the head of the HAPDP said its peers in Burkina Faso and Mali had asked it to present a draft text regulating AI. In the last twelve months no published draft of it has been found. No law on AI itself has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

NGA.short: A 2025 data protection directive sets duties for anyone deploying AI; several AI bills are before parliament and none has passed.
NGA.summary: The data protection commission issued a General Application and Implementation Directive of 2025. Under article 43, an organisation deploying AI must document its parameters, assess unequal outcomes and test the system. Four AI bills passed second reading in the House of Representatives on 3 December 2024. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics described the proposed Artificial Intelligence Bill as covering sovereignty, investment and risk management. No law on AI itself has been found in force. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

RWA.short: A review of September 2026 says Rwanda has no AI act and relies on its 2023 AI policy; no draft is named.
RWA.summary: A university centre wrote in September 2026 that there is no AI Act in Rwanda. It said the country's framework for AI rests on the National AI Policy of April 2023. In the last twelve months, a New Times opinion piece in November 2026 said Rwanda had no binding AI rules. It called for a standalone AI Act. Neither names a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and none has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

SDN.short: The Council of Ministers approved a draft data and AI bill in November 2026; no rule on AI is in force.
SDN.summary: On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Law from the digital transformation ministry. It sent the draft for further study before approval by the interim parliament. In the last twelve months, on 1 November 2026 the Council of Ministers approved the draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Regulation Bill 2026, SUNA reports. The text of the bill has not been found published. No law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

SEN.short: A July 2024 diagnostic found no AI-specific legal text in Senegal; no source found says whether a draft has appeared since.
SEN.summary: An IPAR diagnostic published in July 2024 covers the policy, legal and ethical framework on AI in four West African countries, Senegal among them. It says there is as yet no legal text specific to AI at continental, regional or national level. In the last twelve months no later statement on the position has been found. No source found says whether any draft is under way. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

SLE.short: The justice minister said in September 2026 that no specific AI legislation has been enacted; no draft is named.
SLE.summary: The attorney-general and justice minister spoke at a UNESCO meeting in Riyadh on 16 September 2026. The minister said the country has established a position on AI but has not yet enacted specific AI legislation. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found. The report of his remarks names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and no date by which one is to be written. None has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

SOM.short: A May 2026 analysis reports Somalia has no national AI law and no dedicated AI legislation; no source found says whether any draft exists.
SOM.summary: Ecofin Agency wrote on 17 July 2026 about the launch of a university AI center. It cites an analysis published in May 2026 that reports Somalia has no national AI law and no dedicated AI legislation. In the last twelve months nothing later has been found that changes that position. Nothing found records a draft, a bill or a decree on AI, whether published, out for consultation or before cabinet or parliament. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

SSD.short: In 2025 a cybercrimes bill carried proposed AI provisions; no source found says whether any binding AI rule is in force.
SSD.summary: Digital Rights Frontlines reported on 22 October 2025 that South Sudan's Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Bill 2024, which had not yet passed, contains proposed AI provisions. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

STP.short: UNESCO's 2026 profile and the minister both say the country has no AI-specific laws or regulations; no draft is named.

SYC.summary: A private member's draft Pro-Human Technology Bill covers AI in employment and education among other technologies. It was presented to National Assembly members at a seminar on 6 March 2024. The Speaker told the seminar the bill was still far from reaching the Assembly, and it is expected to go to an Assembly working group. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

TCD.short: In April 2026 a minister said Chad's digital texts cannot regulate AI and set up a committee; no draft law is known.
TCD.summary: On 27 April 2026 the telecoms minister said that existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated in Chad. He installed a 34-member committee and gave it 45 days to propose updated texts for the digital legal framework. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found, and it names no draft text on AI. No source found says what the committee proposed. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

TUN.short: A draft data protection law including AI use was before a committee in February 2026; no rule on AI is known in force.
TUN.summary: Organic law proposal 095/2025 on personal data protection has 132 articles and includes regulation of AI use. It was heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026. In the last twelve months, a lawyer wrote in October 2026 that the proposal was still before the committee. The lawyer added that Tunisia has no law dedicated to AI. No rule on AI has been found in force. Establishing would need a law, decree or regulation in force that names AI and sets a rule for one sector or one use.

TZA.short: Regulations of January 2025 prohibit fabricated AI-generated content online; there is no law on AI itself.
TZA.summary: Government Notice 57 of 28 January 2025 amends the Online Content Regulations of 2020. It adds unethical, fabricated and AI-generated video, audio and still pictures to the content prohibited online. In the last twelve months a university centre wrote in September 2026 that Tanzania lacks a dedicated AI law and that the laws used for AI are mostly data protection laws. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself has been found. Operating would need a law on AI itself in force that applies across sectors.

UGA.short: A review of September 2026 says Uganda has no AI laws in place; a 2025 government assessment found the same.
UGA.summary: A university centre wrote in September 2026 that Uganda has no AI laws in place and uses data protection laws in place of a dedicated framework. The ministry responsible for information and communication technology made an assessment with the International Telecommunication Union, dated 2025. It lists the lack of an AI policy and of a legal and regulatory framework among its main findings. In the last twelve months neither source names a bill or a draft. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

ZAF.short: Two sources of August 2026 say South Africa has no law or regulations on AI; national rules are expected in 2027.
ZAF.summary: South Africa has no law on AI. In August 2026 a technology company's chief executive wrote that it has no law governing AI and that national rules are expected in 2027. In March 2026 the law firm Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr wrote that it has no single law on AI or deepfakes. A research centre wrote in August 2026 that it has no national AI policy or regulations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI.

ZWE.short: An analyst wrote in July 2026 that Zimbabwe has no AI law and no draft; no source found says whether one has been introduced since.
ZWE.summary: On 27 July 2026 Tashinga Magaya of African Law Matters wrote that the National AI Strategy is not a law. She wrote that the proposed regulator has no enabling Act. She said the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today. In the last twelve months this is the only dated statement found. It says a draft AI Act is still to be introduced. No source found says whether one has been introduced since July 2026. Preparing would need a bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI to exist: published, out for consultation, or before cabinet or parliament.

AGO.short: Angola's tax authority used AI to flag suspect filers in its 2026 audits; no single source says AI is in service in several sectors.
AGO.summary: The tax authority AGT cross-checked 2025 corporate income tax filings and flagged irregular filers, its chair said in July 2026. In April 2026 the chair said the audit of the 2024 tax year used AI to flag deviations and suspect cases. In June 2026 AGT launched its ASY5 customs system at Luanda port, with AI risk management that checks cargo from the manifest on. These reports date from the last twelve months, and none says what the position was before. No single source found says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

BDI.short: An AI tool for a public sector's system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
BDI.summary: The national malaria programme trained health workers in Cibitoke and Kirundo on 16 July 2025 on an AI app that reads rapid malaria tests. Enabel calls it a pilot. A team is piloting an AI-powered mpox early-warning dashboard in three health districts of Bujumbura. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says an AI tool is in service in a public sector's system, and neither pilot is reported at work across the health system. Establishing would need an AI tool in service in a public sector's system and producing outputs, such as diagnoses, risk scores, forecasts or notices.

BEN.short: Customs runs AI risk profiling, by the vendor's account in 2025; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
BEN.summary: Webb Fontaine, the vendor, said in February 2025 that Benin's customs system was in use at 44 of the 49 customs offices. It says the system now bases risk management on AI profiling of importers and goods and detects fraud patterns automatically. In 2026, within the last twelve months, the health ministry awarded a contract for 20 AI-assisted malaria diagnostic devices for referral hospitals, which are still being procured. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's TB programme has read X-rays with AI in field campaigns since 2024; no single source says AI serves several sectors.
BFA.summary: The national TB programme's coordinator said the AI tool CAD4TB was introduced in 2024 to read images from the programme's mobile digital X-ray units. It is used in field screening campaigns. The coordinator reported that from September 2024 to April 2025 the campaigns screened 1,730 people and found 61 TB cases. In May 2026, within the last twelve months, the KIX-SEEDS project said a machine-learning module predicting school dropout is among the tools of its pilot in the communes of Manga and Bingo. That is a pilot. No source found says AI is in service in a second sector. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

BWA.short: The national TB programme deployed AI chest X-ray reading in 2025; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
BWA.summary: A vendor partner says Botswana's national TB programme deployed AI chest X-ray reading in April 2025 and trained local teams. The U.S. Embassy says PEPFAR donated AI software for TB detection to the Ministry of Health in 2025. In August 2025 an assistant minister said government is piloting AI for health diagnostics in remote areas. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

CAF.short: An AI X-ray tool has screened for TB at Batangafo hospital, Central African Republic, since 2024; no single source shows AI in several sectors.
CAF.summary: MSF reports that, with the health authorities, it equipped Batangafo district hospital in 2024 with an AI tool that scores chest X-rays. MSF reports that the tool helped detect 90 of the 203 TB cases screened in the Batangafo area in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Every AI tool held is in health, and no single source found says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's tax administration uses AI to segment taxpayers; no source says AI is in service in several sectors.
CIV.summary: In May 2025 the finance minister said the tax administration uses AI to segment taxpayers by category. In March 2024 the state bureau BNETD presented a land-cover map with AI recognition of forests on satellite imagery. Since 5 October 2026, within the last twelve months, health workers in Gontougo have used a platform whose AI gives treatment advice and flags inconsistent data. No earlier position for health has been found. No single source found says AI is in service in several sectors, and no measured results have been found. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

CMR.short: An AI tool was in service in a public sector's system in 2026; AI in several sectors is not on record.
CMR.summary: In February 2026 the director general of the social insurance fund CNPS said the fund runs a symbolic-AI system for automatic processing of old-age pension files. The director general also said its AI tools detect fraud by finding inconsistencies in declarations and contributions. In the last twelve months, on 17 August 2026, the secondary-education ministry presented the official integration of AI-generated simulations in secondary schools. University researchers say a tax fraud detection model was tested at three tax centres, and the tax directorate has not confirmed it. No single source has been found that says AI is in service in two sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

COD.short: DR Congo's education ministry has marked state exam papers with AI since 2025; no source found says AI is in service in several sectors.
COD.summary: The education minister said in August 2025 that an AI system marked the 2025 State Exam papers. In the last twelve months, WHO said its AI-based preparedness platform was in use in the country by October 2026. On 8 November 2026 the health ministry announced Etoile Bleue, an emergency medical response system that uses AI to handle alerts, which has no launch date. No earlier position has been found for either. Each source names one sector, and no source found says AI is in service in two or more sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

The poster comes from the last twelve months, and no earlier position for it has been found. No source found says an AI tool is in service and producing outputs. CPV.short: AI-read heart and eye tests reached all islands with the health ministry in 2026; no source found reports AI elsewhere or measured results.
CPV.summary: In an account of April 2026, the Cabo Verdean American Medical Society, working with the Ministry of Health, says it has distributed cloud ECG devices across all islands that make automatic diagnoses with AI. It says AI also lets nurses diagnose cataracts, glaucoma and retinopathy. The account comes from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. DJI.short: Djibouti's corridor road company detects road defects with AI, and AI weather warnings run since 2025; no single source says AI serves several sectors.
DJI.summary: The ports and free zones authority says an AI road-monitoring system launched in 2024 uses cameras to detect and locate potholes and cracks along the regional transport corridors. In January 2026 the corridor-road company said its system made 2,174 detections across four defect types in its first processing. In the last twelve months the Chinese Meteorological Administration supplied an AI early-warning system, in service from December 2025. Road transport and weather are separate accounts. No single source found says AI is in service in two or more sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

DZA.short: Algeria has used AI since 2024 in trade checks, customs risk analysis and university choice, each in a separate source; none names several sectors.
DZA.summary: In April 2024 the higher education minister launched an AI platform that simulates study-field choices for new baccalaureate holders. The Ministry of Finance says the customs information system relies on AI techniques for risk analysis of imports and exports. In September 2026, within the last twelve months, the Ministry of Foreign Trade said its AI-boosted data analysis and cross-checking system detected anomalies in import programme files. No earlier position has been found for it. No single source found says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors. Operating would need AI tools in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

EGY.summary: In November 2025 the customs head said three smart systems run on the Nafeza platform. In September 2026 the tax authority head said AI now calculates real estate disposition tax. In November 2026 a social solidarity official said the Takaful and Karama cash programme uses AI. The last two come from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found for either. ERI.short: The health ministry's AI chest X-ray units were deployed for TB screening in 2024; no source found reports AI elsewhere or measured results.
ERI.summary: Delft Imaging, the vendor, says the Ministry of Health had 2 portable X-ray units and 6 units of its TB-reading AI deployed in 2024. The units serve the TB programme. Ghana Health Service and Jacaranda Health launched an AI maternal health platform in July 2026. The accounts are separate. Both 2026 dates come from the last twelve months.
