No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels, and no verification service used by several bodies has been reported. No app lets people prove who they are online with the NIU. No source found says the online NIU check is in service. Establishing would need a state-accepted authentication service in use for one purpose, such as an online check of the ID for one system.

COM.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a digital authentication service, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that names a digital authentication service in Comoros. No state-accepted authentication, e-signature or PKI service has been found that is authorised, contracted or piloted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no digital authentication service exists and credentials are checked by eye.

CPV.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2024.
CPV.summary: By January 2026 the national identity system, SNIAC, had issued about 1,291,910 digital certificates for authentication and qualified signature, the justice IT institute IMIJ says. The state platform Autentika gives single sign-on across public and private applications. Holders of the ID card can obtain the Mobile Digital Key online, created by a legislative decree in 2020. In the last twelve months, SNIAC published version 1.9.9 of its card middleware in March 2026. In July 2026 Caboverde24 reported the ID.GOV.CV digital ID wallet. The latest dated fact found is that July 2026 report.

DJI.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
DJI.summary: The Interior Ministry says Mobile ID, launched officially on 10 February 2026, lets citizens authenticate electronically to reach public services and do procedures remotely. It adds that partner administrations use its authentication services, without direct access to the databases. In the last twelve months this launch is the one change found. The director general says the directorate is working on an interoperability system meant to let administrations, banks and social protection bodies verify a national ID card in real time. The latest dated fact found is the launch of 10 February 2026.

DZA.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
DZA.summary: In May 2026 the Interior Ministry said the biometric ID card carries an electronic authentication certificate, backed by a public key infrastructure. In July 2026 the High Commission for Digitalisation said the national portal's first 21 services are reached through the digital identity. In the last twelve months, from August 2026, the Sports Ministry's WADHIFATI platform accepts it without a separate account. In April 2024 the Interior Ministry planned a digital identity reached from phones by the end of that year. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID app or ID wallet is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

EGY.short: From November 2026 citizens proved who they are online in a state identity app for a justice service; no source found says how many use it.
EGY.summary: On 7 November 2026 the justice and communications ministries launched a remote power of attorney service. Citizens prove who they are in the digital identity app by a face scan matched to state biometric records. In the last twelve months, the Interior Ministry announced a pilot of MOIEG-PASS in March 2026, where users scan their national ID and face to sign in. Since July 2026 the Public Prosecution's criminal-judgment enquiry service has checked enquirers through the Digital Egypt identity. No source found gives how many people use the digital identity app. The latest dated fact found is the 7 November 2026 launch.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a digital authentication service or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a digital authentication service, or says there is none.

ETH.short: In 2026 people opened bank accounts remotely with their national digital ID; no source found says how many use its wallet.
ETH.summary: In April 2026 Dashen Bank let customers open accounts remotely with Fayda credentials. By August 2026, 150 enterprises had integrated Fayda for biometric KYC checks. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the central bank told all banks to open new accounts through the VeriFayda 2 eKYC system. In November 2026 FaydaVerse said citizens use the FaydaPass wallet free of charge with their Fayda ID, and that nine government institutions have joined it. No figure has been found for how many people use the Fayda Wallet. The latest dated fact found is that November 2026 statement.

GAB.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
GAB.summary: In September 2026 the Gabon Digital programme, World Bank financed and run by the digital economy ministry, included a national digital identity system for access to public services. Gabonreview reports that on 28 April 2026 the DGI, CNSS and CNAMGS launched work on the Declaration unique des salaires, with operation targeted for July 2026. GabonReview says the SNID will give every resident a digital identity with the same legal value as physical identity. All three items come from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

GHA.short: A government app launched in 2024 creates a digital ID from the Ghana Card for public services; no source found reports its use since.
GHA.summary: On 7 October 2024 the Vice President launched the CitizenApp (CADIS). People scan their Ghana Card to create a digital ID, with biometric single sign-on to services. About 284 institutions used the NIA verification platform by August 2026, the interior minister said, against 191 in February 2024. In the last twelve months, the NIA said in September 2026 that a Ghana Card e-wallet would be activated in phases. Nothing found after October 2024 says the CitizenApp is still in use. The latest dated fact found is the September 2026 statement on the e-wallet.

GIN.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
GIN.summary: On 22 January 2026 the DGE and ONECI signed a convention under which the national register is the sole source of voter identification data. The digital agency ANDE is developing a public key infrastructure to secure electronic signatures. Nine draft texts on its use were under review on 21 October 2026. In the last twelve months, a November 2026 workshop drew up a roadmap that recommends a pilot. It targets public-sector e-signature from early 2027. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication or e-signature service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

GMB.short: An authentication service was in use in 2025; no source found reports use across services.
GMB.summary: The government says the National Identity Management System, launched 30 June 2026, combines a national identity register with biometric technology and real-time verification. A 2025 World Bank diagnostic says the Drivers License System uses the National ID system for biometric verification of applicants, to prevent identity fraud and duplication. The same diagnostic says the national ID's NIN was populated into the eCRVS to cross-verify parents' IDs. The June 2026 launch is the one change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

GNB.short: Nothing found names a digital authentication service or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a digital authentication service, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names a digital authentication service or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a digital authentication service, or says there is none.

KEN.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
KEN.summary: In June 2026 the IPRS Secretary said over 800 organisations are integrated for citizen verification, among them banks, insurers, SACCOs, telecoms and employment agencies. That figure is the one change found in the last twelve months. The government has piloted the Maisha Digital ID, a virtual ID for smartphone users, since November 2023. In October 2025 the Communications Authority required every critical information infrastructure system to use digital certificates only from the certification service providers it licenses. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

LBR.short: An authentication service was in use in 2024; no source found reports use across services.
LBR.summary: The National Identification Registry says an MoU with the Civil Service Agency in May 2024 allows national ID numbers to be used for payroll verification. It also says an October 2024 MoU with the Liberia Telecommunications Authority makes the national ID a requirement for SIM registration. In the last twelve months, a concession with OeSD International for digital identity credentials and authentication awaited ratification by the legislature in September 2026. It is not yet in force. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

LBY.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
LBY.summary: In April 2026 the General Information Authority and the Central Bank of Libya reviewed a link for eKYC that would connect the Level 3 biometric digital identity to banking systems. Technical trials with the Central Bank and a number of banks had begun, ahead of launch and integration. In February 2025 an NESDB summary proposed a digital ID wallet for each citizen. The April 2026 review is the one change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

LSO.short: An authentication service was in use in 2026; no source found reports use across services.
LSO.summary: In June 2026 FinMark Trust listed Lesotho's digital identity cards among domestic eKYC frameworks with uses in financial services. In the last twelve months, the finance ministry sought bids in June 2026 for a recovery site for the identity systems, including a hardware security module for PKI. The 2026 MICSTI-UNICEF work plan continues building MOSIP-based identity infrastructure aimed at secure authentication across government and private services. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

MAR.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
MAR.summary: The digital transition ministry says more than 34 institutions use the digital identity service, with about 100 others preparing to join. The DGSN's 2026 playbook says the platform serves 73 services and 54 partners. An Interior Ministry deck of 2026 counts over 70 million authentications by the population register. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, DGSN officials said Mon e-ID is already in use, letting citizens carry a digital version of their ID card. The latest dated fact found is that June 2026 statement.

MDG.short: A digital signature rule and a key infrastructure were in place but unused in 2025; no source found says whether any service now uses them.
MDG.summary: The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025 that a digital signature regulation and a public key infrastructure are in place, and that they are not yet used. The answer names no service built on them and no date for their launch. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found showing a digital way for people to prove who they are online, or a public service that accepts a digital signature or a login. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

MLI.short: In 2025 the national ID had no digital authentication function; no source found says whether the 2026 online platforms check it.
MLI.summary: DPI Map's record of 17 June 2025 says NINA, Mali's national identification number, has no digital authentication function. In December 2023 the head of the electronic certification and signature service said electronic signature had not officially started in Mali. In the last twelve months, on 10 February 2026, Mali launched two online platforms, ecasierjudiciaire.gouv.ml and enationalite.gouv.ml, for the criminal record and the nationality certificate. Citizens apply with their NINA and civil-status details. No source found says the platforms check the NINA against the register. Preparing would need a state-accepted authentication, e-signature or PKI service authorised, contracted or piloted.

MOZ.short: Authentication was used across services in 2025; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's Digital Certification System (SCDM), launched in 2023, lets accredited users sign and verify electronic documents free of charge. INTIC said more than ten public institutions used it by the end of 2024. In the last twelve months, Decree 40/2026, reported in August 2026, lets acts in the low-risk business procedure be validated by electronic signature. The ATDI tendered a national mobile digital ID and signature infrastructure in May 2026. No mobile ID or digital ID wallet is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

MRT.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2024.
MRT.summary: The Houwiyeti digital ID and digital-government platform, launched in 2023, handles 70 percent of passport requests, the ANRPTS director said in 2025. Tech Rek states Houwiyeti is the gateway public and private services use to verify citizens' identity. TECH5 says a digital ID is created from a passport or ID card and stored on the holder's phone. It is verified by selfie to log in to the e-government portal. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, an op-ed said Houwiyeti issues signed digital birth, marriage, divorce and death documents that can be checked by QR code. The latest dated fact found is that August 2026 op-ed.

MUS.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2024.
MUS.summary: Since 29 September 2026 about 884,000 licence holders can view a digital driving licence on the KOREK! app, L'Express reports, and MauPass handles identification and authentication. The 2024 regulations provide for the MauSign Certification Authority, which issues certificates stored on the ID card and one-time certificates for MauPass users to sign on the mobile ID. Biometric Update says Mauritius launched a mobile digital ID system in 2024. In the last twelve months the KOREK! launch is the one change found. The latest dated fact found is the launch of 29 September 2026.

MWI.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
MWI.summary: The Nzika Digital ID Wallet was launched in Lilongwe on 16 September 2026, and more than 22,000 people had signed up by launch day. The Homeland Security Minister said it lets citizens present verified credentials and reach services before their physical card arrives. The 2026 NRB fee regulations charge for e-KYC checks of mobile money, SIM, bank and utility customers. In the last twelve months, by November 2026, some banks refused the wallet, and the bankers' association said it was piloted with one bank. The latest dated fact found is that November 2026 report.

NAM.short: An authentication service was in use in 2026; no source found reports use across services.
NAM.summary: The Home Affairs minister, Lucia Iipumbu, said Namibia launched its national public key infrastructure under DigiNam in August 2026. In November 2026 the ICT ministry told a financial-sector advisory body it was ready to launch a PKI for legally recognised e-signatures. In the last twelve months the sources disagree. In November 2025 CRAN said the infrastructure was ready for the PKI rollout. In July 2026 an OPM director said electronic identity checks had saved about N$16 million on social grants. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

NER.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
NER.summary: In July 2026 the WURI Niger project said it was developing a National Population Register to identify and authenticate people seeking services, with a first enrolment phase in Niamey's five arrondissements due within weeks. Niger signed an MoU on 27 June 2025 with Libyan firm Al Itissal Al Jadeed for a new electronic national ID card aimed at online authentication. The July 2026 statement is the one change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

NGA.short: In 2026 people used an identity app to prove who they are for SIM, passport, tax and banking; no source says how many use it.
NGA.summary: NIMC's director general says NINAuth processes over 1.3 million identity checks a day for banks, fintechs and government agencies. About 63 government agencies had integrated with NIMC's verification API by October 2026. NIMC says individuals can use NINAuth to verify their identity for SIM registration, immigration and passports, tax filing and financial transactions, with their consent required. In the last twelve months, the NIMC Act 2026 made NIMC the national root certification authority. No figure has been found for how many people hold or use the NINAuth app. The latest dated fact found is the October 2026 agency count.

RWA.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
RWA.summary: A national ID deck of May 2026 says IN Groupe was procured to supply authentication and a PKI for digital signatures. In August 2026 Vital Strategies said digital birth registration linked to the national ID allows real-time identity checks across sectors, and that the system supports access to around 200 essential services. NIDA expects to issue digital IDs in July 2027. No change has been found in the last twelve months beyond the May and August 2026 items. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

SDN.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
SDN.summary: The Cybersecurity Authority calls SUDAPASS the national digital identity platform and says it verifies identity by biometrics, a PIN code and a QR code. The Sudanese Digital Identity smartphone app lets a user hold an account and sign electronic transactions. The transactions are binding and count as evidence in court. The digital ministry and the Central Bank are linking the remaining banks one by one, SUNA reports. In the last twelve months, the Baldna platform let users sign in with the SudaPass digital ID, as its login page showed in November 2026. The latest dated fact found is that November 2026 login page.

SEN.short: An authentication service was in use in 2026; no source found reports use across services.
SEN.summary: The e-Sénégal app, launched on 24 March 2026, signs users in on the NIN of the biometric ID card, and judicial records and nationality certificates were among its first procedures. ARCOP says the APPEL e-procurement platform, opened on 14 October 2025, uses strong authentication and e-signature. In the last twelve months, IPRES opened its proof-of-life campaign for pensioners on 1 July 2026 on the Maa ngi nii platform, which needs the ECOWAS national ID card. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

SLE.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
SLE.summary: NCRA Director General Massaquoi said on 10 August 2026 that NCRA has established an identity verification platform in use. Financial and telecommunications companies are among its users. The Director-General also said NCRA operates an eKYC platform integrated with multiple institutions that verifies identity against the NIN. The NIN covers about 93 per cent of the population. In the last twelve months, Minister Salima Bah told Parliament on 4 August 2026 that the Government remains committed to completing the SIM registration and NIN linkage exercise. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

SOM.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
SOM.summary: In late October 2026 NIRA announced that its Hubiye platform is in operation, letting service providers check an ID against its database by a one-time password sent to the holder. UNDP Somalia reports Hubiye checks across 25 services, public and private. NIRA's eAqoonsi app carries the national ID on a phone, and by August 2026 it had passed 50,000 downloads. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the Accountant General said the government payroll will be checked against NIRA's ID system. The latest dated fact found is the late October 2026 announcement.

SSD.short: Nothing found names a digital authentication service or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a digital authentication service, or says there is none.

STP.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
STP.summary: India's foreign ministry says Ooru Digital is building a MOSIP-based National Digital Identity system and a National Citizen Portal. The portal was launched on 27 March 2026 and gives access to public services through a national ID login. The World Bank mission reports working prototypes of a Verifiable Credentials Infrastructure and an electronic Signature service, with e-signature planned for May 2026. The portal launch is the one dated change found in the last twelve months, and the login is not shown in use. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

SWZ.short: Banks have checked IDs against the civil registry since 2024, through an e-KYC registry from 2025; no source found reports use beyond banks.
SWZ.summary: In July 2024 APC said commercial banks could check the civil registry to verify identity, and that the national ID card did not yet meet the criteria for digital identification. In March 2025 the central bank said financial institutions verify customers against the civil registry. In October 2025 it launched an e-KYC registry that banks, financial institutions and certain public administrations can use to verify clients. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No public body is named using the registry, and no source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

SYC.short: SeyID sign-in was used across government e-services in 2025; no source found reports a state-accepted ID wallet.
SYC.summary: Government e-services that require SeyID need a 60% validation level, reached by checking the holder's NIN card or passport by video against the Civil Status System. The Agency for Social Protection's ASP Connect platform, launched internally on 15 October 2025, is reached through the SeyID portal, which hosts all government entities' systems. The Seychelles Licensing Authority's online services require a SeyID account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. WISeKey said in April 2024 that the SeyID app holds the National ID in an e-wallet, but no state source says the authorities accept that card. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

TCD.short: An authentication or e-signature service was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
TCD.summary: On 8 May 2026 ANATS and Airtel Tchad signed a partnership, Tchadinfos reported, under which ANATS will verify Airtel's customer data and interconnect the two systems to identify mobile subscribers. On 10 March 2026 the finance ministry and ANATS signed a memorandum on consulting the national biometric population register, to improve identification, verification and authentication in administrative and financial procedures. Both agreements are the changes found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an authentication service is in use. Establishing would need one state-accepted authentication service in use.

TGO.short: In 2026 one-time-code login on the ID number served public services and banks; no source found reports remote proof by a digital ID.
TGO.summary: The National Identification Agency (ANID) told ID4Africa in 2026 that one-time-password authentication on the unique identification number is fully deployed and in use. It says its checks serve banks' e-KYC and public services such as hospitals, social protection, education and pensions. In March 2026 the World Bank said the e-ID authenticates beneficiaries of ANADEB's cash transfers on the Novissi platform. In the last twelve months, on 16 November 2026 the finance ministry put BIOSECU-CRT into service, an online face check that pensioners are alive. No source found says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

TUN.short: People could prove who they are online with a digital ID in 2026.
TUN.summary: The 2026 playbook counts over 450,000 Mobile IDs linked to a phone number and 35,000 linked to devices. Holders use them to reach online services and to sign documents and contracts in the citizen portal. The ministry's Mobile ID page lists 18 government portals that take its login or signature. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the communication technologies ministry launched the Khadamet app, which opens administrative services through the digital identity. An agriculture ministry circular of September 2026 requires its bodies to sign users in through E-Houwiya by 15 November. The latest dated fact found is that deadline of 15 November 2026.

TZA.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
TZA.summary: By April 2026 the e-Government Authority counted 723 institutions and service points using NGAO, its multi-factor sign-in for government systems. By August 2026, the government spokesman said, 157 institutions, 72 public and 85 private, were linked to NIDA's system to verify people. In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026 NIDA unveiled the NIDA Wallet, a phone wallet for use with participating institutions. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

UGA.short: A government app verifies users of e-services, with over 10 million subscribers in 2025; no source found reports independent use figures.
UGA.summary: NITA-U told ID4Africa in 2025 that UgPass has over 10 million subscribers and 35 public bodies, and its slides show the app verifying users of e-services without passwords. In October 2026 NITA-U said UGHub links NIRA's registry to more than 150 public bodies. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 NITA-U held the key ceremony for the national root and issuing certification authorities. NIRA says 10 of 107 partner institutions were checking NINs by fingerprint or iris through its system by 28 October 2026. The UgPass figures are NITA-U's own, and its credential wallet is planned for UgPass 2.0. The latest dated fact found is the November 2026 key ceremony.

ZAF.short: Authentication was used across services in 2026; no source found reports remote proof of identity by a digital ID.
ZAF.summary: Home Affairs' Online Verification Service checks identities against the population register in real time, Minister Schreiber said in April 2026. Network operators and banks use it. In August 2026 he told Parliament that the service had been stabilised and now checks faces. In the last twelve months, on 1 October 2026 the minister showed the digital ID in the MyMzansi app on his phone. An operational digital ID is targeted for 2027/2028. No source found since October 2023 says a mobile ID, ID wallet or signed credential is in service. Mature would need a state-accepted mobile ID app, ID wallet or signed credentials in service.

ZMB.short: An authentication service was in use in 2026; no source found reports use across services.
ZMB.summary: The farm-input subsidy's e-voucher system ran in all 116 districts, with redemption closing on 15 January 2026, and the Presidential Delivery Unit says it uses electronic know-your-customer checks to cut duplicate and ghost beneficiaries. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 Altron Security completed a key stage of the national PKI. In May 2026 the Bank of Zambia said a central eKYC platform was being built, checking Home Affairs digital IDs by API and fingerprint. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

ZWE.short: An authentication service was in use in 2026; no source found reports use across services.
ZWE.summary: In September 2026 the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe shut down ghost, fictitious and duplicate mobile money wallets, after linking the Civil Registry's national database with mobile financial services subscriber records. The Justice Minister said the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission was already using the Registrar-General's national population database to verify voter information and clean up the voters' roll. In the last twelve months, the 2027 budget allocated ZiG10 million to a public key infrastructure under the ICT ministry. No source found since October 2023 says authentication is used across services or channels. Operating would need authentication used across services or channels.

AGO.short: Births feed the ID card and registered deaths deregister the citizen, both said in 2026; no figure for records exchanged is known.
AGO.summary: In the last twelve months, Angola's Justice Minister said in July 2026 that the Bilhete de Identidade results from integrating birth-record data. The two computer systems are interoperable, he said. In April 2026 Aristides Marques, national director of Identification, Registries and Notary, said a death registered at the conservatória is sent to the database to deregister the citizen. In March 2026 Mbanza Kongo began registering newborns at a maternity post. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for records exchanged, numbers retired on death or records reconciled. Mature would need such a figure from a source of the past three years.

BDI.short: A link between the civil register and the ID system was under way in 2026.
BDI.summary: In the last twelve months, Burundi's territorial administration directorate said in August 2026 that civil registration is to be integrated with the national digital ID. The interior ministry presented one platform for civil records and the new biometric ID card on 6 May 2026. Burundi's own presentation says the two systems are not yet fully interoperable. Under the ID for D plan of July 2024, births at health facilities are to feed a unique ID number. No source found since October 2023 says a link is in service. Establishing would need records to pass one way or for one event, or one body to hold both registers.

BEN.short: Births and deaths pass between civil status and the ID register; a 2026 pilot reported 30,160 number updates, national figures not known.
BEN.summary: ANIP, the national identification agency, holds both the population register and the civil status file. Since April 2021 every birth is declared to the register, which issues the child's NPI, and a declared death sets the person's status to deceased in the ID system. In the last twelve months, ANIP's review of its birth-desk pilot counted 30,160 number updates in the register. The pilot ran in ten health facilities from 20 August 2025 to 20 February 2026. In September 2026 ANIP issued 50,109 free birth certificates to children under 14. No national figure for records exchanged has been found; the one held comes from the ten-facility pilot.

BFA.short: Nothing found names a link between the civil register and the ID system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BFA.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the civil register and the ID system are linked.

BWA.short: The civil register and the ID system were linked one way or for one event in 2026.
BWA.summary: Statistics Botswana says the Births and Deaths Registration System is integrated with the National Identification System. Since 2003 that system has assigned a unique birth registration number to every citizen child at birth. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 one budget provision of P108,505,050 covered maintenance of both systems. One department, Civil and National Registration, holds both. No source found since October 2023 says births enrol people in the ID system and deaths retire their numbers. Operating would need births to enrol people in the ID system and deaths to retire their ID numbers.

CAF.short: A link between the civil register and the ID system was under way in 2025.
CAF.summary: In November 2025 an article said the Central African Republic plans a national digital identity system, the SNID. The SNID is to unify the country's existing biometric and civil status databases. Implementation of the SNID is set for 2027 to 2032. No change to that plan has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a link is in service. Establishing would need records to pass one way or for one event, or one body to hold both registers.

The minister said the second phase is carried out with the support of the Universal Telecommunications Service Fund. In the last twelve months, on 16 November 2026, the minister told the House that phase two provides for 2,000 rural zones. No period beyond 2026 has been found for the second phase.

It also lists development of a national broadband master plan. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the policy working group at the Africa Broadband Maps national event in Lusaka concluded that Zambia lacks a national broadband policy and recommended formulating one. No stand-alone broadband policy has been found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan has been found for the last three years. In June 2022 the national procurement service director said the Sistema Nacional da Contratação Pública Electrónica, launched in April 2018, processed public purchases online. It had run 1,959 tender procedures since 2018. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

BDI.summary: PAFEN issued a World Bank-financed request for proposals on 23 September 2026 to design, build and deploy an end-to-end electronic public procurement system. Proposals were due on 13 November 2026. The finance minister said the platform is due to enter into force from 2027, with first tests expected in early 2027. Both dates are within the last twelve months. No earlier position has been found. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

BEN.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2023.
BEN.summary: A 2024 evaluation cited by ARMP looked at 757 calls published on SIGMaP in 2023 and found that only 21 reached the automatic contract page. In the last twelve months, the Treasury announced on 19 December 2025 that a new e-Procurement platform will replace SIGMAP. It comes under decree 2025-169 of 9 April 2025. ARMP says the platform is still being acquired and implemented. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The latest dated fact is the Treasury announcement of 19 December 2025.

BFA.short: A government e-procurement platform was being piloted in 2025; no source found says whether tenders are published or bid on it.
BFA.summary: The finance ministry's 2025 public-finance report, cited by OuagaNews, says the procurement-planning module was fully configured on the E-Burkindi platform. The module was piloted with ministries and institutions in 2025. A World Bank-backed project set out in 2022 to acquire, adapt and deploy an online e-GP solution for Burkina Faso. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says government tenders are published or bid online on E-Burkindi. None gives a figure for its use. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

BWA.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
BWA.summary: The PPRA said in December 2025 that it is working with the Ministry of Finance to develop a national e-procurement system. In March 2026 its chief executive told the National Public Procurement Pitso that Botswana has no fully integrated e-procurement platform and runs manual processes. A national system is promised by 2027. The PPADB had launched an Integrated Procurement Management System with online submission in July 2016. Both PPRA statements are from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

CAF.short: Nothing found names a government e-procurement system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government e-procurement system, or says there is none.

CIV.short: A single government e-procurement platform was in service in 2023; no source found says whether all public bodies must use it.
CIV.summary: The finance ministry told the Council of Ministers at the end of 2023 that SIGOMAP is the sole platform for managing public procurement. The Budget Ministry had opened online procurement on SIGOMAP on 25 July 2023, where firms consult notices, buy tender files and submit bids. The same communication says use extends to all contracting authorities of the ministries from 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says SIGOMAP runs to award or payment or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

CMR.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2025.
CMR.summary: The public-contracts minister told the National Assembly's finance committee that Coleps, launched in 2018, published 2,334 tender notices in 2025. It awarded 1,173 contracts from them, against 365 awards from 458 notices in 2024. The second version of COLEPS was launched on 25 June 2025. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the procurement regulator began training 20 procurement officers in Littoral to use Pridesoft, the integrated procurement system. Exclusive electronic award is compulsory from the 2027 financial year. The latest dated fact is that training in November 2026.

COD.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
COD.summary: ARMP said in April 2026 that SIGMAP is not yet in production and that training comes first. This came after a decree on electronic procurement of October 2024. ARMP said in March 2026 that pilot procurement cells were equipped through World Bank projects. Ecofin Agency says SIGMAP was launched in August 2022 after delays, and a shared services centre for procurement opened in June 2026. The April and March 2026 statements are from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

COG.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
COG.summary: Decree 2024-2072 of 10 October 2024 establishes an e-GP system run by ARMP, from programming to archiving. In the last twelve months, a workshop on 4 June 2026 validated the draft bidding document for the firm that will build it. ARMP says a workshop on 21-22 July 2026 adopted the tender file, pending the steering committee. The decree is the earlier position, and no source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

COM.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
COM.summary: In September 2025 a consultant report said Comoros is pursuing a reform to set up an e-Government Procurement system. It specifies an online tendering platform of two modules, with hosting. A draft e-GP implementing decree was under review. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end, is required of all public bodies, or gives a figure. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

CPV.short: A government e-procurement portal was in service in 2026; no source found says whether it is used end to end.
CPV.summary: The government said in March 2026 that electronic public procurement has existed in Cabo Verde since 2020. Central State Administration procedures are carried out through the official public purchasing portal. In the last twelve months it also said that a new e-procurement platform was awarded to ACIN-iCloud Solutions for CVE 70,000,000 over four years. The new platform is to extend e-procurement to local administration and to autonomous services and funds. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

DJI.short: Figures for tenders published on the government procurement portal were reported in 2026; online bidding is not yet in place.
DJI.summary: Decree 2023-038/PRE of February 2023 instituted the electronic public procurement portal. It requires contracting authorities to publish notices, tender documents and cancellations on it. RTD reported in October 2026 that the portal, launched in May 2023, lists 1,300 published contracts and 1,227 recorded awards since 2021. In the last twelve months, RTD also reported that electronic bid submission, e-signature and digital tracking of payments are planned over 2026-2028. A platform covering the whole cycle is due by 2027. Bids are not yet submitted online. Nothing found since October 2023 says the portal is required of all public bodies.

DZA.short: A government e-procurement system was in service in 2026; no source found reports end-to-end use.
DZA.summary: In December 2021 the finance ministry launched a portal for exchanging procurement documents and information, with procurement to be dematerialised progressively. In the last twelve months, TSA reported in March 2026 that Algeria has officially launched an electronic public procurement portal. The portal operates under law 23-12 of 5 August 2023. Firms download tender documents free and submit bids on it. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

EGY.short: Egypt was building a national e-procurement platform in 2025; no source found says it has gone live.
EGY.summary: On 4 August 2025 Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said Egypt's national electronic procurement platform was close to completion. He said it was not yet in operation. No later source found says it has gone live. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says government tenders are published or bid on the platform. None gives a figure for its use. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a government e-procurement system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government e-procurement system, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2025.
ETH.summary: The Public Procurement and Property Administration Authority says 172 federal institutions and 196 branch offices used its e-GP platform in fiscal year 2025/26. Its Director General says more than 597 billion birr in completed transactions went through e-GP that year. The Authority said 308.75 billion birr went through it in EFY 2017. It also says e-GP automates bidding, evaluation, contract signing and payment. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, Addis Ababa's finance bureau ordered 48 of the city's largest-spending agencies onto the electronic procurement platform. The latest dated fact is that order.

GAB.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
GAB.summary: On 27 December 2021 the Budget Minister launched the digital Journal des marchés publics at lejmp.ga, which publishes tender notices and results online. In the last twelve months, on 15 January 2026 the Ministry of Economy and Finance launched SIGFiP, which handles public procurement among all revenue and spending operations. Some procurement modules work and others are still being built. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

GHA.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2024.
GHA.summary: The Public Procurement Authority says GHANEPS, launched on 30 April 2019, had reached 869 public entities in all 16 regions by September 2023. It said in November 2023 that the grace period had ended and all public entities must use GHANEPS. It says 5,048 contracts had been awarded in GHANEPS from 3,205 published tenders by 23 April 2024. Its board chairman said in October 2025 that utilisation of GHANEPS is about 45%. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is that October 2025 statement.

GIN.short: Guinea launched a national e-procurement platform in 2025; no source found says whether tenders are published or bid on it.
GIN.summary: Guinea rolled out TELEMO, a national e-procurement platform built through a Guinea-Rwanda South-South partnership. It was officially launched on 17 November 2025. In the last twelve months, the procurement regulator ARMP said Télémo entered a new phase of use in September 2026, with companies registering on it. No earlier position has been found for that phase. No source found since October 2023 says government tenders are published or bid online through Télémo. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

GMB.short: Government e-procurement was being rolled out in 2026; no system taking tenders online is known.
GMB.summary: In August 2025 GPPA Director General Phoday Jaiteh said the authority had implemented a new e-procurement portal over the past two years, which streamlined business registration. In the last twelve months, the Gambia Public Procurement Authority's training of 8 to 10 October 2026 covered the rollout of the Electronic Government Procurement system. Its Board Vice Chairperson said the system will digitise the procurement cycle. No source found since October 2023 says government tenders are published or bid online through a system in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

GNB.short: Nothing found names a government e-procurement system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government e-procurement system, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2024; none in service is on record.
GNQ.summary: Law 11/2025 of 12 December 2025 brings in GE Compras, an electronic procurement information system for submitting and evaluating bids. A law firm's January 2026 article reports this and does not say the system is live. TACD CARTENA says the finance ministry mandated it, with AfDB support, to design an e-GP system, with a readiness report and roadmap. The law is from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

KEN.short: All government procurement went through e-procurement from 2026, with about KSh 18.3 billion of contracts by November; the share of all purchasing is not found.
KEN.summary: Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi said in August 2025 that e-GP was operational across government. K24 Digital reported in October 2025 that 1,477 procuring entities were listed on it, with no tender then awarded. In the last twelve months, Mbadi said in the 2026/27 Budget Statement that all procurement by government entities goes through e-GP from 1 July 2026. He said in November 2026 that contracts worth about KSh 18.3 billion had been processed through it. The figure is the Treasury's own, and no share of all government purchasing has been found.

LBR.short: Figures for contracts awarded through government e-procurement were reported in 2025; no source found reports its share of purchasing.
LBR.summary: President Boakai launched e-GP on 6 February 2025 for online bidding and made its use mandatory for all government procuring entities. PPCC executive director Bodger Scott Johnson said in September 2025 that contracts worth US$12,219,000 had been awarded through e-GP. In the last twelve months, PPCC said 56 procurement entities were onboarded as Phase II of the rollout began in May 2026. No figure for the share of government purchasing through e-GP has been found.

LBY.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2025.
LBY.summary: The General Information Authority reports 626 tenders announced on Attaat, the Tripoli government's procurement website, during July 2025. They were published by 189 government entities, with 840 entities registered on the platform. The Authority's head announced in February 2024 that the updated platform had started operating. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The latest dated fact is the July 2025 count.

LSO.short: Nothing found names a government e-procurement system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government e-procurement system, or says there is none.

MAR.short: Bids went through the Treasury's procurement portal in 2026; whether it covers the whole cycle, and how much passes through it, is not found.
MAR.summary: A World Bank blog says the portal opened in 2007 and that 68% of bids were filed online in June 2022, against 15% in December 2019. A ministerial order in force from September 2023 puts bid filing on the portal. In the last twelve months, an Al3omk op-ed says the Treasury suspended its procurement portal in late October 2026. Bid deadlines were put back as a result. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

MDG.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
MDG.summary: ARMP and UNDP trained central actors on an earlier e-GP platform in 2022. In the last twelve months, PREA said in February 2026 that the e-GP strategy is validated and an implementation firm is about to be deployed. PREA reports that the e-GP project team held a field mission in Boeny and Atsimo Andrefana in June 2026 to prepare nationwide deployment. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

MLI.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a government e-procurement system, so no stage is set.
MLI.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether government e-procurement is under way or in service in Mali. Every source found for it is dated 2021 or earlier. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that public procurement runs on paper.

MOZ.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
MOZ.summary: The government launched the e-GP project in April 2025, to be delivered in phases. European Dynamics says it won the contract to supply and install the national e-GP system. In December 2024 the CEDSIF chair said most electronic procurement in e-SISTAFE's state asset module was operational. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, O Economico tied the finance ministry's procurement reform to the e-CP system, which it does not say is in service. No source found since the April 2025 launch says tenders are published or bid online through a system in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

MRT.short: A government e-procurement system was in service in 2024; no source found reports end-to-end use.
MRT.summary: ARMP and the digital ministry launched the national public procurement portal on 3 December 2024, which carries procurement plans, tender announcements and results. In the last twelve months, the digital ministry said in July 2026 that SIGMAP's programming phase has run since early 2026. Tender-file management and electronic bid submission are in testing. The ministry counts 200 contracting authorities, over 600 users and 274 procurement plans on SIGMAP. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

MUS.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2024.
MUS.summary: The Procurement Policy Office says the web-based e-Procurement System was launched in September 2015 and that government made its use mandatory from July 2020. In 2023/24 public bodies published 7,681 electronic invitations for bids and received 18,599 electronic bid submissions, and 116 of 205 public bodies used it. A MAPS assessment finds use selective, with bid evaluation and award often offline. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is that tender documents were published on the Public Procurement Portal in September 2025.

MWI.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2026.
MWI.summary: The PPDA reports 562 tenders published on MANePS by 5 October 2026, with 7,417 registered suppliers. A Treasury circular makes MANePS mandatory for all procuring entities from 1 April 2026. Nation Online reports MANePS was formally launched with 174 procuring entities onboarded, and says it manages the cycle from planning and tendering to award and payment. In the last twelve months, Phase II features were in testing with 18 entities for November 2026. The latest dated fact is the 5 October 2026 count.

NAM.short: All public entities were required to use the e-procurement portal in 2025; no source found reports figures for tenders or value through it.
NAM.summary: On 13 October 2022 the Ministry of Finance announced the E-GP portal was operational, publishing bid advertisements, documents, opening reports and notices of award. Namibia's Procurement Policy Unit says all public entities must upload plans, bid adverts, bidding documents, opening reports and award notices to it. An end-to-end platform is planned as phase two. World Bank expert Devesh Mishra said fewer than 5% of public entities use the portal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives the tenders, value or share of purchasing through e-procurement. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a figure for e-procurement: tenders, value or share of purchasing through it.

NER.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a government e-procurement system, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether government e-procurement is under way or in service in Niger. Every source found for it is dated 2022 or earlier. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that public procurement runs on paper.

NGA.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
NGA.summary: BPP Director General Adebowale Adedokun said on 8 October 2026 that the e-GP system the Bureau is building will move federal bidding fully online. He said in February 2026 that from 2 March 2026 MDAs must take bids electronically. The Bureau said in September 2026 that its reform centres on an e-GP system to automate the main stages of procurement across government. All three statements are from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

RWA.short: Government e-procurement ran end to end in 2024; figures for its use are not reported.
RWA.summary: On 27 June 2016 the RPPA Director General launched Umucyo in 8 pilot institutions, with all to use it from April 2017. Law 62/2018 requires all public procurement to use it unless RPPA authorises otherwise. Open Contracting Partnership says Rwanda's Umucyo e-procurement system is used by all national and local government agencies. In November 2021 an RPPA survey counted about 200 procuring entities and over 5,000 bidders on it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for e-procurement. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a figure for e-procurement: tenders, value or share of purchasing through it.

SDN.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
SDN.summary: Minister of State at Finance Mohamed Nour Abdel-Daim announced on 17 March 2026 that design of the national electronic procurement system is complete. The system includes a government tender platform, and its launch is being prepared. The National Medical Supplies Fund ran its first electronic tender for medicines since the war in November 2025, which drew 67 competing companies. That tender was one body's own purchasing. The March 2026 announcement is from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a national e-procurement system is in service. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

SEN.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2026.
SEN.summary: ARCOP says the APPEL platform has been in service since 14 October 2025, its first phase covering publication, submission and opening of bids. It gives figures for APPEL: nearly 400 registered suppliers, over 80 procurement plans published and 15 procedures launched, nine with electronic opening of bids. In the last twelve months, ARCOP said it is extending APPEL, with generalisation targeted from January 2027 and training for more than 325 contracting authorities. No source found says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The latest dated fact is the generalisation target of January 2027.

SLE.short: Government tenders were published online in 2026; no source found says whether bids are taken online across government.
SLE.summary: The National Public Procurement Authority opened an online e-GP portal in January 2026, for supplier registration and tender notices. In the last twelve months, it launched the Procurement Requisition and Bid Publication modules of the Salone e-GP System on 7 July 2026. Training of pilot ministries on electronic bid submission began in June 2026. No source found says e-procurement runs end to end. None says it is required of all public bodies. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

SOM.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a government e-procurement system, so no stage is set.
SOM.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether government e-procurement is under way or in service in Somalia. The one source found for it is dated 2021. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that public procurement runs on paper.

SSD.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
SSD.summary: In February 2025 the PPDAA chairperson said the tender portal ppdaatenderportal.gov.ss had been prepared. The chairperson said bid invitations, bid awards and provider registration shall be carried out through it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is in service. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies, and none gives a figure for it. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

STP.short: A government e-procurement system was in service in 2025; no source found reports end-to-end use.
STP.summary: In November 2025 the government officially launched the Portal dos Contratos Públicos. It was described as the country's first electronic platform of its kind. It centralises procurement notices, contracts and tender plans. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies, and none gives a figure for it. Operating would need e-procurement that runs from tender to award or payment, or is required of all public bodies.

SWZ.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
SWZ.summary: An AfDB appraisal of 2022 found the e-GP strategy approved but not adopted. In the last twelve months, the Auditor General told the Public Accounts Committee in June 2026 that of E18.8 million appropriated for the national e-GP system only E500,000 was spent. The Finance Principal Secretary said the project is implemented. The Central Bank of Eswatini's own e-procurement system went live in October 2025 for the Bank's purchasing. No source found since October 2023 says the national e-GP system takes tenders. Establishing would need government tenders published or bid online through a system in service.

SYC.short: A 2026 loan funds e-procurement reform and an adviser was sought in November 2026; no system has been found built, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: No stage is set. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is procured, being built, piloted or in service. In September 2026 the African Development Bank approved a loan that lists one among the reforms it supports. In November 2026 the Procurement Oversight Unit sought an adviser to help draft the requirements for a system vendor. Both are from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. Preparing would need an e-procurement system procured, being built or piloted.

TCD.short: Electronic payment of suppliers is planned for 2027, but no system is known to be built, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: No stage is set. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement or supplier-payment system is procured, being built, piloted or in service. The 2027 budget orientations plan an electronic payment system for early 2027. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether tenders are published or bid online, and none gives a figure for e-procurement. Preparing would need an e-procurement system procured, being built or piloted.

TGO.short: Togo's procurement regulator sought consultants in 2026 to prepare an e-procurement system; none is known to be built, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: No stage is set. In October 2026 the procurement regulator ARCOP sought four consultants to help prepare a future e-procurement system. That notice is from the last twelve months. A World Bank-backed strategy for such a system was discussed at a workshop in October 2025. No source found since October 2023 says an e-procurement system is procured, being built, piloted or in service. Preparing would need an e-procurement system procured, being built or piloted.

TUN.short: Figures for bids through government e-procurement were reported in 2023; no source found reports the value and share of purchasing through it.
TUN.summary: Government representatives told parliament's administration committee in November 2023 that public procurement runs online through the TUNEPS system. They said it was made general and compulsory for all ministries and public institutions in 2019. The national public procurement observatory reports 1,536 public buyers and 17,835 suppliers registered on TUNEPS in 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for the value or share of purchasing through TUNEPS has been found.

TZA.short: Tanzania's e-procurement system had handled 397,395 procurement proceedings worth 40.4 trillion shillings by August 2026.
TZA.summary: The Public Procurement Regulatory Authority says NeST, introduced in 2023, replaced paper tendering and takes tenders online. The Public Procurement Act of 2023, in force from 17 June 2024, mandates NeST for all procurement. In May 2025 Director General Dennis Simba said NeST had handled 130,032 tenders worth Sh14.9 trillion. In the last twelve months, the Authority said on 29 October 2026 that NeST had processed 430,643 tenders worth Sh42.6 trillion since September 2023. The latest dated fact is that October 2026 count.

UGA.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2026.
UGA.summary: The Ministry of Finance's procurement commissioner said in May 2025 that the home-grown system was piloted in 2020, and rolled out in 2021. PPDA's Benson Turamye said in April 2026 that 36 of more than 400 procuring entities run e-GP end to end. They have done more than 38,000 contracts on it. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Finance and PPDA rolled out eGP 2.0 to another 100 public entities on 20 July 2026, bringing the total to 136. The latest dated fact is that rollout.

ZAF.short: Figures for tenders through government e-procurement were reported in 2026; no source found says whether it runs end to end.
ZAF.summary: A Treasury spokesperson told Business Day in October 2025 that procurement is still largely paper based and that an e-GP system is being developed in phases. In the last twelve months, National Treasury's September 2026 deck says eTenders handles tender publication, online bid submission, online bid evaluation and publication of awards. It gives eTenders an average of 3,300 tenders and 1,800 awards a month. A MAPS assessment found 73% of registered organs of state published tenders on eTenders in 2023-2024. Whether e-procurement runs end to end is not settled.

ZMB.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2024.
ZMB.summary: The Zambia Public Procurement Authority's circular says procurement is carried out on the e-GP system from 16 April 2024. It directs all procuring entities to run all procurements of goods, works or services on e-GP, except listed methods. ZPPA acting director-general Justin Matimuna said 14,732 tenders were published on the system in the third quarter of 2024, from 431 procuring entities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is the third-quarter 2024 count.

ZWE.short: Government e-procurement ran from tender to award in 2025; no source found reports figures for its use.
ZWE.summary: The Herald reports the eGP system, launched in October 2023, became operational on 1 January 2024. Over 9,900 suppliers and 380 procuring entities had registered by 31 March 2024. UGA.short: Firms could register online in 2026; the law made the registration number the tax number, but the switch was not complete.
UGA.summary: In June 2026 the Uganda Registration Services Bureau unveiled its e-Registry, one online portal for business registration that replaced the earlier system. In September 2026 the revenue authority said the number URSB issues to a firm will serve as its tax identifier, under section 4 of the Tax Procedures Code Act. The move away from the separate tax number has begun, and old tax numbers stop working only at full rollout. Both date from the last twelve months. No source found says the switch is complete. Operating would need registration to give a firm one number shared with the tax authority or social security.

ZAF.short: Firms could register online in 2026; no source found reports a number shared with tax, and half of active companies had filed beneficial owners.
ZAF.summary: In 2026 CIPC states external company registration is available only on its e-Services platform, with no manual or e-mail applications accepted. The CIPC says the beneficial ownership register had received more than 3.2 million filings by 27 May 2026. The trade minister said on 22 September 2025 that filings covered 1,139,011 of 2,297,242 active private companies, 49.58 percent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says registration gives a firm one number shared with tax or social security. Operating would need registration to give a firm one number shared with the tax authority or social security.

ZMB.short: A new business register was being built in 2026; beneficial owners were recorded for 44 percent of firms in 2025.
ZMB.summary: In January 2026 PACRA said a three-year, GIZ-funded rebuild of the business register began in December 2025. Open Ownership says it is working with PACRA and GIZ on an in-house system to digitise more than a hundred PACRA services, starting with name clearance, registration and incorporation. The rebuild dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. PACRA said beneficial ownership reporting stood at 44 percent in December 2025. No source found since October 2023 says firms can register online. Establishing would need online business registration in service.

ZWE.short: Firms could register online in 2024; no source found reports a number shared with tax.
ZWE.summary: In September 2024 LEX Africa said company registration in Zimbabwe had moved from a manual paper system to electronic filing, under the 2020 COBE Act, and that the system is now operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says registration gives a firm one number shared with tax or social security. None says the register collects beneficial owners. Operating would need registration to give a firm one number shared with the tax authority or social security.

AGO.short: Final results of the RGPH 2024 were published in 2025, and results of the 2023 household health survey were out by 2026.
AGO.summary: INE released the final results of the RGPH 2024 on 20 November 2025, after enumerating Angola from 19 September to 20 December 2024. Angop reports the count at 36,604,681 residents. In the last twelve months, INE issued provincial reports, the last for Luanda in February 2026. A 2026 Countdown 2030 report on Angola measures health coverage against the results of the DHS 2023 household survey, and breaks them down by wealth, schooling and residence.

BDI.short: The RGPHAE 2024 was counted in 2024 and its preliminary results published in March 2025; no recent household survey is on record.
BDI.summary: Burundi carried out its combined population, housing, agriculture and livestock census in 2024. Decree 100/032 of 27 March 2025 published preliminary results, counting 12,332,788 residents and 2,724,457 ordinary households. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Definitive results have not been found, and no source reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

BEN.short: A population census was being prepared in 2024; none counted since 2016 is known.
BEN.summary: The director general of INStaD announced that main mapping for the fifth census (RGPH5) began on 19 March 2024, covering 74 communes after a pilot in Cotonou, Cove and Parakou. The fourth census's definitive results were adopted by the Council of Ministers on 21 May 2015. INStaD also published the main indicators of the EHCVM survey of 2021-2022. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports a census counted since October 2016. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

BFA.short: Final results of the 5e RGPH were published in 2022; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
BFA.summary: INSD published the key final results of the 5th national population and housing census in June 2022. The census was enumerated in November to December 2019 and counted 20,505,155 residents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A multisectoral continuous survey and an LSMS-ISA survey are named in sources read, with no results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

BWA.short: The PHC 2022 was counted in 2022; no results of it are known to be out.
BWA.summary: Statistics Botswana's annual report for 2023-24 gives a 2022 count of 2,359,609 people and states the Population and Housing Census was conducted. Minister Segokgo cites the 2022 census as the source of Botswana's population figure. In the last twelve months, Statistics Botswana presented findings of the 2024 Household Access and Individual Use of ICTs Survey in September 2026, with fieldwork from June to August 2024. No preliminary or final results of the census have been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

CAF.short: The RGPH-4 was counted and in tabulation in October 2026; no source found says whether any results are published.
CAF.summary: In August 2026 ICASEES presented the third phase of data cleaning for the RGPH-4, the country's first digital census. In the last twelve months, a committee reviewed the first provisional results on 23 to 25 September 2026. ICASEES then held a retreat at Boali on 2 to 5 October 2026 to clean and tabulate the data. No preliminary or final results have been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

CIV.short: The RGPH 2021 was counted in 2021; no results of it are known to be out.
CIV.summary: A World Bank Mission 300 progress report for the first quarter of 2026 bases Cote d'Ivoire's clean cooking access figure on the latest RGPH, 2021. That implies a population and housing census was counted in 2021. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No release of preliminary or final results of that census has been found, and no source reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A MICS 2026 is named in a source read, with no results dated. Operating would need preliminary or final results of the census published.

CMR.short: The RGPH-4 was counted in 2026; no results of it are known to be out.
CMR.summary: Counting for Cameroon's 4th general population and housing census, launched on 24 April 2026, closed on 15 September 2026. It was coupled with the agriculture and livestock census. In the last twelve months, a Prime Minister's order made public on 31 July 2026 set a complementary enumeration from 1 August to 15 September 2026 to find households not yet counted. The government, with FAO and UNFPA, field-tested a hybrid method in October and November 2025. No preliminary or final results have been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

COD.short: A population census was being prepared in 2026; none counted since 2016 is known.
COD.summary: Census-cartography operations for the second census (RGPH-2) were launched on 28 September 2026, and general enumeration is planned from July 2027. In the last twelve months, training of 1,868 census cartographic operators began in Kinshasa on 9 September 2026, with fieldwork from 15 September. In July 2026 the Plan minister cited published results of the Demographic and Health Survey EDS III RDC 2024. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

COG.short: Congo counted its fifth census in December 2023; no published results of it are known.
COG.summary: ADIAC says the fifth general population census, RGPH-5, was conducted in December 2023. In the last twelve months, on 27 November 2025 the national statistics institute opened a workshop to validate indicators and tables drawn from it, where its preliminary results were on display.
