No source found reports preliminary or final results of the RGPH-5 published, or results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Operating would need preliminary or final results of the census published.

COM.short: The RGPH 2017 was counted in 2017; no results of it are known to be out.
COM.summary: The INSEED microdata archive lists the 2017 population and housing census, with data years 2017-2018, added on 24 October 2025. In the last twelve months, INSEED released version 1.0 (April 2026) of the EHCVM 2024 survey data, a nationally representative survey of 5,487 households fielded May to November 2024. INSEED has also set up a digital cartography laboratory to prepare the fifth census, with a pilot in 50 enumeration areas. No preliminary or final results of the 2017 census have been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

CPV.short: A population census was counted in 2021; no release of its results is known.
CPV.summary: The World Bank gives 2021 as Cape Verde's latest census, and its SPI lists counts in 2000, 2010 and 2021. The statistics office's own account of the 2021 count has not been found. A July 2026 opinion piece says INE released partial poverty figures in October 2024, and that the full results of the income survey begun in December 2022 were still unpublished. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No release of 2021 census results has been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

DJI.short: Final results of the RGPH-3 2024 were published in 2026; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
DJI.summary: INSTAD states that RGPH-3 data collection took place in April and May 2024, with provisional results published in June 2024. UNFPA Djibouti lists the definitive-results report of the third census as published, under a site date of 1 January 2026 that may be a system default. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A MICS-7 and an EDAM5 survey are named in sources read, with no results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

DZA.short: A population census was counted in 2022; no release of its results is known.
DZA.summary: The World Bank gives 2022 as Algeria's latest census, and its SPI lists counts in 1998, 2008 and 2022. The statistics office's own account of the 2022 count has not been found, and the World Bank is the only source found for any census in Algeria. The World Bank names the 2018-2019 MICS as the latest health survey and a 2011 household survey as the latest source on income. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No release of 2022 results has been found. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

EGY.short: A census was counted in 2017 and the next is set for 2028; no release of 2017 results is known.
EGY.summary: The World Bank gives 2017 as Egypt's latest census, and its SPI lists counts in 1996, 2006 and 2017. In the last twelve months, the Prime Minister chaired the High Committee for the next census in February 2026. On 6 August 2026 the cabinet moved the census from 2027 to 2028, and a presidential decree is still needed to run it. No release of 2017 results has been found. The World Bank names the 2015 Health Issues Survey as the latest health survey. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

ERI.short: A 2026 source says no census has been counted in ten years and none is being prepared.
ERI.summary: UNECA's synopsis of African population statistics, of August 2026, states that Eritrea has not conducted a population census since independence. It was published in the last twelve months. No census being prepared has been found, and no source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. An Eritrean Population and Health Survey 2025 and a Household Income and Expenditure Survey are named in a UNDP report, with no results dated. A census only promised does not count. Preparing would need a census being prepared, with mapping, a pilot, funding or a date set in the past three years.

ETH.short: The last census on record was counted in 2007; none since 2016 or in preparation is known, so no stage is set.
ETH.summary: No stage is set. The last census on record was counted in 2007, and Addis Fortune said in June 2026 that none has been completed since. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No census in preparation has been found, and no source says none is being prepared. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that no population census has been counted in ten years and that none is being prepared.

GAB.short: The RGPL 2026 was counted in 2026; no results of it are known to be out.
GAB.summary: Gabon's national population and housing census (RGPL) has been enumerated. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the governor of Estuaire province reported census coverage above 95% in her province, in the same source. No count of the population from the census has been found. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published, or results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

GHA.short: Final results of the 2021 census were published in 2026; no household survey result dated since 2023 is known.
GHA.summary: The Ghana Statistical Service's census page gives the 2021 Population and Housing Census as the latest national census and offers its reports, with regional and district profiles. The page projects the next census for 2030. A March 2025 progress form lists the Annual Household Income and Expenditure Survey among current surveys and cites its report on labour force participation, without a release date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national household survey result dated since October 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a survey, with results published in the past three years.

GIN.short: The RGPH-4 was counted in July 2025 and its preliminary results published in February 2026; no recent household survey is on record.
GIN.summary: Guinea's fourth general population census (RGPH-4) was conducted from 1 to 31 July 2025. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Plan, through INS, published preliminary results on 25 February 2026, giving a population of 17,521,167, and a presidential decree of 6 March 2026 gave them effect. Final results have not been found. A post-enumeration survey launched on 30 October 2025 assesses the census's coverage. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Mature would need a national household survey with results published in the past three years.

GMB.short: The 2024 census's preliminary report came out in September 2024, and a 2026 labour force survey was published.
GMB.summary: On 17 September 2024 the Gambia Bureau of Statistics launched the preliminary report of the 2024 digital population and housing census, which gives a population of 2.4 million. Final results have not been found. In the last twelve months, the Bureau lists the Gambia Labour Force Survey GLFS 2026 (Q1), with reports and microdata for download. It also published a report comparing its labour force survey across three rounds, 2023 Q1, 2025 Q1 and 2026 Q1.

GNB.short: The RGPH-4 was counted and its preliminary results published in July 2026; no recent household survey is on record.
GNB.summary: UNFPA states that Guinea-Bissau's first fully digital census, RGPH-4, was completed and its preliminary results presented on 23 July 2026. In the last twelve months, INE released those results after data collection closed, giving 2,191,300 residents, 304,939 households and 559,303 dwellings. Final results have not been found. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

GNQ.short: A population census was being prepared in 2026; none counted since 2016 is known.
GNQ.summary: The National Statistics Council's 27 August 2026 session was to hear progress on the fifth General Population and Housing Census (CGPV-V), authorised by Decree 25/2025 of 3 March. In the last twelve months, the Scientific Committee validated the project document, communication strategy and resource-mobilisation strategy on 20 August 2026. INEGE held a workshop on 27 to 29 July 2026 to validate the project document and mobilisation strategies. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2019 census data were on its open data portal in 2025, and its 2022 household health survey was published in 2024.
KEN.summary: On 31 January 2025 the director general of KNBS said groundwork had been laid for the 2029 census, Kenya's seventh, after a court cancelled the results of the 2019 census for parts of Wajir, Mandera and Garissa. Pollicy reported in 2025 that Kenya's open data portal gives free access to the 2019 census. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest survey found is the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey. The Communications Authority published its ICT fact sheet in December 2024.

LBR.short: Final results of the 2022 Liberia Population and Housing Census were published in 2023; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
LBR.summary: LISGIS enumerated the 2022 Liberia Population and Housing Census, with census night on 11 November 2022 and a total enumerated population of 5,250,187. It released preliminary results in February 2023 and later published the final results. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A Household Income and Expenditure Survey, a National Labor Force Survey and the 2019/2020 DHS are named in sources read, with no results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

LBY.short: A population census was being prepared in 2024; none counted since 2016 is known.
LBY.summary: The Libya Observer reported in August 2024 that the Government of National Unity reviewed progress on the seventh national population census, the first since 2006. Libya had been divided into census areas. Preparations were said to be on track. In the last twelve months, LibyaReview, citing Al Jazeera, said in July 2026 that political division had prevented the launch of a new census. The Ministry of Planning's statistics director says the same. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

LSO.short: The 2026 Housing and Population Census was counted in 2026; no results of it are known to be out.
LSO.summary: The government states that enumeration of the 2026 Housing and Population Census has concluded, with mop-up in Maseru and cattle pounds. In the last twelve months, enumeration with reference night 11 April 2026 concluded, and over 8,000 temporary field staff were employed. The Bureau of Statistics deployed enumerators, with payment delays and an internal probe into enumerators outside the approved lists. The Bureau says results come after review, and none have been found. Its page lists the Labour Force Survey 2024 Indicators as its latest release. Operating would need preliminary or final results of the 2026 census published.

MAR.short: A national household survey published results in 2026, after final census results.
MAR.summary: The government adopted decree 2.24.1009 fixing Morocco's legal population from the RGPH 2024 results, at 36,828,330 on 1 September 2024. The census counted 36.8 million inhabitants, including 148,152 foreign residents, with a new immigration module. In the last twelve months, HCP published the first Q1 2026 results of the new national labour force survey (EMO2026). The survey replaces the Enquete nationale sur l'emploi and has an annual sample of 135,000 households.

MDG.short: The RGPH-3 2018 was counted in 2018; no results of it are known to be out.
MDG.summary: The third general population and housing census (RGPH-3) was held in 2018. In the last twelve months, INSTAT presented the RGPH-4 project document to partners on 12 May 2026, with enumeration planned for 2028 and support from the World Bank's STATCAP II project and UNFPA. A UN Madagascar account dated 5 March 2026 describes MICS7 2025 as a reference data source, carried out by INSTAT with UNICEF on 21,000 households. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

MLI.short: The RGPH5 was counted in 2022; no results of it are known to be out.
MLI.summary: INSTAT's microdata catalogue lists the fifth general population and housing census (RGPH5) of Mali, dated 2022. In the last twelve months, INSTAT's Q4 2025 bulletin reported validation of the Directory of Localities of Mali, produced from RGPH5 data, on 16-18 December 2025 in Bamako. INSTAT published the 2025 annual report of the EMOP household survey in the second quarter of 2026. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

MOZ.short: The Census 2017 was counted in 2017; no results of it are known to be out.
MOZ.summary: INE says the last census, in 2017, counted just over 26 million people. In the last twelve months, a pilot census ran in Magude district in August 2026, ahead of the first digital census planned for 2027. In September 2026 INE's national planning meeting put the preparation of the 2027 census at the centre of its agenda. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the 2017 census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

MRT.short: Final results of the RGPH 2023 were published in 2026; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
MRT.summary: La Depeche reports that Mauritania's fifth general population and housing census counted nearly 5 million inhabitants. In the last twelve months, a regional workshop opened in Nouadhibou on 18 February 2026 to disseminate the definitive results of the fifth RGPH 2023. ANSADE held a workshop in Atar on 3 August 2026, where it presented the final results for Adrar wilaya. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A 2025 EPCV survey is named in a source read, with no results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

MUS.short: The 2022 Housing and Population Census was counted in 2022; no results of it are known to be out.
MUS.summary: Statistics Mauritius says its labour force estimates from 2025 use population figures revised to the results of the 2022 population census. In the last twelve months, its first-quarter 2026 labour force report says the census results were used to review sampling strata from 2023. Statistics Mauritius released its ICT statistics report on 10 July 2026, with 2024 results of the Continuous Multi-Purpose Household Survey. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

MWI.short: The Population and Housing Census was counted in 2018; no results of it are known to be out.
MWI.summary: Malawi held a 2018 Population and Housing Census. In the last twelve months, the same report says Malawi is preparing its 7th census, scheduled for September 2028, and its statistics office held a benchmarking mission in Zambia on 7 to 11 September 2026. Finance minister Joseph Mwanamvekha said the coming census and related economic surveys are budgeted at about $55 million, with the US Census Bureau, UK ONS and UNFPA expected to co-finance them. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

NAM.short: Final results of the 2023 Population and Housing Census were published in 2024; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
NAM.summary: The NSA released the 2023 Population and Housing Census Main Report on 30 October 2024, which it says contains final results. Census night was 24 September 2023, and the population was 3,022,401. Preliminary results had been launched in March 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. The Namibia Household Income and Expenditure Survey 2015/16 and the Labour Force Survey 2016 are among surveys named, with no recent results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

NER.short: A population census was being prepared in 2025; none counted since 2016 is known.
NER.summary: On 8 October 2025 the acting head of the statistics institute INS said Niger's fifth census was fully financed with partners and in active preparation, with a budget above 35 billion FCFA. The INS reported continued pilot enumeration on 7 April 2025. A UNFPA posting set a field pretest for July 2025 and the start of enumeration for December 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

NGA.short: A population census was being prepared in 2026; none counted since 2016 is known.
NGA.summary: Nigeria's last national census was held in November 2006. The next is being prepared as the country's first digital census. In the last twelve months, a minister said in October 2026 that the National Population Commission had mapped more than 65 million properties for the count. By March 2025 the Commission had mapped and demarcated the whole country and trained staff, and a budget of N980 billion had been proposed to the President. No date for the count has been found. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

RWA.short: The 2022 census was counted and its main results published in 2023, and a demographic and health survey published results in 2026.
RWA.summary: NISR states the Fifth Rwanda Population and Housing Census was enumerated from 16 to 30 August 2022, and published its Main Indicators Report in February 2023. A March 2025 presentation gives the count as 13,246,394 people in 3,312,743 households. In the last twelve months, NISR announced the release of the 2025 Demographic and Health Survey on 6 January 2026. Its final report was published in 2026. NISR added the 2025 Labour Force Survey microdata to its catalogue on 8 April 2026.

SDN.short: The last census on record was counted in 2008; none since or in preparation is known, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. The last census on record was counted in 2008. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No census in preparation since October 2023 has been found, and no source says none is being prepared. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that no population census has been counted in ten years and that none is being prepared.

SEN.short: The RGPH-5 2023 was counted in 2023; no results of it are known to be out.
SEN.summary: ANSD's national data archive lists the fifth general population and housing census, Senegal 2023 (RGPH-5), as a catalogued dataset. The ENTICS sample was drawn from the base of the 2023 census, and a DGPSN presentation gives Senegal's population as 18,000,000 from it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. ANSD's archive also lists the national employment survey first quarter 2025 as a dataset, last modified 21 October 2025. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

SLE.short: Final results of the 2021 Mid-Term Population and Housing Census were published in 2022; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
SLE.summary: Statistics Sierra Leone published the final results of the 2021 Mid-Term Population and Housing Census in a report dated September 2022, counting 7,548,702 people. In the last twelve months, Stats SL announced on 7 October 2026 that it was deploying 500 tablets and mapping software. It said the cartographic mapping begun in October 2025 was complete. A mock census enumeration was closing on 19 October 2026. The national census is scheduled for December 2026. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. Mature would need a national household survey with results published in the past three years.

SOM.short: A population census was being prepared in 2025; none counted since 2016 is known.
SOM.summary: In April 2025 WorldPop trained Somali statisticians to map pre-census enumeration areas in five districts, with full enumeration to follow if security permits. Since August 2024 the Gates Foundation has funded UNFPA to collect pre-census enumeration data for population modelling. The World Bank lists 1987 as the year of the latest census. In the last twelve months, UNDP in April 2026 quoted the Director General of the statistics bureau naming the Socioeconomic and Demographic Survey among its outputs. No census counted since October 2016 has been found. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

SSD.short: A population census was being prepared in 2025; none counted since 2016 is known, and no date for it is set.
SSD.summary: With UNFPA support the Bureau of Statistics prepared a census dossier and an operations manual in 2025. Radio Tamazuj quotes the chair of the National Bureau of Statistics saying the Council of Ministers approved the census budget. It is still awaiting funding. In the last twelve months, the Bureau and UNICEF released the 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey on 21 April 2026, covering more than 10,000 households. No census counted since October 2016 has been found, and no date set for the next. Establishing would need a population census counted in the past ten years, with no results out yet.

STP.short: Final results of the V RGPH were published in 2025; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
STP.summary: INE released the final data of the fifth general population and housing census on 25 July 2025. It counted 212,017 people on 15 November 2024, of whom 209,607 were the legal resident population. The enumeration ran from 15 November to 15 December 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A March 2026 article cites the 2017 household budget survey. Mature would need a national household survey with results published in the past three years.

SWZ.short: The Population and Housing Census 2017 was counted in 2017; no results of it are known to be out.
SWZ.summary: The minister said the last population and housing census was conducted in 2017 and was the country's first digital census. In November 2025 the planning ministry and UNFPA launched the 2027 Population and Housing Census, and the Central Statistical Office is running its first phase, mapping and listing. No other change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the 2017 census published. An August 2019 profile listed MICS5 from 2014 as a national health survey. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

SYC.short: Final results of the Population and Housing Census 2022 were published in 2024; no household survey published since 2023 is known.
SYC.summary: The NBS published Volume 2, the main report of the 2022 Population and Housing Census, with results at national, regional and district level, in March 2024. The census was Seychelles' sixth since independence and its first digital one. The NBS benchmarks its population estimates to it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports results of a national household survey published since October 2023. A Quarterly Labour Force Survey is named in a source read, with no results dated. Mature would need a national household survey (DHS, MICS, living standards or labour force) with results published in the past three years.

TCD.short: The RGPH-3 2026 was counted in 2026; no results of it are known to be out.
TCD.summary: INSEED states that collection operations of the third general population and housing census (RGPH-3) officially ended on 6 August 2026. It was the country's first fully digital census. In the last twelve months, a few days before the count closed, the national coordinator for nomadic populations found in Batha that no enumerator had yet reached one herder camp, and ordered a team sent. No source found reports preliminary or final results of the census published. Operating would need preliminary or final results of that census published.

TGO.short: A national household survey published results in 2024, after final census results.
TGO.summary: INSEED published the definitive results of RGPH-5 (November 2022) by region, prefecture, sex and urban/rural, totalling 8,095,498 residents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is a workshop on 13 December 2024. It presented detailed results of the second harmonised household living conditions survey (EHCVM-2), with fieldwork in 2021-2022. The RGPH-5 results were presented alongside them.

TUN.short: A national household survey published results in 2024, after final census results.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's Institut National de la Statistique announced the publication of the official results of the 2024 general population and housing census at a press conference on 17 May 2025. INS gives 2024 census housing counts of 4,265,636 dwellings. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest survey found is the 2023 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey. The economy ministry, the INS and UNICEF presented its results on 12 February 2024, covering 11,000 households with a 90% response rate.

TZA.short: The 2022 census report came out within weeks and a labour force survey published results in 2026; no source found says whether census results were final.
TZA.summary: Tanzania released its 2022 census report within 45 days of data collection, the Statistician General said in March 2024. A March 2026 TCRA presentation gives 61,741,120 people in 14,152,803 private households. In the last twelve months, the NBS microdata catalogue released the Integrated Labour Force Survey 2025 on 15 July 2026 as edited final data for public use, covering 14,232 households. No source found says whether the census report released in 2022 gave preliminary or final results.

UGA.short: A national household survey published results in 2025, after final census results.
UGA.summary: UBOS states the National Population and Housing Census 2024 was enumerated door-to-door from 10 to 26 May 2024, counting 45,905,417 persons and 10,698,913 households. Its final report, Volume I, is dated December 2024. No change to the census results has been found in the last twelve months. UBOS's budget report for 2025/26 says it is finalising and disseminating a disability monograph from the census and producing thematic reports from the 2022 Demographic and Health Survey.

ZAF.short: A national household survey published results in 2026, after final census results.
ZAF.summary: Statistics South Africa states Census 2022 was enumerated with reference night 2 February 2022, and counted 62,027,503 people. It released the first phase of the results in October 2023 and has since published thematic reports. It has withheld some themes, such as income and labour. In the last twelve months, it released the Quarterly Labour Force Survey for the second quarter of 2026, with fieldwork from April to June 2026. The sample is about 30,000 dwellings, and the survey reports an unemployment rate of 33.6%.

ZMB.short: A national household survey published results in 2026, after final census results.
ZMB.summary: Zambia's 2022 Census of Population and Housing, its sixth national census, was enumerated from 18 August to 21 September 2022. The Population Summary Report Volume Two, dated June 2024, gives final figures with a total of 19,693,423. No change to the census results has been found in the last twelve months. In that time, ZamStats presented highlights of the 2025 National Survey on Access and Usage of ICTs, a household survey of 32,500 individuals targeted in 325 enumeration areas.

ZWE.short: The 2022 census was counted and its results published, and a household survey was published in 2026.
ZWE.summary: The Herald reports that Zimbabwe's Population and Housing Census was taken in April 2022. ZIMSTAT's 2025 environment statistics report cites the final census report for a count of 15,178,957 people. Of them, 61.4 percent live in rural areas. In the last twelve months, ZIMSTAT and POTRAZ released the 2025 ICT Access by Households and Use by Individuals Survey in July 2026, covering 9,245 households in all ten provinces.

AGO.short: Angola's central bank authorised payment service providers in 2026 and runs the Kwik instant-payment platform; no source found says Angola is live on PAPSS.
AGO.summary: In January 2026 the Banco Nacional de Angola issued Aviso 1/26, which lets only payment companies it has authorised act as non-bank acquirers. Expansão reports the BNA launched the Kwik instant-payment platform in June 2023. In the last twelve months, the BNA joined the kwanza to the SADC-RTGS from 27 July 2026, with five Angolan banks taking part. No source found since October 2023 says Angola is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Angolan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

BDI.short: Burundi's central bank licensed three e-money issuers by 2024 and launched BurundiPay in 2026; it is not yet shown live on PAPSS.
BDI.summary: The BRB launched BurundiPay, the national instant payment system, on 23 April 2026, and is its promoter. By 4 August 2026, 17 institutions were live on it. The BRB's 2024 report on payment systems names the e-money issuers it had licensed at end-September 2024: Saisai Fintech, Lumicash and Ellis Business Company. In the last twelve months, the BRB moved its Automated Transfer System to ISO 20022 in February 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Burundi is live on PAPSS, and joining does not count. Mature would need Burundian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

BEN.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
BEN.summary: BCEAO launched PI-SPI on 30 September 2025 as a 24/7 interoperable instant payment platform for the UEMOA. In the last twelve months, its communique reports 80 participants connected on 2 April 2026. A BCEAO notice of 2 October 2026 makes PI-SPI compulsory for interoperable e-money transfers, from 2 November 2026. Four payment institutions held a BCEAO licence in Benin at 31 August 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Benin is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Beninese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

BFA.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
BFA.summary: LeFaso.net reports that the BCEAO launched the PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform on 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, the BCEAO had 80 institutions connected by 24 June 2026. As of 24 February 2026 it had authorised nine institutions in Burkina Faso to offer PI-SPI instant payment services to the public, including Orange Money, Coris Bank International and Ecobank. No source found since October 2023 says Burkina Faso is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Burkinabe banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

BWA.short: The central bank licensed payment providers in 2026; no source found reports a national switch it oversees.
BWA.summary: The Bank of Botswana says the Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, have been in effect since 2 April 2026. In the last twelve months, no one may operate an electronic payment service without its licence. The penalty is a P1 million fine or five years in prison. The Bank said the National Payments Switch Act has been drafted, with no tabling date. No source found since October 2023 says the central bank runs or oversees a national switch. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

CAF.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2023; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
CAF.summary: In November 2023 AfricaNenda said BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent. The switch serves payment providers in the Central African Republic. In the last twelve months, PAPSS said BEAC joined PAPSS on 9 July 2026. In April 2026 the UMAC ministerial committee validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, and it was launched over GIMACPAY on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the country is live on PAPSS. Joining does not count. Mature would need banks or payment providers in the country to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

CIV.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
CIV.summary: The BCEAO launched its PI-SPI instant payment platform on 30 September 2025, with 80 institutions connected. In the last twelve months, by April 2026, it ran around the clock with 80 participants, nine of them e-money institutions. In October 2026 the BCEAO said Cote d'Ivoire's Treasury was already connected. Since 2 November 2026 interoperable e-money transfers must route through it. No source found since October 2023 says Cote d'Ivoire is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Ivorian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

CMR.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
CMR.summary: GIMACPAY has been in service since 2021, and BEAC publishes its figures. In the last twelve months, BEAC launched the interoperable CEMAC QR code on 29 July 2026 in Douala. It rests on Regulation 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/COREFI of 8 April 2026, and covers the six CEMAC countries, cleared through GIMAC. No source found since October 2023 says Cameroon is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Cameroonian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

COD.short: The central bank oversees a national payment switch in 2026 and joined PAPSS, but no source found reports payments through it.
COD.summary: The Banque Centrale du Congo's map of the national payment system lists, at end-2023, 15 banks and other credit institutions, 81 money-transfer firms and five other financial companies. Bankable reports that Switch Mosolo is the national payment switch developed under the Central Bank of Congo's oversight. In the last twelve months, an agreement signed on 15 April 2026 connected microfinance institutions and savings cooperatives to the national card switch. Le Point CD reports that the central bank joined PAPSS in September 2026. Banks and fintechs were invited to apply on 21 October 2026. Mature would need Congolese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

COG.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2023; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
COG.summary: AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, provides interoperable payment services to providers in the six CEMAC states, including the Republic of Congo. It says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent. In the last twelve months, the UMAC ministerial committee validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard in April 2026, and it was launched on 29 July 2026 over GIMACPAY. No source found since October 2023 says Congo is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Congolese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

COM.short: The Comoros central bank sets licensing for e-money issuers and launched Komor Switch in 2026; no source found says the Comoros is live on PAPSS.
COM.summary: The Banque Centrale des Comores' financial inclusion strategy cites its regulation no. 1 of 2017 on e-money institutions. That regulation sets the licensing terms for e-money issuers. The BCC operates, supervises and takes part in KomorPay, the interbank payment system, which has run since 23 April 2026. In the last twelve months, Al-Watwan reports the BCC launched Komor Switch. It links all banks and mobile money services. No source found since October 2023 says the Comoros takes part in PAPSS. Mature would need Comorian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

CPV.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2025; no source found reports a regional link.
CPV.summary: The Banco de Cabo Verde says it manages SICIL, the interbank clearing system for cheques, credit transfers and payment cards, and requires payment institutions and e-money institutions to be authorised by it. In 2024 it continued revising the legal framework for payment services and the issuance of electronic money. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Cape Verde takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Cape Verde live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

DJI.short: Djibouti's central bank licensed two e-money issuers and ran an automated clearing house in 2024; two Djiboutian banks were live on PAPSS in 2026.
DJI.summary: The Banque Centrale de Djibouti's 2024 annual report says no institution may offer financial services without its licence. It names two e-money issuers it oversees, D-Money and WAAFI. The same report says its automated clearing house has run since October 2022. AfricaNenda's SIIPS 2024 says Djibouti had integrated with PAPSS, and it was then unclear whether retail transactions were processed. In the last twelve months, PAPSS's June 2026 coverage sheet lists Djibouti as a country with live send-and-receive participants: East African Bank and Salaam African Bank. Its November 2026 sheet still lists Djibouti.

DZA.short: The central bank licensed payment providers in 2026; no source found reports a national switch it oversees.
DZA.summary: In August 2025 Launchbase Africa reported that Bank of Algeria Instruction 06-2025 requires payment service providers to join the national payment and clearing systems, which the Bank oversees. The report names no switch. In the last twelve months, a banking consultant said in March 2026 that the Bank had licensed no provider under its Regulation 25-02. On 23 September 2026 the Bank's Monetary and Banking Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services to set up as a payment service provider. No source found since October 2023 names a national switch or retail clearing system the Bank runs. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

EGY.short: The central bank ran the national instant payment network in 2026; no source found says whether Egyptian banks are live on a continental payment system.
EGY.summary: The CBE says its InstaPay instant payments network had over 16 million users and 1.1 billion transactions by June 2025. InstaPay runs through the bank's Instant Payment Network, the national real-time payment infrastructure. The Central Bank of Egypt agreed to join PAPSS in November 2024. In the last twelve months, six Egyptian banks applied to the CBE for final approvals to integrate with PAPSS, and in September 2026 they were still applying. No source found reports Egyptian payments running on PAPSS. Mature would need Egyptian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS; joining does not count.

ERI.short: The central bank licensed payment providers in 2025; no source found reports a national switch it oversees.
ERI.summary: In 2025 Himbol's guide said Himbol operates under the supervision and licensing of the Bank of Eritrea. Himbol runs the M-Nakfa mobile wallet and remittance payout. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the central bank runs or oversees a national switch. None says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

ETH.short: The central bank licenses payment providers and in 2025 mandated an instant payment system; Ethiopia joined PAPSS in 2026, with no live payments found.
ETH.summary: In May 2025 the National Bank of Ethiopia made interoperability among mobile wallets mandatory. The same directive requires financial institutions to take part in the Ethiopian Instant Payment System. On 12 May 2025 the Bank raised the minimum capital of payment instrument issuers from 50 million to 100 million birr. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Capital newspaper reported that the Bank licenses ETTA's ZooryaPay as a payment system operator. On 15 October 2026 the Bank and PAPSS announced that Ethiopia had joined the PAPSS network. No source found says Ethiopian banks or payment providers send and receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need them to do so.

GAB.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
GAB.summary: BEAC launched the interoperable CEMAC QR code on 29 July 2026 in Douala. It rests on Regulation 02/26/CEMAC/UMAC/COREFI of 8 April 2026. AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent, a switch that serves Gabon. The QR code is the one change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Gabon is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Gabonese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

GHA.short: The Bank of Ghana licensed payment providers, oversaw the national payment switch and linked mobile wallets to a regional payment system in 2026.
GHA.summary: The Bank of Ghana's head of fintech said in October 2026 that the Bank set up GhIPSS in 2007. GhIPSS is a publicly owned national payment infrastructure that connects banks, mobile money operators and other payment providers. In the last twelve months, the Governor launched SaoPay as a new Dedicated Electronic Money Issuer on 7 October 2026. Governor Asiama said the Bank has extended PAPSS to mobile wallets in the Ghana-Nigeria corridor. In November 2026 the Governor said the Bank is developing a legal and regulatory framework for fintech companies.

GIN.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
GIN.summary: In July 2026 the central bank and Guinéenne de Monétique had built NimbaPay, a national instant payment platform. The BCRG's supervision director general said the central bank is putting NimbaPay into operation. It links banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the bank was preparing a payment systems law and a payments strategy for 2027-2030, Agence Ecofin reports. No source found since October 2023 says Guinea takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Guinea live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

GMB.short: The Gambia's central bank authorises mobile money providers, led the BANTABA 2.0 switch in 2025, and seven Gambian banks were live on PAPSS in 2026.
GMB.summary: The Point says the central bank co-led the launch of BANTABA 2.0, the country's first real-time interoperable payment system, in December 2025. Gamswitch says the central bank gave regulatory leadership and oversight for the switch. The Digital Cooperation Organization's 2025 Gambia report says mobile money providers must be authorised by the central bank. In the last twelve months, the central bank launched a National Payment Systems Advisory Committee after BANTABA 2.0 went live. PAPSS's June 2026 coverage sheet lists the Gambia as a country with live send-and-receive participants, naming seven banks.

GNB.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
GNB.summary: The BCEAO runs PI-SPI, the instant payment platform for UEMOA members including Guinea-Bissau, launched on 30 September 2025. The BCEAO's list of payment institutions licensed under Instruction n°001-01-2024 shows one in Guinea-Bissau, INTOUCH Guinée-Bissau, licensed 25 June 2025. In the last twelve months, the BCEAO said Guinea-Bissau had 5 institutions authorised on PI-SPI at 31 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Guinea-Bissau is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Bissau-Guinean banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

GNQ.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2023; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
GNQ.summary: In November 2023 AfricaNenda said BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent. The switch serves payment providers in Equatorial Guinea. In the last twelve months, PAPSS said BEAC joined PAPSS on 9 July 2026. In April 2026 the UMAC ministerial committee validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, and it was launched over GIMACPAY on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the country is live on PAPSS. Joining does not count. Mature would need banks or payment providers in the country to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

KEN.short: The central bank licenses payment providers and regulates a domestic switch; PAPSS payments reach Kenya in 2026, but none is reported going out.
KEN.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya regulates Kenswitch, a domestic payment switch, its November 2026 release says. The CBK's directory of 6 November 2025 lists 41 authorised payment service providers. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the CBK and the National Treasury published a draft National Payment System Policy and Bill, 2026. In November 2026 the PAPSS chief executive said KCB Group and Equity Bank are connected to the network. No source found says Kenyan banks send payments out through PAPSS. Mature would need Kenyan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through it.

LBR.short: The central bank took part in a regional or continental payment system in 2025.
LBR.summary: The central bank launched Pay Na-Na, the country's first instant payment system, on 16 December 2025. It links the two mobile money operators. CBL Directive 002/2025 applies to all licensed Mobile Money Providers. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the Governor said banks and fintechs were still being brought onto Pay Na-Na. The central bank is the settlement agent for PAPSS, launched in Liberia on 27 March 2025. In November 2026 the Executive Governor said Liberian traders' payments to Nigeria and Ghana are settled through PAPSS.

LBY.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
LBY.summary: The central bank runs the LYPay and OnePay instant payment services, launched in 2024. On 31 July 2025 it said it was paying public salaries into commercial bank accounts over its own instant payment network. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, it told banks to switch on LYPay QR payments at point-of-sale devices by 8 March. It also joined PAPSS at the end of December 2025. No Libyan bank is reported live on PAPSS. Mature would need Libyan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS; joining does not count.

LSO.short: Lesotho's central bank licenses five mobile money issuers and leads the national switch, LeSwitch; no source found reports live payments through PAPSS.
LSO.summary: From 11 May 2025 the Central Bank of Lesotho and leading banks routed local card payments at shops through LeSwitch, the national switch. Standard Lesotho Bank says the central bank leads LeSwitch, whose fast-payments phase was launched on 20 March 2024. The Central Bank of Lesotho's list of licensed financial institutions names five mobile money issuers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Lesotho's banks send or receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need Lesotho's banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

MAR.short: Bank Al-Maghrib licensed new payment institutions in 2025 and oversees the SIMT retail clearing system; no source found says Morocco is live on PAPSS.
MAR.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib's 2025 supervision report lists the licences it granted that year. Three created new payment institutions. Bank Al-Maghrib oversees Morocco's payment systems, including the SIMT retail clearing system, under article 10 of law 76-03. Boursenews reported in May 2025 that Switch Al-Maghrib, the national switch, is under the Bank's direct and continuous oversight. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Morocco is live on PAPSS. Mature would need Moroccan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

MDG.short: The central bank licensed payment providers in 2026; no source found reports a national switch it oversees.
MDG.summary: In June 2026 2424.mg reported that the CSBF is attached to the Banky foiben'i Madagasikara. Under the e-money institutions law it can grant or withdraw licences, issue regulatory instructions and audit e-money institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the central bank runs or oversees a national switch. None says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the central bank to run or oversee a national payment switch or interoperability arrangement in service.

MLI.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
MLI.summary: The BCEAO runs PI-SPI, the instant payment platform for UEMOA members including Mali, launched on 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, Mali had 12 institutions authorised by the BCEAO to open PI-SPI to the public as of 2 April 2026. Bénin Web TV reports, from the BCEAO list, that Mali has two licensed payment institutions at 31 August 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Mali is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Malian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

MOZ.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
MOZ.summary: SIMOrede has operated the National Single Network (National Switch) since 2023, under the supervision and control of the Bank of Mozambique. In the last twelve months, the Bank launched the Metix instant payment system on 16 March 2026, run by SIMO. Its communiqué of 30 July 2026 reports over 11,000 transfers a day. PawaPay announced on 8 October 2026 that the Bank had licensed it as a payment service provider. Mozambique joined PAPSS in September 2026, but no bank is reported live on it. Mature would need Mozambican banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

MRT.short: Mauritania's central bank licensed Mattel Money as an e-money institution and oversaw GIMTEL's 2024 app interconnection; no source found says Mauritania is live on PAPSS.
MRT.summary: GIMTEL launched the interconnection of bank apps and e-wallets under the central bank's strategy in October 2024. The governor said oversight of payment systems had been activated. In the last twelve months, Agence Ecofin reports Mattel Money is licensed by the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie as an e-money institution. Mattel Money launched the Mechili payment service on 22 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Mauritania takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Mauritania live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

MUS.short: The Bank of Mauritius licenses payment service providers and runs the MauCAS switch in 2026; no source found says Mauritius is live on PAPSS.
MUS.summary: The Bank of Mauritius's July 2026 guideline says it issues payment service provider licences under the National Payment Systems Act, and payment aggregators must now hold one. A former governor said the bank put MauCAS, the Mauritius Central Automated Switch, in place in 2019. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, Governor Thakoor said the bank's infrastructure includes MauCAS. The same speech says the bank is settlement bank for COMESA's REPSS, a regional system that does not count. No source found since October 2023 says Mauritius is live on PAPSS. Mature would need Mauritian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

MWI.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2025; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
MWI.summary: In 2025 Malawi said the Reserve Bank supervises National Switch Limited, which connects all banks and mobile money operators for instant payments. The Reserve Bank and the Bank of Zambia supervise the COMESA Digital Retail Payments Platform, which links the two countries. In the last twelve months, on 30 September 2026, the Reserve Bank granted the local fintech PayChangu Limited payment service provider licence PSP-003/26. No source found since October 2023 says Malawi is live on PAPSS, and a regional system does not count. Mature would need Malawian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

NAM.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
NAM.summary: The Bank of Namibia said its instant payments solution became operational in June 2026. The first live transactions ran between its Currency Management and Banking Operations Department and Bank Windhoek, Nampost and Letshego Bank Namibia. In the last twelve months, the Bank's PSD-1 determination took effect on 6 January 2026. It sets the licensing of payment service providers under section 45 of the Payment System Management Act 2023. No source found since October 2023 says Namibian banks or providers send and receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need them to do so.

NER.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
NER.summary: BCEAO runs PI-SPI for UEMOA members including Niger. It was launched on 30 September 2025 and had 175 connected participants a year later. In the last twelve months, the BCEAO's list updated to 30 September 2026 authorises 13 participants in Niger to open PI-SPI services to the public. Bénin Web TV reports that Niger had one licensed payment institution at 31 August 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Niger is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Nigerien banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

NGA.short: Nigeria's central bank licenses payment providers, part-owns the NIBSS switch and backed its National Payment Stack in 2026; Nigerian banks are live on PAPSS.
NGA.summary: Premium Times reports NIBSS is owned by the CBN and all licensed deposit banks. NIBSS clears and settles instant interbank transfers. In January 2026 the CBN upgraded the licences of Moniepoint, OPay, Kuda, PalmPay and Paga to national. In the last twelve months, the CBN's payments supervision director urged institutions to join NIBSS's new National Payment Stack, which had carried 26.55 million transactions by August 2026. In November 2026 PAPSS's deputy chief executive said the CBN waives extra documents for PAPSS payments below a threshold. On 10 November 2026 the Senate passed a bill letting the CBN designate, register and supervise fintechs as systemically important.

RWA.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
RWA.summary: eKash was launched nationally on 14 July 2026. The National Bank of Rwanda says it monitors the system and works with providers to fix disruptions. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the National Bank said its passporting agreement with the Central Bank of Kenya covers payment service providers licensed by their home central bank. No source found since October 2023 says Rwandan banks or providers send and receive payments through PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Rwandan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

SDN.short: The central bank licensed payment providers in 2026 and supervised the national switch linking all banks; no source found reports live payments through PAPSS.
SDN.summary: In October 2026 the head of EBS said it runs Sudan's national payments infrastructure under the central bank's supervision. That includes the national switch, which connects all Sudanese banks. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 a central bank director said the national switch had been partly reinstated. On 5 November 2026 the governor said the clearinghouse would run at full capacity from the following Sunday. No source found since October 2023 says Sudan's banks send or receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need Sudanese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

SEN.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
SEN.summary: The BCEAO launched PI-SPI, its interoperable instant payment platform, on 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, it counted 80 connected participants by April 2026, nine of them e-money institutions. At 30 September 2026 PI-SPI had 175 authorised participants across the WAEMU, 43 of them in Senegal. Since 2 November 2026 bank-wallet transfers in Senegal must go through it. No source found since October 2023 says Senegal is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Senegalese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's central bank licensed eight fintechs by 2025, runs the national switch, and eight Sierra Leonean banks were live on PAPSS in 2025.
SLE.summary: The Bank of Sierra Leone launched a national payment switch in April 2023. It added an instant payment switch on 13 February 2025, linking seven banks and two mobile money operators. A Bank of Sierra Leone supervisor's 2025 deck says eight fintechs hold a full BSL licence. PAPSS lists eight Sierra Leonean banks as live in its May 2025 update. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the head of the Bank's National Switch Department said it runs the Salon Payment Switch, which now includes every commercial bank.

SOM.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
SOM.summary: The Governor wrote in July 2026 that SIPS, launched in January 2025, is run by the Somalia Payment Switch. It is a partnership of the central bank and 13 commercial banks. The House of the People passed the National Payment System Bill 154-2, and it goes to the Senate. In the last twelve months, the Central Bank of Somalia joined PAPSS in March 2026. No Somali bank is reported live on it. Joining does not count. Mature would need Somali banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

SSD.short: The central bank licenses payment providers and launched an interbank clearing and settlement system in November 2026; no PAPSS participation has been found.
SSD.summary: On 24 November 2026 the Bank of South Sudan and the Ministry of Finance and Planning launched the South Sudan Interbank Payment and Settlement System. Its real-time gross settlement system takes high-value payments and its automated clearing house takes low-value and bulk payments. In September 2025 the Bank put mobile money operators under the licensing-linked requirements of banks. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, it required non-bank electronic money issuers to obtain its approval under the amended Electronic Money Regulation. No source found since October 2023 says the country takes part in PAPSS. Mature would need South Sudanese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

STP.short: The central bank licenses payment providers and in 2026 was expanding its domestic payment network; no source found says the country is live on PAPSS.
STP.summary: In a communiqué of 20 January 2025 the Banco Central de São Tomé e Príncipe eased some documentation requirements for the licences of payment institutions. In the last twelve months, in 2026, the bank's director of financial inclusion told the Alliance for Financial Inclusion that the bank is expanding Dobra24, the country's domestic interoperable retail payment network. The bank is also setting interoperability requirements for all market players. No source found gives Dobra24's volumes or participants. None says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need the country live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

SWZ.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; no source found reports a regional link.
SWZ.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini says its Eswatini Payment Switch is fully active. As of September 2026 it connects banks and mobile money providers in real time, at all hours. The bank says it oversees national payment systems and lists five licensed payment service providers. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Senate considered draft National Payment System Regulations, 2026. They would let the central bank designate important payment systems and examine providers. No source found since October 2023 says Eswatini takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Eswatini live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

SYC.short: The central bank oversees interoperable interbank payment systems by 2025; no source found says whether the country is live on PAPSS.
SYC.summary: Governor Caroline Abel said in July 2025 that banks interoperate fully on the country's most used payment systems. These are the Seychelles Electronic Funds Transfer and electronic cheque clearing, which run under the Act that governs the oversight of national payment systems. In November 2025 the Central Bank of Seychelles gave Fusepay final approval as a licensed payment service provider. No change to the central bank's role has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says Seychelles takes part in PAPSS. Mature would need Seychelles banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

TCD.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2023; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
TCD.summary: Chad's payment-institution licences are granted by Cobac under the CEMAC regulation of 21 December 2018. AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY and is its overseer and settlement agent, a switch that serves Chad. In the last twelve months, Moov Money Tchad was licensed in 2026. In April 2026 the UMAC ministerial committee validated GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, and it was launched over GIMACPAY on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Chad is live on PAPSS. A regional system does not count. Mature would need Chadian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

TGO.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2026; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
TGO.summary: The BCEAO launched the PI-SPI instant payment platform on 30 September 2025 and sets institutions' deadlines to connect. In the last twelve months, TechCabal reports the BCEAO granted Togolese fintech Semoa its Level 3 payment institution accreditation on 29 January 2026. By 24 June 2026, 80 institutions were connected across the region. By the end of October 2026, 17 Togolese providers were connected and it had processed nearly CFAF 15 billion in Togo. No source found since October 2023 says Togo is live on PAPSS, and PI-SPI is a regional system that does not count. Mature would need Togolese banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

TUN.short: The central bank oversaw the national interbank clearing system in 2026; no source found says whether Tunisian payments run on a continental payment system.
TUN.summary: The BCT states it manages and supervises the SGMT RTGS, in service since November 2006. It also performs surveillance of the SIBTEL clearing system. In the last twelve months, African Manager reports that the BCT published Circular 2026-10 on 2026-09-25 governing payment institutions, which repeals Circular 2018-16. La Presse says the BCT's licensing commission granted OFT Tunisie definitive authorisation as a resident payment institution in March 2026. The BCT has belonged to PAPSS since 6 February 2024. No source found reports Tunisian payments running on PAPSS. Mature would need Tunisian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through it.

TZA.short: The central bank ran or oversaw a national payment switch in 2025; no source found reports a regional link.
TZA.summary: The Bank of Tanzania launched the Tanzania Instant Payment System (TIPS) in 2019, an interoperable platform across banks and mobile money providers. Over 45 institutions take part. In 2024 and 2025 the Bank capped the maximum cost of a single transaction at 2,000/-. In the last twelve months, the finance minister told the National Assembly that 113 service providers were licensed to operate payment system services as of March 2026. No source found since October 2023 says Tanzania takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Mature would need Tanzania live on PAPSS, with its banks or payment providers sending and receiving payments through it.

UGA.short: The Bank of Uganda licensed payment providers in 2025 and runs the RTGS and clearing house; no source found says Uganda is live on PAPSS.
UGA.summary: The Bank of Uganda runs the Real Time Gross Settlement and Automated Clearing House services. In the last twelve months, on 3 November 2026, it said both would close from 5 to 9 November for an upgrade. It called them part of Uganda's national payments infrastructure. Daily Monitor reports the bank approved at least 17 payment licences in one year, covering e-money issuers, payment service providers and aggregators. No source found since October 2023 says Ugandan banks send and receive payments through PAPSS. Mature would need Ugandan banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS; the regional East African Payment System does not count.

ZAF.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2025; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
ZAF.summary: In November 2025 the Reserve Bank bought a 50% stake in BankservAfrica, the national automated clearing house, and renamed it PayInc. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, it published a draft framework for authorising non-bank payment and e-money providers. Its recognition of the Payments Association of South Africa lapsed on 2 September 2026, and licensing, authorisation and registration of payment institutions moved to the Reserve Bank. On 20 October 2026 the governor said that qualifying regional payments run on SADC-RTGS. No source found since October 2023 says South Africa is live on PAPSS. Mature would need its banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

ZMB.short: The central bank oversaw a national payment switch in 2024; live participation in PAPSS is not on record.
ZMB.summary: In 2024 the Bank of Zambia issued fourteen designation certificates to payment service providers, and revoked four designations that year. The Bank says it oversees the national payment systems, including the National Financial Switch. In 2024 the switch processed 140,496,750 transactions worth K131.9 billion, with 34 participants live. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Zambia is live on PAPSS. Its banks used the regional SADC-RTGS in 2024, which does not count. Mature would need Zambian banks or payment providers to send and receive payments through PAPSS.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's Reserve Bank licenses payment providers and regulates the ZIPIT switch (2024); Zimbabwe was processing payments through PAPSS in 2026.
ZWE.summary: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's 2024 annual report says it licenses, oversees and supervises payment system providers. AfricaNenda's 2024 case study says ZIPIT, Zimswitch's instant payment system, is licensed by the Reserve Bank. In the last twelve months, Afreximbank said Zimbabwe is processing $5.8 million a month through PAPSS, reported in October 2026. The Financial Gazette reported on 9 October 2026 that CBZ Bank had gone live on PAPSS.

AGO.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
AGO.summary: In May 2026 civil registration posts in Luanda and most of the country had been without their system for months. The Justice Ministry blamed telecom breakdowns. In the last twelve months, Angola told a registrars' meeting in July 2026 that it is merging the civil register and the identity card system, on the existing civil registry system. The 2023-2024 survey put registration of children under five at 38%, a figure not tied to a digital system. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

BDI.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
BDI.summary: In August 2026 ID Tech reported that 13 municipalities in Burundi have biometric civil registration systems. The Ministry of the Interior has presented a digital platform for managing civil registration, with its infrastructure nearly complete and a decree governing its use awaited. In the last twelve months, the August 2026 report of 13 communes is the widest coverage found. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

BEN.short: Births and deaths are registered digitally in the national civil status file, said in 2026; no source found reports the share of births registered.
BEN.summary: ANIP says Law 2020-34 of January 2021 abolished paper civil registers, and every birth is now registered in the national register of persons. Since May 2026 secure birth certificates have been issued from its data. In the last twelve months, ANIP's 2026 slides say a death declared by a health worker or local chief is registered automatically. A single desk was piloted from August 2025 in ten public health facilities, and ANIP says national scale-up is still to come. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

BFA.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
BFA.summary: In September 2026 delegated officers and transcribing agents in Pouni were trained on the VENEEM platform, which takes real-time entry of births, marriages and deaths. In the last twelve months, the Minister of Territorial Administration said 30 communes now hold fully digitised civil-status registers, as reported by the Primature. AMADE Mondiale lists deployment of a digital birth registration platform among completed activities of its 2025-2028 project in Kaya, Tenkodogo and Koupela. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

BWA.short: Registration was partly automated in 2024 and universal by UNICEF's count; national digital birth registration is not on record.
BWA.summary: Statistics Botswana's 2024 report says the Births and Deaths Registration System dates from 2003 and is only partly automated. It runs through 35 district offices and 17 on-site registration points, and part of the work is still done by hand. UNICEF said in December 2024 that Botswana has universal birth registration, a figure not tied to the digital system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

CAF.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
CAF.summary: In February 2026 the EU-backed digitisation project run by CIVIPOL was extending its pilot in Bangui and towns on the main corridor to new communes. In the last twelve months, the national civil register held more than 225,000 birth records in July 2026, and agents trained that month started digitising old registers. On 17 November 2026 the steering committee named the civil-status software MbetiNet. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

CIV.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2025; 90% birth registration is not on record.
CIV.summary: In February 2026 ONECI said Cityweb was in all 692 civil registration centres. In the last twelve months, ONECI issued its first CityWeb act from Madrid on 11 May 2026, and in October 2026 it said CityWeb had been deployed in all the country's centres. Its director general noted connectivity problems in some. AIP reports that Citiweb registers births, marriages and deaths. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

CMR.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
CMR.summary: In September 2026 the registration bureau BUNEC said 60 of 432 civil-registration centres were digitised. That is 13.9%, up from 42 in April 2022. In the last twelve months, the statistics institute said in April 2026 that a December 2024 law creates a national civil-status file, and a test linking the register with health and statistics systems is under way. In March 2026 NRC was piloting a digital office in Logone-Birni. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

COD.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2025; national digital birth registration is not on record.
COD.summary: In August 2025 four UN agencies were piloting DHIS2 in Masina commune, Kinshasa, to record births, marriages and deaths. A national contract with Afritech and Idemia covered a civil registration system. It was signed in December 2023 and cancelled in August 2024, and nothing has replaced it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

COG.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
COG.summary: In September 2026 ACSI, which built the SIFEC civil-status software, handed its technical documents to the territorial administration directorate. Data centralisation, user training and deployment were still to come. In the last twelve months, the project head told the National Assembly's Ecofin committee in August 2026 that SIFEC computerises the national civil register. On 17 November 2026 ACSI's director general told the committee SIFEC was ready. He named no offices using it. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

COM.short: A 2026 source says civil registration is on paper with no digital register.
COM.summary: In October 2025 La Gazette des Comores reported the AMECC project coordinator saying civil registration is still largely manual, and a digitisation study was launched on 10 October 2025. In the last twelve months, Comores Droit said in March 2026 that births, marriages and deaths have been recorded in paper registers for decades. In August 2026 La Gazette des Comores reported that the system still largely depends on old paper registers. No source found since October 2023 names a digital civil register. Preparing would need a digital civil registration system procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde registers births and deaths in a computerised national register, and birth registration reached 99% in 2026.
CPV.summary: The statistics institute says the registry directorate's services in Cabo Verde have been computerised with NOSi since 2004. Its count of 6,760 births registered in 2023 comes from that registration database, and deaths are drawn from the same database. In the last twelve months, Biometric Update reported in May 2026 that birth registration reached 99 per cent, up from about 91 per cent before the reforms. IMIJ's ID4Africa 2026 deck gives about 99 to 100 per cent, as the presenter's approximation. No change to the register itself has been found in that time.

DJI.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
