DJI.summary: Ville de Djibouti says civil-status events in Djibouti city have been recorded on the SIGEC software since 2011, with the database fed continuously. A diagnostic of it began on 28 April 2024. In the last twelve months, the DGPF director general said in July 2026 that birth and marriage certificates are progressively being integrated into a digital database, as part of an archive digitisation programme. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

DZA.short: Births were registered digitally across the country in 2025; no source found reports digital death registration.
DZA.summary: In 2010 the Interior Ministry launched a computerised civil-status system with a central database, the RNEC. Birth registers were archived digitally, and more than 100 million marriage, death and birth acts have been digitised, per La Sentinelle. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the Interior Minister said administrations can consult civil status data directly in the national automated register. No source found since October 2023 says deaths are registered in the digital system. Operating would need deaths registered in the digital system, in service.

EGY.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2026; 90% birth registration is not on record.
EGY.summary: In 2024 Egypt told the UN that live birth registration was an estimated 96.6 per cent complete in 2022, a figure too old to count. In the last twelve months, Egypt's own country presentation of July 2026 states full nationwide automation of civil registration. It covers 4,571 health offices across 27 governorates, feeding a central births and deaths database in service. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

ERI.short: Nothing found names digital civil registration or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says how births and deaths are registered.

ETH.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
ETH.summary: A July 2026 presentation describes Ethiopia's national eCRVS as a phased rollout, with a pilot in Addis Ababa, then Amharic-speaking regions, then the rest. In the last twelve months, Addis Ababa launched a digital civil registration system in 50 of its woredas in December 2025, replacing 14 years of manual work. A government statement the same month still called the Addis system a pilot. In March 2025 the government put birth registration at 37% complete. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

GAB.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2024; national digital birth registration is not on record.
GAB.summary: The Libreville university hospital launched doctoViene, an online birth declaration platform, in June 2024. Birth certificates are stored in an electronic database. In the last twelve months, the Digital Gabon financing agreement, amended from 2 September 2026, funds a fully digital civil registry and the digitising of paper records. Nothing found says births are registered digitally beyond that hospital platform, or that deaths are registered digitally. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

GHA.short: Births have been registered in a central digital database across Ghana's districts since 2024; no source found says whether deaths are.
GHA.summary: At a March 2024 launch the Vice President said Ghana's digital platform allowed real-time registration of births in all regions. In June 2025 the registry's reform head described a central digital database deployed in 261 districts. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 officers in the Eastern Region were still taking digital registration into communities. No source found since October 2023 says deaths are registered in the digital system. Operating would need deaths registered in the digital system, in service.

GIN.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 28 communes in 2025; national digital birth registration is not on record.
GIN.summary: On 24 July 2026 ONECI and NG Tech Innovation signed an MoU on digital identification and civil status. In the last twelve months, on 28 October 2026 the ministry launched RENEC, the national civil register project, whose first centres open in 2026 and which runs to 2028. The minister told the CNT that digital solutions reached 28 communes in 2025. In October 2025 officers from Conakry's 13 communes were shown the first functions of the electronic national register. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

GMB.short: Births were registered digitally across the country in 2025; no source found reports digital death registration.
GMB.summary: The Registrar General CRVS says an eCRVS system was deployed in Gambia in August 2022. The Registrar General's slides report 1,238,662 births in the eCRVS from August 2022 to March 2025, shown for every local government area. In the last twelve months, the count reached over 1.4 million people registered and issued a birth certificate as of June 2026. No source found since October 2023 says deaths are registered in the digital system. Operating would need deaths registered in the digital system, in service.

GNB.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
GNB.summary: UNICEF says birth registration is done digitally on a tablet platform in hospitals and health centres in Bissau, Tombali and Quinara. Over 20,000 children aged 0 to 7 were registered from October 2024 to June 2025. In the last twelve months, UNDP said in April 2026 that the Santa Luzia Civil Registry Office in Bissau is the first in the country to operate entirely digitally on SIREC, with over 2.4 million records digitised. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

GNQ.short: Nothing found since 2023 names digital civil registration, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether births are registered digitally in Equatorial Guinea. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says civil registration is on paper, or that a digital system has been procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices. Preparing would need a digital civil registration system procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices.

KEN.short: A digital birth e-service recorded nearly 300,000 births by October 2026 while expanding; national digital birth registration is not on record.
KEN.summary: Identity Week reported that Kenya's digital birth e-service had recorded nearly 300,000 births by October 2026, over 270,000 of them in the two months to September. In the last twelve months, the Immigration Principal Secretary said in October 2026 that e-notification would reach all Social Health Authority hospitals by December. In November 2026 he told MPs it had been piloted in Nairobi and Bomet. A nationwide rollout is to follow. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

LBR.short: Births are registered digitally across all 15 counties, said in 2024; no source found says whether deaths are registered digitally.
LBR.summary: In August 2024 UNICEF said Liberia's birth registration reaches all 15 counties and 98% of health districts, using tablets, online registration and digital certificates. In the last twelve months, the government signed a concession with OeSD International in April 2026 for a digital civil registry, and in October 2026 it was still before the legislature. The proposed concession would record deaths as well as births, but it is not ratified. No source found since October 2023 says deaths are registered in the digital system. Operating would need deaths registered in the digital system, in service.

LBY.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
LBY.summary: In the last twelve months, LANA reported a ministerial meeting on 9 July 2026 on finishing Project Intilaqa and developing the civil registry system. The meeting reviewed completion phases and obstacles, including data cleaning and electronic linkage with other bodies. The Civil Registry Authority says 257 offices have completed matching and scanning under the project, which matches electronic civil registry data with paper records. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

LSO.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
LSO.summary: In August 2026 UNICEF said 30 registration stations in Lesotho run on an SMS-based platform, in health facilities in Maseru, Berea and Leribe. In the last twelve months, the August 2026 report of three districts is the widest coverage found. A tablet system in Ha-Tankele feeds the social assistance database. The civil registry plans to take digital birth registration nationwide in 2026-2027. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

MAR.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2024; 90% birth registration is not on record.
MAR.summary: In October 2024 the Interior Ministry said over 1,300,000 acts had been declared or issued through the SGEC, which handles death declarations as well as births, marriages and divorces. The Ministry says a new information system for modernising civil status is being installed. Interior Minister Laftit ordered the walis of ten regions to speed the digitisation of paper civil-status records, and about 20 million records had been digitised in two regions. The source gives no date for the order. No change has been found in the last twelve months that is dated. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

MDG.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
MDG.summary: In May 2026 Intelligent CIO reported nearly 10 million civil records digitised, covering 1,695 communes in 11 regions. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the second phase of the Izaho Tokana 2.0 drive was under way, using biometrics. In 2023 the World Bank reported a digital birth registration pilot in Antananarivo and Toamasina, with over 3,000 newborns registered. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

MLI.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2024; national digital birth registration is not on record.
MLI.summary: In December 2024 UNICEF's Mali representative said a project for a platform digitising births, deaths and marriages had been approved, and the National Directorate of Civil Status has identified ten pilot areas. In the last twelve months, the directorate, DNEC, said in July 2026 that the community birth declaration chain is still on paper. It lists complete digitalisation of the system among its persisting priorities. In December 2024 UNICEF said 87% of children under one were registered. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

MOZ.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
MOZ.summary: UNICEF's 2024 brief says all 165 registry offices in Mozambique are digitised, and 152 of 300 eligible health facilities are linked. In July 2024 hospital births in some Inhambane districts were linked to e-SIRCEV. In the last twelve months, by March 2026 the database held 4.57 million people, against a target of 13 million. The registry's portal gives coverage of all registration centres as a proposal, which differs from the 2024 brief. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

MRT.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
MRT.summary: In February 2025 Law 2025-011 provided that digital civil-status acts can be issued through the adopted information systems, signed electronically. In March 2025 a Justice Ministry official said the national population register agency has developed a modern biometric civil-status system. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the interior minister listed modernising the civil-status system and digitising its services among the reforms. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

MUS.short: Births and deaths were registered in a computerised system in 2026; the share of births it holds has not been found.
MUS.summary: In August 2026 Statistics Mauritius said 6,386 live births were registered in January to June 2026, extracted from the computerised system at the Civil Status Division. The same issue reports 6,333 deaths registered in the period, compiled from that system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives the share of births registered in the digital system. The World Bank's 2024 SPI round listed Mauritius as meeting SDG 17.19.2, a national rate not tied to a digital system. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

MWI.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2025; 90% birth registration is not on record.
MWI.summary: In 2024 EGPAF said Malawi's central civil registration system operated in all 28 district registration offices and in district and central hospitals. NRB Secretary Mphatso Sambo said electronic birth and death registration systems were integrated with the national ID system by February 2025. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the minister said 180 health facilities had been digitalised. A new app, Nzika, linking registration to the national ID, was piloted in 87 places. The bureau said 67% of births were registered in 2023. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

NAM.short: Births and deaths were notified electronically in 2026; no source found reports the share of births registered digitally.
NAM.summary: Home Affairs Minister Iipumbu said the e-death notification, introduced in 2018, now operates in 153 state and private facilities. The e-birth notification system, introduced in 2017, has been implemented nationwide. In the last twelve months, a speaker at the Africa CDC learning visit in March 2026 said Namibia records birth registration coverage of close to 99%. That national rate may include paper registration. The ministry says 126 hospitals have electronic birth notification. No source found reports the share of births registered in the digital system. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

NER.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
NER.summary: Niger's director general of territorial administration set out the reform workstreams on 3 September 2026. They include progressive computerisation of communes and a sovereign platform for a National Civil Status Register, with a first registration phase due soon in Niamey. In the last twelve months, UNICEF's Tahoua office chief said UNICEF contributed to computerising 68% of communes nationwide. The Diffa regional civil-status directorate reports that four communes in the region have been computerised. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

NGA.short: Births and deaths moved onto one digital register in every state in July 2026; no source found reports the share of births it records.
NGA.summary: The population commission launched VitalReg, a digital platform, in November 2023. In June 2026 UNICEF said it ran in 14 states and the capital. In the last twelve months, the commission's chairman said digital registration of births and deaths began in all 36 states and the capital on 1 July 2026, and paper forms are no longer used. In August 2026 Nigeria 24 reported registration through a self-service portal or 4,011 commission centres, in all 774 local government areas. No source found gives the share of births registered on VitalReg since it went national. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

RWA.short: 90% or more of births were registered in 2025.
RWA.summary: The statistics institute counts 356,838 births registered in Rwanda's national digital system in 2025, 92.9% of estimated live births, up from 90.3% in 2024. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the local government ministry said all nine modules of the system were digitised. In June 2026 it launched a new centralised system and was training 2,148 cell officials to use it. The same report says 39,355 deaths occurred and were registered in 2025. In September 2026 the identity agency put birth registration at about 96%.

SDN.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
SDN.summary: In August 2024 a police spokesman said Sudan's registry system for births and deaths had been recovered and was running, with data restored up to 13 April 2023. In the last twelve months, on 17 May 2026 the Al-Hosh office in South Gezira issued its first electronic birth certificate since the suspension. In May 2026 a hospital system with a civil registration module started in two facilities, in Khartoum and Gedaref. On 12 November 2026 the civil registry said its database was fully restored after war damage, and it is widening electronic registration. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

SEN.short: Digital civil registration reached about three in four centres in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
SEN.summary: In July 2025 RTS reported that Senegal's national civil register was operational, with 20 million civil-status acts digitised. In the last twelve months, ANEC's director general said in January 2026 that the register gives real-time statistics only in connected communes. In August 2026 ANEC put its registration software in 74% of centres. In September 2026 it said its modernisation covers 77% of the 629 civil registration centres, in six regions. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

SLE.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2025; national digital birth registration is not on record.
SLE.summary: In March 2025 an official said fully electronic birth registration in Sierra Leone began in 2022. In 2025 the registration authority said over 80% of its registration and ID services are digitised. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the authority said a new integrated eCRVS platform had been developed with EU support. In October 2026 UNICEF described a birth in Bombali registered on a portable device. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

SOM.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
SOM.summary: Ecofin Agency reports the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation piloted a Unified Digital Civil Registration Service in 19 districts on 10 August 2025. National rollout is planned in phases. In the last twelve months, OpenCRVS said in January 2026 that its system had completed 28,391 birth registrations in 30 districts. UNICEF Somalia says it was piloted in 19 districts in 2023 and scaled to 48 in 2025. Not all regions have it. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

SSD.short: About a third of births were registered in 2010; no source found says whether registration is digital, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether births are registered digitally in South Sudan. The latest rate found is 35.4% of births registered, for 2010. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says civil registration is on paper with no digital register. Preparing would need a digital civil registration system procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices.

STP.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2026; 90% birth registration is not on record.
STP.summary: A new system for civil registry and notary services was launched in São Tomé and Príncipe in March 2025. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 an electoral official said birth and death records are fully computerised. In March 2026 the civil registry's chief said births are entered directly from maternity wards. Paper is no longer used there. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's 2023 index lists the country among ten in Africa registering at least 90% of births. It does not say the register is digital. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

SWZ.short: 61% of births were registered in 2025; no source found says whether registration is digital, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether births are registered digitally in Eswatini. The latest rate found is 61% of births registered, for 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says civil registration is on paper with no digital register. Preparing would need a digital civil registration system procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices.

SYC.short: Nothing found since 2023 names digital civil registration, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether births are registered digitally in Seychelles. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says civil registration is on paper with no digital register, or that a digital system has been procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices. Preparing would need a digital civil registration system procured, piloted or rolled out to some offices.

TCD.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
TCD.summary: In December 2023 the TASDJIL system had desks in more than 50 maternity units in Chad, and the aim is to cover every health facility. In July 2025 a desk at Mongo hospital served 18 health centres and logged 10 to 15 births a day. In the last twelve months, an OIF-backed project to June 2026 has been strengthening TASDJIL in N'Djamena, Batha and Hadjer Lamis. In August 2026 a writer said these desks were still to be scaled up. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

TGO.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
TGO.summary: The territorial administration ministry delivered computers and printers on 8 April 2026 to five pilot communes, ahead of national extension. In the last twelve months, the MESPTN, with KfW financing, tendered help in July 2026 for a pilot of the PDiMa project. It would digitalise civil registration in sixteen communes before national roll-out. In November 2026 the health ministry described its e-Vital pilot, begun in August 2026 in four communes. Health facilities there enter births and deaths. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

TUN.short: Births were registered digitally across the country in 2026; no source found reports digital death registration.
TUN.summary: Tunisia has had a centralised national civil status management system since 2004, shown as the information system Madania. In the last twelve months, the May 2026 playbook names Madania as the national civil status system feeding the citizen identifier register. The citizen portal issues the birth act for the account owner and for children. The cabinet council of 15 August 2026 listed 114 projects under way. They include electronic exchange of civil-status annotations between consulates and municipalities. No source found since October 2023 says deaths are registered in the digital system. Operating would need deaths registered in the digital system, in service.

TZA.short: Births and deaths were registered digitally in 2026; 90% birth registration is not on record.
TZA.summary: Since December 2025 the registration agency RITA has issued birth certificates within 48 working hours. RITA says eRITA is the only system it uses, across all 26 mainland regions. In the last twelve months, the minister said in August 2026 that coverage rose from 55% in 2020 to 68% in 2025, which is not tied to the digital system. Zanzibar's eCRVS and a mobile app carry registration in all 11 of its districts. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at 90% or more. Mature would need a source from the past three years that puts the share of births registered in the digital system at 90% or more.

UGA.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
UGA.summary: In July 2026 NIRA said it had integrated a birth and death registration module into the NSIS national ID system, built on open-source OpenCRVS. It issues a NIN automatically on birth notification. In the last twelve months, NIRA lists deploying crvs.nsis.nira.go.ug for birth registration as a next step. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

ZAF.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2025; national digital birth registration is not on record.
ZAF.summary: In November 2023 the Minister of Home Affairs said the department had rolled out online birth registration in 161 health facilities, covering about 68.35% of births delivered. In August 2024 the minister said a rollout strategy connects health facilities to Home Affairs systems to automate birth registration, staggered over five years to 2024/25. In July 2025 Deputy Minister Nzuza said Home Affairs has invested in building an e-birth registration platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

ZMB.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2025; national digital birth registration is not on record.
ZMB.summary: In October 2023 Zambia's civil registration system INRIS ran in 79 districts, covering all city and municipal councils, with some district councils pending. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the Smart Zambia Institute sought a system integrator for the civil registration core modules, financed by the World Bank. In March 2026 ID Tech reported the work covers deployment, integration and enrolment kits. In September 2026 an INRIS official said the system covers death certificates as well as births. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

ZWE.short: Digital civil registration was under way in 2026; national digital birth registration is not on record.
ZWE.summary: In November 2023 the Registrar-General said Zimbabwe's register was being linked to hospitals. In the last twelve months, the Deputy Registrar General said in July 2026 that all 10 provinces and 63 districts were computerised, and only about 20 of 209 sub-offices were. In June 2026 the Hauna sub-office in Honde Valley was issuing computerised birth certificates. In February 2026 the home affairs minister called the population registry system an integrated digital platform that updates birth and death records in real time. No source found since October 2023 says births are registered digitally across the country. Establishing would need births registered in a digital system in service nationally.

AGO.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
AGO.summary: On 15 May 2026 Angola's Institute of Administrative Modernisation (IMA) issued terms of reference to procure an e-learning platform for the civil-service school ENAPP. In the last twelve months, a presidential despacho of October 2026 authorised USD 20 million for a PADA digital-skills programme. It is for working people and public servants. Another ordered a public tender for training centres to raise public servants' digital skills at three levels. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service or gives a number trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

BDI.short: A programme to train 5,000 civil servants in basic digital skills was announced in 2026; no source found says whether it has begun.
BDI.summary: In September 2026 the PAFEN coordinator said in a LinkedIn post that PAFEN will soon launch a basic digital-skills programme. It aims to train 5,000 civil servants in under twelve months. In the last twelve months, that announcement is the only development found for Burundi. No source found says the programme has begun, or that it has trained a stated number of public servants. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

BEN.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
BEN.summary: La Marina BJ reports that the State trained 1,500 public administration agents for ICDL certification in 2022, and that ASIN was to oversee a second wave of 351 agents in 2024. In the last twelve months, ASIN and the Police républicaine's information systems directorate ran a training campaign from 26 June to 8 July 2026. It reached 300 police civil servants in six localities. They learned to protect sensitive state information and to use national e-signature, encryption and secure-messaging tools. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

BFA.short: Tax agents began digital-tools courses in November 2026; a standing programme with a number trained is not on record.
BFA.summary: On 4 November 2026 a public-finance training project, DISMEFIP, began courses for more than 400 tax agents. They learn three of the tax directorate's digital platforms, in four cities. The project runs from 2026 to 2028, paid for equally by Swiss cooperation and the government. In the last twelve months, these courses are the training found for one directorate. The World Bank's PACTDIGITAL project includes public-administration skills, as reported in March 2024. No source found says a standing programme has trained a stated number of civil servants. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

BWA.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
BWA.summary: On 6 October 2026 Statistics Botswana and the Botswana Public Service College agreed to design a statistical and data-literacy course for public servants. In the last twelve months, that agreement is the training found; it is meant for staff across the National Statistical System. Vice President Ndaba Gaolathe said AI training for the civil service was being planned. After a 2023 review of the 1Gov portal, training sessions for civil servants were put in motion, ADM Interactive says. It gives no number trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

CAF.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
CAF.summary: The World Bank counts 367 civil servants and beneficiaries trained, against a target of 2,000 by December 2026, after training sessions held in 2024 under its digital government component. In the last twelve months, on 9 October 2026, the digital economy ministry signed a renewable five-year agreement with HSE University, Moscow. It aims to strengthen civil servants' digital governance skills. A Ministry of Public Service official says computer training of civil servants has started at the Alliance Francaise, beginning with the ministry. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

CIV.short: A digital-skills programme trained civil servants in 2026; reach across government is not on record.
CIV.summary: SNDI's training centre, opened in 2012, had trained more than 28,500 civil servants and state agents by August 2024. In the last twelve months, the total passed 37,500 by July 2026, after a 40-day course for 192 agents in the Hambol region. In February 2026 the public service ministry began the operational phase of a FCFA 8 billion e-learning platform for all civil servants, to run to 2029. The 2026-2028 roadmap plans AI training for over 2,000 public officials by 2027, the digital minister said in October 2026. No source found says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

CMR.short: Digital-skills training reached civil servants across government in 2026; the share trained is not published.
CMR.summary: On 21 September 2026 Cameroon's government launched the online platform train.patnucelearning.cm under PATNUC, with a target of 15,000 civil servants and public-enterprise staff. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the agriculture ministry reported that the PATNUC programme was open to agents of public administrations nationwide. It has five certifying online modules, including AI and blockchain. The programme is stated to be open to agents of all ministries, including deconcentrated services. No source found since October 2023 gives the share of the civil service trained in digital skills. Mature would need the share of civil servants trained published, or the number trained beside the headcount.

COD.short: Digital-skills courses for state agents were held in 2025 and 2026; no source found reports a standing programme with a number trained.
COD.summary: In November 2023 the digital agency ADN and Africa Digital Academy agreed to train 100,000 public agents in 2024-2025 in cybersecurity, AI and digital transformation. In the last twelve months, ADN, with KADEA and ULB-Solvay, held the first session of an executive programme in digital transformation and AI on 28-30 September 2026. It was for cadres of 30 public institutions. In September 2025 the education ministry began 15-day computing courses, in groups of 20, for staff of its central services. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

COG.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
COG.summary: The Agence Congolaise des Systemes d'Information runs an office-skills training programme for staff of public administrations, with a session scheduled from 23 March to 17 April 2026. In the last twelve months, ACSI scheduled that session for staff of the Direction Generale des Comptes Publics et du Patrimoine. Les Depeches de Brazzaville reports that the World Bank-funded PATN project opened training centres for public-sector agents of the Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy department. Sessions run at least 30 hours, on database management. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

COM.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2023; a standing programme is not on record.
COM.summary: In December 2023 AFD said that training under its PAGF-SI project strengthens the digital skills of the Ministry of Finance's agents. The aim is that they can adopt the new tools. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government, or that a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

CPV.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
CPV.summary: In May 2026 Resolução 72/2026 recognised as progress digital-inclusion and skills-training initiatives developed for citizens and public servants. In the last twelve months, the justice modernisation institute said 110 justice professionals had been trained in artificial intelligence by September 2026, among them judges, prosecutors and court officers. The government's national capacity programme is Administração Pública + Digital. It announced a pilot digital-skills course for public servants on 22-26 September 2025 at the state modernisation ministry in Praia. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

DJI.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
DJI.summary: In February 2025 Djibouti's Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation launched a digital-skills programme for government officials with DCO, Oracle University and INAP. It covers cloud, AI, cybersecurity and data management through Oracle MyLearn. The digital economy minister cited the training of 400 public-sector and civil-society executives through Coursera among the government's initiatives in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No news story or official notice found gives the number of officials the Oracle programme has trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

DZA.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2024; a standing programme is not on record.
DZA.summary: In 2024 the Ministry of National Education said it launched a project with UNESCO and the EU to build an e-learning platform. It first trains a core group of inspectors in pedagogical engineering. The inspectors then train teachers to produce multimedia courses. Teachers are counted among the ministry's 1,019,509 fonctionnaires. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme for civil servants is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

EGY.short: Digital-skills training reached civil servants across government in 2025; the share trained is not published.
EGY.summary: In November 2024 the deputy ICT minister said the state capacity-building plan had issued 146,695 training certificates. The Fundamentals of Digital Skills Program, implemented by ICDL Arabia, targets all employees of the state's administrative apparatus. The deputy minister said most of its leaders and staff had been trained. In the last twelve months, between March and May 2026 UNESCO and MCIT trained more than 90 civil servants from 25 ministries in AI literacy. In October 2026 the communications and labour ministries signed an MoU on digital capacity for Labour Ministry staff. No source found since October 2023 gives the share of the civil service trained in digital skills. Mature would need the share of civil servants trained published, or the number trained beside the headcount.

ERI.short: Nothing found since 2023 names digital-skills training for civil servants, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: No stage is set. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether civil servants in Eritrea are trained in digital skills, and no source from the past three years says they receive none. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or prepared a digital-skills programme for civil servants, or to have held digital-skills courses for officials.

ETH.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
ETH.summary: UNCDF reports that the Ministry of Innovation and Technology led a three-day nationwide Digital Financial Literacy campaign, held in April 2026. In the last twelve months, that campaign trained 525 public-sector participants from 26 public institutions, targeting women civil servants. Addis Fortune reports that by August 2025 more than 120,000 Addis Abeba government employees had enrolled in Udacity courses in coding, AI and data science. Many skipped the content to collect certificates. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

GAB.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
GAB.summary: GabonReview says a DGPE course of 7 to 17 October 2025 in Libreville trained nearly 300 agents. In the last twelve months, on 7 September 2026, the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation ran an introductory AI-tools session for over forty agents of the Ministry of Communication and Media. The RCAPE programme plans to train 500 state agents by December 2026. Treasury agents took a three-day course in digital tools and AI at the Centre in September 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

GHA.short: The government committed in 2025 to train 200,000 civil servants in digital skills; the share trained is not published.
GHA.summary: In 2024, 520 public and civil servants from 53 ministries, departments and agencies graduated from the DigSMART Scale-Up programme, Graphic Online reports. In July 2025 the communication minister announced a plan to train 200,000 civil servants in AI and coding, under the One Million Coders Programme. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, Deputy Minister Sukparu said the government has begun an AI capacity-building programme for public-sector officials. It is run with UNESCO, UNDP and Japan. No source found since October 2023 gives the share of the civil service trained in digital skills. Mature would need the share of civil servants trained published, or the number trained beside the headcount.

GIN.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
GIN.summary: On 23 September 2026 the state digitalisation agency ANDE validated the feasibility study for a National Digital Academy. It is to offer short certified courses aimed first at civil servants. In the last twelve months, the National School of Administration trained 30 national and general directors in digital transformation, AI and cybersecurity on 13-15 October 2026, for the public service ministry. On 15 May 2026 the civil service ministry presented nine projects, among them training public servants to use digital tools. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

GMB.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
GMB.summary: In December 2025 The Gambia's Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy signed a framework agreement with Smart Africa, TechAfrica News reports. It is to implement the Smart Africa Digital Academy, which will train policymakers and public sector leaders among others. In the last twelve months, that agreement is the step found towards an academy. No source found says the academy has trained anyone. The Point reports that the Ministry of Public Service ran a five-day Microsoft Power BI data analytics training from 24 March 2025 for at least 16 staff. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

GNB.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
GNB.summary: By June 2026 the government and UNDP, with EU funding, had run a roughly 30-hour Word, Excel and PowerPoint course under the +Digit@l and Justisa pa Tudu Djintis projects. In the last twelve months, the course reached justice and human rights professionals, among others, alongside a 36-hour trainer programme. In October 2025 UNDP and the Technological Institute for Administrative Modernization (ITMA) ran a three-day course on data security and protection. It trained ITMA staff and civil servants to train others across the public service. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

GNQ.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
GNQ.summary: In January 2025 the government presented an INAP training plan for central-administration civil servants, which runs from 23 February 2025 and includes basic digital competencies and typing courses. On 15 July 2025 CNIAPGE began a 10-day training for more than 50 officials of the Primatura on the GEX case-file platform. It is to be extended to ministerial departments. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

KEN.short: A digital-skills programme trained civil servants in 2026; reach across government is not on record.
KEN.summary: In November 2025 UNESCO and the Kenya School of Government launched a free online course on AI and digital transformation for civil servants. The programme behind it aims to train 20,000 by 2027. In the last twelve months, the School says 13,790 public servants completed Phase I of its AI and Digital Skilling Project by February 2026. In October 2026 its eLITI institute opened as 1,239 public officers graduated from that course, out of a first cohort of 2,730. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

LBR.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
LBR.summary: On 22 January 2026 the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission concluded a seven-day digital literacy training for its staff, the information ministry reports. It ended in certification. In the last twelve months, CSquared states that Liberia has begun preparing for AI through AI training for civil servants with the UNDP. No news story or official notice found gives a number of civil servants trained by a standing programme in Liberia. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

LBY.short: Computer-skills courses for government employees were held in 2025; no source found reports a standing programme with a number trained.
LBY.summary: On 14 September 2025 the Ministry of Civil Service launched a one-week computer-applications course for government employees in Benghazi, Libya Update reports, citing LANA. It was the first of a series on electronic archiving. The Ministry of Labour and Rehabilitation held a basic computer-skills workshop for its staff in Sirte that closed on 26 August 2025. In May 2025 the Libyan Digital Lab and Expertise France held a workshop on adapting France's Pix digital-skills platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

LSO.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
LSO.summary: The 2027/28 Budget Strategy Paper directs medium-term budget support to a public-service digital and AI literacy programme and attaches no amount. In September 2025 the ICT ministry and LIPAM held a one-day session for officers in Mohale's Hoek on the use of technology in ministries. In August 2023 the ICT ministry began a cyber security training workshop for government officials, run with Tethics. No standing programme has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

MAR.short: A digital-skills programme had trained over 6,800 civil servants by 2023 and moved online in 2024; no source found reports reach across government.
MAR.summary: In September 2024 the Digital Development Agency launched the e-TAMKEEN e-learning programme on its Academia Raqmya platform. Between 2019 and 2023 it had trained more than 6,800 civil servants at central and local levels on 23 digital topics. In the last twelve months, on 22 September 2026, the National School of Administration and the agency signed a partnership to build public-sector workers' skills in digital transformation, AI and data management. The numbers to be trained had not yet been announced. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

MDG.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
MDG.summary: In August 2025 Minister Delmotte said the ministry is training civil servants to handle the new digital identity systems. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, Madagascar Newsroom reported a training session on AI use in administration. It was held for the Treasury's director general and several colleagues. The partner was the Projet Poles Integres de Croissance (PIC), and the session was described as a first step. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

MLI.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
MLI.summary: On 1 September 2026 AGEFAU financed the launch of office-software and collaborative-tools training for 504 elected officials and staff of 126 communes. In the last twelve months, the Centre de Formation des Collectivités Territoriales has run that training. Its first session drew 84 participants from 21 communes. In September 2022 AGETIC held a workshop, chaired by the minister, to train ministries' communication officers on the gouv.ml government email. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

MOZ.short: A digital-skills programme trained civil servants in 2025; reach across government is not on record.
MOZ.summary: By November 2025 7,033 public servants (3,746 women, 3,287 men) had been trained in digital skills under the Public Administration Reform and Modernisation Programme. Jornal Noticias reports MCTES data showing more than 33,000 public servants, state agents and young people trained in ICT use in 2020-2023 through INAGE. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the communications ministry trained staff of MEC, INTIC and the ministry itself. The training covered the e-SuRA, CorreioGov, CloudGov and Digital Signer systems. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

MRT.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
MRT.summary: In December 2025 the ministers of digital transformation and public service launched a twelve-week cybersecurity and AI course for 300 civil servants. A distance-learning centre runs it with German cooperation. In the last twelve months, GIZ says the centre's cybersecurity and AI courses, each aimed at 150 public-sector staff, were completed by June 2026. GovStack says a five-day workshop in Nouakchott, ending on 2 October 2026, took in 120 newly recruited public servants. In June 2024 the ministry announced the Temekoun platform to teach public servants basic digital skills. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

MUS.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
MUS.summary: In 2025 the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Public Service and Innovation offered a four-level Digital Transformation for Organisational Excellence Programme. The Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reforms sponsors it. It teaches public officers IT skills, Maupass and Mausign, EDMS and AI, and states no number trained. The Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation says in a June 2025 newsletter that its Digital Leadership Training for civil officers and National Digital Literacy Campaign equip public officers. It gives no number trained. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

MWI.short: A six-month School of Government course had trained over 120 civil servants in digital skills by 2024; no source found reports reach across government.
MWI.summary: On 7 November 2023, 112 civil servants completed a six-month digital-skills course at the Malawi School of Government, of about 180 who enrolled. The government ran it with the Tony Blair Institute. In September 2024 the e-government director said the ministry and partners had given digital-skills training to more than 120 civil servants. In the last twelve months, on 13 August 2026, the University of Malawi's Department of Computing opened a two-day computer-skills course for 75 Malawi Police Service officers, under the UNDP-backed IDT4M programme. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

NAM.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
NAM.summary: On 4 June 2026 NIPAM signed an MoU with the Global Cybersecurity Centre to develop and deliver cybersecurity training for Namibian public servants. In the last twelve months, NIPAM announced structured three- to five-day AI courses for civil servants at an AI executive leadership seminar in Windhoek. They start with executive directors and senior management, and the curriculum is being finalised. NIPAM's May 2026 bulletin says its first AI readiness seminar for the public sector, on 12 May, drew more than 100 participants from public and private institutions. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

NER.short: Ministry staff attended digital-platform courses in 2025; no standing programme with a number trained has been found.
NER.summary: In July 2025 the Ministry of Justice and ANSI launched a training for Justice ministry officials on managing mail and documents electronically through the GED platform. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, ANSI ran a three-day training for 175 foreign ministry (MAEC) staff. It covered the government's professional email and electronic mail-management (GEC) platforms. No source found since October 2023 names a standing digital-skills programme for civil servants with a number trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

NGA.short: Federal civil servants were required in 2025 to take a digital-literacy course; about 79% enrolled and over 40% completed by 2026.
NGA.summary: NITDA and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service run the Digital Literacy for All programme on the Cisco Networking Academy. In September 2025 the Head of the Civil Service required all civil servants to complete the Cisco-backed course within two months. In the last twelve months, NITDA's director general said in February 2026 that the 54,377 civil servants enrolled were nearly 79 per cent participation, and that over 40 per cent had completed. Punch puts completion at 38.1 to 44.6 per cent across the four modules. TechTrends Africa put those trained at more than 53,000 by September 2026. The shares given are for the federal civil service; nothing found gives the share for state civil services.

RWA.short: AI training became mandatory for all public servants in 2026 and nearly 200,000 completed it; no source found reports the share of the civil service.
RWA.summary: On 12 January 2026 the ICT ministry's communique made AI training compulsory for all state employees in every sector. In the last twelve months, the public service and ICT ministries launched a free online AI training of four courses for public servants in December 2025. It was to be completed by 31 January 2026. Apolitical says nearly 200,000 public servants had completed it by May 2026, and that at least 76 per cent of them are frontline workers. No source found since October 2023 gives the share of the civil service trained in digital skills. Mature would need the share of civil servants trained published, or the number trained beside the headcount.

SDN.short: Officials attended digital-skills courses in 2025 and 2026; no standing programme with a number trained has been found.
SDN.summary: In November 2025 Sudan Customs and ARADO concluded their third course on IT applications in customs work, and 21 customs officers at colonel rank received completion certificates. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, SUNA reported that Northern State's information centre and training directorate closed four ICT courses. They trained 84 staff of the state secretariat, ministries, councils and localities. The courses were advanced Excel, statistical analysis, internet applications and video conferencing, and printer maintenance. No source found since October 2023 names a standing digital-skills programme for civil servants with a number trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SEN.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
SEN.summary: On 10 September 2026 Senegal's Ministry of Public Service and the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs validated a National Digital Training Plan for Civil Servants. It targets all 183,502 state agents by 2029 in two waves. In the last twelve months, FORCE-N reports that a pilot in the first quarter of 2026 enrolled 583 agents of three ministries in certified digital training. Of the enrollees, 70 per cent did not sit the exams. ITWeb Africa reports that the telecommunications ministry launched a programme to upskill public servants in digital tools, data, AI and cybersecurity. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SLE.short: Ministries launched digital-skills training for civil servants in 2026 and certified a first cohort; the number trained has not been found.
SLE.summary: In June 2026 an agreement between the communication and public administration ministries set a nine-month programme to train 1,000 civil servants. It covers digital tools, data, AI and cybersecurity, delivered through the Public Service Academy. In the last twelve months, the first cohort was certified in September 2026 after three weeks of digital literacy training, with the next due on 9 October. TechReviewAfrica reports the training targets staff across ministries, departments and agencies. No source found gives the number of civil servants the programme has trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SOM.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
SOM.summary: In 2025 a survey of 138 Somali government employees finds 70.3% report having attended ICT or digital-skills training. Of them, 55.1% report an ICT training programme or coordinator in their ministry. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the communications ministry's National Institute of Telecommunications and Technology launched a programme to raise government employees' digital knowledge. It opened with a data protection workshop. In June 2024 the Ministry of Communications and Technology inaugurated a website development and design training for employees of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SSD.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
SSD.summary: In August 2026 the Ministry of ICT and Postal Services said the government has trained its officers in modern technologies for records digitisation. The digitisation effort is not yet complete. Central Equatoria State's Ministry of Information and Communication, with Scenius Hub, is implementing the five-year DISK Program, whose three Digital Skills Centres in government facilities will train civil servants among others. National Revenue Authority Commissioner General William Anyuon Kuol said immigration and revenue officials had already been trained on the new digital passport payment platform. No standing programme has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

STP.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2024; a standing programme is not on record.
STP.summary: In January 2024 Téla Nón reported a workshop on information security in the capital, with public administration staff taking part. The national director of public administration said staff handling the planned civil-service personnel database must be trained. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SWZ.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
SWZ.summary: In October 2025 Prime Minister Dlamini applauded the Eswatini Institute of Management and Public Administration (EIMPA) for offering online and physical cybersecurity training for civil servants. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, Eswatini launched the She Powers Africa Digital Academy, starting with 50 women from government and related institutions. They train in AI, cybersecurity, data science, software development and IT operations. Eswatini Positive News reports that the Ministry of ICT is training Change Agents from various government ministries to lead implementation of the Eswatini Digital Project. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

SYC.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
SYC.summary: From 11 to 22 May 2026 a first cohort of Seychelles civil servants, including National Assembly staff, took a two-week NCGG programme in India. It covered digital public infrastructure and AI. In the last twelve months, India's Press Information Bureau says NCGG began the first programme for 29 senior Seychelles civil servants on 11 May 2026. It is the first milestone of a three-year NCGG-Public Service Bureau MoU to train 250 civil servants. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

TCD.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
TCD.summary: In July 2025 Chad's ADETIC signed a framework accord with 2iE Ouagadougou, We are Tech Africa reported. It is to train Chadian public cadres in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, about 60 officials and curriculum developers were trained, with UNESCO support, to use AI in school curricula, Ecofin reported. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

TGO.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2025; a standing programme is not on record.
TGO.summary: In June 2026 GIZ ProDigiT said Agence Togo Digital's Digital Ambassadors programme had graduated 80 civil servants after 14 months. They were placed in 27 ministries and agencies. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 Agence Togo Digital launched a pilot programme to train 20,000 state employees in basic digital skills. A six-week data science certification for public administration professionals began at the Togo Data Lab on 14 April 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

TUN.short: Tunisia opened a digital-skills platform for its 680,000 civil servants in 2023; no source found gives the number it has trained.
TUN.summary: On 1 December 2023 the communication technologies ministry launched the Digital Learning Academy platform to build the digital skills of the state's civil servants. It says the academy is for all of the state's 680,000 civil servants. In the last twelve months, Korea lists an active 2026 grant for a course training officials of the Prime Minister's office and related ministries in e-training systems. Since June 2024 a KOICA-funded national e-learning platform has offered public agents four pilot modules. No source found since October 2023 gives a number of civil servants trained. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

TZA.short: A government digital-skills programme had trained 500 government staff by 2026; reach across government is not on record.
TZA.summary: By September 2026 the Digital Tanzania Project had trained 500 government staff, project coordinator Bakari Mwamgugu said. Fifty took master's degrees abroad in AI and machine learning and 450 took short local courses. In the last twelve months, on 16 August 2026, Zanzibar's Ministry of Communications, IT and Innovation signed a three-year MoU with Emerson Education Institute to train an initial cohort of 600 officials in AI and cybersecurity. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

UGA.short: A digital-skills programme trained civil servants in 2025; reach across government is not on record.
UGA.summary: The Uganda Institute of ICT trained 2,268 government officers in 2024/25 in digital leadership, data science and ICT awareness. In the last twelve months, by November 2026, 5,587 officers had passed through the institute. In May 2025 the ICT ministry held ICDL-aligned training for communication officers from government bodies. In July 2025 it trained over 200 government communications officers with MultiChoice Uganda. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

ZAF.short: A digital-skills programme trained civil servants in 2025; reach across government is not on record.
ZAF.summary: In August 2025 the public service minister said the National School of Government's free online digital courses had trained 4,725 public servants. In the last twelve months, the Gauteng Department of e-Government reported that 6,461 government employees received digital skills training in its 2025/26 reporting period. In February 2026 the National School of Government agreed with Huawei to add AI, cybersecurity, cloud and digital government courses to its online platform. Deputy Minister Nzuza says Home Affairs set aside R4 million for training. No source found since October 2023 says digital-skills training reaches civil servants across government. Operating would need the programme open to all ministries, or staff trained across most of government.

ZMB.short: Digital-skills training for civil servants was under way in 2026; a standing programme is not on record.
ZMB.summary: In December 2025 SMART Zambia's institute rolled out a decentralised digital-skills programme for the public service on its Cisco Networking Academy platform. In the last twelve months, it launched a training-of-trainers programme in Ndola on 12 January 2026 for 80 people, mainly from public institutions. In July 2026 SMART Zambia's e-Government Division trained 146 public officers in three Southern Province districts. The training covered digital literacy, cybersecurity, Outlook and data protection. No source found since October 2023 says a standing programme is in service. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe trained 105 civil servants in cyber security in 2024 and plans mandatory digital-skills training; no standing programme with a number trained is known.
ZWE.summary: In November 2025 Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube said Zimbabwe's government is set to make digital skills training in AI, cybersecurity and data management mandatory for all civil servants. At least 10,000 public employees are to be trained each year. Minister Mavetera announced a three-tier AI Skills Accelerator Programme for the public sector, with foundational awareness for every civil servant. No standing programme with a stated number trained has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names a standing digital-skills programme for civil servants. Establishing would need a programme, academy or platform in service with a stated number of civil servants trained.

AGO.short: Angola has a hosting policy being written and none in force, so no source found says where public bodies must host.
AGO.summary: In March 2026 the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa issued terms of reference for a five-month consultancy to draft a national policy on managing and hosting public data. The policy is to set hosting rules by category of data, and rules on where data must reside. In the last twelve months this is the only step toward a policy that has been found. No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

BDI.short: Nothing found says Burundi has a government hosting or cloud policy, or says it has none, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government hosting or cloud policy, or says there is none.

BEN.short: Nothing found says Benin has a government hosting or cloud policy, or says it has none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government hosting or cloud policy, or says there is none.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso tells public bodies to host nationally and opened two government cloud data centres in 2026; no source found says which bodies have moved.
BFA.summary: The two government-cloud data centres the Prime Minister inaugurated on 23 January 2026 are to host all public data. A Prime Minister's circular tells public bodies to give priority to national hosting. In the last twelve months the state ICT agency's board set the repatriation of administrations' data to them as its course for 2026. By July 2026 the ministry had inventoried 120 public platforms for hosting in the country. Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

BWA.short: Botswana's government was developing a cloud computing policy in 2025 and none is in force, so no source found says where public bodies must host.
BWA.summary: In February 2025 the Deputy Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Communications and Innovation said the government was developing digital and cloud computing policies. He gave no date for their adoption and did not say who was drafting them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The same statement names no government cloud or data centre that public bodies must use. No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic was preparing a national data hosting strategy in 2026; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
CAF.summary: On 19 May 2026 the Public Sector Digital Governance Programme (PGNSP) held a workshop on preparing a National Data Hosting Strategy, as a participant reported it. In the last twelve months this workshop is the only step toward a policy that has been found. A World Bank-financed project had set a government-wide cloud strategy as a target for December 2026, and its September 2023 progress report recorded that no strategy had been developed. No adopted text has been found. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

CIV.short: A cloud hosting procedure for ministries and institutions was approved in June 2021; no source found says where public bodies must host.
CIV.summary: The ANSUT document Politique d'hébergement des données dans le cloud, version 1.0 dated 14 June 2021, was approved on 17 June 2021. It sets the procedure for ministries and institutions to host applications in the cloud, and no end or replacement is stated. It names a Microsoft Azure public cloud and the Datacenter eGOUV, both run by ANSUT. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says public bodies must use either, or names a list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

CMR.short: Nothing found says Cameroon has a government hosting or cloud policy, or says it has none, so no stage is set.
CMR.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a government hosting or cloud policy, or says there is none.

COD.short: A national data hosting strategy was being developed in March 2026; no adopted policy, or where public bodies must host, is known.
COD.summary: The Digital Transformation Project terms of reference of March 2026 say the government is developing a national data hosting strategy. UNECA and GIZ are helping. The consultants are to propose hosting and cloud decrees and directives. CIO Mag reported on 8 November 2023 that the Council of Ministers had adopted a draft decree on the management of national datacenters. It does not say the decree was later issued. In the last twelve months the terms of reference are the only step toward a policy that has been found. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.
