CPV.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2024; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
CPV.summary: In October 2024 the finance ministry said that SIGOF, the state's public finance system, pays suppliers and staff, and was unstable in October 2024. The ministry describes it as centralising state public finance management across the budget cycle. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the tax authority's system or the civil-service payroll is in use. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

DJI.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

DZA.short: The Treasury system has run state spending since 2023 and tax runs on computer systems; no source found says whether the payroll does.
DZA.summary: The finance minister told parliament that the Treasury's information system has run spending under the programme budget since 1 January 2023. The minister said the Djibayatic tax system covered 40 centres by February 2024. On 29 November 2024 the ministry launched the first phase of its integrated budget management system, SIGB. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need the payroll to run on a computer system, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

EGY.short: Finance, tax and payroll run on computer systems by 2025; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
EGY.summary: The Tax Authority's head said in October 2025 that a unified platform computes employers' wage tax, and passes it to the authority's mechanised system for payment. The Egyptian Cabinet spokesman said the government Payroll system had been activated in 2,281 of 2,675 target accounting units. In June 2024 the finance ministry said it is strengthening the link between its e-payment centre and GFMIS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the financial, tax or payroll system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. Operating would need one of the three core systems to go live on a new or upgraded system in the last three years.

ERI.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

ETH.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2025; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
ETH.summary: In 2025 the Ministry of Finance's full-year EFY 2017 (Sene-2017) federal budget vs expenditure report is drawn from IFMIS. It states that of 174 federal public sites, 118 use IFMIS and 56 use IBEX, reported separately. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the tax authority's system or the civil-service payroll is in use. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

GAB.short: Finance, tax and payroll systems in use, one renewed in 2026; no published map of government systems is known.
GAB.summary: On 15 January 2026 the government launched SIGFIP, which handles the state's spending and revenue on one platform. The minister said the administration built it in house and owns its source code. SIGFIP brings tax, customs and non-tax revenue into one database with one payment interface, Ecofin Agency reports. The public service ministry keeps state staff records on the Fichier unique de référence, in use for about twenty years, which feeds the Solde payroll. In the last twelve months, SIGFIP went live on 15 January 2026, moving Gabon from fragmented systems to one integrated platform (Ecofin Agency). No source found says the government has published an enterprise architecture or an inventory of its systems. Mature would need one to be published.

GHA.short: Finance, tax and payroll run on computer systems by 2026; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
GHA.summary: The finance ministry's 2026-2029 budget guidelines require regional councils and district assemblies to process all transactions through GIFMIS, the integrated financial management system. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the revenue authority said some parts of its new tax administration system, ITAS, were already working. In August 2026 all taxpayers still filed on GITMIS. The Controller and Accountant-General's Department runs the government payroll, linked to the national identity database in January 2024. No source found says a core system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. Operating would need one of the three core systems to go live on a new or upgraded system in the last three years.

GIN.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
GIN.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

GMB.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2026; the tax system is run largely by hand.
GMB.summary: In August 2026 the Accountant General's Department said IFMIS is operational in larger ministries and agencies. The GRA Commissioner General said the current domestic tax administration system is largely manual. The new ITAS is to replace it. In the last twelve months IFMIS was cited and not changed. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau's new civil-service payroll platform went live in 2024; no source found says the financial management system is in use, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: No stage is set. The IMF says Guinea-Bissau launched a blockchain platform for the public payroll in May 2024, under its Extended Credit Facility programme. The IMF said it could cover all 26,600 civil servants and 8,100 pensioners by November 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from 2023 or later says how the budget is executed and paid, or describes the tax system. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

GNQ.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2025; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
GNQ.summary: On 10 February 2025 the Interministerial Council took up new directives for the CONFIN system, which cover the whole public administration and autonomous bodies. CONFIN is described as an integrated public finance management system built for executing current expenditure of the state budget. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the tax authority's system or the civil-service payroll is in use. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

KEN.short: Budget, tax and payroll ran on computer systems by 2026; no renewal of any of them since 2023 is known.
KEN.summary: In October 2026 the revenue authority and the Treasury said all suppliers to government go through the IFMIS payment workflow. A Star column says Kenyans filed annual and VAT returns on the KRA iTax portal in June and August 2026. The Unified Human Resource system holds public-service HR and payroll data. In the last twelve months, the ICT ministry published guidelines on the Government Enterprise Architecture in 2026. No source found says a core system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. The revenue authority said in 2025 it was upgrading iTax's back end. Operating would need one of the three core systems to go live on a new or upgraded system in the last three years.

LBR.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2026; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
LBR.summary: In May 2026 the finance ministry said it is integrating IFMIS with the LITAS and SIGTAS tax systems. It treats IFMIS as an existing system. The revenue authority's IT project coordinator said in August 2025 that filing, assessments, payments and collections run on LITAS. In the last twelve months, the May 2026 statement describes the integration as under way, and no source found says it was completed. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need the payroll to run on a computer system, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

LBY.short: Libya paid August 2025 salaries on a new treasury system; no source found reports a financial management system across government, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: No stage is set. The finance minister said August 2025 public-sector salaries were processed on the new unified treasury account system, after basic data for about 41% of state employees had been uploaded. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the Libyan Tax Authority announced the official start of work on the Unified Tax System. Nothing found says the treasury account system or the tax system replaced an older one. Nothing found from 2023 or later describes a financial management system in use across government. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

LSO.short: Finance, tax and payroll run on computer systems by 2025; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
LSO.summary: The finance ministry's 2026 terms of reference say all ministries and councils use the Epicor-based IFMIS. In December 2023 the World Bank said a human resource management information system was in place, with its payroll module in use. Revenue Services Lesotho's guide of February 2025 describes its e-Taxation platform. In the last twelve months the IFMIS was cited and not changed, in the finance ministry's 2026 terms of reference. No source found says a core system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. Operating would need one of the three core systems to go live on a new or upgraded system in the last three years.

MAR.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
MAR.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

MDG.short: Tax runs online by 2025; no source found says whether the government budgets and pays through a computer system, so no stage is set.
MDG.summary: No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial management system or the payroll is in use. An interview with the finance minister names an Integrated Public Finance Management System (being upgraded), the AUGURE payroll (being modernised) and SIGPensions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

MLI.short: No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial system is in use, so no stage is set.
MLI.summary: No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial management system is in use. In the last twelve months, sources found named a Tier III data centre, Bamako and a Government Intranet, and neither answers that. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

MOZ.short: Finance, tax collection and payroll run on computer systems by 2025; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
MOZ.summary: The state runs its finances on e-SISTAFE, in place since 2004. In November 2024 the finance ministry said e-SISTAFE has 11 modules, all working except internal audit. In November 2025 the finance minister described SESPE, an e-SISTAFE service that collects taxes and fees electronically. In October 2025 the ministry said e-SNGRHE, the civil-service system, removes employees from the payroll automatically when they miss the yearly biometric proof of life. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 CEDSIF listed e-Tributação as the domestic tax system, cited and not changed. No source found says a core system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. Operating would need one to do so in the last three years.

MRT.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
MRT.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

MUS.short: Mauritius runs its accounts, tax and a payroll renewed in 2024 on computer systems, and publishes a list of its operational systems.
MUS.summary: The Central Informatics Bureau lists the Treasury Accounting System as operational. The same November 2024 list names the finance ministry's E-Budget. Individuals filed their 2025 tax returns on the revenue authority's e-filing system. The division built the new payroll system in house and it went live in July 2024, after a parallel run in June. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The bureau's 2025 progress update marks as done the publication of a catalogue of information systems.

MWI.short: The government budgets, pays and runs its payroll through computer systems by 2024; no source found says whether tax does too.
MWI.summary: The Accountant General said in May 2024 that the SAP-based IFMIS, rolled out to all ministries, departments and agencies a year earlier, was fully operational. The Accountant General told a parliamentary committee in February 2024 that the government payroll runs on the human resource management information system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the tax authority's system is in use. Establishing would need tax collection to run on a computer system as well, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

NAM.short: No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial system is in use, so no stage is set.
NAM.summary: No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial management system is in use. In the last twelve months, sources found named the Integrated Social Assistance System (ISAS), the Integrated Beneficiary Registry (IBR) and the GIPF database, and none answers that. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

NER.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

NGA.short: Nigeria runs finance, tax and payroll on GIFMIS, TaxPro Max and IPPIS, moved payroll to a local platform in 2026, and operates an enterprise architecture.
NGA.summary: In April 2025 FIRS ordered all tax collections run through TaxPro Max, the platform for registration, filing and payment. In July 2026 the Accountant-General said IPPIS covers 508 ministries, departments and agencies and over 1,008,800 employee records. In the last twelve months, the IPPIS HR modules went live on 27 July 2026 on SoftSuite, a locally developed platform, replacing the Oracle E-Business Suite. On 28 August 2026 the President ordered an audit of how IPPIS links with GIFMIS, the Treasury Single Account and Sub-TSA. In March 2026 NITDA took over the Nigeria Government Enterprise Architecture from KOICA.

RWA.short: Rwanda runs its budget, tax and payroll on computer systems, upgraded IFMIS in 2026 and publishes a government enterprise architecture framework.
RWA.summary: The revenue authority's 2025 Tax Handbook says taxpayers declare online or by phone on E-Tax and M-Declaration. The public service ministry says IPPIS supports public institutions from recruitment to exit, including payroll management for salary payments. MINECOFIN says it completed a major technological upgrade of the IFMIS, replacing legacy components that had reached end of support. No date for the upgrade has been found, so no change within the last twelve months is shown. RISA's Government of Rwanda Enterprise Architecture Framework, Version 2.1, states the government chose TOGAF.

SDN.short: A civil-service records platform launched in 2026; nothing says the government's finances run on a computer system, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial management system is in use. In the last twelve months the Bayan civil-service records platform was launched, in August 2026, and no source found shows it in service. Sources found name Esali (electronic collection and payment system), a Treasury Single Account (TSA) and an Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

SEN.short: Senegal runs its accounts, tax and payroll on computer systems and renewed its large-taxpayer platform in 2026; no map of government systems is published.
SEN.summary: The Treasury's 2024 report says its revenue and expenditure operations between ASTER and SIGCDD were automated that year. Terms of reference of November 2023 list the eSolde payroll among the state's systems in use. In the last twelve months, the directorate's communiqué of 27 August 2026 says SENTAX now replaces the ETAX application for online declaration and payment by large taxpayers. Since 1 September 2026 the platform has been mandatory for every declaration and payment by large-enterprise taxpayers. No source found says the government has published an enterprise architecture or an inventory of its systems. Mature would need one to be published.

SLE.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2025; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
SLE.summary: World Bank terms of reference of 2025 say the finance ministry has launched IFMIS among its core public finance systems. They say these systems run standalone. In October 2025 the Principal Deputy Financial Secretary said the government had invested over USD 300 million in standalone systems including IFMIS. The Revenue Authority's Commissioner General said taxpayers can now file and pay electronically through ITAS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need the payroll to run on a computer system, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

SOM.short: Finance, tax and payroll run on computer systems by 2025; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
SOM.summary: The FY2025 annual report states digital signatures were introduced in SFMIS to re-engineer payment processes. The Electronic Tax Administration System (ETAS) and other digital platforms improved automation and streamlined revenue collection in 2025. The Office of the Accountant General's letter of 29 August 2026 refers to the existing government payroll system. In the last twelve months, the finance ministry signed a contract in September 2026 to extend SFMIS to four federal member states. No source found says a new or upgraded financial, tax or payroll system went live since October 2023. Operating would need one to do so in the last three years.

SSD.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2025; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
SSD.summary: FreeBalance's press release says South Sudan's Ministry of Finance and Planning is expanding its existing IFMIS to additional ministries, departments and agencies. The contract was signed in Juba on 4 February 2025. In the last twelve months, the South Sudan Revenue Authority Commissioner General directed on 2026-03-13 that all government revenues be paid exclusively through the National e-Tax System, and banned manual collection. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need the payroll to run on a computer system, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

STP.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

SWZ.short: The government's financial system was restored in October 2026; the tax portal went down in November and no source found reports a payroll system.
SWZ.summary: The Ministry of ICT acknowledged on 23 September 2026 outages of government platforms including the Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS). On 23 October 2026 the ministry said IFMIS was among 13 government services restored. In the last twelve months, the revenue service's taxpayer portal, with filing and customs information, went offline when the government shut down systems at its data centre on 17 November 2026. Nothing found describes the civil-service payroll. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

SYC.short: The government budgets and pays through a computer system by 2024; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
SYC.summary: The IMF's April 2024 mission was told the finance ministry uses Visual Account Mate (VAM) and the Treasury Information System (TIS) as the government accounting software. The mission was told of operational challenges and many manual interventions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from 2023 or later says the tax authority's system or the civil-service payroll is in use. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

TCD.short: Finance, tax and payroll run on computer systems by 2026; none is known to have been renewed since 2023.
TCD.summary: The director general of taxes states SIGFIP has been operational since 2021 across public finance execution and State budget execution (Tchadinfos, 5 May 2026). He states E-TAX has been operational since 2021 in the public finance circuit, alongside SIGFIP. The finance ministry launched SIGFiP at Bardai in January 2025, completing its installation across the country. In the last twelve months the systems were cited and not changed, in the May 2026 statement. No source found says a new or upgraded financial, tax or payroll system went live since October 2023. Operating would need one to do so in the last three years.

TGO.short: Togo runs budget execution in SIGFiP and tax returns online in 2026; no source found says the payroll runs on a computer system.
TGO.summary: The finance ministry said in February 2026 that budget execution runs in SIGFiP. In 2025 large and medium firms filed and paid all their VAT returns online. Other taxpayers filed 26% online. In the last twelve months, the February 2026 statement said commitment plans and annual work plans are to be computerised in SIGFiP. Agence Togo Digital publishes the Architecture d'Entreprise Gouvernementale du Togo online. No source found from 2023 or later says the civil-service payroll runs on a computer system. Establishing would need the payroll to run on a computer system, shown by a source from 2023 or later.

TUN.short: Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the government's finance, tax or payroll systems are in use.

TZA.short: The government pays through a computer system by 2025; no source found says whether tax and payroll do too.
TZA.summary: The Ministry of Finance said in February 2025 that it had integrated its CS-Meridian debt system with MUSE, the Government Payment System. It had also trained Kenyan officials on how the link works. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from 2023 or later describes the tax system or the civil-service payroll. Establishing would need tax collection and the civil-service payroll to run on computer systems, shown by sources from 2023 or later.

UGA.short: Uganda runs its finances, tax and payroll on computer systems, is moving payroll to a new HR system and renewed its enterprise architecture in 2026.
UGA.summary: The finance ministry's 2025 reform strategy says IFMS has been rolled out to all 163 central and 176 local government votes. The 2025 strategy says the Human Capital Management system runs HR and payroll in 160 entities. It replaces the old personnel and payroll system in phases. In June 2026 the revenue authority said VAT, rental income tax and local excise returns had moved to web-based platforms. In the last twelve months, EGA reports that the Government of Uganda renewed its Government Enterprise Architecture, led by NITA-U with World Bank support. The article is dated 27 May 2026 and gives no earlier completion date.

ZAF.short: No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial system is in use, so no stage is set.
ZAF.summary: No stage is set. No source found from 2023 or later says the government's financial management system is in use. In the last twelve months, sources found named the Home Affairs revenue administration system and the SITA government network, and neither answers that. Preparing would need a source from 2023 or later that says the government budgets, accounts and pays through a computer system.

ZMB.short: Budget, tax and payroll systems were all in use by 2026; no source found says whether any was renewed or upgraded since 2023.
ZMB.summary: A May 2025 Zambia Revenue Authority presentation shows taxpayers filing returns on its TaxOnline system. The Auditor General's report on the 2024 accounts found the IFMIS, the government's financial system, without logs or offsite backup. In the last twelve months, the Auditor General's report on the 2025 accounts audits the PMEC civil-service payroll as a running SAP system, as at 31 August 2026. No source found says the financial, tax or payroll system went live on a new or upgraded system since October 2023. Operating would need one to do so in the last three years.

ZWE.short: Finance, tax and payroll in use, one renewed, and a map of government systems published by 2024.
ZWE.summary: ZIMRA said the final release of TaRMS went live on 1 October 2024, completing the system. The Public Service Commission said in March 2026 that the SPACE payroll system, in use since 1994, still runs government pay. In the last twelve months, its successor, GovPay, was being tested alongside it. The Auditor-General's report on the 2023 accounts describes the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) as the platform ministries use to process financial transactions. The e-Governance Academy says it completed a government enterprise architecture framework, plan and roadmap for Zimbabwe between September 2023 and September 2024.

AGO.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2025.
AGO.summary: SADC says 2025 trade and interbank transactions between Angola and the other 14 SADC states were about US$3.77 billion across nine currencies. South Africa took about US$2.99 billion. Angola takes part in the SADC-RTGS, the regional settlement system. In the last twelve months, SADC states that the Angolan kwanza was introduced as a settlement currency in the SADC-RTGS system on 27 July 2026. It is the second after the rand. On 8 September 2026 Banco Angolano de Investimentos and Bank of China's Luanda branch signed a memorandum to open a renminbi clearing account. Mercado gives no live date for the account.

BDI.short: A bank launched international transfers in 2025 and the central bank joined PAPSS; no source found reports figures for cross-border payments.
BDI.summary: On 1 August 2025 the Commercial Bank of Burundi, BANCOBU, launched instant international transfers on its eNoti platform. It is built with Thunes and reaches 48 countries. The central bank BRB has acceded to PAPSS, with four Burundian banks authorised to take part. In the last twelve months, EAC central bank governors decided in July 2026 that BurundiPay must connect to other member states' systems. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a figure from the past three years for payments through the country's corridors: volume, value or cost.

BEN.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2024.
BEN.summary: Benin had 8 million intra-UEMOA transfers worth CFA 230 billion in 2024, the BCEAO says. That is an average of CFA 5,172 a transfer. ARCEP Benin counted 2,512 million mobile financial service transactions in 2024. Of these, 0.5% were international transfers, Les 4 Vérités reports. Benin is a UEMOA member state on PI-SPI, the regional instant payment platform operated by BCEAO, with 80 participants connected on 2 April 2026. In the last twelve months, from 2 November 2026 MTN Mobile Money Benin customers can send and receive money through PI-SPI.

BFA.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2024.
BFA.summary: L'Oeil du Sahel cites BCEAO data for 2024. It puts intra-UEMOA transfers at 7.25% of the value of Burkina Faso's 20,139,735 million FCFA of e-money transactions that year. LeFaso.net reports that the BCEAO launched its PI-SPI instant payment platform on 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, as of 24 February 2026, nine institutions in Burkina Faso were authorised to offer services on the WAEMU-wide platform. LeFaso.net says 80 institutions were connected by 24 June 2026.

BWA.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
BWA.summary: Since May 2024 Revolut customers in the UK and most of Europe can send to Orange Money wallets in Botswana. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, PayInc's TCIB scheme went live into Botswana through First Capital Bank, which can receive money instantly from South Africa and Zimbabwe. On 17 November 2026 Stanbic Bank Botswana opened direct access to China's CIPS. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a figure from the past three years for payments through the country's corridors: volume, value or cost.

CAF.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
CAF.summary: AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY carried about 10 million transactions worth $657 million in 2022 across the six CEMAC states. The figure combines domestic and cross-border payments. In the last twelve months, Afreximbank's release of 9 July 2026 says BEAC has joined PAPSS, with CEMAC institutions to be onboarded through end-2026. GIMACPAY launched its interoperable QR Code standard on 29 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a figure from the past three years for payments through the country's corridors: volume, value or cost.

CIV.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2025; cross-border volumes are not reported.
CIV.summary: In August 2024 the BCEAO began piloting an instant payment system across the eight WAEMU states. The BCEAO launched PI-SPI, the regional instant payment platform, on 30 September 2025, with 80 institutions connected. In the last twelve months, SimoCash, an app launched in May 2026, is said to carry instant transfers between Cote d'Ivoire and five neighbours. In November 2026 Wave said its customers in Cote d'Ivoire can send and receive through PI-SPI. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a figure from the past three years for payments through the country's corridors: volume, value or cost.

CMR.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
CMR.summary: In October 2025 TechCabal said fintech REasy links local mobile money to Alipay, WeChat Pay and UnionPay. Cameroon is one of six CEMAC states on GIMACPAY, the regional payment platform. In the last twelve months, Nigerian fintech Grey has since September 2026 sent CFA francs to MTN and Orange mobile money wallets in Cameroon. On 29 July 2026 the central bank BEAC launched an interoperable QR code. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for Cameroon's own cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

COD.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was in service in 2025; no source found reports a regional payment system link.
COD.summary: An Orange Money RDC manager announced the launch of outbound international wallet-to-wallet transfers from the DRC in June 2025. They go to Congo-Brazzaville, Tanzania, Zambia, Senegal and Cote d'Ivoire. ITWeb reports that MTN's MoMo app opened a wallet corridor from South Africa to the Democratic Republic of Congo. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, TechAfrica News says Visa, M-PESA Africa and Onafriq are set to pilot stablecoins for cross-border mobile money transactions. DR Congo is the initial testing ground. No source found since October 2023 says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the country to take part in one in service.

COG.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
COG.summary: Since May 2024 Revolut customers in the UK and most of Europe can send to Airtel Money and MTN wallets in Congo. In June 2025 Airtel Money opened transfers to 31 more African countries, run over GIMAC Pay. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the central bank BEAC joined PAPSS, with CEMAC banks to be connected by the end of 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for Congo's own cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

COM.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was in service in 2024; no source found reports a regional payment system link.
COM.summary: On 21 February 2024 Mvola Comores launched transfers in from Orange Money Europe and Paysend, and out to Orange Senegal, La Gazette des Comores reports. In January 2025 MVola listed transfers out to Madagascar, Tanzania, Uganda, Cote d'Ivoire, Morocco, Guinea and Senegal. The central bank signed a PAPSS membership agreement in July 2024. Afreximbank says implementation began on 23 August 2024, with commercial banks still to integrate. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No live participation in PAPSS has been found. Operating would need the country to take part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.

CPV.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a cross-border digital payment channel, so no stage is set.
CPV.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether a cross-border digital payment channel is in service in Cape Verde. The only item found is Makeba. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no regulated cross-border digital payment channel exists in the country.

DJI.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
DJI.summary: D-Money (Djibouti Telecom) announced in a post of 29 July 2025 that its wallet now sends money abroad to 15 destinations. It works through Herman International Exchange. In June 2026 PAPSS lists Djibouti as a country with live send-and-receive participants: East African Bank and Salaam African Bank. In the last twelve months, IGAD issued terms of reference on 11 February 2026 for a consultant to develop a harmonised regional payment interoperability regulatory framework. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

DZA.short: Nothing found names a cross-border digital payment channel or says there is none, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a cross-border digital payment channel, or says there is none.

EGY.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2026.
EGY.summary: Youm7 cites the NTRA H1 2026 wallet report. Incoming transfers from abroad were 3% of wallet deposits by count and 10% by value. PAPSS chief executive Mike Ogbalu says PAPSS transaction volume rose about 1,000 percent in 2026 and value about 120 percent. Egypt is described as one of the largest economies in the PAPSS network, which the Central Bank of Egypt agreed to join in November 2024. In the last twelve months, Tech Africa News reports that Orange Egypt and UAE fintech Botim announced a corridor on 20 October 2026 for remittances into Orange Cash wallets.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a cross-border digital payment channel or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a cross-border digital payment channel, or says there is none.

ETH.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was in service in 2024; no source found reports a regional payment system link.
ETH.summary: Connecting Africa reports Safaricom extended M-Pesa Global to Ethiopia in October 2024, so that wallets in Kenya and Ethiopia can make cross-border transfers. Ethio telecom says its Visa Direct service lets Visa cardholders in over 190 countries send money to telebirr virtual cards. In the last twelve months, Afreximbank's release says Ethiopia has officially joined the PAPSS network. No source found says an Ethiopian institution is live on PAPSS or another regional system. Operating would need the country to take part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.

GAB.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
GAB.summary: ARCEP Gabon, citing the economy ministry, put mobile money transfers within the CEMAC zone at FCFA 1.489 billion in 2022, up from FCFA 0.894 billion in 2021. For 2024 the finance ministry recorded growth in these transfers of 53.8% in value and 88.8% in volume. In the last twelve months, on 29 July 2026 the central bank BEAC launched an interoperable QR code. GIMAC figures for the first half of 2026 rank Moov Gabon and Airtel Gabon as the network's top two issuers. No source found gives a value or volume for Gabon's own cross-border digital payments after 2022. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure.

GHA.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
GHA.summary: Since March 2026 a Nigerian payment service bank's Send to Ghana service, run over PAPSS, has carried money both ways between Nigeria and Ghana in local currencies. In the last twelve months, the Bank of Ghana said in October 2026 that PAPSS had reached mobile wallets on the Ghana-Nigeria corridor. It is piloting payments with Rwanda and Nigeria. Stanbic Bank Ghana offered direct yuan settlement through China's CIPS in August 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

GIN.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2024; cross-border volumes are not reported.
GIN.summary: UBA Guinée joined PAPSS on 9 September 2024, so its clients can make cross-border payments in local currencies. In January 2025 TechCrunch reported that Guinea-based Cauridor runs remittance corridors to Ghana and Nigeria. Cauridor told TechCrunch it processed $500 million in 2024 across all its payment rails. In the last twelve months, Ecobank's Guinean subsidiary has since March 2026 sent renminbi payments to China through a correspondent bank. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for Guinea's own corridors. Mature would need such a figure: volume, value or cost.

GMB.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2025.
GMB.summary: The IFAD PRIME Africa end-of-project profile (April 2026) reports US$135 million in remittances received digitally through APS. It gives an average APS remittance cost of 5 per cent across PRIME corridors. Africell says Afrimoney Gambia and Afrimoney Sierra Leone are directly connected. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 PAPSS listed Gambia as available for transfers through six live commercial banks. In June 2026 PAPSS lists Gambia as a country with live send-and-receive participants, seven banks in all.

GNB.short: Mobile wallets have received transfers from Europe since 2024 and the country is on the regional instant payment system; no source found reports payment figures.
GNB.summary: Since 28 May 2024 Revolut customers in the UK and most of Europe can send money to Orange Money and MTN wallets in Guinea-Bissau. Guinea-Bissau is part of PI-SPI, the WAEMU's regional instant payment system, in service since 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, five Guinea-Bissau institutions were authorised on PI-SPI at 31 July 2026. The BCEAO's list of September 2026 places it among the eight member states on the rail. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

GNQ.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
GNQ.summary: AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY carried about 10 million transactions worth $657 million in 2022 across the six CEMAC states. The figure combines domestic and cross-border payments. In the last twelve months, Afreximbank's release of 9 July 2026 says BEAC has joined PAPSS, with CEMAC institutions to be onboarded through end-2026. Diario Rombe reported in November 2026 that the Muni Dinero wallet, issued with BANGE, allows transfers within the CEMAC zone. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need such a figure from the past three years: volume, value or cost.

KEN.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
KEN.summary: Kenya is on PAPSS: the central bank joined in September 2023 and KCB went live in March 2025. Since October 2024 M-Pesa wallets in Kenya and Ethiopia can send to each other. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 I&M Bank customers gained PAPSS transfers in Kenyan shillings across participating markets. In November 2026 PesaLink's operator said it carries remittances into Kenya over PAPSS. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

LBR.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2024.
LBR.summary: The Central Bank of Liberia's Executive Governor said Liberia's cross-border transactions grew 17.7% in 2024, to $494.5 million. PAPSS transactions reached about L$37.7 million between June and December 2024. He said PAPSS was officially launched in Liberia on 27 March 2025. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 BnB Liberia and Orange Money Liberia launched a cross-border mobile remittance service to eight African countries. In November 2026 the Governor said Liberian traders' payments to Nigeria and Ghana are settled through PAPSS.

LBY.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
LBY.summary: In February 2026 the Central Bank of Libya's Circular 6 let licensed exchange companies send direct foreign remittances through a unified platform. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 the central bank and the People's Bank of China agreed that Libyan banks will join China's CIPS. No start date was given. In September 2026 Governor Naji Issa said the CIPS project had begun. A pilot is targeted for early 2027. No source found since October 2023 names a cross-border corridor in service from Libya. Establishing would need cross-border mobile money or digital remittances through a named corridor in service.

LSO.short: The country takes part in a regional payment system; in December 2025 Lesotho processed R30.57 billion through SADC-RTGS.
LSO.summary: In December 2025 Lesotho's five participants processed R30.57 billion through SADC-RTGS. That was third by value among the system's 15 countries. The South African Reserve Bank directive says Common Monetary Area low-value transfers, including Lesotho's, run through SADC-RTGS. They must move to the TCIB scheme by April 2027. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, Standard Bank says it has expanded access to China's CIPS to clients in Lesotho among others. In June 2026 TechCabal reports that Lesotho migrant workers in South Africa send money home through the fintech Mukuru.

MAR.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was in service in 2025; no source found reports a regional payment system link.
MAR.summary: In September 2025 Thunes said members of its Direct Global Network can make real-time cross-border payouts to bank accounts in Morocco, in dirhams. In October 2024 Tranglo said it launched real-time bank account transfers into Morocco in dirhams. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 PAPSS listed Morocco as a participant country 'live soon', not yet in service. No source found since October 2023 says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the country to take part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.

MDG.short: A cross-border digital payment corridor was in service in 2024; no source found reports a regional payment system link.
MDG.summary: In October 2023 MFS Africa went live with the MVola wallet, carrying remittances from Europe, the US and the UK. Since January 2024 Orange Money Europe users in six EU countries can send to MVola accounts. Since May 2024 Revolut customers in the UK and most of Europe can send to Orange Money and Airtel Money wallets in Madagascar. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says Madagascar takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system. Operating would need the country to take part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.

MLI.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2024.
MLI.summary: L'Oeil du Sahel cites BCEAO data for 2024. It puts intra-UEMOA transfers at 5.63% of the value of Mali's 18,744,827 million FCFA of e-money transactions that year. Mali is a UEMOA member covered by PI-SPI, the regional instant payment system in service since 30 September 2025. In the last twelve months, Mali has 12 institutions on the BCEAO list authorised to open PI-SPI, the UEMOA regional instant payment platform, to the public as of 2 April 2026.

MOZ.short: Cross-border digital payment volumes or costs were reported in 2026.
MOZ.summary: SARB's per-country table for June 2026 gives Mozambique 215 settled transactions, worth ZAR 261.79 million. In April 2024 ITWeb reported that MTN's MoMo app opened a wallet corridor from South Africa to Mozambique. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 Banco de Moçambique Governor Felisberto Navalha said Mozambique is finalising preparations to join the SADC RTGS. He expects Mozambique to be integrated in the first quarter of 2027.

MRT.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a cross-border digital payment channel, so no stage is set.
MRT.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether a cross-border digital payment channel is in service in Mauritania. No source found names a corridor, a licence, a pilot or a regional payment system for the country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no regulated cross-border digital payment channel exists in the country.

MUS.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2026; cross-border volumes are not reported.
MUS.summary: In July 2026 Governor Thakoor said MauCAS QR payments were interlinked with India's UPI. Bank of Mauritius Governor Thakoor says the bank is settlement bank for COMESA's REPSS. In the last twelve months, Mauritius Telecom CEO Veemal Gungadin announced the launch of cross-border payment capabilities between Mauritius and Seychelles at the AllMyT Summit in July 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

MWI.short: The country took part in a regional payment system in 2025; cross-border volumes are not reported.
MWI.summary: In April 2024 MTN's MoMo app opened a wallet corridor from South Africa to Malawi, ITWeb reported. Malawi takes part in COMESA's Digital Retail Payments Platform, described in October 2025 as the bloc's first interoperable cross-border payment system. In the last twelve months, nine Malawian institutions took part in SADC-RTGS in December 2025. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for cross-border digital payments. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives such a figure: volume, value or cost.

NAM.short: The country takes part in a regional payment system; in 2025 Namibian banks processed R708 billion through SADC-RTGS.

MLI.short: Mali's customs processed declarations in an automated system covering over 95 per cent of procedures in 2026; no source found reports a trade single window.
MLI.summary: Mali's Director-General of Customs said the move to SYDONIAWorld in 2015 built an integrated system that now covers over 95 percent of customs business procedures. ECOWAS says Mali was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system in July 2024. In the last twelve months, Ivorian and Malian customs teams met on 24-25 September 2026 to assess SIGMAT in its operating phase. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window joining customs with the other border agencies is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

MOZ.short: Customs clearance ran on an electronic system in 2025, with breakdowns and paper steps; no source found reports a single window joining other agencies.
MOZ.summary: In March 2024 the economy and finance minister told parliament that MCNET holds the concession for the single electronic customs clearance system. He said the Janela Unica Electronica has operated since 2010. In November 2025 the Centro de Integridade Pública reported frequent breakdowns and hybrid digital and paper procedures. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

MRT.short: An automated customs system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's 2026 customs guide says import and export declarations are registered and printed in SYDONIA World. The system also runs risk circuits, liquidation and payment receipts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 reports the system in use at a main port, airport or border post. Establishing would need customs declarations lodged and processed in an automated system at the main port, airport or border posts.

MUS.short: Customs declarations and a national single window were in use by 2023; no source found since then reports data exchange with another country.
MUS.summary: The Mauritius Revenue Authority's time release study of July 2023 says the TradeLink national single window was fully rolled out. Bills of entry lodged from 10 July to 6 August 2023 were processed in its Customs Management System. In the last twelve months, a WCO Smart Customs Project mission of 12-16 January 2026 found the authority hosts its Customs Management System on a private cloud. The system supports risk management. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data through a system open to its whole regional community. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

MWI.short: A trade single window joined customs and other agencies in 2025; no source found reports exchange open to the whole regional community.
MWI.summary: The Minister of Trade and Industry launched Malawi's National Single Window on 20 May 2025. It had seven MDAs at go-live. SATCP says the Malawi Revenue Authority is upgrading, testing and piloting ASYCUDA World from version 4.3.3 to 4.4.0. In the last twelve months, TradeMark Africa reported that the enhanced CCEDE has been live with the neighbouring authority since November 2025. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data through a system open to its whole regional community. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

NAM.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically in 2026; a single window is not on record.
NAM.summary: The Bank of Namibia says its Trade Verification System, live since 16 October 2023, is integrated with the Namibia Revenue Agency's ASYCUDA. In the last twelve months, NamRA upgraded and rolled out ASYCUDAWorld version 4.4.1 on 5 May 2026. Its notice of 1 April 2026 had moved the go-live from 1 April to 5 May 2026, for training and stakeholder readiness. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

NER.short: Niger's customs enters declarations in SYDONIA, the GUCE-Niger single window joins customs and ministries, and SIGMAT links it to ECOWAS.
NER.summary: ECOWAS says Niger was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system in July 2024. Webb Fontaine says the GUCE-Niger single window was launched in 2022. It connects customs, ministries and the chamber of commerce. The Minister of Economy and Finance said the virtual transaction dossier runs through GUCE-Niger, the foreign trade single window. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the customs director general said duty receipts are generated automatically in SYDONIA, the automated customs system.

NGA.short: A trade single window joined customs and other agencies in 2026; no source found reports electronic exchange with other countries.
NGA.summary: A March 2025 customs presentation lists ASYCUDA e-Declaration, e-Payment and NICIS II among digital systems introduced through 2022. In the last twelve months, Nigeria's National Single Window went live on 27 March 2026, with Customs, SON, NAFDAC, NAQS and NESREA fully integrated. It had processed over 124,614 licences and permits. Licensed customs agents dispute that it works. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data electronically with another country. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

RWA.short: Rwanda's customs runs on ASYCUDA World with an electronic single window, and the EAC platform links it to partners.
RWA.summary: In December 2024 the Rwanda Revenue Authority said Rwanda introduced ASYCUDA++ in 2004 and upgraded to ASYCUDA World in 2012. Its 2025 Tax Handbook says it facilitates trade through the Rwanda electronic Single Window. No change has been found in the last twelve months. TradeMark Africa reported that a revamped East African Community Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform was unveiled on 27 January 2025. It interconnects the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi.

SDN.short: A single window joining customs and other border agencies handled its first export in 2025; no source found reports exchange with neighbours.
SDN.summary: In October 2025 customs completed linking ASYCUDA with the civil registry through Baladna. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the government portal said the first export contract was completed fully electronically on the Baladna platform. The platform links trade, customs, standards, ports, border crossings, tax, Zakat and health clearances as a single window for foreign trade. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data through a system open to its whole regional community. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

SEN.short: A trade single window joined customs and clearance actors in 2024; no source found reports exchange open to the whole regional community.
SEN.summary: In June 2024 Senegal's customs director general said the GAINDE system had come into force that year at Rosso, Ziguinchor, Sénoba and Kaolack. GIE GAINDE 2000 marked 20 years of ORBUS, the single window for foreign-trade formalities. In the last twelve months, the Port Autonome de Dakar and the customs directorate announced a pilot from 2 January 2026 of electronic exchange of Bons à Délivrer. It runs via the electronic port single window. It followed a June 2025 data-exchange protocol with GAINDE 2000. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data through a system open to its whole regional community. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

SLE.short: A trade single window was in service in 2025; no source found reports exchange open to the whole regional community.
SLE.summary: The WTO says Sierra Leone introduced an Electronic Single Window in 2020. In November 2024 ECOWAS noted that SIGMAT, the regional transit data system, was being tested in Sierra Leone. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, a Gambian member of the ECOWAS Parliament listed Sierra Leone among the few countries implementing it. The delegation's vice chair urged Sierra Leone to advance its implementation. In January 2026 UNCTAD committed to speed up an upgrade of the ASYCUDA system. No source found says Sierra Leone exchanges transit data through SIGMAT in service. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

SOM.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically by 2022, a 2024 government plan says; a single window is not on record.
SOM.summary: The finance ministry's 2024 to 2027 customs strategic plan says Mogadishu Customs implemented SOMCAS in February 2022. SOMCAS runs alongside the current Port Customs Management Information System. In August 2025 the finance minister and the UK ambassador reviewed progress on digital customs systems at Mogadishu Port. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

SSD.short: An automated customs system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
SSD.summary: In September 2025 One Citizen Daily reported that the South Sudan Revenue Authority reviewed its E-Customs reform, which aims to digitise import-export procedures. The review notes strides in automating customs clearance, alongside limited infrastructure and staff capacity gaps. In the last twelve months, the trade minister and the revenue authority commissioner met on 5 January 2026 to coordinate a one-stop border post at Nimule. The four-year, USD 10.8 million EU-funded post combines customs automation and electronic clearance. No source found since October 2023 says customs declarations are processed in an automated system. Establishing would need customs declarations lodged and processed in an automated system at the main port, airport or border posts.

STP.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically in 2025; a single window is not on record.
STP.summary: The General Customs Authority officially launched Sydonia World 4.4.0 on 23 May 2025, across the whole national territory at once. UNCTAD's ASYCUDA Programme said the new version went live on 1 May 2025. It replaced ASYCUDAWorld 4.2, in use since 2011. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

SWZ.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically in 2026; a single window is not on record.
SWZ.summary: In a 3 February 2025 presentation, the Eswatini Revenue Service says customs declaration data is automatically exchanged with the South African Revenue Service. In the last twelve months, the service said customs payments made through FNB Eswatini now show almost instantly on ASYCUDA. It says the integration was completed on 12 June 2026. Trade Minister Manqoba Khumalo says a National Single Window System is under development to digitise customs procedures. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

SYC.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically in 2026; a single window is not on record.
SYC.summary: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement database record says the Seychelles Revenue Commission runs ASYCUDA World version 4.3.2, enhanced from September 2021 to May 2024 with express courier, manifest, excise bonded warehouse and tariff modules. In the last twelve months, the commission announced the first phase of the ASYCUDA World upgrade to version 4.4.1 for 13-14 March 2026. UNCTAD conducts it, adding trader self-assessment and paperless bill-of-entry processing. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

TCD.short: Customs declarations were processed electronically in 2026; a single window is not on record.
TCD.summary: The customs directorate says SYDONIA World was officially put into service on 15 October 2022, replacing SYDONIA++ in use since 2001. It says its SYDONIA World system processes declarations, with e-payment of all duties and taxes linked to it since 21 February 2024. The directorate opened an evaluation workshop for SYDONIA World on 22 April 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a trade single window is in service. Operating would need a trade single window in service, joining customs and other border agencies.

TGO.short: Togo's customs runs on SYDONIA, manifests pass through its foreign-trade single window, and SIGMAT links it to ECOWAS.
TGO.summary: ECOWAS says Togo was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system for its customs administration in July 2024. Customs directors general of the Sahel Confederation states and Togo reviewed the interconnection of their customs IT systems in Lome. The instruments for it were signed at Niamey on 23 July 2024. In the last twelve months, from December 2025, free-zone import manifests are processed through the foreign-trade single window, GUCE. An order of 14 October 2026 will replace GUCE and GUFORD with one port system, with no go-live date set.

TUN.short: An automated customs system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
TUN.summary: Decree 2023-160 of February 2023 created a finance-ministry unit to acquire, develop and put a new customs information system into operation. On 12 November 2025 customs spokesman Chokri Jarraya said the SINDA 2 customs system will be ready in 2026. He said its first applications would enter service at the end of 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says customs declarations are processed in an automated system. Establishing would need customs declarations lodged and processed in an automated system at the main port, airport or border posts.

TZA.short: Customs exchanged data with East African partners through a regional platform in 2025, and a single window joined the port and regulators.
TZA.summary: In early 2025 the ports authority said the Revenue Authority rolled out a new version of its customs system, TANCIS, with clearance requests filed online. TradeMark Africa says the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi are linked through the EAC Single Customs Territory platform. In December 2023 e-GA said the Tanzania Electronic Single Window System lets traders lodge data once for all border agencies. In the last twelve months, on 2 June 2026, the Revenue Authority launched the Zanzibar Single Window System. It brings several agencies under one gateway.

UGA.short: Customs has shared declarations with East African partners through a regional platform since 2024, beside a single window joining 22 agencies.
UGA.summary: Uganda's WTO notification of 12 June 2024 reports 22 of a target 45 agencies actively operational on the e-Single Window. TradeMark Africa reports that the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi are interconnected. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A KRA officer writing in WCO News says the EAC platform was built for six partner states. It has shared customs declarations and scanned-cargo images since July 2024.

ZAF.short: A national single window was being phased in with no completion date in 2026; no source found says whether declarations are processed electronically.
ZAF.summary: SARS says a new customs management system was fully operational from 18 August 2013 for all commercial cross-border trade. In September 2023 SARS implemented its Single Window electronic inspection workflow, which shares inspection cases with the Border Management Authority. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, SARS told Freight News that the National Single Window is being introduced in phases, with no completion date. No source found since October 2023 says customs declarations are processed electronically. Establishing would need customs declarations lodged and processed in an automated system at the main port, airport or border posts.

ZMB.short: A trade single window joined customs and other agencies in 2026; no source found reports exchange open to the whole regional community.
ZMB.summary: On 16 December 2025 ZRA, UNCTAD and TradeMark Africa signed an agreement for an 18-month, UK-funded project to upgrade and stabilise the ASYCUDAWorld customs system. In the last twelve months, on 19 October 2026 the authority outlined assessments, pilot testing and officer training. These are for its move to ASY5. No completion date was set. The authority says the Zambian Electronic Single Window has an enhanced e-bond module. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data through a system open to its whole regional community. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

ZWE.short: A trade single window joined customs and other agencies in 2025; no source found reports electronic exchange with other countries.
ZWE.summary: ZIMRA says the Zimbabwe Electronic Single Window was introduced in 2022 with UNCTAD support. Public Notice 77 of 2024 says it rolled out its Port Health and Radiation Protection Authority modules on 9 October 2024. ZIMRA is upgrading ASYCUDA from version 4.3.2 to 4.4.0 in phases, the first rolling out on 18 August 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says customs exchanges data electronically with another country. Mature would need customs to exchange data electronically through a system open to every country of its regional economic community.

AGO.short: Angola approved a national cybersecurity strategy by 2026; no source found reports an incident handled or public alert issued by a national body since October 2023.
AGO.summary: The Executive approved Angola's National Cybersecurity Strategy in 2025. In the last twelve months, Lei n.º 9/26 of 28 September 2026 set up a National Cybersecurity Centre, with CERT.ao as its operational arm. It requires operators of critical infrastructure and essential services to register with the Centre within 180 days. It also requires them to notify significant incidents to CERT.ao, with deadlines to be set by separate instrument. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

BDI.short: The country had a cybersecurity strategy by 2026; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
BDI.summary: Burundi's Council of Ministers adopted a National Cybersecurity Strategy on 14 October 2026. The Prime Minister's office records the same adoption in its communique of the meeting. In the last twelve months the strategy is new: the digital master plan reported in March 2026 that Burundi had no computer incident response team. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. No designation of critical information infrastructure has been found. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

BEN.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2025; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
BEN.summary: In October 2021 a decree's annexed policy said Benin had adopted its national digital security strategy. ASIN's director general says ASIN sets cybersecurity policies and runs an alert and incident response centre. ASIN presented Benin's first national report on cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents, covering 2021 to 2024. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 the digital minister cited the recent creation of a National Agency for Cybersecurity and Resilience. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

BFA.short: The national agency handled 79 major alerts in early 2025; no source found says whether critical information infrastructure is designated.
BFA.summary: In April 2025 the government put the security operations centre and response team of ANSSI, the national information systems security agency, into service. Its director-general says ANSSI treated 79 major alerts in the first half of 2025. In the last twelve months, the Council of Ministers appointed its director-general on 16 April 2026. No designation of critical information infrastructure or duty on operators to report incidents has been found. No figures after June 2025 have been found. Operating would need the country to designate its critical information infrastructure, or to bind the operators of critical systems to report incidents to the national body.

BWA.short: The national cyber body issued a public alert in 2026; no critical infrastructure designation is known.
BWA.summary: BOCRA's 2025 annual report says the national CSIRT sits within BOCRA. It was set up in 2020. In the last twelve months, the Botswana Computer Security Incident Response Team led the first National Cyber Drill in late February 2026. On 23 October 2026 the national CSIRT, through BOCRA, issued an urgent public advisory on the PHP2Shell flaws. It asked organisations to patch and to report compromise to it. No designation of critical information infrastructure has been found. Operating would need the country to designate its critical information infrastructure, or to bind the operators of critical systems to report incidents to the national body.

CAF.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2024; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
CAF.summary: A law of January 2024 created the Agence Nationale de la Cybersécurité, which appears in neither FY2026 budget volume. The network-security line is FCFA 4,000,000 (proposed, 2026). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. No designation of critical information infrastructure has been found, and no count of incidents handled. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

CIV.short: Critical information infrastructure designated by 2026; the national body publishes no recent account of incidents it dealt with that is known.
CIV.summary: Decree 2024-958 of 30 October 2024 created ANSSI, the national information systems security agency. It took over ARTCI's cybersecurity missions on 30 April 2025. Companies must by law report cyber incidents to ANSSI, with administrative sanctions for failing to. In the last twelve months, ANSSI ran CYBER.EX 2026, the first national cyber crisis exercise, on 28 and 29 October 2026. ANSSI states it recorded more than 12,100 cybercrime cases in 2024. No account of how it dealt with incidents in the past year has been found. Mature would need the national body to publish evidence of dealing with incidents, responding, containing or notifying and not only recording them, for a quarter or more ending within the past year.

CMR.short: The national cyber body responded to an incident or issued an alert in 2026; no critical infrastructure designation is known.
CMR.summary: ANTIC, the national ICT agency, runs Cameroon's national Computer Incident Response Team. In the last twelve months, the team received new equipment worth over FCFA 735 million on 20 January 2026. In March 2026 it went on site to a ransomware attack that took down half a public body's IT system. ANTIC says the law requires companies to report cybercrime to it. No designation of critical information infrastructure has been found. Operating would need the country to designate its critical information infrastructure, or to bind the operators of critical systems to report incidents to the national body.

COD.short: DR Congo set up a national cybersecurity agency by ordinance in May 2026; no source found reports an incident it handled or alert it issued.
COD.summary: Ordonnance n° 26/033 of 16 May 2026 tasks the Agence Nationale de Cybersécurité (ANCY) with setting up a national CERT. Article 4 requires public institutions and operators of vital importance to inform ANCY of all attacks and intrusions. In the last twelve months, the minister said in September 2026 that the agency had been created by presidential ordinance. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

COG.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2026; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
COG.summary: ANSSI of the Republic of the Congo is stated to have signed the AAECA-Net accession charter in Tunis on 26 June 2026. In the last twelve months, ANSSI held a working session in Brazzaville on 28 July 2026. It was to validate a draft qualification standard for cybersecurity audit providers. In November 2026 the minister said no public service goes live without the agency's approval. A national SOC and CERT are planned for 2027. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

COM.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2021; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
COM.summary: In 2021 Law 21-012/AU made the national digital development agency (ANADEN), through its cybersecurity directorate, the competent national cybersecurity authority. It oversees the security of information systems, networks and trust services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. No designation of critical information infrastructure has been found, and no count of incidents handled. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

CPV.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2025; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
CPV.summary: Ecofin Agency reports Cabo Verde launched a CSIRT within the State's Private Technological Network. It is described as a national cyber alert-and-response hub for public institutions and private organisations. The record states the national SOC and CSIRT were launched on 30 October 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

DJI.short: The country had a national cyber body by 2026; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
DJI.summary: The Minister Delegate for the Digital Economy said at the 3 September 2026 national AI forum that Djibouti has established a cyber security agency. The document gives no name for it. The same minister said Djibouti has adopted a national cyber security strategy running from 2024 to 2029. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.

DZA.short: The country had a cybersecurity strategy by 2026; no incident response by a national body is known since 2023.
DZA.summary: In September 2026 a national cybersecurity strategy was in force, and the Information Systems Security Agency oversees its implementation. The Agency, part of the Ministry of National Defence, is stated to exist and operate under a Director General. It is stated to have run the strategy's launch, including text messages to citizens via all mobile operators. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No incident handled or public alert issued by the national body has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need the national body to have handled a cyber incident or issued a public alert in the past three years.
