GHA.summary: In June 2022 Onix Accra 1 opened as Ghana's only Uptime-certified Tier IV data centre, and Onix says it sells cross connects and a meet-me room to business customers. In August 2024 NITA, the state IT agency, said its certified Tier 3 data centre serves all public institutions and private businesses. In October 2025 Digital Realty opened ACR2, a carrier-neutral data centre of 1.7 MW in Accra. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No global cloud region has been found. Mature would need a global cloud provider to sell its services from a cloud region in the country.

GIN.short: A data centre for hire at Tier III or above in service by 2025; no second one held.

COREX's deputy director-general said it is certified Tier 3 Design by the Uptime Institute, with Tier 3 construction certification still to come. The presidency's chief of cabinet said it is open to offering hosting services. GUILAB describes its operating data centre in Conakry as a colocation room serving telecom operators, ISPs and other customers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A second data centre for hire at Tier III or above has not been found. Operating would need two or more data centres for hire at Tier III or above.

The statement covers carrier-neutral facilities only. GAMTEL's service page says businesses and ISPs can rent space at any of its 43 sites to co-locate servers and networking hardware. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that a data centre for hire in The Gambia is Tier III or above. Establishing would need one data centre for hire at Tier III or above.

The TransSahara Tripoli Data Center sells colocation, and its operator says it is Tier III or above. In August 2024 Al Sabaah said the Libyan International Telecommunications Company's data centres had Uptime Institute Tier III certification. They are not said to rent space to others. No source found states that a data centre for hire in Lesotho is Tier III or above, and no global cloud region has been found. Establishing would need one data centre for hire at Tier III or above.

MAR.summary: Orange Maroc says its Casablanca data centre meets Tier III design and facility standards, and it hosts the AWS Wavelength zone. DXC Technology Morocco holds Uptime Institute Tier III certification for its built data centre, which serves customers. In 2025 Global Finance counted 23 data centres in Morocco. In the last twelve months, Oracle's public cloud region in Casablanca was announced as running on 7 April 2026. Oracle calls it the first hyperscaler region in North Africa, and it is preparing a second region at Settat.

STELLARIX offers colocation from two data centres in Antananarivo, advertised at 99.982% availability. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that a data centre for hire in Madagascar is Tier III or above, and no global cloud region has been found. Establishing would need one data centre for hire at Tier III or above.

The ministry says it gives administrations, companies and start-ups a hosting environment. In 2022 the ITU reported that the state company SMTD runs a government data centre offering colocation, IaaS and backup. In the last twelve months, SMTD-SA said in 2026 that it runs a public cloud with a self-service portal from Bamako. A second data centre for hire at Tier III or above has not been found. The state news agency AMI says it holds a Level 3 (Tier III) certification, and that it offers in-country cloud hosting and backup to public administrations, financial institutions and startups. The US Country Commercial Guide also states it is Tier III, with no certifier named. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The guidelines name POTRAZ as the body whose prior written approval is required for any exception to local hosting. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No approval granted or refused has been found, and no organisation ordered or penalised. Mature would need a dated source naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that moved data to comply.

AGO.short: Angola's authority, appointed in 2019, fined named companies in 2024, 2025 and 2026; no yearly count published by the authority itself is known.
AGO.summary: Lei 22/11 of 17 June 2011 created the Agência de Protecção de Dados. Decreto Presidencial 277/19 of 6 September 2019 appointed a president and two executive administrators. In the last twelve months it fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 on 10 August 2026. On 14 July 2026 it fined the Luanda water utility EPAL USD 150,000 over customer data. Its own register lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026, and PTI counts three of them in 2025. No count published by the authority itself has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2026 law creates an authority, but no appointment, ruling or published figure is known.
BDI.summary: The law adopted on 15 January 2026 creates an independent administrative authority responsible for enforcing data protection, and the law was promulgated on 10 March 2026. In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026, the Council of Ministers approved a draft decree on the agency's duties, membership and resources, subject to adjustments. No appointment to the agency has been found. No ruling against an organisation and no published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

BEN.short: Benin's data protection authority was sitting in 2026, with officers sworn in; no source found reports a ruling against a named organisation.
BEN.summary: Book V of the Digital Code, Articles 462 to 473, established the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles as an independent administrative authority. In the last twelve months, Decree 2026-422 of 1 July 2026 named its eight members, who were sworn in before the Supreme Court on 6 November 2026. Its 2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso has an authority, active in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known, and no figures it publishes are known.
BFA.summary: The 2021 data protection law creates the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) as the supervisory authority. It has nine members appointed by decree. In the last twelve months, on 3 August 2026 the legislative assembly adopted a bill merging the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD. A decree of 16 October 2026 named W. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo president of the merged regulator. On 19 November 2026 the Council of Ministers named the ten councillors of ARCOD's first college. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

BWA.short: Botswana has an authority, and in July 2026 it ruled against a government body; no figures it publishes are known.
BWA.summary: Botswana's Information and Data Protection Commission works under the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024. The Minister said it was established in 2022. Mmegi reported on 11 February 2026 that Kepaletswe Somolekae is the newly appointed commissioner. In the last twelve months, in a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM. DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic had no authority appointed in January 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
CAF.summary: Article 57 of Loi n° 24.001, promulgated in January 2024, gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set up the data protection agency. Data Protection Africa states that the authority has not yet been appointed, as of 28 January 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's data protection authority warned two named bodies with a formal notice in January 2024; no published count of its decisions is known.
CIV.summary: Law No. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 governs personal data protection. A decree of 4 February 2015 names ARTCI as the body that imposes withdrawals and fines under it. On 16 January 2024 the authority issued decision 2024-0996, a warning and formal notice to METFPA and Kaydan Groupe. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 Agence Ecofin reported 210 complaints and 18 inspections, and no financial sanction by ARTCI. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent period has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 law creates a data protection authority, yet to be set up in 2025; no ruling or published figures are known.
CMR.summary: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 sets up the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection. The law names no head or members. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the OBS-CC observatory said it was still not installed, and the decree to put it in place had not been taken. No source says the Authority's head or members have been appointed. No ruling and no published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

COD.short: The DRC's authority is not set up in 2026; the telecoms regulator does its work. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
COD.summary: Article 262 of the Digital Code of 13 March 2023 creates an independent Autorité de protection des données. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 gave its missions to the telecoms regulator ARPTC until it is set up. In the last twelve months, on 13 September 2026, Beto.cd reported that the authority is not installed. The ARPTC's decision of September 2025, published on 23 April 2026, sets the authorisations and declarations owed to it. No ruling against an organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

COG.short: Congo has had a data protection commission since January 2026; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
COG.summary: Congo's National Personal Data Protection Commission has members appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025. In the last twelve months, on 22 January 2026 the ICT minister installed the members and described the commission as able to advise, warn and sanction. That states a power, not its use. No ruling against an organisation has been found, nor any complaint count or annual report. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

COM.short: Comoros law creates a data protection authority, but it was not yet operating in 2024; no appointments, rulings or figures are known.
COM.summary: The 2014 data protection law institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés in Article 19, with nine members to be named by decree under Article 24. A 2025 review states that, as of 2024, the authority was not yet constituted or operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No appointment, ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde has an operating data protection commission in 2025, but no published figures; no ruling against an organisation is known.
CPV.summary: Cape Verde's National Data Protection Commission (CNPD) marked its tenth anniversary in March 2025 under its president, Faustino Varela. The Assembly's budget appropriates CVE 36,313,115 for 2025. In the last twelve months, on 23 February 2026 its head signed a joint statement with 60 other authorities. The same budget source says the CNPD published no activity report for any year since 2016. No ruling against an organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

DJI.short: Djibouti's 2025 Digital Code creates a data protection authority; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
DJI.summary: The National Assembly voted Djibouti's Digital Code on 30 June 2025, and Jones Day reports that the regime establishes the CNDP, the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. A review of 5 November 2025 describes it as independent with administrative and financial autonomy, and does not say it has been constituted or its members appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling by the commission and no published figures have been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

DZA.short: Algeria has a working authority with a named president in 2026; it has issued decisions but no ruling against an organisation or figures are known.
DZA.summary: Algeria's national data protection authority (ANPDP) enforces Law 18-07, and in July 2026 Samir Bourehil is named as its president. In the last twelve months it adopted a deliberation at its sitting of 15 July 2026, and on 11 November 2026 it announced Deliberation No. 05 on personal data in CVs. It also issued a decision in early 2026 on employee and candidate drug test results. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

EGY.short: Egypt has a data protection authority in 2026, still led by an acting chief; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
EGY.summary: Law 151 of 2020 created the Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC), and the executive regulations of November 2025 confirm it as the supervisory authority. An acting chief executive, Susan El-Okbawy, leads it, and ACTPOL states it had no board as of January 2026. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 it launched its electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications. The centre had published no decisions on its website when ACTPOL checked on 25 September 2026. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection authority and has issued no rulings or figures, as of 2026.
ERI.summary: Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. Levellers states that Eritrea has no data protection statute and has not appointed an authority, on a page reviewed on 8 June 2026. The Horn of Africa Initiative update of June 2025 says Eritrea remains without regulatory oversight for data protection. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

ETH.short: Ethiopia has an authority, the Communications Authority, in 2025. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
ETH.summary: The data protection proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator, in an overview of July 2024. By November 2025 Shega described the Authority as enforcing the law, and its Director General, Balcha Reba, said data processors and collectors now need its permission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling against a named organisation has been found, and no published count of decisions or complaints. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

GAB.short: Gabon has an authority and fined a bank 90 million FCFA in 2024. No published figures are known.
GAB.summary: Article 7 of Loi n°025/2023 creates the APDPVP as an independent administrative authority. By deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024 its plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 its president demanded the immediate suspension of a data-sharing operation, and on 4 September 2026 Joël Dominique Ledaga was still speaking as head of the authority. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

GHA.short: Ghana's data protection commission directed named unregistered companies to report to the police in October 2026; no source found reports yearly counts of its rulings.
GHA.summary: The Data Protection Commission describes itself as an independent statutory body established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). In the last twelve months, on 14 October 2026 it directed named companies to report to the police and regularise their registration. They included Polytex Ghana Limited, JA Biney Packaging and Menkish Impex Ltd. On 13 October 2026 it said it had registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026. No published count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 law provides for a data protection authority, but none is known to be in place, to have ruled, or to publish figures.
GIN.summary: The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law defines an Autorité de Protection and gives it functions covering declarations, authorisations, transfer approval and investigation. It names no constituted body or members. In June 2024 the National Transition Council's commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, with the designation of members still contested. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

GMB.short: The Gambia's 2025 law names the Information Commission as its data protection authority, which was acting by 2026; no ruling or published figure is known.
GMB.summary: The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 (Act No. 11 of 2025, assented 7 November 2025) names the Information Commission as the Commission. A review of 26 December 2025 describes it as an independent oversight Commission. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 a notice has it developing a communication strategy on the Act. No ruling or published figure from the Commission has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no ruling against an organisation and publishes no figures.
GNB.summary: A speaker said on 22 September 2026 that Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, and that several institutions handle these matters sector by sector. The Data Protection Africa factsheet, published 25 May 2022, states that the country has no data protection law and that its authority is not appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's 2016 law creates an authority, but by 2022 it was not appointed; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
GNQ.summary: Articles 15 and 29 of Law No. 1/2016, dated 22 July 2016, name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body. It is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure. Data Protection Africa, in a factsheet published 23 May 2022, states that the authority is not yet appointed or operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says whether its head or members have been appointed since 2022. No ruling or figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

KEN.short: Kenya's authority, set up in 2020, fines businesses and counts its decisions, most recently in November 2026; no yearly count is known.
KEN.summary: The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was set up under the Data Protection Act, 2019. Immaculate Kassait has been the first commissioner since 2020. Its own bulletin gives running totals to March 2025, with 7,128 complaints received and 215 determinations. In the last twelve months, on 4 December 2025 it ordered Platinum Credit to pay a complainant KES 400,000. In November 2026 Kassait said that over six years the office handled more than 13,000 complaints and issued 459 determinations. President Ruto nominated Lydia Sitienei to succeed her. No edition of the bulletin after March 2025 has been found.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2026 Act gives the work to an existing commissioner; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LBR.summary: Liberia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was printed on 23 March 2026. Sections 8 and 10 give data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner. The Freedom of Information Act of 2010 created that body. In February 2025 a minister told the Africa-China Reporting Project that Liberia had no national data protection authority. In the last twelve months, the Act was printed on 23 March 2026. Nothing found says the Commissioner has begun acting under it, or that any ruling or figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

LBY.short: SMEX said in July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority; no ruling or published figure is known.
LBY.summary: SMEX said on 22 July 2026 that Libya currently has no functioning data protection authority, in its review of the country's new artificial intelligence strategy. The statement describes the position at that date, so no authority can be counted as appointed and in office. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found names a body that was ever set up, and no ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2012 law creates a commission, unappointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LSO.summary: As at 31 October 2025 the law firm Z. Mayet and Associates states that the Commission and Commissioner mandated by the Data Protection Act had not been appointed. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 Cenfri said the Commission has remained unappointed, and Digital Rights Alliance Africa wrote that it had still not been established. Nothing found says the Commission or its Commissioner has since been appointed. No ruling or published figure has been found. Establishing would need the authority's head or members appointed, or an existing body given the job.

MAR.short: Morocco has an authority, the CNDP, active in 2026; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MAR.summary: Morocco's CNDP, the national commission for the control of personal data protection, works under Law 09-08 and was installed in 2010. In the last twelve months, on 28 November 2025 it validated five new deliberations, D-939 to D-943 of 2025. On 8 February 2026 it signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's authority, and in August 2026 it informed parties and citizens of the data rules for the 23 September 2026 elections. No ruling against a named organisation is on record. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

MDG.short: Madagascar's authority, the CMIL, was sworn in during 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known for 2026.
MDG.summary: Law 2014-038 provides for the CMIL: article 28 institutes an independent authority of nine members with regulatory and sanctioning powers. Seven members were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025. In the last twelve months, a government announcement of 27 March 2026 says the CMIL is now effectively in place, and its annual report, published January 2026, says no processing declaration has been registered. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

MLI.short: Mali has an authority, the APDP, which fined a clinic and published figures for 2025.
MLI.summary: Mali's APDP is an independent administrative authority of 15 members under Article 20 of Law 2013-015. Its 2025 annual report, summarised by Sahel Tribune, gives about 1,000 formal notices, fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints, 28 of them handled. The authority fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission. In the last twelve months, it opened a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025. It held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 with all commissioners present.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection authority yet; none has ruled against an organisation or published figures, as of 2025.
MOZ.summary: A UNECA inception report of June 2025 states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority. The World Bank restructuring paper says the Data Protection Office was not yet established as of October 2025. A September 2025 review says the draft law would give the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

MRT.short: Mauritania has a data protection authority, in session in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
MRT.summary: Article 64 of Law 2017-020 creates an independent Authority for Personal Data Protection attached to the Prime Minister. On 30 July 2025 it adopted deliberation 005/2025, a general rule and not a finding against an organisation. In the last twelve months, it held monthly meetings on 29 April 2026 and 30 June 2026, and its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

MUS.short: Mauritius's Data Protection Office was issuing guidance in 2026; no source found reports a ruling against a named organisation in the last three years.
MUS.summary: The Data Protection Office has operated since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. For January to December 2024 it reports 179 new complaints, 39 complaints closed, 105 personal data breaches notified and 112 cross-border transfers authorised. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 regulations on data protection officers gave the Office roles in receiving notifications, certifying officers and approving training institutions. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

MWI.short: Malawi's regulator MACRA has acted as its data protection authority since 2024; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MWI.summary: Section 4 of the Data Protection Act, 2024 designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority. The Act came into force on 3 June 2024. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 Daniel Chiwoni was named as its Head of Data Protection. On 11 November 2026 it held a validation workshop on proposed registration fees in Blantyre. No ruling against a named organisation has been found, and no published figures. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

NAM.short: Namibia has no data protection authority, a May 2026 source states, and the bill that would create one is not enacted.
NAM.summary: A governance professional wrote in The Namibian on 17 May 2026 that Namibia has no dedicated data protection authority and no comprehensive data protection law in force. A draft Data Protection Bill would create a supervisory authority, two analysts wrote in Technews in April 2025, and the 2020 draft bill names it the Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

NER.short: Niger abolished its data protection authority in June 2026 and repealed the law founding it; no source found says whether the ministries do the job.
NER.summary: Article 6 of Law 2022-59, as amended by Law 2023-31, created the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP). Its president took office on 18 September 2024. In the last twelve months, a presidential decree of 8 June 2026 abolished the HAPDP and ended its officials' functions. Its missions passed to the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. An ordonnance of the same day repealed the provisions of the 2022 law that founded it. Nothing found says those ministries supervise data protection. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a data protection commission that fined Multichoice 766 million naira in 2025; no yearly count of its rulings is known.
NGA.summary: The 2023 Data Protection Act created a formal Data Protection Commission, headed by National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji. On 18 February 2025 it issued a Final Order fining Meta $32.8 million. In 2025 it fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500. In the last twelve months, it issued a Notice of Investigation on 1 April 2026. In October 2026 Olatunji said it had investigated more than 240 breach cases and issued over 20 major remediation orders, giving no period. No count for a stated recent period has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

RWA.short: Rwanda's cyber security authority is its named data protection supervisor in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
RWA.summary: The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, an article of 26 January 2026 states. In December 2024 the East African Community said Rwanda is among five of its eight Partner States that had established dedicated data protection authorities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or fine against a named organisation has been found in the last three years. No count of complaints or decisions has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

SDN.short: A 2022 factsheet says Sudan has no data protection authority; nothing more recent is known, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. A factsheet last updated on 24 May 2022 says Sudan has no data protection authority appointed. No law found names an authority, and no source from the last three years says whether that still holds. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no data protection authority, and no law in force that names one.

SEN.short: Senegal has an authority, created in 2008. It has ruled against organisations, in 2024 and 2026, and publishes quarterly figures.
SEN.summary: Law no. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 set up the Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) as an independent administrative authority. In April 2024 its plenary served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it ordered a company to uninstall a meeting-room camera. It handled 317 files in January to March 2026 and 195 in April to June 2026. On 5 November 2026 it warned the public about scams using AI voice cloning.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no authority yet; one is named only in a 2025 bill. No rulings or figures are known.
SLE.summary: No stage is set. No law found names a data protection authority in Sierra Leone, and no source from the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in a bill of 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no data protection authority, and no law in force that names one.

SOM.short: Somalia has an authority, inaugurated in 2024. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
SOM.summary: Article 6 of the Data Protection Act establishes the Data Protection Authority as an independent agency, and it was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. In the last twelve months, by June 2026 it was accepting registration applications from controllers and processors. Its Registration Guidelines, version 1.0 of January 2026, set fees, a 30-day approval timeline and mandatory registration. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no rulings and published no figures.
SSD.summary: A 2022 factsheet stated that South Sudan had appointed no data protection authority and that no law established one. In December 2024 the Tanzania Times reported the East African Community as saying South Sudan was yet to form one. In February 2026 Digital Rights Frontlines said the country still lacks a fully operational, independent authority. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling or published figure has been found. Preparing would need a law that names a data protection authority.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe has had a data protection agency since at least 2022; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
STP.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe has a National Personal Data Protection Agency, the ANPDP, which the 2022 ALT Advisory factsheet says Law 03/2016 establishes, with an appointed head. In the last twelve months, on 1 June 2026 Macau's data protection office signed a cooperation memorandum with it. In 2026 Téla Nón described it as the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing. A 2024 International Bar Association chapter says the agency imposes fines, but names no sanction, decision or count. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a data protection authority and issued enforcement notices to three organisations in 2024 and 2025; no counts of decisions are known.
SWZ.summary: The Data Protection Act 2022 designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority, as an authority notice states. Its enforcement page lists enforcement notices issued in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited. It lists one issued in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. In the last twelve months, in early 2026 it issued a directive requiring controllers and processors to map their data by 31 March 2026. In September 2026 it ran an outreach campaign. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

SYC.short: Seychelles has an authority, active since 2023; no ruling against an organisation and no figures for its rulings are known.
SYC.summary: Section 5 of the Data Protection Act, 2023 names the Information Commission as the authority, and the Commission says it took on the mandate at the end of December 2023. Its 2025 annual report shows a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post. In the last twelve months, the National Assembly lists the 2025 report as published on 13 April 2026. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

TCD.short: Chad's data protection directorate had its director and deputy appointed by decree in June 2026; no rulings or figures are known.
TCD.summary: Decree 2011/PR/2026 of 1 June 2026 appointed a director, replacing a predecessor, and a deputy director of the Direction du contrôle et de la protection des données personnelles. The directorate is part of the Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Electronique (ANSICE). In the last twelve months, that decree filled its two senior posts. A July 2026 legal analysis states that Loi n°007/PR/2015 gives ANSICE the formalities for data transfers. No ruling, fine or order against a named organisation has been found. No count of decisions or complaints has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

TGO.short: Togo has an authority, active since 2024; no ruling against an organisation is known, and no figures it publishes are known.
TGO.summary: Article 55 of the 2019 data protection law creates a national authority, the IPDCP, which became operational in 2024 and launched its activities on 28 March 2025. In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026 it certified 28 correspondents, and on 2 and 3 October 2026 it hosted a delegation from Benin's authority in Lomé. It signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's authority on 23 September 2026. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

TUN.short: Tunisia has an authority, appointed in 2021, but a 2026 report says it is at a standstill; no ruling or figures are known.
TUN.summary: The 2004 organic law names a national authority for personal data protection, the Instance, and a government decree of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members for three years. A bill tabled in July 2025 provides for a new personal data protection authority. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the Forum Chawki Gaddes said the authority's activities are at a standstill and called for its reactivation. No renewal of the 2021 appointments, and no ruling or figures, have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

TZA.short: Tanzania has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against organisations in 2025; no published figures are known.
TZA.summary: Section 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. On 19 August 2025 it ruled against an Instagram business page that the report does not name. It also ruled in Abdul Said Naumanga v. Mi Casa Company Limited. In the last twelve months, Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026. It certifies data protection officers under a programme launched with the Open University of Tanzania on 14 July 2026. No count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

UGA.short: Uganda has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against Google in 2025 and WhatsApp in 2026; no published figures are known.
UGA.summary: On 18 July 2025 the Personal Data Protection Office, set up under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, found Google LLC in breach of its registration and transfer duties. It ordered Google to register within 30 days. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the director prosecuted a company's finance manager. On 20 February 2026 the Office issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine. In July 2026 it confirmed that WhatsApp had complied on time. No count of its decisions, fines or settled complaints has been found. Mature would need a count of its decisions, fines or complaints settled for a recent quarter or longer.

ZAF.short: South Africa has an authority that has fined and ruled against organisations since 2023, and it published complaint figures for 2024/25.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to enforce the data protection and access to information laws. National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for it for 2025/26. Its first fine, R5 million on the justice department, came in July 2023. In the last twelve months, the Polokwane High Court reduced its fine on Blouberg Local Municipality to R250,000 in April 2026. In October 2026 it fined Central Johannesburg TVET College R500,000 and First National Bank R1 million. On 11 September 2026 Parliament invited comment on candidates for its vacant positions.

ZMB.short: Zambia has an authority, in post in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZMB.summary: The Data Protection Commission of Zambia is treated as an existing body in a World Bank tender dated 10 August 2026, which describes it as conducting investigations, issuing determinations and enforcing the law. Its first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. In the last twelve months, the Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke on oversight and registration of data controllers in June 2026. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has an authority, acting in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZWE.summary: Section 5 of the Cyber and Data Protection Act makes the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (POTRAZ) the Data Protection Authority. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it said it had received 1,123 data controller licence applications that year. It issued Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 on compliance inspections, which start on 1 September 2026. On 23 October 2026 the ICT minister directed POTRAZ to investigate unlawful processing of personal information. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. Operating would need a decision, fine or order against a named organisation in the past three years.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 data protection law has regulations and its agency counts fines: three in 2025, six by August 2026; no source found dates the revision.
AGO.summary: Lei n.º 22/11 was published on 17 June 2011 and entered into force that day. The Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD) fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, USD 115,000 in kwanzas on 10 August 2026. PTI, citing the APD's register, counted three fines totalling USD 250,000 in 2025 and five totalling USD 600,000 in 2024. In the last twelve months, on 25 June 2026, the Assembleia Nacional rejected a UNITA bill to amend it. An APD administrator said on 17 June 2026 that the public consultation on a new law was complete. No count of the APD's fines for the whole of 2026 has been found, and no date for the revised law.

BDI.short: Burundi promulgated its first personal data protection law in March 2026; when it took effect, and any decision under it, are unknown.
BDI.summary: Burundi's National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026. The head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026. In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026, the Council of Ministers approved a draft decree on the agency's duties, membership and resources, subject to adjustments. No commencement date, regulation or decision under the law has been found, and no appointment to the authority it establishes. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

BEN.short: Benin's data protection law is in its 2018 digital code and was applied in 2025; no source found says how many regulations are in force.
BEN.summary: Benin's data protection rules are Book V of the Code du numérique, Law no. 2017-20, promulgated on 20 April 2018. La Nation reported the 2025 annual report of the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles (APDP): 907 files examined, 793 validated, 64 inspection missions and 20 complaints treated. In the last twelve months, Decree 2026-422 of 1 July 2026 appointed its eight members, who took office on 6 November 2026. On 11 November 2026 the APDP warned content creators that publishing identifying data needs consent. No source found states how many regulations are in force under the Code.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso has a 2021 data protection law and a new regulator named in 2026; no source found says whether any sanction has been imposed.
BFA.summary: Law n°001-2021/AN was adopted on 30 March 2021. It makes the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) the supervisory authority. On 26 June 2025 the CIL validated its public report for 2024. In the last twelve months, a law adopted on 3 August 2026 merges the CSC and the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD. On 19 November 2026 the Council of Ministers named the ten members of its first college. No regulation under the 2021 law and no named sanction has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

BWA.short: Botswana's Data Protection Act 2024, in force since January 2025, was applied in July 2026; no source found says whether regulations exist under it.
BWA.summary: Botswana's Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024) came into operation on 14 January 2025. In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the Information and Data Protection Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM. DPSM suspended the ePayslip portal on 22 July 2026. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the new commissioner vowed firmer enforcement against non-bank financial institutions. No regulation made under the Act has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled under the law, published for a period ending within the past two years.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic adopted a data protection law in 2024; when it took effect, and any regulation or decision under it, are unknown.
CAF.summary: Loi n° 24.001 on the protection of personal data was adopted in mid-January 2024 and promulgated. It provides for a data protection agency, with the ministry in charge of the digital economy holding its missions meanwhile. The World Bank reported in December 2024 that activities were planned to support drafting of the law's implementing decrees. In the last twelve months, on 28 January 2026 Data Protection Africa recorded the authority as not yet appointed. No regulation, decision or commencement date has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2013 data protection law is applied, with a formal notice to named controllers in 2024; no yearly count of decisions is known.
CIV.summary: Decree no. 2015-79 names ARTCI as the body that receives declarations and imposes fines under Law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013. On 16 January 2024 the authority warned the vocational training ministry and the company Kaydan Groupe and gave them formal notice. In the last twelve months, on 2 July 2026, ARTCI launched Certinum, an online platform for compliance and authorisation requests. The minister said a national register of data protection correspondents was set up in 2026. No yearly count of decisions has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 data protection law came into force in June 2026, with its authority not installed; no source found reports a decision under it.
CMR.summary: Cameroon's general law is Loi n° 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on the protection of personal data. In the last twelve months, the law came into force on 23 June 2026, the budget directorate reported on 6 July 2026. The OBS-CC observatory reported on 12 September 2026 that the authority had not yet been installed. It said the implementing decree under article 53 had not been taken. No decision, sanction or judgment applying the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

COD.short: The 2023 Digital Code, in force, covers personal data; a data protection officers' network launched in 2026; no source found reports any decision under it.
COD.summary: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Digital Code, sets the rules on the protection of personal data in its Book III. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally transferred the authority's missions to the telecommunications regulator. In the last twelve months, on 12 March 2026, the Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa. The regulator's decision no. 039/ARPTC/CLG/2025 on prior formalities was published in the Journal officiel of 23 April 2026. No decision or sanction under the Code has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

COG.short: Congo has a 2019 personal data protection law with a commission inaugurated in January 2026; no source found reports a decision under it.
COG.summary: Congo's general law is Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection. In the last twelve months, the Commission's members were appointed by decree of 31 December 2025. The same source, of 22 January 2026, reports that the National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated and elected its President, Vice President and Rapporteur. No regulation made under the law and no decision, sanction or count of complaints has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

COM.short: Comoros enacted a personal data protection law in 2021; no decision under it is on record, and no source found says it is in force.
COM.summary: The Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021. The law names a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés as the supervisory body, and as of mid-2024 the authority had not been formally constituted. In the last twelve months, ESCWA's profile of December 2025 said Comoros has no comprehensive data protection law in place. No source found says whether the law has commenced. No regulation or decision under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's data protection law is in force and its commission decided 297 requests in 2023; no source found reports a sanction.
CPV.summary: Law 133/V/2001 is Cabo Verde's general data protection regime. The CNPD says it was amended on 17 March 2021. The Comissão Nacional de Protecção de Dados (CNPD) report for 2023 counts 297 processes decided out of 326 requests, and seven complaints received. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the CNPD published an account of its eleven years. No change to the law has been found. No count of decisions for a year after 2023 has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

DJI.short: Djibouti enacted a data protection law in June 2025; when it took effect, and any decision under it, are unknown.
DJI.summary: The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code on 30 June 2025, with a data-protection regime embedded in it. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was enacted in June 2025. It describes the regime as creating the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No date of promulgation or commencement, no appointment to the commission and no decision under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

DZA.short: Algeria's 2018 data protection law has been in force since 2023 and its authority issues rules; no source found reports a sanction on a controller.
DZA.summary: Law n° 18-07 of 10 June 2018 came into force on 10 August 2023, the US International Trade Administration states. The Autorité nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel (ANPDP) adopted a deliberation on 15 July 2026 setting conditions for processing and publishing images of people. In the last twelve months, the authority decided in January or February 2026 that a positive or negative test result alone is standard health data. No decision or sanction on a named controller has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

EGY.short: Egypt's 2020 data protection law is in force and a court applied it in a 2025 damages judgment; no count of decisions is published.
EGY.summary: Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law, Law No. 151 of 2020, entered into force in October 2020, Shura Law Firm said. The Alexandria Economic Court ordered a telecoms operator to pay EGP 10 million in damages under the law, as reported in 2025. In the last twelve months, in early 2026, the Personal Data Protection Center published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing, officers, records and breach notices. Full enforcement began in early November 2026, after a transitional period to 31 October 2026. No count of cases settled has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection law as of 2026 and no supervisory authority; no source found says whether a bill is being drafted.
ERI.summary: Eritrea has no comprehensive data protection law in force, as of 1 August 2026, and no supervisory authority. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 placed the country at a nascent stage, without data protection legislation. In the last twelve months, the position was unchanged at 1 August 2026: no law, no regulator and no enforcement. No bill or draft of a data protection law has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law announced, being drafted, before parliament, or passed and not yet promulgated.

ETH.short: Ethiopia published a data protection proclamation in 2024 and its regulator approved about 10 data transfers by 2025; no source found reports decisions on controllers.
ETH.summary: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 was approved on 4 April 2024 and published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. It names the Ethiopian Communications Authority as regulator. In November 2025 the Director General said the Authority had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and approved them as a temporary measure. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No directive under the proclamation has been found as approved, and no sanction or order on a named controller. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

GAB.short: Gabon's 2023 data protection law is in force and its authority reported 12 sanctions in 2025.
GAB.summary: Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023 amended Gabon's data protection law. The authority's president said on 27 January 2026 that its 2025 review counts 12 administrative and pecuniary sanctions. In the last twelve months, on 20 January 2026, it supervised the destruction of the personal data of unsuccessful 2022 bidders. From 10 to 20 November 2026 it ran a campaign in Port-Gentil briefing administrations and businesses on their duties. Whether any regulations have been issued under the law has not been found.

GHA.short: Ghana's 2012 Data Protection Act was applied by a court in 2024 and against named companies in 2026; no source found reports regulations under it.
GHA.summary: On 18 September 2024 a circuit court in Accra found Bolt Holdings OU in breach of sections 20, 21, 28 and 30 of the Data Protection Act, 2012. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the Commission announced that 2026 would be a year of enforcement. On 14 October 2026 it cited six named companies for operating unregistered or with expired certificates. No regulation made under the Act has been found. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled in a year has been found. Mature would need such a count, published for a recent period.

GIN.short: Guinea has a 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, said in 2025 to be in place; no decision under it is on record.
GIN.summary: Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Condé in 2016. In October 2025 the ministry's secretary-general said Guinea has put in place the law. The ministry's report on its 2025 work says texts on personal data protection are in progress, with no stage or date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation, decision or constituted authority has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

GMB.short: The Gambia enacted its first general data protection law in 2025; no source found gives its commencement date or reports a decision under it.
GMB.summary: President Barrow assented to the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act on 7 November 2025. In the last twelve months, on 13 May 2026, the minister said the country already has the law in place, with oversight given to the Access to Information Authority's commissioners. In November 2026 GIZ described the Information Commission, with Commissioner Ya Amie Touray in post, as the body enforcing data protection. No commencement date has been found, and no decision, sanction or count of complaints under the Act. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law; the cabinet approved a bill with amendments in May 2026, and no source found says it has reached parliament.
GNB.summary: The government's February 2025 report to the Universal Periodic Review lists a data protection bill among several awaiting discussion in the National People's Assembly. In the last twelve months, on 8 May 2026, the Council of Ministers approved the Data Protection Law with amendments. On 22 September 2026 a law professor said the country does not yet have specific data protection legislation. No source found says the bill has gone to the Assembly. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force, whether it stands alone or is part of a larger law.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea has had a personal data protection law since 2016; whether it has been applied, or its supervisory body created, is unknown.
GNQ.summary: Ley Núm. 1/2016, de Protección de Datos Personales, was sanctioned and promulgated by the President on 22 July 2016. It names the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, to be created by a decree. It places the power to sanction with the Minister of Telecommunications and New Technologies. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated after 22 July 2016. No decree creating the Órgano Rector, regulation or decision has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2019 Data Protection Act is in force and its commissioner issued 51 determinations in 2024; no later yearly count is known.
KEN.summary: The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019. An April 2025 analysis counted 51 determinations by the office in 2024. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, it ordered St Luke's Orthopaedic Hospital to compensate patients and an events company to pay KES 300,000, according to Amnesty Kenya. In November 2026 the High Court set aside a KSh1.25 million award by the office. The same month a successor to the first commissioner was nominated. No yearly count after 2024 has been found.

LBR.short: Liberia approved a data protection act in March 2026; it has no recorded decision, and no source found says whether the Commissioner has begun acting.
LBR.summary: Liberia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. In the last twelve months, President Boakai's promulgation of the law was announced on 19 August 2026. The House of Representatives had referred the President's bill to committee on 10 June 2025. No regulation, decision or sanction under the Act has been found, and no source says the Independent Information Commissioner has begun acting under it. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

LBY.short: Libya's government was drafting a data protection law as of July 2026, with adoption targeted for 2026; no bill before parliament is known.
LBY.summary: SMEX reported on 22 July 2026 that Libya's data protection law remains in draft, with adoption targeted for 2026. In January 2024 the General Information Authority reported a committee drafting a national personal data protection law. In the last twelve months, on 26 October 2026, the National Council and a House of Representatives committee began a joint review of the council's draft. No source found says a government bill has been tabled. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force, whether it stands alone or is part of a larger law.

LSO.short: Lesotho has a Data Protection Act of 2011 with no commission appointed; no source found says whether it has ever been applied or has regulations.
LSO.summary: Cenfri's article of 23 March 2026 says the Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade. It dates the Act to 2011. It also says that the Data Protection Commission has remained unappointed, and gives no date for that position beyond its own publication. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation made under the Act and no decision applying it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2009 data protection law is in force and courts decided 80 criminal data protection cases in 2024.
MAR.summary: The CNDP, the commission that supervises Morocco's Law 09-08 on personal data, was installed in 2010. Moroccan courts handled 153 personal data cases in 2024, and of 109 criminal cases 80 were decided. In the last twelve months the CNDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's data protection authority on 8 February 2026. Its president said on 4 August 2026 that a recast of the law has been sent to the Secrétariat général du gouvernement. No regulation under Law 09-08 has been found, and no sanction by the CNDP on a named controller.

MDG.short: Madagascar has a data protection law of 2015 and an authority seated in 2025; no source found says whether the law has been applied.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 9 January 2015. Its authority, the CMIL, elected a president and two vice-presidents on 14 August 2025. In the last twelve months the commission approved its first procedures manual on 17 October 2025. It also joined the AFAPDP on 24 November 2025 and obtained a budget line of Ariary 2,411,579,000 in the 2026 Finance Law. No decision, sanction or count of cases under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

MLI.short: Mali has a 2013 data protection law, applied by its authority with fines and complaints handled in 2025; no source found gives its commencement date.
MLI.summary: Mali's Law no. 2013-015 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 21 May 2013. For 2025 the APDP's annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, counts fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints received. In the last twelve months the APDP opened an extraordinary session on 6 October 2025 to review about 2,000 files and opened a regional office at Ségou on 4 December 2025. Its session of 3 August 2026 had over 1,000 files to examine. No commencement date for the law has been found, and no figure for sanctions issued in 2026.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection law; its bill was on parliament's agenda in October 2026, and no source found says when it will pass.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique has no data protection law. In April 2026 the ministry said the government had approved the bill and sent it to the Assembly of the Republic. On 26 October 2026 the Assembly set the plenary debate for 6 November 2026. In the last twelve months, in October 2025 the bill had not been approved by Cabinet or sent to Parliament, and on 25 August 2026 the head of INTIC said the authorities were preparing to submit it. No source found says when the bill reached parliament. No data protection authority exists. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

MRT.short: Mauritania's 2017 data protection law is applied by its authority through opinions and rules; no source found says whether any controller has been sanctioned.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's Law 2017-020 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 22 July 2017. Its authority, the APD, issued deliberations 004/2025 of 14 July 2025 and 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 on transfers and cloud services abroad. On 19 November 2025 the APD approved a control reference framework and empowered its sworn agents to take part in inspection missions. In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026, it approved amendments to those two deliberations and discussed complaints 008-2025 and 001-2026. No sanction, order or decision on a named controller has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

MUS.short: Mauritius has the Data Protection Act 2017, and its office reported complaints closed and transfers decided in 2024; no source found reports figures for 2025.
MUS.summary: Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017 came into force on 15 January 2018. For 2024 the Data Protection Office reports 179 new complaints and 39 closed, with 105 breaches notified and 112 cross-border transfers authorised. In the last twelve months, on 17 June 2026, the Minister made regulations requiring every controller to designate a data protection officer, from 1 January 2027. In May 2026 the Commissioner said amendments to bring in administrative fines are being introduced. No figures for 2025 have been found.

MWI.short: Malawi's Data Protection Act of 2024 is in force and applied through guidance only; no source found reports a decision or sanction under it.
MWI.summary: Malawi's Data Protection Act, 2024 was passed on 7 December 2023, assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority published a compliance guideline and checklist on 17 October 2025. Breach notification guidelines followed on 22 October 2025, setting a 72-hour notice. In the last twelve months, on 13 July 2026, MACRA consulted stakeholders in Blantyre on draft regulations carrying annual registration fees. No decision or sanction under the Act has been found, and no regulation in force. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

NAM.short: Namibia has no data protection law; a cabinet committee approved the bill in 2026, and no source found says when it reaches Parliament.
NAM.summary: Namibia has no data protection law, and on 13 July 2026 the ICT minister, Emma Theofelus, said that Namibia was finalising the bill. In the last twelve months the position moved. In August 2025 the minister said the bill would be tabled in September 2025. In January 2026 she said it was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation. The 2026/27 budget estimates say the committee approved it and sent it to the justice ministry. No source found says the bill has been tabled in Parliament, passed or enacted. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

NER.short: Niger's 2022 data protection law is in force, with compliance files and inspections in 2025; no source found reports a decision under it.
NER.summary: Niger's Law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection is the general law. In July 2025 the president of the HAPDP, the authority it created, said it had processed 139 compliance files since September 2024. In the last twelve months, on 13 June 2026, Africa Data Protection reported that the government had abolished the HAPDP by decree. The government's communiqué confirms the decree of 8 June 2026. No regulation made under the law and no decision under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

NGA.short: Nigeria's Data Protection Act of 2023 is in force and applied through fines and court orders; no source found counts decisions since mid-2024.
NGA.summary: President Tinubu signed the Nigeria Data Protection Act on 12 June 2023. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in July 2025. A Commission order fining Meta $32.8 million was set aside by consent judgment on 3 November 2025. In the last twelve months, on 29 July 2026, a court ordered Stanbic IBTC Bank to pay two former customers N15 million and erase their data. On 28 July 2026 the Commission directed unregistered major controllers and processors to register. In October 2026 its chief cited over 20 remediation orders, giving no period. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2021 Data Protection Act is in force and the authority registers and trains controllers; whether any sanction or decision has been made is unknown.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021. Its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023. By January 2026 the National Cyber Security Authority had registered data controllers and processors. It also trained over 100 Data Protection Officers in the public sector. In the last twelve months the authority chose a theme for Data Privacy Week, 26 to 30 January 2026, and now expects controllers to prove that they comply. No dated sanction or decision under the Act has been found. No source says whether regulations are issued. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

SDN.short: Sudan's cabinet approved a data and artificial intelligence bill in November 2026, with no law yet to apply; no source found reports the bill's content.
SDN.summary: Sudan has no data protection law, and on 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed the draft data and artificial intelligence bill and directed further study. In the last twelve months the cabinet approved the bill on 1 November 2026. Its text has not been published, and no vote by the interim parliament has been found. In July 2026 an analyst wrote that no independent body oversees data protection. No regulations and no decisions have been found. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2008 data protection law is in force and its authority publishes quarterly counts of decisions, most recently July to September 2026.
SEN.summary: Senegal's Law no. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008. For July to September 2026 the CDP reported 214 files handled, examined 13 complaints and carried out five inspections. For April to June 2026 it reported 195 files handled. In the last twelve months the CDP relaunched the updating of the law at a two-day workshop at Saly, reported in July 2026. In March 2026 an expert said a bill was reported to be in the circuit. Whether any regulation is in force under the law has not been found.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no data protection law; its bill passed second reading in November 2026 and is in committee; no source found reports its passage date.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone has no data protection law, and on 12 November 2026 the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill passed its second reading and was committed to the Legislative Committee. In the last twelve months the Bill moved from final national validation in November 2025 to Cabinet approval on 21 April 2026. In November 2026 it was tabled in Parliament and read a first time. No law is enacted, and no regulations or decisions have been found. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 data protection law is in force and its authority opened registration in 2026; no source found says whether any decision or sanction followed.
SOM.summary: Somalia's Law No. 005 of 2023, the Data Protection Act, was ratified by both chambers of parliament, and the President signed it in March 2023. The Authority was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. In the last twelve months the Regulatory Framework was approved after the Ministry of Communications and Technology said it had cleared constitutional, legal and technical procedures, reported on 6 February 2026. The Authority opened registration of controllers and processors, reported on 2 June 2026. No named and dated decision, sanction or order under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection law; a bill was still being prepared in September 2026, and no source found says it has reached parliament.
SSD.summary: South Sudan has no data protection law, and the World Bank's identity diagnostic of 1 May 2026 says the country has no national data protection or privacy law. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the ICT minister said the bill would be introduced in 2026. A workshop of over 30 people to validate it was reported on 5 May 2026. On 8 September 2026 the ICT ministry's undersecretary said the bill was still in preparation. No bill tabled in parliament has been found, and no regulation or decision. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe enacted a data protection law in 2016; no source found reports a decision or regulations under it.
STP.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's Lei n.º 03/2016 on the protection of personal data was published on 10 May 2016. In January 2026 the director of its data protection agency, the ANPDP, said it would publish a list of non-compliant bodies and apply fines. In the last twelve months, on 1 June 2026, the ANPDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau's data protection office. No regulation made under the law has been found. No named sanction, decision or count under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a Data Protection Act of 2022, applied through enforcement notices in 2024 and 2025; no source found reports the number of decisions made.
SWZ.summary: Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022 was assented to and gazetted on 4 March 2022. The Authority lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act, issued to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited in June 2024 and to the Royal Science Technology Park in March 2025. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs. In September 2026 it was setting up information desks in major towns. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated year has been found. Mature would need that count published for a period ending within the past two years.

SYC.short: Seychelles' Data Protection Act 2023 is in force and its commission handled 14 cases in 2025; no yearly count of decisions is published.
SYC.summary: Seychelles' Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023. The Information Commission received four data protection cases in 2024 and 14 in 2025. In the last twelve months the National Assembly lists the Commission's annual report for 2025 as published on 13 April 2026. In it the Chief Commissioner states that the Act remains at risk of being largely unenforced because the one budgeted technical post is unfilled. No yearly count of cases settled has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

TCD.short: In 2026 Chad's 2015 personal data law is treated as in force, with a replacement being drafted; no decision under it is known.
TCD.summary: A July 2026 analysis by the law firm Cabinet Thomas Dingamgoto applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data and treats its articles 29 to 32 as the transfer rules in force. Transfers abroad need notification to or prior authorisation from ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification. The analysis says how far the agency acts on this is not documented. In the last twelve months the minister said on 9 December 2025 that authorities were finalising a digital law. On 27 April 2026 the minister installed a committee of 34 members to propose modernised digital texts. No regulation, decision or sanction under the 2015 law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

TGO.short: Togo has a 2019 data protection law; its authority trained correspondents in 2026, but no source found says whether any sanction has been issued.
TGO.summary: Togo's Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the protection of personal data was adopted and promulgated. Its authority, the Instance de protection des données à caractère personnel (IPDCP), officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025.
