In the last twelve months it signed a cooperation memorandum with the broadcast regulator HAAC on 10 December 2025. On 18 November 2026 it certified its first 28 correspondents for three years. No regulation made under the law has been found, and no named sanction or decision under it. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 2004 data protection law is in force and a replacement has been before parliament since 2025; no source found says the law is applied.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's organic law 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 sets the rules for processing, consent and rights, and was still in force in September 2026. In February 2026 a health ministry official told the Assembly that its authority, the INPDP, has ceased its activities since 2024. In the last twelve months the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee heard the sponsors of a replacement bill on 17 February 2026. The bill, 95/2025, went before the Assembly on 14 July 2025. No dated sanction, decision or count under the 2004 law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act 2022, in force since 2023, was applied in a 2025 ruling; no source found counts its decisions.
TZA.summary: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Chapter 44) commenced on 1 May 2023. On 19 August 2025 the Commission ruled in Complaint No. PDPC/CMP/002/2025 against the operator of an Instagram business page, awarding damages of TZS 20 million and a fine of TZS 5 million. In the last twelve months, on 8 January 2026, the Minister gave unregistered institutions a final three months to register. On-site inspections began on 31 August. No published count of the Commission's decisions for a stated year has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

UGA.short: Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act is in force and was applied in decisions of 2025 and 2026; no source found reports yearly decision counts.
UGA.summary: On 18 July 2025 Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office found Google LLC in breach of the Act and ordered it to register within 30 days. On 20 February 2026 it issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine. In the last twelve months, on 3 December 2025, a magistrate fined the finance manager of Vuka Africa Ltd sh100,000 for failing to register with the office. In August 2026 its director said 14,697 of an estimated 50,000 entities required to register had done so. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated period has been found. Mature would need that count published for a period ending within the past two years.

ZAF.short: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 has been in force since 2021 and is applied; no source found reports the planned amendment's text.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act of 2013 has been in force since 1 July 2021. In 2024/25 the Information Regulator received 1,355 complaints under it and resolved 745. In the last twelve months, regulations on health information were published on 6 March 2026. On 26 October 2026 the Regulator fined Central Johannesburg TVET College R500,000 and First National Bank R1 million. On 18 August 2026 a commissioner said work is under way to amend the Act. No bill or draft of the amendment has been found.

ZMB.short: Zambia's Data Protection Act of 2021 is in force, applied so far through registration and training; no source found reports a decision under it.
ZMB.summary: Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 is named in a tender of 10 August 2026 as the Act being implemented. Data controllers and processors had until 30 April 2025 to register under the Act. On 7 June 2026 Lusaka Star reported that enforcement and compliance remained a challenge. In the last twelve months the same tender seeks consultants to help the Commission develop regulatory instruments for implementing the Act. On 19 November 2026 the minister, Felix Mutati, said the government is reviewing the data protection framework towards a Data Management Act. No regulation made under the Act has been found, and no decision under it. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 2021 data protection law has regulations and its regulator had resolved 15 complaints by October 2025; no source found gives a yearly count.
ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act, No. 5 of 2021, was gazetted on 11 March 2022. By October 2025 POTRAZ had received 20 formal complaints and investigated and resolved 15. By November 2026 it had issued over 195 enforcement notices and licensed over 2,500 controllers. In the last twelve months, Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026, published in July 2026, announced mandatory compliance inspections of data controllers from 1 September 2026. No count of decisions for a stated year has been found, and no named sanction. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

AGO.short: Law in force since 2011; the authority is appointed and working, and fined a hotel company in August 2026.
AGO.summary: Angola's Lei n.º 22/11 on personal data protection was published on 17 June 2011. The Agência de Protecção de Dados was set up by Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16. In June 2026 the Assembleia Nacional rejected a bill to amend the law. Its register of fines lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026. In the last twelve months, on 10 August 2026 the authority fined Lizária, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 under Deliberação n.º 006/2026.

BDI.short: A law was promulgated in March 2026; no source found says whether it is in force, nor an appointed authority or any ruling.
BDI.summary: Burundi's National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026. In the last twelve months the position changed from DLA Piper's guide of 17 January 2024, which described only sector confidentiality provisions and no national authority. Community Voice reports that the head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026. The law establishes an independent administrative authority. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature of the Malabo Convention. No source has been found saying the law is in force or the authority constituted. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

BEN.short: Law in force since 2018; the authority published figures for its decisions in 2025. No source found reports A ruling against a named organisation.
BEN.summary: Benin's personal data protection sits in Book V of the Digital Code, law no. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, amended by law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021. Benin ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 May 2024. The APDP's 2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

BFA.short: Law in force since 2021; authority working, its merged successor given a president in October 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
BFA.summary: Law no. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 abrogates law no. 010-2004/AN on personal data protection in Burkina Faso. In the last twelve months, on 3 August 2026 deputies adopted the law creating ARCOD, which merges the CIL and the CSC. By decree of 16 October 2026 the CSC's president, Wendingoudi Louis Modeste Ouedraogo, was named president of ARCOD. On 19 November 2026 the government named the ten councillors of its first college. No act of ARCOD has been found, and no ruling against a named organisation in the last three years. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

BWA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2025, the commission is working, and it ruled against an organisation in 2026.
BWA.summary: Botswana's Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024 came into operation on 14 January 2025. In the last twelve months, Mmegi reports Kepaletswe Somolekae as the newly appointed Information and Data Protection Commissioner on 11 February 2026. On 17 July 2026 the Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM. It ordered the ePayslip portal suspended and a DPIA and revised privacy notice submitted within one month. Mmegi reports DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

CAF.short: A data protection law is in force, but no authority is appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation, as of 2026.
CAF.summary: Data Protection Africa states in its factsheet of 28 January 2026 that the Central African Republic has a data protection law in place. The promulgated text of Loi n° 24.001 was adopted in January 2024 and gives no commencement date. Article 57 gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy a set period to set up the data protection agency. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found saying the Malabo Convention is signed or ratified, or that an authority has been appointed. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

CIV.short: A data protection law is in force and its authority is working, but no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
CIV.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's law of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection is the framework for a 2015 decree on filing fees and prior authorisations. In the last twelve months, ARTCI launched Certinum on 2 July 2026, an online platform for compliance and authorisation requests. It replaces about 100 paper files a month. ARTCI issued a communique on 3 August 2026 inviting controllers to use it. By then it had received 210 complaints and carried out 18 inspections. No ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

CMR.short: A data protection law came into force in 2026, but no authority is appointed, so no ruling against an organisation is known.
CMR.summary: Cameroon's Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 governs personal data protection. The Direction Generale du Budget states that its deadline for entry into force was reached on 23 June 2026. The law makes the Autorité an independent public body with supervision and enforcement powers. In the last twelve months, on 29 October 2026 CLG Global said it was not yet operational. It awaited a presidential decree, with no head or members appointed. The African Union Commission's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Cameroon signed the Convention on 12 August 2021. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

COD.short: The telecoms regulator has acted as data protection authority since 2023 and set declaration rules in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
COD.summary: DR Congo's Digital Code, Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023, entered into force in 2023 and provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 gave the authority's missions to the telecoms regulator, ARPTC, until the authority is set up. In the last twelve months, the ARPTC's decision on prior formalities under the Code was published in the Journal officiel on 23 April 2026. It sets how organisations declare their processing. Beto.cd reported on 13 September 2026 that the Autorité itself is not installed. No ruling by the ARPTC against a named organisation has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

COG.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority was appointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
COG.summary: Congo's Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection is in force as of 22 January 2026. In the last twelve months, the National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated in January 2026 when its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025. On 22 January 2026 ITWeb Africa reported that ICT minister Leon Juste Ibombo installed its members. No source dated in the last three years has been found. None shows it registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has done one of those things in the past three years.

COM.short: Comoros passed a data protection law in 2021; no source found says it is in force, and no appointed authority or ruling is known.
COM.summary: TechHive Advisory states the Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021. The Assembly adopted Loi n°14-029/AU on personal data protection on 26 June 2014. Article 19 of the 2014 law institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, and TechHive says the authority had not been formally constituted as of mid-2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found showing that the law has commenced, or that the authority has been constituted since. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

CPV.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is working in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
CPV.summary: The CNPD president says the base data protection law of Cabo Verde dates from 2001. It was amended in 2013 and again on 17 March 2021. The CNPD's members took office on 24 April 2015. Resolução n.º 160/X/2024 gives it CVE 36,313,115 for 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

DJI.short: A data protection law was passed in 2025 but is not in force; no authority is appointed or has ruled against an organisation.
DJI.summary: The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code, with a data-protection regime embedded in it, on 30 June 2025. It was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. The Code creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. On 9 November 2023 the Assembly adopted law 18/AN/23 ratifying the Convention, but the African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records only a signature. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found giving when the Code was promulgated or took effect. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

DZA.short: The law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is reported.
DZA.summary: The US International Trade Administration states that Algeria's Law No. 18-07, enacted on 10 June 2018, came into force on 10 August 2023. In the last twelve months, the national authority, the ANPDP, adopted a deliberation on 15 July 2026, with twelve members named. On 11 November 2026 it announced Deliberation No. 05, setting rules for personal data in CVs under Law 18-07. Tech Hive Advisory reports a decision in early 2026 on employee drug test results. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

EGY.short: Egypt's law is in force and its acting-led authority issued guidelines in 2026 and opened licence applications; no ruling against an organisation has been found.
EGY.summary: Shura Law Firm says Egypt's Law No. 151 of 2020 entered into force in October 2020. Its executive regulations are dated 1 November 2025 and give organisations a year to comply. In the last twelve months, Tech Hive Advisory says the Personal Data Protection Centre published guidelines in January and February 2026, with breach-notification templates. Baker McKenzie says the Centre opened an electronic portal in early October 2026 for licence and permit applications. A 7 August 2026 report still names an acting chief executive. No ruling by the Centre against a named organisation has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

ERI.short: No data protection law is in force and no authority is appointed in 2026, so none has ruled against an organisation.
ERI.summary: Law Lab Africa states that no comprehensive data protection law is in force in Eritrea, as of a verification pass on 1 August 2026. A June 2025 Horn of Africa Initiative update says Eritrea remains without data protection legislation. Law Lab Africa also states that no supervisory authority has been established. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature of the Malabo Convention by Eritrea. No draft data protection law has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

ETH.short: Ethiopia published a data protection law in 2024 and its communications regulator oversees it; no ruling against an organisation is known.
ETH.summary: Ethiopia published its Personal Data Protection Proclamation in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. Shega reported in November 2025 that it took effect on publication. The Tech Hive review says the Ethiopian Communications Authority is the regulator under Article 5. In November 2025 its Director General said data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

GAB.short: Gabon's data protection law was published in 2023, its authority is working, and it fined Citibank Gabon in 2024.
GAB.summary: Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023 amended Gabon's 2011 data protection law. The APDPVP's president, vice-president and six other commissioners were appointed by the Council of Ministers on 12 July 2023. In the last twelve months, its president gave its review of 2025 on 27 January 2026, counting 12 administrative and financial sanctions on controllers in breach in 2025. By September 2026 it had logged about 715 declarations of conformity and about 30 complaints.

GHA.short: Ghana's commission registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026 and referred a clinic to police in October; no count of its rulings has been found.
GHA.summary: The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) is the law Ghana's Data Protection Commission enforces in 2026. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the Commission declared 2026 the 'Year of Enforcement'. It registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026. On 12 October 2026 it directed Nyaho Medical Centre to report to the Police CID over an expired registration certificate. On 20 October 2026 it warned a ministry and media houses over disclosing evacuees' personal data. No count of the Commission's rulings has been found.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 data protection law is in force and the Malabo Convention ratified, but no authority is appointed and no ruling is known.
GIN.summary: Guinea's 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, Loi L/2016/037/AN, was adopted and promulgated by President Alpha Condé. The law defines an Autorité de Protection and sets its functions. The CNT reported on 20 June 2024 that its commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, and that the designation of members was still contested. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No authority constituted or appointed has been found. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

GMB.short: A law was enacted in 2025 but no start date is known; an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GMB.summary: President Barrow assented to the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 on 7 November 2025. No grace period and no commencement date are given. In the last twelve months, a notice of 17 August 2026 says the Information Commission of The Gambia is to develop a communication strategy to raise awareness of the Act. The Gambia signed the Convention on 2 December 2022. The African Union's list of 2 February 2026 records signature and no ratification. No commencement date for the Act has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law in force in 2026 and no authority appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GNB.summary: A professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said on 22 September 2026 that Guinea-Bissau does not yet have specific data protection legislation. A national report of 18 February 2025 lists a personal data protection bill awaiting discussion. The professor said Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015 and had not ratified it. The stage of the bill has not been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

GNQ.short: A law has been in force since 2016, but its authority was not appointed as of 2022 and no ruling is known.
GNQ.summary: Ley Núm. 1/2016 of 22 July 2016 sets rules for personal data processing in Equatorial Guinea. Articles 15 and 29 name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, to be created by a decree. In the last twelve months, the African Union's Infrastructure and Energy Department reports that Equatorial Guinea's foreign minister signed the Malabo Convention in Addis Ababa on 28 July 2026. No ratification of the Convention has been found. No appointment to the authority and no ruling against an organisation has been found. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

KEN.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority has ruled since 2022, 459 determinations by 2026; its first commissioner leaves in November 2026.
KEN.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, with Immaculate Kassait as its first commissioner from 2020. By March 2025 it had received 7,128 complaints, issued 215 determinations and penalised 10 entities. In the last twelve months, the outgoing commissioner counted 459 determinations in six years, with enforcement action against the Ministry of Agriculture and Migori County Assembly. She leaves on 16 November 2026 after six years. A successor was nominated on 10 November. On 8 September 2026 Citizen Digital reported that Kenya had not yet formally joined the Malabo Convention.

LBR.short: A data protection law is in force from 2026; no authority is known to be working and no ruling against an organisation is known.
LBR.summary: Liberia's printed Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. It takes effect on publication into handbills. In the last twelve months, on 13 September 2026 the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said that it is aware of its responsibilities under the Act. The Act gives data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner, created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010. It does not state that the Commissioner has begun acting under it. No ratification of the Malabo Convention has been found, and no appointed authority. Establishing would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or an appointed authority.

LBY.short: Libya's data protection law was still a draft in 2026, no authority is known, and Libya has not signed the Malabo Convention.
LBY.summary: Libya's National AI Strategy, adopted on 1 June 2026, says that the Data Protection and Privacy Law is still in draft. It sets the law's adoption as a 2026 target. SMEX reported in July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification by Libya. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No data protection law in force has been found, and no authority. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

LSO.short: A data protection law is in force; the authority it creates has not been appointed, and no ruling against an organisation is known (2026).
LSO.summary: Lesotho enacted its Data Protection Act in 2011. The Act provides for a Data Protection Commission. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Cenfri says the Commission had not been appointed by 23 March 2026, and an article of 27 March 2026 says no independent body exists to enforce the law. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Lesotho ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 5 February 2025. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

MAR.short: Law 09-08 is in force and the CNDP authority is working, issuing guidance in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MAR.summary: The president of the CNDP, interviewed on 4 August 2026, speaks of Law 09-08 as in force for more than fifteen years. The CNDP, Morocco's national commission for the control of personal data protection, validated five new deliberations on 28 November 2025. In the last twelve months, in a communiqué dated 28 August 2026 it gave guidance on Law 09-08 to political parties and voters for the 23 September 2026 elections. It also opened a 3020 information line. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

MDG.short: A 2015 law is in force and its authority was sworn in during August 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MDG.summary: Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 9 January 2015. Seven members of the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale announced the CMIL is now effectively in place. The CMIL's annual report of January 2026 says no processing declaration has been registered yet, and that the commission has no premises or staff. No source dated in the last three years shows it issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

MLI.short: Law 2013-015 is in force and its authority works; it fined a Bamako clinic and a company in 2025.
MLI.summary: Law no. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013, as amended, is the basis the authority's president cited for its sanctions when opening its session on 3 August 2026. In 2025 the Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP) fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission. It also fined Société Aminata Konaté SARL 5 million F CFA for refusing one. In the last twelve months, it opened a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025. It held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 under president Pr Mamoudou Samassekou.

MOZ.short: No law is in force and no authority is appointed; a draft law is on parliament's October 2026 agenda. No ruling is known.
MOZ.summary: DLA Piper states that Mozambique has no specific data protection legislation, in a guide last modified on 17 February 2026. The World Bank says the Data Protection Act had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament as of October 2025. In the last twelve months, on 1 October 2026 the Assembly's Standing Commission placed a draft law on the agenda of the session opening 28 October. A review of the draft law says it designates the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT as the National Authority. Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention on 2 December 2019. No law in force and no appointed authority has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

MRT.short: A 2017 law is in force and its authority met monthly and took decisions in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's Law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on personal data protection is applied in the authority's deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026. In the last twelve months, the Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) approved amendments to its transfer and cloud deliberations at its 29 April 2026 meeting. It held its ordinary monthly session on 30 June 2026. Its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

MUS.short: A law is in force and the authority reported figures for 2024; no source found reports a ruling against a named organisation.
MUS.summary: The Data Protection Office reports on its 2024 enforcement of the Data Protection Act 2017, and has been operational since 16 February 2009. For 2024 it reports 179 new complaints and 39 closed. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 it co-led the launch of the National Data Strategy 2025-2029 with the ministry. In September 2026 it told management companies to register as controllers and name their own officers. On 29 October 2026 the Minister said 23,000 of some 60,000 entities required to register had done so. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

MWI.short: A law is in force and an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
MWI.summary: Malawi's Data Protection Act, 2024 was assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority's compliance guideline says other Malawi controllers and processors had to comply from 3 June 2026. The guidelines state that MACRA is the designated Data Protection Authority under the Act. In the last twelve months, Nyasa Times reports it convened a stakeholder consultation on draft regulations in Lilongwe in July 2026. In November 2026 MACRA, as the Authority, held a workshop in Blantyre on proposed registration fees. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

NAM.short: Namibia has no law in force and no authority appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation; a bill is being finalised in 2026.
NAM.summary: Minister Theofelus said on 14 August 2025 that the ministry would table a Data Protection Bill in September 2025. In the last twelve months the position changed: Minister Theofelus said in July 2026 that Namibia is finalising the bill. An opposition MP told the Windhoek Observer in August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute. Namibia ratified the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019. No law in force, no appointed authority and no activity by one has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

NER.short: A law is in force, but its authority was abolished by decree in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
NER.summary: The president of the HAPDP said in an interview published on 28 July 2025 that law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 repealed and replaced the 2017 law. The authority's consolidated text of April 2026 presents it as the operative general law. In the last twelve months, Africa Data Protection reports, in a report published on 13 June 2026, that the government has abolished the HAPDP by decree. It split the HAPDP's powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. No authority appointed after the decree has been found. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

NGA.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it fined Multichoice Nigeria in 2025.
NGA.summary: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 was signed by President Tinubu on 12 June 2023. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in 2025 for violating the Act. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 it served a compliance notice on 649 higher-education institutions. A federal circular dated 27 July 2026 directed all federal ministries, departments and agencies to comply with it. In August 2026 the Commission opened an investigation into Hackerbella Ltd, the University of Lagos and Lotus Bank. In October 2026 its National Commissioner said 41,000 organisations had registered with the Commission in 2026.

RWA.short: A data protection law has applied since 2023 and an authority registers controllers (2026); no source found reports a ruling against an organisation.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021, and its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for data protection under the Act. In the last twelve months, The New Times reported in January 2026 that the Authority has registered data controllers and processors over four years. It has trained over 100 public sector data protection officers. In July 2026 CIPESA said Rwanda's AI policy gives it oversight of data protection in AI systems. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

SDN.short: Sudan has no data protection law in force in 2026; two authorities set up by decree in 2025 have issued no binding rules.
SDN.summary: The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says Sudan has no privacy law governing personal data, and that a 2018 draft bill was never enacted. In the last twelve months, on 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft data and artificial intelligence bill and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament. The Center says a November 2025 decree established the Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority and the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority. The same Center says neither had issued binding rules as of mid-2026. Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

SEN.short: A 2008 data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it ordered a company to remove a camera in March 2026.
SEN.summary: A reference summary states that Senegal's Law No. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority set up by that law. In the last twelve months, on 12 March 2026 the CDP, after a complaint, inspected Digicommunication International unannounced and ordered the meeting-room camera uninstalled. For April to June 2026 it reported 195 files handled, 39 authorisations issued and one processing rejected. An expert told APS in March 2026 that a bill to replace the law is reportedly in the circuit.

SLE.short: In 2026 the data protection law is still a draft bill and no authority is appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone has a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill. In November 2025 the Information Minister said it had finished its final national validation, with Cabinet and Parliament still to come. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy and authorised a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act. The 2025 Bill would establish a single independent authority, which is not yet constituted. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Sierra Leone had not ratified the Malabo Convention. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

SOM.short: Somalia's data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and taking registrations since 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SOM.summary: Somalia's Data Protection Act, Law No. 005 of 2023, was enacted on 23 March 2023. Somalia inaugurated its Data Protection Authority on 24 February 2024. In the last twelve months, its January 2026 Registration Guidelines set fees and a 30-day approval timeline. On 2 June 2026 the Authority began accepting registration applications from controllers and processors. Its own service page of the same date lists the registration forms it issues. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

SSD.short: In 2026 South Sudan's data protection law is still a draft bill; no authority is appointed and no ruling against an organisation is known.
SSD.summary: The World Bank's 2026 diagnostic states there is no national data protection or privacy law in South Sudan. The ICT Minister said in December 2025 the government will introduce its first Data Protection Bill in 2026. In the last twelve months, a workshop of over 30 stakeholders reviewed the Data Protection Bill, 2025, according to a post dated 5 May 2026. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature of the Malabo Convention. No enacted data protection law and no operating authority has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law in force.

STP.short: The 2016 data protection law is in force; the authority, appointed, signed a cooperation agreement in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
STP.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's Lei n.º 03/2016 was published in the Diário da República of 10 May 2016. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais has a president, José Manuel Costa Alegre. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 he met the National Assembly president to plan oversight of personal data in the electoral roll. On 1 June 2026 the agency signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau. No source dated in the last three years has been found showing the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

SWZ.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it has ruled against named organisations, most recently in 2025.
SWZ.summary: Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022 was gazetted on 4 March 2022. The notice of 2024 states the Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. The Authority issued enforcement notices under section 41 in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited. It issued another in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs. In September 2026 it was led by an acting chief executive.

SYC.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working, handling 14 cases in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SYC.summary: Seychelles' Data Protection Act, 2023 was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023. The Information Commission is named in section 5 as the competent authority. In the last twelve months, in 2026 it marked Data Protection Day with guidance to organisations and the public. In 2025 it handled 14 cases under the Act: 6 on data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests and 1 consultation. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

TCD.short: Chad's 2015 personal data law is treated as in force and the security agency holds data protection duties; no ruling is known.
TCD.summary: Chad's personal data law of 2015 is treated as in force. A Chadian law firm's analysis published on 6 July 2026 applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data. The minister announced on 9 December 2025 that authorities were finalising a digital law. In the last twelve months, Ecofin reported on 16 March 2026 that the Senate ratified a reform law on 13 March 2026. It broadens the mandate of ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification, to cover personal data protection. No source has been found showing ANSICE registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has registered organisations, taken breach reports, issued guidance or inspected in the past three years.

TGO.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
TGO.summary: Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated. The IPDCP officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025. In the last twelve months, it ran a three-day training for 35 data protection correspondents from 22 to 24 June 2026. On 15 September 2026 it convened a compliance meeting for public administrations. On 18 November 2026 it certified the first 28, from banks, insurers, telecom operators and local authorities among others. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

TUN.short: A 2004 law is in force; an authority appointed in 2021 is reported at a standstill in 2026, with no ruling against an organisation known.
TUN.summary: Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 sets the general processing, consent and rights regime. A replacement bill, no. 095/2025, was deposited before the Assembly on 14 July 2025. The Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members to the national personal data protection authority. In the last twelve months, the Forum Chawki Gaddes issued a statement on 3 October 2026 saying the activities of the authority, INPDP, are at a standstill. No source dated in the last three years has been found showing the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. Operating would need an appointed authority that has done one of those things in the past three years.

TZA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2023, the Commission is working, and it ruled against a company in 2025.
TZA.summary: The Personal Data Protection Act, Chapter 44, commenced on 1 May 2023. Section 6 of the Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate. A ruling reported in August 2025 awarded TZS 20,000,000 against Mi Casa Company Limited. In the last twelve months, The Citizen reported on 28 August 2026 that the Commission will inspect compliance with the Act from 31 August 2026. PDPC figures cited in October 2026 show 15,146 institutions registered and 445 complaints received by August 2026.

UGA.short: A data protection law is in force, the Personal Data Protection Office is working, and it ruled against Google in 2025.
UGA.summary: Uganda's Personal Data Protection Office applied the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, in its decision of 18 July 2025. On 18 July 2025 it found Google in breach and ordered it to register within 30 days. In the last twelve months, the PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026 partly upheld a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms and issued corrective orders. On 17 July 2026 it confirmed WhatsApp had implemented them. In July 2026 the Office supervised more than 13,400 registered data controllers and processors. It briefed government IT officers on data protection on 13 August 2026.

ZAF.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2021; the Information Regulator is working and issued an enforcement notice to a college in 2026.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's data protection law came into force on 1 July 2021. The African Union's list of 2 February 2026 records that South Africa signed the Malabo Convention on 16 February 2023, with no ratification. The Information Regulator has received over 8,000 reports of security compromises, 1,220 of them since April 2026. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, it gave the South African Bureau of Standards 90 days to revise its policies and put security measures in place. No bill or draft has been found for the planned amendment of the law on artificial intelligence.

ZMB.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZMB.summary: A World Bank tender notice of 10 August 2026 treats Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 as the law being implemented. The first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. The Commissioner's office opened online registration for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

ZWE.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] is applied through SI 155 of 2024, which took effect in September 2024 and made a Data Controller Licence mandatory. POTRAZ states it is the designated Data Protection Authority under section 5 of the Act. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 it reported 1,123 licence applications so far that year and 1,218 data protection officers trained. Its Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 announces mandatory compliance inspections from 1 September 2026. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. Mature would need a ruling against a named organisation in the past three years, or a count of its rulings.

AGO.short: Since 2011 a transfer needs notice to the agency if the destination is adequate, authorisation if not; no published list is on file.
AGO.summary: Angola's Law 22/11 of 17 June 2011 requires notice to the data protection agency, the APD, for a transfer to a country with adequate protection. A transfer to any other country needs the APD's authorisation. In the last twelve months, Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 that the APD fined Crescer Tech about US$505,000 for a transfer to a cloud abroad without notice or authorisation. No source found says the APD has published a list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the APD to publish one of them.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2026 data protection law requires adequate protection abroad; no source found says when the law takes effect, and the Malabo Convention is unratified.
BDI.summary: Burundi Times reported in November 2026 that Burundi promulgated Law No. 1/03 on the protection of personal data on 10 March 2026. Its Article 15 requires a country receiving personal data from Burundi to give an adequate level of protection, and the law allows other transfers where appropriate safeguards are in place. This law is the change found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the date it takes effect, and the agency it creates was still being set up. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

BEN.short: Benin ratified the Malabo Convention in 2024, but no source states its rule on sending personal data abroad.
BEN.summary: No stage is set. In the last twelve months, the data protection authority's president said on 21 October 2026 that the Code numérique requires critical servers to be sited on national territory. Levellers says Benin ratified the Malabo Convention by Decree 2024-772 of 1 February 2024 and deposited its instrument on 26 November 2024. No source found says what Benin's law rules on sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

BFA.short: Sending personal data abroad needs the data authority's authorisation, per its September 2026 form; no open route is on file; Malabo is unratified.
BFA.summary: Burkina Faso's data protection authority, the CIL, published an application form in September 2026 for authorisation to transfer personal data to a foreign country. A transfer abroad needs the CIL's authorisation. In the last twelve months, the Prime Minister's instruction of 23 January 2026 called for public administration data hosted abroad to return to national datacentres. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the CIL's permission. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

BWA.short: Since January 2025 data may go only to approved countries, with a copy kept in Botswana; the Malabo Convention is unratified.
BWA.summary: Mmegi reported on 25 November 2025 that Botswana's Data Protection Act, in effect since January 2025, allows transfers abroad only to approved countries. It also requires a copy of the data to remain in Botswana. A DIAL expert comment of 15 June 2026 says Botswana has an adequacy list on which only two African countries appear. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how the copy requirement works beside transfers to approved countries. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time, with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

CAF.short: A 2025 account says transfers outside CEMAC and ECCAS need sufficient protection in the recipient state; no open route is on file.
CAF.summary: Jurist Laurent-Fabrice Zengue wrote on 16 September 2025 that the Central African Republic's data protection law conditions transfers to a state outside CEMAC or ECCAS on sufficient protection in the recipient state. He added that other transfers face further requirements. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the authority's permission. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

CIV.short: Since 2015 every transfer abroad needs the telecoms regulator's prior authorisation; Côte d'Ivoire ratified the Malabo Convention in 2023.
CIV.summary: Decree 2015-79 of 4 February 2015, issued under law 2013-450, requires prior authorisation from the telecoms regulator, ARTCI, to transfer personal data to a third country. The destination must give equal or higher protection. The decree names no route without authorisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Côte d'Ivoire's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 8 March 2023. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without ARTCI's permission each time.

CMR.short: Since the 2024 law every transfer abroad needs the authority's authorisation, though the authority is not yet created; Cameroon has not ratified Malabo.
CMR.summary: Authors at African Law & Business wrote on 23 December 2024 that Cameroon's Act requires the data protection authority to authorise every cross-border transfer of personal data. In the last twelve months, ACTPOL reported that the compliance period ended on 23 June 2026 and that the Authority has not been created. No route without authorisation is named. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Cameroon's signature of the Malabo Convention on 12 August 2021 and no deposit. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

COD.short: The DR Congo's 2023 Digital Code lets personal data go to countries with equivalent protection; no published list or model terms has been found.
COD.summary: The Code du numérique, articles 262 to 270, creates a data protection authority. It authorises or refuses cross-border transfers of personal data to third states. Since 17 August 2024 a ministerial order has given those duties to the regulator ARPTIC. In the last twelve months, a June 2026 legal summary said the Digital Code lets a transfer go where the destination gives equivalent protection. Otherwise the minister must authorise it. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

COG.short: Since April 2025 the data authority can authorise cross-border transfers; no open route is on file. Congo ratified the Malabo Convention in 2020.
COG.summary: Law no. 5-2025 of 29 March 2025 was published in the Journal officiel on 10 April 2025. It gives the data protection authority, the CNPD, the power to authorise cross-border transfers of personal data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the CNPD's permission. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Congo's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 24 September 2020. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

COM.short: Since 2021 transfers abroad rest on adequacy, safeguards or derogations; no published list is on file, and Malabo is signed only.
COM.summary: The Comoros Protection of Personal Data Law, enacted on 29 June 2021, governs international transfers on a risk-based model. The model rests on adequacy, appropriate safeguards and derogations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Comoros's signature of the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2018 and no deposit. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

CPV.short: Transfers go to adequate countries or on consent and listed grounds since 2013; no published list is on file. Cape Verde ratified Malabo in 2020.
CPV.summary: Law 41/VIII/2013, published on 17 September 2013, allows transfer abroad only to a country with adequate protection. The authority, the CNPD, decides which states are adequate, and article 20 sets other grounds, such as consent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Cape Verde's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 13 November 2020. No source found says the CNPD has published its list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the CNPD to publish one of them.

DJI.short: The Code Numérique, published September 2025, allows transfers abroad with equivalent protection, on consent or by contract; no published list is on file.
DJI.summary: The Code Numérique, published on 18 September 2025, bars a controller or processor from sending personal data to a third country unless the recipient ensures an equivalent and sufficient level of protection (article 99). Exceptions let data go on consent, contract, public interest, legal claims and vital interests. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Djibouti's signature of the Malabo Convention on 12 May 2023 and no ratification. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

DZA.short: Transfers need adequacy and authorisation, or consent, yet one source says data must also be stored in Algeria; no list is issued. Malabo is unsigned.
DZA.summary: Digital Policy Alert says the 2023 personal data law allows transfers to states with adequate protection and with prior authorisation from the authority, the ANPDP. It also allows them on conditions such as explicit consent. The US International Trade Administration's guide states that data localisation is mandatory under Law 18-07, in force since 10 August 2023. In the last twelve months, the authority's Deliberation 04 of 15 July 2026 treated publication on foreign-run platforms as a transfer abroad. No source found says the general localisation rule has been lifted. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

EGY.short: Every transfer abroad needs the Centre's licence and consent; no adequacy list or standard clauses exist, and Egypt has not signed the Malabo Convention.
EGY.summary: Shura Law Firm states that transferring personal data outside Egypt requires a licence from the Personal Data Protection Centre and the person's consent. Full enforcement starts on 31 October 2026. In the last twelve months, Legal 500 says, Executive Regulations were issued in November 2025 with a grace period to 1 November 2026. ACTPOL said on 25 September 2026 that the regulations provide no standard contractual clauses. No source found says any transfer goes without the Centre's licence. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection law and no rule on sending data abroad, as reviewed in June 2026; it has not signed the Malabo Convention.
ERI.summary: Levellers, in a page reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no data protection legislation and no restriction on cross-border transfer of data in its law. The UNECA digital trade profile states that Eritrea does not require local data storage. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature, ratification or deposit of the Malabo Convention. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

ETH.short: The 2024 Proclamation allows transfers on adequacy or consent but also requires locally collected personal data to be stored in Ethiopia; Malabo is unsigned.
ETH.summary: Techhive Advisory says the Personal Data Protection Proclamation, published on 24 July 2024, makes transfers abroad depend on an adequacy decision by the Authority. Explicit consent, necessity or public registry purposes also serve. Digital Policy Alert records that the Proclamation also requires locally collected personal data to be stored on servers in Ethiopia. In the last twelve months, Shega reported in November 2025 that the Authority had approved about 10 requests to transfer data abroad as a temporary measure. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

GAB.short: No rule on sending personal data abroad is on file; sources disagree on whether Gabon has ratified the Malabo Convention.
GAB.summary: No stage is set. Law 027/2023, article 27, promulgated on 11 July 2023, requires data judged confidential or sensitive to be hosted on national territory. The authority may grant a written derogation. In the last twelve months, NotreAfrik states that Gabon ratified the Malabo Convention in 2026. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 shows no action. No source found says what Gabon's law rules on sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

GHA.short: Amendments adding rules on international transfers were in draft in 2025; Ghana ratified the Malabo Convention in 2019.
GHA.summary: A 2025 roundup says amendments to Ghana's Data Protection Act 2012 are in process and would add rules on international transfers. A draft Data Protection Act, 2025 has been published, and the roundup says it requires domestic storage of certain data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union list of 2 February 2026 records Ghana's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 13 May 2019. No source found says what the draft rules on sending personal data abroad. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 law gives the data authority approval over transfers abroad; no source shows which transfers go without approval, and no body is named.
GIN.summary: Guinea's 2016 law on cybersecurity and personal data protection gives the data protection authority the power to approve transfers of personal data abroad. The text published in July 2016 names no constituted body and no appointed members. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without the authority's approval. No source found says the authority has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

GMB.short: Gambia's Personal Data Protection Act has its Commission assess cross-border transfers; no source shows which go without permission or that the Commission is constituted.
GMB.summary: A law-firm note of February 2026 describes Gambia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, which provides a Commission that assesses cross-border transfers and may impose conditions on them. The note does not say the Commission is constituted or its members appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without the Commission's permission. No source found says the Commission has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015; no source found shows a rule on sending personal data abroad.
GNB.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015. No ratification date is entered. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's parliament approved ratifying the Malabo Convention on 25 March 2026; no source found shows a rule on sending personal data abroad.
GNQ.summary: No stage is set. In the last twelve months, on 25 March 2026 the Chamber of Deputies approved ratification of the Malabo Convention. The African Union says the foreign minister signed it on 28 July 2026. The status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature or deposit. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

KEN.short: Kenya's Data Protection Act and the Commissioner's guidance of September 2026 set conditions for transfers abroad; no source shows which go without permission.
KEN.summary: Kenya's Data Protection Act of 2019 governs sending personal data abroad. In the last twelve months, a report of 9 September 2026 said the Data Commissioner's guidance sets the conditions for a lawful transfer, including the safeguards required and the mechanisms for adequate protection. No source found says which transfers go without the Commissioner's permission. No source found says a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation has been published. Cabinet approved the Malabo Convention in 2025, and the National Assembly has yet to approve it. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

LBR.short: Liberia has not signed or ratified the Malabo Convention as of February 2026; no source found shows a rule on sending personal data abroad.
LBR.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature, ratification or deposit of the Malabo Convention by Liberia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

LBY.short: Libya's central bank bars banks and payment firms from storing personal data abroad from July 2026; no general rule on sending data abroad is found.
LBY.summary: No stage is set. Central Bank Circular No. 18 of 1 June 2025 bars banks, fintechs and payment providers from storing personal data outside Libya from 1 July 2026. It covers those sectors only. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature or ratification of the Malabo Convention. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad in general. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, with no rule on sending it abroad.

LSO.short: Lesotho's Data Protection Act of 2012 sets cross-border transfer rules; no Commissioner is appointed and no source shows which transfers go without permission.
LSO.summary: Lesotho's Data Protection Act of 2012 is in force and has cross-border transfer rules modelled on the SADC rules. A law firm wrote in October 2025 that the Commission and Commissioner have not been appointed, so no authority exists to approve transfer mechanisms. It also wrote that standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules are not yet in place. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The status list of 2 February 2026 records Lesotho's signature of the Malabo Convention on 30 November 2023. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

MAR.short: Morocco's law 09-08 protects transfers abroad and its 2015 adequacy list names countries data may go to; none are African.
MAR.summary: The Council of Europe's committee described Morocco's law 09-08 in October 2012. Articles 43 and 44 protect transfers of personal data to foreign countries, in particular where the country does not provide an adequate level of protection. Morocco's 2015 adequacy list names the countries personal data may be sent to, and the DIAL research group records that it did not recognise a single African country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature or ratification of the Malabo Convention. Mature would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol, or treating an African partner's protection as good enough in practice.

MDG.short: Madagascar ratified the Malabo Convention on 17 July 2025; no source found shows a rule on sending personal data abroad.
MDG.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list records Madagascar's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 17 July 2025. The Constitutional Court ruled on 10 July 2024 that the Convention and the authorising law conform to the Constitution. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

MLI.short: Mali's 2013 law lets personal data go abroad where the authority finds the receiving state's protection sufficient; no route without its decision is shown.
MLI.summary: Mali's law 2013-015 of 21 May 2013 lets a controller transfer personal data to a foreign state when the data protection authority finds the receiving state's protection sufficient. Where contract clauses or internal rules cover a transfer, the authority decides. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a transfer may go without the authority's decision, or that it has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature, ratification or deposit by Mali. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a data protection bill with transfer rules in March 2026; it ratified the Malabo Convention in 2019.
MOZ.summary: INTIC reports that Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a Personal Data Protection Bill on 3 March 2026 for the Assembly of the Republic. It allows international transfers only where equivalent protection is assured. In the last twelve months this bill is the new step, and it is not in force, so no transfer condition binds controllers until the Assembly passes it. A UNECA, GIZ and African Union inception report of 19 June 2025 states that Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention in 2019. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

MRT.short: Mauritania bars transfers abroad without sufficient protection, publishes a list of adequate countries since July 2025, and ratified the Malabo Convention in 2023.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 bars a controller from sending personal data to a third country unless it ensures a sufficient level of protection. Deliberation 004/2025 of 14 July 2025 sets the conditions for transfers abroad, and the authority publishes and updates a list of countries it judges adequate. NotreAfrik reports that Mauritania ratified the Malabo Convention by May 2023. In the last twelve months, the authority's meeting of 29 April 2026 listed amendments to deliberations 004/2025 and 005/2025. No source found shows the outcome of the April 2026 amendments.

MUS.short: Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017 governs transfers; the Office authorised 112 and rejected 12 in 2024, and no route without asking is shown.
MUS.summary: Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017 sets a rule on transfers in section 36. The Data Protection Office reports that in 2024 it authorised 112 cross-border transfers and rejected 12 under that section. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without authorisation. No source found says the Office has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. The African Union status list records ratification of the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2018. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

MWI.short: Malawi's Data Protection Act, in force since 3 June 2024, lets data go abroad on adequacy, binding rules, contract or consent; no list is published.
MWI.summary: Malawi's Data Protection Act came into force on 3 June 2024. Sections 38 to 40 restrict transfers of personal data outside Malawi unless the receiving country has adequate protection or binding corporate rules are in place. The Act of 2024 also lets a transfer go on a contractual clause, a code of conduct, certification or consent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the authority has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the authority to publish one of them.

NAM.short: An opposition MP said on 4 August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute, so no rule on transfers abroad.
NAM.summary: On 4 August 2026 opposition member Rodney Cloete told the Windhoek Observer that Namibia has no data protection statute, so no rules govern cross-border transfers of data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows a law, regulation or draft that sets a condition for sending personal data abroad. The African Union status list records Namibia's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

NER.short: Niger ratified the Malabo Convention on 22 February 2022; no source found shows a rule on sending personal data abroad.
NER.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list records Niger's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 22 February 2022. It also records deposit on 16 March 2022. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

NGA.short: Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 lets data go abroad on adequacy decisions or approved corporate rules; no list is published and Malabo is not ratified.
NGA.summary: Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 has a Part VIII on cross-border transfers, in sections 41 to 43. The Commissioner says the Commission decides the adequacy of other countries' protection as a basis for transfer. The Commission also approves binding corporate rules, codes and certification mechanisms. In the last twelve months, a central bank circular of 15 June 2026 kept payment data in Nigeria, for payment operators only. No source found says the Commission has published a list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the Commission to publish one of them.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2021 law allows transfers on approval, consent or exceptions and has standard clauses, but one source says it generally keeps personal data in Rwanda.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's law 058/2021 of 13 October 2021 sets the rule in article 49. Digital Policy Alert says it allows transfers abroad through the authority's authorisation, the person's consent or specific exceptions. It also says the law generally requires personal data to be stored in Rwanda unless the supervisory authority grants a certificate. A market brief of July 2025 says there is no blanket requirement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

SDN.short: As of July 2026 no Sudanese law governs sending data abroad; the country signed the Malabo Convention in 2023 but has not ratified it.
SDN.summary: The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies reported on 19 July 2026 that no statute governs cross-border transfer of data in Sudan. Global Voices wrote on 21 October 2023 that Sudan has no law imposing data localisation. The African Union status list records that Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ratification is on record. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2008 law bars transfers to countries without sufficient protection and needs the authority's authorisation; it ratified the Malabo Convention in 2016.
SEN.summary: Article 9 of Law 2008-12 bars a data owner from sending data to a country that does not give sufficient protection. A law-firm note of 11 May 2018 says the data protection authority must be informed and its authorisation sought. It names no route that avoids authorisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Senegal ratified the Malabo Convention on 3 August 2016. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone requires telecoms regulator approval to send subscriber registration data abroad (2020); no general transfer rule or Malabo ratification is on file.
SLE.summary: No stage is set. Regulation 22(3) of the 2020 subscriber registration regulations bars sending subscribers' registration information outside Sierra Leone, unless the National Telecommunications Commission gives prior approval. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Sierra Leone signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2016. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets a condition on sending personal data in general abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, with no rule on sending it abroad.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 data protection law lets personal data go abroad on adequacy, contract or consent; it has not ratified the Malabo Convention.
SOM.summary: Articles 30 and 31 of Law No. 005 of 2023, signed on 22 March 2023, bar a controller from sending personal data abroad. Two cases are exempt: the recipient gives adequate protection, or a stated exception applies. The law lets data go where the recipient is bound by law, binding corporate rules or contract clauses, and on the person's consent. In the last twelve months, civil society called on 20 July 2026 for Somalia to sign and ratify the Malabo Convention. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

SSD.short: No rule on sending data abroad is on file for South Sudan, and it has not signed or ratified the Malabo Convention.
SSD.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 shows no signature, ratification or deposit of the Malabo Convention by South Sudan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law or regulation on sending personal data abroad, or a data localisation rule. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

STP.short: Sao Tome and Principe's 2016 law lets data go to adequately protected countries or on consent; it ratified the Malabo Convention in 2023.
