STP.summary: Articles 19 and 20 of Law No. 03/2016, promulgated on 18 March 2016, allow personal data to leave the country only where the receiving legal system gives adequate protection. A factsheet updated on 24 June 2022 adds a route by notification with the person's unequivocal consent, and lists the authority as operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

SWZ.short: Eswatini's data protection authority must authorise every transfer of personal data abroad; the country has not ratified the Malabo Convention.
SWZ.summary: The Eswatini Data Protection Authority's 2024 application form requires authorisation before personal data leaves the country. The applicant supplies the recipient country's law, contracts and an impact assessment. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of ICT reported on 10 July 2026 a workshop with senators on ratifying the Malabo Convention. No source found says any transfer goes without authorisation. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

SYC.short: Seychelles' Data Protection Act, in force since December 2023, allows transfers abroad with adequate protection or safeguards; it has not signed the Malabo Convention.
SYC.summary: DLA Piper reports that Seychelles' Data Protection Act 2023 came into force on 22 December 2023. It permits transfers outside Seychelles only where the transfer ensures an adequate level of protection, and it allows transfers with appropriate safeguards or legal mechanisms. The Information Commission's 2025 annual report counts 6 data transfer cases handled as guidance and advice. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish one of them.

TCD.short: Chad's 2015 law sets conditions for sending data abroad, by notification or prior authorisation; no transfer is shown going without permission.
TCD.summary: A Cabinet Thomas Dingamgoto analysis of 6 July 2026 says articles 29 to 32 of Loi 007/PR/2015 require a legal basis and adequate safeguards for sending personal data out of Chad. It says transfers need notification or prior authorisation by the authority, ANSICE, without saying which need which. No change has been found in the last twelve months. ACTPOL, citing the African Union list of 2 February 2026, says Chad signed the Malabo Convention without ratifying it. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

TGO.short: Togo ratified the Malabo Convention in 2021; no rule on sending data abroad is on file.
TGO.summary: No stage is set. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Togo signed the Malabo Convention on 2 April 2019 and ratified it on 30 September 2021. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or guidance on sending personal data abroad. No localisation rule is on record. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 2004 law makes every transfer abroad wait on the authority's prior authorisation; a revised regime is before parliament.
TUN.summary: Articles 50 to 52 of Organic Law 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 allow transfer of personal data abroad only to a country with an adequate level of protection. The law requires prior authorisation of the authority, INPDP, in every case. DIAL wrote on 15 June 2026 that Tunisia's 2018 adequacy list names only five African countries. In the last twelve months, lawyer Zied El Air wrote in 2026 that organic bill 095/2025 contains a revised framework for international transfers. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 2023 data protection law conditions transfers abroad and the Commission issues transfer permits; whether any transfer needs none is not shown.
TZA.summary: Part V of the Personal Data Protection Act, published on 13 June 2023, sets rules for transfer to a state with adequate protection and to a state without it. The Commission says it regulates transfers through a cross-border data transfer permit, and reports 121 permits offered by August 2026. No source found says a transfer to an adequate country goes without a permit. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model terms or general authorisation has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2019 Act lets data go abroad on equivalent protection or consent; no route without asking is published, and Malabo is not ratified.
UGA.summary: CIPESA says section 19 of Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 requires data sent abroad to go to a country with equivalent protection, with the person's consent. The regulator applied the rule against Google on 18 July 2025. In the last twelve months, the decision of 20 February 2026 on WhatsApp ordered an adequacy assessment by the company. It names no list of countries or model terms. Operating would need the regulator to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

ZAF.short: South Africa's POPIA, in force since 2020, lets data go abroad on adequacy, consent or contract, but names no adequate countries.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act bars sending personal information abroad unless the recipient is under adequate legal protection. Transfers may also go on the person's consent or where a contract requires it, with no authorisation step. The same source, of January 2024, says the Act names no countries with adequate protection and no way to recognise them. The sender judges adequacy itself. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published route that needs no case-by-case judgment: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

ZMB.short: The data law has been in force since 2024 but keeps personal data in Zambia unless the Minister allows otherwise; no source found reports the exceptions.
ZMB.summary: The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, enacted on 24 March 2021, sets conditions in sections 70 and 71 for sending personal data out of Zambia. In February 2024 the Commissioner said section 70(1) requires data to be processed and stored in Zambia, with exceptions the Minister sets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exceptions the Minister has set. No approved contract terms or list of countries have been found. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 2024 guideline bars transfers abroad unless the authority is notified and conditions are met; whether any transfer needs no permission is not shown.
ZWE.summary: POTRAZ guideline CDPG 5 of 2024, issued on 13 November 2024, bars controllers from sending personal data abroad unless they notify the Authority. They must also run an impact assessment and show consent, adequate protection and a data-sharing agreement. In the last twelve months, POTRAZ reported on 26 December 2025 that 24 transfers have been authorised. No source found says which transfers go without prior authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

AGO.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2024; rural and urban use is not measured.
AGO.summary: Conecta Angola, launched in June 2023 for remote areas operators do not serve, had reached more than 300,000 people by October 2024. In the last twelve months, on 20 October 2026 the President authorised US$50 million and a tender for the Programa Conectividade. In November 2026 the ICT minister said 71 small internet providers take part in Conecta Angola. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

BDI.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
BDI.summary: In August 2026 the regulator ARCT said a new universal service fund will help rural people reach the internet. SETIC signed a $5.9 million contract with ONATEL for 92 rural hills lacking 2G or 3G, which is expected to serve about 372,000 people. PAFEN and Lumitel signed a USD 10 million contract for rural 4G, 44 per cent paid by the government. No site connected under these contracts has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

BEN.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a programme to connect rural areas, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether a programme to connect rural areas is under way. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a programme to bring internet access to rural or underserved areas that the government or its universal service fund has launched, funded or prepared in the past three years.

BFA.short: Over 400 rural white-zone localities were connected in 2025; rural and urban internet use is not measured by a survey.
BFA.summary: The ministry reported covering more than 400 new white-zone localities in 2025, after 138 in 2024, built with a State subsidy through the universal service fund. In the last twelve months, on 8 October 2026 the minister said 750 villages would get calls, internet and mobile money by end-2026. Figures shown at a national justice forum in June 2026 put internet access at 72% in urban areas. In rural areas it was 27%. No household survey or statistics office figure since October 2023 has been found for internet use in rural and urban areas. Operating would need such a survey or statistics office figure of the past three years.

BWA.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
BWA.summary: The Universal Access and Service Fund had connected 279 villages to 4G by March 2025, and aims at full rural connectivity by 2029. In May 2025 the state fibre operator BoFiNet said it had connected 223 of 503 gazetted villages with fibre. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 the ministry said the village connectivity project still extends internet to rural communities. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

CAF.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
CAF.summary: In July 2025 the body that oversees the universal service fund began work. The fund is funded by 2% of operator revenue, and operators are to build the infrastructure in uncovered areas. In the last twelve months, on 15 April 2026 the regulator ARCEP named finishing the fund a priority for 2026. No site connected under the fund has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

CIV.short: Rural and urban internet use were measured in 2025, rural use below four-fifths of urban.
CIV.summary: In September 2025 ITU figures put internet penetration at 52.7% urban and 24.6% rural. Phase one of the rural connectivity programme, finished in 2024, built 160 radio sites in 175 localities for about 221,000 people. In the last twelve months, a government communique of 24 August 2026 said the FCFA 38 billion programme continues towards 575 localities. In August 2026 the agency ANSUT said 70% of rural households have no internet. No source found since October 2023 puts rural internet use at four-fifths of the urban rate or more. Mature would need rural internet use of 80 per cent or more of the urban rate, from a household survey of the past three years.

CMR.short: Forty rural sites were connected under a World Bank-backed programme by November 2026; no source found reports internet use in rural and urban areas.
CMR.summary: On 31 October 2025 the posts minister opened bidding for the rural part of the World Bank-backed PATNUC. It has 55 billion XAF to connect 328 localities without 3G by 2028. In the last twelve months, by 13 November 2026 Orange had commissioned 40 of PATNUC's 120 white-zone sites, all due by March 2027. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

COD.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
COD.summary: On 12 February 2026 the universal service fund (FDSU) presented its National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035. It plans a subsidised, TowerCo-led roll-out in five zones and three phases to connect about 68 million rural Congolese. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the FDSU signed subsidy agreements with Vodacom, Airtel, Africell and Orange for at least 40 towers in peri-urban and rural areas. No count of sites already connected has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

COG.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
COG.summary: In January 2026 the universal service fund FASUCE connected two localities, Miaba and Ehota. Its committee chair said that in five years it deployed 254 sites in 244 localities. In the last twelve months, on 26 February 2026 the PATN steering committee adopted a 2026 budget of 21.872 billion FCFA, with rural connectivity a 2026 priority. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

COM.short: Nothing found names a programme to connect rural areas or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether rural areas are being connected or how far rural internet use lags urban.

CPV.short: No rural connectivity programme is known; a 2025 survey puts rural internet use at 86% of urban.
CPV.summary: No stage is set. INE's 2025 continuous survey shows 22.7% of people aged 10 and over did not use the internet in the previous three months. The same survey implies rural internet use of 68.8% against 80.0% urban, which is 86% of the urban rate. No source found says a programme to connect rural areas is under way. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a programme to bring internet access to rural or underserved areas that the government or its universal service fund has launched, funded or prepared in the past three years.

DJI.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
DJI.summary: In April 2026 the regulator ARMD said a World Bank-funded mission had delivered a draft decree, a draft bylaw and an operations guide. They are to set up a Universal Service Fund for equitable access across the whole country. In the last twelve months, the fund has been found only as a draft decree, and no site connected has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

DZA.short: Universal-service 4G reached its first rural localities in 2024; rural and urban use is not measured.
DZA.summary: On 21 October 2024 the minister switched on 4G in Djelida and El Amra, in Ain Defla. Two ministerial orders of June 2024 had awarded the universal-service mobile lots for low-density localities. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the State gave Mobilis a universal service programme for 201 4G sites in under-covered zones. On 7 September 2026 the regulator ARPCE opened a tender to extend mobile coverage to 3,000 sparsely populated localities. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

EGY.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
EGY.summary: By end-December 2024 the planning ministry reported fibre extended to 409 villages in the first phase of Haya Karima, the Decent Life initiative for rural Egypt. Mobile coverage was completed in 901 of 1,164 villages by September 2025, and MCIT reports 1,180,723 buildings covered by fibre under phase one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a programme to connect rural areas or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether rural areas are being connected or how far rural internet use lags urban.

ETH.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
ETH.summary: A regulation that requires Ethio Telecom and Safaricom to pay 1.5% of revenue into the Universal Access Fund is dated to March 2026 by The Reporter Ethiopia. It brings in about 2.5 billion Birr a year. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the innovation minister directed the Authority to expand connectivity in rural and underserved communities, against measurable targets. No source found since October 2023 gives a count of rural sites, towers or people connected. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

GAB.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
GAB.summary: On 16 February 2024 Arcep launched phase two of the universal service, paid for by an operator fund, to extend coverage to 200 villages in all nine provinces. In December 2024 ARCEP's chairman said three of 20 planned rural sites had been built and were about to enter service. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 minister Marc Alexandre Doumba said the government would speed up the universal service. In October 2026 he said more than 200 villages were still not connected. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

GHA.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
GHA.summary: In September 2026 the minister said about 1,400 Rural Telephony Project sites carry traffic. Another 300 were complete and awaiting connection, towards 2,016 sites. The opposition NPP says 1,961 sites had been built by the January 2025 handover, many now not working. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the minister said Ghana plans 800 new and 2,000 upgraded cell sites this year, with underserved areas prioritised. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

GIN.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2025; sites connected are not counted.
GIN.summary: On 22 July 2025 the universal service agency ANSUTEN presented a study mapping white zones. It aims to cover 90% of the rural population by 2030, with a tender to follow. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the deputy national director of telecommunications said Guinea's digital planning master plan targets 857 priority rural localities. No site connected has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

GMB.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2024; sites connected are not counted.
GMB.summary: In April 2024 the minister said the government was embarking on initiatives for rural Gambia, including using satellite as a source of connectivity. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether these initiatives are delivering, and no site connected under them has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

GNB.short: A plan to extend the network to rural centres was prepared in 2025; sites connected are not counted.
GNB.summary: In October 2025 consultants to the World Bank-financed WARDIP project delivered a strategic plan for the Universal Access and Service Fund, known by its Portuguese initials, FAU. It includes fibre links that extend the national backbone to less-served rural centres, and it proposes a pilot to subsidise phones. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No site is yet reported connected under the plan or by the fund. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

GNQ.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2023; sites connected are not counted.
GNQ.summary: In November 2023 the Vice-President ordered Huawei to draw up a project for telephone and internet coverage of the whole territory. It includes the interior and is to be assessed before a first phase is approved. In April 2023 the state infrastructure manager GITGE linked the island province of Annobon to the national fibre network, by a submarine cable from Sao Tome. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 counts sites connected by a rural programme. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

KEN.short: The Universal Service Fund had connected 155 sub-locations by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
KEN.summary: In August 2025 the Communications Authority said 155 of the 369 sub-locations targeted by its mobile phases 1-4 were connected. By September 2024 it had laid 1,300 km of fibre across 19 counties. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the government asked counties to name unconnected wards for the fund to target. The KDHS 2022 gave internet use by men aged 15 to 49 of 80.0% in urban and 40.7% in rural areas. It predates October 2023. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

LBR.short: The Universal Access Fund supported 15 towers in underserved areas in 2026; no source found reports the rural and urban shares of internet use.
LBR.summary: On 26 October 2026 the Liberia Telecommunications Authority said the Universal Access Fund already supports 15 towers. It has found sites for 15 more. In May 2025 the fund began restoring rural sites after nine of its twelve towers were found inactive for almost two years. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the Authority reported a new fund tower at Vahun, and in November 2026 it said 15 remote towers were being upgraded from 2G to 4G. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use for rural areas or for urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

LBY.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a programme to connect rural areas, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether a programme to connect rural areas is under way. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a programme to bring internet access to rural or underserved areas that the government or its universal service fund has launched, funded or prepared in the past three years.

LSO.short: A fund-financed tower connected 10 villages in 2024; rural and urban use is not measured.
LSO.summary: In May 2024 a Vodacom tower at Ha-Tsepe, Leribe, paid for by the fund and the AfDB, was inaugurated, and it connects 10 villages. The Lesotho Communications Authority's annual report 2024/25 says the Universal Service Fund pays to extend telecommunications to unserved and underserved areas. In August 2025 the Community Digital Inclusion Model was launched with UNDP. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

MAR.short: Rural and urban internet use were measured in 2024, rural use below four-fifths of urban.
MAR.summary: The 2024 census found that 70.2% of urban residents aged 15 and over had used the internet in the previous three months. Among rural residents it was 40.4%. Over 10,640 rural zones gained 2G, 3G and 4G between 2018 and 2024, the minister said. In the last twelve months, on 20 April 2026 the minister told parliament that phase two of the national broadband plan targets 2,000 rural zones in 2026. No source found since October 2023 puts rural internet use at four-fifths of the urban rate or more. Mature would need rural internet use of 80 per cent or more of the urban rate, from a household survey of the past three years.

MDG.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
MDG.summary: In August 2025 the minister said she had launched a USD 55 million DECIM subsidy for towers and fibre in remote areas. A pilot of 73 RuralStar sites in Menabe was announced in July 2025. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 the digital development minister said solutions were in place in 146 fokontany, under a programme that targets 3,844 fokontany. Roll-out depends on funding. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

MLI.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
MLI.summary: On 23 July 2026 the state fund AGEFAU adopted a revised programme to extend network coverage and internet access, with universal access centres and Wi-Fi points added. For 2025 AGEFAU had planned FCFA 43.35bn to extend coverage and universal access centres. In the last twelve months, its revised 2026 budget of FCFA 27.89bn keeps coverage of 162 localities. No locality is yet counted as connected. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

MOZ.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
MOZ.summary: In August 2026 the government said it had connected 149 localities to the internet, and 418 schools, against a target of at least 300 localities. In October 2025 the regulator awarded Vodacom 60 rural mobile stations with public Wi-Fi in nine provinces. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the regulator INCM said a July 2026 decree lets it turn operators' fines into universal-service duties. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

MRT.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
MRT.summary: In February 2025 the regulator ARE said the universal service fund's southern border project had built 144 radio sites, serving more than 400 localities. On 28 December 2024 the President launched phases two and three, with 100 sites over 964 km. In the last twelve months, the digital transformation ministry has opened digital service centres with free internet access. They are in Ouadane, opened in December 2025, and Bassikounou, opened in February 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

MUS.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a programme to connect rural areas, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether a programme to connect rural areas is under way. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a programme to bring internet access to rural or underserved areas that the government or its universal service fund has launched, funded or prepared in the past three years.

MWI.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
MWI.summary: In September 2026 the government switched on the 36th tower of the Last Mile Rural Connectivity Project, at Kalira, and it plans 99 more towers by June 2027. In the last twelve months, a plan for 100 towers in underserved areas, with the Universal Service Fund, has entered procurement. By August 2026 safeguards checks were done for over 500 public institutions to be connected. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

NAM.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
NAM.summary: CRAN says Universal Service Fund towers opened at Epinga on 19 November 2025 and Ehomba on 30 January 2026. In the last twelve months, by March 2026 the phase-two roll-out was 39% complete, and a phase three of about N$65 million was being prepared. In August 2026 Kavango East's education director said the region had received only one fund tower. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

NER.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
NER.summary: By 6 August 2025 the Smart Villages project had brought mobile broadband to 780 villages without coverage, which was 35.86 per cent of the 2,175 planned. On 13 October 2025 the minister installed a committee to draft the universal access strategy. In the last twelve months, Smart Villages was due to close on 23 October 2026, and no later count of villages has been found. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

NGA.short: The first tower of a national programme for unconnected communities was serving Bende in 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
NGA.summary: The Federal Executive Council approved 4,000 rural towers in 2025. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 minister Bosun Tijani commissioned the first tower of the national programme NUCAP, in Bende, Abia State. He said 3,700 towers will connect about 20 million unconnected Nigerians, and BusinessDay reports a blended-funding plan for those towers, 200 of them by December 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

RWA.short: Towers and fibre were completed in one rural district in 2024 under a national programme; no source found reports rural and urban internet use.
RWA.summary: On 14 March 2024 the ICT ministry launched phase 2 of Connect Rwanda in Kirehe District, and announced 58 towers and 42 kilometres of fibre completed there. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national count of rural sites connected has been found. The newest rural and urban figures found are from the EICV5 household survey of 2016/17, which gave home internet access for 38.1% of urban households and 12.2% of rural households. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

SDN.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
SDN.summary: In 2022 Paradigm Initiative reported that the fund, set up in 2018, had agreements with Zain and MTN, to cover 93 of 168 uncovered areas, with obstacles to delivery. TPRA says the Universal Service Fund exists to provide telecom services in remote and rural areas. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the digital minister said 4G would reach about 200 villages during the year. No count of sites connected has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

SEN.short: The universal service fund had opened rural network sites by 2025; no source found reports rural and urban internet use.
SEN.summary: By June 2025 the fund and Sonatel had inaugurated rural network sites in Tambacounda, Kolda and Kedougou, with 1,540 eligible localities still to cover. In September 2025 the fund said it would deploy 774 sites in four zones for about 436,000 residents. In the last twelve months, on 10 April 2026 the telecoms minister launched free satellite kits in Kolda. In March 2026 the Prime Minister said a universal connectivity programme for white zones was under way. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

SLE.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
SLE.summary: In August 2025 the Universal Access Development Fund told parliament it had built five towers since 2018, with three more nearly finished for underserved rural communities. In July 2024 the fund said its Rural Telephony Project had connected about 47,700 people in 114 rural and remote localities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

SOM.short: A 2025 policy plans broadband for underserved areas; no source found reports no rural site is counted as connected, and internet use by area.
SOM.summary: The ministry's Digital Inclusion Policy of August 2025 gives priority to broadband in unserved and underserved areas, with a roadmap budgeted at about $32 million over five years. The policy says the government has not intervened to widen access in underserved areas. The 2023 ICT Survey it cites found access to internet connections of 22.7% in rural and 47.1% in urban areas. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 counts sites a rural programme has connected, and none gives the share of people using the internet by area. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

SSD.short: The universal service fund opened a rural network site in 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
SSD.summary: In July 2025 MTN South Sudan and the Universal Service and Access Fund launched a network site at Abuyong, in Lakes State. Three more sites are planned in Greater Pibor and Cueibet. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the National Communication Authority announced its agenda for the year. It aims to speed the roll-out of infrastructure that brings reliable connectivity to rural and under-connected areas. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

STP.short: The government agreed in 2024 to bring internet to 42 communities; no site is known to be connected.
STP.summary: In September 2024 the government and Huawei signed a memorandum of understanding to install solar power and internet in 42 communities, which Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada announced. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says any of the 42 communities has since been connected, and no other programme to bring internet to rural areas has been found. No survey of rural and urban internet use has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

SWZ.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
SWZ.summary: On 6 August 2026 the regulator ESCCOM, through the Universal Access Service Fund, co-funded a digital skills hub at Macetjeni, in Lubombo, which offers internet access. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the government commissioned a Starlink gateway meant to serve remote and underserved areas. The ministry's E1.2 billion Eswatini Digital Project gives E648 million to affordable broadband, fibre and last-mile links. No count of rural sites, towers, localities or people connected has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

SYC.short: Nothing found names a programme to connect rural areas or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether rural areas are being connected or how far rural internet use lags urban.

TCD.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2026; sites connected are not counted.
TCD.summary: In March 2026 the PATN project unit said its connectivity component aims to lay 200 km of fibre and to bring 3G and 4G to 500 localities. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the telecoms secretary of state said about 500 communities lack connectivity. In November 2026 the minister told the ITU conference that 500 sites were being deployed with World Bank support, and 1,000 more were planned. No count of sites connected has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

TGO.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a programme to connect rural areas, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether a programme to connect rural areas is under way. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a programme to bring internet access to rural or underserved areas that the government or its universal service fund has launched, funded or prepared in the past three years.

TUN.short: A programme to bring internet to rural areas was under way in 2025; sites connected are not counted.
TUN.summary: In June 2025 the ministry launched tender 02/2025 to extend telecom and broadband coverage to 103 white zones, in 15 governorates. In 2022 the ministry closed its earlier white zones project, funded with TND 38 million, covering 94 sectors and 180,000 inhabitants. In the last twelve months, on 19 November 2026 the minister told parliament that TND 76 million funds a Tunisie Telecom contract to cover white zones, with works started. No count of white zones connected since October 2023 has been found. Establishing would need a rural programme that has connected a stated number of sites or people.

TZA.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
TZA.summary: By 23 October 2025 the UCSAF programme had activated 741 of 758 planned masts, connecting about 1,300 of 1,407 target villages. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 Helios Towers completed 133 sites under the government's universal service fund programme, UCSAF. In November 2026 the fund's implementation report showed 2,199 of 2,324 planned towers completed. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

UGA.short: The universal service fund had paid for more than 85 base stations by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
UGA.summary: In February 2024 the Uganda Communications Commission launched its Access Infrastructure Program in Agago. Of 63 subsidised sites for sub-counties under 30% 3G coverage, 7 were built and 4 operational. In the last twelve months, by April 2026 the fund had invested in more than 85 base stations in underserved areas. In November 2026 the ICT minister said the fund's work had helped bring network coverage to 96 per cent of the population. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

ZAF.short: SA Connect had reached 361,000 rural and township households by 2024; rural and urban use is not measured.
ZAF.summary: In March 2024 the minister said SA Connect had reached 361,000 households through 2,502 Wi-Fi hotspots, and it aims to connect 5 million rural and township households. By June 2025 Sentech and Broadband Infraco had installed more than 11,500 of 32,055 planned hotspots, the department said. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the British High Commission began funding community networks in rural KwaZulu-Natal. The minister approved the Universal Service and Access Fund manual, USAASA said in October 2026. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

ZMB.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2025; rural and urban use is not measured.
ZMB.summary: In September 2025 ZICTA said 43 of 51 remote-area towers were complete, within a roll-out of 152. In September 2025 the Smart Zambia Institute installed satellite internet in Moomba Chiefdom, Kazungula District, connecting a rural health clinic and two primary schools. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 ZICTA's board toured fund projects in Muchinga, Northern and Luapula provinces. In November 2026 the Smart Zambia Institute said the World Bank-backed Digital Zambia Acceleration Project plans 300 towers. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

ZWE.short: A rural connectivity programme had connected a stated number of sites or people by 2026; rural and urban use is not measured.
ZWE.summary: By September 2025 the POTRAZ tower relocation project had switched on 30 towers in rural and border communities. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the ICT minister said more than 10,000 remote sites had been connected. Free Wi-Fi reached rural business hubs under the Presidential Internet Scheme. On 23 October 2026 the minister directed POTRAZ to set fund targets for schools, clinics, chiefs' courts and rural business centres. No source found since October 2023 gives internet use in rural and in urban areas. Operating would need rural and urban internet use published from a household survey of the past three years.

AGO.short: Angola's identity law, amended in 2017 and 2021, gives each citizen a unique number on a chip card. No rules since 2023 are known.
AGO.summary: Angola's identity card rests on Law 4/09 on civil identification. The National Assembly amended it in August 2017 and in January 2021. Under the law as amended, each card's number acts in law as the unique citizen number. In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers reviewed a civil and criminal identification bill, and on 30 October the Assembly approved two of its chapters in detail. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the law, made in that time.

BDI.short: Burundi's identity card runs on ministerial orders of 1978 and 1986; in 2026 the texts for a national identification file were still to be adopted.
BDI.summary: Burundi's identity card runs on ministerial ordinances of 1978 and 1986, which the government's procedures page, held as published in January 2026, lists as its main texts. The page names no identity law. It says further texts remain to be adopted before the national identification file is instituted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law, ordinance or decree-law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card, however old.

BEN.short: Benin's 2017 identification law, amended in 2025, sets up a biometric register and a personal number. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
BEN.summary: Benin's law no. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 on the identification of natural persons is the law behind the national register and the personal identification number. In June 2025 the National Assembly adopted law no. 2025-12 amending its article 6. Article 6 as amended provides for a national biometric population register and a personal identification number. In July 2025 the Council of Ministers adopted a decree setting assurance levels for electronic identification schemes, made under the digital code. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the identification law, made in the past three years.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's 2024 identity law frames the national enrolment begun in November 2026; no rule made under it is on record.
BFA.summary: On 11 October 2024 the transitional legislative assembly adopted the bill on unique electronic identification of the natural person. On 19 August 2025 the minister for digital transition said the law had been adopted the previous year. In the last twelve months, Africa24 TV reported on 22 November 2026 that the national enrolment under way since 11 November is framed by the 2024 law. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found. Mature would need a rule made under the law in the past three years, such as a regulation or decree applying it.

BWA.short: Botswana's 1986 registration law, amended in 2025, gives each registered person an identity number; no rules made under it since 2023 are known.
BWA.summary: Botswana's National Registration Act commenced on 31 December 1986. The National Registration (Amendment) Act 2025 was assented on 23 March 2025, to start on a date the minister sets. Under it the registrar assigns an identity number to each person in a Unified Population Register. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the minister said it now lets passports and driving licences serve as identification while identity cards are replaced. No rule made under the Act since October 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the register.

CAF.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for the Central African Republic, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2019 law on digital identification is the basis of its biometric identity card. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
CIV.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's biometric identity project is backed by the Law on Digital Identification, no. 2019-566, an enacted law of five articles. A 2025 study of ten African identity systems treats it, an executive decree and the 2013 data protection law together as the legal basis of the system. The study says the 2019 law establishes the legal basis for the biometric digital identity and describes the identity document as a secure card serving several applications. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 civil registration law provides a unique personal identification number for every citizen. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
CMR.summary: Cameroon's Law 2024/016, the new civil registration law, is the law the national civil status office is implementing. This was reported in October 2025. The law authorises digital birth, marriage and death certificates and a unique personal identification number for every citizen. It is an identity law as well as a civil registration law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found since September 2023. Mature would need a rule made under the law in the past three years, such as a regulation or decree applying it.

COD.short: The DRC's population file rests on a 2022 decree; a bill on identifying persons was tabled in parliament in June 2026.
COD.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's population file was created by the Prime Minister's decree no. 22/07 of 2 March 2022, and no identity law is among its legal bases. In the last twelve months, on 12 June 2026 two deputies tabled a private member's bill on the general rules for identifying natural persons. The bill is to go to committee. It had not been debated by the end of September 2026. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

COG.short: Congo's identification number and identity card rest on decrees of 2004 and 2009, the latter amended in 2024; no identity law is known.
COG.summary: The Republic of the Congo's unique identification number was instituted by decree no. 2004-469 of 3 November 2004, and no law is named behind it. The national identity card rests on a 2009 decree, which decree no. 2024-2692 of 13 November 2024 amended. An order of 12 October 2022 made the number mandatory for eight economic transactions and five administrative formalities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No identity law has been found, and no bill for one. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

COM.short: The Comoros's 2014 law institutes a biometric identity card. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
COM.summary: The Comoros has law no. 14-023/AU of 24 June 2014, promulgated by decree no. 14-137/PR. The Ministry of Justice describes the 2014 law as instituting the Comorian digital, biometric identity card. That title is what is held on the law's content. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a rule made under the law in that time, or one that others must check identity against the system.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's 2013 law and 2014 decree-law set up an electronic identity card; the last rules known under them date from 2017.
CPV.summary: Cabo Verde's national civil identification and authentication system was created by Law 43/VIII/2013 of 17 September 2013. The national identification card was then created by Decree-Law 19/2014 of 17 March. The card is an electronic one whose chip holds a digital certificate. Two rules were made under the decree-law in 2017, one on biometric capture and one on the card's validity. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need a rule made under it in that time.

DJI.short: Djibouti's 2019 identification law sets up a unique number and biometric register; the last rules known under it date from 2020.
DJI.summary: Djibouti's law no. 39/AN/19 on the identification of natural persons was published on 21 January 2019. It creates a unique national identification number and a national register. A decree of 13 July 2020 was made under its article 9 and requires administrations, hospitals, schools, utilities and traders to carry the number on their documents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rule made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

DZA.short: Algeria's February 2026 law covers electronic identification, with a national number required since 2010. No rules made under the law are known.
DZA.summary: On 2 November 2025 Algeria's Council of Ministers approved a draft law on trust services and digital identification. In the last twelve months it became law no. 26-02 of 17 February 2026, which sets the rules for electronic identification. The Ministry of the Interior says executive decree 10-210 of 16 September 2010 instituted the national identification number. No regulation or decree applying the 2026 law has been found. Mature would need a rule made under the law, or one that others must check identity against the system.

EGY.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Egypt, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Eritrea, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's 2023 Digital Identification Proclamation sets up a biometric identity database. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
ETH.summary: Ethiopia's Digital Identification Proclamation, no. 1284/2023, passed the House of Peoples' Representatives in March 2023. It was signed by the President on 18 April 2023. The proclamation sets up a digital identification system that collects demographic and biometric data in a central database. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports a regulation or decree applying the law since September 2023. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years.

GAB.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Gabon, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

GHA.short: Ghana's identity Acts of 2006 and 2008 are in force; 2026 regulations require biometric verification against the national register.
GHA.summary: Ghana's identity system rests on two Acts that the National Identification Authority lists as its laws: the National Identification Authority Act, 2006 and the National Identity Register Act, 2008. In the last twelve months, regulations made under the 2008 Act were gazetted on 27 March 2026 and in force from 9 June 2026. They require organisations to verify identity through the Authority's system, in real time against its database. Before them, a notice of 15 February 2024 had specified the portable card readers that may be used. The regulations came into force on 9 June 2026.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023 identification law is in force, and an April 2025 decree applying it set up a biometric register with an identification number.
GIN.summary: Guinea's Law L/2023/019/CNT of 25 October 2023 on the identification of physical persons is the law under which a decree of April 2025 is made. The decree sets up a register of biographic and biometric data with a personal identification number. In the last twelve months, on 26 February 2026 the head of the identification office named the law at a workshop. A January 2026 workshop at Kindia reviewed and validated further draft decrees and orders applying the identification and civil status laws. No source found says those drafts have been signed.

GMB.short: A law in force gives citizens aged 18 or over the right to an identity card, reported 2026; no source found reports digital identity in it.
GMB.summary: Section 17 of the Nationality and Citizenship Act gives Gambian citizens aged 18 or over the right to a national identity card, Jollof News reported in June 2026. No separate national identity act has been found. The National Identification Authority runs the National Identity Management System. A National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028 was validated in 2024, and it is a strategy, not a law. In the last twelve months no source found says the law provides for a biometric register, a unique identity number or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

GNB.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Guinea-Bissau, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Equatorial Guinea, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

KEN.short: Kenya's digital identity system rests on a 2018 executive order and 2020 regulations, added to a 1947 act; it has no law of its own.
KEN.summary: Kenya's National Integrated Identity Management System began under executive order no. 1 of 2018, and Kenya has no stand-alone digital identity law. The government then wrote the system into the 1947 Registration of Persons Act by an omnibus amendment. The High Court ruled in January 2020 that a comprehensive regulatory framework should be enacted before roll-out. The system is anchored on the Huduma Namba regulations of 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2011 National Identification Registry Act sets up a biometric identification system. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBR.summary: Liberia's National Identification Registry Act was approved by the President on 1 August 2011 and published on 8 August 2011. It repeals a 1983 decree and sets up the National Identification Registry. The Act sets up a National Biometric Identification System and a biometric card for each person, enrolled with a fingerprint and a photograph. No later amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years, or one that others must check identity against the system.

LBY.short: Libya's 2014 national number law gives each citizen a unique number in a biometric database. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBY.summary: Libya's Law No. 8 of 2014 on the National Number was issued by the General National Congress on 24 March 2014 and took effect on issue. The law provides for a twelve-digit national number unique to each citizen. It also provides for a national database completed with ten fingerprints, an iris print, a photograph and a signature. No amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2011 identity cards law, in force since 2013, sets up a biometric register and unique number. No rules since 2023 are known.
LSO.summary: Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act, 2011 was published in the Government Gazette on 21 March 2011 and commenced on 1 July 2013. The Act establishes a National Identity Register that records fingerprints and an image for everyone aged sixteen and over. It assigns each entry a unique national identity number and provides for a chip card. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a rule made under it in the past three years, or one that others must check identity against the system.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2020 law creates a population register against which identity is checked online. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
MAR.summary: Morocco's law no. 72-18, on the targeting of beneficiaries of social support programmes, was promulgated on 8 August 2020 and published in the Bulletin officiel on 7 January 2021. It creates the national population register and the national registers agency. Its second article defines authentication as checking declared data online and in real time against the national population register. No bill to replace the law is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

MDG.short: Madagascar's parliament passed an identification law in July 2025 and the constitutional court cleared it. No source found says whether it has been promulgated.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's law no. 2025-019 on the identification of natural persons was adopted by the National Assembly on 3 July 2025 and by the Senate on 4 July 2025. The President referred it for review before promulgation. On 26 August 2025 the High Constitutional Court ruled that it conforms to the Constitution. That decision is the last step on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the law has been promulgated or that a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

MLI.short: Mali's 2006 law gives each person a unique identification number; the last rule known under it is a decree of November 2022.
MLI.summary: Mali's law no. 06-040 of 11 August 2006 institutes the national identification number and a national identification register. A decree of 18 October 2006 fixes the fourteen-digit number and obliges public services to use it. A decree of 3 November 2022 requires the number for any biometric identity card application and cites the 2006 law as its basis. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's 2022 civil identification and identity card law is in force; no source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
MOZ.summary: On 16 March 2022 the Assembly of the Republic passed a bill in first reading on civil identification and the identity card. In May 2025 the ICT regulator listed Law 6/2022 on civil identification and the identity card among the laws in force. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 a tender was launched for a consultancy on mobile digital identity and signatures. No source found says whether Law 6/2022 provides for a biometric register. None says whether it provides for a unique number or an electronic check. Operating would need a digital identity in the law in force.

MRT.short: Mauritania's civil status code, amended in February 2025, provides for a national biometric population register. No rules made under it since are known.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's identity system rests on its Civil Status Code, law no. 2011-003 of 12 January 2011. Law no. 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 replaced three of its articles. The code as amended provides for the national biometric population register in its new article 31. Its new article 15 provides for digital civil status acts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

MUS.short: Mauritius's 1985 identity card law is in force; 2024 regulations under it set a new card with a digital seal and fingerprints.
MUS.summary: Mauritius's identity card rests on the National Identity Card Act, No. 60 of 1985, which the identity card unit lists as the law behind the card system. The National Identity Card Regulations 2024 were made by the minister on 16 February 2024 and revoke the regulations of 2013. Through them the Act provides for a card that is biometric and can be checked electronically. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is the issue of the new card from 19 February 2024.

MWI.short: Malawi's 2010 National Registration Act founds its digital identity system; no rule applying it since 2023 is known beyond a fee change.
MWI.summary: Malawi's National Registration Act of 2010 mandates the registration bureau to run the national registration and identification system, the Principal Secretary says. A 2025 presentation says the National Registration Act No. 13 of 2010 was enacted as the legal foundation for the national digital identity system. In the last twelve months, on 23 July 2026 the Homeland Security Minister made amendment regulations under it, which raised registration fees. Fee changes do not count. No other rule made under the Act since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need a regulation applying the Act, or a rule that others must check identity against it.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2024 Civil Registration and Identification Act provides a unique number and electronic identity documents. No rules made under it are known.
NAM.summary: Namibia's Civil Registration and Identification Act, No. 13 of 2024, is the statute for civil registration and legal identity. The Act assigns each person a unique identity number and authorises physical or electronic identity documents. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 an official of the Office of the Prime Minister said it allows institutions to accept either the physical card or its digital version. No change to the Act has been found. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

NER.short: Niger's cabinet adopted a draft ordinance in April 2026 adding a unique identifier and biometrics to its registers. No source found says it was signed.
NER.summary: On 22 April 2026 Niger's Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance on the civil status regime. It amends law no. 2019-29 of 1 July 2019 and would add biometric parameters and a unique identifier to the registers that law set up. In the last twelve months this draft is the one change: until it is signed, the 2019 law stands as a civil status law. No source found says the draft has been signed, or that a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a national identity law in force.

NGA.short: Nigeria's NIMC Act 2026, signed in June, makes the identity number foundational and provides for electronic verification. No rules made under it are known.
NGA.summary: Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 was signed into law on 26 June 2026, repealing the 2007 Act. The Act reaffirms the national identification number as the foundational identity and makes the Commission responsible for verifying electronic identities. It makes the Commission the national repository for biometric data. On 29 July 2026 a civil society speaker said the gazetted text was not yet available. In the last twelve months this Act replaced the 2007 Act. No regulation made under it has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

RWA.short: Rwanda's single digital identity law, reported in 2026, ends old identity cards by June 2027. No rules made under it are known.
RWA.summary: In March 2026 The New Times reported that Rwanda's law governing registration into its single digital identity system sets a June 2027 deadline after which existing national identity cards are no longer valid. The system is built on a unique digital identification number, a derived token and a card with a QR code. The identity agency's head said the identity law was amended in 2023. The law's number and date are not given. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under it since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule.

SDN.short: Sudan's 2011 Civil Registry Act gives each citizen a unique national number in an electronic register. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
SDN.summary: Sudan's Civil Registry Act 2011 was signed by the President, repealed the 2001 Act and came into force on signature. The Act defines the national number as a unique number given to each citizen on registration. It provides for civil registry records to be stored electronically and for a central database. No later amendment is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2016 law institutes a biometric identity card; a bill to extend card validity was before parliament in September 2026.
SEN.summary: Senegal's identity card rests on a 2016 law instituting the ECOWAS biometric identity card. In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a bill to amend it and extend how long cards are valid. On 29 September 2026 that bill, numbered 21/2026, was before the National Assembly. An Interior Ministry official said on 24 September 2026 that the amending text would extend the 2016 cards. No regulation or decree made under the 2016 law has been found from the last three years. Mature would need such a rule.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone validated a draft civil registration and identification bill in November 2025; it had still to reach Cabinet and Parliament.
SLE.summary: On 17 November 2025 Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority held the final national validation of the draft National Civil Registration and Identification Bill and its regulations. The bill has still to go to Cabinet and then to Parliament. It is the draft that would replace the present registration law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law, ordinance or decree-law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 identification law is in force; a 2024 regulation applies it and sets rules for banks and phone companies checking identity.
SOM.summary: Somalia's Public Identification and Registration Law, Law No. 009 of 20 March 2023, is in force. On 8 June 2024 the Prime Minister signed an implementing regulation made under it, which took effect on signature. The regulation applies the law and sets rules for relying parties, among them banks and phone companies, which check identity against the system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact is the regulation of 8 June 2024.

SSD.short: South Sudan's 2018 Civil Registry Act and 2024 regulations provide for a personal identification number; the World Bank calls them under-implemented.
SSD.summary: South Sudan's Civil Registry Act of 2018, with the Nationality Act of 2011, is the legal foundation of its identification system, a World Bank diagnostic of May 2026 says. The Civil Registration and National Identity Regulations, 2024, were made under sections 33 and 39 of the Act. The Bank says the two lay the foundation for an interoperable digital identity system based on a personal identification number. In the last twelve months the Act and regulations were cited and not changed. The Bank calls the framework under-implemented, and how far it is applied is the open question.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe had a new identity law in draft in September 2025. No source found says whether it has been approved.
STP.summary: A World Bank mission of 8 to 12 September 2025 flagged as urgent the review, public consultation, finalisation and approval of São Tomé and Príncipe's new identity law. The mission's note calls it the aggregated identification document law and treats it as drafted and not yet approved. It warned that without the law's approval the collection of data could be constrained. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national identity law is in force. Establishing would need a law in force that sets up the identity number, the register of persons or the identity card.

SWZ.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Eswatini, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

SYC.short: Seychelles' identity cards law, amended in 2023, is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
SYC.summary: Seychelles' National Identity Cards Act, Cap. 294, is in force. The Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2023, assented to on 8 November 2023, amended it. The 2023 amendment adds a card for non-resident citizens and new rules on disclosing card information. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no replacement bill is on record. No source found says the law provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

TCD.short: A 2020 ordinance, ratified by law, sets up a biometric population register and unique national number; no source found reports rules made since 2023.
TCD.summary: Chad's Ordinance 002/PR/2020 of 14 February 2020 on civil status was ratified by Law 006/PR/2020 of 29 May 2020. It sets up a system that issues a unique national identification number through the national biometric population register. In the last twelve months the ordinance was cited and not changed, in a UNHCR study of April 2026. In April 2025 the telecoms regulator ARCEP said every SIM card sold must be linked to an NNI under the texts in force. No source gives the rule or its date. Mature would need a regulation or decree applying the law, made in the past three years.

TGO.short: Togo's 2020 biometric identification law, amended in 2022, sets up a unique number; the last rule known under it is a September 2022 decree.
TGO.summary: Togo's law no. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on the biometric identification of natural persons created the national identification agency. Law no. 2022-010 of 24 June 2022 amended several of its articles. The amended law defines a unique identification number issued after verification of demographic and biometric data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest rule found is a decree of 9 September 2022, and no rule made under the law since September 2023 has been found. Mature would need such a rule, or one that others must check identity against the system.

TUN.short: Tunisia's organic law of March 2024 provides for a biometric identity card with an electronic certificate. No rules made under it are known.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's Organic Law No. 2024-22 of 11 March 2024 amends and completes the 1993 law on the national identity card. It provides that the identity card carries an encrypted electronic chip, which holds an electronic certificate for verifying identity and signing documents. In September 2025 La Presse reported that the decrees on the card's model, specifications and security standards were still being prepared. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation or decree applying the law has been found. Mature would need such a rule, made in the past three years.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 1986 registration and identification law is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
TZA.summary: Tanzania's Registration and Identification of Persons Act, first passed in 1986, is recorded as still in force in the 2023 revised edition of the laws. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the government said it would table an Infant Registration Bill in the session starting 27 January 2026. The bill would let the identification authority register children from birth. No report says it has been tabled or passed. No source found says the 1986 Act provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2015 Registration of Persons Act provides a unique number and biometric register; regulations were made under it in August 2024.
UGA.summary: Uganda's Registration of Persons Act, 2015 was assented to on 26 March 2015. The Act has the Authority assign a unique national identification number to every person registered and defines identity data to include fingerprints. Regulations made under it on 12 August 2024 set the card's validity at eleven years. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A Parliament release of 20 August 2026 describes the Authority as working under the Act, and in June 2026 the Authority said registered foreigners are given a unique identification number under the Act. The latest dated fact is the release of 20 August 2026.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 1997 Identification Act is in force, with a replacement bill due in 2027 or 2028. No source found says it covers digital identity.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's Identification Act of 1997 is in force. It makes Home Affairs the sole authority keeping the National Population Register, and its regulations were last amended on 23 June 2025. In the last twelve months, Home Affairs gazetted draft regulations in May 2026 that would regulate access to identity information; they were still drafts at the end of September 2026. A replacement bill is due in Parliament only in 2027 or 2028. No source found says the 1997 Act provides for a biometric register, a unique identity number or electronic checks. Operating would need a law in force that provides for digital identity.

ZMB.short: Zambia's National Registration Act is in force, with regulations of 2019. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
ZMB.summary: Zambia's National Registration Regulations, 2019, Statutory Instrument No. 34 of 2019, were made under section 14 of the National Registration Act. The regulations prescribe the registration procedure, and require an application, a photograph, fingerprints and a birth certificate. No amendment to the Act since 2019 is on record, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the Act provides for a biometric register. None says it provides for a unique number or electronic checks. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.
