ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 1976 National Registration Act is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe's National Registration Act commenced on 24 September 1976. It provides for the registration of residents and a register kept by the Registrar-General. A statutory instrument gazetted on 30 January 2024 was made under its section 11 and amends the registration fees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the Act, or an amendment to it, provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person or an identity checked electronically. Operating would need the law in force to provide for a digital identity.

AGO.short: The president authorised national digital-skills training programmes in 2026; a count of people trained has not been found.
AGO.summary: In June 2024 the interbank services company EMIS said its Cidadão Digital project had trained over 500,000 young people. By December 2024 it reported over 600,000 people reached since 2022. No government body is named for these counts. In the last twelve months, a presidential order of August 2026 gave US$5 million to a national programme in basic digital skills. In October 2026 President João Lourenço authorised US$20 million for digital-skills centres. No count of people trained by a government programme has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, that has trained a stated number of people.

BDI.short: Burundi's digital ministry trained 102 girls from all provinces in digital skills in 2025; no survey measures the share.
BDI.summary: On 25 September 2025 the digital economy ministry launched phase III of the AGCCI coding camps. The camps trained 102 girls aged 17-25 from all provinces in digital literacy and coding. UN Women Burundi and Belgium funded them. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the coordinator of the PAFEN project said a basic digital skills programme to train 10,000 young people within a year would start soon. No survey share of people with basic digital skills has been found. Operating would need a measured share of adults, or of the population, with basic digital skills, published from a survey.

BEN.short: The government opened applications for national digital-skills training in 2025; a count of people trained has not been found.
BEN.summary: In October 2025 the government opened a national call for digital skills training for young people. The training is the OIF's D-CLIC programme, run through the School of Digital Professions. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, Benin became the first pilot country of the SNAEIA network's AI initiative. Its programme trains young people in digital tools and skills. No count of people trained by a programme in service has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

BFA.short: A World Bank-financed digital project includes digital-skills training from 2023; a national programme's count of people trained has not been found.
BFA.summary: Burkina Faso's digital skills work runs through PACTDIGITAL, a World Bank-financed project. Its appraisal document of 22 December 2023 gives US$22 million to a digital skills component, which aims to widen access to digital skills programmes. In the last twelve months, on 9 November 2026, the ministry's secretary general announced a free ICT training campaign of about five weeks. It covers office software, AI, cybersecurity, networks and web and mobile development. No count of people trained by a national programme has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

BWA.short: Botswana ran digital-skills sessions and a library roadshow from 2023; no source found reports the number of people any programme trained.
BWA.summary: The government's EU-funded digital programme began in August 2024. It includes digital-skills training for women and young entrepreneurs. Statistics Botswana's 2024 ICT household survey found 59.2 per cent of individuals had e-skills. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the regulator BOCRA ran ICT training at four schools. Statistics Botswana presented the survey to an ITU expert group in 2026. No count of people trained by a public programme in more than one location has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

CAF.short: A UNESCO digital-skills project allocates funds to the country; no government programme has been found, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: No stage is set. The only fact found is a UNESCO digital-skills project that covers several countries and allocates funds to the Central African Republic. It names no government programme. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Looked for and not found: a government programme to teach the public digital skills, a count of people trained, and a survey of the share of people with basic digital skills. No source from the past three years has been found that says no such programme exists. Preparing would need the government, alone or with partners, to have launched, piloted or be preparing a programme to teach digital skills to the public.

CIV.short: The government planned and funded digital-skills training in 2025 and 2026; a count of people trained has not been found.
CIV.summary: A youth ministry adviser said in July 2025 that the government's youth programme had given digital skills to 51,601 young people since 2023. In February 2025 the Prime Minister launched the GENIE project. In the last twelve months, the 2026-2030 national plan sets out digital-training investments of about 95 billion FCFA. In November 2026 the digital minister set a target of 200,000 people trained in cybersecurity, networking and AI by 2030. No location has been found for the 51,601 young people trained. Establishing would need the government programme to be in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

CMR.short: The ICT agency and posts ministry launched digital-skills campaigns for young people in 2024 and 2025; no source found says how many were trained.
CMR.summary: In July 2024 the national ICT agency ANTIC launched the sixth Cameroon Digital Skills Campaign in Douala. The three-day event drew over 100 students. In June 2025 the posts and telecommunications minister launched a Digital Citizenship Festival that aims to train 50,000 young people through regional and national events. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count of people trained by a government programme has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

COD.short: A national programme to train 250,000 young people certified its first trainers in 2026; no source found says how many have been trained.
COD.summary: In October 2025 the youth ministry signed an accord with Cisco and Cybastion to train 250,000 young people in digital skills. The first train-the-trainer phase, with 500 trainees, ended in Kinshasa in February 2026. In the last twelve months, on 28 February 2026, the digital economy minister gave the trainers their certificates. They are to be deployed nationwide over five years. The 500 counted are trainers, and no count of young people trained has been found. Establishing would need the programme to be in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

COG.short: The government launched a digital project with public skills training in 2025; a count of people trained has not been found.
COG.summary: The EU part of the government's digital transformation project was launched on 17 June 2025. It aims to develop the digital skills of the population, especially young people and women. The earlier Congo Digital Transformation Project, launched in January 2023, provides for 3,000 people to acquire certified digital skills from basic to advanced. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count of people trained has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

COM.short: Nothing found names a national digital-skills programme or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the public is taught digital skills.

CPV.short: The government launched a digital-skills programme for 3,000 young people in 2026; a count of people trained has not been found.
CPV.summary: In January 2026 the government launched Skodji Digital to train up to 3,000 young people. Its first phase took 1,050 participants. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, a 15-station TechLab opened in Brava as a national pilot of the programme. A national digital-skills strategy is being prepared under the World Bank-funded Digital Cabo Verde project. No source found says the programme is in service in more than one location with a stated number of people trained. Establishing would need that: a government digital-skills programme for the public in service in more than one location, with a stated number trained.

DJI.short: A national digital-skills programme was under way in 2026; how many it trained is not on record.
DJI.summary: The World Bank counted 226 people, 79 of them women, given improved digital skills under the Djibouti Digital Foundations Project by 31 August 2024. The project's coding academy had not started by then. In the last twelve months, the government launched a feasibility study (statement of 13 May 2026) for Digital Houses in five inland regions under the E-SKILLS programme. The programme aims to train at least 3,000 young people and women by 2029 for about EUR 7 million. No count of people trained by a public programme in service has been found. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

DZA.short: The vocational training ministry launched a national AI skills course in 2026; a count of people trained has not been found.
DZA.summary: The national 7-77 digital inclusion programme opened in July 2026. By August its 40 online sessions had reached 1,166 people. Algérie Télécom began in-person sessions for 600 people at Sétif on 9 August 2026. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the vocational training ministry launched a national 12-week training programme in artificial intelligence. The count of 1,166 is for online sessions and is not tied to more than one location. Establishing would need a government digital-skills programme for the public, in service in more than one location, with a stated number of people trained.

EGY.short: The communications ministry's programmes had trained about 277,000 people by 2025; no survey of the share with digital skills has been found.
EGY.summary: The communications ministry says its Digital Egypt Generations initiatives trained about 156,000 people in 2025. They had trained about 277,000 since launch through the end of 2025. In November 2024 the deputy minister said the ministry's digital literacy initiatives had reached 1,122,837 citizens. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, Minister Raafat Hindy said the ministry's digital-skills programmes run in all governorates. He said over 2 million citizens benefited over ten years. No survey share of people with basic digital skills has been found. Operating would need a measured share of adults, or of the population, with basic digital skills, published from a survey.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a national digital-skills programme or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the public is taught digital skills.

ETH.short: A national digital-literacy certification had trained about 200,000 students and 3,000 community members by 2025; no survey share has been found.

No count of people trained by the programme has been found. Cyber Liberia 2030 is to train 20,000 people in digital literacy and cybersecurity from October 2026. No survey share of people with basic digital skills has been found. It names no government programme. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Looked for and not found: a government programme to teach the public digital skills, a count of people trained, and a survey of the share of people with basic digital skills. No source from the past three years has been found that says no such programme exists. Preparing would need the government, alone or with partners, to have launched, piloted or be preparing a programme to teach digital skills to the public.

LSO.short: A 2023 household survey found 35.1 per cent of people had ICT skills; no survey share of half or more has been found.

No count of people trained by a programme in service has been found. MOZ.summary: An ITU-EU pilot in Matola trained 50 young people and 5 teachers. In May 2025 the education ministry signed to expand the DiGi school project. The Machel Fidus Association runs it in 24 secondary schools and has trained over 900 students. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the youth ministry signed for a national programme to train about 40,000 young people. It is piloting in five provinces. No count of people trained by a government programme in more than one location has been found. Simplon said its earlier work with the French embassy gave basic digital skills to nearly 5,000 people. No count of people trained by a government programme has been found. MUS.short: Mauritius launched community digital training in 2025 and a free online course portal in 2026; no source found reports the number of people trained.
MUS.summary: In May 2025 the IT minister launched the first Community Digital Empowerment Programme in Bel Air. Similar events are planned in other regions. The 2024 ICT household indicators give 62.2 per cent of people aged five and over able to use a computer. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, Mauritius Telecom and AWS launched a free portal of 16 digital and AI courses, toward the government's target of 50,000 people trained. No count of people trained by a public programme in more than one location has been found. MWI.short: A 2024 statistics office study found 1.4 per cent of Malawians had digital skills, while government hubs trained over 19,000 people.
MWI.summary: The government's World Bank-funded Digital Malawi Project had taught digital skills to over 19,000 people by August 2024. The training ran at 10 tech hubs. A study by the National Statistical Office and the regulator MACRA found that 1.4 per cent of Malawians had digital skills. It was reported in May 2024. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, UNDP launched a programme for 30 students to train 3,000 people. No survey has been found that shows half or more of adults with basic digital skills. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, its Hardap office ran a two-week course for 20 people in Maltahohe. In October 2026 the ICT minister highlighted Project 1000, for young people's digital skills. In May 2026 Huawei launched a Women in Tech programme. No survey share of people with basic digital skills has been found. Operating would need a measured share of adults, or of the population, with basic digital skills, published from a survey.

By February 2025 its coordinator put the number trained at 350,000, with digital centres in all eight regions. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the governor of Tahoua launched free digital training for 140 young people. NGA.short: A 2026 national survey found 77.5 per cent of adults could do at least one of eight digital tasks; no source found says which tasks.

It found 77.5 per cent of adults able to perform at least one of eight digital tasks. NITDA plans to measure the same indicators each year. President Tinubu said in December 2025 that the 3MTT programme had trained 30,000 young people. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, NITDA's National Digital Literacy Dashboard recorded about 2.76 million training achievements since January 2022. The Federal Government launched a Digital Training Academy on 14 September 2026. The eight digital tasks the survey counted are not listed in the source found.

RWA.short: The Digital Ambassadors Programme had trained over 4.5 million people in every district by 2025; no source found reports the share with digital skills.

The programme has run since 2017, with over 2,000 ambassadors in every district. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the education and ICT ministries, with Huawei, launched the DigiTruck, a mobile classroom for free digital skills training. The World Bank-funded Digital Acceleration Project will take the Digital Ambassadors Programme to all 2,148 cells, The New Times reports. No survey share of people with basic digital skills has been found. Operating would need a measured share of adults, or of the population, with basic digital skills, published from a survey.

In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the ICT minister said the Digital Skills Ambassadors Programme had trained over 2,300 people in one district in a week. Mature would need a measured share of half or more of adults, or of the population, with basic digital skills, to be published.

At the opening the telecoms ministry said the government cloud is expected to keep information within national borders. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

BDI.short: Keeping state data under national control was a stated goal in 2026; a rule in force is not on record.
BDI.summary: Iwacu reports that Burundi's national AI strategy was validated at a workshop in April 2026. The strategy provides for modernising the Setic data center and developing a sovereign cloud. In the last twelve months, the strategy validated on 22 April 2026 is the step found: it pairs sovereign cloud solutions with data centre modernisation. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

BEN.short: Keeping state data under national control was a stated goal in 2026; a rule in force is not on record.
BEN.summary: Decree 2026-579 of 2 September 2026 created a National Digital Committee under the President, with protection of strategic data among its priorities. In the last twelve months, Benin's digital agency ASIN proposed in June 2026 a governance framework for generative-AI use in public administration. It calls for sovereign hosting and contractual reversibility. In October 2026 an official said Beninese data stays in Benin. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

BFA.short: Government data or a core system was hosted in the country in 2026; contract terms on data are not on record.

The ANPTIC portal says the G-Cloud has 4 datacentres and 8 cloud nodes. In the last twelve months, an official said in August 2026 that over 120 government platforms are hosted abroad and their repatriation has begun. No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit. Mature would need a foreign-provider contract with terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or source code.

BWA.short: Botswana is moving government systems to a national data centre; no rule in force covers state data.
BWA.summary: Mmegi reports that Botswana's Data Protection Act, in effect since January 2025, requires a copy of data sent abroad to remain in Botswana. It covers personal data in general, not state data. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the communications minister said the whole government system is being migrated to a secure government cloud. In April 2026 BoFiNet's chief executive said government had decided to move its critical services to the Digital Delta Data Centre. No source found since October 2023 says a rule in force covers state data. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

CAF.short: A 2024 source says no rule governs where state data is held.
CAF.summary: Paradigm Initiative's Londa 2023 report, published in 2024, says the Central African Republic has no stand-alone data protection law or regulation. It has none specifically on biometric databases or on data localisation, and no officially recognised national cybersecurity strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says control of state data is a stated goal. Preparing would need a government strategy, plan or draft rule to keep state data or systems under national control.

CIV.short: Keeping state data under national control was a stated goal in 2024; a rule in force is not on record.

Such data must be processed and stored inside Côte d'Ivoire. In the last twelve months, the digital minister said in December 2025 that the national data centre at VITIB Grand-Bassam will host the State's strategic data. In July 2026 Digital Mag reported the centre due by the end of 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a rule on state data is in force. Establishing would need a law or policy in force that classifies state data or keeps it in the country.

CMR.short: Cameroon hosts government data at Camtel's Zamengoe data centre; no rule in force covers state data.
CMR.summary: At SAGO 2026, Le Jour reports, Camtel presented the Tier III Zamengoe data centre it is building. Its aim is to preserve data generated on national territory. In the last twelve months, CAMTEL said at the SAGO conference of 9 June 2026 that the centre ensures the security, continuity and local control of government data. Cameroon's personal data protection law imposes local storage requirements. It covers personal data in general, not state data. CMR.summary: The Plan stratégique Cameroun numérique 2020, dated May 2016, calls itself the adopted strategic plan and names no adopting act. Its period ended by 2025. A workshop on 3 July 2025 discussed the diagnostic for updating it. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the minister said a draft national strategy for the digital economy was being finalised. No adopted text or period has been found for the new strategy. Establishing would need that strategy adopted, with a public text and a period that has not ended.

COD.short: DR Congo adopted a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period; no source found says its 2026 successor has been adopted.
COD.summary: The national validation workshop of 3-5 September 2019 validated the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, whose full text is on the Presidency's site. The ADN coordinator said in November 2023 that it was adopted in 2019. In the last twelve months its successor, the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030, was technically validated on 21-22 July 2026. No adopting act has been found for the plan or its successors. Establishing would need an adopted successor with a public text.

COG.short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; no source found reports its successor awaits approval, and its action plan and monitoring.
COG.summary: Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019 approves Vision Congo Digital 2025, and it appeared in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019. The ITU repository gives the time frame as 2021 to 2025. A successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, was reported complete on 13 October 2025 and awaits approval by decree. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No public text of the strategy has been found, and no domestic budget line. Establishing would need a public text of an adopted strategy whose period has not ended.

COM.short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; no source found reports results against its targets.
COM.summary: The digital health strategy says the Government drew up Comores Numérique 2028 and adopted it in 2018. Its text is public on ANADEN's site, and its roadmap runs from 2018 to 2028. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: on 25 August 2026 the minister said ANADEN is to contribute to implementing the strategy across the economy. No published report on results against the strategy's targets has been found. Operating would need such results published, and a domestic budget line.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; no source found reports its public text, plan and reporting.
CPV.summary: Resolução 72/2026 lists the Estratégia para a Economia Digital de Cabo Verde as approved in September 2024, covering 2025 to 2030. On 25 November 2025 it was presented to the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital. In the last twelve months, a consultation on 6 August 2026 covered the Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035, which the resolution only establishes the bases of. No public text of the strategy has been found. Establishing would need that text to be public.

DJI.short: Djibouti's cabinet heard a digital economy roadmap in March 2023; no source found says whether it was adopted.
DJI.summary: The minister delegate for the digital economy presented the roadmap to the Council of Ministers in March 2023, as the Djibouti Smart Nation roadmap for the digital economy. The government record notes no adoption. The Council of Ministers of 7 October 2025 listed drawing up a national digital strategy among the main challenges left. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No adoption, text, period, delivery plan or report has been found for the roadmap. Establishing would need a national digital strategy adopted, with a public text and a period that has not ended.

DZA.short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but no source found reports costs and results against its targets.
DZA.summary: On 12 May 2025 the High Commissioner called the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 the approved strategy. Its text is published on the High Commission's site, in an August 2024 version. In the last twelve months, the National Digital Services Centre was inaugurated on 5 July 2026, and on 12 July 2026 the Council of Ministers gave administrations one month to connect to the National Data Center. No adopting act, cost for the plan or domestic budget line has been found. Operating would need published results against the strategy's own targets.

EGY.short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but no source found reports its text, plan and recent progress.
EGY.summary: The ITU repository's 2025 listing records the Digital Egypt Strategy as adopted, with a time frame of 2016 onward. On 13 March 2024 the Prime Minister listed approval of a National strategy for building a fully digital state among the Supreme Council's objectives. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest figures found are from the 17 November 2024 briefing. No adopting act, public text or domestic budget line has been found, and no approval of the fully digital state strategy. Establishing would need a public text of an adopted strategy.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; no source found says whether any is in preparation.
ERI.summary: Levellers, in a legal-status page reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy. The page also says Eritrea has no published national AI strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The only statement of absence is a third-party page, and no Eritrean government source has been found. No instrument in preparation has been found. Preparing would need a national digital strategy announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030, running to 2030, in November 2025, but no source found says whether its text is public.
ETH.summary: The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 on 29 November 2025. The Prime Minister launched it on 20 December 2025 as the successor to Digital Ethiopia 2025, which covered 2020 to 2025. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology describes the new strategy as a five-year journey to 2030. In the last twelve months, on 30 July 2026, the National Digital Transformation Council reviewed progress on the Digital Ethiopia Strategy, Fayda and 5 Million Coders. No public text has been found for Digital Ethiopia 2030. Establishing would need that text to be public.

GAB.short: Gabon was drafting a national digitalisation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in 2026; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
GAB.summary: On 3 April 2026 the minister presented the main orientations of the national digitalisation strategy to state IT directors. On 13 May 2026 the draft Stratégie nationale de Digitalisation et d'Innovation went to the technical committee. In June 2026 he outlined a digital development plan for 2025 to 2030. All three steps came in the last twelve months. The strategy is to follow the earlier Gabon Digital strategy, whose time frame was 2020 to 2025. No adoption or public text has been found. Establishing would need the strategy adopted, with its text public.

GHA.short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; no source found says whether any progress report exists.
GHA.summary: The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation adopted the Digital Economy Policy in October 2024. The policy and strategy text is public, published in 2024. It sets a target timeline of 2028 for its objectives and lists actions with assigned responsibilities, but states no cost. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The ministry began a successor strategy in April 2025, still in preparation. No progress report and no mandated body have been found. Operating would need published results against the policy's own targets, a mandated body and a domestic budget line.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but no source found says whether any progress report exists.
GIN.summary: Version 1.2 of the strategy, dated 11 June 2024, calls itself the Transition Government's strategy. The full text is published as a PDF, and the strategy runs from 2023 to 2027. In the last twelve months, on 24 April 2026, the digital economy ministry sought a consultant to draft a new ICT and digital economy policy for 2026 to 2030. In December 2024 the minister had said the current strategy had been in implementation since 2022. No implementation or results report has been found, and no adopting act. Operating would need results published against the strategy's own targets.

GMB.short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; no source found reports its delivery plan and any progress report.
GMB.summary: The National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is issued by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy. Its PDF is on the ministry's website, published in 2024. The Digital Cooperation Organization reports that the government adopted the master plan. Its data is current to September 2024. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. An article of 7 October 2026 gives it as running 2024-2034. No delivery plan, reporting or adopting act has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against its targets.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but no source found reports any report on results.
GNB.summary: Decreto 10/2025 approves the ENTD.GW 2025-2030. The Council of Ministers approved it on 13 March, and the decree was published in the Boletim Oficial on 28 March 2025. The strategy's full text is public as the annex to the gazetted decree, with 55 interventions that each have a start and end date. In the last twelve months, on 9 September 2026, UNU-EGOV discussed a project document for carrying out the strategy with a ministry delegation. No published report against the strategy's targets has been found, and no cost for its actions. Operating would need published results against its own targets, and a mandated body.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026; no source reports its adoption or a published text.
GNQ.summary: The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation opened a World Bank-supported working week on 2 September 2026 to complete and validate the Estrategia Nacional de Economía Digital. The ministry expected a consensus roadmap at its close. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda was launched by the ministry in 2019 for 2019 to 2025. The working week is the one step found in the last twelve months. No adopting act, period, plan, reporting or published text has been found for the strategy. Establishing would need the strategy adopted, with its text public.

KEN.short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but no source found reports any published report against its targets.
KEN.summary: The Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is issued by the Ministry of ICT, Innovation and Youth Affairs. It was unveiled and launched by ICT Cabinet Secretary Joe Mucheru on 12 April 2022. Its full text is published on the ICT Authority site. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. An ICT Authority tender of 15 September 2026 cites the plan's national target of 100,000 km of fibre network. No published report against the plan's targets has been found. No domestic budget line has been found. Operating would need results against the plan's own targets, published within three years.

LBR.short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but no source reports results against its targets.
LBR.summary: The strategy covers 2025 to 2029, and its full text is on the ministry's website. It was officially launched at the National Coordination Session of Digital Liberia Week, held during 28-30 October 2025. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the National Data Governance Policy of March 2026 lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the instruments Liberia has adopted. No progress report against the strategy's targets has been found, and no adopting act or date. Operating would need results published against its own targets.

LBY.short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but no source found reports its approved text.
LBY.summary: The Prime Minister approved the strategy on 21 April 2025, following the General Information Authority's December 2022 proposal. In the last twelve months, on 19 April 2026, the Authority described Level 3 biometric digital identity trials as part of implementing the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030. A National Committee for Digital Transformation is named responsible for it in November 2026. Only the December 2022 proposal has been found as text, and no budget or results report. Establishing would need the approved text to be public.

LSO.short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but no source found reports its action plan and results.
LSO.summary: The finance minister told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that the Digital Transformation Strategy had been approved. The strategy's text is published on the government's website, self-dated 2024 and running to 2030. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the 2027/28 Budget Strategy Paper of October 2026 commits government to fast-track the 2024-2030 strategy. No adopting act or date has been found, and no finance or results report. No detailed action plan has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the strategy's targets.

MAR.short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but no source reports a public text.
MAR.summary: The ITU repository lists Digital Morocco 2030 among the strategies it says countries have adopted, with a time frame of 2024-2030. The Government Council heard a presentation of its general orientations on 25 January 2024. In the last twelve months, the ministry signed a memorandum with Capgemini Maroc on AI skills on 17 July 2026 and one with Orange Morocco on 4 June 2026. Both were presented as implementing Maroc Digital 2030. No public text has been found, and no adopting act or date is stated. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

MDG.short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but no source reports its adoption and public text.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's digital ministry estimates its budget at USD 800.169 million for the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028. Newsmada reports the digital minister presented the plan on 19 January 2024. In the last twelve months, the ministry and UNDP handed over the final Digital Readiness Assessment report on 17 December 2025, which is to be the basis for a national roadmap. On 16 October 2026 GSMA said its priorities support the plan. No source found says the plan was adopted or approved, and no public text has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

MLI.short: Mali has a digital economy policy validated in 2024 with an action plan to 2029, but no source found reports its adoption.
MLI.summary: Mali's Politique nationale de développement de l'économie numérique was validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024. The validated policy comes with an action plan for 2025-2029, while Malijet describes the policy itself as covering 2021-2034. The minister is quoted giving an execution rate of 27.30% for the previous version, 2015-2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that the policy was adopted, and no public text has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

MOZ.short: In 2019 Mozambique approved a national information society plan running to 2028, but no source found reports its delivery plan and published results.
MOZ.summary: The Council of Ministers approved the Plano Estratégico para a Sociedade de Informação 2019-2028 by Resolução n.º 52/2019, together with its Plano Operacional, on 26 February 2019. In the last twelve months, Decreto n.º 4/2026 of 10 March 2026 tasked a new agency with mobilising resources for the Information Society Policy and its plans. In May 2026 the draft digital transformation strategy went through regional validation. The ITU says it covers 2027-2036 and awaits Council of Ministers approval. No source found gives actions or costs for the Plano Operacional, and no published report against the plan's targets has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the government's own targets.

MRT.short: Mauritania approved a costed national digital agenda for 2022 to 2025 that has now ended; no source found reports results against its targets.
MRT.summary: The government drew up and approved the Agenda national de transformation numérique 2022-2025 in 2022. The agenda is broken into 25 initiatives and 77 projects, for a global investment of 400 million dollars. In the last twelve months, on 4 December 2025 the digital ministry announced the start of preparation of an Agenda National de la Transformation Numérique 2030. The earlier agenda covered 2022 to 2025. No report against the agenda's own targets has been found, only accounts of activity, and the 2030 agenda has no adopted text. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

MUS.short: Mauritius launched a national digital transformation blueprint for 2025 to 2029 in 2025; no source found reports its cost or results against targets.
MUS.summary: The ministry officially launched the Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029 on 26 May 2025, and its full text is published on the MITCI site. It follows the Digital Mauritius 2030 Strategic Plan, published in 2018. The Blueprint lists actions per pillar and enabler and contains a phased roadmap with milestones and indicators. In the last twelve months, a government notice of 1 September 2026 named the Blueprint as the instrument the Digital Service Framework will help implement. It was cited and not changed. The Blueprint states no cost, and no report against its own targets has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the government's own targets.

MWI.short: Malawi has a National Digitalization Policy for 2023 to 2028, approved by Cabinet, but no source found says whether its text is public.
MWI.summary: The National Digitalization Policy 2023-2028 was approved by Cabinet, per a MACRA presentation of October 2023. The Open Government Partnership action plan of June 2025 lists its adoption and operationalisation. In the last twelve months, a draft National Digital Transformation Strategy went to a validation workshop on 18 and 19 February 2026. In May 2026 the National Local Government Finance Committee said Malawi has one ICT policy for the nation, so the 2023 policy was cited and not changed. No source says the policy's text is public. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

NAM.short: Namibia launched its National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 in August 2025 with a public text; no source found reports any delivery plan or progress report.
NAM.summary: The Namibian reports that the ICT minister officially launched the National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 on 5 August 2025. The International Science Council paper of February 2026 cites its text on the ministry's website. In the last twelve months, on 31 March 2026 the minister said the ministry's N$682 million appropriation for 2026/27 will support implementation of the strategy. The national public key infrastructure DigiNam, launched on 31 August 2026, was described as aligned with the strategy. No source names the body or act that adopted it, and no costed delivery plan or progress report has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the government's own targets.

NER.short: Niger's digital development policy for 2026 to 2035 was validated in March 2026 and awaits an approving decree; no source found reports its text.
NER.summary: The drafting committee handed the policy, the Politique nationale de développement du numérique 2026-2035, to the Minister of Communication on 13 October 2025. In the last twelve months, a national validation workshop opened on 11 March 2026. In June 2026 the minister listed the decree approving the policy among coming steps. The policy follows the Politique nationale du numérique 2021-2030. No adoption of the 2026-2035 policy is on record, and its text has not been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a ten-year digital economy strategy unveiled in 2019, but no source found reports results against its targets and its funding.
NGA.summary: President Buhari unveiled the National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy on 28 November 2019. The strategy is titled and dated for 2020 to 2030, and it sets eight pillars with listed government actions and dated targets. In the last twelve months, NITDA's National Cloud Investment Strategy of August 2026 says the strategy continues to provide the overarching national policy framework. It was cited and not changed. The text states no cost. At the 20 December 2022 commissioning of the National Shared Services Centre, implementation was said to have produced progress, with no figure given against a target. Operating would need results published against the strategy's own targets.

RWA.short: Rwanda's Smart Rwanda plan, issued in 2015, ended in 2020, and a successor was in preparation in 2023, but no source reports its current status.
RWA.summary: The Government of Rwanda issued the Smart Rwanda Master Plan in October 2015. The sector review names the Smart Rwanda Master Plan I as covering 2016 to 2020, and its October 2023 edition lists Smart Rwanda Master Plan II among policies under development. A Digital Transformation Strategy for Rwanda (ICT Master Plan 2021-2025) is listed with that period. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no source gives the status of Master Plan II since October 2023. No source says whether the text is public, and no delivery plan or reporting has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

SDN.short: Sudan's digital transformation ministry announced a strategy in 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted or its text published.
SDN.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan issued a request for proposals on 7 April 2026 that refers to the digital transformation strategy announced by the digital transformation ministry in 2025. In the last twelve months, this request is the one source found, so the strategy was cited and not changed. No source found says whether the strategy was adopted by any act or whether its text is public. No period, plan, reporting or governance fact has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

SEN.short: Senegal launched its New Deal Technologique for 2025 to 2034 and published the text, but no source says whether results are measured against its targets.
SEN.summary: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye launched the New Deal Technologique on 24 February 2025, and its text is published on the Presidency site. The Digital Master Plan sets 12 priority programmes and 50 priority projects, costed at FCFA 1,105 billion. In the last twelve months, on 24 March 2026 Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko launched the New Deal's structuring projects. On 16 October 2026 he installed the digital governance committee GouvNum. At the first anniversary, authorities said significant progress had been made. No source names an act adopting the strategy, and reporting covers first-year activity measured against no targets. Operating would need results published against the government's own targets.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone approved its National Digital Development Policy in 2021 and publishes the text, but no source found says who approved it.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone's National Digital Development Policy 2021 was approved in 2021, and the policy text is hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site. The policy contains no action plan and no costs, and instructs the Ministry to develop the implementation plan. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Health's 2024-2026 roadmap said the Universal Access Development Fund was established through the policy. The policy was cited and not changed. No act or body is named for the approval, and the policy text only recommends approval. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the government's own targets.

SOM.short: Somalia launched a Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025 to 2030 after a consultation in October 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted.
SOM.summary: In October 2025 the government launched the Digital Strategy 2025-2030, after a two-day consultation on 12-13 October 2025 to validate it. The Ministry of Communications and Technology hosted the October 2025 national consultation to validate the Digital Transformation Strategy with the ITU. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source reports adoption of the strategy, and no act or body is named for the launch. No text has been found. The Council of Ministers approved a separate Inclusive Digital Policy in January 2025, with no period or text given. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

SSD.short: South Sudan was still developing its digital road map and master plan in June 2024; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
SSD.summary: A consulting firm was developing the Digital Development Road Map and Master Plan for the Government, the World Bank aide-memoire of 3-7 June 2024 records. Consultations on draft recommendations had been held. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and the aide-memoire is the last dated source. No adopting act, body, text, period, plan or reporting has been found for the Road Map and Master Plan. A South Sudan Digital Transformation Strategy and a Digital Government Strategy are named without further description. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

STP.short: The government of São Tomé and Príncipe had launched a national digital transformation strategy by March 2026; no source reports its adoption, text and period.
STP.summary: The World Bank program document of 11 March 2026 says the government of São Tomé and Príncipe has launched a national digital transformation strategy. It follows the 2020 Estratégia Nacional para a Governação Digital, approved by the Council of Ministers, which covered 2020/2024. The document describes the new strategy as expanding broadband connectivity and modernising the legal and regulatory framework. In the last twelve months, that document is the one record of the strategy found. Its title, adopting act, date, text, period, plan and reporting have not been found, and a launch alone does not show adoption. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a 2024-2028 digital strategy named in sources, but no source found reports its standing, text and plan, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not found. No instrument could be staged for Eswatini. An Eswatini Digitalisation Strategy (2024-2028, 'Government in Your Hand') and a Digital Transformation Roadmap in procurement are named, with nothing that sets their standing, text, period, plan or reporting.

SYC.short: Seychelles validated a 2026-2031 digital and AI strategy in July 2026; no source found reports its adoption and text.
SYC.summary: A consultant on the drafting team says the National Digital & AI Strategy 2026-2031 passed its national validation workshop by July 2026. The World Bank says the strategy is still to be operationalised. It names the Inter-Ministerial Digital and AI Coordination Committee and the Department of Information and Communications Technology as mandated to lead. In the last twelve months, the validation workshop is the one change found. No adoption is recorded, and no public text, delivery plan, reporting or budget line has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

TCD.short: Chad opened the drafting of a national digital transformation strategy in November 2026; no adopted strategy or public text is known.
TCD.summary: On 4 November 2026 a framing meeting opened work on a national digital transformation strategy, with UNDP paying an international firm to help draft it. In 2023 the World Bank recommended adopting a Chad Digital Strategy Horizon 2030, and said Chad lacked a comprehensive national digital strategy. In the last twelve months, drafting opened on 4 November 2026. In June 2026 ADETIC also named a Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2020-2030, without a link to its text. No source says a national digital strategy was adopted, or gives its text. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

TGO.short: Togo's president said in 2022 the Togo Digital 2025 strategy was adopted, but no source reports its text and its 2025 to 2030 successor's progress.
TGO.summary: In his independence address of 27 April 2022 the President said Togo had adopted the Stratégie Togo Digital 2025. A successor, Togo Digital 2025-2030, was in preparation from 22 May 2025, when the ministry began recruiting a consultant. In the last twelve months, the government portal reported on 4 May 2026 on the Stratégie nationale Togo Digital 2025, under which 181 classrooms were connected. The strategy was cited and not changed. No public text of Togo Digital 2025 and no delivery plan have been found, and reporting is activity counts only. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 2021-2025 digital strategy has ended and the government was preparing a 2026-2030 successor in 2025; no source found says it is adopted.
TUN.summary: The EBRD board report of July 2024 gives the earlier National Digital Strategy a period of 2021 to 2025. In September 2025 the minister said that strategy had ended and was being evaluated. The minister also said the government is preparing Tunisie numérique 2030 on five axes. On 18 November 2025 a ministry official described a national digital strategy with six axes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No adoption, text, delivery plan, governing body or finance has been found for the 2026-2030 strategy. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 was launched in 2024 and is public; no source found reports its cost and any report on its targets.
TZA.summary: President Samia Suluhu Hassan launched the Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 on 29 July 2024, and the Ministry publishes the framework on ictc.go.tz. The Citizen lists its dated targets, all by 2029. In the last twelve months, at the 9th Tanzania Annual ICT Conference on 19 January 2026, Minister Angellah Kairuki said delivery must meet the framework's targets on time. The Ministry presented 758 towers built by December 2025 as supporting the strategy. No published report against the targets and no finance line tied to the framework have been found. Operating would need results published against the framework's own targets, and a domestic budget line.

UGA.short: Uganda published its Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in 2022 with a costed plan; no source found reports any report on progress.
UGA.summary: The Ministry published the Vision in September 2022 as the Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040, with a foreword by President Museveni. It carries a cost implementation matrix putting first-phase financing to 2030 at UGX 6.08 trillion. A newer Digital Transformation Roadmap was launched by the Government on 17 August 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Vision has the working group prepare quarterly, semi-annual and annual implementation reports, but no report against it has been found. The Roadmap has no adopting act or public text on record. Operating would need results published against the government's own targets.

ZAF.short: South Africa has a final draft digital masterplan dated 2021, not public, with its 2020-2025 period ended; no source found reports its adoption.
ZAF.summary: The final draft of South Africa's ICT and Digital Economy Masterplan is dated 22 February 2021 and covers 2020 to 2025. Economist Impact says the final version is not public, and no source found says it was adopted. The department's 2023/24 plan lists a Digital Economy Framework and Strategy still to go to Cabinet. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a strategy adopted, published and still running.

ZMB.short: Zambia adopted a public national digital transformation strategy in 2023, running to 2027, with no cost stated; no source found reports progress against its targets.
ZMB.summary: The Ministry of Technology and Science published the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027 on 12 October 2023, and a 2023 journal study says it was adopted that year. It sets out interventions with numeric targets, such as 998 communication towers and 200 district digital transformation centres. In the last twelve months, Freight News described the strategy's five pillars on 3 September 2026. It was cited and not changed. ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan was launched in 2024 and runs to 2030; no delivery plan or results are known.
