No execution report, settlement law or audited account has been found giving what was spent in 2024 or later. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's FY2026 budget gives digital lines 55.5 per cent more than FY2025; no fund acting now is known.
SLE.summary: For FY2026, Sierra Leone's 40 digital lines held in both years total 1,064,019,424 new leones against 684,090,124 for FY2025, a rise of 55.5 per cent. The budget gives 1,074,150,124 new leones to 45 digital lines in all. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No execution report, settlement law or audited account has been found giving what was spent in 2024 or later. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying in the last three years. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2026 budget gives the digital lines held in both years 5.7 per cent more than 2025; no fund is known.
SOM.summary: For 2026, Somalia's 2 digital lines held in both years total 2,312,240 US dollars against 2,187,720 for 2025, a rise of 5.7 per cent. 13 lines are held for 2026, totalling 6,247,842 US dollars. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No execution report, settlement law or audited account has been found giving what was spent in 2024 or later. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying in the last three years. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

SSD.short: The 2025/26 budget gives 291,958,444,904 South Sudanese pounds to digital lines; no source found says whether it rose, and what was spent,.
SSD.summary: South Sudan's budget for FY 2025/26, dated 1 November 2025, gives 291,958,444,904 South Sudanese pounds to 15 digital lines. The National Communication Act, 2012 (Act No. 24) sets out in Chapter XIII, sections 73 to 83, a Universal Service and Access Fund, with a board of trustees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No other year's figure has been found, so no source found says whether the money rose. Nothing found says the fund collected or paid for anything, or what was spent. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

STP.short: The 2024 budget gives 33,599,219 dobras to digital lines, but the year before and no source found says what was spent.
STP.summary: The state budget of Sao Tome and Principe for 2024 gives 33,599,219 dobras to 24 digital lines, in approved tables dated 14 February 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for the year before has been found, so no source found says whether the money rose. Nothing found names a fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes, or says what was spent. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

SWZ.short: Eswatini raised its digital budget by 14.8 per cent for 2026/27; no source found says whether its universal service fund has paid for anything since 2023.
SWZ.summary: Eswatini's budget for 2026/27 gives 416,824,106 emalangeni to 14 digital lines. Thirteen of them are held in both years and total 408,074,106 emalangeni for 2026/27 against 355,552,868 for 2025/26, a rise of 14.8 per cent. In 2023 the Universal Access and Service Fund paid for a backbone redundancy project with EPTC. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years shows the fund collecting money or paying for a project, and the 2023 project is the latest found. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

SYC.short: Seychelles cut its digital budget by 8.9 per cent for 2026 and its universal service fund is not shown collecting or paying.
SYC.summary: In Seychelles the 12 digital lines held in both years total 84,802,000 rupees for 2026 against 93,076,000 for 2025, a fall of 8.9 per cent. In the last twelve months, the 2027 Appropriation Bill gave the Department of Information Communications Technology 186.4 million rupees. No 2026 figure for the department sits beside it, so no rise is shown. The Communications Act 2023, assented on 13 April 2023, sets up a universal access and universal service fund in Part XII. No collection or payment by the fund has been found. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before.

TCD.short: The 2026 budget's digital lines held for both years fell 27.8 per cent from 2025; no source says whether any fund pays for digital programmes.
TCD.summary: Chad's 2026 budget, in a document dated 26 December 2025, gives 3,645,150,873 CFA francs to nine digital lines. Six of the nine are held for both years and total 2,422,606,681 CFA francs for 2026 against 3,355,272,681 for 2025, 27.8 per cent lower. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for money spent on the lines from 2024 has been found. No law, decree or dated report has been found showing a fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes created, collecting or paying. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

TGO.short: The 2026 budget gives 28.2 billion CFA francs to 47 digital lines; no source found reports the previous year's figure.
TGO.summary: Togo's 2026 budget, in the finance ministry's document of 15 January 2026, gives 28,214,736,000 CFA francs to 47 digital lines. None of the 47 is held for 2025 as well, so the two years cannot be set side by side. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found gives the money for digital transformation in two budget years running, so no source found says whether it rose. No spending figure has been found, and no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

TUN.short: The ICT ministry's 2026 budget rose 7 per cent on 2025; no fund, levy or commitment to pay at home is known.
TUN.summary: In November 2025 L'Economiste Maghrébin reported the communication technologies ministry's 2026 budget at 197.335 million dinars, against 184 million in the 2025 finance law. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the minister put a proposed 2027 budget for the ministry to two parliamentary committees, 9.3% above the year before. The ministry's 2026 budget includes the telecommunications and ICT development fund. No source found shows that fund created, collecting or paying in the last three years, and no minister has been found saying digital work must be paid for at home. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

TZA.short: The ministry's 2026/27 budget fell 23.6 per cent though digital lines overall rose 7.9, and the service fund built towers; no source reports 2026/27 spending.
TZA.summary: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology's 2026/27 proposal of 222,589,451,000 shillings is 23.6 per cent below the 291,533,139,000 approved for 2025/26. The digital lines held for both years total 429,376,230,416 shillings for 2026/27 against 398,020,452,091 for 2025/26, 7.9 per cent higher. In the last twelve months, on 5 October 2026, the chief executive of the Universal Communications Service Access Fund said it will build 250 school computer laboratories this financial year. In November 2026 The Citizen reported 15.3 billion shillings allocated through the fund to build and upgrade 37 TBC radio sites. Nothing found shows the ministry's own budget higher than the year before. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget.

UGA.short: In 2026/27 the ICT ministry's budget rises to 144.7 billion shillings and a levy-funded universal access fund pays out; nothing further is unknown.
UGA.summary: The Auditor General's report on the Uganda Communications Universal Service and Access Fund gives 68.07 billion shillings spent by the fund in FY 2024/25. The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance budgets 144.696 billion for 2026/27 against 105.963 billion approved for 2025/26. The digital lines held for both years total 752.4 billion for 2026/27 against 862.0 billion for 2025/26. The fund is paid by a levy of 2% of operators' gross annual revenue. In the last twelve months, in 2026, ATC Uganda paid 20.9 billion shillings into the fund. On 29 September 2026 the Uganda Communications Commission sought a partner to run Phase III of the National e-Booster Programme through the fund for 2026/27.

ZAF.short: The digital and postal access budget rises for 2026/27 and the universal service fund spent 1.09 billion rand in 2025/26; nothing further is unknown.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's digital lines held for both years total 8,082.2 million rand for 2026/27 against 7,685.6 million for 2025/26. The 2026 Estimates raise the digital and postal access subprogramme from 742.9 million rand in 2025/26 to 767.2 million for 2026/27. In the last twelve months, the Universal Service and Access Fund's own figures, given in a ministerial reply, show 1,087.9 million rand spent in 2025/26. ICASA collected 281.2 million rand for it in 2025/26, and the fund has not been abolished. The 2026 Estimates put 146.0 million rand of 2026/27 towards the universal service and access bodies.

ZMB.short: The digital lines in Zambia's 2026 budget total more than in 2025; no fund or levy is known.
ZMB.summary: In Zambia the digital lines held for both years total 1,792.9 million kwacha for 2026 against 1,594.5 million for 2025, a rise. The Appropriation Act, 2025 authorises 1.15 billion kwacha for Smart Zambia e-government for 2026. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, the minister announced approval of 255 million kwacha to upgrade digital infrastructure, mainly in rural areas. The budget document names no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes, and none has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's ICT ministry budget rises about 3 per cent to 763.5 million Zimbabwe Gold for 2026; no source found reports spending and any fund.
ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe's Budget Statement gives the ICT ministry's Vote 23 budget as 763.5 million Zimbabwe Gold for 2026, against 741 million for 2025, a rise of about 3 per cent. The digital lines held for both years total 4,503.5 million Zimbabwe dollars for 2026 against 5,703.9 million for 2025, 21.0 per cent lower. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for what was spent has been found, and no fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 presidential decree on information society services covers e-signatures and contracts; no rules made under it are known, and a 2026 regime awaits enactment.
AGO.summary: Angola's Presidential Decree 202/11, published on 22 July 2011, approves the regulation on information society technologies and services. It covers electronic documents, qualified electronic signatures, certification and electronic contracts. In the last twelve months, on 30 July 2026 the Assembleia Nacional approved, by 166 votes, a bill authorising the President to legislate a regime for electronic signatures and digital certification. That regime has not been enacted. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2011 decree has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2024 communications code governs e-commerce, and in June 2026 the regulator ordered online sellers to declare conformity; no declaration received is known.
BDI.summary: Burundi's Loi N°1/22 of 22 August 2024 is the code des communications électroniques et postales. In the last twelve months, on 29 May 2026 the regulator ARCT published national e-commerce ecosystem guidelines on interoperability, transaction security and consumer protection. On 26 June 2026 it called e-commerce platforms and merchant sites to declare their conformity under the code. It annexed a procedures manual, a conformity checklist and a declaration form. No declaration of conformity received, licence or penalty under the code has been found.

BEN.short: Benin's 2018 digital code is in force with a 2025 decree on electronic archiving providers; no use of it since 2023 is known.
BEN.summary: Benin's Loi n° 2017-20, the Code du numérique, was promulgated on 20 April 2018. It includes a title on the obligations of trust service providers. In the last twelve months, Decree 2025-363 of 2 July 2025 set the conditions for providers of electronic archiving, who must be qualified by the competent authority as trust service providers for three years at a time. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the code in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's 2009 law on electronic services and transactions is in force with implementing decrees; no source found reports accreditations or licences under it.
BFA.summary: Burkina Faso's Law n°045-2009/AN, promulgated on 4 December 2009, regulates electronic services and transactions. It covers electronic signatures, e-commerce contracts and trust service providers. In the last twelve months, a report on the launch of FasoSign on 15 September 2026 said the platform gives effect to the law and its implementing decrees. The decrees are not named. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

BWA.short: Botswana's 2014 electronic communications and transactions act has been in force since 2016 and covers contracts, signatures and online buyers; no rules are known.
BWA.summary: Botswana's Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2014 (Act No. 14) was assented to on 14 May 2014. It gives electronic communications, contracts and signatures legal effect and covers the protection of consumers who buy online. The regulator BOCRA records the Act as in force since 1 April 2016. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The only instrument found that was made under the Act is the ministerial Order that brought it into force. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic's regulator lists a 2022 electronic transactions law among the country's laws; no rules made under it are known.
CAF.summary: The regulator ARCEP lists Loi 22.002 of 11 January 2022, regulating electronic transactions in the country, on its official index of laws and ordinances. The index page was published on 21 February 2024 and presents the law as one of the country's laws. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The index shows no decree, regulation or order made under the law, and the text of the law has not been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CIV.short: A 2013 electronic transactions law is in force with 2014 and 2016 decrees, but no use of it is dated in the last three years.
CIV.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Loi n°2013-546 of 30 July 2013 on electronic transactions is the law that a decree of 12 March 2014 states it implements. That decree sets rules on secure electronic signatures and qualified electronic certificates, and on the approval of certification service providers by ARTCI. Ordinance 2024-950 of 30 October 2024 repealed its Article 50 and left the rest in place. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: AIP reported on 25 July 2026 that the national public key infrastructure was in service. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

CMR.short: A 2010 e-commerce law is in force with a 2011 application decree, but no use of it is dated in the last three years.
CMR.summary: Cameroon's Law No. 2010/021 of 21 December 2010 governs electronic commerce. It defines electronic signatures, certificates and certification authorities. Decree no. 2011/1521/PM of 15 June 2011, issued by the Prime Minister, fixes the modalities of its application. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

COD.short: A 2023 digital code governs e-signatures, with a March 2026 order on authorisation, but no licence under it is dated in the last three years.
COD.summary: DR Congo's Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Code du Numérique, governs electronic writings, electronic signatures, trust service providers and digital services. In the last twelve months, the ministerial order of 11 March 2026 set an authorisation regime for qualified trust-service providers, marketplaces and e-commerce platforms. ACP reports it was published on 17 March 2026, with a transition to 30 June 2026. No authorisation granted under it, and no other accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years, has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

COG.short: A 2019 electronic transactions law is treated as in force in 2026, but no rule made under it is known.
COG.summary: The Congo's Loi n° 37-2019 of 12 December 2019 on electronic transactions is cited as a legal basis by four arrêtés of 9 July 2026. Décret n° 2026-101 of 31 March 2026 cites the same law. Both concern the certified electronic invoicing system, and both treat the law as existing. In the last twelve months the law was cited and not changed. No decree, regulation or order made under it is named in the sources found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

COM.short: A 2021 law on cyber security gives electronic signatures legal effect; nothing is known of rules made under it or of its use.
COM.summary: The UNECA Digital Trade Regulatory Integration profile, published in 2024, states that the Comoros's 2021 law on cyber security and the fight against cybercrime, Law No. 21-012/AU, fills gaps in electronic transactions. It gives electronic signatures the same legal effect as handwritten ones. The profile also states that the Comoros has no stand-alone law on electronic transactions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The profile names no decree, regulation or order made under it and no provider accredited under it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CPV.short: Cape Verde was said in 2025 to have a law on digital transactions, but no rule made under it is known.
CPV.summary: In July 2025 the Secretary of State for the Digital Economy, Pedro Lopes, cited Cape Verde's modern laws on data protection and digital transactions as regulatory progress. The report was published on 31 July 2025 and is the only statement found on the law on digital transactions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law is named in the sources found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

DJI.short: Djibouti's National Assembly passed a Digital Code covering e-commerce in June 2025; no source found says whether it is in force or has implementing rules.
DJI.summary: Djibouti's National Assembly adopted the Digital Code unanimously on 30 June 2025. The text has nearly 800 articles and covers the regulation of online commerce among other areas. Jones Day reports that the law was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel, and that it is to be supplemented by regulatory decrees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the Digital Code has been promulgated or is in force has not been found. Establishing would need a law in force on electronic contracts, signatures or online sales.

DZA.short: Algeria's Law 18-05 on e-commerce is in force, and UNCTAD lists a 2019 decree on its registers; no later application is dated.
DZA.summary: Algeria's Law No. 18-05 of 10 May 2018 sets general rules for e-commerce. It covers registration of e-suppliers, electronic contracts, payment, advertising and penalties. UNCTAD's Global Cyberlaw Tracker lists Executive Decree 19-89 of 5 March 2019 as Algeria's electronic transactions legislation, and it fixes how registers of electronic commercial transactions are kept. In the last twelve months, Law 26-02 of 17 February 2026 set rules on trust services for electronic transactions. No accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under Law 18-05 has been found in the last three years. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

EGY.short: Egypt's Law 15/2004 on e-signatures is in force and has executive regulations, per 2025 legal guides; no dated licence or penalty is known.
EGY.summary: Egypt's Law No. 15/2004 regulating e-signatures was issued on 21 April 2004. It gives electronic signatures and electronic writing the evidential effect of paper, and sets up ITIDA to license certificate issuers. A law firm's ICLG chapter of July 2025 states that its executive regulations require e-signature applicants to secure the confidentiality of information. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. In November 2026 a Public Prosecution course named the law among those related to data protection. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

ERI.short: A 2022 UN Africa commission profile said Eritrea had no e-commerce or e-signature law; nothing newer is held, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: No stage is set. No law or draft on electronic transactions or e-commerce is on record for Eritrea as at September 2026. No source dated in the last three years says the country has none. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country has no law on electronic transactions or e-commerce and no draft of one.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's e-signature Proclamation 1072/2017 is in force and its regulation was approved by the Council of Ministers in 2025; no source reports publication and use.
ETH.summary: Ethiopia's electronic signature law is Proclamation No. 1072/2017, with its amendment. In November 2025 the Council of Ministers unanimously approved the Electronic Signature regulation under the proclamation, to take effect on publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette. The Ethiopian News Agency called the regulation a step toward fully operationalizing the law. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no publication of the regulation has been found. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

GAB.short: Gabon's Law 025/2021 regulates electronic transactions, and in September 2026 ministers adopted a draft trust-services decree; no source found reports use of the rules.
GAB.summary: Gabon's Law No. 025/2021 of 28 December 2021 regulates electronic transactions. It gives electronic acts, writings, signatures and invoices the same probative force as paper. It also sets rules for e-commerce, distance contracts and consumer withdrawal. In the last twelve months, on 18 September 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree setting how the qualified signature certificate and other trust services are issued. It covers approval conditions and duties of providers. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

GHA.short: Ghana's 2008 Electronic Transactions Act is in force; no source found reports a decree, regulation or order made under it.
GHA.summary: Ghana's 2008 Electronic Transactions Act is in force, and the US Country Commercial Guide, published 20 September 2024, calls it the baseline for e-commerce and e-signature. In November 2023 the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation issued an enforcement notice under the Act. It required all e-commerce platforms and digital delivery companies to register by January 2024. In the last twelve months the Act was cited and not changed: a MyJoyOnline op-ed of 16 October 2026 names the Act as part of Ghana's existing legal foundation. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act is named in the sources found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GIN.short: Guinea has a 2016 transactions law, a 2021 decree and a 2026 e-signature decree; no source found says how far they are applied.
GIN.summary: Guinea's Law L/2016/035/AN of 26 July 2016 on electronic transactions applies to all electronic transactions including online commerce. Decree D/2021/092/PRG/SGG, signed on 25 March 2021, names the ARPT as regulator with sanction powers. In the last twelve months, a presidential decree signed on 19 August 2026 gives an electronic signature the same probative force as a paper writing and requires every electronic-certification service provider to be approved by ANDE. On 20 November 2026 the minister said the decree's regulatory framework and implementing orders were complete. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

GMB.short: UNCTAD lists The Gambia's 2009 Information and Communications Act as its electronic transactions law; no rules made under it have been found.
GMB.summary: UNCTAD's Global Cyberlaw Tracker lists the Information and Communications Act No. 2 of 2009 as The Gambia's electronic transactions legislation. A first reading of the Communications Bill 2025 took place on 19 November 2025. In the last twelve months, the National Assembly approved the Communications Bill 2025 at second reading on 2 March 2026. The Minister said it will recognise electronic signatures and contracts and cover electronic commerce services. No source found reports that it has been enacted. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2009 Act on electronic transactions has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau put a draft Electronic Transactions Law to consultation until 28 May 2026; no law in force is known.
GNB.summary: In May 2026 Guinea-Bissau's regulator ARN-TIC put the draft Electronic Transactions Law out for public consultation, with responses due by 28 May 2026. The 112-article text would give data messages, electronic records, contracts and electronic signatures legal effect. In the last twelve months, on 17 November 2026 the Council of Ministers examined the proposed Electronic Transactions Law, and on 24 November 2026 it approved the bill with amendments. The text enters into force only on a date the Minister designates. No law in force has been found. Establishing would need a law in force on electronic contracts, signatures or online sales.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea enacted a law on electronic signature and documents on 10 January 2017; no rules made under it or application are known.
GNQ.summary: The official gazette compilation of Equatorial Guinea, published 10 January 2017, lists Ley Núm. 2/2.017, of 10 January 2017, on Firma y Documentos Electrónicos, as a law of the country. The entry gives its title and date, so what the law requires has not been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and nothing found shows the law being applied. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

KEN.short: Kenya gave electronic signatures legal effect and made certification rules by 2020; nothing is known of licences or penalties in the last three years.
KEN.summary: Kenya's Business Laws (Amendment) Act, 2020 came into force on 18 March 2020. It allows advanced electronic signatures in place of wet-ink signatures in nearly all legal documents. On 1 September 2020 the Communications Authority required all foreign electronic certification providers to apply for recognition within 30 days. As at October 2020 only two certification service providers were licensed, and neither had started issuing advanced electronic signatures. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law dated in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2002 Electronic Transactions Law gives electronic contracts and signatures legal effect, but no regulation under it is known.
LBR.summary: Liberia's Electronic Transactions Law, Chapter 13 of Title 14 of the General Business Law, was approved on 8 January 2002 and published on 19 June 2002. It gives electronic records, contracts and signatures legal effect. The law applies at once to matters under Titles 5 and 21 of the General Business Law. Elsewhere it applies only as regulations of the Minister of Foreign Affairs bring it into effect. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No such regulation, and no decree or order made under the law, has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LBY.short: Libya's 2022 electronic transactions law is in force and covers online sellers; its executive regulation was unpublished in 2023, and no later rules are known.
LBY.summary: Libya's Law No. 6 of 2022 on Electronic Transactions was issued by the House of Representatives on 4 October 2022. It gives electronic signatures, records and contracts legal effect, and sets pre-contract disclosure and return rules for online sellers. In December 2023 Eltumi Partners stated that the government had not yet published the executive regulation to the law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation, order or decision made under the law is named. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LSO.short: Lesotho had no electronic transactions law in 2026; a revised bill went to validation in September 2026, and no passage date has been found.
LSO.summary: The government opened a two-day validation workshop in Maseru on 28 September 2026 on the Electronic Transactions and Communications Bill, 2026, which revises a 2022 bill of the same name. The ministry responsible says Lesotho lacks a legal and regulatory framework for electronic transactions. In the last twelve months the bill reached validation, and the draft is to go next to the Office of the Parliamentary Counsel for refinement. No passage date has been found, and no law in force has been found. Establishing would need a law in force on electronic contracts, signatures or online sales.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2020 trust services law is in force, with a 2023 decree and three approved qualified providers listed in September 2026.
MAR.summary: Morocco's Law 43-20 on trust services for electronic transactions was promulgated on 31 December 2020. It covers signatures and certificates, not online selling. Decree 2-22-687 of 16 November 2022 was made to apply the law. The DGSSI approved Damanesign as a trust service provider on 3 March 2025. In May 2025 the Mouvement populaire group filed a private bill adding a chapter on online selling to consumer protection Law 31.08. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the DGSSI named three approved providers: EURAFRIC INFORMATION, Barid Al Maghrib and DamaneSign. It also lists the conformity certificates it has issued, six of them current, the latest dated 18 March 2026.

MDG.short: Madagascar has had electronic transactions and signature laws since 2014, and no source found says a 2025 draft decree on electronic signature has been adopted.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's transactions law, Loi no. 2014-024, dated 10 December 2014, defines electronic signature and regulates e-commerce. A separate law of the same date covers electronic signature. Decree 2024-1911, published on 13 November 2024, gives documents signed through a certified electronic signature device the same recognition as paper, and cites both laws as its legal basis. In September 2025 Newsmada reported that a draft decree on electronic signature and interoperability was in preparation. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no source found says the draft decree has been adopted. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MLI.short: Mali's 2016 law on electronic transactions regulates e-commerce and is cited by the state in 2025, but no source found reports rules made under it.
MLI.summary: Mali's Law no. 2016-012 of 6 May 2016 on electronic transactions, exchanges and services regulates electronic commerce. It gives legal effect to electronic writings, signatures, certificates and archiving, and was published in the Journal officiel of 27 May 2016. In November 2025 the Director General of Taxes cited the law on electronic transactions as part of a solid legal framework for digitalising public payments. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2016 law is named in the sources found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MOZ.short: In 2026 Mozambique's electronic transactions law is applied through 19 operator licences, with about 170 companies under evaluation; no source found reports wider enforcement.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's Electronic Transactions Law, Law no. 3/2017 of 9 January, sets rules on electronic marketing consent, intermediary service providers and personal data, with fines for breach. Decree no. 59/2023 of 27 October, amended by Decree no. 44/2025 of 28 November, requires intermediary electronic service providers and digital platform operators to register and be licensed with INTIC. In the last twelve months, on 8 June 2026 INTIC's board president said 19 licences had been issued. About 170 registered companies were under evaluation. Decree No. 40/2026 gives the electronic signature the same legal standing as a handwritten one. No enforcement figure beyond the licences has been found.

MRT.short: A 2018 law on electronic exchanges is in force, with a draft decree reported in 2024; no source found says whether any decree was adopted.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's Law no. 2018-022 of 12 June 2018 on electronic exchanges is the law under which Tech Rek reports a draft decree. It reported on 23 April 2024 a draft decree made under the 2018 law, headed as approving a national agency for cybersecurity and electronic certification. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found on whether the draft decree was adopted, and no decree, regulation or order made under the 2018 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MUS.short: In 2026 Mauritius enacted an electronic transactions amendment act, to start on a date set by Proclamation; no source found reports rules made under it.
MUS.summary: Mauritius passed Act No. 5 of 2026, the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act, on 19 May 2026 and assented to it on 25 May. Law firm Appleby says it recognises electronic signatures, electronic transferable records and contracts formed by automated systems. It comes into operation on a date to be fixed by Proclamation. In the last twelve months, on 29 July 2026 the ICT minister said the amendments had modernised the framework for digital commerce. The Electronic Transactions Act 2006 is treated as existing law. No regulation made under either Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MWI.short: Malawi's electronic transactions act has been in force since June 2017; regulations under it were in draft in 2024, and none made has been found.
MWI.summary: Malawi's Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act, Act 33 of 2016, commenced on 1 June 2017. It gives legal effect to electronic writing, electronic signatures and digital signature certificates. In February 2024 the government put draft regulations on cryptography and certification authorities to stakeholders. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the ICT minister said the government would review the Act and introduce an E-Transactions and E-Commerce Bill. The text of the Act names no regulation made under it, and none made has been found beyond drafts. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2019 e-transactions law was applied in 2026, with a first certification provider accredited in September; the consumer protection chapter is not yet in force.
NAM.summary: Namibia's Electronic Transactions Act 4 of 2019 was published in the Government Gazette on 29 November 2019. Most of it came into force on 16 March 2020. In the last twelve months, the minister made the Electronic Signature Regulations under section 20 on 27 November 2025. On 17 December 2025 CRAN published regulations on accrediting security products and certification service providers. Section 20 and Chapter 5 came into force on 15 June 2026, and DigiNam, the national public key infrastructure, was launched under the Act on 31 August 2026. In September 2026 CRAN accredited the Ministry of Home Affairs as Namibia's first certification service provider, for four years. No date for Chapter 4 on consumer protection has been found.

NER.short: Niger's 2019 electronic transactions law gained an implementing decree in November 2024; no source found says whether it has been applied to any provider or seller.
NER.summary: Niger's Loi 2019-03 of 30 April 2019 on electronic transactions covers electronic signatures, contracts and payments, data retention and sanctions. At a workshop in March 2025 the minister named an implementing decree, no. 2024-715 of 15 November 2024, made under the law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No accreditation of a signature provider, registration of online sellers or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found, and no date of entry into force has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

NGA.short: Nigeria's cybercrimes law, amended in 2024, gives electronic signatures legal effect; no source found says whether any rules have been made under it.
NGA.summary: Nigeria's Cybercrimes Act gives electronic signatures legal effect, and PLAC Legist says section 17 of the Act, as amended in 2024, sets which transactions are valid by electronic signature. In the last twelve months, TechCabal reports that the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill would give qualifying electronic signatures the same validity as handwritten ones. By May 2026 the House of Representatives had approved it. In July 2026 the Senate ICT committee chair said the bill was at third reading, with assent expected within weeks. No source found names rules made under the Cybercrimes Act on electronic signatures. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

RWA.short: Rwanda's consumer law has had an e-commerce chapter in force since 4 March 2026; no source found reports rules made under it.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's Law 011/2026 of 26 February 2026 on competition and consumer protection carries a chapter on e-commerce, from Article 41 onward, setting obligations for an e-commerce enterprise and for an online intermediary. It came into force on its publication in the Official Gazette on 4 March 2026. In the last twelve months, the e-commerce chapter has applied from that date. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SDN.short: Sudan's Electronic Transactions Act of 2007 is the law cited in the May 2026 SudaPass terms; no source found reports rules made under it.
SDN.summary: Sudan's Electronic Transactions Act of 2007, with its amendments, is the law cited in the SudaPass terms of use, published on 21 May 2026. They state that a digital signature meeting its requirements is equivalent to a handwritten signature (Article 8), and they cite its Article 28 for punishing forgery. In the last twelve months, these terms are the one use of the Act found in a government service. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2008 law on electronic transactions and its 2008 implementing decree are in force; no source found reports any use of them since 2023.
SEN.summary: Senegal's Law no. 2008-08 of 25 January 2008 on electronic transactions gives electronic records and signatures equivalence with paper. It also sets rules for electronic commerce. Decree no. 2008-718 of 30 June 2008 on electronic commerce was made to apply it. In the last twelve months the law was cited and not changed: in March 2026 the justice minister named it in Senegal's legal framework, as the law that recognises digital documents. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's Electronic Transactions Act has been in force since 2019, but in July 2026 its enforcement was not fully set up.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone's Electronic Transactions Act, Act 89 of 2019, is in force, and the SierraLII record gives assent and commencement on 5 December 2019. Sierra Loaded reports that the Act gives legal recognition to electronic signatures, consumer protection and digital communications in courts. In the last twelve months, at a government dialogue on 27 and 28 July 2026 on implementing the Act, its enforcement structures were not yet fully established. These include digital certification authorities, electronic evidence procedures, dispute resolution and penalties. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SOM.short: Somalia's E-Transactions Law was described in August 2026 as moving through the legislative process; no law is known to be in force.
SOM.summary: In August 2026 a Ministry of Information adviser wrote, in an article published on 19 August 2026 and in a personal capacity, that Somalia's E-Transactions Law is moving through the legislative process. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 the communications ministry said the House of the People had approved the Digital Transactions Bill by 137 votes. The Senate stage and assent are not stated. No law in force on electronic transactions or e-commerce has been found. Establishing would need a law in force on electronic contracts, signatures or online sales.

SSD.short: No law on electronic transactions or e-commerce, or draft of one, is known for South Sudan as at 2026, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a law on electronic transactions or e-commerce, or a draft of one. Nothing found says there is none.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe passed an e-signature law, reported in 2025; no rules made under it or use of it are known.
STP.summary: In April 2025 the World Bank said that an E-Signature Law has been passed in São Tomé and Príncipe. A World Bank mission note of September 2025 describes an electronic signature service, Assinatura Electrónica. It was built by INIC and the registry office DGRN. In the last twelve months, on 27 October 2026 the justice minister listed an e-commerce bill in preparation, financed by the World Bank. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has had an Electronic Transactions Act since 2022, named by ministers in 2025 and 2026; no rules made under it are known.
SWZ.summary: The Prime Minister said in October 2025 that the Electronic Transactions Act was passed in 2022. APC, in an article published on 22 July 2024, lists the Electronic Communications Transactions Act of 2022 among the ICT laws the regulator ESCCOM oversees. In the last twelve months the Act was cited and not changed: on 29 April 2026 Minister Savannah Maziya listed the Electronic Transactions Act of 2022 among Eswatini's existing legal groundwork. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SYC.short: Seychelles has had an electronic transactions act in force since 2001, recognising electronic records and digital signatures; no source found reports rules made under it.
SYC.summary: Seychelles' Electronic Transactions Act, 2001 (Act 8 of 2001) commenced on 20 December 2001. It gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures. In May 2025 the Supreme Court held that the Act provides the legal framework for digital signatures. The consolidated text, current to 29 March 2018, lists Statutory Instrument 12 of 2024 as an outstanding amendment. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The text names no regulation on electronic signatures, on those who certify them or on those who sell online. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TCD.short: Chad has a 2015 law on electronic transactions, and electronic signatures count in finance ministry correspondence from 2026; no source reports rules under the law.
TCD.summary: Chad's Law No. 008/PR/2015 on electronic transactions is listed in the regulator ARCEP's register of laws, which gives its year, 2015. In the last twelve months, Article 53 of Law No. 008/AN/SENAT/2025, the finance law for 2026, made electronic signature compulsory for administrative correspondence in the finance ministry from 1 January 2026. It states that this signature has the same legal value as a handwritten one. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2015 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TGO.short: Togo's 2017 electronic transactions law, amended in 2023, and its 2018 decree on sellers, signatures and trust providers are in force.
TGO.summary: Togo's Decree 2018-062/PR of 21 March 2018 was made in application of Law 2017-007 of 22 June 2017 on electronic transactions. It has 105 articles and covers formalities for e-commerce sellers in Article 6, electronic signatures and qualified certificates, trust service providers and the accreditation procedure. Law 2023-012 of 19 July 2023 amends the 2017 law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

TUN.short: Tunisia has had an electronic exchanges and commerce law since 2000, with certification decrees reported, but no dated use of it is known.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's Law no. 2000-83 of 9 August 2000 on electronic exchanges and commerce gives electronic documents and signatures legal effect and creates the national electronic certification agency ANCE. Decree-law 2020-31 of 10 June 2020 gives a reliable electronic signature the same evidentiary force as a handwritten one. The ID4Africa country playbook of May 2026 reports that decrees of 2000-2001 organise certification and the accreditation of certification providers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law in the last three years has been dated. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Electronic Transactions Act is in force and was amended by the Finance Act of June 2026; no source found reports rules made under it.
TZA.summary: The communications ministry says the government enacted the Act in 2015. That is Tanzania's Electronic Transactions Act, Chapter 442. In the last twelve months, Part III of the Finance Act, 2026, published on 30 June 2026, amends section 13 of the Act and leaves the rest standing. It is an act of parliament, not a regulation or order made under the Act. Its text names no regulation on electronic signatures, on those who certify them or on those who sell online. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2011 Electronic Transactions Act and its 2013 regulations are in force; no source found reports any application of them in the last three years.
UGA.summary: Uganda's Electronic Transactions Act (Act 8 of 2011, now Chapter 99) commenced on 15 April 2011. It gives data messages, electronic signatures and electronic contracts legal effect and sets consumer rules for online sellers. The Minister responsible for ICT made the Electronic Transactions Regulations, 2013 (S.I. 2013 No. 42) on 10 September 2013 under section 35 of the Act. In the last twelve months the Act was cited and not changed: in October 2026 the Daily Monitor said Uganda relies on a piecemeal framework including the Act. No accreditation, licence or penalty under the law in the last three years has been found. Mature would need an accreditation, licence, registration or penalty under the law.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 2002 electronic communications and transactions act is in force; three accreditations under it are undated, and no regulation under it has been found.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's law is the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act of 2002. Home Affairs listed it in May 2025 as the law that regulates electronic transactions, and no bill to replace it is named. TechCentral reported on 11 September 2026 that the South African Accreditation Authority accredits providers of advanced electronic signatures under it. Altron Security, TrustFactory and Impression Signatures hold accreditation, and the report gives no date for any of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a regulation made under the Act.

ZMB.short: Zambia's 2021 electronic communications and transactions act is in force, with amendments in consultation; no source found reports regulations made under it.
ZMB.summary: Zambia's law is the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act No. 4 of 2021, which gives a legal framework for electronic transactions and secure electronic signatures. Cabinet approved amendments to it in principle in September 2025. In the last twelve months, as reported on 30 September 2026, the Ministry of Technology and Science began consulting stakeholders on them. The regulator ZICTA was designated National Root Certification Authority under the Act, and on 7 September 2026 the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Technology and Science said the Act provided its legal foundation for the national public key infrastructure. No regulation made under the Act is named. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has a 2013 government draft electronic transactions bill, not presented in Parliament by February 2026, and no law in force.
ZWE.summary: FinMark Trust said on 18 June 2026 that Zimbabwe does not have comprehensive legislation of the kind an Electronic Transactions Act provides. A first draft of the Electronic Transactions and Electronic Commerce Bill, dated 11 June 2013, is an ITU-assisted government draft. It covers legal recognition of electronic communications and signatures, electronic contracts, online consumer protection and service provider liability. The President's address of October 2025 named the bill. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 Veritas reported that it had been neither presented in Parliament nor published in the Gazette. No law in force has been found. Establishing would need a law in force on electronic contracts, signatures or online sales.

AGO.short: In 2025 the contractor said the technical-vocational education system was designed to link with the ministry's records; no link in service has been found.
AGO.summary: In May 2025 LBC, the contractor, said the technical-vocational education system SIETP was designed for integration with SIGE. SIGE is Angola's Education Information and Management System. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the two systems exchange data in use, or that one learner identifier is used across education systems. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

BDI.short: A human resources module for the education data system was being built in 2024; no link in service has been found.
BDI.summary: From 29 July to 2 August 2024 the ministry and UNESCO held a workshop on a human resources module for the central SIGE. The module is to work with the STATEDUC application and serve teacher recruitment, deployment and posting. The project was agreed in December 2022 and runs to 14 February 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the module is in service or that two education systems exchange data. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use: the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

BEN.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

BFA.short: A national pupil file was piloted in 2024 and reviewed by ministers in 2025; no link in service has been found.
BFA.summary: On 25 June 2025 the digital transition and basic education ministers reviewed progress on the national pupil file, online enrolment and school identity cards, La Tribune du Faso reports. Built with WURI support, the file is to track pupils from primary to university. In February 2024 a ministry report recorded a pilot of the unique pupil identification file, FIUE-BF. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

BWA.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

CAF.short: In 2026 the teacher records system was linked to the payroll, covering 98 percent of teachers; no shared learner identifier has been found.
CAF.summary: In June 2026 a World Bank completion report said the HRMIS built under the Education Sector Plan Support Project is linked to the payroll. It records 98.01 percent of teachers on payroll with a certificate of presence, against a 95 percent target. The CARE project uses it for teacher recruitment and deployment. The report dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

CIV.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CIV.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

CMR.short: A 2026 agreement with UNESCO includes interconnecting the education databases; no link in service has been found.
CMR.summary: On 31 July 2026 UNESCO and Cameroon's PAEBC project unit signed a technical assistance agreement. It is worth 8 million euros over 36 months. It includes updating the MINEDUB WebSIG platform and interconnecting the education databases. The agreement dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

COD.short: In 2026 the national pupil records service said other education departments collect teacher and school data separately; no link under way has been found.
COD.summary: In August 2026 the director of SERNIE, the national pupil records service, wrote that other education departments collect teacher and school-infrastructure data. They collect it separately from SERNIE's learner records. The director stated no link between them. The article dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a link between education systems is under way. Preparing would need a link between two education systems to be contracted, being built or piloted.

COG.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COG.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

COM.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

CPV.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

DJI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

DZA.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

EGY.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

ERI.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

ETH.short: From 2025 a project works to connect local school data systems in four regions to the national system; no link in service has been found.
ETH.summary: From November 2025 a UNICEF-backed project has worked to connect local school, woreda and zone systems to the national DHIS2-Ed EMIS. It covers the SER, SWEPR, Oromia and Benishangul Gumuz regions, HISP Ethiopia reports. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the World Bank proposed US$750,000 for EMIS enhancement. It would bring all 57 refugee primary schools and their learners into the national EMIS. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data. None says they do in service. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body or teacher payroll.

GAB.short: A 2012 law gives each learner a unique number; nothing found since 2023 shows it in use, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names education systems exchanging data. Sources found name a Système d'Information pour la Gestion de l'Éducation (SIGE) and an exam management database, and show no link between them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country's education systems exchange no data.

GHA.short: A 2024 ministry dashboard interface takes data from agencies; no source found says the link is in service.
GHA.summary: In 2024 the Ministry of Education's PMDV Dashboard API documentation listed endpoints serving EMIS school statistics, enrolment rates, schools and NST test scores. A further endpoint takes data from agencies by agency code. It does not say which systems feed it or that it is in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

GIN.short: Guinea announced a university management system linked to other education platforms in 2025; no source found reports two education systems exchanging data in service.
GIN.summary: In September 2025 the Minister of Higher Education announced the Système Intégré de Gestion des Universités (SIGU) as a centralised digital tool interconnected with other national platforms, named as ANSAE, the Porte Educ platform and SIGOU. In March 2021 exam candidate lists passed between central level, IRE, DPE and schools by agents' personal email in Excel files. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the EMIS exchanges data with another education system in use. Examinations, payroll and learner registration were looked for. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use.

GMB.short: In 2026 the education and health ministries agreed to link their data systems; no link in service has been found.
GMB.summary: In July 2026 the education and health ministries signed an MoU to link the EMIS with the HMIS. The link is planned, not yet running. The MoU dates from the last twelve months. In October 2022 a DHIS2 for Education use case found separate databases for HR, examinations and infrastructure, and none brought them together. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

GNB.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

KEN.short: Since 2026 learner records are checked against the examination databases; no learner identifier shared across systems has been found.
KEN.summary: The Principal Secretary for basic education said KEMIS would go live on 9 January 2026 and integrate basic education, higher education and TVET with the examinations council and the Teachers Service Commission. A Ministry of Education circular says the KEMIS Learner Validation Engine is operational. It compares learner records with the official examination and assessment databases. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, a State House meeting with the Public Service Commission, the examinations council and the ministry agreed to integrate the systems that authenticate academic certificates. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

LBR.short: A 2025 peer review found the education data system linked to neither examination results nor teacher records.
LBR.summary: An AU-IPED peer review held on 1-2 September 2025 found Liberia's EMIS has no integration with WAEC exam data. It found no integration with teacher service records either. The exams, curriculum and teacher databases are not linked. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a link between education systems is under way. Preparing would need a link between two education systems to be contracted, being built or piloted.

LBY.short: A 2026 platform shows parents which private schools are licensed; nothing found names two education systems exchanging data, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names two education systems exchanging data, or says none do. Sources found name an Education Management Information System (EMIS), an OpenEMIS and an Education GIS, without showing a link between them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country's education systems exchange no data.

LSO.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

MAR.short: Morocco's school enrolment drew learner data from the civil register in 2024; no source found reports a link between education systems, so no stage is set.
MAR.summary: No stage is set. A ministry circular of 2024 has school heads and provincial offices register and check pupils' records in Massar. It gives each pupil a digital identifier in Massar, with a single national learner register as the aim. Massar's online enrolment services for parents rely on digital identity and can download the pupil's data held in the civil status register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names two education systems exchanging data. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

MDG.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MDG.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

MLI.short: In 2025 a donor project began linking a school attendance and results tool to the ministry's education system; no source found says whether the link works.
MLI.summary: On 5 June 2025 the PASCOFI project, run by EUMC and funded by Global Affairs Canada, called for a consultant to strengthen the ministry's education management system so that JIGITUGU can be integrated with it. The work includes a module to synchronise the ministry's education portal with JIGITUGU, by API or webhook. JIGITUGU collects pupils' and teachers' attendance and pupils' results in real time. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says the link is in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

MOZ.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MOZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

MRT.short: Mauritania's certificate service ran on the national ID platform in 2025; no source found reports a link between education systems, so no stage is set.
MRT.summary: No stage is set. In July 2025 the education ministry launched a service on the Houwiyati platform to extract and confirm national certificates. It covers certificates issued after 2013 or already linked to the holder's national number (NNI). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 names a link between education systems at any stage. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

MUS.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

MWI.short: An education data portal joining ministry and partner datasets was being built in 2026; no link in service has been found.
MWI.summary: In July 2026 the Unlocking Data Initiative Malawi team was developing an Education Data Portal (EDaP). It is to bring together datasets from the education ministry, MoEST, which runs the EMIS. Other datasets come from the gender and social welfare ministry, the National Statistics Office, development partners and academia. The portal work dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

NAM.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
NAM.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

NER.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

NGA.short: In 2026 the ministry said learner identification numbers were integrated with national identification numbers through the education data system.
NGA.summary: In 2026 Biometric Update reported that the Ministry of Education and NIMC integrated the Learner's Identification Number of 80 million students with the NIN registry, done via the digital NEMIS. The Federal Government says it launched the nationwide Learner Identification Number, building on DNEMIS. It says over 1.9 million candidates registered for the 2026 WAEC and NECO examinations have been issued one in the first phase. These reports date from 2026, within the last twelve months. The Minister of Education said more than 250 higher education institutions are integrated with the Nigeria Education Repository and Data Bank (NERD).

RWA.short: In 2026 the ministry and partners worked on linking its student and school data systems; no link in service has been found.
RWA.summary: In February 2026 HISP Rwanda worked with the education ministry on integrating SDMS, SEMIS and partner platforms. In May 2026 the national ID agency said the ministry was integrating education data systems with the Single Digital Identity. It named harmonising the EMIS with the population register for children under 16 as a challenge. Both reports date from the last twelve months. No source found says which education systems already exchange data. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

SDN.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

SEN.short: Every pupil carries a national education identifier, but no source names a second system that uses it.
SEN.summary: No stage is set. The ministry's GREEN guide says every pupil and teacher has a national education number, the IEN. The ministry says the IEN is deployed nationwide. No source names a second system that uses it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 names two education systems exchanging data or using one learner identifier. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

SLE.short: In 2026 the ministry began building a hub to connect its separate education data systems; no link in service has been found.
SLE.summary: In April 2026 MBSSE launched work, funded by GPE with UNICEF support, on a DHIS2-based national education data hub. Its interoperability layer will connect the annual school census, teacher management, learning assessments, school quality data and examination results. It is rolling out across all 16 districts. The launch dates from the last twelve months. The same source says those records are held in separate systems, with no reliable way to track a learner across them. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in use. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

SOM.short: Somalia's certificate system drew examination results from the exam registry in 2026; no source found reports one learner identifier across education systems.
SOM.summary: In May 2026 GovStack's showcase page showed the High School Certificate System connecting the MOECHE Examination System registry. Exam results are retrieved automatically and verified digital certificates are issued online. Somalia's Finance Minister countersigned the World Bank letter of amendment on 2 October 2025, which finances expansion of the Teacher Management Information System and its integration with the EMIS. The showcase page dates from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

SSD.short: In 2025 the refugee education data system drew on the ministry's records and fed enrolment data back; no shared learner identifier has been found.
SSD.summary: In September 2025 an ERICC working paper said REMIS, UNHCR's refugee education data system, relies on data from the ministry's EMIS. Only the ministry receives REMIS enrolment and attendance data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

STP.short: In 2023 the education ministry's information systems were not linked; nothing found since, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names education systems exchanging data. Sources found name a Sistema Integrado de Gestão Escolar (SIGE) and dashboards for national education supervision, and show no link between them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country's education systems exchange no data.

SWZ.short: Eswatini's school records were keyed to the national ID in 2024; no source found reports a link between education systems, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: No stage is set. In 2024 the DHIS2 for Education profile described Eswatini's EMIS data as connected to national identity. The SEMIS App holds individual learner and staff data by PIN and has been national in scale since a 2020 pilot. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a link between education systems is contracted, being built, piloted or in service. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

SYC.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

TCD.short: In 2021 the education ministry's platforms could not link; nothing found since 2023, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names education systems exchanging data. Sources found name a Système d'Information pour la Gestion de l'Éducation (SIGE) and a UNHCR refugee-school EMIS, and show no link between them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says the country's education systems exchange no data.

TGO.short: In 2025 the ministry's education data system connected planning, examinations and the inspectorate; no shared learner identifier has been found.
TGO.summary: In 2025 the implementing researchers and Ministry staff stated that Togo's ministry has developed an integrated education data system, StatEduc with DHIS2. It connects the Department of Planning, the Examinations Department and the General Inspectorate of Education. A World Bank mission noted non-appropriation of the project to interconnect platforms and databases, under the basic education project P172674. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

TUN.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

TZA.short: The teachers' commission's system exchanged teacher data with the school information system in 2024; no learner identifier shared across systems is known.
TZA.summary: The Teachers Service Commission said in August 2024 that its teacher information system, TSCMIS, is connected to three other systems: the School Information System, the civil service HR system and the Treasury pensions system. The links exchange teacher data. In the last twelve months, on 13 July 2026 the Permanent Secretary told institutions to speed up linking their platforms to the Education Sector Management Information System. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need one learner identifier used by two or more education systems.

UGA.short: Exam results and a health link run through an education data platform in pilot sites in 2026; the national system lacks an exam-board link.
UGA.summary: In June 2026 the ministry's statistics lead said the EMIS lacks integration with the national examinations board's system, so not all Senior One and Senior Five students are captured. He said the ministries and the board are working to close the gap. In the last twelve months, a HISP Uganda brief of April 2026 said 2025 primary leaving results were brought into DHIS2 for Education. In 2023 that platform ran in 10 of 175 administrative sites. No source found since October 2023 says the national EMIS exchanges data with another system in service. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

ZAF.short: Since at least 2025 the national learner register has taken learner records from provincial school systems; no identifier shared across systems has been found.
ZAF.summary: The Department of Basic Education told Parliament in December 2025 that LURITS, its learner register, consolidates the learner records schools submit. Schools submit them through provincial school administration systems and provincial data warehouses. In August 2026 MICT SETA told Parliament that an Integrated Learner Management System is being piloted in a couple of SETAs, to join the post-school bodies' systems in one platform.
