Both statements date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says one learner identifier is used across education systems. Operating would need learners to carry a unique identifier used by two or more education systems.

ZMB.short: Nothing found names education systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ZMB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names education systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

ZWE.short: In 2026 UNICEF sought a consultant to build a school registration system linked to the ministry's records; no link in service has been found.
ZWE.summary: In April 2026 UNICEF sought a consultant to build a web-based school registration system for the education ministry. The system is to be integrated with the EMIS. In June 2026 the ministry's spokesperson said an Early Warning System is now part of the EMIS. These steps date from the last twelve months. In 2019 an ADEA peer review found no formal structures for sharing data among education stakeholders. No source found since October 2023 says two education systems exchange data in service. Establishing would need two education systems exchanging data in use, such as the EMIS with the examinations body, teacher payroll or learner registration.

AGO.short: Education statistics were collected through the ministry's information system in 2025; no source found reports a record for each learner.
AGO.summary: Angola's planning office says the data for its 2022/2023 statistical yearbook were collected through SIGE. It calls the platform in operation but not a finished product. ADEA says the ministry is discussing an EMIS legal framework and a modernised national EMIS. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the Angolan firm Mwango Brain took on the technical work of that project with the planning office. No source found since October 2023 says SIGE holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

BDI.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
BDI.summary: Under a December 2022 agreement with UNESCO, Burundi's education ministry built a human-resources module for the SIGE, UNESCO said in December 2024. A workshop in mid-2024 planned the module's link to the STATEDUC statistics tool. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 UNESCO trained seven ministry staff in database administration. In June 2026 an African Union Commission workshop in Bujumbura set out to strengthen the system. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through it. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

BEN.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
BEN.summary: In August 2026 the EducMaster portal of Benin's education ministries said the SIGE produces statistical reports and national indicators by department. The platform lists 1,804,826 learners, 63,305 teachers and 17,330 schools. This position dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found to compare it with. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

BFA.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2024; a record for each learner is not on record.
BFA.summary: In September 2024 IIEP said it had helped integrate education-in-emergencies data into Burkina Faso's SIGE. This let the education ministry update the annual school census results and report school reopenings to central government. The director general of education studies and statistics, Sylvain Ouédraogo, said the SIGE is being renovated. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

BWA.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national education information system, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether an education information system is under way or in service in Botswana. No source has been found since that date that names a national education management information system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the education ministry to procure, pilot or build an education management information system.

CAF.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national education information system, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether an education information system is under way or in service in the Central African Republic. No source has been found since that date that names a national education management information system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the education ministry to procure, pilot or build an education management information system.

CIV.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
CIV.summary: Fraternité Matin reports the education minister launched the SIGE on 10 July 2025, funded by the MCC. It was tested in Bouaké and San Pedro and is to be extended nationwide when financing allows. Ecofin Agency reports that since 2022 the Education Ministry has deployed an Integrated Education Management Information System (SIGE) with MCC support under a $536 million Compact. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

CMR.short: Education statistics were published through an online information system in 2024; no source found reports a record for each learner.
CMR.summary: In June 2024 the National Institute of Statistics published the first education and training sector yearbook, for 2021-2022. It pointed users to the online EMIS platform for more detailed data. On 8 May 2025 the basic education ministry presented the integrated sectoral SIGE platform, which is designed to hold the statistics of every education and training subsector. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the platform holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

COD.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
COD.summary: In June 2023 a World Bank paper said DIGE had collected 2022/23 school data through the e-SIGE-DRC application. That collection covered the 10 project provinces. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission says a workshop in Kinshasa on 12-14 May 2026 supports the DRC in assessing and strengthening its Education Management Information System. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

COG.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
COG.summary: In December 2025 the World Bank's TRESOR project recorded no integrated EMIS in Congo, with one targeted by July 2030. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 an African Union workshop in Brazzaville reviewed the state of the country's EMIS. In August 2026 the state IT agency ACSI presented its integrated education management project, the SIGE, to the National Assembly's Ecofin committee. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through a system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

COM.short: A national education platform held data on 80,000 pupils and 700 schools in 2025; no source found says whether every school is on it.
COM.summary: Comoros runs a national education platform, e-Msomo, built by the education ministry with the digital agency ANADEN and UNICEF. In December 2025 UNICEF said it held over 80,000 pupils, 700 schools and 3,000 teachers in one national database, and that it follows each pupil's school path, attendance and marks. Schools are still being added. An earlier AFD project, run from 2019, listed deploying the SIGE information system among its aims. In the last twelve months, UNICEF's account of December 2025 is the latest position found. No source found since October 2023 says every school's pupils have records in the system. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

CPV.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
CPV.summary: In March 2025 the national education directorate said SIGE was in use in basic and secondary schools. In July 2025 the directorate began national training on a new special-needs module in SIGE. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the GPE approved a US$1 million grant for PRISE 2026-2028, whose work includes expanding and modernising SIGE. No source found since October 2023 says the school census or education statistics are produced through SIGE. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

DJI.short: An education information system was under way in 2025; a school census run through it is not on record.
DJI.summary: In September 2025 La Nation reported a circular of the education minister dated 1 September 2025. It makes consolidating the Système d'Information pour la Gestion de l'Éducation (SIGE) a priority. The work runs through the GOSE and SMIS platforms, to produce reliable, regularly updated data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

DZA.short: An education information system was under way in 2024; a school census run through it is not on record.
DZA.summary: In November 2024 the education ministry said an updated 2025 version of the national education sector information system was being prepared. It was to be ready in March 2025, after a nationwide evaluation. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no source found since October 2023 says the 2025 version was issued. No source found since that date says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

EGY.short: The ministry's central database produced the 2024/25 statistical yearbook; a record for each learner with a unique number is not on record.
EGY.summary: The ministry says its central database is the source of the 2024/25 statistical yearbook. It holds every element of the education process. In June 2025 the ministry took kindergarten and grade 1 applications for public schools online through its EMIS portal. A 2025 book chapter says the ministry's Digital Identity Project stores data on each student in central databases. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found names a unique learner number in national service. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

ERI.short: An education information system was under way in 2024; a school census run through it is not on record.
ERI.summary: On 19 April 2024 Eritrea's Ministry of Education submitted a programme document to GPE. It seeks US$14.02m, through UNICEF. The funds include strengthened routine data collection, processing, storage and use in the national EMIS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

ETH.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2023; a record for each learner is not on record.
ETH.summary: The Ministry of Education's EMIS and ICT Executive Office published the Education Statistics Annual Abstract 2022/2023 in October 2023. The office says the EMIS is available at decentralised levels and collects education performance data. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the education minister said the EMIS and its higher-education counterpart were being strengthened. He said this would connect data on students, teachers, institutions and outcomes. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

GAB.short: An education information system was under way in 2025; a 2021 school census was published, but not one run through the system.
GAB.summary: In August 2025 the education ministry began adding school health indicators to its education management information system, the SIGE. In October 2024 SOSUP launched a national operation to identify schools and give each learner a unique national identifier. Provincial and zonal delegates collect the school and pupil files for it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. The census of 2021 is not tied to it. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

GHA.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2025; a record for each learner is not on record.
GHA.summary: The Ministry of Education completed a review of Education Management Information System indicators at a 17-18 December 2025 workshop. Stakeholders agreed to integrate the revised indicators into the next national school census. This review dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier set of indicators has been found to compare it with. The Ministry of Education's PMDV Dashboard API documentation lists an EMIS schools statistics endpoint. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

GIN.short: Guinea's education ministry was reinforcing its education information system in 2023; no source found reports a school census run through it.
GIN.summary: In December 2023 a World Bank report said work to strengthen the ministry's EMIS under a UNESCO contract was delayed. Since 2024 the education ministry, through its examinations directorate DGECS, has run a platform on which schools enrol their pupils, Educationactu reported in October 2026. In 2024-25 it covered grades 7 and 11. In the last twelve months, in 2025-26 it was extended to the intermediate classes of primary and secondary school, except grade 9. No source found since October 2023 says the education information system produced an annual school census. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

GMB.short: The education information system held a record for each learner in 2025; a link to the national ID is not on record.
GMB.summary: The Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education began building its education information system on DHIS2 in 2018. In August 2025 DHIS2 said the ministry's digital student registry gives each learner a unique ID. It holds nearly 80% of Gambian learners. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the ministry opened the Education Data Center to the public. It brings the school census, attendance reports and other sources into one portal. No source found since October 2023 says learner records are linked to the national ID or another government system. Mature would need learner records linked to the national ID, or data exchanged with another government system.

GNB.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
GNB.summary: In October 2025 FEC said practical training began on the SIGE 2.0 education information and management platform. The EU-funded PESIDE project runs it with the Ministry of Education. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 a Global Partnership for Education blog said PESIDE aims to strengthen the Education Management Information System (EMIS). No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names a national education information system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the education ministry holds its statistics in an information system.

KEN.short: The education information system held a record for each learner in 2026; a link to the national ID is not on record.
KEN.summary: In September 2025 the government moved from NEMIS to KEMIS, the Daily Nation reports. A Ministry of Education KEMIS Secretariat circular says KEMIS holds learner records. KEMIS generates a Unique Learner Identifier (ULI) for learners in schools. In the last twelve months, KEMIS was the required platform for the 2026 Grade 10 selection. By 10 November 2026 it held about 5.06 million primary learners of 7.2 million expected. No source found since October 2023 says learner records are linked to the national ID or another government system. Mature would need learner records linked to the national ID, or data exchanged with another government system.

LBR.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
LBR.summary: The ministry's EMIS portal shows academic year 2024-25 census data for all 15 counties. It lists 1,274,610 enrolled students in 6,394 registered schools. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the education ministry said regular Annual School Census collection had resumed, after an interruption following 2021. The EMIS portal says it tracks every enrolled learner with a unique identifier, but in September 2026 the ministry was still seeking a digitised EMIS. No source settles whether a record for each learner is in service. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

LBY.short: An education information system was under way in 2024; a school census run through it is not on record.
LBY.summary: In July 2024 the Ministry of Education, supported by UNICEF Libya, launched its Education Management Information System (EMIS). Al-Wasat named the system OpenEMIS. The launch followed a pilot in 205 educational institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

LSO.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
LSO.summary: Lesotho's national education information system is LEMIS. In May 2026 the ministry said LEMIS was still being built. It is meant to cover 4,819 institutions and was not yet live for nationwide collection. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 an AU-IPED brief said Lesotho had adopted DHIS2 for Education as the platform for LEMIS. All 365 secondary schools report through it, the brief said. No source found since October 2023 says the school census or national statistics were produced through it. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

MAR.short: Massar gives each pupil a digital identifier and draws on the civil status register, from 2024; no source found says how many pupils hold one.
MAR.summary: The ministry ran the 2025-2026 annual school census from 20 October to 20 November 2025, and a ministry letter named Massar as the main source of its statistics. A 2024 ministry circular says Massar digitises each pupil's school file and gives each pupil a digital identifier, and that its enrolment services rely on digital identity and can download data from the civil status register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how many pupils hold the digital identifier. None counts the records drawn from the civil status register.

MDG.short: An education information system was under way in 2024; a school census run through it is not on record.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's authorities launched at a 15-17 July 2024 workshop in Toamasina the digitisation of schools, starting in Atsinanana, covering data collection and a pupil register. A financing law for the TALIM programme, adopted by the Senate in 2025, provides for modernising the education management information system. In April 2023 INSTAT said the planning directorate collected the 2022-2023 school census and entered it in ministry software. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

MLI.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
MLI.summary: In October 2024 UNESCO said the education ministry's planning unit (CPS) collected 2023-24 national data on school-health indicators integrated into the SIGE. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 UNESCO said the SIGE holds national data, collected regularly by the ministry. A March 2026 workshop analysed its data for the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 school years. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

MOZ.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
MOZ.summary: The education ministry's Planning and Cooperation Directorate runs the annual 3 March school census (Levantamento Escolar 2024, public and private schools). Its Statistics Department publishes the resulting education statistics brochure each year. In the last twelve months, an assessment on 3-4 August 2026, supported by GPE KIX, found an established EMIS with several data subsystems and electronic platforms. It found that education statistics already inform teacher deployment and resource allocation. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

MRT.short: Nothing found names a national education information system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MRT.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the education ministry holds its statistics in an information system.

MUS.short: A secondary-school education information system was piloted in 2025; a school census run through a national system is not on record.
MUS.summary: A UNESCO IITE project with Chengdu Group, completed in 2025, piloted an education management information system for secondary schools. The pilot is the only education information system on record for the country. Nothing found says the ministry runs its school census through a national system. Nothing found says it publishes its education statistics from one either. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

MWI.short: Malawi's EMIS produced the 2023/24 school census and tracks learners by number; no link to the national ID is known.
MWI.summary: The ministry's Education Statistics Report 2023/24 comes from the Annual School Census, run through the EMIS. It counts 5,420,159 primary pupils and 538,800 secondary students. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 a policy brief said pupils get Learner Identification Numbers on entry to school, and that cohort tracking within the EMIS generates longitudinal learner-level data. No source found since October 2023 says learner records are linked to the national ID or another government system. Mature would need learner records linked to the national ID or birth registration number, or exchanging data with another government system.

NAM.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2024; a record for each learner is not on record.
NAM.summary: In 2024 the Ministry of Education, Arts and Culture said its EMIS division collects data from all state and private schools twice a year. It publishes the Fifteenth School Day Report and the Annual Education Census. The ministry lists census reports for 2019 to 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

NER.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national education information system, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether an education information system is under way or in service in Niger. No source has been found since that date that names a national education management information system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the education ministry to procure, pilot or build an education management information system.

NGA.short: The national education information system supplied enrolment and teacher data in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
NGA.summary: In September 2026 Minister Alausa said the digitised Nigeria Education Management Information System was providing data on enrolment, teachers, classrooms, laboratories, libraries and connectivity. He said over 240,000 schools were geo-mapped and the Annual School Census was being digitised. These statements date from the last twelve months, and no earlier statement of the system's coverage has been found to compare them with. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

RWA.short: The education information system held a record for each learner in 2025; a link to the national ID is not on record.
RWA.summary: The ministry's web-based School Data Management System (SDMS) tracks enrolment, attendance, results, school finance and school feeding. In 2025 the ministry's chief digital officer said annual education statistics are compiled through it, and school compliance had risen from 40% to 70-80%. A headteacher interviewed in 2025 said every student is assigned a unique ID in the SDMS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The 2025 report says the SDMS does not yet fully connect with other management systems. No source found since October 2023 says learner records are linked to the national ID or another government system. Mature would need learner records linked to the national ID or birth registration number, or exchanging data with another government system.

SDN.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
SDN.summary: In the last twelve months, UNESCO states it handed IT equipment to the Red Sea State Ministry of Education on 12 May 2026. The equipment comprised 30 tablets, two desktops, routers and other gear for the state's Education Management and Information System pilot project. UNESCO states it handed over EMIS and Monitoring and Evaluation hardware to Sudan's Ministry of Education, funded by the Global Partnership for Education, reported on 26 April 2026. No earlier position has been found to compare these with. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

SEN.short: The ministry was deploying its education information platforms nationwide in 2026; no source found says whether the school census runs through them.
SEN.summary: In August 2026 the coordinator of SIMEN, the ministry's integrated management system, said the ministry had built 41 platforms in-house and was deploying them across the country. A workshop in Saly from 13 to 15 August 2026 planned the national roll-out of five of them for the 2026-2027 school year. The ministry described the same identifier in 2018, and in the last twelve months, in August 2026, the coordinator said it is still being deployed. No source found says a school census was run through SIMEN. None says how many schools use it. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

SLE.short: The school census was published through the education information system in 2025; a record for each learner is not on record.
SLE.summary: The MBSSE EMIS page lists Annual School Census reports for 2015 to 2022 and 2025. It says EMIS is a centralised database with information about every student, teacher and school. UNICEF published request for proposal 9200546 for a Unique Learner ID (ULID) system and data warehouse, with a deadline of 28 October 2025. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the ministry began building a DHIS2-based learner-centred education data hub. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner with a unique learner number. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

SOM.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2024; a record for each learner is not on record.
SOM.summary: The ministry's July 2025 terms of reference describe its online EMIS, rolled out nationwide in 2019. GPE says MOECHE initiated the EMIS in 2016, and that it collects and analyzes data from schools on an annual basis. In July 2025 the ministry sought a firm to add individual student-level data to the system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

SSD.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a national education information system, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether an education information system is under way or in service in South Sudan. No source has been found since that date that names a national education management information system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the education ministry to procure, pilot or build an education management information system.

STP.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
STP.summary: In the last twelve months, on 1 April 2026 AFAP, the World Bank-financed project agency, announced a procurement of specialist technical assistance. The assistance covers technological infrastructure, resource management and training. It is for implementing the Sistema Integrado de Gestão Escolar (SIGE). No earlier position has been found to compare it with. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

SWZ.short: Learner records were linked to the national ID or another government system in 2024.
SWZ.summary: DHIS2 for Education describes a fully operational Eswatini EMIS. It served as the source for the country's 2022 UIS reporting on enrolments, repeaters and staffing. GPE KIX says Eswatini's PIN-driven EMIS introduced individual-level student and staff tracking across all 976 schools. Aggregate and individual EMIS data are connected to national identity, the Eswatini implementation page says. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The system produced a 2026 bursary list for orphans and vulnerable children, which is the latest dated fact found.

SYC.short: An education information system was under way in 2026; a school census run through it is not on record.
SYC.summary: In March 2026 Community Systems Foundation, resharing its project lead, said the Ministry of Education's new Education Management Information System (EMIS) had gone live. The post tags the system OpenEMIS. This position dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier system has been found to compare it with. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through it. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

TCD.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
TCD.summary: UNICEF Innocenti says Chad's EMIS has routinely collected data from schools since 2009, analysed centrally. In the last twelve months, UNESCO says it handed over about USD 550,000 of GPE-financed computing equipment to education ministry bodies on 15 June 2026. The higher-education ministry trained its statistics and digitalisation staff on the StatEduc application on 20-25 July 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

TGO.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
TGO.summary: In May 2026 Togo's SIGE added DHIS2 on top of CSPro-based statistical infrastructure, with StatEduc used for the annual school census. Togo's education ministry processes annual census data through StatEduc, per the implementing researchers and ministry staff. The Ministry of Primary, Secondary, Technical Education is piloting DHIS2 alongside the existing StatEduc application. This position dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found to compare it with. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

TUN.short: Tunisia's education ministry ran a national school-life system in 2026; no source found reports a school census run through it.
TUN.summary: On 18 November 2026 Tunisia's education minister told parliament that the school-life system is an integrated government system. It was built with the communication technologies ministry. Teachers enter and follow pupils' marks in it, and it holds pupils' school records and teachers' careers. In the last twelve months, the minister's account is the only dated position found, and no earlier one has been found to compare it with. No source found says the school census is run through the school-life system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

TZA.short: Tanzania publishes yearly education statistics, and its school information system keys learners by number and shares data with the exams council.
TZA.summary: The statistics bureau's 2025 abstract draws its school tables from the 2025 edition of Basic Education Statistics, which PO-RALG publishes each year. They count 3,425,822 secondary students in 2025. In May 2018 the education ministry launched PReM, funded through GPE and Sweden, giving each public and private primary pupil a unique identification number. The School Information System shares learner data with NECTA, the examinations council, and with the ministry. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated fact found is the 2025 edition.

UGA.short: Learner records were linked to the national ID or another government system in 2026.
UGA.summary: In June 2026 New Vision reported that under EMIS every learner is assigned a unique Learner Identification Number (LIN). By 3 October 2024 the EMIS had registered 13.3 million learners from 75,850 schools, the ministry told The Observer. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the HISP Uganda brief said the DHIS2-Ed system was linked to the Ministry of Health's eIDSR platform. The link carries school-based surveillance indicators. The latest dated fact found is the June 2026 report.

ZAF.short: The education information system held a record for each learner in 2026; a link to the national ID is not on record.
ZAF.summary: The Department of Basic Education records learner enrolment through LURITS, with 13,596,869 learners recorded for 2025. In the last twelve months, in January 2026 the minister said LURITS holds data for each learner, with ID numbers. On 2-4 February 2026 the department's EMIS directorate tested a modernised, cloud-based SA-SAMS with NECT. A phased primary-school pilot and a national rollout are to follow. Nothing found since October 2023 says learner records are linked to the national ID or exchange data with another government system. Mature would need learner records linked to the national ID, or data exchanged with another government system.

ZMB.short: An education information system was under way in 2024; a school census run through it is not on record.
ZMB.summary: In December 2024 a World Bank aide memoire said technical assistance to review the Teaching Council of Zambia teacher database was being considered. It placed that review within the broader EMIS reform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the school census is run through the system. Establishing would need the ministry to collect or publish an annual school census or education statistics through its education information system.

ZWE.short: The school census was run through an education information system in 2026; a record for each learner is not on record.
ZWE.summary: In November 2026 the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education said it compiles school enrolment figures through the revised EMIS. It sends them to the Ministry of Finance for each year's education budget. It said 12,324 schools nationwide are equipped to use the system. In the last twelve months, the ministry's EMIS Report, cited by NewZimbabwe, counts 39,736 learners who dropped out in 2025, in June 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the system holds a record for each learner. Operating would need the system to hold individual learner records with a unique learner number, in service for schools across the country.

AGO.short: Government services were going online in 2026; ten or more online are not on record.
AGO.summary: The Simplifica programmes of 2021 and 2023 put certificates, registrations, authorisations and licences on www.sepe.gov.ao. In the last twelve months the SEPE portal was cited and not changed. In October 2026 Portal de T.I. reported that the SEPE portal is online and working, with registration, sign-in and a catalogue of services. In November 2026 the migration service moved border-visa applications fully online for registered entities. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online. None says that one account reaches several ministries' services, or counts users of SEPE. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

BDI.short: Burundi's revenue office moved the land tax declaration online in 2026; ten or more services online are not on record.
BDI.summary: In July 2026 the Burundi Revenue Office said the land tax declaration for 2026/2027 must be filed online on its UMUTANGAKORI II platform. The deadline was 30 September 2026. Since 6 May 2024 the urban planning office has taken building-permit applications online, Burundi Eco reports. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the World Bank listed a tender for a national e-Gouv portal under the PAFEN project. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online. None says that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

BEN.short: Benin's national portal offers over 200 services online through one user account, and publishes its request counts.
BEN.summary: In November 2026 service-public.bj listed 1,208 services, 131 of them available online, by its own count. Users of service-public.bj create an account or sign in to a personal space. Over 50 institutions offer services through the portal, Cybernetica said in February 2025. In the last twelve months, since 1 November 2026, a criminal record certificate is issued at once on the portal. On 18 November 2026 the digital minister said Benin had deployed more than 250 e-services. In November 2026 the portal showed more than 2.5 million requests.

BFA.short: Ten or more government services could be completed online in 2026; a single gateway is not on record.
BFA.summary: On 5 May 2026 the government launched service-public.gov.bf to bring public services online in one place. The portal offers 95 procedures completed online and links 183 public institutions. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the government launched version 2 of the Service Public BF portal. In December 2025 three justice platforms opened for complaints, prison visit permits and commercial registry papers. No source found says how users sign in to the portal, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

BWA.short: Ten or more government services could be completed online in 2026; a single gateway is not on record.
BWA.summary: In February 2026 the 2026/27 budget confirmed continued investment in the platform, which the government calls its integrated e-services platform, 1Gov1Citizen. In the last twelve months the budget speech put 52 public services fully online on the 1Gov1Citizen platform, BWTechZone reports. A further 179 services were then in final integration testing. A 2023 review found the earlier 1Gov portal unstable, poorly linked to agencies and little used, ADM Interactive says. No source found says how users sign in to 1Gov1Citizen, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

CAF.short: A national portal for public services opened in 2026; no source found says whether ten or more services can be completed on it.
CAF.summary: On 14 October 2026 the government launched a national digital portal for public services, Africa Business Insight reports. On it people can apply for driving licences and urban transport passes, request criminal record extracts and nationality certificates, and obtain school attendance and baccalaureate certificates. The portal carries services of the transport, justice and education sectors. It is the one change in the last twelve months that has been found. No source found says how users sign in to it, or that ten or more services can be completed on it. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire had 315 procedures online on its national portal by 2025; no source found says how users sign in.
CIV.summary: SNDI, the state IT company, said 315 administrative procedures had been digitised and put online by 31 December 2025. They are on the national public services portal. In May 2025 the trade ministry said the GUCE-CI single window lets businesses complete import, export and transit formalities online. In the last twelve months, on 10 November 2026, the tourism ministry opened a digital one-stop shop for tourism operators. They file procedures, pay and track applications online, first in four regional offices. No source found says how users sign in to the national portal. None counts its users. Operating would need one national portal that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

CMR.short: Government services were going online in 2026; ten or more online are not on record.
CMR.summary: In August 2023 the finance ministry unveiled Tresor Pay for paying non-tax public services online, by mobile money, post office or card. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the tax directorate launched registrations.dgi.cm for registering deeds online. Three public procurement acts could be registered and paid for by mobile money. More than 120 other acts in its catalogue were shown as unavailable. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

COD.short: A national digital ID with one login for government services began pilot testing in 2026; no service yet reached through it is named.
COD.summary: In June 2026 the government launched RDC-Pass, a national digital identity platform, in Kinshasa. Its rollout began with pilot testing. In the last twelve months, on 19 November 2026, the civil service ministry announced E-Services RDC, a portal and app publishing the procedures and official fees of public services in six languages. In July 2026 the business one-stop shop GUCE presented a site that tracks company files in real time and an app for formalising informal operators. No source found names a ministry service that users reach through RDC-Pass, or says that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

COG.short: Congo's e-Citizen Portal let people file procedures and pay online in 2026; no source found reports a count of ten or more services online.
COG.summary: The digital economy ministry says citizens can use the e-Citizen Portal to file administrative procedures, pay taxes and fees, and track their files in real time. The ministry describes the e-Citizen Portal as the single entry point to all digital public services. In June 2024 the budget ministry reviewed E-Bourses, a project to let students apply online for scholarships. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, and no count of users has been found. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

COM.short: Government services were going online in 2024; ten or more online are not on record.
COM.summary: In June 2024 the national digital agency ANADEN held a technical meeting to present e-Bourse, a national portal for online scholarship applications. ANADEN lists the portal among its projects and marks it as in progress. In June 2025 its procurement notice listed an upgraded government portal with e-services and digital payments, funded by the AfDB. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says that one national portal carries several ministries' services, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

CPV.short: Government services were going online in 2024; ten or more online are not on record.
CPV.summary: On 18 December 2024 the government launched the Portal de Justiça. Users of the Portal de Justiça sign in through Autentika, the state's authentication platform. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the government launched Gov.cv, a single portal for public services. It takes criminal record, nationality and higher education applications and tracks each request. No source found says how users sign in to Gov.cv, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

DJI.short: Nothing found since 2023 names government services online, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether government services can be used online in Djibouti. No source found names a services portal or app, or a service that can be applied for or paid online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government services portal or app launched, or a service piloted that can be applied for or paid online.

DZA.short: Algeria's national portal carried 91 services of several ministries on one account in 2026, with about two million registered users.
DZA.summary: In July 2026 the High Commission for Digitalisation said the national portal, Dzair Digital Services, carried 21 digital services, with 62 planned by the end of 2027. In the last twelve months the count has risen. By 10 November 2026 the portal offered 68 services. On 19 November 2026 a High Commission for Digitalisation expert put it at 91 public services. Twenty tourism and handicraft services were added on 16 November. The expert said one account reaches services of the interior, local government, employment, social security, tax and justice sectors. On 19 November 2026 the expert gave about two million registered citizens and nearly 11 million visits.

EGY.short: Use of the national government services portal was published in 2026.
EGY.summary: In September 2026 communications minister Raafat Hindy said the Digital Egypt platform provides more than 240 government services in 29 bundles. In the last twelve months the stated count has risen. In November 2026 the assistant minister put the count at 261 services in 29 packages, plus 21 apps. Enterprise reports that one Digital Egypt account, opened with the 14-digit national ID and a mobile number, works across civil status, traffic, real estate and court services. In October 2026 an assistant minister said Digital Egypt had about 13.5 million users. In November 2026 the ministry put active users at 13.7 million, up from 10.4 million a year earlier. Transactions rose from 23.8 million to 36 million.

ERI.short: Government services were going online in 2024; ten or more online are not on record.
ERI.summary: On 24 September 2024 the Eritrean embassy in the United States launched the Consular Affairs Processing System (CAPS). The foreign ministry built it. Through CAPS, applications for ID cards, entry visas and passport renewals are begun online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No other government service in Eritrea has been found online since October 2023, and no source found says whether a national portal exists. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

ETH.short: A one-stop digital platform for government services with national ID sign-in ran in 2026; no source found says how many use it.
ETH.summary: National ID Ethiopia's May 2026 deck calls MESOB a digital one-stop shop for e-government services built on the Fayda ID. Prime Minister Abiy inaugurated the Unified MESOB Application, which brings 27 services from several institutions onto one platform. In the last twelve months, on 30 March 2026, Ethio Telecom launched teleSign, where people apply online for document authentication, powers of attorney and professional licences, paid by telebirr. In October 2026 the trade ministry said 1,088,787 business registration and licensing services were delivered online in three months. No source found gives users, applications or transactions through a national portal. Mature would need a number of users, applications or transactions through the national portal published.

GAB.short: Government services were going online in 2025; ten or more online are not on record.
GAB.summary: In November 2023 the immigration directorate DGDI opened an e-services portal for renewing passports, ID cards and residence permits. In the last twelve months the Gabon Connect platform was set up in March 2026 to put tax, customs, land and social security procedures online. On 22 October 2026 the vice-president of the government presented Gabon Connect as a single digital window, with a first phase due to finish in December 2027. On 16 November 2026 the state pension fund CPPF launched its Baana platform nationwide. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or counts users of a national portal. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

GHA.short: Interior ministry permits could be applied for online in 2025; no source found says whether ten or more services can be completed online.
GHA.summary: The Interior Ministry opened an online services portal, fully working from 15 December 2025. It takes applications for immigrant quota permits, citizenship renunciation, dual nationality, naturalisation and licences. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Lands Commission's portal let buyers pay for a land search and receive the report by email, live in 10 of 16 regions. The digital economy policy describes Ghana.gov as the portal that centralises access to government services. No source found counts ten or more services online, or says how users sign in to Ghana.gov. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

GIN.short: Government services were going online in 2026; ten or more online are not on record.
GIN.summary: On 7 May 2026 the minister launched the deployment of the national e-Services platform, built inside the digital agency ANDE. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the livestock ministry launched Ngaynaako, a portal for livestock requests. On 26 October 2026 the fisheries ministry launched Konkoe, where fishers apply for licences and track their files. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

GMB.short: Government services were going online in 2025; ten or more online are not on record.
GMB.summary: In September 2024 the minister said the government was building a one-stop platform for its services. In 2025 the communications ministry presented MYGOV, a one-stop platform starting with five pilot services, modelled on Bangladesh's platform, with UNDP and ECOWAS support. In 2025 the National Records Commission opened a portal for information requests, tracked online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says that MYGOV is in service, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

GNB.short: Nothing found since 2023 names government services online, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether government services can be used online in Guinea-Bissau. No source found names a services portal or app, or a service that can be applied for or paid online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government services portal or app launched, or a service piloted that can be applied for or paid online.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea has run an online e-visa since 2023; no source found reports ten or more services online.
GNQ.summary: Equatorial Guinea's e-visa service opened on 1 July 2023, run for the government by the company VFS Global. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the document agency CNEDOGE put requests for official documents online, with payment notes and status tracking. In October 2026 the Vice-President said it had processed about 35,127 e-visas since its launch, against 200,000 a year expected. No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, or names a single national portal. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

KEN.short: One national portal carried over 22,000 services with over 15 million active accounts in 2026; no source found reports its 2026 transaction count.
KEN.summary: In October 2024 the Treasury Cabinet Secretary told the Senate the platform carried 16,000 services, up from 397. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the ICT Cabinet Secretary said more than 22,500 services were available on eCitizen. The draft 2026 Budget Policy Statement put services onboarded at over 17,668, from more than 350 agencies. In December 2024 eCitizen's Director General put active accounts at 13.5 million. A May 2026 government presentation gave over 15 million active eCitizen accounts. No count of transactions through eCitizen in 2026 has been found.

LBR.short: Several agencies took applications or payments online in 2025 and 2026; no source found says ten or more services can be completed online.
LBR.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority says it launched an Online Duty-Free Application Platform in July 2025. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the consulate general in New York put payment for all consular services online, among them visas and passports. The mines ministry's deputy minister said its online system for mining licence applications was fully operational. No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, names a single gateway with national ID sign-in, or publishes a portal's use. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

LBY.short: Government services were going online in 2024; ten or more online are not on record.
LBY.summary: On 3 March 2024 the Government of National Unity's interior ministry launched a package of e-services, including the start of an e-government portal project. In December 2024 Cabinet Decision 705 created the Dawlati platform to provide e-services and issue official documents. In the last twelve months, in late October 2026, the passports authority's e-visa unit received 773 applications in a week and approved 610. No source found says whether a national portal is in service, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

LSO.short: Government services were going online in 2026; ten or more online are not on record.
LSO.summary: In June 2024 UNDP and the communications ministry launched the E-Service Outlet Model. Under it, internet and print shops and mobile money agents help people use government e-services. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, a minister said an integrated online services platform with a payment gateway was close to launch. Also in May 2026 the ministry validated the first stage of automating e-services with Home Affairs, Public Service, Public Works and Finance. No source found says the platform has launched, that one sign-in reaches several ministries, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

MAR.short: Ten or more government services could be completed online in 2026; a single gateway is not on record.
MAR.summary: On 18 September 2026 the digital transition ministry relaunched the national Idarati portal. The ministry says Idarati gives access to 874 online services and 2,533 published administrative acts. That is up from 605 at the end of 2023, as counted by the Court of Audit. In the last twelve months, from 9 November 2026, Moroccans abroad can apply online for criminal record certificates through the police's Epolice portal. No source found says how users sign in to Idarati, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

MDG.short: Government services were going online in 2024; ten or more online are not on record.
MDG.summary: In May 2024 the Digital Governance Unit made Torolalana a portal for transactions as well as information, integrating services of public bodies. In the last twelve months, on 31 October 2026, the anti-corruption bureau BIANCO launched i-Fanagna for filing asset declarations remotely. In November 2026 the higher education ministry opened e-Courrier for submitting and tracking mail online. In the last twelve months, a commissioner put the register at 22.1 million voters in April 2026. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

LBR.short: The voters' roll was held digitally in 2023; voters checking it is not on record.
LBR.summary: A 2023 paper says Liberia's National Elections Commission uses a biometric voter registration system, which holds the voters' roll. The paper gives 2,471,617 registered voters in 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll was published or that voters could check their entries online, by text message or at centres. None says the roll is drawn from the national ID, population or civil register. Operating would need a source showing the roll was published or open to voters to check, online, by text message or at centres.

LBY.short: Voters could check the roll by text message and lists were published in 2025; no source shows it checked against the civil registry.
LBY.summary: In February 2025 HNEC let voters check their registration by text message, sending their national number to 17017. In April 2025 HNEC published the voter lists for municipal elections, with 560,896 voters. In the last twelve months, HNEC's Decision 253 of December 2025 set up registration by text message and in person. It defines updating the register as checking HNEC's databases against changes in the Civil Registry Authority's. No source says the check has been carried out. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

LSO.short: Lesotho's electoral commission ran a modernised registration system with online registration in 2024; no source found says whether voters could check the roll.
LSO.summary: The IEC re-registered voters nationwide from 2024, at its offices and through an online portal. In 2024 it said the register then in use dated from 2001. In the last twelve months, the IEC told an AU mission in July 2026 that more than 579,520 citizens had registered on its modernised system. It said the system is integrated with the National Identity and Civil Registry. In September 2026 it hired a private auditor to examine the roll, its servers and its registration systems. No source since October 2023 says the roll was published or that voters could check it online, by text message or at centres. Operating would need a source showing the roll was published or open to voters to check, online, by text message or at centres.

MAR.short: Voters could check the digital roll in 2026; no source found reports a link to the ID or civil register.
MAR.summary: The Interior Minister said on 13 January 2026 that the ministry audited the electoral lists in its central information system. Of 382,170 new registrants, 254,740 came through the electoral-lists website. In the last twelve months, Order 503-26 of March 2026 let registered voters view their own entries at listeselectorales.ma. In September 2026 the ministry said voters can also check by text message to 2727 or through the MonBV app. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

MDG.short: The 2026 overhaul of the roll is mainly on paper; equipment for a biometric list was received in October 2026.
MDG.summary: Ceni's 2026 overhaul of the roll collects voter data mainly on paper forms, with tablets in a limited number of centres. An electoral agent told L'Express in August 2026 that no digitalisation was planned for it. In the last twelve months, Ceni received USD 750,000 of IT equipment from Japan and UNDP in October 2026 to prepare a biometric list. The government's programme of November 2025 says it will continue digitalising the roll. No source since October 2023 says a digital or biometric roll is in service. Establishing would need a digital or biometric voter register in service.

MLI.short: The voters' roll was drawn from or checked against the ID or civil register in 2026.
MLI.summary: The AIGE trained 54 agents on 26 January 2026 on Elector mobile, the central software for the electoral file. Under the amended electoral law the new list is posted at the commune, embassy or consulate at least seven days before the vote. In the last twelve months, Bamada.net reported in October 2026 that the lists are drawn from the biometric civil-status database, with the NINA as each voter's unique identifier. The 2026 revision opened on 1 October.

MOZ.short: Voters could check the digital roll in 2024; no source found reports a link to the ID or civil register.
MOZ.summary: The Commonwealth Observer Group says the CNE has used biometric voter registration since 2008. It registered 17,169,239 voters for the 2024 elections, and the final register was published from 4 to 9 July 2024. Copies are displayed where registration brigades worked, and voters can scrutinise them and complain in writing. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

Voters could check the register online at electoral.govmu.org, by SMS or phone with their national identity card number, and at the centres. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a digital or biometric voters' roll is under way or in service. Preparing would need a digital or biometric voter register procured or piloted.

Parliament made the national ID card the only proof of identity for voter registration. No source says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Its fingerprint system removed 15,560 duplicate registrations from about 1.4 million voters in 2024. The Namibian reports that the final 2024 voters' roll was published and given to political parties to inspect. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. OIF and ECOWAS experts audited the file in 2020 and judged it reliable. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

In the last twelve months, INEC put the preliminary register on its website on 26 October 2026, where the public could view it and report missing details. About 1.2 million invalid entries were purged, leaving over 103 million voters. INEC's acting chairman said in September 2026 that INEC has integrated National Identification Numbers through its registration portal to audit, verify and clean the register. SERAP says INEC disclosed on 1 November 2026 that its biometric system had flagged 268 records for review.

Voters abroad can check where they are registered on the National Electoral Commission's site, signing in with their ID number and mother's name. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The High Commission in Nigeria said in May 2024 that Rwandans aged 18 or over with a national ID are on the voters' list automatically.

SSD.summary: The National Elections Commission chair said on 2 September 2026 that voter registration will be manual. Biometrics are ruled out. Records are to be typed into computers later, and the original records are to be kept in state offices. In the last twelve months, the chair ruled out biometrics on 2 September 2026. No source found says a digital roll is under way. Preparing would need a digital or biometric voter register procured or piloted.

STP.short: The voters' roll was drawn from or checked against the ID or civil register in 2026.
STP.summary: The roll for the presidential election of 19 July 2026 was compiled automatically from civil registry data. The Universidade de Aveiro built the platform under the EU-funded PReSE project, which links the civil register database with the electoral register database. In the last twelve months, a new electoral registration law took effect after its publication on 26 March 2026. The provisional roll of 146,510 voters was open for consultation from 1 to 8 August 2026. It was open at electoral commissions and online on the CEN website.

SWZ.short: Voters could check the digital roll in 2026; no source found reports a link to the ID or civil register.
SWZ.summary: The EBC sends a preliminary voters' register to the chiefdoms for validation, where registered voters can verify their details. In the last twelve months, the EBC said in October 2026 that over 15,000 people had registered to vote electronically. Registration runs by mobile phone and at registration corners. In September 2026 it said continuous registration uses computers and biometric systems ahead of the 2028 elections. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

SYC.summary: Voters can check their name by sending their NIN by SMS to 9600, on www.ecs.sc or at the nearest registration centre. [The Commission receives a monthly list of the dead from the Department of Immigration and Civil Status](https://ecs.sc/faq/. It removes those names when the register is certified. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Electoral Commission opened an online voter registration system on ecs.sc in July 2025, where voters can check their status, transfer, correct details or object.

A decree of 1 April 2025 opened a revision of the file from 7 to 23 April, in which CENI issued biometric voter cards. ZETES and SNEDAI trained data-entry operators on biometric kits for the revision. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll was published or that voters could check it online, by text message or at centres. From 20 May 2024 the ISIE ran a free SMS service for voters to check their polling centre. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

TZA.short: The voters' roll was drawn from or checked against the ID or civil register in 2025.
TZA.summary: INEC said in March 2025 that its upgraded biometric registration kits integrate with the NIDA database. Online corrections to the register require a NIDA National Identification Number, which verifies the details being corrected. The preliminary register was displayed from May 2025 so citizens could verify, correct or object to entries. No change has been found in the last twelve months. On 23 August 2025 INEC denied any integration with other systems for electoral purposes, which conflicts with its own statements of March 2025.

UGA.short: The voters' roll was drawn from or checked against the ID or civil register in 2025.
UGA.summary: The Daily Monitor reported in October 2025 that the national voter register was compiled from biometric data extracted from NIRA. NIRA is the National Identification and Registration Authority. The Commission says the National Voters Register, covering 21,681,491 voters, was displayed in 2025. It urges the public to verify their details at ec.or.ug/register. In the last twelve months, a December 2025 statutory instrument requires biometric voter verification at every polling station. Kits check each voter against the register at the polls.

ZAF.short: The voters' roll was drawn from or checked against the ID or civil register in 2026.
ZAF.summary: ITWeb reported 29.2 million South Africans on the roll for the 2026 local government elections. The IEC's data-free online registration portal lets voters check their registration status and confirm their voting station, the chief electoral officer said in July 2026. In the last twelve months, [the home affairs minister said in September 2026 that his department and the IEC share an electronic interface](https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2026-09-23-home-affairs-investigating-21-cases-of-identity-theft-and-fraudulent-ids/. It verifies identity details given at registration and at voting, against the National Population Register. He gave the same answer in a written reply to Parliament on 16 September 2026.

ZMB.short: Voters could check the digital roll in 2026; no source found reports a link to the ID or civil register.
ZMB.summary: The ECZ deployed 2,354 biometric voter registration kits nationwide. The EU mission says the register was certified at 8,786,300 on 4 May 2026. In the last twelve months, voters could inspect the provisional register online or by USSD until 8 March 2026. It was also on display at all 12,152 polling stations, and the SADC mission saw it displayed at 73% of polling stations it observed. No source since October 2023 says the roll is drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register. Mature would need the roll drawn from or checked against the national ID, population or civil register.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's biometric voters' roll could be checked online or by text in 2025 and was cleaned against the population database in 2026.
ZWE.summary: A 2025 report says the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission keeps biometric voter databases. In August 2025 it told voters in by-election wards to check their registration online or by a code on NetOne. It said it displays the voters' roll two days before polling. The minister said ZEC already uses the Registrar-General's national population database to clean up the voters' roll and to see who is of voting age. In the last twelve months, voter registration and roll management began passing to the Registrar-General in August 2026. The handover includes the biometric registration kits and network infrastructure.

AGO.short: The ICT ministry's consultation portal took public contributions on draft laws in 2025 and 2026; no source found says whether what was received is published.
AGO.summary: The ICT ministry, MINTTICS, runs a public consultation portal for draft sector documents. In April 2025 the regulator INACOM reported that the ministry's draft cybersecurity laws were open for comment on the same portal and by email. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the portal carried the draft law on artificial intelligence, showing 18 contributions from companies, 18 from specialists and 5 from the general public. In May 2026 the institute IMA put the draft Digital Government Law on the public consultations portal. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

BEN.summary: In April 2025 the Open Government Partnership reported that the BousProB application lets citizens in Benin follow the stages of the budget process and comment on them. The application belongs to an Open Budget Hub run by the budget directorate. The hub opens 13 of the 17 stages of the budget process to civil society. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

It asked the public for written comments by email by 30 January 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. The consultation document was on its website, and replies were taken by email. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, ARTCI published the operators' replies to the consultation on its website. No source found since October 2023 names a consultation portal in service, and none shows one taking comments on more than one draft. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the observatory OBS-CC reported that consultation. No source found since October 2023 says a portal is in service. None says comments were published. None says a rule requires drafts online. Establishing would need a consultation portal or online platform open to the public for more than one draft.

In September 2025 the Minister of Youth launched the National Youth Consultations 2025 with an online form for young people. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft.
