In June 2025 the government put its fiscal transparency portal out to public consultation, from 27 June to 17 July 2025. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the regulator ARME opened a public consultation on a proposed framework for satellite communications. Submissions were open until 31 August 2026. It stayed open until 30 January 2025. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. The page shows how many comments each has received: 2 on one draft and 9 on another. It does not show the comments. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

One was the Broadcasting and Online Content Regulations, 2026. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. No source found since October 2023 says a portal takes comments online on more than one draft. In May 2026 the information ministry posted its draft National Data Governance Policy online for public comment, due by 5 June 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the government published what it was told online. Operating would need published comments, a report or an answer.

LBR.summary: No stage is set. The Liberia Telecommunications Authority published its draft quality of service regulations online in March 2021. On 4 March 2024 it issued a final report on the consultation, setting out the inputs received and its decision on each. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a named draft was posted online for public comment. Preparing would need a named draft posted online for public comment, or an online consultation on one.

No source found says a global content network has a cache at either exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MDG.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
MDG.summary: Internet Society Pulse lists one active IXP in Madagascar, MGIX in Antananarivo, with 4 members as of February 2026. In the last twelve months, the Internet Society said in July 2026 that Madagascar has revived MGIX. Its Foundation's grant record says MGIX, Madagascar's first IXP, had been suspended since 2019. A 2024 grant of USD 49,958 to iRENALA is to restart it. No source found says a global content network has a cache at MGIX or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MLI.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
MLI.summary: The ECOWAS SIGTEL regional inventory, read in 2026, lists one Internet Exchange Point in Mali, Mali IX (MLIX) in Bamako, among 14 in the ECOWAS member states. The inventory gives no member count or traffic. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MOZ.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
MOZ.summary: MOZIX, the Mozambique Internet Exchange in Maputo, says it was created in May 2002 and now has 18 peers. In May 2025 CIUEM's director called MozIX the only internet exchange point in the country. The same month he put its peak traffic at over 150 Gbps, with 19 peering members. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in August 2026 the communications minister called MozIX the national traffic exchange point. No global content network has been found peering there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MRT.short: An exchange point in service by 2025; no global content network is known to serve from it.
MRT.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation officially launched the national internet exchange centre at International Mauritanian Telecommunications on 28 May 2025. A feasibility study of June 2014 stated that Mauritania had no exchange point yet, with Dakar in effect acting as the IXP for its operators. In August 2025 the ministry called the exchange recently launched. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MUS.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
MUS.summary: Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data of May 2026, lists the Mauritius Internet Exchange Point (MIXP) in Ebene with 19 members and 95 Gbps of cumulative port capacity. MIXP's own route-server looking glass showed Route Server 1 (IPv6) last reconfigured on 15 June 2026. Five of the members are registered abroad, in the United States, South Africa and Guadeloupe. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

MWI.short: Global content networks served caches from Malawi's exchange in 2024; no traffic growth over a year is known.
MWI.summary: MISPA says the Malawi Internet Exchange (MIX) in Blantyre began operating on 4 December 2008. In April 2024 MISPA's chair said the MIX provides content caches from Google, Facebook and Akamai. In the last twelve months, the Internet Society said in July 2026 that the Lilongwe Internet Exchange (LLIX) had launched with five peers. A MACRA deck of September 2023 had said Malawi had one exchange, in Blantyre. No source found gives the MIX's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

NAM.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
NAM.summary: In 2026 Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB, listed the Windhoek Internet Exchange Point (IXP Namibia) with 6 member networks and 23 Gbps of cumulative port capacity. One new member joined in the 12 months before. Pulse also lists Paratus Africa, registered in Mauritius, as a member. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

NER.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
NER.summary: Agence Ecofin reports that Niger inaugurated a new Internet Exchange Point in Niamey on 19 August 2025, opened by the Minister of Communication and New Information Technologies. ANP, citing the Smart Villages project (PVI), reports the creation of Niger's first Internet Exchange Point with the operator Niger Telecoms. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

NGA.short: Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok peer at the exchange, its peak traffic rose to 1.7 Tbps in 2025, and it reaches Abuja and Enugu.
NGA.summary: IXPN, founded in 2006, says it serves more than 130 networks from several Lagos data centres, as of October 2026. Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok are among its members, per IT Pulse Nigeria in February 2026. Its aggregate peak traffic rose from 4 Gbps in 2015 to 1.7 Tbps in 2025. In the last twelve months, Digital Realty added an IXPN point of presence at its Ibeju-Lekki data centre in Lagos in April 2026. In October 2026 IXPN reported regional connectivity in Abuja and Enugu, beside its points of presence in Lagos.

RWA.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
RWA.summary: In July 2026 the Internet Society said RINEX, the Rwanda Internet Exchange, has become a central part of Rwanda's digital ecosystem. It expanded its operations through the Society's grant programme. Gewape Cloud Group says on its own LinkedIn account that it is connected and live on RINEX, run by RICTA. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives RINEX's members or says a global content network has a cache there or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

SDN.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
SDN.summary: Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data of August 2026, shows SIXP Sudan (Sudan Internet Exchange Point) with four members at 1 Gbps each. PeeringDB's record, operated by the National Information Center of Sudan in Khartoum, shows 4 peers and 4G total capacity, last updated 2020-01-22. The Center's WSIS Forum 2016 deck lists a National Internet Exchange Point among its services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

SEN.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
SEN.summary: In September 2026 the Internet Society's IXP Tracker listed HubSIX, an exchange point in Dakar, with six member networks, five of them at the route server. They have 260 Gbps of port capacity between them. In the last twelve months, a second exchange opened in Dakar. the African IXP Association lists SENIX, opened in 2017, and HubSIX, opened in 2026. No source found says a global content network serves from either exchange. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

SLE.short: An exchange point in service by 2025, with a global content network serving from it.
SLE.summary: PeeringDB's record for Michcom-IX, an open-access exchange in Freetown run by Michcom Limited, lists 5 peers, 6 connections and 60G total capacity, last updated 2026-06-03. The operator's own site says a Microsoft Connected Cache node caches Microsoft content locally at the exchange. It also says operators across Sierra Leone, Guinea and Liberia exchange traffic there, with points of presence in Conakry and Monrovia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

SOM.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
SOM.summary: Packet Clearing House's directory lists the Somali Internet Exchange Point (SoIXP) in Mogadishu, run by the National Communications Authority Somalia and established 20 November 2018, with status Active. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the exchange's members or gives its traffic. None says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

SSD.short: A 2025 source says no exchange point operates in the country.
SSD.summary: In July 2025 Internet Society Pulse's Internet Resilience Index, from PCH and PeeringDB data, scored South Sudan 0/100 on IXP coverage of population centres. It also scored 0/100 on peering efficiency, the share of networks peering at an IXP. Nothing dated later names an exchange in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

STP.short: A 2026 source says no exchange point operates in the country.
STP.summary: In 2026 the Internet Society Pulse IXP Tracker stated there are no active Internet Exchange Points in Sao Tome and Principe, and none listed in PeeringDB with three or more member ASNs. Nothing dated later names one in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows networks handing each other traffic directly at an exchange point, whoever runs it. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

SWZ.short: An exchange point in service by 2014; no global content network is known to serve from it.
SWZ.summary: The African Union Commission, with Swaziland's Ministry of ICT and the Internet Society, launched the national Internet Exchange Point in Mbabane on 10 April 2014 under the AXIS project. The Commission says it donated equipment and services for it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the exchange's members or gives its traffic. None says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

SYC.short: An exchange point in service by 2015; no global content network is known to serve from it.
SYC.summary: The African Union Commission says the Internet Exchange Point in Seychelles was launched on 20 February 2015, with the Vice President and ICT Minister officiating. The Commission lists Seychelles among eight Member States that have set up IXPs with its AXIS support. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the exchange's members or gives its traffic, and none says a global content network has a cache there or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

TCD.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
TCD.summary: In March 2024 the Internet Society said Chad had one exchange point, run by ADETIC, with at least nine networks peering there. In August 2024 it said no content delivery network had caches in Chad. In the last twelve months, Digital Business Africa said in May 2026 that TCHADIX, run by ADETIC, had operated for a year. Russell Southwood reported in November 2026 that DJAMIX, the N'Djamena exchange, had nine members, down from 11 in 2024. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

TGO.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
TGO.summary: In 2026 ISOC Pulse, from self-reported PeeringDB data, listed the Togo Internet Exchange Point (TGIX) in Lomé with 9 member ASNs and 18 Gbps of cumulative port capacity. One ASN joined and none left in the 12 months before. Pulse lists members registered outside Togo, including PCH and GVA of Côte d'Ivoire. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

TUN.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
TUN.summary: Inflect, a colocation marketplace, states in September 2025 that TunIXP is Tunisia's primary national exchange point, keeping local traffic in the country. ATI (Tunisie Internet) states on its institutional page that it operates and manages Tunisia's national internet exchange point, TUNIXP. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the exchange's members or gives its traffic, and none says a global content network has a cache there or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

TZA.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
TZA.summary: On the exchange's own statistics, TIX average traffic rose from about 110 Gbps in September 2025 to about 205 Gbps in late September 2026, an increase of more than 80% in a year. The same report says TIX in Dar es Salaam, run by TISPA, connects 66 networks. That rise is the change found in the last twelve months. TISPA manages six IXPs: TIX plus Arusha, Dodoma, Mbeya, Mwanza and Zanzibar. No source found says a global content network has a cache at TIX or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

UGA.short: An exchange point in service by 2024, with a global content network serving from it.
UGA.summary: UIXP deployed a Netflix cache in 2024, reachable by connected networks through its route servers, with cache-fill donated by Lyca Mobile. UIXP says it began and ended 2024 with 32 connected networks, six of them at the Raxio data centre. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Internet Society Pulse records that UIXP was exempted from the January 2026 election shutdown order as critical infrastructure. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

ZAF.short: An exchange point in service by 2026, with a global content network, traffic growing and reach beyond one city.
ZAF.summary: In November 2025 Teraco said 680 networks peer at NAPAfrica, among them Akamai, Cloudflare, Google, Meta, Netflix and TikTok. Teraco gives its traffic peak as over 4 Tbps in 2023 and 5 Tbps in February 2025. It says NAPAfrica runs exchange points in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban. Its members come from over 50 countries. In the last twelve months, NAPAfrica reached 6 Tbps in November 2025, and over 7 Tbps with more than 690 networks in November 2026.

ZMB.short: An exchange point in service by 2026; no global content network is known to serve from it.
ZMB.summary: In August 2024 PeeringDB listed 12 peers at the Lusaka IXP, with 76 Gbps of capacity. In the last twelve months, AFRINIC said in December 2025 that its name servers at the exchange had gone live. In August 2026 the Lusaka IXP gave its peak traffic as 2.8 Tbps, with more than 14 networks connected. The African IXP Association lists two exchanges in Lusaka: ZIXP, opened in 2006, and the Lusaka IXP, opened in 2022. No source found says a global content network serves from either. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

ZWE.short: An exchange point in service by 2020; no global content network is known to serve from it.
ZWE.summary: In 2020 POTRAZ said the Harare Internet Exchange Point (HIX) is operating, and that all internet access providers are connected to it. It is housed at the TelOne Exchange and was set up with a USD 200,000 African Union grant. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

AGO.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
AGO.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

BDI.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

BEN.short: The telecoms regulator's complaints channels handled about a hundred cases in 2025; no source found says whether a channel reaches across government.
BEN.summary: La Marina reported in June 2026 that the telecoms regulator ARCEP handled about a hundred formal consumer complaints in 2025. They came by green line, counter, email and social networks. Benin's Treasury (DGTCP) says its Centre d'Ecoute Clients has been in a pilot phase since July 2024. In the last twelve months, ARCEP was preparing to link its channels to one automated back-office, by the paper's account. No source found since October 2023 says a complaints channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about most ministries or local governments, or routes them across government.

BFA.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
BFA.summary: In February 2026 the Commission de Régulation des Dysfonctionnements launched DenonciationPro, an online platform for reporting dysfunctions in public administration. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Health launched Lafiako in November 2026, a platform for complaints and suggestions about health facilities, with a ten-day target for handling them. In March 2019 the public-service ministry had launched a complaints system with an online form. No source found since October 2023 says whether one is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

BWA.short: The government told a 2025 World Bank survey it runs a feedback platform for service delivery; no source found reports its case numbers and results.
BWA.summary: Mmegi reported that Parliament launched BW Speaks on 28 July 2022, an online platform for citizens to voice issues to MPs and be responded to. The government told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025 that it has a platform for citizens to give feedback on service delivery, at botswanaspeaks.gov.bw. The survey record gives no launch date or case count. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints or cases handled. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

CAF.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

CIV.short: Work to put the national survey of public service quality online began in 2026; no channel in service with cases on record is known.
CIV.summary: In November 2026 the Ministry of Digital Transition sought a firm to digitalise the National Barometer of Public Service Quality, under a World Bank project. The plan is to collect ratings of public services by web forms, offline tablets, phone surveys, USSD and SMS. In the last twelve months, that tender followed a 2024-2025 round of the barometer that was run largely by hand. The Miliê citizen portal, launched in February 2019, was built to collect and handle users' concerns. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

CMR.short: An online complaints platform for two regions was being prepared in 2024; no count of complaints received is known.
CMR.summary: In December 2024 the Public Independent Conciliator for the North-West and South-West trained its staff on an online complaints platform. The office was about to launch the platform, built on SharePoint. In June 2022 the public service ministry said it handled users' concerns by phone and WhatsApp on the green number 1522. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No case count has been found for any digital complaints channel. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

COD.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
COD.summary: In May 2026 the Ministry of National Economy launched the 'Loba' chatbot for consumer complaints in regulated sectors, including public health and electricity. Its competition commission, COMCO, runs the chatbot, which is piloted in Kinshasa first. In the last twelve months, that launch was followed by the electricity regulator's presentation of an online complaints platform on 5 October 2026. Consumers and operators can file complaints on it and follow them. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

COG.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COG.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

COM.short: A food programme's grievance mechanism was being set up in 2026; no channel for complaints about public services is known, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Comoros. The only item found is the Grievance Redress Mechanism of the Food Systems Resilience Programme, a mechanism of a World Bank food programme and not a channel for public services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with or complain about public services.

CPV.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2024; no source found reports one in service with cases on record.
CPV.summary: In May 2024 the minister said the E-participa platform takes citizens' complaints, reports and suggestions on public services. She gave no count of cases. Since January 2021 the Ombudsman has also taken complaints through eparticipa.gov.cv. In the last twelve months, on 3 November 2026 the labour inspectorate launched a portal where workers and employers file labour complaints online. No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints received through E-participa. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

DJI.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
DJI.summary: ARULoS, Djibouti's agency for urban rehabilitation and social housing, runs an online complaints platform, E-DOLÉANCES. People with a complaint about the agency's housing file it there online. The platform sends problems with the recovery of payments to the agency's DOCR division and technical problems to its DLS directorate. The platform's page gives no date and no number of complaints. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

DZA.short: The national mediator's complaints portal reached all administrations and published its share of cases closed in 2024; no source found reports later figures.
DZA.summary: The Mediator of the Republic's online grievance-register portal had received 52,262 grievances by 22 April 2024, counted from October 2023. The Mediator's office said 40,145 of them had been handled and closed, or 76.81 per cent. Its digitisation director said the portal serves all administrations and public establishments. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of Youth launched the Sawtoukoum platform in April 2026. On 26 October 2026 the Ministry of Internal Trade opened the Tawassol portal, where consumers report overcharging and hygiene breaches. No resolution figures newer than April 2024 have been found.

EGY.short: Results of the national complaints channel were published in 2025.
EGY.summary: The Cabinet said its Unified Government Complaints System handled 1.46 million items in 2023, 15% more than in 2022. The monthly report to the Prime Minister gives complaints resolved per ministry and body. In the last twelve months, the monthly count was 195,000 items in September 2025 and 206,000 in May 2026, per the State Information Service. The system takes them by the 16528 hotline, a portal, the Fi Khedmetak app and WhatsApp. In May 2026 it referred 172,000 of the 206,000 submissions to the competent authorities.

ERI.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

ETH.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
ETH.summary: In October 2026 the Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman's home page offered a Submit Complaint service. Citizens can file administrative grievances online. In the last twelve months, Ethiopian Investment Holdings launched Adera, an online platform, in January 2026. Citizens report complaints and corruption on it at the state-owned enterprises it manages. In 2025 the government told the World Bank's GovTech survey it has a platform for feedback on service delivery. It named ecompliant.gov.et. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

GAB.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2023; one in service is not on record.
GAB.summary: In November 2023 the DGDI, Gabon's directorate for documentation and immigration, opened an online complaints space, the Espace Réclamation, on its new portal. Users of its services can file a complaint there and follow it online. In the last twelve months, on 29 October 2026 the police inspectorate signed an agreement with Group IDENTITY to pilot the Identitysecu app for complaints about police officers. The pilot is to run for six to twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

GHA.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
GHA.summary: On 16 March 2026 the Minister for Transport launched the Passenger Complaints Portal at the Ghana Civil Aviation Authority. Air passengers report and track complaints on the web or by QR codes in the terminal. In November 2024 the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolitan Assembly launched Twin-City Connect, which takes citizens' complaints. In the last twelve months, the passenger portal is the one new channel found. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

GIN.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GIN.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

GMB.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
GMB.summary: In February 2015 the Office of the Ombudsman launched a website that let citizens file a complaint online for the first time. In the last twelve months, NAWEC, the national water and electricity company, launched a mobile app in April 2026. Customers can lodge complaints and report faults on it in real time, with photos. No source found since October 2023 gives resolution rates, response times or a number of cases received. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

GNB.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

GNQ.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Equatorial Guinea, whether under way or in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a government body is preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with public services. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing such a portal, app or messaging service.

KEN.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2023; one in service is not on record.
KEN.summary: In November 2023 the Commission on Administrative Justice was developing an app, the PASHA Ombudsman platform, for complaints about public services, with the Ministry of Public Service. In May 2022 the Commission launched the public portal of its complaints system, and its chair said complaints could be lodged against any public entity. Makueni County launched a project-tracking dashboard in March 2024 with a feedback tool for residents. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

LBR.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
LBR.summary: In May 2023 IDAD, with UNDP funding, began a ten-county rollout of the Citizens Feedback Mechanism. It is a national SMS and web platform for reporting on public services. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the Cabinet Director General said citizens would give feedback on government performance by SMS. Cabinet Director Nathaniel Kawbo announced President Boakai's 'Citizens Feedback' platform. It takes reports on officials and stalled projects by SMS to shortcode 2424. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

LBY.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
LBY.summary: The Citizen Service Centre received over 4,000 requests and complaints on its first day, 12 October 2021. It referred each complaint to the delegate of the ministry concerned. In the last twelve months, the economy ministry launched a platform for enquiries and complaints about obstacles to trade in November 2026. On 31 August 2026 the health ministry put a link on its website for complaints, comments and reports. On 7 April 2026 the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock launched a platform for complaints and inquiries from farmers and citizens. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

LSO.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2024; one in service is not on record.
LSO.summary: In August 2024 the Ministry of Communications said the National Contact Centre takes complaints by telephone and email. Its agents pass each one to the public relations officer of the ministry concerned, who must report back within three days. The ministry said the centre was still being established. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The ministry's account gives no number of complaints taken or answered. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

MAR.short: Results of the national complaints channel were published in 2025.
MAR.summary: Statistics on Chikaya.ma show over 1,677,000 complaints filed since its launch in January 2018. The portal gives access to 38 government departments, 116 public institutions and 1,590 local authorities. Minister Seghrouchni told parliament it recorded about 176,000 complaints in 2024. In the last twelve months, Morocco World News reported that citizens filed 163,694 complaints through it in 2025. It says Chikaya.ma processed 66.14% of them, with an average processing time of 16 days.

MDG.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2024; one in service is not on record.
MDG.summary: On 26 February 2024 Madagascar's Ministry of Justice launched a complaints website, Fitsarana valio ny tarainako, for users of justice and prison services. A complaint costs 500 ariary and is filed after registration with the national identification number. The site takes complaints about the courts and prisons and about nothing else. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The report of the launch gives no number of complaints filed. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

MLI.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MLI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

MOZ.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
MOZ.summary: In June 2026 AURAS, Mozambique's regulator of water and sanitation services, presented a new digital complaints platform, RECO. Any citizen can use it to submit a complaint or an appeal online about the regulated water and sanitation services. In the last twelve months, RECO is the one new channel found, and it covers that one sector. The regulator's presentation gives no number of complaints received or settled. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

MRT.short: Mauritania's complaints app recorded about 9,000 requests and complaints by May 2025; no source found says whether it reaches across government.
MRT.summary: In May 2025 the Minister of Digital Transformation said the Ain app had recorded about 9,000 requests and complaints on access to basic services. Ain was launched in October 2024, and the minister said 96% of the requests and complaints had been processed. That month the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree on the Khadamati portal, which is to take citizens' grievances, reports and complaints. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the ministries whose services Ain covers. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about the services of most ministries or of local governments, or routes them across government.

MUS.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; no source found reports one in service with cases on record.
MUS.summary: In May 2026 the ICT minister told parliament that the Korek app takes online complaints about water leaks. The app was launched on 30 January 2026. The Citizen Support Unit has run an online complaints portal at csu.mu since April 2017. In the last twelve months, Korek is the one new channel found, and no count of complaints made through it has been found. The Prime Minister's figures for the unit date from 2020. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

MWI.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2025; one in service is not on record.
MWI.summary: On 4 June 2025 Malawi's Independent Complaints Commission launched an Online Citizen Engagement Platform, with UNDP support. Citizens can use it to file complaints about police misconduct, follow their case and receive updates. No change has been found in the last twelve months. UNDP's account of the launch gives no number of complaints filed or resolved. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

NAM.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2025; one in service is not on record.
NAM.summary: In November 2025 Walvis Bay Municipality launched Ovakalimo, an online platform for reporting problems with municipal services. A resident sends a report with a photo, and the platform passes it to the department responsible. In July 2024 the City of Windhoek launched a mobile app for residents to report potholes and broken traffic lights. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The municipality's spokesperson gave no number of reports. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

NER.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Niger, whether under way or in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a government body is preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with public services. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing such a portal, app or messaging service.

NGA.short: A national complaints website published cases resolved per federal agency in 2024; no source found reports resolution figures for the newer national platform.
NGA.summary: ReportGov.ng, described as the official public service complaint website, logged complaints against federal agencies in November 2024. Its report for that month gives the complaints received and resolved for each agency. In August 2024 it was described as taking complaints about any federal agency, with 53 ranked. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 SERVICOM Presidency launched the Nigeria Electronic Grievance Management platform, which it says tracks complaints across all tiers of government. No resolution figures for ReportGov.ng newer than November 2024 have been found, and none for the SERVICOM platform.

RWA.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
RWA.summary: The Ministry of Local Government states that the revised Citizens' Assembly guidelines have assembly reports supported by the electronic software e-Citizen Complaints, which receives and solves citizens' complaints online. In the last twelve months, the ministry began designing the Mbaza AI agent for complaints in October 2025, aiming to deploy it in early 2026. In November 2026 the Rwanda AI Agency sought firms to pilot AI agents on Mbaza. No source found since October 2023 gives a number of complaints received or solved. Establishing would need a channel in service with a number of complaints or cases on record.

SDN.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2025; one in service is not on record.
SDN.summary: In August 2025 a committee of the Khartoum State government met telecom companies to allocate unified WhatsApp numbers for citizens' complaints. It proposed adding a call centre beside them, and the companies said they were ready to supply the numbers. No channel was yet running when the committee met them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

SEN.short: A complaints mechanism for oil and gas operations opened in 2026; no channel for complaints about public services is known, so no stage is set.
SEN.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Senegal. The nearest item is the Mécanisme de Gestion des Plaintes for the oil and gas sector, a mechanism for complaints about extractive operations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service through which people report problems with or complain about public services.

SLE.short: A messaging service for complaints about electricity was launched in 2026; no source found reports one in service with cases on record.
SLE.summary: In April 2026 the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation, the electricity distributor EDSA and the Ministry of Energy launched a WhatsApp chatbot. Citizens use it to report electricity faults, and each report gets a ticket number for tracking. It replaced paper complaint forms. In the last twelve months, this launch is the one new channel found, and it takes reports on electricity supply alone. The launch post gives no number of reports. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

SOM.short: Complaints channels are on record only for World Bank projects, in 2024 and 2026; none for public services is known, so no stage is set.
SOM.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in Somalia. The nearest items are the EA-RDIP Grievance Redress Mechanism and a Citizen Engagement and Grievance Redress Mechanism platform, both for World Bank projects. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service for complaints about public services.

SSD.short: Nothing found since 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 names a digital channel for complaints about public services in South Sudan, whether under way or in service. The one item found is the South Sudan Safety Net Project grievance mechanism, a World Bank project mechanism dated before the last twelve months. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government body to have launched, piloted or be preparing a web portal, app or messaging service for complaints about public services.

STP.short: Nothing found names a digital channel for complaints about public services or says there is none, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether people can complain about public services online.

SWZ.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
SWZ.summary: On 21 September 2026 the National Road Transport Council announced BIKA, a platform for reporting problems on public and freight transport. The public can report corruption and abuse there, anonymously if they choose, and track each report by a reference number. In the last twelve months, BIKA is the one new channel found, and it covers transport only. In June 2020 the Ministry of Health and UNICEF launched a feedback mechanism for health clients. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

SYC.short: The revenue authority opened complaints lines by email and messaging in 2025; no source found reports one in service with cases on record.
SYC.summary: On 18 February 2025 the Seychelles Revenue Commission opened a complaints email address and hotline. Taxpayers use it to comment on the service they received from its officers, and at weekends they can send feedback by WhatsApp on the same number. In April 2023 the finance ministry set up an online feedback form for itself and its agencies. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Commission's announcement gives no number of complaints. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

TCD.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2024; one in service is not on record.
TCD.summary: In June 2024 Chad's Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, with UNDP, was preparing an online platform for filing complaints and requests. Its committee for mapping the procedures met for the first time on 6 June 2024. Nothing had yet been built, and no date was given for the platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a channel reaches most ministries or local governments. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

TGO.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2026; one in service is not on record.
TGO.summary: On 27 March 2026 the national health insurance institute INAM announced an online platform, plaintes.inam.tg, where insured people and partners file and track complaints. It sits beside counters and a toll-free line, 8220. In the last twelve months, that launch followed the Ministry of Security's online platform of January 2025 for citizens to report abuses by security forces. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

TUN.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2025; one in service is not on record.
TUN.summary: In July 2025 the Presidency of the Government launched the online platform e-Mouaten, where citizens report obstacles met with the administration and follow their requests. The Médiateur Administratif takes petitions through its website, a mobile app and its social network, and 95 came in through those electronic channels in 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says whether a channel is in service with cases on record. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints or cases on record.

TZA.short: A national complaints channel covered services across government in 2024; its results are not published.
TZA.summary: The e-Government Authority's e-Mrejesho system works by USSD, mobile app and website, and citizens send feedback, complaints or compliments to government institutions. In December 2022 e-GA's director general said all government institutions were connected to it. It passes a misdirected complaint to the right institution and allows appeal to a higher level. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives resolution rates, response times or a report of the cases handled. Mature would need the share of complaints resolved, response times, or a report of the cases and what was done about them published.

UGA.short: The Auditor General's feedback platform had cases resolved on record in 2025; no source found says whether a channel reaches across government.
UGA.summary: GIZ said in 2025 that the Citizen Feedback Platform lets Ugandans report concerns about service delivery to the Office of the Auditor General. Since 2022, 2,300 citizens had registered on it and on two other apps, and some 900 cases reported through the three had been resolved. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a national channel takes complaints about most ministries or local governments. Operating would need a national channel that takes complaints about the services of most ministries or of local governments, or routes them across government.

ZAF.short: Results of the national complaints channel were published in 2024.
ZAF.summary: In January 2025 DPME said the Presidential Hotline had received 339,579 cases since September 2009. It said it assigns complaints through its case system to departments and municipalities. The Minister said 991 of the 1,832 complaints of April to June 2025 were resolved. That is a rate of 55 per cent. In the last twelve months, the Information Regulator took POPIA complaints online from October 2025 and PAIA complaints from January 2026.

ZMB.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2024; one in service is not on record.
ZMB.summary: In July 2024 SMART Zambia, the government's digital agency, said it had developed the Citizens Support Services Portal. It takes complaints through the portal, SMS, WhatsApp, a mobile app and a chatbot, and gives each a tracking number. The date of its official launch was still to be announced. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The announcement gives no number of complaints. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

ZWE.short: A digital channel for complaints about public services was under way in 2025; one in service is not on record.
ZWE.summary: In July 2025 Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care launched a Digital Grievance Redress Mechanism, covering the health services it runs. Patients can rate services, write feedback, use mobile apps or go to public feedback booths. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the Ministry of Public Service presented progress on a proposed Grievance Redress Feedback Mechanism in Stockholm. In August 2026 the City of Bulawayo launched a digital Citizen Engagement Scorecard. Establishing would need a digital channel in service, with a number of complaints, reports or cases it has received or handled on record.

AGO.short: Backbone fibre reached every province or region by 2023; no source found says whether other operators buy capacity on it.
AGO.summary: In May 2023 the ministry's director of telecommunications said Angola's terrestrial fibre exceeds 22,000 km and connects all provincial and communal capitals. In the last twelve months, the first link of a new national broadband backbone, from Luanda to Benguela, opened at Lobito in September 2026. It is meant to reach all 21 provinces. In November 2026 the minister said the national broadband network is still being extended across the country. No source found says other operators buy capacity on the backbone, or that it runs on open-access or wholesale terms. Mature would need other operators to buy capacity on it, or it to run on open-access or wholesale terms.

BDI.short: Backbone fibre reached every province or region by 2024; no source found says whether other operators buy capacity on it.
BDI.summary: ARCT states BBS's fibre (1,750 km) covers all provinces of Burundi and that the national territory is now covered by fibre optic, as at 31 December 2024. BBS is the Burundi Backbone System, listed in the regulator's 2024 indicators report as a fibre infrastructure operator. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says other operators buy capacity on this fibre, or that it runs on open-access or wholesale terms. Mature would need other operators to buy capacity on it, or it to run on open-access or wholesale terms.

BEN.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to the north by 2018; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
BEN.summary: Benin Telecom signed a contract with Huawei in 2014 for rehabilitating a 1,060 km fibre backbone from Cotonou to Malanville. Implementation began in December 2016, and the deal record gives the project as completed, with 2018 as its end year. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing found dates new backbone works since 2018. No source found says the backbone reaches every department, or that other operators buy capacity on it. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

BFA.short: Backbone fibre reached every province or region by 2025, and other operators buy capacity on it.
BFA.summary: SMART Burkina, about 800 km of fibre linking 22 cities, was completed in August 2025. Its operator says the network has run commercially since March 2023 and covers almost the whole territory. In the last twelve months, Bridge Fiber Solutions, which runs the state backbone, sold capacity on it to 44 customers in August 2026. It had 7 in 2023. They include all three mobile operators, internet providers, state firms and banks. Its prices follow a catalogue that ARCEP and the ministry validate each year.

BWA.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
BWA.summary: In May 2025 BoFiNet's acting chief executive said it had laid about 12,400 km of fibre. In the last twelve months, the communications minister said in March 2026 that about 16,000 km of fibre is laid across Botswana. It links the country to South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia. BoFiNet reported 99.7% availability across its backbone at its August 2026 annual meeting. No source found says the backbone reaches every district. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

CAF.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2025; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
CAF.summary: AfDB says that at project close in September 2023 the first national optical backbone was installed. It had 900 km of fibre, eleven technical sites, a network operations centre in Bangui and two community digital centres, and links the country to Cameroon and Congo. The Minister and Africa24 state 1,200 km of fibre optic is in place in CAR. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region. Operating would need a source that states it does.

CIV.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
CIV.summary: In June 2026 ANSUT's infrastructure director said its national broadband network has more than 6,600 km of fibre. ANSUT is the universal service agency. In the last twelve months the length laid rose from the 5,207 km of a planned 6,632 km that ANSUT reported in April 2025. In April 2025 it said the network carries traffic for Orange CI, MTN CI and Moov Africa CI, and for internet providers. No source found says the backbone reaches every region. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

CMR.short: Backbone fibre reached every region by 2024, and other operators buy capacity on it.
CMR.summary: The telecoms regulator ART reported that in 2024 Camtel's national fibre backbone served all ten regional capitals. It also reached 51 of 58 divisional capitals. Camtel makes dark fibre available to MTN Cameroon under a contract, Digital Business Africa reported in December 2024. In the last twelve months, NewsWatch put Camtel's backbone at over 15,000 km in July 2026, against nearly 12,000 km in ART's 2024 figures. In November 2026 ART said its audit of the 112 sections of Camtel's network found serious degradation, with repeated cuts and some sections out of service.

COD.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
COD.summary: The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications told the Council of Ministers that 7,000 km of fibre is currently deployed. It adds 11,500 km more under the Digital Transformation Project. Minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba said about 12,000 km of a planned 55,000 km national fibre backbone was completed; it mainly links major urban hubs. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says it reaches every province. Operating would need a source stating the backbone reaches every province.

COG.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2024; no source found says whether it reaches every department.
COG.summary: In August 2024 the French Treasury said the national coverage project had laid about 3,000 km of fibre. It links Pointe-Noire, Dolisie, Brazzaville, Oyo and Ouesso, and Congo Telecom operates it. In the last twelve months, Xalam Analytics described the project as still under way in January 2026, at about 3,000 km connecting key towns. No source found says the backbone reaches every department, or that other operators buy capacity on it. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

COM.short: Nothing found says a national fibre backbone is being built or in service, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national fibre backbone, or says there is none.

CPV.short: Nothing found says a national fibre backbone is being built or in service, so no stage is set.
CPV.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national fibre backbone, or says there is none.

DJI.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2025; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
DJI.summary: The Ministry of Communication (MCPT) says DFN has deployed over 200 km of fibre in Djibouti-ville and the interior regions. The fibre connects hospitals, schools and public bodies. MCPT says the World Bank-financed DFN and EARDIP projects are deploying fibre optic networks in Djibouti-ville, Balbala and the five interior regions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region. Operating would need a source that states that it does.

DZA.short: Backbone fibre reached every province by 2026, and other operators buy capacity on it.
DZA.summary: In the last twelve months, Algérie Télécom's chief executive said in 2026 that the group had finished nearly 300,000 km of backbone fibre. It covers every wilaya. Earlier, Algérie360 had reported in April 2025 a network of 260,000 km. It covered 95 per cent of the territory. In November 2024 the company told an ITU meeting that more than 40,000 km of its fibre was available to other operators. In October 2026 L'Echo d'Algérie reported the same length of cable laid across all wilayas.

EGY.short: Telecom Egypt sold transmission capacity to other operators in 2025; no source found says where its backbone runs, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: No stage is set. Telecom Egypt says it sells transmission and wholesale services to all the other operators. In February 2025 it extended its transmission agreement with Orange Egypt to 2032. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says where its backbone runs, or that it links Cairo to other regions. Establishing would need backbone fibre in service between the capital and at least one other region, whoever owns it.

ERI.short: Nothing found says a national fibre backbone is being built or in service, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national fibre backbone, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
ETH.summary: Ethio telecom says that in its reporting period it deployed 793 km of new backbone fibre, bringing its national backbone network to 23,442.1 km (regions served not listed). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region, or that other operators buy capacity on it. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

GAB.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
GAB.summary: In October 2026 the head of SPIN, the state infrastructure holding, said its backbone runs about 2,000 km. It follows the railway from Libreville to Franceville and reaches Makokou and Cameroon. Two of the nine provinces are not yet connected. In the last twelve months, on 14 September 2026 SPIN signed a 20-year partnership with Gabon Fiber, which takes over the existing 1,782 km. A 196 km section to Mouila was commissioned on 6 October 2026. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

GHA.short: Nothing found says a national fibre backbone is being built or in service, so no stage is set.
GHA.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national fibre backbone, or says there is none.

GIN.short: Backbone fibre reached every province or region by 2025; no source found says whether other operators buy capacity on it.
GIN.summary: WeAreTech Africa reports the minister's 2025 sector review as saying nearly 12,000 km of fibre optic was deployed to connect all administrative regions. In the last twelve months, on 20 May 2026 SOGEB, the national backbone operator, announced an upgrade to the first loop of the national fibre-optic backbone. It raised the loop from 200 to 400 Gb/s. It had raised it from 50 to 200 Gb/s in December 2024. No source found says other operators buy capacity on it. Mature would need them to buy capacity, or open-access terms.

GMB.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2019; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
GMB.summary: WBBA states GAMTEL's National Broadband Network was deployed in 2019, with 420 km of fibre-optic links and around 31 central office sites. It extends the 2015 ECOWAN backbone and 947 km of legacy fibre in four rings. WBBA calls it a national backbone serving all key areas of the country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

GNB.short: A 2025 source says the country has no national fibre backbone.
GNB.summary: Agence Ecofin reported in August 2025 that Guinea-Bissau's international connectivity is confined to the coast. It said the country still needs a national backbone to link its main cities. Nothing dated later says one is being built or is in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No plan, study, tender or money promised counts. Preparing would need a national fibre backbone under contract, or works begun, in the past three years.

GNQ.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2025; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
GNQ.summary: Gabon's state infrastructure holder SPIN reports that on 10 November 2025 the Gabonese and Equatorial Guinean ministers inaugurated the interconnection of the two national fibre backbones. Tests confirmed stable traffic exchange between Bitam and Ebebeyin and between Libreville and Bata. The document names no regions or length for the Equatorial Guinean network. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

KEN.short: Backbone fibre reached every province or region by 2017; no source found says whether other operators buy capacity on it.
KEN.summary: The Ministry of ICT says phase 2 connected the remaining 18 counties and 3 towns in 2017, giving all 47 counties a connection. ODI wrote in 2025 that phase 2 was still incomplete. It names no county without fibre. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the ICT Authority opened a tender for national backbone links, and in October 2026 the ICT principal secretary said a 17,000 km project to link all public institutions is under way. No source found says other operators buy capacity on the government backbone. Mature would need that, or open-access or wholesale terms.

LBR.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2026; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
LBR.summary: CSquared, USAID and Digital Invest committed to building a 350 km backbone crossing 13+ towns in Margibi, Bong and Nimba counties. It connects Monrovia to the Ivory Coast and Guinea borders, and CSquared describes it as Liberia's first open-access fibre backbone. LTA Chairman Massaquoi says the fibre line had already reached Loguatuo from Monrovia, and gives no length or date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

LBY.short: Nothing found says a national fibre backbone is being built or in service, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national fibre backbone, or says there is none.

LSO.short: A national fibre backbone was being built in 2025; none is known to be in service.
LSO.summary: The Minister of Finance told Parliament that optical fibre deployment is being implemented, with a 96km stretch from Roma to Thaba-Tseka underway. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says any of it is in service between the capital and another region. Establishing would need backbone fibre in service between the capital and one other region.

MAR.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2025; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
MAR.summary: Inwi says its network has a long-distance, high-speed backbone extending across the nation, with more than 9,000 km of own and leased fibre. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the backbone reaches every province or region, or that other operators buy capacity on it. Operating would need a source that states the backbone reaches every province or region.

MDG.short: Backbone fibre linked the capital to other regions by 2025; no source found says whether it reaches every region.
MDG.summary: Orange Madagascar's Antananarivo-Toamasina fibre link was put in place in 2024, with works launched in August 2024. In the last twelve months, Orange Madagascar inaugurated on 1 December 2025 a 558 km fibre link from the capital Antananarivo to Mahajanga, which it calls a national backbone. TZA.summary: Firms in Tanzania reported 0.74 outages in a typical month in the World Bank's Enterprise Survey for 2023. Earlier surveys put the count at 9.36 in 2013, so it has fallen by 8.6 a month since. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Of the 48 countries with a figure for 2023 or later, 4 have fewer outages a month than Tanzania. No regulator's or utility's interruption figure for 2023 or later has been found.

UGA.short: In 2025 the power went off 3.94 times a month, as reported by firms surveyed by the World Bank.
UGA.summary: Firms in Uganda reported 3.94 outages in a typical month in the World Bank's Enterprise Survey for 2025. Earlier surveys put the count at 6.37 in 2013, so it has fallen by 2.4 a month since. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 2 or fewer outages a month has been found, and no regulator's or utility's interruption figure for 2023 or later. Operating would need two outages a month or fewer.

ZAF.short: No count of power outages for 2023 or later has been found, so no stage is set.
ZAF.summary: No stage is set. Firms in South Africa reported 7.66 power outages in a typical month in the World Bank's 2020 Enterprise Survey. That is older than 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for 2023 or later has been found for how often the power goes off. Preparing would need a count for 2023 or later of ten outages a month or fewer.

ZMB.short: In 2025 the power went off 21.42 times a month, as reported by firms surveyed by the World Bank.
ZMB.summary: Firms in Zambia reported 21.42 outages in a typical month in the World Bank's Enterprise Survey for 2025. Earlier surveys put the count at 4.62 in 2013 and 12.72 in 2019. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 10 or fewer outages a month has been found, and no regulator's or utility's interruption figure for 2023 or later. Preparing would need ten outages a month or fewer in a count for 2023 or later.

ZWE.short: In 2025 the power went off 3.88 times a month, as reported by firms surveyed by the World Bank.
ZWE.summary: Firms in Zimbabwe reported 3.88 outages in a typical month in the World Bank's Enterprise Survey for 2025. Earlier surveys put the count at 4.59 in 2016, so it has fallen by 0.7 a month since. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 2 or fewer outages a month has been found, and no regulator's or utility's interruption figure for 2023 or later. Operating would need two outages a month or fewer.

AGO.short: Clinics report on paper, and municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2025).
AGO.summary: GEPE, the health ministry's Office of Studies, Planning and Statistics, oversees the health information system and has been moving it onto DHIS2 since 2015, a June 2025 article states. Health facilities report on paper. Municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into DHIS2. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, a WHO Angola and HISP UiO mission assessed the platform. The ministry and its partners agreed to build dashboards for decision-makers and train staff at all levels. No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

BDI.short: Health centres enter their own reports into the national reporting system (2023), but no figure shows how many of them do.
BDI.summary: Burundi's health ministry collected its 2023 data through the national DHIS2 platform from health centres, district hospitals and national hospitals. Its yearbook of July 2024 states this. The World Bank reported in March 2023 that the entry into DHIS2 is made at the facility. In the last twelve months, a memorandum of 6 February 2026 with the United States provided support for linking DHIS2 with SIDAinfo and other systems, to 31 December 2030. No share or count of health centres keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

BEN.short: Health zone offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system in 2022; how many clinics enter their own is not published.
BEN.summary: Benin's health ministry adopted DHIS2 from 2014, its 2022 statistical yearbook says. In 2022 a facility in every zone sanitaire sent its paper report to the zone before the 5th of each month, and the zone keyed it into DHIS2. No dated event has been found in the last twelve months. No number or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found, and no tier below the health centre is named. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

BFA.short: Clinics and hospitals reported into the national system in 2024, entered at district or facility; the share of clinics entering their own is not published.
BFA.summary: The Ministry of Health's Direction générale des études et des statistiques sectorielles coordinates the national health information system, its manual of July 2023 sets. In 2024 health facilities sent their monthly reports to the district, where data managers keyed them into Endos-BF. In districts with decentralised entry, the heads of health facilities entered their own monthly activity reports. In the last twelve months, Enabel reported training at Dédougou and Tenkodogo in July 2026. The training included quality control of DHIS2 data. No number or share of primary clinics keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

BWA.short: All public health facilities reported into the national system in 2016-18; they report on paper (2025), and it is unclear where the figures are entered.
BWA.summary: WHO's country office report for 2024-2025 describes DHIS2 as the Government's selected "gold standard" platform for aggregate data. The same report lists facilities' heavy reliance on paper-based reporting as a challenge. MEASURE Evaluation gives 100% of public health facilities as reporting through DHIS2 for 2016 to 2018. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source gives the level at which paper reports are keyed, and no share or count of clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

CAF.short: The national reporting system runs in all 35 districts (2025), but only 21.4% of 14 facilities checked in 2024 entered data electronically.
CAF.summary: A DHIS2 Community poster of May 2026 says the ministry undertook the reform of the national health information system (SNIS) and adopted DHIS2 as the national platform. By 2025 DHIS2 had been deployed in all 35 health districts, with data managers recruited and offline and VSAT connections. The IMPULSE study assessed 14 facilities chosen for access and security, on data to July 2024. It found that 21.4% of them used a functional electronic system for routine data entry. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows primary clinics entering their own reports. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

CIV.short: In 2020 departmental health offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system; nothing more recent shows where reports are entered.
CIV.summary: The health ministry's annual report for 2020 calls DHIS2 the national database of routine data. In 2020 each first-contact establishment drew up a monthly report from its registers. The district's surveillance officer keyed it into DHIS2 at the departmental health directorate. By the ministry's account, first-contact establishments did not enter their own reports. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found after 2022 says where clinics' reports are keyed. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

CMR.short: The national system is in use countrywide with entry at the facility (2022 ministry plan), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so.
CMR.summary: The ministry's DHIS2 plan of April 2022 states that a nationwide HMIS is in place for aggregate data. Data entry is at the facility level. The family health directorate gives completeness of monthly activity reports in DHIS2 as 96% nationally for October to December 2025.
