In the last twelve months, the ministry published its digital health plan for 2026 to 2030 in March 2026. The 96% measures reports received. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

COD.short: Health zone offices enter facilities' paper reports into the national system (2021), covering 75.3% of all health facilities (2022); no current plan is known.
COD.summary: DHIS2.org in December 2025 calls the national DHIS2 locally owned and managed infrastructure of the Ministry of Health. The ministry's report of 14 August 2022 states that 12,050 of the 16,010 health facilities listed in DHIS2 report in it. A HISP evaluation in late 2021 found that facilities send paper reports to the zone office for DHIS2 entry. The HIV Insight Dashboard is built inside the national DHIS2. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, Lualaba became the first province to make it its primary tool for provincial data validation. No share or count of facilities entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

COG.short: All 52 health districts enter clinics' paper reports into the national system (2024); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
COG.summary: The health ministry's national health development plan for 2023 to 2026, published in September 2024, names DHIS2 as the principal platform for collecting and processing health information. It states that nearly all facilities compile their reports on paper and send them to the health districts for entry. No change dated within the last twelve months has been found. WHO's annual report for 2025 says 401 data collectors were equipped for electronic transmission of data, without naming their tier. No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

COM.short: The national reporting system reached all 91 public health facilities (WHO, 2025), but no source found reports it where their reports are entered.
COM.summary: WHO Comoros reports that DHIS2 was extended to all 91 public-level health structures in 2025. The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 describes the earlier national system as semi-electronic and computerised at the level of the regions. DHIS2 states that almost 99% of all public health facilities used DHIS2 for health service reporting in 2024. No event dated within the last twelve months has been found. No source found says where DHIS2 reports are keyed, and the 99% counts all public facilities. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

CPV.short: The national reporting system operates in every public health facility (February 2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
CPV.summary: The Ministry of Health's terms of reference of February 2024 name DHIS-2 as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry. They state that it is in operation in all structures of the national health service. The structures include 32 health centres, 34 health posts and 114 basic health units. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Nothing found says who keys them. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

DJI.short: 84% of all health facilities entered their own data in June 2025; with no figure for primary clinics alone, it stays at stage 3.
DJI.summary: UNFPA Djibouti reported on a workshop dated 2 February 2025 that the Ministry of Health ensures national governance of the integrated DHIS2 and GBVIMS-Health platform. The World Bank records 84% of all health facilities with DHIS-2 data entry at the facility level at 30 June 2025, against an end target of 65% for May 2027. Its baseline was 35% in May 2022. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The 84% is of all health facilities, with no numerator or denominator. No share or count of primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

DZA.short: The ministry began training staff on the national reporting system in December 2023, starting with a team of 20; nothing yet shows it in use.
DZA.summary: The Ministry of Health, with WHO support, began training health practitioners and IT staff to use the DHIS2 platform, the WHO Algeria office reports. The first session ran for five days in December 2023, led by an international expert. It trained a first team of 20 health practitioners and IT staff. The national digital health strategy was still a draft in November 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no use of the platform after the first training has been found. Establishing would need a national system that takes the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from paper forms, with a minority of primary clinics entering their own or no figure published.

EGY.short: Births and deaths are entered at district level into the national health information system (2025); routine clinic reporting is not shown.
EGY.summary: Egypt's answers to the WHO EMRO civil registration questionnaire, published in 2025, describe the Ministry of Health's national health information system. Health offices notify births and deaths. Copies go to the health department at district level. The district department processes the notifications electronically into the national system. The answers state that automation of the health offices is under implementation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the source's latest year is 2011. Establishing would need a national system that takes the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms.

ERI.short: Reports are entered at zone and sub-zone offices (2024); no primary clinic is shown entering its own.
ERI.summary: The sector plan HSSDP III, dated October 2021, states that DHIS2 had been rolled out to about 40 per cent of facilities at secondary level and above. WHO Eritrea reported in 2022 a functional DHIS-2 at national level, at sub-national level and in 44% of the districts. A DHIS2 Community post of March 2024 describes the flow. Data enters the national DHIS2 from zones and sub-zones over the ministry's local networks, running offline. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No primary clinic has been found entering its own reports, and no share or count of clinics has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

ETH.short: Hospitals and health centres enter their own reports into the national system (2024); no source found reports it whether health posts do.
ETH.summary: On 23 December 2025 Ethiopia signed a memorandum with the United States that names DHIS2 as the country's HMIS. Interviews from October 2023 to March 2024 found that health information technicians key routine reports into DHIS2 at their own facilities. Health posts record largely on paper and send monthly to their health centre, as surveyed in 2019 and 2020. A 2025 study puts over 4,000 primary health care institutions, 95% of those eligible, on DHIS2. No change has been found in the last twelve months. That 95% counts institutions of all kinds, and no share of primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GAB.short: The national system was launched in December 2024, with 122 data managers trained across 51 health departments; clinics are not shown entering their own reports.
GAB.summary: DHIS2 was launched nationally on 6 December 2024, as HISP Rwanda reported. WHO Gabon says it integrated all functional public health facilities and trained 122 data managers and 10 regional health directors in 2024. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 data managers of the Libreville region's university hospitals were trained to send data through DHIS2. No source names the tiers that report. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GHA.short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national system, and some community health posts enter their own (2024); how many is not published.
GHA.summary: The Ghana Health Service's strategy for 2023-2027 lists DHIMS II first among its digital health solutions. The Ministry of Health's plan of June 2022 states that most facilities validate and enter their data into DHIMS2 themselves. In March 2024, CHPS staff in three Northern Region districts said their compounds lacked login details and computers. Paper reports went to the sub-district or the district office for upload. In the last twelve months, in November 2026 the Health Minister directed that DHIMS be joined to GHIMS, the hospital system. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GIN.short: All levels reported into the national system in early 2026, with clinics' paper reports entered at district offices.
GIN.summary: The ministry's bulletin for the first quarter of 2026 says All regions and all levels of the health pyramid transmitted their data on time. Its PASA2 page of 2025 states that health posts, health centres and prefectural hospitals collect SNIS data on paper primary tools. The data are keyed into DHIS2. In the last twelve months the SNIS reached what the ministry calls a historic record of 100% completeness. The 2021 yearbook says first-level centres' monthly reports were either entered in DHIS2 or sent to the district team for entry. No share or count of centres or posts entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GMB.short: Clinics reported on paper, and regional health offices entered the figures into the national reporting system, in 2024.
GMB.summary: The Ministry of Health's National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030, published in February 2024, calls DHIS2 the central reporting system for all national health information. It places the electronic HMIS at the seven regional health directorates and the ministry. At the facility the HMIS is paper, in registers and monthly return forms. A tuberculosis pilot at 11 sites between June and November 2024 saw the sites kept generating their monthly reports for the DHIS2 aggregate system from paper registers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GNB.short: Health centres' paper reports were entered into the national system at 11 health directorates (June 2023); how many clinics enter their own is not published.
GNB.summary: The Ministry of Public Health's PNDS III of June 2023 states that all the SNIS paper forms and reports are digitised in the 11 health directorates, on the DHIS2 platform. INASA's 2022 yearbook tabulates the monthly reports of health centres entered in DHIS2, 1,747 of 2,073 expected. In the last twelve months, on 6 October 2026, the DHIS2 project announced an agreement to support INASA on the national system's data quality. It brings new HIV and tuberculosis patient-tracking tools. No number or share of health centres keying their own reports has been found. No fact on tablet entry follows the 2018 pilot. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

GNQ.short: The national reporting system was piloted in two districts, Baney and Añisok, in 2025; a planned national expansion in 2026 is not confirmed.
GNQ.summary: The health ministry announced the conclusion of the DHIS2 pilot on 25 November 2025, in the districts of Baney and Añisok. It said the pilot would be the reference for a national expansion of DHIS2 foreseen for 2026. In the last twelve months, UNDP handed DHIS2 over to the health ministry on 16 November 2026. EHAS states that elsewhere health facilities filled paper register sheets, which ministry staff transferred to spreadsheets. In the pilot, data is entered at the District Office where digital means are lacking. No source counts the facilities entering data in the pilot. Establishing would need a national system that takes the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms.

KEN.short: Facilities across the country enter their reports online into the national system (2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so themselves.
KEN.summary: The Ministry of Health uses the Kenya Health Information System (KHIS) to collect health data from facilities nationwide, as IDinsight reported in October 2024. Facilities record services in paper daily registers, then enter and submit the summaries online. Legal Notice 77 of 2025, in force from 11 April 2025, made the Digital Health Agency responsible for maintaining the Health Management Information Services Platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The mid-term review reports 94% of all health facilities submitted reports within KHIS in 2019/20. That is a reporting rate, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

LBR.short: All facilities report monthly into the national system (2024), with district and county clerks entering the figures from paper forms (2022).
LBR.summary: The Ministry of Health's report for 2024 states that its HMIS runs on DHIS2. Evidence Action surveyed 48 facilities in three counties, from records of May to July 2022. It found that all of them filled paper HMIS forms monthly, and data clerks entered them into DHIS2. The ministry's Data Quality Improvement Plan of June 2022 runs 2022 to 2026 and is costed at US$7,312,887.50. In the last twelve months, Liberia signed a memorandum with the United States on 9 December 2025. It plans US$1,338,372 of US funding for HMIS/DHIS2 over 2026 to 2030. No national figure for clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

LBY.short: The national system was rolled out to 465 primary care facilities and 51 hospitals in 2023; how many clinics enter their own reports is unknown.
LBY.summary: WHO states that in 2023 it and the ministry rolled out DHIS2 in 40 municipalities. The rollout covered 465 primary health care facilities and 51 hospitals. WHO also says DHIS2 reached 100% national geographic coverage by March 2023, and that consistent reporting from health facilities remains a challenge. Libya Review reported on 7 November 2025 a meeting of the ministry and WHO that explored the feasibility of extending DHIS2 in public facilities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

LSO.short: 231 facilities report HIV figures into the national system (2025); clinics entering their own data is shown only in four pilot districts, up to 2017.
LSO.summary: Lesotho's Health Management Information System has run on DHIS2 since February 2015. Under a primary health care reform pilot from July 2014 to June 2017, each health facility nurse in charge was given a computer and submitted the monthly report from the facility in four districts. The registers stayed on paper. In November 2025 the ministry's HIV programme stated that facility reports are automated from its electronic medical record into DHIS2. In 2025 Lesotho endorsed its National Digital Health Strategy 2025-2030. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

MAR.short: A national reporting system was working in every public health centre by December 2019; no figure shows how many centres enter their own reports.
MAR.summary: The World Bank's completion report gives Morocco's SMIPF-SC reporting system as operational in 100% of public health centres by December 2019. In June 2025 it reported that an integrated and digitalised health information system was deployed at hospitals. Deployment had begun in primary health care centres. In the last twelve months, the National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 names that system, the SIIS, and makes the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and the territorial health groups accountable for deploying it. No share or count of health centres entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

MDG.short: Health centres in all 114 districts report into the national system, with district offices entering their paper forms (2023).
MDG.summary: Madagascar's PSRSIS 2023-2027, the health ministry's plan for its information system, states that DHIS2 was scaled to all 22 regions and 114 districts in January 2019. As at the plan, the basic health centres' data go up to the districts on the integrated monthly report in paper form. In the last twelve months, WHO Madagascar's report on 2024-2025 lists an audit of the DHIS2 platform and secured cloud hosting. No count or share of health centres keying their own report has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

MLI.short: Community and referral health centres and hospitals had routine data in the national system in 2019; no source found says how many clinics enter their own.
MLI.summary: Mali's health ministry plan of February 2021 states that since 2016 the routine data of community health centres (CSCom), reference health centres (CSRéf) and hospitals has been on the DHIS2 platform. A USAID assessment of April 2023 states that by September 2019 the ministry had deployed DHIS-2 in 98 percent of community health centers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. The 98 percent is a deployment share. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

MOZ.short: In 2025 facilities' paper data was still entered into the national system at district level; no clinic is shown entering its own reports.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's health ministry dated its Plano de Melhoria de Qualidade de Dados 2025-2029 in January 2025; it is a national plan for the quality of data in SIS-MA, the ministry's aggregate health information system. A 2019 assessment found that in 14 districts facilities' monthly data reached the district health office on paper forms. A 2025 DHIS2 Community account has child health data still collected on paper at facilities and entered as aggregates at district level. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No clinic is shown entering its own reports. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

MRT.short: District offices enter health posts' paper reports into the national system (2023); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's Arrêté n° 1496 of 14 December 2021 assigns collection and analysis of SNIS data to the ministry's regional and circonscription services, the SNIS being the health ministry's information system. The World Bank's assessment of 2023 states that health posts report on paper to health centres. A ministry analysis of June 2025 states that only the hospitals of Hodh Gharbi and Guidimagha have data integrated in DHIS2. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

MUS.short: In January 2022 the national system was used only at regional and national level, with entry by clinics still planned; nothing more recent is held.
MUS.summary: DHIS2's country story of January 2022 states that the government, through the Ministry of Health and Wellness, has begun implementing DHIS2 as the national health information system. It says the authorities planned to decentralise DHIS2 to district and primary health care level. WHO's SCORE assessment, using data from 2013 to 2018, rates a standardised system of electronic data entry for aggregate reporting at district or comparable level as 'not there'. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing on the system is dated after January 2022. Establishing would need a national system taking the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level.

MWI.short: District offices enter paper reports from 1,266 facilities into the national system (2023); how many health centres enter their own is not published.
MWI.summary: Malawi's Ministry of Health has collected aggregated facility data since 2002 through a unified HMIS, a study of December 2024 states. An August 2023 survey found that facilities compile monthly reports on paper and deliver them to the district health office. In the last twelve months, a project began in December 2025 and runs to March 2027. It will deploy DHIS2 climate and health tools on the national HMIS, first in four districts. No count or share of health centres entering their own reports has been published. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

NAM.short: Clinics report on paper, and district officers enter their monthly forms into the national reporting system (2026 study).
NAM.summary: Managers interviewed for a study published in March 2026 said that the Ministry of Health and Social Services manages DHIS2 centrally, on a server at headquarters. Facilities send monthly paper summary forms, and district HIS officers key them into the DHIS2 aggregate module at the district office. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the ministry launched the National Digital Health Policy (2026-2036). On 6 May 2025 the minister said health data collection had expanded to over 90 clinics beyond district and hospital levels. No total was given. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

NER.short: A 2023 ministry guide has health centres enter their monthly reports into the national system; no figure shows how many do.
NER.summary: Niger's health ministry monitoring guide of December 2023 has every health establishment key its monthly report into DHIS2. Health posts send their data to their CSI, where it is checked and keyed, the CSI being the integrated health centre. In the last twelve months, OpenFn reports that workflows moving STELab laboratory results and CommCare community data into DHIS2 were running by May 2026. The guide gives CSI report completeness of 97.90% and timeliness of 54.63% for 2021. No count of centres keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

NGA.short: 91.5% of all health facilities reported into the national system in June 2025, with local government offices entering the figures from paper.
NGA.summary: The Federal Ministry of Health's bulletin of the National Health Management Information System (NHMIS) puts the rate at 91.5% for June 2025 for facility reporting on DHIS-2. Gavi's Zero-Dose Learning Hub states that monthly reports are entered manually into DHIS2 at LGA offices. In the last twelve months, in a memorandum of 19 December 2025, Nigeria commits to use DHIS2 as its national health data warehouse. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

RWA.short: Health facilities enter their own reports (audit to 2023), but no source found says whether health posts do, so it stays at stage 3.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's Ministry of Health upgraded the HMIS, established in 1998, to web-based DHIS2 from 2012. In 2017 the facility's own data manager uploaded the data into DHIS2 by the 5th of the month. The Global Fund's Inspector General states that DHIS2 has been rolled out at all health facilities, in an audit covering July 2021 to December 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No measured share of clinics entering their own reports has been found. No source shows whether the health posts key theirs. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

SDN.short: Local health offices entered facilities' reports into the system in 144 of 189 localities in 2020; nothing since April 2023 shows where data is entered.
SDN.summary: WHO's 2020 assessment states that facility data are entered into DHIS2 at the locality level. In the last twelve months, at the review meeting of February 2026, the Federal Minister of Health said data reporting coverage rose from 13 per cent at the onset of the crisis. It reached more than 56 per cent by the end of 2025. The ministry's Director General of Health Information called for a full transition from paper-based to digital reporting through DHIS2. Nothing dated after April 2023 says where data is keyed. No source shows a facility entering its own reports. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

SEN.short: The national system is used at every level, with figures entered from the district upwards (2021); how many clinics enter their own is unknown.
SEN.summary: The Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action sociale has run the DHIS2 implementation since 2013, a DHIS2 Community post of 2 March 2021 states. The ministry's IT master plan of 31 December 2021 states that DHIS2 runs from the health districts up to the minister's cabinet. In the last twelve months, the World Bank published a programme document dated 11 December 2025. It states that health worker strikes over the past 2.5 years have left gaps in data collection, storage and reporting across DHIS2. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

SLE.short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national reporting system (2020 procedure, 2023 assessment).
SLE.summary: Under the Ministry of Health's HMIS procedures manual of April 2020, peripheral health units compile monthly reports from paper registers. A district data entry officer keys them into DHIS2. A GIZ and ministry assessment of January 2023 surveyed 246 health facilities, 202 of them primary. It states that DHIS2 was deployed in 96% of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

SOM.short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system (2022), and 111 primary facilities report digitally (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
SOM.summary: The Ministry of Health's bulletin for July to September 2023 states that the ministry decided to use DHIS2 as the exclusive national HMIS platform. A ministry case study of 2023 to 2025 reports that 111 public primary healthcare facilities across six states produce their DHIS2 aggregate reports digitally from the RAAD record. In the last twelve months, ISDP ran a three-day HMIS training of trainers in Bosaso on 3 to 5 February 2026. It trained 16 health workers. A commentary of August 2026 by ministry staff says DHIS2-based reporting remains uneven across facilities and administrative levels. No share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

SSD.short: The ministry says 30% of all health facilities entered their own reports into the national system in 2025, without giving the numbers behind it.
SSD.summary: In the ministry's report for 2024-25 the Minister of Health calls DHIS2 the ministry's official national health information platform. The ministry reports that 30% of all health facilities reported directly through DHIS2 in 2025. The plan's target was 55%. The report adds that entry is frequently centralised or delayed. In the last twelve months, the World Bank's mission of November 2025 records that facilities in DHIS2 were verified with State Ministries of Health. No share of primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

STP.short: The national reporting system was introduced in all districts in 2024-2025; who uses it and where reports are entered is not yet known.
STP.summary: The Ministry of Health launched DHIS2 as the health information system on 18 December 2019. Its National Health Development Plan 2023-2032, of September 2022, carries a costed health information pillar that names DHIS2. Two years after implementation, its use covered only the vaccination, reproductive health, tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS and malaria programmes. In the last twelve months, the WHO country office's report on the 2024-2025 biennium says DHIS2 was implemented in all districts. No source found says how many primary clinics enter their own reports. Establishing would need a national system taking the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms.

SWZ.short: Hospitals and maternity units record births and deaths digitally (2022), and the national reporting system was introduced in 2024; clinic reporting is not yet shown.
SWZ.summary: MEASURE Evaluation's country profile of August 2019 records no electronic system for aggregating routine facility or community service data. WHO's country office reports that DHIS2 was introduced nationally in 2024 as a single platform for health data, where the data had sat in separate programme databases. In the last twelve months, the ministry's HMIS unit says that in the first quarter of 2026 reporting from CMIS to DHIS2 was strengthened with automated, FHIR-aligned data flows. No source found says which tiers enter routine reports. None says how many primary clinics enter their own. Establishing would need a national system taking the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms.

SYC.short: Sources disagree on whether health data is captured on paper or electronically (2022 to 2025); nothing shows digital reporting, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: No stage is set. No tier reporting digitally and no primary clinic entering its own reports has been found for Seychelles. Sources do not agree on whether health data is captured on paper or electronically. The ministry has a disease surveillance system and laboratory digital platforms, each single-function. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that routine health reporting is not entered digitally at any level of the health system.

TCD.short: District offices enter health centres' monthly paper reports into the national system (Gavi audit, 2024); no source found says how many centres enter their own.
TCD.summary: The DHIS2 programme stated in November 2022 that the Ministry of Public Health and Prevention runs DHIS2. The national health plan for 2022-2030 lists extending DHIS2 to the health centres as an action still to be carried out. Gavi's audit of August 2024 records that in one district the immunisation officer keys the monthly reports of 16 health centres into DHIS2 himself. In the last twelve months, WHO's Chad office reports the updating of the reporting tools and their integration into DHIS2. No share or count of health centres entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

TGO.short: 96.5% of all health facilities entered complete reports in 2021, the ministry says; with no figure for primary clinics alone, it stays at stage 3.
TGO.summary: The health ministry's monitoring and evaluation plan of October 2023 names DHIS2 as the platform of what the ministry calls the SNIS, the national health information system. It requires each health facility to key its validated monthly or quarterly activity report into DHIS2. The plan gives 96.5% for 2021 as the share of all health facilities due to report that keyed a complete SNIS report into DHIS2. In the last twelve months, HISP's July 2026 round-up reports a field mission to integrate the eRDQA data quality app into national DHIS2. No figure for primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

TUN.short: Nothing found describes routine health reporting; a national health information system was named in 2021 with no sign of use, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not found. Nothing is held on routine aggregate reporting, at any tier. The ministry's performance report for 2021 names a unified national health information system being put in place and says nothing of its use.

TZA.short: Clinics report on paper, and council offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2024).
TZA.summary: The Ministry of Health's methodology for its 2024 statistics states that each facility aggregates its registers and tally sheets monthly. The figures are entered into DHIS2 at council level. In 2025 all public facilities in two councils, Dodoma and Bahi, entered their own data in DHIS2. The ministry's guidelines of May 2019 state that aggregated data is entered into DHIS in some health facilities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

UGA.short: Every level reported into the national system in 2023/24, but in 2026 a mid-level health centre carried its report to the district office.
UGA.summary: A census of all 265 government Health Centre IVs and hospitals, published in October 2025, found DHIS2 in use in 98.8% of them. The National Health Compact 2025-2030, adopted in December 2025, commits to scale DHIS2 up to all facilities. In the last twelve months, Makerere University's METS programme said in April 2026 that reporting through DHIS2 rose from 58 percent in 2020 to 98 percent in 2025. The Uganda Muslim Medical Bureau said on 11 August 2026 that many Health Centre IIIs lack computers and connectivity to submit reports. No share of primary clinics has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports, on a published share or count.

ZAF.short: The national system is used at facility, district, provincial and national level (July 2026); no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
ZAF.summary: On the National Department of Health's bid terms of 24 July 2026, the Director-General has overall ownership of the District Health Information System. The department described the system as used at facility, district, province and national level. Nine provincial instances capture the routine data, on its account. In the last twelve months, on 24 July 2026 the department issued bid NDOH 09/2025-2026 for a provider to host, maintain, support and enhance the system. Thabethe and Mathews state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape province used DHIS2 from April 2017 to March 2020. No national share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

ZMB.short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system each month, with a few facilities entering directly (April 2024).
ZMB.summary: Gavi's programme audit of April 2024 calls DHIS2 the Ministry of Health's own system. It states that data entry into DHIS2 is done monthly at the district level, and the audit says that a few health facilities report directly into DHIS2. Interviews of 2019 describe facilities aggregating patient data onto paper reports each month. In the last twelve months, the Countdown to 2030 country team states that 99% of expected monthly facility reports were in DHIS2 in 2024, against 93% in 2019. No count or share of facilities entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

ZWE.short: All levels of the health system report on paper, and district offices enter the figures into the national system (2023).
ZWE.summary: The U.S. President's Malaria Initiative's profile, published in 2023, describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health and Child Care's system, to which donors and partners have very limited access. It states that monthly collection is on paper at village, health facility and hospital levels. The district health information officer enters the paper records into DHIS2. The profile's routine table gives 1,776 health facilities reporting into the HMIS/DHIS2 in 2022. In the last twelve months, the Countdown to 2030 synthesis report states that the national reporting rate of health facility data in DHIS2 was above 92% in 2024. No count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.

AGO.short: One hospital was testing a prototype electronic record for maternity care in 2019, entered after the event; nothing is known since.
AGO.summary: In November 2019 the Irene Neto Maternity Hospital in Lubango ran an electronic obstetric record prototype that was part of a doctoral research project at the University of Beira Interior, Portugal. The prototype was in its test phase. Between March and September 2019, two Luanda tuberculosis facilities kept clinical and surveillance data entirely on paper records and registers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found is dated after 2019. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

BDI.short: 41 of 71 hospitals kept electronic patient records and six health centres were piloting them in 2023; records are not shown to be shared.
BDI.summary: Forty-one of 71 public and faith-based hospitals are computerised, patient health records included, the World Bank reported in March 2023. Thirty-nine of them run OpenClinic. The hospitals are not interconnected, and each has its own patient identifier. Six health centres are computerised under a pilot financed by Enabel, the same report says. In the last twelve months, a memorandum signed on 6 February 2026 commits Burundi to roll SIDAinfo out in 460 facilities by 2026 and 572 by 2028. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

BEN.short: Only a promised digital health booklet is held, from 2026; nothing says whether patient records are electronic or on paper, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: No stage is set. No source found, as at 13 October 2026, states a tier, a place of digitisation or a clinic count for electronic patient records in Benin. A digital health booklet is held only as a pledge. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

BFA.short: Electronic patient records ran at two pilot hospitals in 2025 and one university hospital in 2023; primary clinics are not shown using them.
BFA.summary: NetAfrique reported on 18 July 2025 that OpenClinic, a hospital management system with clinical and nursing records, is deployed at pilot sites, the CHUR of Ouahigouya and the CHR of Manga. At Manga the 2024-2025 pilot ended in full digitisation of admissions. By April 2023 a study found the public health system lacked computerised patient records. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The position at primary clinics has not been found. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts, with each record staying in the facility that made it.

BWA.short: All public hospitals kept electronic patient records in 2019-20, and a central system reached 22 facilities in one district by March 2026.
BWA.summary: The Ministry of Health's budget speech of 5 March 2026 states that it and the Ministry of Local Government and Traditional Affairs will roll out the completed EMR. It covers the remaining 29 districts in 2026/27. In the last twelve months, on 5 March 2026, the Assistant Minister told Parliament that Phase 1 of the ministry's centralised Electronic Medical Record had been implemented, covering 22 health facilities in Ngami. On 19 November 2025 the Minister of Local Government had said the Electronic Medical Records system was being piloted in two districts. No source shows a unique patient identifier in use. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

CAF.short: An electronic patient record is being introduced in stages at hospitals and health centres (2026); no source found reports the number of sites.
CAF.summary: HISP Rwanda reported on 18 March 2026 that it is supporting deployment of the HISP EMR, known in the country as e-SENI. In the last twelve months, the report describes a phased deployment under way. It covers site assessments, configuration in French and staff training. It states that medical records in many facilities are still kept in paper registers. No source found gives the number of e-SENI sites or any clinics figure. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

CIV.short: The ministry's patient record was used in 258 facilities of unstated type in 2026; no source found reports use by most hospitals or by primary clinics.
CIV.summary: The health ministry's digital health directorate deployed its patient record, the DPI, in August 2024. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the directorate's officials said 258 health facilities use it, without giving their type. On 4 September 2026 a national workshop named the patient record among ten quick wins due by the end of 2026. No source found shows primary clinics using the record, as against having it deployed. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

CMR.short: The ministry's patient record was installed in about fifty pilot facilities between 2020 and 2024; routine use in hospitals is not shown.
CMR.summary: The Ministry of Public Health's electronic medical record, the DME, runs on Bahmni. Its plan for 2026 to 2030 states that the record was deployed in about fifty pilot health facilities during the 2020-2024 plan. The plan budgets for 2026 the selection of a partner and a public-private partnership contract to deploy one. In the last twelve months, the SmartMobileClinic project ran 12 rural campaigns between November 2025 and January 2026. The level of the pilot facilities has not been found. Routine use at any hospital has not been shown. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

COD.short: A government agency has delivered computers and hospital systems to named hospitals since 2024, but none is yet said to use electronic patient records.
COD.summary: The national agency ANICNS leads the health-sector digital transformation project, Actualite.cd reported on 23 November 2024. On 12 July 2024 it handed digital kits and three hospital information systems to three sites in Kinshasa. In the last twelve months, on 16 June 2026, it opened a call for the now-mandatory approval of hospital information systems. Each system is to include a complete computerised patient record. A survey of seven Kananga hospitals in 2023 found 4.7% of 86 staff managing patient information electronically. No source found states that any facility uses an electronic patient record. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

COG.short: A February 2026 decree names a hospital information system at one public hospital, but no source describes patient records, so no stage is set.
COG.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found, as at 30 September 2026, says whether patient records are kept on paper or digitally at any tier. A public hospital's organisation decree names a hospital information system, without saying that it holds the clinical record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

COM.short: The Ministry of Health stated in July 2021 that the country has no electronic patient records; nothing since confirms or changes this.
COM.summary: In July 2021 the Ministry of Health stated in its digital health strategy that the electronic patient record does not exist in the country. The strategy plans a modular application for reception, consultations, tests, hospitalisation and billing. The World Bank recorded a hospital management information system as not functional at 31 August 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated after July 2021 confirms or replaces the ministry's statement. Preparing would need electronic patient records in use in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system procured or being prepared, with primary clinics not using them beyond pilot sites.

CPV.short: Electronic patient records are in use only in Praia, at its health centres and central hospital (February 2024).
CPV.summary: The Ministry of Health's terms of reference of February 2024 name Medicine One as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry. As at February 2024 it was in use only in Praia's health facilities, namely its health centres and the central hospital. In the last twelve months, on 18 December 2025, the Minister of Health said each citizen will get a unique patient code giving access to a digital clinical history. No count of sites or share of primary clinics has been found. The patient code is not shown in use. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

DJI.short: A 2024 report describes patient follow-up on paper without saying where; no electronic record system is named, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: No stage is set. A report of 2024 describes medical follow-up on paper, and names no tier and no system. No electronic medical record is named at any tier. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

DZA.short: In September 2026 the electronic medical record ran in pilot facilities, with all public establishments due by November; no source found says how many use it.
DZA.summary: From 2018 the ministry put an earlier record, DEMDZ, into certain pilot hospitals. In July 2026 it launched a national deployment plan aiming at over 2,500 health structures in all 69 wilayas. In the last twelve months, El Watan reported in September 2026 that the record was under way in several pilot facilities, with 15 November 2026 set as the deadline for all public health establishments. Annaba's El Bouni primary-care facility trained staff for the record going live on 15 November 2026. No count or share of hospitals or primary clinics using the record has been found. No source states where it is keyed. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

EGY.short: Electronic records run in 265 primary care centres in six insurance governorates (2026); no source found reports the share of primary clinics nationally.
EGY.summary: The National Health Compact of December 2025 put electronic health records at early pilots. In the last twelve months, the Egypt Healthcare Authority's head said in July 2026 that its health information system runs in 265 primary care centres and units. They are in the six first-phase insurance governorates. On 9 November 2026 the Authority's chairman said a unified platform lets patients be treated in any governorate it covers. It held about 6.2 million electronic health files. No national share of primary clinics has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic patient records, entered at the point of care and retrievable at another facility.

ERI.short: Only a patient-tracking programme is held; no electronic patient record is named and nothing says records are on paper, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: No stage is set. The joint external evaluation of August 2025 recommended a USSD-based national electronic reporting system and a mobile-based data system for essential health service use during emergencies. The Ministry of Health has a DHIS2 tracker program, and Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) serves one function. No electronic medical record has been found at any tier. No dated statement that patient records are on paper at every tier has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need electronic patient records in use in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system procured or being prepared.

ETH.short: More than 70 facilities had electronic patient records by December 2024, 10 of them paperless; a national pilot is due in 2026.
ETH.summary: The Ministry of Health stated in December 2024 that electronic medical records were introduced in over 70 health facilities. In the last twelve months, on 23 December 2025, Ethiopia and the United States signed the memorandum. It schedules a national multi-tenant EMR, with piloting in 2026, 48 facilities by 2027 and 438 by 2030. Its baseline is 0% of hospitals and health centres implementing the full national EMR. No source gives the tier of the 70-plus facilities or the total they are drawn from. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GAB.short: A national patient record ran at 13 pilot sites in greater Libreville in February 2026, two of them health centres.
GAB.summary: On 11 February 2026 the health information system eGabon-SIS worked in 13 pilot sites across Grand Libreville, on Gabonactu's account. The Libreville university hospital and the regional hospitals were not yet covered. In the last twelve months, the World Bank project was officially closed on 24 June 2026. The Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital went live on 13 July 2026. Two health centres, Lalala and Glass, were confirmed using the system on 23 October 2025. No count of primary clinics using the system, and no denominator, has been found. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GHA.short: The national hospital record system's contract lapsed in December 2024 and a replacement was ordered in October 2025; its reach is not yet known.
GHA.summary: The Vice President said on 31 October 2024 that the Lightwave system LHIMS was deployed in all six teaching hospitals, 10 regional hospitals and 243 district hospitals. Its vendor's contract expired on 31 December 2024. A ministry directive of 28 October 2025 ordered GHIMS rolled out nationwide in November 2025 as the only authorised platform for patient registration. In the last twelve months, a Ghana Medical Journal editorial of January 2026 says the ministry discontinued LHIMS after its contract expired in December 2024. No source shows which tiers or how many facilities use GHIMS. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GIN.short: Three separate patient record systems ran in some hospitals and pilot facilities in 2026, with records entered during care; no totals have been found.
GIN.summary: By August 2026 Visa Medical was deployed in 19 public establishments, Dubréka hospital among them. A ministry mission of 17 to 22 August 2026 reviewed five digitised facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts running OpenClinic. In the last twelve months, the Dalaba prefectural hospital deployed OpenClinic in January 2026. In March 2026 the Swiss Re Foundation had the Clinic+O record in use in rural communities and at Community Health Centers. No count of hospitals has been found against which these figures can be set. No count or district has been found for health centres using Clinic+O. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GMB.short: One referral hospital piloted an electronic medical record in 2023; no source found reports it whether that pilot, or a contracted four-facility one, still runs.
GMB.summary: The Point reported in August 2023 the pilot launch of an Electronic Medical Records system at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital. In June 2023 the World Bank described the OpenClinic system as still to be piloted, in four health facilities. The National Health Sector Policy of February 2024 states that the health sector does not have a robust electronic medical record system in place. The World Bank's identity diagnostic of 2025 says a health information system is managing patient records and issuing health cards, and names no facility. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source shows whether either pilot was running at 30 September 2026. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GNB.short: The only record held is one private clinic's in Bissau (June 2023); nothing describes hospitals or primary clinics more widely, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: No stage is set. As at June 2023, the one electronic patient record found is at a single private clinic in Bissau, and no source states its tier. Nothing has been found on tiers, primary clinics or governance. Nothing has been found for the last twelve months. No admissible source states that patient records are kept on paper, and none says at which level of the health system. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

GNQ.short: One hospital in Bata had an electronic patient record in 2018, by its vendor's account; no source found says whether it still runs.
GNQ.summary: Vannin Group, the vendor, says it deployed Greencube at Hospital Nuevo INSESO in Bata in 2018. Its case study, dated 2018, describes the platform as the unified electronic health record platform of Hospital Nuevo INSESO, a hospital of 85 beds. It then counted 600 active users of its Greencube platform at Hospital Nuevo INSESO and 60,000 patient records. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated after 2018 shows the record still in use, and no other facility keeping electronic patient records has been found. No source shows where the record is entered, or any use in primary clinics. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

KEN.short: Public dispensaries, health centres and sub-county hospitals were reported moved onto the government's digital health system in September 2026; shared records are not confirmed.
KEN.summary: The US-Kenya Cooperation Framework of 4 December 2025 says TaifaCare HMIS was deployed in 1,500 public health facilities. It sets deployment at 2,000 facilities by 2026, 4,000 by 2027 and 8,000 by 2028. In the last twelve months, the government set 30 September 2026 for the move to HMIS, then extended it to 30 October. By 6 October 38 of 518 faith-based facilities had moved, beside 6,427 public ones. Regulations in force from 11 April 2025 require certified systems to query and update a shared health record within twenty-four hours of each encounter. No national share of primary clinics has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic patient records, entered at the point of care and retrievable at another facility.

LBR.short: A vendor's system runs at a handful of pilot clinics and health centres (September 2026); no source found reports the exact number.
LBR.summary: In a memorandum of 9 December 2025 with the United States, Liberia commits to an open-source EMR in clinics, health centers and hospitals. The targets are 20% of public facilities in 2026 and 100% in 2030. In the last twelve months, the ministry's National Health Intelligence Center launched enumerator training on 8 May 2026 for a nationwide EMR readiness assessment. OneHealthEHR says its platform went into live clinical use on 1 September 2026 at four facilities across Liberia and Ghana. It reports the deployment grew from four to seven active clinics and health centers, counted across both countries together. No count of Liberian facilities live has been found. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

LBY.short: One teaching hospital was partly using a system in 2025, and two clinics ran a trial in 2022 that is not shown continuing.
LBY.summary: Libya Herald reported in May 2022 that the trial operation of the system was inaugurated at two clinics, in Tripoli and Benghazi. In January 2024 the National Centre for Health System Reform launched the National Comprehensive Health Care Programme and the Health Number System in Tripoli. They are the ministry's option for the electronic health file. In the last twelve months, a Sabratha University study of 24 December 2025 said the move towards electronic medical records is slow or stalled in many government hospitals. Nothing found shows the 2022 trial continuing, or the file launched in January 2024 in use anywhere. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

LSO.short: An electronic register ran in 197 public facilities in November 2025, while rural health centres recorded general care on paper (2023).
LSO.summary: The ministry's HIV programme stated in November 2025 that the OpenMRS/Bahmni-based EMR/eRegister is in 197 public facilities. The MCC compact of 12 May 2022 funds the expansion of the e-Register into a national electronic medical record system for all primary health care patients. A hospital EMR was introduced in 2013 across 16 public hospitals in the 10 districts. The ministry's assessment of 18 October 2017 found it discontinued in several facilities and in substandard use in others. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No denominator for the 197 facilities has been found, and nothing shows the expansion to all primary care patients delivered. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MAR.short: A hospital record system is reported in all public hospitals (2024), and one province's primary clinics keep electronic patient files; sharing is not shown.
MAR.summary: Morocco's framework law 06-22 of 9 December 2022 creates a shared medical record within the national health information system. A government document of December 2024 states that the integrated hospital information system has been deployed in all public hospitals of the twelve regions. In the last twelve months, Medias24 reported in July 2026 that the Government Council had adopted draft law 52.26. On 1 June 2026 the health minister said the ministry is still working to put the unified medical record in place. No share or count of primary clinics using a patient record has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping point-of-care records, each retrievable at another facility.

MDG.short: Some private establishments and some health centres kept electronic records in 2024; no numbers have been found, and no hospital use is shown.
MDG.summary: A round table attended by the health ministry on 5 November 2024 heard that the electronic personal medical record was described as functional in some private establishments and some basic health centres. In January 2025, 2424.mg reported that two pilot sites had been chosen to start the hospital digitalisation project. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count, share or district has been found for the facilities keeping an electronic record. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MLI.short: One Bamako hospital records care electronically as it happens (2026), and 27 community health centres were equipped under a project in 2022.
MLI.summary: The health ministry's agency ANTIM told USAID in July 2022 that it had digitalized a dozen of the 65 reference health centers. In the last twelve months, on 27 July 2026, the Hôpital dermatologie de Bamako ran a fully digitised consultation circuit, from registration through consultation and laboratory to pharmacy, the ministry's communication network reports. The SanDi project of 2021 to 2022 deployed OpenClinic in 27 community health centres. No count or share of primary clinics using the record has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MOZ.short: One hospital, Mavalane General, went digital in December 2024; no clinic is shown using electronic patient records.
MOZ.summary: Jembi Health Systems states that in December 2024 Mavalane General Hospital in Maputo became Mozambique's first digital hospital. In the last twelve months, the health memorandum of 15 December 2025 with the United States targets a minimum viable version of SIS-RME for September 2026, the integrated electronic medical record system. No release of SIS-RME has been found. None of the 16 public primary care facilities selected for the 2016-17 study had an electronic system. No count or share of clinics using electronic records has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MRT.short: One health centre digitised its records in 2022, and 12 centres were chosen in 2026 to pilot a shared record; no source found reports wider use.
MRT.summary: The state news agency AMI reported in 2022 that one health centre had digitised its patients' records, Sebkha in Nouakchott-Ouest. In the last twelve months, on 21 February 2026, the health minister said the electronic medical record would start two days later. In October 2026 Bluesquare said 12 of 21 health centres assessed in Nouakchott, Trarza and Brakna were confirmed as pilot sites for OpenClinic GA. Nothing after 2022 shows whether the Sebkha record still runs. No OpenClinic GA site is shown in use. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MUS.short: A shared electronic patient record was piloted at about thirty public facilities in two regions in 2026; no source found says how many are primary clinics.
MUS.summary: The health ministry's Health Sector Strategic Plan gave the share of all health facilities using EMR as 0 in 2019, against a target of 100% by 2024. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, the health minister said the system, which he calls e-Health, is operational at New Flacq Hospital. By October 2026 it was in pilot in about thirty public health facilities of the East and Centre. Primary clinics are not counted apart from hospitals. No share of primary clinics using it has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

MWI.short: A national record system is being piloted at one central hospital and selected health centres (September 2026); how many centres is not stated.
MWI.summary: The Digital Health Governance Framework 2025-2030, signed in June 2025, sets the system's nationwide scale-up across public and private facilities. The system is the Malawi Health Care Information System, Mahis. In the last twelve months, on 3 September 2026, Mahis was in pilot at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre. It was also in pilot at selected health centres nationwide. The number of health centres in the pilot has not been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

NAM.short: An electronic system is fully in place at only two hospitals; most hospitals and clinics keep paper records (2025 study).
NAM.summary: The Ministry of Health and Social Services launched its Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS) in Windhoek in 2011. A study of September 2025 states that it was fully deployed only at Windhoek Central Hospital and Oshakati State Hospital. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, Namibia launched a National Digital Health Policy for 2026 to 2036. In March 2026 the minister said the system still faces paper-based records. No count of primary clinics keeping an electronic record has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

NER.short: Computerised patient records were set up in health centres and district hospitals in three districts (November 2024); no source found says how many centres.
NER.summary: The mid-term evaluation of November 2024 for Enabel states that the PASS Sutura project had set up digitalisation, including computerised medical records and billing in the integrated health centres (CSI) and district hospitals of Dioundiou, Gothèye and Gaya. In the last twelve months, the Directorate of e-Santé described OpenClinic, its project for a hospital information system and patient record. At the workshop of 8 July 2026 it presented it as already under way. No count of health centres using the record has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

NGA.short: 100 of Lagos State's 326 primary clinics record care electronically as it happens (May 2025); there is no national figure.
NGA.summary: On 22 May 2025 the Lagos State Ministry of Health reported the EMR platform deployed in 100 of the state's 326 primary health care facilities. In the last twelve months, the federal ministry issued the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture in December 2025. It sets interoperable electronic health record systems across all levels of care as its first pillar. On 16 September 2026 the minister of state for health said the electronic medical record systems deployed in health facilities are fragmented. No national share or count of primary clinics using an EMR has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping point-of-care records, each retrievable at another facility.

RWA.short: All 42 district hospitals used electronic patient records in 2023, and the national system reached most public facilities by 2026; shared records are not shown.
RWA.summary: A survey of 2023 found that 71 of 215 randomly sampled public health centres (33.0%) used one, an electronic medical record. In the last twelve months, Rwanda Biomedical Centre slides of April 2026 say eBuzima had been rolled out to the majority of public health facilities. In September 2026 Tom Frieden wrote that eBuzima is in more than two thirds of health centres. No unique patient identifier and no record retrieved at another facility has been established. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping point-of-care records, each retrievable at another facility.

SDN.short: A hospital system with electronic medical records was launched at two hospital sites on 11 May 2026; routine use is not yet shown.
SDN.summary: A thesis of March 2021 states that Sudan's hospitals had no electronic medical records and kept patients' records on paper. In the last twelve months, the Prime Minister in a directive of 30 March 2026 orders hospital systems digitised within two weeks. Phase one of the hospital management system started on 11 May 2026 at two hospital sites. No source shows whether the two sites are in routine use. None gives where the record is entered. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

SEN.short: The patient record runs only at pilot sites, in 1% of the 102 health centres (October 2025); health posts are not counted.
SEN.summary: The ministry states that its Dossier Patient Informatisé has been in use since November 2024 at the Thierno Birahim Ndao regional hospital in Kaffrine. The World Bank's results framework gives 1 per cent of the 102 district-level health centres as using electronic medical records at 31 October 2025. In the last twelve months, the World Bank recorded that a pilot of the record across 51 health centres had not started as of December 2025. Nothing found says whether the pilot began in 2026. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

SLE.short: Electronic records run at one government hospital and one clinic (2026); no source found reports a national system to have been bought.
SLE.summary: The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 commits the Government to roll out Electronic Medical Records to all medical facilities by 2030. It gives a baseline of 5 health facilities implementing the system. The OpenMRS case study of April 2026 states that the EMR has run at Wellbody Clinic since 2015. In the last twelve months, the Maternal Center of Excellence opened on 14 February 2026 with the EMR covering all its inpatient wards. On 18 December 2025 the Ministry's project unit asked firms to express interest in a national system. No contract for it has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

SOM.short: Two electronic record systems run in over 40 facilities (April 2026) and 111 primary facilities (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
SOM.summary: The Ministry of Health developed RAAD as a national electronic health record for primary healthcare, implemented between 2023 and 2025. Its case study reports RAAD deployed in 111 public primary healthcare facilities across six states between 2023 and 2025. The CaafimaadPlus consortium said in April 2026 that its Caafimaad+ Digitalized Data System is operational in over 40 facilities. In the last twelve months, the consortium reports growth from a five-facility pilot in mid-2024 to over 40 facilities by April 2026. No count of all primary clinics has been found for either system. No unique patient identifier is stated. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each under a unique patient identifier and retrievable at another facility.

SSD.short: A decision support tool recorded patient visits at 12 facilities in 2026; no source found says how many are primary clinics, and who owns it,.
SSD.summary: In September 2026 WHO counted 12 facilities in 10 states and administrative areas logging visits on the Digital Care Companion, a clinical decision support system. The series names Lafon PHCC, a primary health care centre, among the facilities using the Digital Care Companion. In the last twelve months, UNDP South Sudan issued a tender on 11 March 2026 for an OpenMRS pilot at two Juba facilities. The 2019 record at Juba Teaching Hospital and Nimule Hospital did not reach routine clinical use. No count of primary clinics using electronic records has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

STP.short: A patient record was piloted at the central hospital and in one health area in 2022; no source found says whether it was extended.
STP.summary: The National Health Development Plan 2023-2032, dated September 2022, sets a strategic axis on expanding what it calls the single clinical process to the whole national health system. The Joint SDG Fund programme's final report of 26 July 2022 states that the Single Process module for patient files was developed inside DHIS2. At that date the Single Process had not been rolled out to other districts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No evaluation of the pilot and no count of facilities using it has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

SWZ.short: A shared electronic record runs in 73% of all health facilities (2026); with no figure for primary clinics alone, it stays at stage 3.
SWZ.summary: Data.FI said in April 2026 that CMIS is used in 73% of the country's health facilities, with 233 live sites. For the period ending March 2024 it reported CMIS in use at 75% (247 of 327) of healthcare facilities. In the last twelve months, the US State Department said in May 2026 that it is working to transfer CMIS's ownership and management to the government. In October 2026 the ministry's HMIS programme was named lead for the health information systems. In November 2026 Nhlangano's staff got iPads to record inpatient care at the point of care. Both shares count all facilities. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, counted for primary clinics alone.

SYC.short: A ministry system with electronic medical records has run since the end of 2021; no source found says whether clinics record on it or on paper.
SYC.summary: On 17 October 2023 the health minister said the Ministry of Health is investing in an Electronic Health Information System encompassing Electronic Medical Records. The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 sets specific objective 6.8, "Implement eHIS". In June 2023 the Health Care Agency's chief executive said some doctors still use handwritten notes. The agency said it was training doctors to use the electronic medical records clinic by clinic. A ministry press release of January 2024 states that the system has been operational since the end of 2021. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count of clinics using it has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

TCD.short: The ministry signed a partnership for electronic medical records in its hospitals (reported August 2026); no facility is yet shown using one.
TCD.summary: In the last twelve months, on 15 April 2026 the ministry's Secretary-General chaired a high-level meeting devoted to modernising the patient medical record. HISP Rwanda states that the Ministry of Public Health and Prevention leads the electronic medical record initiative. Guinéenews reported on 13 August 2026 a partnership for the national digitalisation of the country's hospitals with the Visa Medical digital medical record. Kouma Academy had signed its partnership with the ministry by that date. No pilot site, budget, timetable or count of facilities using electronic records has been found. Establishing would need electronic records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

TGO.short: The World Bank reported in December 2025 that no electronic health record system was in place.
TGO.summary: The World Bank's additional-financing paper of 24 December 2025 records "No" at December 2025 for the establishment of an electronic health record system. Its results framework gives a baseline of 0 facilities contracted with the national health insurance scheme holding an EHR at December 2025. In the last twelve months, on 24 December 2025 the World Bank put forward additional financing, a EUR 60.6 million credit and US$11 million in grants. The work starts with a pilot. No source found says records are digital in any facility outside the insurance scheme. Preparing would need electronic records in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system procured or being prepared.

TUN.short: Electronic records are fully used in 50% of university hospitals and 32% of regional hospitals (2025), with pilot sites in one region's primary care.
TUN.summary: The World Bank's project document of 2 April 2025 gives the record as fully installed and used in 50 per cent of university hospitals and fully operational in 32 per cent of regional hospitals. In district hospitals it is neither installed nor used. In the last twelve months, in April 2026 the Director General of Health announced the record's generalisation in most public hospitals. No count of hospitals was given. On 25 September 2026 the ministry's account gave 99 healthcare facilities at various stages of implementing electronic medical records. Establishing would need electronic records in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

TZA.short: Electronic records reached over 67% of dispensaries and all regional hospitals in 2026; records are not shown to be shared between facilities.
TZA.summary: The mid-term review of Health Sector Strategic Plan V, of March 2025, states that all 28 regional hospitals use Afya eHMS. It cites the SARA survey of 2023, which gives 23.25% of all health facilities using GOT-HoMIS, against 44.9% of health centres and 10.63% of dispensaries. In the last twelve months, on 30 September 2026 the deputy health minister put electronic patient records in over 67% of dispensaries. The integrated records system was introduced in October 2025, and in October 2026 the ministry said it now connects 222 public facilities. No source found shows a record retrievable at another facility. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.
