UGA.short: The ministry's electronic record ran in referral and general hospitals and seven health centres in 2025; records are not shown to be shared.
UGA.summary: The Ministry of Health says that in 2025 the EMR ran in referral and general hospitals and some health centres. It counts 5 Health Centre IVs and 2 Health Centre IIIs using the EMR in 2025. A census of all 265 government HC IVs and hospitals, published in October 2025, found 94.3% keeping both paper and digital records. In the last twelve months, on 31 March 2026 Makerere University's METS programme handed the UgandaEMR repositories to the ministry. In September 2026 staff in Kiryandongo said the EMR slowed care for want of connectivity, power and computers. Nothing found shows a record retrievable at another facility. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

ZAF.short: Hospital systems run in five provinces and 308 Western Cape primary facilities use electronic records (2025); the national system is in beta, count not known.
ZAF.summary: The Minister of Health told Parliament on 1 August 2025 that the National Department of Health is developing a single common Electronic Medical Record for primary health care facilities. The reply states that the National EMR beta ran in 36 primary health care facilities in late 2024 and early 2025. In the last twelve months, in March 2026 the department invited bids to scale up its EMR to all fixed primary health care facilities in eight provinces. In June 2026 the Minister said beta testing continues and a rollout training tender was advertised. Nothing found shows a record retrievable at another facility. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

ZMB.short: An electronic record system was in use at 877 of 3,540 health facilities of all kinds (April 2025); the share of primary clinics is unknown.
ZMB.summary: At April 2025 the Global Fund states that SmartCare Pro is in use at 877 health facilities, out of 3,540 in the country. In January 2026 the implementers described a nurse at a rural clinic in Kafulafuta identifying a patient by fingerprint to reach his record. In the last twelve months, SmartCare 2.0 Hospital Edition went live as a pilot at Ndola Teaching Hospital on 27 April 2026. On 7 July 2026 SMART Zambia's national coordinator said SmartCare Pro has been deployed in approximately 80% of health facilities nationwide. The 2026 figures give no count for primary clinics. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

ZWE.short: An electronic record system ran in 1,254 health facilities of all types in August 2025, out of 1,900 planned; shared records are not shown.
ZWE.summary: The Global Fund said in August 2025 that the Government of Zimbabwe has been developing a national EMR system since February 2015. It reports 1,254 health facilities implementing Impilo as of August 2025, with deployment planned for all 1,900 health facilities. On 17 November 2024 the Permanent Secretary put deployment at 1,178 health facilities. In the last twelve months, the Herald on 23 September 2026 described Impilo as the Ministry of Health's own electronic health records platform. The counts cover facilities of all types, not primary clinics alone. No record retrievable at another facility has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

AGO.short: Links between DHIS2 and the vaccination and medicines systems were being built in 2026; none is reported in routine use.
AGO.summary: In December 2025 hospital directors said Angola's hospitals have no integrated information system and share no patient data. In the last twelve months, the Secretary of State for Health said in February 2026 that Angola is making the ReDIV and IOTA systems interoperable with DHIS2. After a March 2026 mission, the ministry, WHO, HISP UiO and Saudigitus agreed to improve DHIS2's link with the eLMIS. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use.

BDI.short: Three HIV programme systems exchanged data in routine use in 2026; no source found reports a national patient identifier linking records.
BDI.summary: In June 2026 OpenFn said its workflows automatically exchange HIV programme data between SIDAInfo, IBIPIMO and DHIS2, on a server the health ministry manages. In the last twelve months, the position changed. In April 2026 the ministry said DHIS2, SIDAInfo and OpenClinic did not really communicate, causing duplication, and by June 2026 OpenFn reported three systems exchanging data in production. No source found since October 2023 says patient records are linked through the national ID or a national health identifier. Mature would need patient records linked across systems through the national ID or a national unique health identifier.

BEN.short: Nothing found names health systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names health systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

BFA.short: A roadmap to link community health data with DHIS2 was drafted in 2025; no health systems exchanging data are reported.
BFA.summary: In September 2025 Living Goods and partners said community health worker data are not linked to the national DHIS2. The ministry drew up a roadmap with Africa CDC, Living Goods and UNICEF to give that link priority. It still had to be finalised, approved and funded. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

BWA.short: A national health information exchange was being implemented in 2026; no two health systems are reported exchanging data in routine use.
BWA.summary: In March 2026 the health ministry said the Health Information Exchange is being implemented. In November 2025 a minister told Parliament that four patient and data systems are active but not linked across facilities. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the World Bank approved US$13.1 million to link the electronic record, disease surveillance and registries to the exchange. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use.

CAF.short: A hospital record system sent clinical data to the national DHIS2 in 2026; no third system exchanging data is reported.
CAF.summary: HISP Rwanda said in March 2026 that the e-SENI hospital record system sends its clinical data automatically to the national health information systems. The data go into platforms built on DHIS2. In the last twelve months, that account is the only exchange found, and no earlier dated position has been found. No source found says three or more health systems exchange data. Operating would need three or more health systems exchanging data, or a national health information exchange in service that no source shows linking fewer than three.

CIV.short: A community health platform sent data to the national DHIS2 in 2025; no third system exchanging data is reported.
CIV.summary: In September 2025 mHealth Africa said its community platform sends data to the national DHIS2, SIGSANTE, automatically. In June 2023 the surveillance tools DHIS2, MAGPI and SORMAS were found not to exchange data with each other. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the health ministry said it is setting up a national platform for its health information systems to exchange data. No source found since November 2023 says three or more health systems exchange data. Operating would need three or more health systems exchanging data, or a national exchange in service.

CMR.short: A national platform linked the health insurance enrolment and billing systems in 2026; a third system connected is not found.
CMR.summary: The health ministry said in November 2026 that a national interoperability platform is in use. It links the enrolment and billing systems of universal health coverage. In the last twelve months, that platform is the only exchange found, and no earlier dated position has been found. The ministry said at a workshop of 27 to 31 October 2026 that not all systems are yet connected to the platform. No source found since October 2023 says three or more health systems exchange data. Operating would need three or more health systems exchanging data, or a national health information exchange in service that no source shows linking fewer than three.

COD.short: A national health data centre to link existing systems was put out to tender in 2026; no exchange in service is reported.
COD.summary: In June 2026 ANICNS, under the health ministry, called for expressions of interest in a national health data centre. The centre is to gather national health data and link existing systems. The call closed on 12 July 2026. In the last twelve months, that call is the only change found, and no earlier dated position has been found. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

COG.short: Nothing found names health systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COG.summary: Not found. Nothing found names health systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

COM.short: DHIS2 worked with the vaccination register and medicines system in 2026; no source found says whether three systems exchange data.
COM.summary: On 27 October 2026 the health ministry's statistics directorate said other applications are integrated into DHIS2 or work with it. It named the electronic vaccination register and the system for managing medicines and supplies. In the last twelve months, that statement is the only position found, and no earlier dated position has been found. The same meeting named interoperability of tools among the main challenges still ahead. No source says whether the vaccination register and the medicines system are modules of DHIS2 or separate systems. Operating would need three or more health systems exchanging data, or a national health information exchange in service.

CPV.short: A laboratory system linked to DHIS2 and a unique patient code were being prepared in 2026; no exchange between health systems in service is reported.
CPV.summary: In April 2026 the health ministry sought a consultancy for a laboratory system for 20 public laboratories. It must link with DHIS2, existing laboratory systems, the health information system and surveillance. In December 2025 the health minister said a unique patient code, digital records and e-prescriptions are being advanced. In the last twelve months, no earlier dated position has been found for either plan. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

DJI.short: Nothing found names health systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names health systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

DZA.short: A national platform for patients' medical records was set up in 2026; no source names two health systems exchanging data through it.
DZA.summary: On 11 April 2026 the health minister said a digital platform for following patients' medical records had recently been set up. It is meant to speed the exchange of information between health structures across the country. The minister gave no figures and named no connected structures. In the last twelve months, that statement is the only position found, and no earlier dated position has been found. No source found names two health systems exchanging data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

EGY.short: A health information exchange was being activated in 2026; no source found shows two health systems exchanging data in routine use.
EGY.summary: In June 2025 the ministry signed with eHealth to operate the National Digital Health System. In the last twelve months, on 30 September 2026 the deputy health minister met Vodafone, the communications ministry and the insurance authority on digital integration, and the ministry stressed activating the health information exchange. In September 2026 it proposed a smart healthcare platform to share patient histories between facilities. No source found names two health systems exchanging data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use.

ERI.short: Nothing found names health systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names health systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Health partners chose a medical record pilot to test interoperability in 2026; over 70 health platforms still worked apart.
ETH.summary: In March 2026 DIAL reported that health stakeholders chose a multi-tenant medical record pilot as the next step to test interoperability. No launch date was given. In the last twelve months, that pilot is the only change found, and no earlier dated position has been found. DIAL says Ethiopia's digital health sector has more than 70 siloed platforms. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

GAB.short: The DHIS2 Tracker was being rolled out to health districts in 2026, but it is part of DHIS2, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: No stage is set. Gabon began rolling out the DHIS2 Tracker from 2026, and it is part of the national DHIS2. No source found names two separate health systems exchanging data. No change in exchange between separate systems has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need an exchange between health systems that is contracted, being built or piloted, or a health information exchange being set up.

GHA.short: A national health information exchange was being set up in 2024; no two health systems are reported exchanging data in routine use.
GHA.summary: In November 2024 the health ministry's head of research said the Ghana Health Information Exchange sought to link systems for real-time data sharing. He named limited interoperability as the main obstacle. No change to the exchange has been found in the last twelve months. In August 2026 the Ghana Health Service launched an emergency operations centre with integrated dashboards. No source found says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

GIN.short: A hospital system able to link with DHIS2 ran in five facilities in 2026; data exchanged between them in routine use is not shown.
GIN.summary: A health ministry mission in August 2026 found OpenClinic in five facilities of Mamou and Dalaba. The hospital system offers interoperability with the national DHIS2. Paper reporting to the national health information system continues alongside it. In the last twelve months, in November 2025, a Conakry workshop trained staff on interoperability and mapped the sector's digital tools. No source found says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

GMB.short: The health and education ministries agreed in 2026 to link their information systems; no health systems exchanging data in service are reported.
GMB.summary: In July 2026 the health and education ministries signed a memorandum to link the HMIS with the education system. A joint working group was set up. In the last twelve months, that memorandum followed a World Bank report of November 2025 that counted none of four systems interoperable, the health insurance system among them. No source found since November 2023 says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

GNB.short: A national data platform drew on several DHIS2 instances and programme systems in 2026; no identifier matching patients is reported.
GNB.summary: In August 2026 Zenysis said the national data platform NIA integrates data from several DHIS2 instances. It also draws on programme systems and partner datasets. In the last twelve months, that account is the only change found, and no earlier dated position has been found. The only account of NIA found is the vendor's, given when Zenysis and the ministry signed a five-year memorandum in August 2026. Mature would need patient records linked across systems through the national ID or a national unique health identifier.

GNQ.short: Nothing found names health systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names health systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

KEN.short: A national health information exchange was in service across insurance-contracted facilities in 2025; no source found says whether records are matched by a national identifier.
KEN.summary: In August 2025 the ministry launched a health information exchange for hospitals, counties and national systems. The ministry said in January 2025 that the national exchange, with its client, provider and facility registries, was fully deployed by December 2024. A legal notice in force from 11 April 2025 sets up a service bus routing messages between certified health systems. No change to the exchange has been found in the last twelve months. In August 2026 the Cabinet Secretary said a Safaricom consortium is building the national system for insurance registration and claims. No source found says patient records are linked by the national ID or the biometric health identifier. Mature would need patient records linked across systems through the national ID or a national unique health identifier.

LBR.short: Liberia joined a regional pilot in 2026 to send routine health data automatically from its DHIS2; no exchange in routine use is reported.
LBR.summary: In March 2026 Liberia was one of four pilot countries for automated transfer of routine data from national DHIS2 systems. The West African Health Organisation runs the pilot. Its first phase is to design and test a secure architecture for the transfer. In the last twelve months, that pilot is the only change found, and no earlier dated position has been found. No source found says two health systems exchange data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use, such as the HMIS with patient records, a laboratory or a supply-chain system.

LBY.short: A medicines tracking system linked the pharmacy department, the supply agency and hospital pharmacies in 2025; it is one system, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: No stage is set. The health ministry's health information centre page names DHIS2. No source found names two health systems exchanging data. The medicines tracking system activated in 2025 is one system used by several bodies. No change in exchange between separate systems has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need an exchange between health systems that is contracted, being built or piloted, or a health information exchange being set up.

LSO.short: The national medical record system fed DHIS2 by 2025; no source found shows three health systems exchanging data.
LSO.summary: A 2025 study says the health ministry's eRegister medical record is integrated with the national DHIS2. The eRegister has been in use since 2018. WHO said Lesotho advanced interoperability across its HMIS, workforce, logistics and surveillance platforms in 2025. MAR.short: A law and a shared patient record linking health systems were being prepared in 2026; no source found reports systems exchanging data in routine use.

In the last twelve months, that piece is the only change found, and no earlier dated position has been found. No source found names two health systems exchanging data in routine use. MOZ.short: A laboratory system sent viral load results to patient records in over 500 facilities in 2025; no wider exchange is reported.

In the last twelve months, the layer went from installation to use with four systems. Before that, in July 2025 Bluesquare helped the e-health directorate install the OpenHEXA platform on ministry servers. No source found says patient records are linked through the national ID or a national health identifier. Mature would need patient records linked across systems through the national ID or a national unique health identifier.

No source found names two health systems exchanging data in routine use. Establishing would need two or more health systems exchanging data in routine use.

In the last twelve months, a Global Fund case study of January 2026 says the laboratory systems, the HMIS and the reagent system are interoperable. M-KOPA's Nairobi factory, opened with HMD in January 2023, had made over 1.5 million phones by November 2024. No change in the export figure has been found in the last twelve months. In August 2026 the Universal Service Advisory Council noted progress at the JKUAT Device Assembly Plant.

AGO.short: Angola adopted its ICT white paper for 2023-2027 by presidential decree in December 2024; no source found says whether its text is public.
AGO.summary: The Livro Branco das TIC 2023-2027 was approved by Presidential Decree 272/24 of 5 December 2024. The approval repealed the Livro Branco das TIC 2019-2022. In the last twelve months, a March 2026 article cited the policy as setting plans for a space studies centre and expert training. It was cited and not changed. The ministry's site carries only Presidential Order 129/19 of 22 July 2019, with a download link, which approved the earlier white paper. No source found says whether the 2023-2027 text is public. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public.

BDI.short: The ICT development policy ran to 2025; no source found reports a successor for 2025-2034 was put out to consultants in 2023, and its adoption.
BDI.summary: In November 2023 the project PAFEN called for consultants to evaluate the national ICT development policy and draft a new one for 2025-2034. The policy it would replace was adopted by the Council of Ministers on 13 July 2011 and ran from 2010 to 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source says the 2025-2034 policy has been drafted, validated or adopted, and no text of it is known. Establishing would need a sector policy that is adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

BEN.short: A digital economy sector policy declaration adopted in 2016 ran to 2021; no source found says whether a successor exists, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: No stage is set. The Déclaration de politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique ran to 2021. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on a mandated body, finance or a report against the policy's targets. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption, or a successor in preparation now that the period has ended.

No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether a successor sector policy has been announced, drafted, validated or adopted. Nothing has been found on a delivery plan, reporting or finance for the 2016-2020 policy. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A report of December 2025 refers to it as Botswana's existing policy. Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan or a report against its targets. No source of finance has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's own targets.

No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

No text, report against it, responsible body or budget line has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

A Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030 was also found, and no source found says whether it succeeds the 2009 policy. Nothing has been found on the 2009 text, the cost of its targets, reporting, governance or finance. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy in preparation.

COG.summary: The government drew up its national ICT development policy in 2008-2009, the minister told the Council of Ministers on 6 March 2019. An appraisal document of 4 May 2011 treats the National ICT Policy as existing. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether the policy's text was published, when and by what act it was adopted, or what period it covers. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

COM.short: A telecommunications and digital sector policy, which the minister said in 2022 was being implemented; no source found reports its text and adoption date.

The ministry's mission page, dated to 2016, names the new sector policy beside the Comores numérique strategy. Nothing on the policy is dated after September 2022, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. No text, adoption date, period, delivery plan or report against it has been found. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

The Schéma stratégique intégré, approved by a law published in February 2015, covered the sector before it and ran for ten years, from 2014 to 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No text of the new policy has been found, and nothing gives its adoption date, period, costs or budget line. Establishing would need the policy's text to be public and its period not ended.

No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

The same paper states that no National ICT Development Plan exists. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing later confirms or contradicts the paper. Nothing has been found on governance or finance. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

ETH.summary: Ethiopia's National ICT Policy and Strategy was developed in 2016 and endorsed by the Council of Ministers in 2017, with financial support from the World Bank for the 2017 revision. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest dated account, from September 2021, has the policy still being implemented. No source found says whether the policy's text is published or what period it covers. Establishing would need the text to be public and the period not ended.

GAB.short: Gabon had formulated a national ICT policy by 2022, a JICA study says; no source found reports its adoption date, text and period.
GAB.summary: A JICA baseline study of public service digitalisation in African countries was published in March 2022. It states that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy, the Politique nationale des TIC, consistent with the PSGE Vision 2025, and gives no date of adoption. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing on the policy is dated since. The policy's text, period, delivery plan, reporting, mandated body and finance have not been found. Establishing would need an adopted policy with its text public and its period not ended.

GHA.short: Ghana's telecommunications policy of 2005 is in force with no end date; no source found says whether it reports against its targets.
GHA.summary: The Ministry of Communications released the National Telecommunications Policy as final on 10 January 2005, and the full 33-page text is on the National Communications Authority's website. The policy states no end date for itself. A report published on 8 October 2025 recommends updating it and the ICT for Accelerated Development Policy of 2003. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report against the policy's targets, no cost for its actions and no source of finance has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the policy's own targets.

GIN.short: Drafting of a telecommunications policy for 2026-2030 began in July 2026; no adopted sector policy is in force.
GIN.summary: In June 2024 the national digitalisation strategy announced a digital sector policy letter and lists it as a document still to be drafted. In the last twelve months, on 9 July 2026, the digital economy ministry opened a national workshop to draft a telecommunications policy, strategy and action plan, with support from the World Bank's WARDIP project. The policy is to cover 2026 to 2030. The government adopted an ICT policy and strategy in 2010. No source says the new policy has been validated or adopted. Establishing would need it adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

The presentation lists the statement among the country's existing policies, strategies and legal frameworks. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in October 2026 a Principal Assistant Secretary at the ministry named it among The Gambia's ICT policies. No source found links or quotes its text, and none says it is unpublished. Nothing has been found on a delivery plan, a mandated body or finance. Establishing would need the text to be public.

GNB.summary: An ICT strategy was in preparation in Guinea-Bissau in December 2021, when the regulator, ARN, issued a preliminary report on it. The Guinea-Bissau Digital Economy Diagnostic, published in 2022, takes data from the regulator's preliminary ICT strategy report. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated since shows whether drafting continued. No source says the strategy was adopted. No text, period, delivery plan, responsible body or finance has been found. Establishing would need a sector policy that is adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

GNQ.short: No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found; no source found says whether one is adopted or in preparation, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: No stage is set. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found for Equatorial Guinea as adopted or in preparation. No dated statement that the country has none has been found. Nothing has been found on a mandated body, finance, a delivery plan or a report. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

KEN.short: Kenya has a national ICT policy adopted in 2019 and gazetted in 2020; no source found reports its period, delivery plan and reporting.
KEN.summary: Kenya's ICT Sector Policy Guidelines 2006 were reviewed and updated to a National ICT Policy in 2019. The policy was gazetted in 2020 as Gazette Notice No. 5472. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. An analysis of July 2026 names the ICT policy among Kenya's existing instruments. A Communications Authority consultation of September 2026 says the policy directs government agencies to promote and license private investment in carrier-neutral data centres. Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan or a domestic budget line. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's own targets.

LBR.short: Liberia's ICT policy, adopted in 2019, ran out in 2025 and a 2025-2030 successor is in draft; no source says when it will be adopted.
LBR.summary: Liberia's government adopted the policy in 2019, and the full text is on the ministry's website. It was extended to 2025, and the ministry's draft of its successor, dated 7 January 2025, lists it as expired. In the last twelve months, the national digital strategy of 3 February 2026 said the successor has been drafted and is in consultation, with approval targeted for the last quarter of 2025. A press release of 8 September 2026 lists a draft National ICT Policy. No adoption of the National ICT Policy 2025-2030 is on record. Establishing would need an adopted policy whose period has not ended.

LBY.short: Libya has a telecommunications and informatics strategy for 2023 to 2027, in use in 2025; no source found says whether its text is published.
LBY.summary: In October 2025 the General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GACI) announced root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi. It presented them as implementing the National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027. In the last twelve months, on 15 February 2026, GACI held a workshop in Tripoli. There officials stated the aim of drafting legislation and a guidance manual for data centres and cloud computing. No text of the strategy has been found, and no source says whether it is published. No adopting act, delivery plan or budget line has been found. Establishing would need the strategy's text to be public.

LSO.short: Lesotho has a communications policy adopted in 2008 with no end year; no source found reports its delivery plan and reporting.
LSO.summary: The government adopted the policy in 2008, and the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology published the full text. The Lesotho Communications Policy states no end year or review date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A 2025 tender notice says the ministry will review the policy with the authority. No delivery plan and no report against the 2008 policy has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the policy's own targets.

MAR.short: A telecommunications sector policy note adopted in 2019 ran to 2023; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
MAR.summary: No stage is set. The Note d'orientations générales du secteur des télécommunications à horizon 2023 was adopted on 26 December 2019 and ran to 2023. No successor note has been found as adopted or in preparation. No report against its targets and no finance for it has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

MDG.short: A national ICT for development policy dates from 2004, with targets assessed in 2022; no source says whether its text is public or still open.
MDG.summary: The MPTDN formulated the Politique nationale des TIC pour le développement in 2004 with support from UNDP. A JICA study of March 2022 describes it as the Malagasy government's main ICT policy, and found that legal and regulatory reform was relatively advanced. Its targets run to 2015 for the digital network. No change has been found in the last twelve months; the latest account is JICA's. The policy's text, an act adopting it and a stated period have not been found, so no source says whether it is still open. Establishing would need its text to be public and its period not ended.

MLI.short: A national ICT policy was adopted in 2005; no source found says whether its text is public and what period it covers.
MLI.summary: The Government adopted the national information and communication technology policy in 2005, after adopting the Déclaration de politique sectorielle des télécommunications in 2000. The strategy Mali Numérique 2020, of November 2014, sets out the 2005 policy's six priorities. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No text of the 2005 policy has been found, and no source says it is unpublished. No period, delivery plan, results report, mandated body or budget line has been found. Establishing would need the text to be public.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's Information Society Policy was adopted in 2018 with no end date; no source found says whether results against its targets are reported.
MOZ.summary: The Council of Ministers approved the Política para a Sociedade da Informação on 20 March 2018 by Resolution 17/2018, in force from 21 June 2018. The full text is printed in the Boletim da República, I Série, no. 122, of 21 June 2018. The policy states no end date and no review year. In April 2026 Mozambique told a UNCTAD ministerial roundtable that the policy aims at widespread adoption of ICT. The statement names no change to it, so it was cited and not changed in the last twelve months. No report against the policy's own targets has been found. Operating would need results published against those targets.

MRT.short: A sector policy declaration was adopted in January 2013; no source found says whether its text is public and whether it is still in force.
MRT.summary: The ministry's presentation of April 2019 states that a new sector policy declaration was adopted in January 2013. It gives the declaration's four pillars. Nothing on the declaration is dated after April 2019, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. Its text has not been found. Nothing gives its period, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body or a budget line. Establishing would need the text to be public and the period not ended.

MUS.short: A national ICT policy issued in 2007 ran to 2011; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: No stage is set. The National ICT Policy 2007-11 was issued in September 2007 and ended in 2011. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. The National ICT Strategic Plan it relies on has not been found. No report against the policy has been found, and no change in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

MWI.short: Malawi has a National ICT Policy dated 2013 with its text public; no source found says whether the 2022 draft policy was adopted.
MWI.summary: Malawi's National ICT Policy 2013 is listed in the policy framework of a 2025 management plan for the government data centre. An essay of March 2026 links a copy of the 2013 policy's text in the ITU national strategies repository. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A GSMA report of August 2026 lists the National ICT Policy 2013 among prior policies. The Presidential Delivery Unit produced a draft National ICT and Digitalization Policy in 2022. No source says it was adopted. No delivery plan of the 2013 policy has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's targets.

NAM.short: Namibia launched a national ICT policy in January 2026; no source found reports its text, end year, delivery plan and budget.
NAM.summary: In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the Ministry of ICT launched the policy at Opuwo, and the minister said it would guide the ICT sector over the next five years. It follows the Overarching ICT Policy 2009 and the earlier National ICT Policy / Broadband Policy, to which the ITU's repository gives a time frame of 2018 to 2022. The text of the National ICT Policy 2026 has not been found, and its period has no end year. No delivery plan, report against it or budget line is on record. Establishing would need the text to be public.

NER.short: A telecommunications and ICT sector policy was adopted in 2013 and ended in 2020; no successor sector policy is known, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: No stage is set. The Document de politique sectorielle des télécommunications et des TIC 2013-2020 ended in 2020. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation, and an update instructed in July 2017 has not been found. The Politique nationale du numérique 2021-2030 was also found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on the policy's text, a mandated body or its finance. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

NGA.short: Nigeria's telecommunications policy of 2000 is still in force and is being rewritten in 2026; no source reports its finance and reporting against its targets.
NGA.summary: The Minister of Communications' preface of May 2000 presents the policy as approved by the President, and the Ministry published the full text. On 9 February 2026 the Nigerian Communications Commission's consultation paper calls it the subsisting sector policy. In the last twelve months the Commission published fifteen proposals for rewriting the policy, and in May 2026 held a review workshop. The rewrite is still being drafted. No report against the policy's own targets has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against those targets.

RWA.short: Rwanda has an ICT sector plan for 2024-2029, released in August 2024; no source found says whether results against it have been reported.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029 covers the financial years 2024/25 to 2028/29. The ministry published the plan, dated 1 January 2025 on its cover, as one it is committed to implement, and JICA says the government released it on 10 August 2024. In the last twelve months, after a cabinet briefing on 24 July 2026, the ministry set 30 June 2027 as the date 3G is switched off nationwide, as part of the plan. No report against the 2024-2029 plan's own targets has been found. Operating would need results published against those targets, within the past three years.

SDN.short: The National ICT Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. The National ICT Strategy 2021-2025 ran to 2025. Nothing found records a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting or validated. No text, delivery plan or date of adoption has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A Quarter century plan 2007-2031 was also found. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

SEN.short: Senegal validated a sector policy letter for 2025-2029 in February 2025; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
SEN.summary: In February 2025 the ministry's secretary general chaired the final validation workshop for the Lettre de politique sectorielle 2025-2029, which covers 2025 to 2029. In the last twelve months, terms of reference of July 2026 state that the ministry has validated the letter. No adoption of the letter is on record. Its text, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body and a budget line have not been found. Establishing would need the letter adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

SLE.short: The 2009 ICT policy, reviewed in 2017, was replaced in 2021 by a national digital policy; no successor is known, so no stage is set.
SLE.summary: No stage is set. Sierra Leone's National ICT Policy was approved on 28 October 2009 and reviewed in 2017. The National Digital Development Policy 2021 replaced it in 2021. No sector successor has been found as adopted or in preparation. No report against the 2009 policy and no budget line for it have been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

SOM.short: A National ICT Policy and Strategy for 2025-2029 was reported approved in 2025; no source found says whether its text is published.
SOM.summary: The Cabinet adopted the previous policy on 28 November 2019 for 2019 to 2024. On 9 July 2025 the minister said the Council of Ministers approved the National ICT Policy earlier in 2025. In the last twelve months, a ministry notice of 11 November 2025 seeks a firm to renew the 2019-2024 policy as a 2025-2029 one, and expressions of interest were due on 29 November 2025. The two statements differ on whether the new policy is approved or still to be written. No text of the 2025-2029 policy has been found. Establishing would need it adopted, with its text public and its period not ended.

SSD.short: A national ICT policy published in 2012 is public and was said in 2025 to be in implementation; its period, plan and results are unknown.
SSD.summary: The Government of South Sudan published its National ICT Policy in 2012, and the policy text is public on the ICT Policy Africa document page. On 12 June 2025 the minister said the government is implementing the revised ICT Policy of 2012. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The policy's period, a delivery plan, a mandated body, a budget line and any report against its own targets have not been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against those targets.

STP.short: An ICT sector strategy prepared in 2012 still awaited adoption in 2015; no source found says whether it was adopted, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: No stage is set. The ICT sector strategy prepared in 2012 was last recorded in June 2015, still awaiting adoption by the Council of Ministers. Nothing since shows it adopted, in preparation or replaced. Its text, period, delivery plan and reporting have not been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has an ICT infrastructure policy adopted in 2006 with no end year; no source found reports its delivery plan and reporting.
SWZ.summary: Cabinet adopted the National Information and Communication Infrastructure (NICI) Policy in August 2006, and the government site gov.sz hosts the policy as a PDF, in one file with its Implementation Plan 2012-2016. The Prime Minister launched the policy on 3 August 2007. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No period of the policy's own has been found; the only one on record, to 2016, is the Implementation Plan's. No report against the policy has been found. Operating would need an adopted delivery plan, and published results against the policy's own targets.

SYC.short: Seychelles has a National ICT Policy from 2007 with its text public; no source found says whether it has a delivery plan or reports results.
SYC.summary: Seychelles has a National ICT Policy, recorded as published in 2007, whose full text is on the SCRA website as a PDF. It states no end year or period. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: a World Bank report of September 2026 treats it as in force and gives no adoption date or scope. No delivery plan and no report against the policy has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the policy's own targets.

TCD.short: A sector ICT plan adopted in 2017 ended in 2021; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: No stage is set. The newest sector plan found is the Plan Tchad Numérique 2017-2021, and no sector policy has been found following it, adopted or in preparation. The Plan stratégique de développement du numérique et des postes 2020-2030 was also found. No text, delivery plan, report, mandated body or finance has been found for that plan, the NICI plan 2007-2027 or the 1997 sector policy declaration. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

TGO.short: A digital economy sector policy declaration of 2017 ran to 2022; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: No stage is set. The Déclaration de politique du secteur de l'économie numérique 2018-2022 was adopted in October 2017, and its period ended in 2022. No successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. Its text, delivery plan and finance have not been found, nor any report against it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a successor sector policy that is announced, in drafting, or validated and awaiting adoption.

TUN.short: Tunisia has a national digital strategy but no ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: No stage is set. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found for Tunisia as adopted or in preparation. The instruments found are national digital strategies such as the National Digital Strategic Plan (Digital Tunisia), a ministry's Annual performance project (PAP) 2025 of the Communication Technologies mission and a programme. None of them is a sector policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a sector policy that is announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

TZA.short: Tanzania adopted its National ICT Policy in 2016 and a costed strategy ran to 2020/21; no source found says whether the 2023 review was adopted.
TZA.summary: The National ICT Policy 2016 was signed by the Minister for Works, Transport and Communication in May 2016, and its full text is published as a PDF on the ministry's website. Its implementation strategy covers 2016/17 to 2020/21. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in August 2026 the ICT Commission's director general described the 2016 policy as the one that followed the 2003 policy. The ministry issued a successor text dated June 2023, which states no adoption date. No report of results against the 2016 targets has been found. Operating would need such results to be published.

UGA.short: Uganda has a National ICT Policy of 2014, with a replacement drafted in 2022; no source found says whether the 2014 text is public.
UGA.summary: The Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040, dated September 2022, lists the National ICT Policy 2014 among Uganda's key policies, as being reviewed. The ministry's report of June 2022 says drafting of the replacement was complete and awaiting Cabinet approval. In the last twelve months, NITA-U's terms of reference of August 2026 cite a "Draft National ICT Policy, 2022". No text of the 2014 policy has been found, and no adoption of the 2022 draft is on record. Establishing would need an adopted policy with its text public and its period not ended.

ZAF.short: South Africa adopted an ICT policy white paper in 2016, and no source says whether it has a delivery plan or reports against its targets.
ZAF.summary: The department issued the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper in Government Gazette 40325 of 3 October 2016. Its stated purpose is to use ICTs to eliminate poverty and reduce inequality by 2030. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: a World Bank report of June 2026 lists it among the anchors of South Africa's policy framework. No delivery plan for the White Paper has been found, and no report against its own targets. Operating would need both, with a report published within three years.

ZMB.short: Zambia has a National ICT Policy published in 2023 with no end year; no source found says whether results against it have been reported.
ZMB.summary: The Ministry of Technology and Science published the policy on 11 October 2023, and the full text is on the ministry's website as a PDF. The policy states no end year. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in December 2025 the policy working group of an ITU event in Lusaka recognised the policy as Zambia's overarching ICT framework. No report, review or evaluation against the policy's targets has been found. Operating would need results published against those targets.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has a public National ICT Policy for 2022 to 2027 with an uncosted action plan; no source found reports results against its targets.
ZWE.summary: The National ICT Policy titles itself for 2022 to 2027, and the full text of the policy, published in 2022, is public. The ICT minister launched it on 7 March 2024. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: Cabinet named the policy on 14 July 2026, and on 20 July 2026 the head of the statistics agency referred to an ICT Policy for 2026 to 2030. No report against the policy's targets has been found. Operating would need results published against those targets, and a costed delivery plan.

AGO.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2025.
AGO.summary: In 2024 the government's strategic plan for universal identity cards put holders of the Bilhete de Identidade at 14.8 million of 35.1 million Angolans. That is about 42%. In September 2025 the Secretary of State for Justice, Osvaldo Amaro, said 16,297,777 citizens held the card, a little under half of about 35 million people. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 counts two-thirds of the population holding a national ID. Establishing would need a source from the past three years that counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID.

BDI.short: Nothing found names a count of people holding a national ID or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. Nothing found counts the people holding a national ID.

BEN.short: Two-thirds of the population or more held a national ID in 2026.
BEN.summary: In June 2024 the World Bank said about 99 percent of Beninese citizens held a legal and digital identity. In the last twelve months, the World Bank said in May 2026 that nearly 99% of the population was biometrically enrolled. In October 2026 a Benin official put the share with a digital identity above 99%. Shares of 98 to 99% are given, and no count of 99.9% has been found since October 2023. Operating would need a source from the past three years that counts 99.9% of the population or more holding a national ID.

CIV.summary: In October 2024 ONECI's deputy director general said only 8 million of 29 million inhabitants were in ONECI's base. In the last twelve months, ONECI's director general said in July 2026 that 11 million people held the national identification number. That is about a third of a population of 32.7 million. No later count has been found. No source found since October 2023 counts two-thirds of the population holding a national ID. Establishing would need a source from the past three years that counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID.

COD.summary: In September 2026 Veille Citoyenne pour la Bonne Gouvernance said the President was still the only Congolese publicly issued the national ID card. No source found since October 2023 counts a third of the population or more holding a national ID. ETH.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2026.
ETH.summary: In October 2024 the programme office said close to 10 million people had received Fayda cards. In the last twelve months, the programme's executive director said in March 2026 that more than 37 million people were enrolled in Fayda. Enrolments reached 49.1 million by 24 August 2026, and by 9 October 2026 registrations had passed 52 million. Against a population of 135.5 million, that is about 38%. Establishing would need a source from the past three years that counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID.

GAB.short: Fewer than a third of the population held a national ID in 2026.
GAB.summary: In June 2026 the Interior Minister told the National Assembly that 335,384 people had enrolled in the electronic identity card campaign since 2024. That is about 13% of a population of 2.6 million. No other count has been found, and holders of the older card are not counted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source from the past three years that counts a third of the population or more holding a national ID.

GHA.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2024.
GHA.summary: In March 2024 the NIA's Executive Director said 17.8 million Ghanaians were on the National Identification Register. That is about half of a population of 35.1 million. In the last twelve months, National Identification Authority data at 30 October 2026 showed 20,610,948 people enrolled for the Ghana Card, as Dubawa reports. The Ghana Statistical Service projects a population of 34,378,768 for 2026, so about 60% are enrolled. Establishing would need a source from the past three years that counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID.

GIN.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2025.
GIN.summary: In July 2025 the Interior Ministry said 9,010,191 people were on the RNPP, after 111,319 duplicates were removed. That is about 60% of a population of 15.1 million. No other count has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a source from the past three years that counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID.

GMB.summary: No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 counts the people holding a national ID. The only count, from February 2023, is older than three years. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no other source on this has been found. Absent would need a source from the past three years that counts fewer than a third of the population holding a national ID.

LBR.short: Fewer than a third of the population held a national ID in 2026.
LBR.summary: By December 2024 it had enrolled 740,000, about 13% of 5.7 million, the registry said. At a June 2025 briefing the registry gave about 759,000 enrolled, about 14 percent. In the last twelve months, a September 2026 proclamation counted about 720,000 enrolled, near 12.6% of the population. In November 2026 the registry's executive director told a House committee it held about 740,000 records, with about 5.3 million people still to enrol. Preparing would need a source from the past three years that counts a third of the population or more holding a national ID.

LSO.short: A 2025 government figure put national ID coverage at 90%; no source found says whether that is of the whole population.
LSO.summary: A government deck shown at ID4Africa in 2025 puts national ID coverage at 90%. The deck is undated and gives no base, so the figure may be a share of those eligible rather than of the population. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 counts two-thirds of the population or more holding a national ID. MAR.summary: In February 2025 the national police spokesperson said 32 million electronic identity cards had been issued since 2008. He put the share of citizens identified at 87%. A May 2025 ID4Africa presentation counted 31 million citizens holding the card, out of 36.6 million people, about 85% of the population. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 counts 99.9% of the population holding a national ID. Operating would need a source from the past three years that counts 99.9% of the population or more holding a national ID.

MDG.short: Fewer than a third of the population held a national ID in 2026.
MDG.summary: In October 2023 the World Bank put holders of the new ID number at 0.01% of the population, against a 50% target. In the last twelve months, the World Bank said over 3.25 million adults were enrolled by 10 June 2026. Authorities put enrolment above six million by June 2026. In September 2026 the interior minister said nearly 5 million were enrolled in the first phase of Izaho tokana, about 15% of 32.7 million. Preparing would need a source from the past three years that counts a third of the population or more holding a national ID.

No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at all births and deaths at 80% or more. Mature would need birth registration to reach all births, each given the number, and death registration of 80% or more.

The minister said in April 2025 that work on the biometric identity card and passport was being accelerated. In the last twelve months, a ministry circular made the unique identifier of the national digital identity system E-Houwiya the exclusive reference for new digital services, reported in September 2026. It follows a pilot that dematerialised public hydraulic domain authorisations through it. No source found since October 2023 says the system checks people by biometrics. Operating would need the system to check fingerprints, face or iris to stop one person enrolling twice.

TZA.short: The national ID system checked people by biometrics in 2026; no certification or audit is known.
TZA.summary: In May 2026 the Deputy Minister for Home Affairs said the main data processing centre can verify applicants and match fingerprints so that each applicant is uniquely identified. In the last twelve months, on 22 October 2026 the Deputy Minister told a parliamentary committee that NIDA had generated 23,718,060 numbers. By 29 October 2026 NIDA had registered 27,648,911 Tanzanians, the Home Affairs minister said. A new edition of the card is issued to people registering from 18 November 2026. No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. Mature would need a security certification, audit or assurance level, and the ID held by all or nearly all the population.

UGA.summary: In February 2026 Biometric Update reported that NIRA deduplicated multiple biometric databases during the migration and found about 200,000 duplicates over about seven months. In May 2025 the minister said NIRA held biometric and biographic data on over 27.7 million Ugandans. In the last twelve months, by November 2026 10 million of 15.4 million printed new cards had been collected. In October 2026 Lwengo district leaders closed a NIRA office over alleged extortion. No source found since October 2023 reports a certification, audit or assurance level for the system. AGO.short: Another system's use of the national ID was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
AGO.summary: A presidential order, Despacho 300/26 of 13 August 2026, authorised US$28 million and opened a public tender for a national digital identity and e-signature platform. The platform is meant to let citizens and companies verify the identity of their customers electronically. In the last twelve months this order is the one step found. It is to be bought through the tender, and no source found since October 2023 says a service in use checks people against the ID. Establishing would need a service in use checking people against the national ID, such as SIM registration or a bank's KYC.

Nothing found since October 2023 says SIM registration, or any other system, checks people against an ID register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No bank KYC check or social programme enrolment against the register has been found either. Preparing would need another system's use of the national ID to be contracted, being built or piloted, such as a SIM-registration link or a bank's KYC check.
