ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe launched the Digital Land Administration Platform in May 2025 to process title deeds electronically. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the minister said three manual land databases had been merged into one digital platform. In November 2026 The Herald reported that the One National e-Cadastre held over 80% of an estimated 1.3 to 1.4 million property records. Its spatial records cover about 60% of the country. No source found since October 2023 says the digital land register covers the whole country. Operating would need the digital land register in service nationally or in all land offices.

AGO.short: In 2026 counters in municipal administrations work in a national database, in the 11 municipalities of one province; no source found reports the national count.
AGO.summary: On 14 August 2026 twelve counters were working in the 11 municipalities of Zaire province, the provincial director said. The Ministry of Territorial Administration runs a national programme of V/SAT satellite antennas for commune seats. In the last twelve months the data update began on 15 June 2026 with 254 counters in a first phase and 634 intended. No national count of municipalities with a working counter has been found. Nothing found says how the counters at municipal seats are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

BDI.short: A commune began keeping its accounts in a national financial platform in 2026; no source found says how many commune offices are connected.
BDI.summary: In October 2026 Butihinda commune's accountants and tax collectors were entering its revenue and spending into AK-SOFT, a financial-management platform. They said they need a stable Internet connection. In the last twelve months, in the same month, the Primature trained communal finance officers on AK-SOFT. The sector strategy of February 2021 names the extension of the government's fibre-optic interconnection to the communes under its e-government project. No source found says how Butihinda's office is connected or how many communes are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of communes connected by the state.

BEN.short: Twelve more communes' town halls joined the state's administration network in 2024, of 77 communes; no source found reports the total connected.
BEN.summary: In 2024 town halls used the services of the Réseau National de l'Administration, the state's own network. The finance ministry counts 12 new town halls using the network's services in 2024, and Benin has 77 communes. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the state agency ASIN presented the connection of Bantè's mairie to the network at its town hall. On 11 September 2026 a connection failure hit several of Cotonou's arrondissement offices. No cumulative total of town halls on the network has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of town halls connected by the state.

BFA.short: Town halls are on the state's network and 78 civil status centres were networked in 2025; nothing found reports the share of the 351 communes.
BFA.summary: In January 2024 ANPTIC listed the interconnection of local governments' buildings to RESINA, the government network. The territorial administration ministry gives 78 principal civil status centres networked in 2025. In the last twelve months those results were validated on 25 June 2026. ANPTIC's report for 2020 had named five town halls on RESINA or being put on it. No share of the 351 communes' town halls connected has been found, and the 78 centres are a count with no total. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

BWA.short: Four councils had partnerships to deploy office Wi-Fi in 2022/23; no source found says whether any council office's connection is in use.
BWA.summary: BoFiNet's annual report for financial year 2022/23 records partnerships between BoFiNet and four local authorities to deploy premises Wi-Fi in their Rural Administration Centres. The four are Serowe and Mahalapye District Councils and Bobirwa and Boteti Sub District Councils. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The partnerships stood in March 2023. No source states that a council's own office has a connection in use, or gives the total of councils. Establishing would need some council offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

CAF.short: A fund meant to bring broadband to town halls was still being set up in April 2026; nothing found says how many communes are connected.
CAF.summary: The Central African Republic's universal service fund was not yet in operation on 15 April 2026, Agence Ecofin reports. Its framework provides for broadband internet access in mairies. In the last twelve months ARCEP presented a draft budget of 6.2 billion FCFA on 15 April 2026 and said the fund's effective set-up was planned for 2026. The committee that manages the fund began its activities in July 2025. No source found states that any mairie is connected, or gives a count or share of communes. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

CIV.short: A loan-financed programme to connect the communes' town halls was ratified in February 2026; no source found says how many are connected.
CIV.summary: On 17 October 2025 Côte d'Ivoire and IDA concluded the loan agreement for PADCI phase 1. The project runs from 2025 to 2030 and carries US$45 million for broadband to targeted public institutions, town halls among them. In the last twelve months, on 4 February 2026, the Council of Ministers ratified the loan of 84,356,070,200 FCFA by decree. No source found states a town hall connected and in use, or gives a count or share of town halls connected. Establishing would need some town hall offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

CMR.short: Two commune offices in the East Region had an internet connection in August 2026; nothing found says how many of the 360 communes are connected.
CMR.summary: In August 2026 UNDP Cameroon stated an internet connection at two East Region commune offices: Bétaré-Oya, where it is unstable, and Bertoua 1er. In the last twelve months, on 2 June 2026, the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion programme to connect and equip local authorities, and its financing was still being sought. Cameroon has 360 communes and 14 urban communities. No share or total of communes connected has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

COD.short: In 2026 one province handed satellite kits to 45 chiefdoms and a national pilot tender was issued; nothing found says any office works over them.
COD.summary: On 17 March 2026 the governor of Haut-Uélé handed satellite kits to the heads of the province's decentralised entities at Isiro. They went to 45 chiefdoms and sectors of Haut-Uélé, beside 6 territories. In the last twelve months, on 4 June 2026, the national project unit issued a tender to connect the buildings of 7 governorates and 44 territories in a pilot phase. No source found says any chiefdom, sector or commune office works over a connection. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

COG.short: In February 2026 a World Bank-funded project was asked to extend internet access to town halls; no source found says how many communes are connected.
COG.summary: The World Bank's appraisal of May 2022 expects shared connectivity to be supplied to decentralised local authorities under the Patn digital project. In the last twelve months, on 26 February 2026, the project's steering committee recommended continuing and intensifying the extension of internet access. It approved reallocating funds towards the connectivity component. No source found says any town hall is connected: no count, share or place is given. Establishing would need some town hall offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

COM.short: Only civil-status and central systems are held, the latest from 2026; nothing found says whether the communes' offices are connected, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found states whether the office of any of the 54 communes is connected. No published count of connected communes was found.

CPV.short: Municipal councils worked in national systems in 2025, 21 of 22 supplied with state digital services; no source found says how many offices are connected.
CPV.summary: On 6 October 2025 NOSi, a public enterprise, said that 21 of the 22 municipalities, all but Mosteiros, were receiving its services regularly. NOSi's plan of March 2020 lists the municipal councils' local area networks among those served by basic access to the state's private network. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of councils connected has been found. The source of the 21 of 22 does not say how their offices are connected. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

DJI.short: In 2024 Djibouti city's three communes recorded civil status in the city's system; no source found reports connection of local governments outside the capital.
DJI.summary: In February 2024 the civil-status centres of Djibouti city's three communes recorded civil-status events in SIGEC, the city's computerised system. They are in Balbala, Ras Dika and Boulaos. The records they enter sit on a central server at the town hall. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states how the centres are connected, or places a local government office outside Djibouti city on a connection. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

DZA.short: All 1,541 communes worked in national systems over the interior ministry's network in 2019; capped because no current plan or budget line is known.
DZA.summary: The interior ministry's presentation of June 2019 shows 1,541 commune databases on the civil-status network, the ministry's own, which is 1,541 of 1,541 communes. In the last twelve months, on 5 April 2026, municipal services began the third phase of generalising the national vehicle-registration system. The phase ends manual and local procedures. The commune of Bouira bears its own annual internet subscription, the Court of Accounts found in September 2023. No count of communes connected after June 2019 has been found, and no current plan with a stated period. Operating would need a current plan or budget line for the communes' connection.

EGY.short: In 2024 one governorate was the pilot for linking districts and local units; no source found says whether any local unit office is connected.
EGY.summary: On 15 January 2024 Egypt's minister of communications named a project to automate local administration and governorate headquarters. It is to start at governorate headquarters, move to governorate capitals and districts, and end with local units. Minya was chosen as the pilot, and the link was expected during 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says whether the Minya link was made, or whether any local unit office is connected. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

ERI.short: No source found says whether any sub-zoba administration office is connected as at 2026, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Whether any sub-zoba administration has a connection. What is held concerns the zoba population registers and central systems.

ETH.short: Addis Ababa piloted a connection from the centre to its woredas in 2025; nothing found says whether any woreda office outside the capital is connected.
ETH.summary: In the last twelve months, on 5 December 2025, Addis Ababa's mayor launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology. He said implementation would start in 50 of the city's woredas on 8 December. On 22 December 2025 a government statement said connectivity has been created from the central level down to the woreda level for civil registration. It called this a major pilot, in Addis Ababa only. No woreda office outside Addis Ababa has been found on a connection provided to it. Establishing would need some offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

GAB.short: One commune's town hall, at Oyem, was on the state administration network in 2026; no source found says how many of the communes are connected.
GAB.summary: Gabon Review reported on 1 April 2026 that the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem is on the RAG, the Réseau de l'Administration Gabonaise, a fibre network. ANINF brought it into service there. In the last twelve months this activation followed fibre that was installed in 2010 and inactive until ANINF brought it into service. Gabonclic.info reported in June 2025 that Akanda and Owendo are linked to the RAG by fibre. No total of communes connected or to be connected has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

GHA.short: The government network connected all 274 planned sites of metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies in 2024; nothing found says how many of the 261 assemblies.
GHA.summary: In February 2024 the communications minister's table gives the assemblies 274 of 274 planned sites connected to the government network, within 950 of 951 government sites. In the last twelve months, on 3 September 2026, the Local Government Service signed a memorandum of understanding with Celltel Networks. Its head described the state the Service is moving from as "disconnected offices". Nothing found says how many of the 261 assemblies the 274 sites cover. Operating would need a published share, or a count given with its total, showing more than half of local governments connected by the state.

GIN.short: Commune registry staff worked in a national civil-registration system in 2026, with rural offices on paper; no source found says how many communes are connected.
GIN.summary: Enabel, the Belgian development agency, issued the tender of 27 July 2022 for the internet connection of 10 pilot communes. Its evaluation draws on fieldwork in April 2026. It says civil-status officers and data-entry agents at civil registry centres work in the national civil register's central database, with paper still used in parallel. In the last twelve months, the relocation of the system's data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted service to commune offices, reported on 2 September 2026. No delivery under the tender has been found, and no count of communes connected. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past the pilot, or working in a national system.

GMB.short: All councils had the government's finance system by late 2024 and most used it; capped because no current plan or budget line is known.
GMB.summary: IFMIS, the government's Integrated Financial Management Information System, had been implemented in all Local Government Area Councils by the end of 2024, on the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs' report. The report names eight councils. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 describes IFMIS in use or being installed at four of them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of councils with a connection provided to the office has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

GNB.short: No sector administration, nor the Bissau municipal chamber, is known to have an office connection in 2026, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found puts a sector administration or the Bissau municipal chamber on a connection. No local elections have been held, and the documents found concern the national backbone.

GNQ.short: In 2024 the government's network did not reach local government offices, which worked largely on manual systems; nothing found says whether any has another connection.
GNQ.summary: In 2024 the World Bank's digital economy diagnostic stated that the government's central network does not extend to local government branches. It adds that many ministries at the centre operate on manual systems, and that this is more pronounced at the local level. In the last twelve months, on 18 December 2025, Gabon's Council of Ministers approved an agreement to interconnect the fibre-optic networks of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea. These are the two countries' national networks. No programme to connect local government offices has been found. Preparing would need a programme prepared or piloted, with equipment handed over, a contract signed or pilot offices connected.

KEN.short: All 47 counties were on the government network by 2017 and work in national systems; no source found says how many county offices are connected.
KEN.summary: The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy states the counties were connected by secure connections into the national private governmental voice and data network. It calls the network NOFBI. The last county was connected by 2017. In the last twelve months, on 25 August 2026, the National Treasury set a deadline of 30 September 2026 for all 47 county governments to finish integrating the national electronic procurement platform with its financial management system. No share of county offices connected has been found since 2017. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

LBR.short: A 2019 policy targeted internet access at every county Superintendent office; no source found says whether any is connected, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: No stage is set. As at 30 September 2026, no source found says whether any local government office has a connection of its own, how it is connected, or what it does over the connection. No programme to connect the offices has been found, and no count or share of local governments connected. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Staff working on their own phones or modems would not change this. Absent would need a dated source that states local government offices have no connection of their own.

LBY.short: The mayors of 21 municipalities were given access to the ministry's online systems in October 2025; nothing found says how many municipal offices are connected.
LBY.summary: The Ministry of Local Government's digital transformation project director said on 2 November 2023 that official e-mail accounts would be created for the heads of administrative units in the municipalities. The ministry runs the system. In October 2025 the ministry gave the mayors of 21 municipalities access to its electronic systems, a count with no total. A 2021 study of three authorities finds internet access at the authorities' offices that is slow, often disconnected or not always available. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

LSO.short: Two community councils had internet installed under a pilot by 2019; no source found says whether any connection has gone beyond the pilot.
LSO.summary: The e-Government Project built and connected two community council buildings, under the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology, and handed them to the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftainship Affairs on 31 July 2019. The Minister said that the two buildings have the Internet installed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. On 17 June 2024 the ministry's Principal Secretary said its roll-out of 74 digital services would also connect Community Councils. No number, date or funding was given. Establishing would need councils connected past the pilot, or working in a national system.

MAR.short: A revenue system was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers by 2020; no source found says how commune offices are connected.
MAR.summary: An Interior Ministry circular of 19 May 2020 gives a figure for GIR-CT, the revenue system for local authorities. It was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers, 60.9 per cent. In the last twelve months, the World Bank's status report of 30 January 2026 counts 59 of 97 participating municipalities with the civil registry back-office system operational. A diagnostic of 2016 said municipal councils equip those offices from their own budgets. No source found says the state provides a connection to the commune offices. Operating would need a published share above half.

MDG.short: About 10 per cent of communes had a secure connection to a State finance system, on a 2024 plan; nothing found reports the figure's year.
MDG.summary: The Plan National de Décentralisation Emergente 2023-2030 was validated by decree on 2 August 2023. It appeared in June 2024. It gives a baseline of 10 per cent of the country's 1,695 communes with direct access to the SIFC over a secure connection. The target is 50 per cent for 2030. On 30 April 2025 the ministry handed internet boxes and a subscription to all 38 communes of the Antananarivo agglomeration. In the last twelve months, communes using the civil registration system SIECM rose from 75 to 336 in the six months to December 2025. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

MLI.short: Certain communes were connected by 2014 and a network for local governments was contracted in 2022; no source found says how many communes are connected.
MLI.summary: The Council of Ministers of 1 June 2022 adopted a draft decree approving the contract for the Projet d'Accès au service de télécommunication des collectivités territoriales. The contract was awarded to SIMO TELECOM for CFA 9,407,295,000 over twelve months. The only earlier fact found is a draft strategy of November 2014, which counts the connection of certain communes as a result achieved under the government's 2005 national ICT policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says any local government office is connected. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past any pilot, or working in a national system.

MOZ.short: In 2026 the government network reached public institutions in 141 districts, with expansion planned; no source found says how many local government offices are connected.
MOZ.summary: The European Union's action document of June 2026 says GovNet has connected about 1,000 public institutions and organs at central level and across 141 districts. It also says underinvestment in middle- and last-mile infrastructure leaves many local administrations insufficiently connected. In the last twelve months, the EU's annual action plan for 2026, dated 17 June 2026, carries a EUR 7.1 million Team Europe action to expand GovNet in selected districts. No source found puts a local government office on GovNet. No count of local governments connected has been found. Establishing would need offices outside the capital connected past any pilot, or working in a national system.

MRT.short: Communes run budgets in a national finance system, deployed in 90% of 232 regions and communes in 2023; nothing found says how offices are connected.
MRT.summary: The PEFA assessment of public financial management, dated January 2025, states that SIGeL, the integrated local finance management system, was deployed in 90 per cent of local authorities at the end of 2023. The share is of 232 authorities: 13 regions and 219 communes. Until 2022 the local authorities ran their budgets in the off-line system El Khazin. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The assessment states no connection for the offices, and no owner, plan or finance for one has been found. Operating would need a published share above half of local governments with a connection provided to the office.

MUS.short: All 12 municipal and district councils worked online in a shared ministry system in 2024; no source found says how their offices are connected.
MUS.summary: The Ministry of Local Government's report for 2023-2024 says its I-Council project was piloted at Moka from 27 August 2018. It took three years to implement in all local authorities. The report says all employees of the twelve local authority digital offices do their daily tasks in real time. The ministry's permit table for the year to 30 June 2025 lists all 12. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says who provides the offices' connection. Operating would need a connection provided to the office by the state or the authority, shown by a share or a count with its total.

MWI.short: District and city councils used internet on the government network in 2024; no source found says how many of the 35 councils are connected.
MWI.summary: Minutes of consultations with councils in June and July 2024 say the Department of E-Government manages the councils' internet on the government network. The minutes name Kasungu as on the network. They record on 25 June 2024 that Dowa was yet to be connected. In the last twelve months, GIZ Malawi says the government launched a six-month pilot in mid-June 2026. In it, District Council Offices in Balaka and Dowa take on-demand updates to the national social registry. No share of the 35 councils connected has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

NAM.short: In 2007 one local authority of two surveyed gave some staff e-mail; no source found says how many are connected, so no stage is set.
NAM.summary: No stage is set. As at 30 September 2026, no source found says whether any local government office has a connection of its own, how it is connected, or what it does over the connection. No programme to connect the offices has been found, and no count or share of local governments connected. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Staff working on their own phones or modems would not change this. Absent would need a dated source that states local government offices have no connection of their own.

NER.short: Broadband was reported extended to 266 communes in 2026; the total of communes and no source found says what their offices do over it.
NER.summary: The Projet Villages Intelligents is financed by the State of Niger and the World Bank at USD 100 million and closes on 23 October 2026. On 15 April 2026 the news agency ANP reported the project saying broadband internet had been extended to 266 communes, 339 health centres and 298 schools. In the last twelve months, the project's connectivity for the town halls was officially received at a ceremony on 6 May 2026. No share of communes connected has been found. Operating would need a published share above half, or a count given with its total.

NGA.short: 510 local government administration offices were counted on broadband in December 2025; nothing found says how many offices there are, and what they do online,.
NGA.summary: The World Bank's BRIDGE project was approved on 6 October 2025. It sets a target of 3,428 local government administration offices on broadband by September 2030. The Bank counts 510 local government administration offices connected to broadband at 17 December 2025, the same number as in July 2025. In the last twelve months, the credit was signed on 30 December 2025. On 22 September 2026 the communications minister cut the delivery timeline from five years to three. Operating would need more than half of local governments connected, as a published share or a count given with its total.

RWA.short: District offices worked in the national civil registration system in 2024 and 2025; no source found says how many of the districts are connected.
RWA.summary: The Governance and Decentralisation Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029, of 14 November 2024, costs an intervention giving local government entities ICT equipment and internet connectivity. The civil registration system NCI-CRVS was fully operational at district, sector and cell offices for 2025. It was also in 2024. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the Ministry of Local Government stated that births and deaths are registered at the cell, where before they were at the sector. No share or count of district offices connected has been found. No source says who pays for a district office's connection. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

SDN.short: A 2022 meeting recommended fibre for localities that ask; no source found says whether any locality office is connected, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. No source found puts a locality office on a connection, names what an office does over one, or counts the localities connected, as at September 2026. The one statement found is a meeting's recommendation of 22 November 2022, which asked that Sudatel connect by fibre the localities that ask, at their own cost. No locality is reported connected, and nothing has been found on the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local government offices have no connection of their own.

SEN.short: By June 2026, 400 civil-status centres run by communes were linked to the national register; no source found reports the share of communes connected.
SEN.summary: In August 2025 the civil-status agency ANEC said the state company SENUM SA had put network equipment in on site at 383 centres. Of these, 235 were in service and connected. In the last twelve months NEKKAL's final steering committee reported 400 civil registration centres interconnected on 29 June 2026. On 27 April 2026 ANEC's director general said that in some centres the circuit was never completed. Elsewhere, he said, it is very slow. No share of communes connected has been found. No source sets the 400 centres against a count of communes. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

SLE.short: All 21 councils had internet and a national accounting system live in early 2026, the finance ministry says; no source found says who pays afterwards.
SLE.summary: In the first quarter of 2026 the Ministry of Finance's accounting system PFM Smart went live in all 21 local councils. Its roll-out included the provision of an internet facility for 21 local councils and a local area network at 21. In 2023 seven councils outside Freetown reached the internet through individually provided modems. In the last twelve months solar panels and batteries were installed at 18, and the internet contract is shown as completed on 18 November 2025. The report gives no rural share, and no source says who pays for the service afterwards. Mature would need a published share of at least 90 per cent connected and working in national systems, with the rural share.

SOM.short: A 2022 report says finance systems are implemented in all municipalities; no source found says how their offices are connected.
SOM.summary: The National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 set a goal. All local authorities of the federal government and the member states were to have internet access by its third year. The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic of 2022 says the finance systems are implemented in all municipalities of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and the policy's period has ended. No source says how any municipal office is connected. No count of municipalities is given. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

SSD.short: One county office of eleven assessed had its own satellite link in 2021; no source found says how many of the country's counties are connected.
SSD.summary: In late 2021 the International Organization for Migration assessed eleven local governments, ten counties and Wau Municipality. One has a satellite terminal at the Commissioner's office, and ten have none. In Renk and Rubkona the only terminal is the Health Department's. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing has been found on any event since 2021. No count of connected offices across all the country's counties has been found. No use is named for the Maban terminal, and nothing says who pays for it. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

STP.short: No source found says whether any district council office is connected as at 2026, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not found. Which institutions are on the government network, and whether any district council is. The digital governance strategy is held cut off before its network chapter.

SWZ.short: One town council, Ezulwini, reported its own office internet line in the year to March 2024; no source found says how many councils are connected.
SWZ.summary: In the year to March 2024 Ezulwini Town Council carried its five office telephone lines over the office's internet line. The Municipal Council of Mbabane pays for internet among its utility services, in its report for the year to March 2023. In the last twelve months the House of Assembly gave a second reading on 21 September 2026 to the three Bills enabling the project's loans. COMESA reports that from January to June 2026 the project was in preparation, with its infrastructure assessment begun. No share of local governments with a connected office is published. No Tinkhundla centre is reported connected. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

SYC.short: All 27 listed district administrations had a government email address in 2025; no source found says how their offices are connected.
SYC.summary: The Office of the President's government directory of 1 March 2025 lists 27 districts, Praslin's two and La Digue among them, and places the district administration offices under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs. It gives each district administration office a gov.sc mailbox beside an office telephone number. No change has been found in the last twelve months. How the district administration offices are connected has not been found, and none is said to be on the government network. No system the offices work in has been found. Establishing would need some district offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

TCD.short: Internet kits and subscriptions were handed to 23 communes in 2026; nothing found says whether the links are in service and the total of communes.
TCD.summary: The World Bank's appraisal of the Chad Digital Transformation Project, dated 4 September 2024, provides for last-mile connectivity to selected public institutions, local government offices among them. In the last twelve months, on 19 May 2026, the finance ministry reported the official handover of the kits and subscriptions, with computers, printers and copiers. They went to the 23 communes that are provincial capitals. The kits are Starlink Business kits with antenna, router and Wi-Fi. Nothing says that a commune's link is in service. No national total of communes is given beside the 23. Establishing would need some local government offices outside the capital connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

TGO.short: A birth-records platform was at pilot in four communes in 2026 and town hall fibre had not begun; nothing found says how town halls connect.
TGO.summary: The digital ministry's resettlement plan of July 2026 names the ministry's project unit as promoter of the fibre extension to town halls. On 7 February 2026 the government's site said the town hall digitalisation project would connect the 136 municipal buildings themselves. In the last twelve months, the Vo pilot has been deployed since February 2026, in four communes. The July 2026 plan states that the fibre works to the 136 town hall buildings had not begun. Nothing says how any town hall is connected. Establishing would need some town halls connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

TUN.short: Sixteen municipalities worked in a national permit system in 2026; no source found says how many municipalities have a connected office.
TUN.summary: The Ministry of Communication Technologies' performance plan for 2025 targets 98 per cent in 2025 and 100 per cent from 2026. The target is for public bodies' sites connected to the administrative network. The plan names RNIA3 as the administrative network for local collectivities and municipalities. In the last twelve months, on 24 June 2026, the Municipality of Tunis issued the first building permit handled entirely online. Taamir's extension to 16 municipalities began that day. The number of municipalities whose offices are connected has not been found. Nor has the total to set the 16 against. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

TZA.short: In 2025, 174 district councils worked in a national loans system and councils are on the government network; no source found reports the share connected.
TZA.summary: The e-Government Authority's roadmap of February 2024 states local government authorities are on GovNet, the government communication network. It gives 265 ministries, departments, agencies and local authorities on it as one figure. The Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 targets 184 local government authorities on a structured office network and GovNet by June 2026. In the last twelve months, on 1 May 2026, the Geita Regional Commissioner directed District Executive Directors and other employers to fund employees' internet from internal revenues. The trade union congress had said that many public employees in the region buy internet bundles with their own money. The share of councils whose own offices are connected has not been found. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

UGA.short: In 2022, 60.6 per cent of districts, municipalities and town councils answering a survey had office internet; no source found reports the share of all.
UGA.summary: NITA-U's survey of early 2022 found 60.6 per cent of responding local government administrations had institutional internet. In October 2026 the finance ministry said the IRAS revenue system had been rolled out to all 176 local governments. In the last twelve months, on 22 September 2026, the local government ministry launched its web-based accounting tool in Hoima city's two divisions. For 2024/25 the Auditor General found 18 of 30 sampled local governments on unstable internet in IRAS. No share of all local governments connected has been found, nor any later than 2022. Mature would need a published share of at least 90 per cent connected and working in national systems, with the rural share.

ZAF.short: Municipalities across the Eastern Cape have worked in a shared disaster system since 2025; no source found says how many municipalities' offices are connected.
ZAF.summary: In November 2025 Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality told the National Council of Provinces it had appointed a service provider to upgrade its network infrastructure across its seven towns. The first phase was under way. In the last twelve months the State Information Technology Agency said municipalities across the Eastern Cape are operational on a disaster management system. It went live on 21 November 2025, with training for provincial and municipal users. AARTO entered its second phase in July 2026, expanding to 62 municipalities. No share or count of municipalities connected against the national total has been found. Operating would need a published share of local governments connected, or a count given with its total.

ZMB.short: Government counted 93 of 116 councils on its network in 2025 and all 116 in March 2026; no source found reports the rural share.
ZMB.summary: The budget address of 26 September 2025 says Government connected local authorities to the Government Wide Area Network, and each government count puts at least 93 of the 116 councils on it. In the last twelve months Smart Zambia's chief technical officer said on 24 March 2026 that all 116 were connected. On 7 July 2026 Smart Zambia said all local authorities in North-Western Province were on it over fibre. Nothing found says whether the 116 stated in March 2026 included the North-Western Province councils reported connected later. The rural share has not been found. Mature would need a published share of at least 90 per cent connected and working in national systems, with the rural share.

ZWE.short: Government handed over 250 satellite kits for local authorities in 2025; no source found says whether any council office is connected.
ZWE.summary: The Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services donated 250 Starlink satellite kits to the Ministry of Local Government for local authorities. This was reported on 24 July 2025, when installation and use were still to come. In the last twelve months, in the first half of 2026, 104 Starlink kits were distributed in Masvingo Province, as one total for schools, clinics and local authorities. In April 2026 Manyame Rural District Council's chief executive said its US$491,039 digitalisation programme, connectivity included, is funded from the approved council budget. No installed or activated kit is reported. Manyame's connection is not said to be live. Establishing would need some local government offices connected, past any pilot, or working in a national system.

AGO.short: A finance ministry system recording municipal payers and fees reached all 164 municipalities by 2021; no source found says how many use it.
AGO.summary: The Ministry of Finance launched and runs the Portal do Munícipe under Presidential Decree 47/18. On 10 November 2021 its Secretary of State said the Portal was implemented in all 164 municipalities, with telecommunications problems in some. No share or count of municipalities whose staff record in it has been found. Nothing dated after November 2021 has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

BDI.short: Thirty communes collect revenue electronically and one keeps a register of payers (2026); no source found reports the share of communes.
BDI.summary: The Interior ministry developed E-taxe, with CRDB Bank as collection interface, which began in 12 pilot communes on 23 August 2024. Its third-quarter report for 2025/26 lists 30 communes digitalised in communal revenue and gives no total. In the last twelve months, VNG International said in September 2026 that Nyanza had put its taxpayer information into its accounting software. It is the only commune shown with a register of payers. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of communes keep a digital register of payers.

BEN.short: Twelve of 77 communes were selected in 2019 for cash-desk software that records payments; no source found says whether they were equipped and use it.
BEN.summary: In September 2019 the PAACOL project, coordinated by the AIMF and implemented with the ANCB, the communes' association, had selected 12 of Benin's 77 communes to be equipped with the cash windows. The cash-desk software records each payment, and the equipping was due during 2019/2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the 12 communes were equipped and their cash desks went into use has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

BFA.short: Only the capital records market traders and their tax payments digitally (2025); no commune outside it is known to record.
BFA.summary: The commune of Ouagadougou runs SYSCOTAX for local taxes through its tax base office, launched in four pilot markets on 19 March 2024. On 19 November 2025 its tax-base director said SYSCOTAX records market traders by phone number and tracks who has paid what. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No commune outside Ouagadougou has been found recording its revenue digitally, and no source says where the capital's record is kept. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

BWA.short: One city council takes rates payments online (2024); no source found says any council keeps a digital record, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: Not found. Whether any council keeps a digital revenue register or receipt record. Nothing found says the national tax system collects any council revenue.

CAF.short: Bangui agreed with a private firm in December 2025 to digitise its municipal revenue; no source found says whether the system is in use.
CAF.summary: An agreement was signed with the Mairie de Bangui in December 2025. Under it, BMI-WFS, a firm under Ivorian law, is to run the city's digital collection system. In the last twelve months, the only change found is that agreement, signed on 12 December 2025. Before it, a city-centre trader told RFI in December 2020 that Bangui town hall had no computerised file of taxpayers. No source says the system is in use, and no commune other than Bangui is named. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

CIV.short: A ministry-built register system was in a 22-commune pilot of 201 in December 2025; no source found says whether any commune records in it.
CIV.summary: The Directorate General of Decentralisation and Local Development developed the SYGIDAN Recettes software in its own services. It was at pre-validation in April 2024. The African Development Bank's appraisal of July 2021 places its pilot in 22 of 201 municipalities. In the last twelve months, on 9 December 2025 the directorate handed the commune of Assinie-Mafia its taxpayer database, within the PAMREC pilot. No fact has been found saying the system is in use in any commune, or giving a count of communes recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

CMR.short: A platform for traders to register and pay local tax was presented for two councils in 2023; no source found says any council uses it.
CMR.summary: The AIMF reports that FEICOM presented Inform'All City, a platform for collecting local tax from informal traders, on 21 March 2023. Informal traders register and pay on it. It was to be deployed first in the councils of Yaoundé II and Douala III, in the political and economic capitals. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the platform was deployed in any council, and where its record is held, has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

COD.short: Tools to track revenue and register taxpayers were being assessed with 20 decentralised territorial entities in 2024; no source found says whether any uses one.
COD.summary: The digital tools for the decentralised territorial entities are supported by USAID's Good Governance Activity, launched in July 2023. A workshop of 23 to 24 July 2024 was to standardise and assess tools for tracking revenue, registering taxpayers and budgeting, with 20 entities in four provinces. No change has been found in the last twelve months. What the tools record, where the record is held and whether any entity uses one has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

COG.short: A state platform for local governments' revenue was validated in February 2026; no source found says whether any local government yet records on it.
COG.summary: In February 2026 the finance ministry said the PDRCL platform for local governments' revenue has a back-office module for local government agents and a market-collector module, Zando collecte. In the last twelve months, the platform passed final validation at Kintélé on 14 February 2026. The state agency ACSI presented it to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026. A pilot was to follow at the Ndjindji central market in Pointe-Noire once municipal staff had been trained. No local government has been found recording on it. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

COM.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

CPV.short: A new municipal system was rolled out to all 22 municipalities in October 2026; no source found says it records payments yet.
CPV.summary: Cape Verde's decentralisation ministry is bringing a new municipal information system, Simpol, to the municipalities, to support the new property tax from 2027. In the last twelve months, on 28 October 2026 the Directorate-General for Decentralisation said Simpol would be applied in all 22 municipalities from that day. Municipal staff were trained. Before it, the municipal system in use, SIM 2.0, handles accounting, budget execution and the allocation of revenues and expenses. No municipality has been found recording payers or payments in Simpol. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

DJI.short: In 2020 local authorities could not levy taxes; no source found says how records are kept, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: No stage is set. The one source found, on 2020 fiscal data, says local authorities are not empowered to levy taxes and that none of the nine collects its own. No source found says how a local authority keeps any revenue record, and none names a system in preparation. Nothing found is dated since 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local governments keep their revenue records on paper, with no system in use.

DZA.short: A 2018 audit found most communes reviewed had no current tax-base census; no source found says how communes record revenue, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: No stage is set. The one fact found is an audit of 22 communes over 2014 to 2018, which found most had no updated census of their taxable base. It does not speak for the country. The interior ministry put a computerised system for following each commune's financial position in service from 11 December 2022. No source found says how communes keep their revenue records, and none names a revenue system in preparation or on pilot. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local governments keep their revenue records on paper, with no system in use.

EGY.short: A central authority collects the real estate tax, a quarter for local government (2020); no source found reports local records, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not found. Whether any governorate or local unit keeps its own digital revenue record. No source on local government revenue records has been found.

ERI.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

ETH.short: A property tax platform built for three pilot cities in 2016 was never fully implemented; no source found says any city still uses it.
ETH.summary: LoGRI's project page says the Computerized Property Tax Administration (CPTA) platform was developed for three pilot cities in 2016 and was never fully implemented. In the last twelve months, the Addis Ababa City Government Revenues Bureau began a property-tax reform pilot in July 2026, covering property identification and valuation. The pilot moves from the land-rent and building-tax arrangement to a value-based property tax. Nothing has been found on what CPTA records or where its record is held. Nor has anything been found on whether any of the three cities still uses it. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

GAB.short: Libreville's mayor said in July 2026 the city runs its own digital revenue system; no source found says whether any other local government records.
GAB.summary: Libreville's pilot platform, launched on 29 July 2025, is developed by the company GTI Gabon for the city hall. On 3 July 2026 the mayor said the city has its own operational system digitalising municipal revenue and securing collection. In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 Owendo signed an agreement with the tax directorate to use Digitax for municipal taxes. By October 2026 Libreville's E-Tax had recorded over 4,000 transactions. No local government outside Libreville has been found recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

GHA.short: Some assemblies record payers and bills in a shared national system, nine of 260 in 2019; no source found says how many do now.
GHA.summary: Nine of Ghana's 260 assemblies, 3.5 per cent, used the dLRev revenue software throughout 2019. It holds a register of businesses and properties with their owners, and has been hosted on the National IT Agency's platform since 2017. In the last twelve months, a training of 350 staff of 35 Municipal Assemblies began in February 2026. About 150 officers in six regions were trained in July 2026. No figure for assemblies recording in dLRev has been found dated after February 2020. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

GIN.short: A donor project digitised market and taxi tax collection in one town in 2026; no commune is known to record payers outside a project.
GIN.summary: In November 2025 Enabel, the Belgian aid agency, awarded the REVIS project in Mamou to a consortium of Global Itec and Le Partenariat. REVIS digitised the census of market traders and motorcycle taxis there, and the collection of their taxes. In the last twelve months, the consortium reported in August 2026 that Mamou's market revenue had risen fourfold. Enabel held a workshop on 16 July 2026 on repeating the project in other local authorities. No commune has been found recording its payers outside a donor project, and no source says where the REVIS record is held. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

GMB.short: One council outside the capital keeps a digital tax register, reported in 2024 and 2025; no source found reports the share of councils recording.
GMB.summary: Basse Area Council implemented a digital tax register in 2024. The ministry of finance's report of September 2025 names one council, Basse, as operating the system. In the last twelve months, a UN agency tendered in June 2026 for a property tax digital management system for Kanifing Municipal Council. No award has been found. The April 2026 evaluation of the public finance strategy reports the Digital Tax Collection System largely unimplemented in Banjul City Council. No total of councils has been found beside any count. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

GNB.short: Only national tax declaration and online payment systems are named (2022); no source found reports local governments' revenue records, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Whether any local government keeps a digital revenue record. Neither system held is stated as serving a local government.

GNQ.short: Only the finance ministry's national tax systems are named (2023 to 2026); no source found reports municipalities' revenue records, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. Whether any municipality keeps a digital revenue record. No municipal system is named.

KEN.short: Thirty-three of 47 counties had automated revenue collection by 2020, issuing electronic receipts; no source found says whether they hold a register of payers.
KEN.summary: A paper of September 2020 said thirty-three of the 47 counties, 70 per cent, had automated their revenues, some in part. A 2018 policy brief had found most counties that had automated did not own their system. In the last twelve months, standards gazetted on 27 July 2026, say counties are to own their systems and revenue data. The Vision 2030 Delivery Secretariat's review of 23 February 2026 names five with well-established systems and cashless collection. No source has been found saying counties hold a register of payers. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

LBR.short: Only the capital bills businesses digitally, and a property tax system is a pilot (2026); no other local government records past a pilot.
LBR.summary: UNDP reported in June 2026 that the firm KWARECOM runs the Real Property Tax Expansion pilot with UNDP and Sweden, with the Liberia Revenue Authority. Monrovia City Corporation's Ewallie platform holds business invoices marked paid or pending. Three neighbouring local governments say they have no access to it. In the last twelve months, a joint mission in June 2026 visited the pilot in Grand Bassa, Margibi and Nimba. No local government outside Monrovia has been found recording past a pilot. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

LBY.short: A 2024 ministry programme signed by 27 municipalities includes electronic collection; no source found says how many municipalities use its local revenue system.
LBY.summary: The Ministry of Local Government of the Government of National Unity runs the National Programme for Activating Local Revenues. On 10 June 2024, 27 municipalities signed a sponsorship document committing them to implement the programme. Its projects include an electronic collection system and a database of municipal economic activities. The programme director gave no count of municipalities where the local revenue system is activated, and the 27 signatories are not said to use it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

LSO.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

MAR.short: Communes issue local tax bills in a national system, in more than 100 large municipalities in August 2025; no source found reports the share recording.
MAR.summary: GIR-CT is the integrated revenue management system for local authorities. It was reported on 29 May 2025 as run by the Interior Ministry's directorate for local authorities with the national treasury. The World Bank's status report on its mission of August 2025 puts GIR-CT in place in more than 100 large municipalities. It gives no total of municipalities. The Interior Ministry's circular had it deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities on 19 May 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

MDG.short: Mahajanga commune has recorded taxpayers and their payments in its own software since 2024; no count of communes doing so has been published.
MDG.summary: In February 2024 Mahajanga commune put two programs into use, SIGRL for local revenue and one for registering taxpayers. They hold each taxpayer's registration, payments and transfer orders. Mahajanga is the one commune outside the capital shown recording its taxpayers. In the last twelve months, Antananarivo launched the digital collection of market dues on 7 October 2026, after registering its market traders on tablets. No share or total of communes recording their payers has been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

MLI.short: Communes tested tax registers in 2023 and Koutiala began a pilot in March 2026; no source found says whether any uses one as routine.
MLI.summary: A Pro-ARIDES note of July 2024 says ReCoDe, the communes' software, was chosen by the national local finance committee and rolled out by the DGCT and the treasury. It was deployed in 680 communes for testing. After training in 27 communes, only Kava was willing to carry tax digitalisation through. In the last twelve months, a project launched on 6 March 2026, starting with Koutiala. It is to give pilot communes a digital solution and equipment for financial management and the collection of communal taxes. No commune outside Bamako has been found using the local tax module as routine. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

MOZ.short: One municipality outside the capital bills property tax from a digital register (2025); no source found says how many others record.
MOZ.summary: Partners for Water reported in March 2025 that Beira linked its digitised land registry to its tax collection system, so the municipality knows who owns what and who must pay property tax. Beira is the one municipality running the linked registry and tax system. In Nampula a 2025 case study found no electronic system for the personal municipal tax. In the last twelve months, on 8 August 2026 CEDSIF, the state's information systems centre, published a page setting out the e-SGA modules, which does not say e-SGA is in use. No total of municipalities has been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

MRT.short: About 30 municipalities record taxpayers in a revenue system in use since 2020 (2025); no source found reports the share of all communes.
MRT.summary: In April 2025 the Interior Ministry's decentralisation directorate said the El Mouhassil application, in use since 2020, now serves about 30 municipalities. It gave no total of communes. The mayor of Ksar said in December 2023 that El Mouhassil runs a full taxpayer census whose data go into the municipal database. Each commune keeps its own record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The total of communes against which the 30 can be set has not been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

MUS.short: Local authorities run permit and document systems (2024); no source found says any council keeps a digital revenue record, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: Not found. Whether any council keeps a digital revenue register or receipt record. Nothing found says the national tax portal collects any council revenue.

MWI.short: Five of 35 local governments recorded revenue digitally by 2025, three with registers of payers; no source found reports the cities' position since 2022.
MWI.summary: The International Growth Centre found in 2022 that revenue management systems had been introduced in all four city councils since 2017, of 35 local governments. In Blantyre, Lilongwe and Mzuzu the systems held property and business owners with their payments and liabilities in one database per city. In February 2025 the United Nations Development Programme named one district council, Mwanza, with its own system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No system has been found in the other 30 local governments. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

NAM.short: The capital billed water accounts to named customers in its own system in 2024; no source found says other local authorities record revenue.
NAM.summary: As reported for February 2024, the City of Windhoek bills water accounts for named customers in the system it calls Solar. Payments and arrears are recorded against each account, and the billing system ran on the city's own servers. On 2 July 2024 the city confirmed irregularities in its water billing system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No local authority outside Windhoek has been found recording revenue, and no total of those recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

NER.short: The capital registers its taxpayers digitally and one commune outside it began in December 2025; no source found says how many communes record.
NER.summary: The City of Niamey launched the Naneye Yarda platform on 3 October 2024 under its 2025-2027 strategic plan. In January 2026 its administrator said the project had enumerated 35,000 taxpayers and follows each notice to payment. In the last twelve months, the commune urbaine of Diffa put the system into service on 11 December 2025, replacing manual collection and incomplete taxpayer files. No count of communes recording has been found, and nothing reports use in Diffa since. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

NGA.short: Two local government areas in one state registered payers digitally from 2017; no source found says how many record across the country.
NGA.summary: In March 2017 the Edo State government introduced an automated revenue collection system under the Edo Jobs Initiative. A journal article of November 2018 describes an app in which agents register payers, businesses and vehicles and collect and print receipts. It says two of Edo State's local government areas use the system, Oredo and Egor. Before it, revenue was collected on manual receipts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the two still use it, and how many local government areas keep a digital revenue record, has not been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

RWA.short: The revenue authority collects for districts and keeps their tax register (2024); no source found reports districts' own records, so no stage is set.
RWA.summary: Not found. Whether any district keeps a revenue record of its own. What is held is the national revenue authority's record, kept on the districts' behalf.

SDN.short: One locality began electronic collection as a model site in May 2026; no source found says whether it keeps a register of payers.
SDN.summary: The Sennar state finance ministry launched Isali electronic collection on 12 May 2026 at the transport and petroleum department and Sinja locality, as reported in May 2026. Sinja was one of two model sites in Sennar State at the launch. In the last twelve months, that launch followed preparation from January 2026, in stages of networking, account opening and training. No other locality has been found collecting electronically. Whether collection in Sinja ran past its model stage, whether a register of payers is kept and where the record is held has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

SEN.short: More than 20 communes were equipped with a vendor's municipal software by November 2025; no source found says whether any records its revenue in it.
SEN.summary: The vendor Linking Development states, as at November 2025, that more than 20 communes in Senegal are equipped with Terlink, its municipal software. It says Terlink includes accounting and taxation modules covering the recovery and management of communal taxes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on whether any commune uses the software, what it records of payers, or where the record is held. No total of communes beside the count has been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

SLE.short: Three of 22 councils run a property tax register, two outside the capital (2026); the rest are not yet on it.
SLE.summary: The Ministry of Finance runs the rollout with the Ministry of Local Government, as at May 2026, of the Moptax property tax system. LoGRI says Moptax runs in Freetown, Kenema and Makeni, and the ministry counts three of 22 local councils with the upgraded system in December 2025. In the last twelve months, Freetown City Council was upgraded to MOPTAX 2.0 in December 2025. In May 2026 the ministry invited firms to roll the system out in Bo and Koidu New Sembehun. No council beyond the three has been found recording on the system. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

SOM.short: Four Puntland local governments kept a digital register of payers and payments in 2022; no source found reports the share of all local governments.
SOM.summary: Four Puntland local governments, Galkacyo north, Garowe, Qardho and Bosaso, used the system to collect taxes in October 2022. In Garowe, Qardho and Galkacyo properties were mapped and registered in the local government financial system, which replaced printed receipts and books. In November 2022 no local government or district in Galmudug and Benadir had a financial management system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No total of local governments has been found, so the four are a count and no share. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

SSD.short: Juba City Council moved its revenue operations to a digital system in October 2026; no council outside the capital is named.
SSD.summary: In October 2022 Stateman Software & Telecom Ltd was named as developer, implementer and manager of Juba City Council's digital revenue system. A council notice invited businesses to register on it. In the last twelve months, the Central Equatoria State Government launched a digital revenue collection system and e-services for the council in September 2026. In late October 2026 the caretaker mayor said the council had moved all its revenue operations from manual forms to a digital payment system. No council other than Juba City Council has been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

STP.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

SWZ.short: One council, Manzini, billed ratepayers by account and took payment by phone in 2024; no source found reports other local governments' records.
SWZ.summary: For 2024/2025 the Municipal Council of Manzini issued rates bills to individual ratepayers by post, email and bulk SMS, on its notice of April 2024. It keeps their contact and ownership details, and ratepayers check their rates balance and pay by USSD code. In December 2020 it said rates had been billed in April 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No local government other than Manzini has been found keeping such a record. AGO.short: The state's own data centre, opened in 2026, sells hosting at Tier III; no source found reports a second national one at that tier.
AGO.summary: The government inaugurated its National Data Centre and Cloud at Camama on 28 April 2026. Infosi, the state's IT institute, runs it. In the last twelve months, Menos Fios reported in May 2026 that its modules are certified Tier III. The building awaits the Uptime Institute's assessment. In April 2026 the telecoms ministry said the state-owned centre hosts data in the national territory. No second nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III has been found. Operating would need two or more such centres at Tier III or above.

BDI.short: A nationally owned data centre for hire in service by 2020, none found at Tier III or above.
BDI.summary: As at 30 September 2026, the World Bank reports that Burundi Backbone System (BBS) has one level-3 data center, built at a cost of USD 2 million. BBS uses it to offer hosting to customers, and other public agencies use it to back up their systems. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source has been found that says a nationally owned data centre for hire is Tier III or above. Establishing would need one nationally owned data centre for hire to be Tier III or above.

BEN.short: A state-run data centre for hire is in service and the state centre hosts ministries' systems (2026); none is known at Tier III.
BEN.summary: In April 2026 an ASIN official said Benin has several data centres. One of them is run commercially by SBIN, the Société béninoise des infrastructures numériques. In the last twelve months, La Marina BJ reported in August 2026 that the state data centre hosts ministries' applications. ASIN, the state's digital agency, manages it. MTN Bénin rents servers and storage to businesses. No source has been found that says a nationally owned data centre for hire is Tier III or above. Establishing would need one such centre at Tier III or above.

BFA.summary: As at 12 November 2026, BTW Media describes VTS's Virtix data centre in Ouagadougou as Tier III. It is in service and offers colocation, and no certifying body is named. In the last twelve months, on 11 November 2026, President Traoré said the data of the new unique identifier is hosted in Burkinabè data centres run by public bodies. No second nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III or above has been found. Operating would need two or more such centres at Tier III or above.

No second nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III or above has been found. Operating would need two or more nationally owned data centres for hire to be Tier III or above.

Ministries and state administrations host data there, and in June 2026 Camtel called Zamengoé a critical national asset for the local control of government data.

The source gives no date for either, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. No second nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III or above has been found. TUN.short: Two nationally owned data centres for hire are Tier III or above by 2025, and the state's CNI hosts national platforms in 2026.
TUN.summary: In May 2025 Orange Tunisie opened a 1,000 square metre data centre at Kalaa Kebira, near Sousse, and Orange describes it as Tier III. TZA.short: TTCL's state data centre for hire reached Tier III by its own account in 2026; no source found reports a second national one at Tier III.

UGA.summary: NITA-U's strategic plan reports the National Data Centre in operation, with 99.5% average uptime in FY2023/24. It sells colocation and data centre services to ministries, local governments and private clients. The World Bank reports 162 government applications hosted at the data centre in June 2024, against a target of 400. BCX states its two operating Midrand data centres were developed to tier-4 specifications as rated by the Uptime Institute, with no certification mentioned. ZMB.summary: As at 30 September 2026, the Zambian government's ministerial statement describes the active Zambia National Data Centre (ZNDC), which hosts private clients for a fee, as a Tier 3 facility (stated by the government; no certifier named). The statement says all Government ICT hosting infrastructure has been consolidated and housed in the ZNDC. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No second nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III or above has been found. Operating would need two or more nationally owned data centres for hire to be Tier III or above.

ZWE.short: A nationally owned data centre for hire at Tier III or above by 2026; no second one held.

AGO.short: Private money went into Angolan digital firms in 2025 and 2026, some from a Luanda fund; no public project with private money is known.

In the last twelve months, in December 2025, CAP Capital, a European holding, bought all of TSMARTS. It announced EUR 50 million of investment over three years. In March 2026 BFA Asset Management of Luanda put $1.2 million from its Kimbo Fund into Anda, a motorcycle-taxi start-up. No source found says the government brought private money into a public digital project. BDI.summary: In 2026 Lumitel Burundi, a subsidiary of Vietnam's Viettel group, signed a USD 10 million contract with the PAFEN project to extend rural 4G. It financed 56 per cent of it itself, about USD 5.6 million. The source carries no date, so the contract is dated to its publication on 3 March 2026. In the last twelve months this is the only amount found from 2024 on, and no source found says whether private money came in more than one year. Establishing would need named amounts signed or started in two different years from 2024.

BEN.summary: On 29 July 2024 BOAD, MTN Bénin and Banque Atlantique Bénin signed a FCFA 20 billion financing agreement for MTN Bénin's 5G, fibre and platform upgrade. In 2025 MTN Group committed over USD 215 million of its own money in Benin through 2026. Banque Atlantique Bénin was the mandated lead arranger of the 2024 loan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the government brought private money into a public digital project. Mature would need a partnership, concession or joint venture signed from 2024 in which a private partner puts a named amount into a public digital project, or a state fund that private investors have paid into.

In the last twelve months, a national strategy for governing, opening and using public data was presented in final draft on 26 March 2026. It still awaited the government's endorsement in August 2026. No source found reports the strategy to have been adopted.

It went to the Ministry of Finance for submission to Cabinet in December 2016, and by June 2017 it had not been officially adopted. The portal opendata.go.tz, launched in September 2015, then held 163 datasets from 11 institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether the policy was adopted after June 2017. Establishing would need the government to adopt the policy, and the policy not to have run out.

The statistics office INE launched the Portal do Censo 2024 and the INE Angola app, giving anyone online census indicators, tables and maps. INE's own site publishes the definitive 2024 census results for download. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 states an open licence for the data.
