MDG.short: Madagascar's Telma has been part of the METISS cable consortium with Mauritian operators since 2021; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
MDG.summary: The METISS consortium states that its 3,200 km sea cable entered service on 5 March 2021. It links Mauritius, Réunion and Madagascar, landing at Fort Dauphin, to a landing near Durban. Telma is its Malagasy member, beside Mauritius's CEB and Emtel. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, memorandum or financing for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

MLI.short: Mali's backbone was joined to Senegal's in October 2026 and works within the regional backbone network; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
MLI.summary: In June 2024 Mali's SMTD and Guinea's SOGEB agreed to interconnect the two countries' fibre networks, with ministry support. In the last twelve months, Senegal's SENUM and SMTD inaugurated the interconnection of their national backbones at the Kidira and Diboli border on 5 October 2026. The chairman of ROA-BN, the West African network of national backbones, said in November 2025 that its network is working. Mali is connected to Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea and Senegal within it. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's fibre interconnector with Zambia was commissioned in 2026; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's communications minister launched the interconnectivity project with Zambia at Cassacatiza on 20 February 2026, a cross-border fibre partnership of Vodacom Moçambique and Bayobab Zambia. Zambia and Mozambique officially launched the Chanida to Cassacatiza fibre interconnector, reported on 23 February 2026. In the last twelve months, Mozambique's and Angola's ministers also signed a memorandum on 22 June 2026 for a sea cable from Nacala to Lobito. It is still at the concession stage. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

MRT.short: Mauritania joined the West African research network's backbone in 2025; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
MRT.summary: Mauritania joined the backbone of WACREN, the regional research and education network, in 2025, with five other West African countries. AfricaConnect projects co-funded by the European Commission support the expansion, which serves universities and research institutes. WACREN also activated a link from Lagos to Cape Town in the same expansion. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

MUS.short: Mauritian operators have run the METISS cable with Madagascar's Telma since 2021; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
MUS.summary: The METISS consortium states that its 3,200 km sea cable entered service on 5 March 2021, linking Mauritius, Réunion and Madagascar to a landing near Durban. CEB and Emtel are its Mauritian members, beside Madagascar's Telma. No change has been found in the last twelve months. South African networks are members of the Mauritius Internet Exchange Point, PeeringDB data of May 2026 show. Foreign members joining an exchange are commercial use. No data facility run with another country has been found, and no exchange point shared under an agreement. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

MWI.short: Nothing found names infrastructure Malawi shares with another African country under an agreement, so no stage is set.
MWI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names digital infrastructure Malawi shares with another African country under an agreement. Nothing found says it has none.

NAM.short: Namibia's MTC and Botswana's state fibre company completed cross-border fibre in 2026; no source found reports it to carry traffic.
NAM.summary: Telecom Namibia, Angola Telecom and the cable company SATCAB signed a master service agreement on 12 June 2026 joining the Southern African Regional Submarine System to the Equiano cable. In the last twelve months, MTC Namibia and Botswana's BoFiNet signed a memorandum on 17 February 2026 on cross-border fibre. The Angosat-2 work began as a proof of concept in October 2025, and Telecom Namibia then signed a pilot agreement with Angola's space programme office. No source found says building has begun on the cable work with Angola. None says a shared link, exchange or data centre is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

NER.short: Niger and Algeria opened their trans-Saharan fibre link in October 2026; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
NER.summary: Niger's minister received 1,031 km of the trans-Saharan fibre backbone on 14 November 2025, reaching the Algerian, Chadian, Nigerian, Beninese and Burkinabe borders. In the last twelve months, Niger's and Algeria's ministers opened the link at Assamaka on 6 October 2026. Niger's ministry declared it officially in service. Algeria reports a capacity of up to 100 gigabits a second from the start. No source found says the links to Chad, Nigeria or Benin are working, or that an exchange point or data centre is shared. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

NGA.short: Phase3 and Senegal's Sonatel activated a Lagos to Dakar fibre route in 2025; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
NGA.summary: Phase3 and Senegal's Sonatel activated a 3,500 km fibre route from Lagos to Dakar in May 2025, running through Benin, Togo and Ghana. In the last twelve months, Nigeria's Backbone Connectivity Network and Equatorial Guinea's transport minister signed a sea cable agreement in Malabo in February 2026. No source reports works begun on it. Phase3, CSquared and Benin's SBIN announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025, tested but not yet open. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

RWA.short: Rwanda and Uganda completed a shared fibre link in 2026; no source found reports it to be switched on yet.
RWA.summary: Uganda's head of Northern Corridor projects said in August 2026 that Uganda and Rwanda made the final fibre connection at the Mirama Hills border earlier in 2026. In the last twelve months, the link was built under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects. Operators on both sides must still agree capacity before it is switched on. Foreign networks are members of the Rwanda Internet Exchange, which is commercial use. No source found says the Mirama Hills link, or any other shared facility, is in service. No data facility run with another country has been found. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

SDN.short: Sudan's fibre link to Egypt, opened in 2004, runs under a 2021 Sudatel and Telecom Egypt agreement; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
SDN.summary: Egypt's minister launched a 400 km fibre cable to Sudan on 26 October 2004, built to carry calls and internet between the two countries. Telecom Egypt and Sudatel signed a cooperation agreement in April 2021 to make better use of that fibre. In the last twelve months, Sudatel, Djibouti Telecom and Ethio telecom signed a tripartite agreement on 4 February 2026 for Horizon, a fibre corridor to Sudan. In September 2026 Horizon was still being presented to carriers before deployment. No source reports work begun on the Sudanese section. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

SEN.short: Senegal's backbone was joined to Mali's in 2026, beside operator links to Gambia and Nigeria; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
SEN.summary: Sonatel and Phase3 activated a fibre route from Dakar to Lagos in May 2025. In the last twelve months, SENUM and SMTD joined their national backbones at the Kidira and Diboli border on 5 October 2026. Gambia's Gamtel holds 28 Gbps with the Senegalese operator Free on a backup link, its profile of September 2026 says. Senegal and Guinea signed a memorandum in November 2025 to work on joining their telecommunications networks, and no contract or works under it have been found. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's backbone link to Guinea, agreed in 2024 and 2025, was working in 2025; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone and Guinea signed an agreement in November 2024 to interconnect their national backbones, the regulator NatCA says. Guinea's SOGEB and Sierra Leone's Leoncom then signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry, published in June 2025. Guinea's telecoms ministry lists the interconnection among four working in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no Sierra Leonean source on its opening has been found. Michcom-IX runs an exchange with points in Freetown, Conakry and Monrovia, but one company runs it, with no agreement between national bodies. No data facility shared with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

SOM.short: Somalia joined a regional World Bank fibre project, effective by 2025; no source found names a Somali party to a working shared link.
SOM.summary: Somalia is one of five recipients of the World Bank's Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project. A June 2026 status report says it became effective for all five between 2023 and 2025. The 2023 grant agreement pays for cross-border links. In the last twelve months, consultancies have prepared fibre deployment in Somalia and Somaliland, and broadband deployment in Somaliland was expected to start in the second half of 2026. No source found says building has begun on the project's links, or names a Somali party to a working shared cable. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

SSD.short: South Sudan signed a connectivity memorandum with Kenya and tendered fibre to its border in 2026; no source found says works began.
SSD.summary: South Sudan and Kenya signed an agreement at the EACO assembly in June 2025 for a 2,420 km fibre link into South Sudan. An August 2025 mission said South Sudan was to tender fibre to the Kenyan and Sudanese borders. In the last twelve months, bids for 397 km on the Juba to Nadapal route closed on 26 October 2026. A World Bank report of June 2026 counts a cross-border connectivity memorandum between Kenya and South Sudan as signed. No source found says a contract was awarded or works began on the fibre to Kenya. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

STP.short: The national operator has been in the ACE cable consortium, in service since 2013; no shared exchange or data centre was found.
STP.summary: The national operator CST joined the ACE cable consortium in 2010 by signing its construction and maintenance agreement. The ACE cable was commercially launched in February 2013 after tests across the 16 countries it connects. The segment from Côte d'Ivoire to São Tomé was among those in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No agreement, memorandum or financing for new shared infrastructure dated in the last three years has been found, nor any exchange point or data facility run with another country. SWZ.summary: No stage is set. An alternative route through Maputo dates from October 2023, and South Africa's Broadband Infraco names no Eswatini party. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports shared infrastructure agreed in the last three years or in service, and none says the country has none. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says Eswatini shares no digital infrastructure with another African country.

SYC.short: Nothing found names infrastructure Seychelles shares with another African country under an agreement, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: Not found. Nothing found names digital infrastructure Seychelles shares with another African country under an agreement. Nothing found says it has none.

TCD.summary: Chad told ITU-D in March 2026 that its 35 km link from N'Djamena to Cameroon is working, interconnected with the network of CAMTEL, Cameroon's state operator. Chad's operator SOTEL has bought capacity from CAMTEL over it since 2015. Chad's section of the trans-Saharan backbone started works in 2023, and in the last twelve months it was 60% complete in February 2026. A planned operator route to Cameroon was suspended by the regulator in February 2026. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

TGO.short: A Lagos to Accra fibre route through Togo was agreed with Beninese and Nigerian partners in 2025; no source found says it is in service.
TGO.summary: CSquared, the Nigerian operator Phase3 and Benin's state infrastructure company SBIN announced a fibre route from Lagos to Accra in May 2025, running through Benin and Togo into Ghana. The partners said it was configured, activated and tested, and gave no date for it to enter service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No Togolese public body has been found as a party to the route. An Ivorian network holds a port at the Lomé exchange TGIX, PeeringDB data of July 2026 show, and a foreign member joining an exchange is commercial use. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

TUN.short: Tunisia and Algeria agreed in 2026 to upgrade their land link; no source found dates it or names the agreement it runs under.
TUN.summary: Tunisian and Algerian delegations on their joint technical commission agreed on 6 June 2026 to upgrade the land link between the two countries. The same commission discussed a new sea cable to Europe. In the last twelve months, the two countries agreed this upgrade, and the source names no contract or start of works, no capacity and no date for it. It calls the land link existing but gives no date or terms for it. No link, exchange point or data facility in service under a named arrangement has been found. Establishing would need a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid in the past three years.

TZA.summary: TTCL and Kenya's ICT Authority launched a fibre link between Dar es Salaam and Mombasa in July 2025, and the two governments officially opened the route at Horohoro. TTCL says it runs at 1.6 terabits a second. In the last twelve months, Tanzania reaffirmed the Kalemie to Kigoma lake cable with Congo in September 2026. On 18 August 2026 its communications ministry reported the Kigoma end of the link 5 per cent built, with completion expected in April 2027. No exchange point or data facility run with another country has been found. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service: a traffic exchange or data storage.

UGA.summary: Uganda and Rwanda made the final fibre connection at the Mirama Hills border earlier in 2026, under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects. In the last twelve months, the same report says, Uganda and Kenya completed a connection at Busia, and an agreement between NITA-U and Kenya's ICT Authority is still to be finalised there. On 11 May 2026 Uganda's ICT ministry and the Congolese telecoms ministry signed a memorandum, one of whose projects joins Uganda's backbone to Congolese fibre. NITA-U and Tanzania's TTCL signed a memorandum on 29 September 2023. No source found says a shared link is in service. Operating would need one kind of shared infrastructure in service under an arrangement both countries are party to.

ZAF.summary: Mozambique's research network MoRENet has a border point in Cape Town, connected to South Africa's research networks TENET and SANReN. It carries Mozambique's international capacity of 60 Gbps, and was described as operational in October 2025. That month WACREN announced a 10 Gbps link from Lagos to the ZAOXI exchange point in Cape Town, through the same networks. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a second kind of shared infrastructure in service, such as an exchange point or data centre shared under an agreement between national bodies.

ZMB.summary: In January 2025 a World Bank document said cross-border infrastructure was missing in Zambia, hindering digital trade. In the last twelve months, Zambia and Mozambique commissioned the Chanida to Cassacatiza fibre interconnector, reported on 23 February 2026. It joins Zambia's national backbone to Mozambique's sea cable network. Zambia's science and technology minister attended the launch of the project with Mozambique on 20 February 2026. No exchange point or data centre shared with another country has been found, No report that building has started on the Lake Tanganyika cable to Burundi has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2016 and has not ratified it.
SLE.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Sierra Leone as having signed it on 29 January 2016, with no ratification or deposit. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates a ratification or accession, and no national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Establishing would need ratification or accession, by a law or decree or by depositing the instrument.

SOM.short: Somalia had not signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention by February 2026; no other shared digital law is known.
SOM.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Somalia. Civil society groups called on the federal government on 20 July 2026 to sign, ratify and deposit. No change in Somalia's position has been found in the last twelve months. No national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Preparing would need a signed African legal text on a digital matter, or a named regional act that binds Somalia.

SSD.short: South Sudan had not signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention by February 2026; no other shared digital law is known.
SSD.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for South Sudan. The register counts 21 signatures and 20 instruments deposited among the Union's 55 member states. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Preparing would need a signed African legal text on a digital matter, or a named regional act that binds South Sudan.

STP.short: Sao Tome and Principe ratified the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2023; no national law giving effect to it is known.
STP.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Sao Tome and Principe as having signed it on 29 January 2016, ratified it on 25 September 2023 and deposited the instrument on 15 February 2024. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

SWZ.short: Eswatini had not signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention by February 2026; no other shared digital law is known.
SWZ.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Eswatini. The minister briefed senators on ratifying the convention on 10 July 2026. No change in Eswatini's signature status has been found in the last twelve months. No national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Preparing would need a signed African legal text on a digital matter, or a named regional act that binds Eswatini.

SYC.short: Seychelles had not signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention by February 2026; no other shared digital law is known.
SYC.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Seychelles. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found, and no licence or signature recognised under one. Preparing would need a signed African legal text on a digital matter, or a named regional act that binds Seychelles.

TCD.short: Chad signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2015 and has not ratified it.
TCD.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Chad as having signed it on 14 June 2015, with no ratification or deposit. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates a ratification or accession, and no national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Establishing would need ratification or accession, by a law or decree or by depositing the instrument.

TGO.short: Togo ratified the African Union's cyber security convention in 2021 and applied a customs data-sharing protocol in 2025; no source found reports cross-border use.
TGO.summary: On 6 March 2025 the Office Togolais des Recettes issued notice 004/2025, applying a protocol on linking customs IT systems. Togo signed it with the Confederation of Sahel States on 23 July 2024. It says a pilot customs link between Togo and Mali, through Burkina Faso, has run on the Lome to Bamako corridor from 10 March 2025. The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Togo's ratification on 30 September 2021. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No report of the customs link in use since the pilot began has been found. Mature would need a shared law reported applied across a border, such as a licence recognised, a request answered, a ruling, or a finding that Togo complies.

TUN.short: Tunisia signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2019 and has not ratified it.
TUN.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Tunisia as having signed it on 23 April 2019, with no ratification or deposit. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates a ratification or accession, and no national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Establishing would need ratification or accession, by a law or decree or by depositing the instrument.

TZA.short: Tanzania's parliament approved acceding to the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in November 2026; no national law giving effect is known.
TZA.summary: The African Union's register of its Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Tanzania. In the last twelve months, on 5 November 2026, Parliament approved the resolution for Tanzania to accede to the convention. No deposit of the instrument of accession is recorded. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

UGA.short: Uganda had ratified the East African ICT networks protocol by 2026; a national law giving effect to it is not found.
UGA.summary: In the last twelve months, Uganda's parliamentary foreign affairs committee said in November 2026 that Uganda has ratified the East African Community Protocol on ICT Networks. The committee said only Uganda and Rwanda have signed and ratified it. The protocol, adopted in 2013, covers infrastructure sharing, cross-border connectivity and cybersecurity. No earlier source on Uganda's ratification has been found, and the date has not been found. The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, shows no signature for Uganda. No national law giving effect to the protocol has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

ZAF.short: South Africa signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2023 and has not ratified it.
ZAF.summary: The African Union's register of 2 February 2026 records that South Africa signed the Malabo Convention on cyber security and personal data protection on 16 February 2023. It records no ratification. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023, with 20 instruments deposited among the Union's 55 members. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law giving effect to a shared African legal text has been found for South Africa. Establishing would need South Africa to ratify the convention.

ZMB.short: Zambia ratified the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention in 2020; no national law giving effect to it is known.
ZMB.summary: The African Union's register of the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026, records Zambia as having signed it on 29 January 2016, ratified it on 15 December 2020 and deposited the instrument on 24 March 2021. The convention has been in force since 8 June 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No national law, decree or regulation passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Operating would need such a law, decree or regulation passed or amended.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe was reported in 2026 to have signed the African Union's cyber security and data protection convention; no ratification is known.
ZWE.summary: The African Union keeps a register of its Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection, known as the Malabo Convention, dated 2 February 2026. It shows no signature, ratification or deposit for Zimbabwe. In the last twelve months MISA said in July 2026 that Zimbabwe has signed the convention and has not ratified it. No date of signature has been found. No national law passed to give effect to a shared African text has been found. Establishing would need ratification or accession, by a law or decree or by depositing the instrument.

AGO.short: Angola signed a communications agreement with Mozambique and hosted southern African radio and cyber meetings in 2026; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
AGO.summary: Angola signed a memorandum of understanding with Mozambique in June 2026 on communications, information technology, information and meteorology. In the last twelve months it also hosted in Luanda the third preparatory meeting of the Southern African Development Community for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference in August 2026. In October 2026 it hosted the seventh SADC Cyber Drill in Luanda, from 5 to 9 October. No source found says anything Angola agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

BDI.short: Burundi joined East Africa's shared roaming area in 2024, and regional figures for 2025 show its cross-border calls more than doubling.
BDI.summary: Burundi entered the East African Community One Network Area on 1 August 2024. Its regulator's rules cut regional roaming tariffs. The regional regulators' organisation reports that inbound cross-border voice traffic rose 126 per cent in 2025, from 89.6 million to 202.9 million minutes. In the last twelve months Burundi took part in the Community's Digital for Development Forum in Arusha in June 2026. In November 2026 an East African Community official named Burundi among six of eight partner states that have put the roaming framework into effect. Its telecoms regulator also took part in an East African Communications Organisation working group in Juba from 23 November 2026.

BEN.short: Benin has had free roaming with Togo and Ghana since 2024, and a 2025 consumer review found calls worked; no source found reports traffic figures.
BEN.summary: Free roaming with Togo took effect on 1 January 2024, and free roaming with Ghana was launched on 9 October 2024. In March 2025 Togolese consumer associations tested it in Cotonou and Porto-Novo. Every test call from Togo's two networks went through, while tariffs, billing and mobile data fell short. In the last twelve months, free roaming with Senegal and Togo together began in Lome on 24 April 2026. No source found gives figures of roaming traffic.

BFA.short: Free roaming among Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, agreed in 2024, was working by September 2026; no source found reports figures of its use.
BFA.summary: Burkina Faso's regulator signed a free roaming memorandum with those of Mali and Niger in Niamey in November 2024. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, it signed a convention with Mali and Niger creating the Council of Sahel Regulators. On 25 September 2026 Niger's regulator head, in Ouagadougou, said free roaming among the three Sahel states was already working. No source gives figures of its use or a decision of the regulators' council. Mature would need figures of its use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what it delivered.

BWA.short: Botswana cut roaming charges with Namibia in 2024 and applied southern Africa's shared roaming tariffs in 2026; no source found reports figures of their use.
BWA.summary: Reduced roaming rates between Botswana and Namibia took effect in August 2024. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, Botswana's operators applied the new One Network Area roaming tariffs, with cuts of 10 to 98.6 per cent. Its communications minister also signed a cooperation memorandum with Namibia in Kasane on 7 August 2026. No source from the last three years gives figures of use or a joint body's decision. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic joined Smart Africa by 2026 and signed Africa's 2025 declaration on artificial intelligence; no agreement of its own is known.
CAF.summary: The Central African Republic joined the Smart Africa Trust Alliance in May 2024. It is listed among the 49 signatories of the Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence of April 2025. In the last twelve months Smart Africa welcomed it as a member in March 2026. No source found dates an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won in the last three years. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

CIV.short: Cote d'Ivoire's free roaming with Ghana, launched in 2023, cut charges for its subscribers; no figures of its use are known.
CIV.summary: Its regulator says free roaming with Ghana, launched on 14 June 2023, cut charges for Ivorian subscribers in Ghana by as much as 90 per cent. In the last twelve months Cote d'Ivoire signed a roaming agreement with Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou on 23 October 2026. In September 2026 it hosted in Abidjan the fourth and last African preparatory meeting of the African Telecommunications Union for the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference. No source found gives figures of the roaming's use. Mature would need figures of its use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what it delivered.

CMR.short: Two Cameroonian operators had free roaming links with Congo and Gabon by 2024, of 213 planned in Central Africa; no source found reports figures of use.
CMR.summary: In April 2024 ARTAC counted two live free roaming links between Central African operators, out of 213 planned. Both involved Cameroon: MTN Cameroon with MTN Congo, and Orange Cameroun with Airtel Gabon. In the last twelve months, on 20 and 21 October 2026, the Central African telecoms regulators fixed the headquarters of their assembly, ARTAC, in Cameroon. No source found gives figures of roaming use or a review of it. Mature would need figures of its use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what it delivered.

COD.short: The DR Congo hosted Central Africa's regulators and won back the African telecommunications union's headquarters in 2026; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
COD.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo hosted in Kinshasa in February 2026 the tenth ordinary session of ARTAC, the Central African telecoms regulators' assembly. At its opening its regulator signed a roaming agreement with Gabon's. The roaming agreement with Gabon was to take effect on 30 June 2026. In the last twelve months the African Telecommunications Union's conference also validated the move of its headquarters from Nairobi to Kinshasa on 23 July 2026. No source found says the roaming agreement has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

COG.short: Congo has had free roaming with Gabon since 2019, and its regulator published monthly call counts to 2024.
COG.summary: Free roaming with Gabon went into service for voice on 15 October 2019, and later took in text messages and data. Congo's regulator publishes monthly Congo-Gabon roaming call counts from January 2020 to December 2024. December 2024 had 81,563 calls. In the last twelve months the Republic of the Congo was elected to the 25-member council of the African Telecommunications Union on 24 July 2026. Brazzaville hosted the CEMAC council of ministers on 13 June 2026.

COM.short: The regulator reported cooperation agreements with four African regulators in 2025; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
COM.summary: In July 2025 the regulator ANRTIC reported cooperation agreements with four other regulators, those of Madagascar, Senegal, Morocco and Mauritius. No signing dates are given. In the last twelve months delegates from Comoros took part in a SADC workshop on data governance in Harare in August 2026. On 24 July 2026 the African Union's development agency launched a programme for island economies that names Comoros. No source found says anything Comoros agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's operators charged West Africa's regional roaming tariffs by 2024; no source found says how much the roaming is used.
CPV.summary: In November 2024 Praia hosted the sixteenth meeting of the West African regulators' focal points on regional roaming. ECOWAS reported that Cabo Verde's mobile operators offer roaming at the tariffs the regional roaming regulation sets. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, Cabo Verde's data protection authority sat on the fifth board of the Network of African Data Protection Authorities. No source found gives figures of roaming use. Mature would need figures of its use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what it delivered.

DJI.short: Djibouti hosted an African Union forum in December 2025 that adopted a digital economy declaration; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
DJI.summary: Djibouti joined the Eastern Africa regional digital integration project, which is to lay terrestrial fibre along the northern road corridor. In the last twelve months it hosted the sixteenth African Union Private Sector Forum on 8 to 10 December 2025. Its officials attended the East Africa regional data governance workshop in Nairobi in June 2026. The fibre is not reported as built or lit. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

DZA.short: Algeria has a joint communications commission with Tunisia, which met for the fourth time in June 2026; no source reports figures of use or results.
DZA.summary: Algeria and Tunisia have a standing joint technical commission on communications. Its fourth session in June 2026 agreed joint projects, and none is reported as started. In the last twelve months, on 6 to 8 December 2025, African ministers meeting in Algiers adopted the Algiers Declaration on fair, safe and responsible digital platforms. No source from the last three years gives figures of use or a joint body's decision. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

EGY.short: Egypt says it contributed to the African Union's artificial intelligence strategy, stated in 2026; no agreement or seat in an African body is known.
EGY.summary: Egypt's assistant foreign minister for African affairs said on 22 September 2026 that Egypt contributed to developing the African Union's continental artificial intelligence strategy, and that Egypt continues to work on it. That statement was made in the last twelve months. Nothing Egypt has done at home under the strategy is reported. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

ERI.short: Nothing found shows Eritrea's part in an African body that makes digital policy, or an agreement, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names the country's part in an African body that makes digital policy, or an agreement. Nothing found says it stands outside.

ETH.short: Ethiopia signed a three-year digital identity memorandum with Mozambique in April 2026 and holds one with Zambia; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
ETH.summary: In the last twelve months, on 27 April 2026, Ethiopia's national identity programme signed a three-year memorandum of understanding on digital identity with Mozambique's digital transformation agency. In September 2026 Ethiopia sent representatives to the East African regional digital integration workshop in Nairobi. No identity service or exchange is reported as started under the memorandum. No source found says anything Ethiopia agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

GAB.short: Gabon has free roaming with Central African neighbours and launched the Smart Africa Digital Academy in 2026; no source found says how far either is used.
GAB.summary: ARCEP says Gabon has opened free roaming with Rwanda, Congo, Togo and Cameroon, as of February 2025. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, it signed a roaming agreement with the Congolese regulator at ARTAC's session in Kinshasa. It removes roaming charges between Gabon and the DRC from 30 June 2026. In October 2026 Gabon was elected third vice-chair of its bureau at the African Union's technical committee on communication and ICT in Libreville. No source found gives figures of roaming use. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

GHA.short: Ghana's free roaming with Benin and Togo started in 2024 and with Liberia in 2026; no source reports figures of its use.
GHA.summary: Free roaming between Benin and Ghana took effect on 1 July 2024. In the last twelve months Ghana concluded its agreement with Liberia in May 2026, and Liberian subscribers have roamed in Ghana without charges since 17 July 2026. Ghana's minister took the chair of the African Union's ICT committee on 29 October 2026. No source found gives figures of roaming use. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

GIN.short: Guinea hosted Smart Africa's summit in November 2025 and signed a roaming protocol with Sierra Leone; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
GIN.summary: Guinea hosted the seventh Transform Africa Summit of the Smart Africa Alliance in Conakry in November 2025. There Sierra Leone's regulator and Guinea signed a protocol introducing free mobile roaming between the two countries. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, a regional platform of regulators that Guinea's audiovisual regulator belongs to issued a communique with Niger's regulator. Free roaming with Sierra Leone is not reported as started. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

GMB.short: The Gambia's free roaming with Senegal began in December 2025 and with Liberia in July 2026; no source reports figures of its use.
GMB.summary: Free roaming between Senegal and The Gambia was introduced in December 2025, with calls received free and made at local rates for up to 30 days. In the last twelve months The Gambia and Senegal signed a memorandum of understanding on telecommunications, information technology and the digital economy in Dakar on 12 June 2026. The first steering committee under it met in Banjul in August 2026 to set a roadmap. No source found gives figures of roaming use. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau joined a Lusophone data workshop in 2025 and endorsed African proposals for the 2026 ITU conference; no agreement is known.
GNB.summary: ECOWAS names Guinea-Bissau among the countries carrying out the West Africa regional digital integration programme, declared effective in March 2024. In the last twelve months its regulators and policymakers took part in a data governance workshop for Portuguese-speaking African countries in December 2025. On 16 October 2026 the African Telecommunications Union reported the country among 23 states that have endorsed the 49 African Common Proposals. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years is recorded. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea held the rotating presidency of the Central African community in 2026; nothing it agreed is known to be in effect.
GNQ.summary: Equatorial Guinea is listed among the 49 countries that signed the Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence at Kigali on 4 April 2025. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, it held the rotating presidency of ECCAS, the Economic Community of Central African States. The Statistical Commission for Africa elected Equatorial Guinea to chair it for 2026 to 2028 at its tenth session in Addis Ababa. No source found says anything Equatorial Guinea agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

KEN.short: Kenya is in East Africa's shared roaming area, and regional figures for 2025 show its cross-border calls rising by about a fifth.
KEN.summary: The regional regulators' organisation publishes Kenya's One Network Area cross-border voice figures for 2025. Inbound calls ran to 461.5 million minutes, up 19.2 per cent, and outbound to 603.5 million. In the last twelve months Kenya's central bank signed a memorandum with Rwanda's in March 2026. It lets payment providers licensed in one state operate in the other. In November 2026 an East African Community official named Kenya among six of eight partner states that have put the roaming framework into effect.

LBR.short: Liberia's free roaming with Sierra Leone began in 2025 and with Ghana and The Gambia in 2026; no source reports figures of its use.
LBR.summary: Free roaming between Liberia and Sierra Leone took effect in August 2025, with calls at local rates across the border. In the last twelve months, in Accra on 30 April 2026, Liberia signed free roaming memoranda with Ghana and Sierra Leone. On 17 July 2026 its regulator launched free roaming with Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia. No source found gives figures of its use. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

LBY.short: Libya sent a delegation to the African telecommunications union's conference in July 2026; no digital agreement, meeting hosted or seat won is known.
LBY.summary: Libya's General Authority for Communications and Informatics sent a delegation to the seventh plenipotentiary conference of the African Telecommunications Union. The conference was held in Abuja in July 2026, within the last twelve months. Attending a meeting is not an agreement signed or a seat won. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

LSO.short: Lesotho's operators cut roaming prices under southern Africa's One Network Area in 2026; no source found says how much the roaming is used.
LSO.summary: Botswana's regulator says Lesotho's mobile operators cut roaming prices for data, voice and SMS by 10 to 98.6% under southern Africa's One Network Area, reported in March 2026. In the last twelve months Lesotho's minister chaired the African Union's ICT committee until 29 October 2026. Lesotho also held a validation workshop in Maseru on Smart Africa's national data blueprint. No figures of roaming use have been found. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

MAR.short: Morocco won a seat on the African telecommunications union's council in July 2026; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
MAR.summary: Morocco is one of three pilot countries for the continental free trade area's cross-border data exchange system, announced in May 2026. The pilot is not reported as running. In the last twelve months Morocco was elected to the administrative council of the African Telecommunications Union for 2027 to 2031 in July 2026. Morocco holds the permanent secretariat of the African Network of Data Protection Authorities, whose new bureau first met in Rabat in September 2026. No source found says anything Morocco agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

MDG.short: Madagascar took part in African Union and southern African training and meetings, most recently in 2026; no agreement, meeting hosted or seat won is known.
MDG.summary: Madagascar joined the Smart Africa Trust Alliance at Barcelona in February 2024, its digital minister signing the accession. In the last twelve months a delegation attended the Southern African Development Community's public service assembly in August 2026. Beyond that accession, no agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years is recorded. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

MLI.short: Free roaming among Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger was working by September 2026; no source found says how much it is used.
MLI.summary: In November 2024 Mali's regulator signed a free roaming memorandum with those of Burkina Faso and Niger in Niamey. In the last twelve months it signed a convention with the regulators of Burkina Faso and Niger, reported in September 2026. On 25 September 2026 Niger's regulator said free roaming among Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger was already working. The council the convention created is not reported meeting. No figures of roaming use have been found. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

MOZ.short: Mozambique signed a communications memorandum with Angola in 2026; nothing it agreed is known to be in effect.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique and Angola signed a memorandum on communications and information technology in June 2026. It provides for technical cooperation and exchanges. In the last twelve months Mozambique's customs and those of four neighbours adopted a plan for customs data exchange on 26 August 2026. On 12 October 2026 INTIC was elected to the ANCA-CERT committee for southern Africa. Nothing is reported as started under the memorandum. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

MRT.short: Mauritania's data protection authority signed a cooperation convention with Morocco's in January 2026; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
MRT.summary: In the last twelve months Mauritania's data protection authority and Morocco's data protection commission signed a cooperation convention in Marrakech in January 2026. It provides for exchanges of expertise and experience, and none is reported as having taken place. In April 2026 Mauritania was among the states at the general assembly of the West African telecommunications regulators' association in Lome. No source found says anything Mauritania agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

MUS.short: Mauritius belongs to SADC, Smart Africa and COMESA's payment system as at 2026; no agreement, hosting or seat in the last three years is dated.
MUS.summary: Mauritius hosted southern Africa's first regional cyber drill at Ebene in September 2018. Nothing adopted from it is reported. In the last twelve months Smart Africa welcomed it as a new member in March 2026. The central bank governor says the Bank of Mauritius settles COMESA's regional payment system, as at July 2026. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

MWI.short: Operators in Malawi cut roaming prices under SADC's shared network area in 2026; no source found reports figures of its use.
MWI.summary: A March 2026 report cites Botswana's regulator: mobile operators in Malawi introduced roaming price cuts of 10 to 98.6 per cent under SADC's One Network Area. In the last twelve months Malawi's regulator hosted its 46th executive committee meeting at Mangochi on 14 to 16 September 2026, of the Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa. It holds the rotating chair of the association. No figures of use of the cheaper roaming have been found. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

NAM.short: Namibia cut roaming charges with Botswana in August 2024 and signed a cooperation memorandum with it in 2026; no source found reports figures of use.
NAM.summary: Botswana's regulator says Botswana and Namibia were the first in SADC to bring in reduced and harmonised roaming rates, in August 2024. In the last twelve months Namibia's and Botswana's ministers signed a cooperation memorandum in Kasane in August 2026. Namibia's regulator hosted the first legal and policy committee meeting of the Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa on 10 to 12 August 2026. No source found gives figures of use or a joint body's decision. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

NER.short: Free roaming among Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali, agreed in 2024, was working by September 2026; no source found reports figures of its use.
NER.summary: Niger's regulator signed a free roaming memorandum with those of Burkina Faso and Mali in Niamey in November 2024. In the last twelve months, on 25 September 2026, it signed the protocol in Ouagadougou creating the Council of Sahel Regulators. Its regulator head said free roaming among the three Sahel states was already working. In October 2026 Ecofin reported no recent confirmation that the roaming agreement announced for January 2025 was working. Mature would need figures of its use, a council decision, or a review of what it delivered.

NGA.short: Nigeria hosted the African telecommunications union's conference in July 2026 and took its chair; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
NGA.summary: Nigeria hosted the seventh conference of plenipotentiaries of the African Telecommunications Union in Abuja in July 2026. The conference adopted the Abuja Declaration on Meaningful Connectivity. In the last twelve months Nigeria also hosted the second digital trade forum of the continental free trade area in Lagos on 1 and 2 July 2026. In September 2026 it initialled a digital cooperation communique with Chad. No source found says anything Nigeria agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

RWA.short: Rwanda is in East Africa's shared roaming area, with rising cross-border calls reported for 2025, and hosted the 2025 summit behind Africa's artificial intelligence declaration.
RWA.summary: The regional regulators' organisation publishes Rwanda's One Network Area cross-border voice figures for 2025. Inbound calls ran to 107.4 million minutes, up 41 per cent, and outbound to 74 million. In the last twelve months Rwanda's central bank signed a memorandum with Kenya's in March 2026. In November 2026 an East African Community official named Rwanda among six of eight partner states that have put the roaming framework into effect. Its national identity system was connected through Smart Africa's data exchange, with those of Benin and Ghana, reported in October 2026.

SDN.short: Sudan is listed on Africa's 2025 declaration on artificial intelligence; no agreement or role of its own is known.
SDN.summary: Sudan is listed among the 49 countries that signed the Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence at Kigali on 4 April 2025. In the last twelve months Sudan was among the 23 states that had endorsed the 49 African Common Proposals for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026. The African Telecommunications Union reported this on 16 October 2026. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

SEN.short: Senegal's roaming arrangement took effect in April 2026 and a regional backbone council was installed in October 2026; no source found reports figures of use.
SEN.summary: Free roaming between Senegal, Togo and Benin took effect on 24 April 2026, with incoming calls free for up to 30 days. In the last twelve months Senegal and The Gambia signed a memorandum of understanding on telecommunications, information technology and the digital economy in Dakar on 12 June 2026. On 23 October 2026 Senegal signed a roaming agreement with Burkina Faso in Ouagadougou. No published figures of use have been found. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone introduced free roaming with Liberia in 2025 and signed more roaming agreements in 2025 and 2026; no figures of its use are known.
SLE.summary: Liberia's regulator says the free roaming agreement with Sierra Leone took effect in August 2025, with calls at local rates across the border. In the last twelve months Sierra Leone entered the West African free roaming agreement with Liberia and Ghana, reported in February 2026. In July 2026 Liberia launched free roaming with Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia. No source found gives figures of use. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

SOM.short: Somalia consulted operators in 2025 on East Africa's shared roaming area but had not joined by 2026; no agreement, hosted meeting or seat is known.
SOM.summary: Somalia is a full East African Community member since 4 March 2024. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, an East African Community official said Somalia had yet to put the 2014 One Network Area roaming framework into effect. He said it had committed to aligning its rules with it. In April 2026 Somalia presented its plan for adopting artificial intelligence at a meeting of the East African Science and Technology Commission. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

SSD.short: South Sudan is in East Africa's shared roaming area, its traffic up 900 times across members by 2023; no source found reports South Sudan's own figures.
SSD.summary: In November 2023 the Northern Corridor ICT ministers, South Sudan's among them, reported the One Network Area for voice, data and SMS in operation. Traffic among the partner states had risen over 900 times. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, an East African Community official named South Sudan among six of eight partner states that have put the 2014 One Network Area roaming framework into effect. On 23 November 2026 its communication authority hosted and opened an East African Communications Organisation working group meeting in Juba. No figures of South Sudan's own traffic have been found.

STP.short: Sao Tome and Principe joined the Central African regulators' assembly in 2026 and attends Lusophone data workshops; no agreement of its own is known.
STP.summary: In March 2025 Sao Tome and Principe was one of ten countries selected for Smart Africa's project on digital payments and e-commerce policy. In the last twelve months its regulator joined the Central African telecoms regulators' assembly as its eighth member in Libreville on 21 October 2026. Its regulators took part in a data governance workshop in Maputo on 8 to 10 December 2025. No agreement signed, meeting hosted or chaired, or seat won in the last three years has been found. Establishing would need an agreement signed, a meeting hosted or chaired, or a seat won.

SWZ.short: Eswatini's regulator signed a cooperation agreement with Lesotho's in October 2026; no source found says whether any agreement has been put into effect.
SWZ.summary: In the last twelve months Eswatini's communications regulator signed a memorandum of understanding with the Lesotho Communications Authority on 3 October 2026. It covers information exchange, joint research, training and cybersecurity cooperation. In June 2025 its ICT minister and South Africa's signed a declaration of intent in Pretoria. Nothing done under the memorandum is reported. No source found says anything Eswatini agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

SYC.short: Seychelles signed a digital trade memorandum with the African free trade area's secretariat in March 2026; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
SYC.summary: The government of Seychelles signed a memorandum of understanding on digital trade with the secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area and a company in March 2026. In the last twelve months it took part in the Southern African Development Community's data governance forum, held in Seychelles in May 2026. On 31 August 2026 the joint venture agreement for the digital trade corridor was signed in Accra. The corridor is not reported as operating. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

TCD.short: Chad hosted a regional internet governance forum in October 2026 and initialled a Nigeria communique; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
TCD.summary: Gabon's regulator said in February 2025 that free roaming with Chad, under a protocol signed in 2021, had been interrupted. In the last twelve months Chad hosted the closing of the 2026 Central Africa Internet Governance Forum in N'Djamena on 15 October 2026. In September 2026 Chad's and Nigeria's communications ministers initialled a final communique setting out a digital cooperation framework. No roaming cut is reported in force. Operating would need something agreed put into effect.

TGO.short: Togo's free roaming with Senegal and Benin began in April 2026; no source found reports figures of its use.
TGO.summary: Free roaming with Benin had taken effect on 1 January 2024. In the last twelve months the free roaming arrangement between Senegal, Togo and Benin took effect on 24 April 2026 in Lome, with free incoming calls for up to 30 consecutive days. In April 2026 the head of Togo's regulator was elected president of the West Africa Telecommunications Regulators Assembly. No published figures of use have been found. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

TUN.short: Tunisia has a joint communications commission with Algeria, which met for the fourth time in June 2026; no source reports figures of use or results.
TUN.summary: Tunisia and Algeria have a standing joint technical commission on communications. Its fourth session, held in Tunisia in June 2026, agreed joint projects, and none is reported as started. In the last twelve months Tunisia was elected on 24 July 2026 to the administrative council of the African Telecommunications Union. Its National Frequency Agency hosted in Tunis in September 2026 the Union's third African preparatory meeting for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

TZA.short: Tanzania hosted regional meetings in October 2026 and is in East Africa's shared roaming area, with 2025 outbound cross-border calls up by more than half.
TZA.summary: The regional regulators' organisation reports Tanzania's cross-border voice traffic under the One Network Area for 2025. Inbound calls ran to 148 million minutes, up 36.4 per cent. Outbound calls rose 59 per cent to 577.7 million. In the last twelve months, on 14 October 2026, Tanzania hosted the fifth East African Communications Organisation postal and logistics meeting in Arusha. In November 2026 an East African Community official named Tanzania among six of eight partner states that have put the roaming framework into effect.

UGA.short: Uganda chaired an East African e-commerce meeting in 2026 and won a seat on the African telecommunications union's council; 2025 roaming-area call figures are published.
UGA.summary: The regional regulators' organisation reports Uganda's inbound cross-border voice traffic under it fell 28 per cent in 2025, from 1,103.2 million to 794.4 million minutes. The report puts this down to internet calling replacing voice. In the last twelve months Uganda was elected to a four-year seat on the administrative council of the African Telecommunications Union in Abuja on 24 July 2026. In November 2026 the regional affairs minister told Parliament about the East African Payment System. It links the national RTGS payment systems of Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda.

ZAF.short: South Africa signed a digital cooperation declaration with Eswatini in 2025; nothing agreed is known to be in effect.
ZAF.summary: In June 2025 South Africa's ICT minister signed a declaration of intent on digital cooperation with Eswatini, covering policy harmonisation, broadband, cybersecurity and data protection. Its 2026/27 budget provides 2.073 million rand for membership of the African Telecommunications Union. In the last twelve months, it hosted and chaired the Southern African Development Community's summit in August 2026, with digitised borders a priority of its chairship. No border system is reported as started under that priority. No source found says anything South Africa agreed has been put into effect. Operating would need an agreement put into effect.

ZMB.short: Zambia's operators cut roaming charges with Southern African neighbours in 2026; no source found reports figures of use.
ZMB.summary: Botswana's regulator says Zambia put the framework into effect jointly with Botswana, with roaming data prices to Zambian networks cut by 82 to 93 per cent, reported in March 2026. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, Zambia's regulator said operators in the area had cut roaming tariffs by 3 to 93 per cent. In November 2026 Zambia hosted the COMESA workshop that validated a regional digital inclusion strategy. Figures of use of the lower tariffs are not recorded. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's operators cut roaming charges under the Southern African single network area in 2026; no source found reports figures of use.
ZWE.summary: Citing Botswana's regulator, a March 2026 report says Zimbabwe's mobile operators introduced roaming price cuts of 10 to 98.6 per cent under SADC's One Network Area. In the last twelve months Zimbabwe's ministry hosted in Harare the Southern African Development Community's regional workshop on data governance in August 2026. Its ICT minister chairs Smart Africa's council of ICT ministers, reported in August 2026. Figures of use of the lower tariffs are not recorded. Mature would need figures of use, a joint body's decision, or a review of what was delivered.

AGO.short: Since 2023 births are entered digitally at offices in Luanda and three other cities; no source reports most offices use paper, and the digital count.
AGO.summary: Presidential Decree 267/24 of 28 November 2024 approved a plan to December 2026 for a single database fed daily by civil registration. Births have been registered in RCI since 2023 at civil registration posts. As of 2024, RCI is in Luanda's registries and in one post each in Huambo, Benguela and Lubango. In the last twelve months, Novo Jornal reported on 5 May 2026 that identification and civil registration posts in almost the whole country had been without their system. No count of the offices registering in RCI has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

BDI.short: Digital civil registration runs in about twelve pilot communes in 2026, most acts still on paper; no source says how the pilot record is made.
BDI.summary: On 18 July 2026 the interior ministry's presentation records a pilot digitalisation project in 12 communes. The same presentation says the majority of civil-status acts are still recorded in physical registers. The project launched at Rumonge on 19 July 2024 is for the digital registration of births and deaths at the commune's civil status service. In the last twelve months, on 6 May 2026 the ministry presented a digital platform for civil registration and biometric identity card production. No source has been found that says the system is past its pilot, or how the pilot record is made. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

BEN.short: In 2023, 174 civil-status centres in five departments were equipped for digital birth registration; no source found reports the share of offices registering.
BEN.summary: From 20 August 2025 the declaration and registration of a birth are done on site in about ten public health facilities. In 2023 174 of 233 civil-status centres in five departments were equipped for birth registration. In the last twelve months, ANIP's director general gave an account of the pilot on 16 July 2026. The pilot ended in February 2026 and a consolidation phase is running in the same ten facilities. No share of local offices registering births digitally has been found, and no plan with a period. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

BFA.short: Birth-entry software was deployed in 170 civil registration centres in 2025; the total number of centres, and no source says how many register in it,.
BFA.summary: The ministry reported the software deployed in 30 main and 140 secondary centres in 2025. In 2024 it was in 20 main and 96 secondary centres. In the last twelve months, agents of the commune of Koloko were trained on the software and given equipment, as reported on 22 June 2026. On 25 June 2026 the director general for the modernisation of civil status said deployment in communes was continuing. No total of centres has been found, and no source says how many of the 170 register in the software. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

BWA.short: A national system registered births and deaths in 2024; no source found says how many of the 35 district offices enter records in it.
BWA.summary: Statistics Botswana reported in August 2026 that the department operates 35 district registration offices and 17 on-site registration points at hospitals and clinics. Electronic on-site registration had opened in 13 hospitals by September 2015. In the last twelve months, the minister told Parliament on 6 March 2026 of about 15 hospital kiosks for on-site birth registration. He said 9 were operating and 6 had closed. No count of the district offices entering records in the system has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

CAF.short: A civil registration application was still being developed in July 2026 and offices register on paper; no source found reports the number of pilot offices.
CAF.summary: The director general for decentralisation and civil status described an all-paper system on 18 July 2026, with 70% of civil registration centres without electricity. In the last twelve months, the territorial administration ministry said in July 2026 that it is preparing the deployment of a civil registration application with CIVIPOL as technical operator. An operational map of 45 centres had been validated by 18 July 2026. No office has been found entering a birth or a death digitally, and no count of pilot offices. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

CIV.short: In March 2026 the registrar said 98 per cent of civil status centres were computerised; no share of centres registering births digitally has been found.
CIV.summary: ONECI's director general said in July 2024 that 298 centres were connected to the central City Web system. The World Bank said on 18 September 2025 that the registry is still on paper. In the last twelve months, ONECI gave every town hall and sub-prefecture centre computers carrying the software. On 23 October 2026 its director general said it is deployed in all centres, with connectivity still a problem. No share of centres registering births in the software has been found, and the 298 comes with no total. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

CMR.short: In September 2026, 60 of 432 principal civil status centres were digitised, 13.9 per cent; no source found reports the share of all local offices.
CMR.summary: On 14 September 2026 BUNEC's Director General counted that 60 of 432 principal civil status centres were digitised, 13.9 per cent. The count was 42 in April 2022. On 8 October 2026 he described paper as dominant. In the last twelve months, by August 2026 two East Region centres, Bertoua 1er and the Bertoua City Council, were in production. No share of all local offices has been found, since the 60 are counted against principal centres only. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

COD.short: In August 2025 one commune of the capital was piloting digital civil registration; no source says whether any birth or death has been registered digitally.
COD.summary: UNFPA reported on 18 August 2025 that one commune, Masina in Kinshasa, has a pilot at its municipal civil-status office. The pilot aims to automate the collection and management of data on births, marriages and deaths. Terms of reference posted on 3 April 2026 state that the civil registers are mostly manual. In the last twelve months, a UNDP tender closing on 25 April 2026 sought a consultant to assess the digitalisation of civil registration. No source has been found that says any birth or death has been registered digitally. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

COG.short: A civil registration system was built and validated by September 2026 but no office uses it; no source says whether older urban systems still run.
COG.summary: On 22 September 2026 ACSI, the agency that built the system Congo calls SIFEC, handed the system's operating documents to the territorial administration directorate. After the handover seven steps remained, user training and deployment among them. In the last twelve months, on 20 February 2026 a workshop at Kintélé validated 17 recommendations on SIFEC. In 2021 the World Bank found electronic records stored locally in some centres of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. No office has been found using SIFEC, and nothing since 2021 says whether those local records are still kept. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

COM.short: In 2026 offices register on paper while a digital system is studied and costed; no source found says when its three-centre pilot starts.
COM.summary: The Ministry of the Interior's strategic plan for modernising civil registration runs from 2024 to 2028. Births, marriages and deaths are registered in paper registers, and the digital system, an eCRVS, is only proposed, by a preliminary study. In the last twelve months, the study was launched in Moroni on 2 October 2025 and validated on 25 March 2026. On 11 March 2026 the Council of Ministers did not adopt the draft decree for a national civil status agency. No source has been found that says when the pilot starts, or that any office keeps records other than on paper. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

CPV.short: In 2017 offices in all 22 municipalities entered births and deaths digitally, in urban centres only; no source says whether records reach the national register.
CPV.summary: UNICEF's profile, compiled to November 2017, states that all vital events are recorded directly in the computer. It puts the applications in the conservatórias of all 22 municipalities. Registration stations exist only in the urban centres of those municipalities. The Civil Registry Code of 2014 requires entries in electronic form, held in a national civil registry database. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of offices newer than 2017 has been found. Nothing shows whether the entry made at the conservatória reaches the national register. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

DJI.short: Nine civil-status sites in Djibouti-Ville have entered births and deaths digitally since 2011, as stated in 2024; no source reports digital entry outside the capital.
DJI.summary: The Ville de Djibouti stated on 28 April 2024 that the registration of births, marriages, divorces and deaths in Djibouti-Ville has rested since 2011 on software. Terms of reference of February 2024 list nine civil-status sites, all in Djibouti-Ville. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A 2025 ESCWA survey, found only in summary, says local offices hold no electronic records of births or deaths. Nothing dated 2025 or 2026 says any office outside Djibouti-Ville enters digitally, and no national count of offices has been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

DZA.short: Births are registered in a national digital register across 1,541 communes, a 2019 count; no source found reports the share of local offices entering digitally.
DZA.summary: Law 14-08 of 9 August 2014 creates the national automated civil-status register under the Ministry of the Interior and Local Authorities. The ministry's deck of 19 June 2019 shows 1,541 commune databases where entry, control and update are done. Under the 2014 law each commune still inscribes acts on three paper registers kept in duplicate. In the last twelve months the register was cited and not changed. In July 2026 the ministry presented it as its own, created in 2014. No total of local offices has been found against the 1,541. No source says the entry is made at the commune office at registration. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

EGY.short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at 4,571 health offices, as stated in 2026; no source found reports the share of all offices.
EGY.summary: Egypt's presentation to the 2026 APAI-CRVS registrars-general meeting gives full nationwide automation of 4,571 health offices across the 27 governorates. A conference paper on the system implemented in 2017 states that data entry is done at the health office. The planning ministry's report of 2 August 2025 says 4,666 health offices are electronically linked. In the last twelve months, on 20 January 2026 the health ministry instructed all health affairs directorates to unify and improve their data's quality. No total of health offices has been found against either count. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

ERI.short: Births and deaths were handwritten at local offices and entered in regional electronic registers one level up in 2017; no source found reports current practice.
ERI.summary: Eritrea's five-year Strategic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Plan for 2024-2028 is recorded by the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child in observations adopted in April 2026. A Dutch foreign ministry report of February 2017 says births and deaths are registered in the sub-zoba's digital database after entry in the kebabi's handwritten register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on how a birth is entered today. No count of offices doing the digital entry has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

ETH.short: Digital registration of births and deaths is in pilot, in Addis Ababa and 1,300 of 19,202 kebeles in 2025; no source reports use beyond pilots.
ETH.summary: In July 2026 Ethiopia's rollout of its national eCRVS begins with a pilot in Addis Ababa, then Amharic-speaking regions, then the rest of the country. A tablet system, ME-CRVS, has been piloted in 1,300 kebeles and health facilities. In January 2025 the city agency's digitisation was in a pilot phase in 21 of 116 woredas. In the last twelve months, the mayor of Addis Ababa launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology on 5 December 2025.
