He announced full implementation in 50 woredas from 8 December. No source has been found that shows any digital system past its pilot outside Addis Ababa. None gives the rollout phase reached by July 2026. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

GAB.short: No office registered births or deaths digitally in May 2026; a system is being prepared with funding to 2028; no source reports its first offices.
GAB.summary: Law 008/2022 of 15 June 2022 makes the Centre National de l'Etat Civil (CNEC) the public service that builds the digital, biometric and centralised civil register. The World Bank described the civil registry as entirely paper-based in June 2021. In the last twelve months, on 28 September 2026 an inter-ministerial workshop opened at Ntoum to define the conditions for putting the CNEC into operation. A mapping exercise to prioritise the departments whose offices will register digitally was under way at 31 May 2026. No pilot office has been named, and the CNEC is not yet in operation. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

GHA.short: Births were registered digitally at two Accra registry centres in 2024; no source says how many offices do so, and how the record is made,.
GHA.summary: The Births and Deaths Registry develops and administers the births and deaths registration system under Act 1027 of 2020. Births in Ablekuma West, a municipal district of Greater Accra, are registered on the Registry's digital registration platform, which registered 1,722 of them from March to October 2024. In April 2025 the Acting Registrar said the Registry was taking steps to digitise all offices. In the last twelve months, in 2026, the Eastern Regional Registrar said officers are expected to complete birth registrations digitally in communities. No national count or share of local offices entering births digitally has been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, into the national register.

GIN.short: Commune offices made digital birth certificates in September 2026, when a paper shortage halted printing; no source found says how many offices do so.
GIN.summary: Guinea's 2023 civil status law makes the ministry in charge of civil status responsible for the equipment of civil status centres. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the territorial administration ministry launched the RENEC civil status register project through ONECI. RENEC is paid for from the national development budget. On 2 September 2026 Ratoma commune's civil status officer said commune offices establish digital birth certificates on secure paper. Printing had stopped for about two weeks because the paper had run out. No count or share of offices has been found, and no source says the entry is made at the office. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally when they are registered.

GMB.short: Births are registered on a central digital system, with 79 local offices holding digital registers in 2025; no source reports the total number of offices.
GMB.summary: The Registrar General said that by June 2026 over 1.4 million people were registered in the system he calls the eCRVS. They were issued a birth certificate. A 2025 World Bank diagnostic counts 79 civil registration offices with digitalised registers issuing birth certificates in 2025. In the last twelve months, a Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Bill had its first reading in the National Assembly on 5 March 2026. The total number of civil registration offices has not been found, so the 79 have no share. No source states that the record is keyed at the registration point when the birth is registered. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, shown by a share or a count with its total.

GNB.short: One Bissau office registers births and deaths digitally in 2026, and health posts in three regions register births; no source reports the share of offices.
GNB.summary: The system the country calls SIREC was implemented at the Ministry of Justice's Direção-Geral de Identificação Civil, Registo e Notariado, launched in January 2025. In the last twelve months, in the first quarter of 2026, Santa Luzia became the first civil registry office in the country to operate entirely digitally. In June 2026 a mobile caravan was to take birth registration on SIREC to 16 communities. The statistics office counts 13 conservatórias and 80 registry posts in its yearbook for 2018 to 2022. The number of offices and posts entering records digitally, set against that total, has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally into the national register.

GNQ.short: A digital pilot registers births in Malabo only; in 2025 a system to register newborns from hospitals was set up, its reach not known.
GNQ.summary: The Ministry of Justice put the system it calls SIREC into service in December 2018, with the support of UNICEF and the European Union. The World Bank said in 2024 that the pilot in Malabo allows the digital registration of new births. It said the seven regional offices collect and store data on paper. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the state IT centre CNIAPGE told parliament that in 2025 it had set up a new system to register newborns from hospitals. How the pilot and the hospital system make the record has not been found. Nor has the number of offices using them. Establishing would need births entered digitally when they are registered, past the pilot, in some local offices.

KEN.short: More than 270,000 births were registered digitally from hospitals in two months of 2026; no source says how many offices or hospitals use the system.
KEN.summary: Civil Registration Services sits in the Ministry of Interior and National Administration's State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services, under an executive order of January 2023. In the last twelve months, ESTDEV said in September 2026 that more than 270,000 births were registered in two months through the new digital birth registration solution. Parents confirm the birth and enter the data while still in the hospital. The Star reported in March 2026 that the Civil Registration Service led the validation of the Births and Deaths Registration Bill 2025. The number of hospitals or offices using the system has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally when they are registered.

LBR.short: County teams registered births online in 2024, with deaths added to the platform; no source found says how many of the 58 centres enter them.
LBR.summary: The Ministry of Health registers and certifies births and deaths through its Bureau of Vital Statistics, by its report for 2024. The report says birth and death registration have been integrated into the DHIS2 platform. In May 2024 the World Bank found most services at the 15 County Service Centers remained paper-based. UNICEF Liberia in December 2024 counted birth registration services in all 15 counties and 58 centres. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how many of the 58 centres enter births on the platform. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a published share or a count given with its total.

LBY.short: All civil registration offices were automated and linked to one database, the health ministry said in 2022; no source says whether events are entered there.
LBY.summary: The Civil Registration Authority manages the collection of births and deaths data and issues the legal documents, the 2022 vital statistics report says. The report states that all of the Authority's offices are fully automated and electronically linked to its centre. It counts 12 branches, 133 issuing offices and at least 380 service offices. In the last twelve months, on 1 March 2026, the Attorney General's office reported that he had discussed the project to create the electronic civil registry database with the head of the Authority. Whether a birth is entered at the office when it is registered has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

LSO.short: Births were registered digitally at 30 health-facility stations in three districts in 2026; no source found reports the total number of local offices.
LSO.summary: The Department of National Identity and Civil Registry, in the Ministry of Home Affairs, is the lead agency for civil registration, it said in July 2026. In the last twelve months, UNICEF Lesotho reported on 5 August 2026 that 30 birth registration stations had been established in health facilities, in Maseru, Berea and Leribe. In July 2026 the Department listed nationwide scale-up of digital birth registration as an action for 2026-2027. A World Bank note of May 2022 says all 15 enrolment centres that allow for birth registration are linked to a central server. No total of local registration offices is published. Neither count is a share. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

MAR.short: Offices enter births and deaths in a ministry system said in 2024 to reach every office; no source reports the share of offices registering digitally.
MAR.summary: In October 2024 the Ministry of the Interior said its civil-status system SGEC handles birth and death declarations digitally. It was generalised to all the Kingdom's civil-status offices. In April 2025 its territorial authorities directorate was running a project to digitise the registers and build one information system for 1,821 offices. In the last twelve months, the World Bank gave its civil registry back-office system as operational in 59 of 97 participating municipalities on 30 June 2024. The figure was unchanged on 30 January 2026. No count of offices registering digitally has been set against the country's total. Operating would need such a count to show more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

MDG.short: Communes register births digitally, 336 of them in December 2025; no source found reports the share of all communes this represents.
MDG.summary: A decree of 2 December 2020 set up the Centre National d'État Civil et de l'Identité under the technical supervision of the Interior ministry. In the last twelve months, the World Bank reported that communes using the digital registration system SIECM rose from 75 to 336 in the six months to December 2025. It gives the 336 as 40% of the project's target. In March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale described the birth registration platform as being deployed progressively at national scale. The share of all communes using the system has not been found. Nothing found says what has funded the system since the project's financing closed on 30 June 2026. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

MLI.short: Births were registered on paper in July 2026 and a digital platform had ten pilot areas named; no source found says whether any has started.
MLI.summary: An ordinance of 14 February 2025 creates the Agence nationale de Sécurisation des Actes d'Etat civil, a national public establishment. A platform approved by December 2024 is to consolidate births, deaths and marriages. The National Directorate of Civil Status had identified ten pilot areas for the platform. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the head of digitalisation at the Directorate described the birth chain as paper. It named complete digitalisation of the system as a priority. No office has been found entering an event digitally. Whether the pilots have started has not been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally when they are registered, past any pilot, in some local offices.

MOZ.short: Births are entered directly at district offices and all 68 conservatories were digitised by 2025; no source reports the share of local offices entering digitally.
MOZ.summary: The National Director of Registries and Notaries said in 2025 that all 68 civil registration conservatories are digitised. The Directorate holds the main database of the system it calls e-RCEV. In the last twelve months, Jornal Notícias reported on 24 September 2026 that the justice sector is installing 100 civil registration posts in health units with maternity wards. About 250 birth registration posts already work, about 25 per cent of some 1,000 health units. The posts below the conservatories are left out of the digitised count. Nothing found shows whether the new maternity posts enter the record digitally. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a share or a count with its total.

MRT.short: By law births are recorded centrally at citizen reception centres, 153 of 168 equipped in 2021; no source found says whether centres enter births digitally.
MRT.summary: Law 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 requires a birth to be declared within 60 clear days at the Centre d'Accueil des Citoyens. Law 2011-003 has births and deaths declared at the centre and recorded in the central database. The population register agency's director general said on 3 August 2021 that 153 citizen reception centres had been received and equipped. There were to be 168, built in communes and administrative centres. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Outside the law, nothing found says a centre enters a birth digitally when it is declared. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, shown by a share or a count with its total.

MUS.short: Births and deaths were registered in the Civil Status Division's computer system in 2023/2024; no source found says how many of its 36 offices enter records.
MUS.summary: The Civil Status Division's report for 2023/2024 says the CSD System has run since November 2001. It counts 36 Civil Status Offices and gives no share entering records. On 2 September 2025 the Division announced that its CSD System was being revamped. Offices opened on 6 and 7 September 2025 to register births and deaths during the revamp. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years says births are entered at the office, or gives a share of offices doing so. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a published share.

MWI.short: Births and deaths were entered digitally at 87 local service points in five districts in 2025; no source found reports the share of local offices.
MWI.summary: The National Registration Bureau, under the Ministry of Homeland Security, is the body responsible for civil registration, and its plan of September 2025 says kits at district registration offices register births and deaths and print the certificates. UNDP counts 87 service points in five districts in 2025, against 415 Traditional and Sub-Traditional Authorities listed for expansion by 2030. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, 74 health facilities issued instant birth certificates through Nzika, with no total given. On 9 October 2026 UNDP handed over 152 printers. No share of local offices registering digitally is published. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

NAM.short: Local offices enter births and deaths in the national register, as reported in 2024; no source found reports the share of offices doing so.
NAM.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security registers births and deaths on the National Population Registration System, the statistics agency said in April 2024. The system's death module was deployed in 2012 and its birth module in 2013. The agency also said that some registration offices in remote areas lack computers or internet connectivity, which delays capture. In the last twelve months, in December 2025 the ministry said it had deployed its staff to 24 state hospitals. They issue birth certificates right after delivery. No count or share of local offices registering digitally is published. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a share or a count with its total.

NER.short: The digital register ran in 101 of 266 communes in December 2024, a share of communes; no source found reports digital death registration outside Niamey.
NER.summary: The computerised system was in production in 101 of 266 communes and communal arrondissements in December 2024, by the statistics office. The government counted 102 communes on 22 April 2026. In the last twelve months, an ordinance of 22 April 2026 provides for the national civil-status register, and its decree followed on 18 May 2026. On 11 August 2026 the ministry announced the computerisation of all communes and declaration centres and a new platform as works to come. Whether village declaration centres are computerised is not stated. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

NGA.short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at ward and local government offices from July 2026; no source reports the share of local offices doing so.
NGA.summary: The National Population Commission says births and deaths have been registered digitally across the country since 1 July 2026. It calls the platform VitalReg. In the last twelve months, the platform became operational in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory on 1 July 2026, replacing paper. On 18 July 2026 the Registrar General's Department reported 3,372 wards activated and 304 registration workstations deployed. A registrar in Lagos said in August 2026 that his team takes details on a form when the network fails. No total of wards has been found. The 4,011 registration centres are not said to enter on the platform. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

RWA.short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at all categories of registration office in 2025, the statistics office says; no source found reports the rural share.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's statistics institute states that in 2025 its civil registration system, NCI-CRVS, is fully operational at all five categories of registration office. They are health facilities, cells, sectors, districts and embassies. The finance law of 30 June 2026 appropriates RWF 116,184,997 to civil registration for 2026/27, domestically financed. In the last twelve months, birth registration completeness rose from 90.3% in 2024 to 92.9% in 2025, and death registration completeness rose from 46.1% to 50.5%. The share of deaths registered within 30 days fell from 96.3% to 89.9%. No count of offices using the system and no rural share has been found. Mature would need at least 90 per cent of local offices registering births and deaths digitally, on a figure published within two years that gives the rural share.

SDN.short: Births are registered in a national electronic registry, with one local office named in 2026; no source says how many offices enter records, and where,.
SDN.summary: The civil registry centre of South Gezira locality issued an electronic birth certificate at its Al-Hosh office on 17 May 2026. Landinfo reported in March 2023 a centralised electronic registry introduced in 2011. In the last twelve months, the Al-Hosh office resumed work in May 2026 after a stoppage caused by insecurity and displacement. The governor of Gezira State inaugurated civil registry work in Umm al-Qura locality on 29 April 2026. A lawyer told the BBC in August 2026 that the conflict in Darfur has shut down civil registry offices. Nothing since the war began says how a birth record is made. No total of offices has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SEN.short: In 2026 civil-status centres register births in one national system, with 77% of 629 centres digitised; no source found reports the share entering data.
SEN.summary: On the data of the civil status agency, ANEC, its system held 14,839,577 births and 487,259 deaths at 17 July 2026. Its software, the LGEC, was in 437 of the 629 centres, 70%. In the last twelve months, ANEC's director general said on 5 August 2026 that the LGEC had passed its pilot phase. By 16 September 2026 deployment was effective in the Dakar, Thiès, Louga, Diourbel, Fatick and Kaolack regions. He put the modernisation process at 77% of the 629 centres. Every figure counts centres digitised, deployed or covered. None counts centres entering events in the system, and no rural share has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SLE.short: In 2023 births were entered digitally at the registration authority's hospital centres and sent to a central registry; no source reports the number of offices.
SLE.summary: In May 2024 the National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA) presented the integrated eCRVS and ID management system as its own. NCRA told the ID4Africa meeting of 22 May 2025 that over 80% of its services are digitised, birth and death registration among them. In March 2023 UNICEF reported that at NCRA's hospital centres the child's details are entered when the mother registers the birth. In the last twelve months, UNICEF said in October 2026 that digital birth registration is now part of the civil registration system. No count or share of offices entering events digitally has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SOM.short: By January 2026 local administrations in 30 districts registered births digitally into one central database; no source found reports the total of districts or offices.
SOM.summary: Somalia's Law No. 46, published on 5 April 2026, charges a Directorate under the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation with creating and running a digital registration system. In the last twelve months, OpenCRVS's country page of January 2026 counts 30 districts. The ministry had launched a pilot of the Unified Digital Civil Registration Service in 19 districts on 10 August 2025. OpenCRVS counts 28,391 completed birth registrations. No total of districts or offices has been found, so no share can be read, and reports of the number of districts differ. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SSD.short: A digital civil registration system was announced in July 2026 and no birth is registered digitally; no source found reports its design and start date.
SSD.summary: The World Bank's diagnostic of May 2026 gives the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration as operator and owner of the planned civil registration system. It found that birth registration is yet to be implemented and birth certificates do not exist. In the last twelve months, on 24 July 2026 the government announced plans for a digital system recording births, deaths, marriages and divorces. On 31 July 2026 the Directorate was reported to be planning to link civil registration with the national ID system. No office registering digitally has been described, and no design, procurement, pilot office or start date has been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

STP.short: Births are entered directly in the national database at maternities, as of 2026; no source found reports the share of local offices doing so.
STP.summary: The chief conservator of the civil registry said in March 2026 that births are registered by entering the data directly into the directorate's database. The World Bank said in 2023 that its system, SIGA, was implemented by 2018 and registers births, deaths and marriages. In the last twelve months, the chief conservator said the directorate is eliminating paper by registering births directly from the maternities. The chief conservator said registration is done in all the country's maternities. In 2023 the World Bank counted 11 centres and seven birth registration posts in maternities. No share of local offices entering records has been published. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SWZ.short: Births and deaths were entered in the national register at 14 service centres in 2022; no source found reports the total number of offices.
SWZ.summary: The Central Statistical Office's report for 2022 says births and deaths are captured into the National Population Register on registration. It also says the registration officer fills the form by hand and a typist enters it into the register. The Ministry of Home Affairs' 2024/25 report gives 15 service centres and 5 hospital registration points. In the last twelve months, the World Bank appraised the Digital Eswatini Project on 8 June 2026 to upgrade the existing ID and civil registration systems. Its document says paper birth and death records are stored locally without centralised backups. No total of local offices has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

SYC.short: A computerised record of vital events was kept beside the manual register in 2018; no source found says where it is entered.
SYC.summary: The Civil Status Act, as in force on 1 November 2022, makes the Chief Officer of Civil Status keeper of the registers of births and deaths. It provides a Central Civil Status Office in Victoria and offices at Praslin, La Digue and Anse Royale. A contributed article in Seychelles Nation of 10 August 2018 states that the Civil Status records were computerised in 1989, with a computerised record kept beside the manual register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says where the computerised record is entered, or how many local offices enter it. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

TCD.short: Births were registered digitally at 97 hospital registry points in 2025; no source found reports the total of local offices.
TCD.summary: The World Bank states Chad created ANATS in 2016, the institution in charge of operationalising the civil registry. An account published in June 2025 quotes ANATS's coordinator that more than 120,000 children had been registered through hospital-based registry offices since 2023. It gives 97 digitised hospital points, to be raised to 600. In the last twelve months, on 23 September 2026 the commune of N'Djamena launched a project to digitise its civil registry and signed a memorandum with ANATS. The town hall cited the still heavy recourse to physical procedures. No total of local offices has been found. Entry at the office is said only of six hospitals in 2023. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

TGO.short: Digital birth registration runs only in pilots: one town hall in 2024, four communes in 2026; no source shows an office past a pilot.
TGO.summary: In 2024 UNDP Togo supported the development, deployment and operation of a digital birth registration platform, piloted at one town hall, Golfe 3. In the last twelve months, on 21 August 2026 the territorial administration ministry launched the re-reading of the 2009 civil status law. In November 2026 e-Vital Togo began as a pilot in four communes, financed by Vital Strategies. The digital ministry tendered a sixteen-commune digitalisation pilot in July 2026, with German financing. No source says how the record is made on the 2024 platform, or whether the 16 Savanes communes register on it. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

TUN.short: Registrars enter births and deaths into the national database after the paper register, all offices connected in 2020; no source found says how many register.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's national civil status system, Madania, holds births and deaths as well as marriages and divorces in a centralised database, a 2025 report says. A 2020 account says the registrar writes each event by hand in the paper register and then records it directly in the central database. An IDRC chapter of 2020 counts 350 principal offices and 170 subsidiary offices. In the last twelve months, on 4 and 11 December 2025 workshops trained civil status officers from 72 municipalities on the system. No source gives the share of offices that enter events in Madania. Nothing on offices is dated after 2020. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

TZA.short: In 2024 57% of mainland registration centres were active, entering births by phone; capped because no current plan or domestic budget line has been found.
TZA.summary: Tanzania's Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA) introduced the Civil Registration System in 2017 and runs it. The national audit of October 2024 found that at under-five registration centres officers record a birth by hand in a register and then enter it online by phone. RITA's monitoring plan counts 6,341 of 11,053 under-five registration centres as active, 57 per cent. In the last twelve months, Zanzibar's registration agency reported a 2025/2026 improvement of its system, with streamlined workflows and a unified mobile app. No mainland change has been found in that time. The 57 per cent counts centres RITA calls active, not centres entering digitally. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

UGA.short: District offices enter births and deaths into the central register, in most districts in 2020; no source found says how many offices do so.
UGA.summary: Uganda's National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) holds all of Uganda's civil registration systems, it said on 18 July 2026. Its Mobile Vital Records System registered 498,439 live births and 22,182 deaths in 2024, on the statistics bureau's figures. A 2020 brief says the system was used in at least 112 of 135 districts. In the last twelve months, NIRA registered 123,526 births and 9,935 deaths in 2025/26 to 31 December 2025. On 18 July 2026 it said it had built a births and deaths module on its identity system. No share or count of offices making the entry has been found, and nothing on offices is dated after 2020. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

ZAF.short: Births are registered online at 242 equipped health facilities, as of March 2026; no source found reports the share of local offices registering digitally.
ZAF.summary: The Department of Home Affairs reports that its online birth registration system was available at 242 health facilities by the end of 2024/25. The National Department of Health counts 299 health facilities able to register births at the end of 2024/25. The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 also counts 325 front offices and 220 mobile offices. In the last twelve months, the Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs reports that the 2025/26 target of automated birth registration at 47 health facilities was missed. The rollout was deferred to 2026/27. No share of local offices registering births digitally has been found, and how the front offices make the record is not described. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

ZMB.short: Births are registered in a national system deployed in eleven districts in 2026; no source found says how many local offices enter records themselves.
ZMB.summary: In a 2026 statement to the National Assembly the Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security describes INRIS as the ministry's civil registration system, deployed in eleven districts. The ministry said in December 2025 that about 1.3 million citizens have been enrolled on INRIS. A September 2025 preprint states death notification forms on paper are carried weekly from local offices to headquarters and entered there. In the last twelve months, the Lavushimanda district office registered over 3,000 children under five in the four months to September 2026. In October 2023 INRIS was rolled out in 79 districts. No count of offices that enter events in INRIS themselves has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

ZWE.short: Births are entered digitally at computerised offices; at least 93 of 282 offices were computerised in 2026, and no source says how many register digitally.
ZWE.summary: The Deputy Registrar General said on 22 July 2026 that all 10 provinces and 63 districts have been computerised, as have more than 20 of 209 sub-offices. UNICEF Zimbabwe stated in July 2025 that computerised offices and sub-offices allow real-time data entry at the office. In the last twelve months, in October 2025 the Minister of Home Affairs announced plans to computerise sub-offices across the country. On 7 August 2026 UNICEF and the government announced a China-funded project for 10 sub-offices in eight districts. UNICEF said some decentralised sub-offices are not computerised. No count of offices registering births digitally has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

AGO.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
AGO.summary: The Banco Nacional de Angola launched Kwik in June 2023. It carries instant transfers between banks and digital wallets. In February 2026 KWiK handled 3.14 million transfers worth Kz 74.6 billion, EMIS reported. In the first half of 2026 wallets sent Kz 209.6bn to bank accounts over Kwik. Digital wallets sent Kz 212.7bn of the Kz 557.4bn moved over Kwik in the first half of 2026, Expansão reports from EMIS data. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

BDI.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
BDI.summary: BurundiPay, the national instant payment system run by the BRB, had about 224,000 users on 4 August 2026. On BurundiPay 17 institutions (5 commercial banks, 10 microfinance institutions, 2 payment institutions) are live, per the BRB. The BRB says BurundiPay already allows exchanges between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile wallets locally. In the last twelve months, Burundi Pay, the national instant payment system, has been operational since March 2026, per the central bank's deputy governor.

BEN.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
BEN.summary: The BCEAO launched PI-SPI, its regional instant payment platform, on 30 September 2025. Bank transfers can credit mobile money wallets in seconds through it, and the reverse. At 31 July 2026 nine of Benin's 15 banks and financial establishments were connected, with Moov Money and MTN, two of its three mobile money issuers. In the last twelve months, wallet and bank transfers began to route through PI-SPI. From 2 November 2026 MTN, Moov Money and UBA Benin route transfers between wallets, other operators and banks through PI-SPI. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

BFA.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
BFA.summary: In September 2026 Orange said Max It is interconnected with almost all the country's banks for transfers between bank accounts and Orange Money. The BCEAO's PI-SPI instant payment platform, launched on 30 September 2025, connects banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions. In July 2026 Wave Burkina said traders, farmers and young entrepreneurs use its service for payment, money transfer and savings. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

BWA.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2025; no source found reports a national switch.
BWA.summary: In September 2026 Orange Money, Mascom's MyZaka and BTC's Smega operated as mobile money platforms. Mobile money in Botswana is now interoperable with traditional bank accounts, The Voice reported. It dates the position to March 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

CAF.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
CAF.summary: The CEMAC QR Code standard was launched on 29 July 2026 across six states including the Central African Republic. It lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state. That includes the Central African Republic. Telecel Money mobile money is in service in the Central African Republic, according to Telecel and ENERCA. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

CIV.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
CIV.summary: PI-SPI, which the BCEAO launched on 30 September 2025, carries instant transfers between bank accounts, wallets and microfinance accounts. In the last twelve months, transfers between e-money providers, and between banks and wallets, came under a rule to route through it. From 2 November 2026 transfers between e-money providers, and between banks and wallets, must route through it. SimoCash moves funds directly from one mobile money operator to another. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

CMR.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
CMR.summary: BEAC says the QR code launched 29 July 2026 lets any bank or microfinance mobile app read any merchant's code. This holds regardless of institution or CEMAC country. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state. That includes Cameroon. Tech Africa News reports that LBPay lets users transfer funds across different mobile money networks. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

COD.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
COD.summary: In April 2026 Vodacom Congo's CEO said about $88 million had moved into the formal banking sector through wallet-to-bank transfers over the past year. At 30 June 2024 Orange Money RDC held CDF 6.8bn of receivables from interoperability with Airtel Money and M-Pesa. In May 2026 almost 30 million citizens had a mobile money account, though cash still dominates. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

COG.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
COG.summary: The CEMAC QR Code standard was launched on 29 July 2026 across six states including Congo. It lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state. That includes the Republic of Congo. GIMAC said that in the first half of 2026 payment institutions and mobile money operators, including those of Congo, dominate GIMACPAY transaction volumes. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

COM.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
COM.summary: The central bank describes Komor Switch as the national payment infrastructure. It interconnects all banks, financial institutions and mobile money services. Al-Watwan reports the president launched Komor Switch, a national platform connecting all banks and mobile money services. The central bank says Komor Switch allows instant real-time transfers between banks and mobile money. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

CPV.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2024; no source found reports payments between providers.
CPV.summary: Banco de Cabo Verde's 2025 payment system report counts 50,866 users of televinti4, which puts the vinti4 card on a mobile phone. They made 1,284,291 transactions moving money in 2025, Expresso das Ilhas reports. The app was launched in 2021, is run by SISP and carries transfers, QR code payments, bills and phone top-ups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

DJI.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2024; no source found reports payments between providers.
DJI.summary: Djibouti Telecom's D-Money launched its new smartphone application on 26 September 2024. Open to all Djiboutians since 21 September, it serves money transfers, bill payment and online purchases of services. In November 2020 the Ministry of Communication said D-Money, then recently launched, already had thousands of subscribers, three ministers among them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

DZA.short: A national switch connected Algerie Poste and bank accounts in 2025.
DZA.summary: Interbank mobile payment, DZ Mob Pay, launched in January 2025. A national mobile switch has been in service since June 2024. In the last twelve months, the post ministry said the mobile switch lets clients of the banks and of Algerie Poste pay and transfer money instantly by QR code. GIE Monetique's director says the banks' mobile solutions are integrated into it. By the end of August 2026 it had 131,705 personal and 18,730 merchant accounts, per GIE Monetique data.

EGY.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
EGY.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt's deputy governor said mobile wallets numbered about 67 million by September 2026. InstaPay, the instant payments network launched in March 2022, carries personal, commercial and account-to-wallet transfers. Ahram Online describes InstaPay as a state-backed payment app licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt. Orange Egypt says its Orange Cash wallet had about 10 million users in October 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

ERI.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
ERI.summary: Himbol's terms of service, in force from November 2025, describe its M-Nakfa mobile money wallet. It carries cash-in and cash-out, transfers between people, merchant payments and utility bills, under Bank of Eritrea oversight. The Fintech Times said in 2026 that wallets linked to the state-owned EriTel are the main entry point to digital financial services. It called their functions still limited. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

ETH.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
ETH.summary: In November 2026 EthSwitch's EthioPay carried interoperable person-to-person payments across 51 institutions and QR payments across 40. Capital describes EthSwitch as Ethiopia's national payment switch linking banks, payment-service providers, merchants and the mobile-money platforms. Capital says telebirr and M-Pesa are both connected through EthSwitch, which provides interoperability linking banks, payment-service providers and merchants. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

GAB.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
GAB.summary: The CEMAC QR Code standard was launched on 29 July 2026 across six states including Gabon. It lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state. That includes Gabon. Moov Gabon issued 1,969,325 transactions worth 68.1bn FCFA and Airtel Gabon 1,950,401 worth 55.8bn FCFA in H1 2026, per GIMAC statistics. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

GHA.short: Mobile money, payments between providers and a national switch linking wallets and banks were all in service in 2026.
GHA.summary: The Bank of Ghana counted 85.8 million registered mobile money accounts in August 2026, 26.4 million of them active. GhIPSS links banks and mobile money operators. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Bank of Ghana's head of fintech called it the national interoperable payment infrastructure. The Bank of Ghana reports mobile money interoperability in August 2026 at 35.7 million transactions worth GHC 6.5 billion. Nothing on the three questions is missing.

GIN.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
GIN.summary: NimbaPay went live on 23 July 2026, linking banks and electronic money institutions. AGUIDUTEN described NimbaPay as the national instant payment platform. It connects banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions. The BCRG's supervision director general cited NimbaPay as a platform ensuring interoperability between banks, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions. In the last twelve months, by 15 October 2026, seven institutions were connected to NimbaPay, which had carried about 67,000 transactions worth over GNF 68 billion.

GMB.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
GMB.summary: Gamswitch called BANTABA 2.0 the country's first real-time, fully interoperable payment system in February 2026. The Point calls BANTABA 2.0 a national backbone run by Gamswitch. One switch connects banks, mobile money operators, microfinance institutions, fintechs and payment providers. In the last twelve months, since its launch in December 2025 it has moved money instantly between bank accounts and mobile wallets, whatever the provider.

GNB.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
GNB.summary: On 30 September 2026 the BCEAO listed Orange Money Guinea-Bissau among 7 institutions in Guinea-Bissau authorised to open PI-SPI services to the public. In September 2026 the BCEAO said interoperable e-money transactions in UEMOA, which includes Guinea-Bissau, go through PI-SPI. In the last twelve months, Guinea-Bissau had 5 institutions authorised on PI-SPI at 31 July 2026, and 7 by 30 September. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

GNQ.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
GNQ.summary: The CEMAC QR Code standard was launched on 29 July 2026 across six states including Equatorial Guinea. It lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state. That includes Equatorial Guinea. GIMACPAY, the CEMAC card-mobile-transfer ecosystem in service since 2021, processed over sixteen million mobile transactions in 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

KEN.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
KEN.summary: Kenswitch calls itself Kenya's domestic payment switch. In November 2026 Kenswitch said it links banks, SACCOs, microfinance institutions and mobile money providers. Transfers between M-PESA, banks and other wallets such as Airtel Money pass through several platforms. In the last twelve months, on 10 November 2026, Airtel Kenya and IPSL agreed to let Airtel Money users send money to accounts at 30 banks, SACCOs and microfinance banks on Pesalink. IPSL's chief said Pesalink reaches all banks and has begun till, paybill and QR payments to merchants. No source says one national switch connects all wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need one national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

LBR.short: Mobile money networks have been interoperable since December 2025; banks are not yet on the national system, with a switch due in 2027.
LBR.summary: The Central Bank of Liberia launched the Inclusive Instant Payment System on 16 December 2025. It had carried more than 5.3 million transactions since launch. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 the deputy governor said the system enables payments across banks and mobile network operators. In November 2026 the governor said banks and fintechs were still being brought onto Pay Na-Na. A National Electronic Payment Switch joining banks, fintechs and mobile money operators is targeted for early 2027. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

LBY.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
LBY.summary: Digital-wallet transactions rose from 109 million dinars in October 2024 to 703 million in August 2026, the governor said. In January and February 2026 Libya had 187,335 electronic wallets and 6,096 acceptance points. Over the same months the instant payment services LYPay and OnePay carried more than 44.6 billion dinars. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

LSO.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
LSO.summary: In May 2025 LeSwitch, formerly the National Payment Switch, connected banks and mobile money wallets. LeSwitch fast payments, launched on 20 March 2024, give digital interoperability between banks and non-bank entities. In July 2026 Vodacom Lesotho said M-Pesa customers across urban, peri-urban and rural Lesotho use their mobile wallets. It now carries local ATM and POS debit card transactions, with POS in pilot from 11 May 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

MAR.short: A national switch carried payments from both banks and mobile money institutions in 2026.
MAR.summary: Morocco has wallets and an interoperable mobile payment system, though Switch Al Maghrib's director general says traffic on it remains limited. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, Switch Al-Maghrib's managing director said every transaction through the national switch is risk-scored in real time. This covers transactions from a bank or a mobile money institution. CMI says its Fatourati platform connects 32 banks and payment institutions.

MDG.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
MDG.summary: In September 2026 Gasy Money users could transfer money to another Gasy Money account, a bank account or Airtel Money. BGFIBank Madagasikara's Gasy Money app, presented in September 2026, allows national transfers in partnership with the mobile phone operators. In October 2026 Mvola, a mobile money service, had close to 4 million users, over 60,000 cashpoints and over 50,000 merchants, its CEO said. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

MLI.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
MLI.summary: On 30 September 2026 the BCEAO listed Moov Money, Sama Money and Orange Finances Mobiles Mali among 19 institutions in Mali authorised to open PI-SPI services. The BCEAO list shows banks and mobile money providers in Mali authorised together on PI-SPI. In the last twelve months, wallet transfers moved onto PI-SPI. APA news reports that from November 2026 Mali's wallet-to-bank and wallet-to-wallet transfers ran through the BCEAO's PI-SPI. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

MOZ.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
MOZ.summary: The Bank of Mozambique's instant payment system, run by SIMO around the clock, has connected banks and mobile wallets since 2 March 2026. Called Metix, it joins banks, microbanks and e-money institutions, and wallet operators must take part. In the last twelve months, the governor said in October 2026 that it handled about 12,000 transactions a day, up from about 3,000 at launch. PawaPay says Mozambique's mobile money market exceeds 12 million active accounts.

MRT.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2024.
MRT.summary: In October 2024 GIMTEL launched transfers between bank apps and e-wallets. BreadCash, Bamis Digital, BCI Pay, Bankili, Amanti, Sedad and Qlik had already joined. GIMTEL's launched interconnection links national bank apps and e-wallets in one system, with further providers in technical testing. In the last twelve months, on 9 November 2026 the operator Mattel launched its licensed e-money subsidiary, Mattel Money, and its Mechili wallet, Le Quotidien reports.

MUS.short: Mauritius's banks took QR and instant payments in 2025 and 2026; no source found reports payments between wallets or with banks.
MUS.summary: AfricaNenda's 2024 case study describes MauCAS as Mauritius's national instant-payment switch for real-time retail payments. MCB reported that QR payments through its Juice app grew 67% in 2025. They include payments made with MAUCAS QR, the central bank's QR code. In September 2026 Platform Africa reported that customers can move funds between their bank accounts through fintech platforms. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

MWI.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
MWI.summary: In July 2025 the bankers' association said the National Switch connects banks and wallets for transfers both ways. The National Switch, rolled out in 2015, linked banks, mobile money platforms and ATMs into one network. The Digital Retail Payments Platform integrates banks and non-bank players, mobile-money operators among them. In June 2026 Airtel Money Malawi and Admarc launched a digital payment platform in Blantyre. No change to the National Switch has been found in the last twelve months.

NAM.short: Namibia's MTC mobile money paid refugees in 2025, and a bank instant payments system went live in 2026; no wallet transfers between providers were found.
NAM.summary: The Bank of Namibia's instant payments solution went live in June 2026 with Bank Windhoek, Nampost and Letshego Bank Namibia as first participants, Deputy Governor Leonie Dunn said. E-money issuers are to join the Instant Payment Solution, in phased rollout. In 2025 UNHCR and the government paid cash to about 6,000 refugees through MTC's mobile money service. In the last twelve months, the solution went live, and no mobile money provider is among its first participants. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

NER.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
NER.summary: On 26 June 2026 Banque Atlantique Niger and NITA launched Bank to Wallet and Wallet to Bank services in Niamey. They give instant transfers between a bank account and an electronic wallet. At 30 September 2026 the BCEAO listed 13 institutions in Niger authorised to offer PI-SPI to the public: eleven banks, Airtel Money Niger and i-FUTUR. No other change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

NGA.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
NGA.summary: Premium Times reported in October 2026 that NIBSS had rolled out the National Payment Stack, an ISO 20022 instant payments platform. It connects banks and mobile money operators. It has carried over 100 million transactions. Business Post reports the central bank upgraded the licences of OPay, Moniepoint, PalmPay, Kuda and Paga to national in January 2026. No other change has been found in the last twelve months.

RWA.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
RWA.summary: Rwanda made eKash its national instant payment system in July 2026, connecting banks and mobile-money platforms through a common payment infrastructure. In the last twelve months, eKash was launched nationwide. NBR calls eKash Rwanda's national instant payment system, reached through banks and mobile money providers, launched nationwide on 14 July 2026. It links banks and mobile money wallets. BNR's October 2026 financial sector report puts eKash active accounts at 10.3 million and monthly transactions at 28.9 million in September 2026.

SDN.short: Wallet users could send money to and from all banks in 2026; no source found says whether a national switch joins wallets and banks.
SDN.summary: Sudani Fintech launched Sah on 14 April 2026, a licensed app and USSD service that gives each user a basic bank account number. Users can send and receive money to and from all banks in Sudan. Zain's Bede wallet added the same bank account number service in October 2026, Sudan Horizon reports. In the last twelve months, wallets in Sudan reached bank accounts through these two services. EBS is the Central Bank of Sudan's electronic payments arm. By July 2026 it had processed over 234 million account-to-account transfers between banks. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

SEN.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
SEN.summary: PI-SPI, the BCEAO's instant payment platform, carries transfers and payments between banks, e-money and payment institutions. In February 2026 19 Senegal institutions were authorised on it. In the last twelve months, bank-wallet transfers moved onto PI-SPI. From 2 November 2026 bank-wallet transfers run through PI-SPI, replacing the banks' own services. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

SLE.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone launched real-time transfers between mobile money operators, banks, and mobile money and bank accounts on 13 February 2025. Seven banks and two mobile money providers were connected. The Bank of Sierra Leone's national instant payment switch connects mobile money accounts and bank accounts. The Bank of Sierra Leone says its Instant Payment System carried about 600,000 transactions between banks and mobile money platforms by late 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

SOM.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
SOM.summary: The Central Bank says SIPS, launched in January 2025, carries real-time transfers between banks, mobile wallets and point-of-sale terminals, whatever the provider. The Central Bank launched the national Somalia Instant Payment System in early 2025, TechCabal says. It links mobile wallets and banks. SONNA reports it carries transfers between individuals and payments to merchants. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

SSD.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
SSD.summary: In September 2026 South Sudan had rules for operating electronic money systems, with transaction limits by customer tier and agent reporting. In August 2026 MTN MoMo trained 1,225 South Sudanese entrepreneurs to accept digital payments, sell airtime and provide cash-in services. In July 2025 the Bank of South Sudan said mobile money is a legal form of payment. No change in payments between providers has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

STP.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2025; no source found reports payments between providers.
STP.summary: In January 2025 GTI Holdings launched the Sao digital financial platform, with a mobile wallet, a prepaid card, POS payments and agents. On 3 December 2020 the youth ministry signed a contract with Golfintech for Dobra Digital, a phone money-transfer service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

SWZ.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
SWZ.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini says the national Eswatini Payment Switch connects banks and mobile money providers in service, 24/7. Eswatini Positive News says DeltaPay users can send money within seconds, 24/7, to customers of participating banks and digital wallets. Standard Bank Eswatini says customers can send and receive payments in real time between participating bank accounts and wallets. No change to the switch has been found in the last twelve months. Standard Bank Eswatini says its Unayo wallet has over 200,000 registered retail customers and about 5,000 business clients. It closes on 31 December 2026.

SYC.short: An e-money wallet was in service in 2024; no source found says whether payments move between providers or with banks.
SYC.summary: Nebula FinTech's eboo e-money wallet went live on the iOS and Google Play stores on 30 and 31 January 2024. The governor said Airtel Seychelles had introduced e-money with a licensed mobile money transfer service in 2015. In November 2025 Fusepay said it had received a payment service provider licence from the Central Bank of Seychelles. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

TCD.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
TCD.summary: On 29 July 2026 the CEMAC QR code standard was launched in six states, Chad among them. A client of any bank, wallet or microfinance account pays by scan. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY connects banks and mobile money wallets for instant payments in each CEMAC state, Chad included. Airtel Money and Moov Money interoperate through GIMACPAY across the CEMAC zone. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

TGO.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
TGO.summary: The BCEAO's PI-SPI instant payment platform, launched on 30 September 2025, links banks, e-money and payment institutions. By the end of October 2026 it connected 17 providers in Togo, from banks to microfinance institutions, for instant transfers between them. Mixx users can send money through it to wallets, banks and microfinance institutions in all eight WAEMU countries. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

TUN.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
TUN.summary: Central Bank of Tunisia data show 719,000 e-wallets at the end of September 2026. They carried 7.1 million transactions, 64.2% of them payments, Tunisie Numérique reports. The BCT says Société Monétique Tunisie runs the mobile payment system, and banks, the Post and payment institutions issue wallets. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

TZA.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
TZA.summary: In March 2025 more than 1.5 million transactions a day went through TIPS, which the Bank of Tanzania launched in 2019. Over 45 banks, mobile money providers and other institutions were taking part. The Tanzania Instant Payment System, a national system, connects 47 financial service providers including for bank-to-wallet transfers, per the report. The government reduced the cost of interoperability transfers, moving funds from bank accounts to mobile phone wallets or vice versa. No change to TIPS has been found in the last twelve months.

UGA.short: Mobile money wallets could send money to and from bank accounts in 2026; no source found says whether a national switch joins wallets and banks.
UGA.summary: In the last twelve months, Airtel's wallets were linked to banks and other institutions. In October 2026 Airtel had partnered with 25 commercial banks, credit institutions and microfinance institutions. The partnerships move money between their accounts and its wallets. In October 2025 pawaPay processed mobile money payments through direct links with MTN MoMo and Airtel. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

ZAF.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
ZAF.summary: In October 2026 the Reserve Bank governor said PayShap, the real-time low-value payment rail launched in 2023, had passed 1 billion transactions. They were worth over R1 trillion. Capitec Pay is a bank-to-bank online payment service that lets clients pay on websites and apps using their phone number. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. Operating would need payments between different mobile money providers, or between wallets and banks, in service.

ZMB.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
ZMB.summary: Times of Zambia says Lipila lets businesses and institutions accept Airtel Money, MTN Mobile Money, Zamtel Money and bank payments. It cites 15 million active mobile money wallets in 2026. The National Financial Switch connects banks, non-bank financial institutions, payment service providers, fintechs and mobile money operators. ITWeb reports this, quoting a Sybrin manager. An existing MTN MoMo and FNB partnership already lets customers transfer funds between MoMo wallets and FNB accounts. No change has been found in the last twelve months.

ZWE.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
ZWE.summary: In July 2026 O-Mari wallet holders could withdraw cash at CABS ATMs and EcoCash customers at TN CyberTech Bank ATMs. ZIPIT already allows some cross-platform transfers. ZimSwitch's chief executive described it as the national payment switch, with mobile wallet integration on its e-commerce platform. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. Mature would need a national switch in service that connects mobile money wallets and bank accounts.

AGO.short: In 2025 about 36% of current revenue, oil taxes excluded, was paid through the state payment reference; customs e-payment was only partial.
AGO.summary: In July 2026 the tax authority AGT directed that taxes be paid electronically as a rule, through its taxpayer portal. Expansão, from EMIS data, put payments through RUPE in 2025 at about Kz 6.7 trillion, roughly 36% of Kz 18.9 trillion of current revenue, oil taxes excluded. In 2025 the UN's global survey on trade facilitation reported electronic payment of customs duties in Angola as partially implemented. In the last twelve months, the July 2026 directive is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically.

BDI.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
BDI.summary: The OBR says taxes have been declared and paid online through the Umutangakori portal since August 2023, with receipts issued electronically. In the last twelve months, on 19 January 2026 the OBR launched e-KORI for online tax filing and payment of taxes and fees. In June 2026 the finance and digital economy minister said E-Kori already allows online filing and payment for some taxpayers. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

BEN.short: Nearly a third of state revenue was collected through digital channels in 2026; no source found says whether customs duties are paid electronically.
BEN.summary: In March 2026 a release said taxpayers can declare and pay taxes online, by automated bank transfer or mobile money. Receipts are instant. In March 2026 a release said nearly a third of state revenue was collected through digital channels. The tax directorate's 2025 activity report puts electronic payments above 96% for most taxes, mostly from medium and large firms, ICTD reports. In the last twelve months, Decree 2026-617, signed on 18 September 2026, requires fees for justice chancellery and court acts, tax stamps included, to be paid only electronically. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically.

BFA.short: Taxes were filed and paid online in 2026 and customs duties paid electronically from 2025; no figure for revenue paid electronically has been found.
BFA.summary: In November 2026 the tax directorate's eSINTAX JAVA portal took tax returns and payments online. In January 2025 the Faso Arzeka platform took customs duties by app, web and USSD. In the last twelve months, the eSINTAX portal opened, and in September 2026 Orange said public-administration payments can be made directly in Max It. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

BWA.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2024; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
BWA.summary: Botswana's record shows that in February 2024 the finance minister listed online tax filing and electronic payment among BURS e-services in operation. In the last twelve months, Andersen says Botswana's tax rules in force from 1 July 2026 make electronic billing and invoicing mandatory. The rules support tax administration with digital filing, and compliance deadlines are still to apply. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

CAF.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
CAF.summary: On 24 March 2025 the tax administration launched e-Tax for online tax information, declaration and payment, per Agence Ecofin. In August 2025 the finance minister said taxes are to be paid online through e-Tax, and over half of the large taxpayers concerned did not yet use it. In the last twelve months, Orange Centrafrique, Webb Fontaine and NGSER launched payment of the DPI customs fee through Orange Money. Receipts pass in real time to the SYDONIA customs system. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

CIV.short: TresorPay collected FCFA 36 billion in 2024; no source found says whether the main taxes and duties are paid electronically.
CIV.summary: The finance ministry says online filing and online payment of taxes and duties have operated since 2017. The finance minister says collections through TresorPay reached FCFA 36 billion from 2.5 million transactions in 2024, against FCFA 3 billion in 2021. TresorPay is the Treasury's e-payment platform. The last twelve months bring one dated change: in October 2026 the BCEAO said Treasuries on PI-SPI can receive taxes and duties from any account. The open question is the share of all revenue paid electronically, because the figure found covers TresorPay collections only.

CMR.short: In 2026 taxes were declared and paid online and customs duties could be paid digitally; the electronic share is not reported.
CMR.summary: In March 2026 Visa's country manager said customs duties paid with the GUCE x BGFIBank Business Card are now paid fully digitally. In June 2026 an editorial said the tax directorate has for several years taken tax declarations and payments online. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, taxpayers at a Yaoundé tax centre could pay tax notices through Tresor Pay or by MTN MoMo and Orange Money. Receipts were printed at once. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

COD.short: Two provinces put provincial tax payment online in 2026; no source found says whether the main taxes and customs duties are paid electronically.
COD.summary: Kinshasa's provincial revenue directorate launched irms-dgrk.com on 5 March 2026 for filing and paying provincial taxes online. Tshopo province launched Veri-Gov on 21 August 2026 for paying provincial taxes by mobile phone. Nationally, a ministerial circular of 18 January 2024 lets banks and e-money institutions collect central-government taxes, customs duties and fees through digital channels. Both provincial platforms were launched in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

COG.short: Taxes and customs duties are paid through one national electronic platform, which collected about FCFA 107 billion from June to November 2026.
COG.summary: Arrêté no. 1009 of 22 May 2026 makes payment of public revenue exclusively electronic through the Fouta platform. Since 3 August 2026 taxpayers file on the E-Tax or Sydonia platforms and pay taxes, levies and customs duties online through Fouta, L'Economie reports. In the last twelve months, on 17 November 2026 the finance minister told the National Assembly that FOUTA had collected nearly FCFA 107 billion since 1 June. That was FCFA 94 billion of taxes through e-Tax and FCFA 13 billion through SYDONIA. Its predecessor e-Pay had brought in about FCFA 1 billion. The ministry put the total at 8.5% of 2026 tax revenue.

COM.short: Electronic payment of taxes or fees was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
COM.summary: On 15 April 2026 the Directorate General of Taxes launched a three-day workshop. AFD's PAGFSI project funded it, to validate the legal framework for fiscal teleprocedures. It prepared the progressive rollout of tax e-filing (télédéclaration) and e-payment (télépaiement), under the 2026 finance law. In the last twelve months, the workshop is the step found. No source found since October 2023 says some taxes or fees can be paid electronically. Establishing would need electronic payment in service for some taxes or fees.

CPV.short: Tax returns were filed and taxes paid online in 2024, customs clearance paid online in 2026; no figure for revenue paid electronically has been found.
CPV.summary: In May 2024 the tax directorate (DNRE) said tax returns are submitted and taxes paid through its portal. In the last twelve months, in 2026 the DNRE's online customs clearance page took payment by DUC reference, which adds online payment of customs duties to the 2024 tax portal. It accepts Vinti4 or Visa cards issued by Cabo Verdean banks, with SISP one-time-password security. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically.
