Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

DJI.short: Electronic payment of taxes or fees was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
DJI.summary: In 2025 the World Bank committed US$20m to the Djibouti Economic and Financial Governance Project. It sets a target of 70% tax e-filing adoption by December 2029. At the January 2026 review that indicator stood at 0%. In the last twelve months, that review is the one reading found. No source found since October 2023 says some taxes or fees can be paid electronically. Establishing would need electronic payment in service for some taxes or fees.

DZA.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
DZA.summary: Since 25 July 2026 the tax directorate's Jibayatic portal has been open to all taxpayers for remote payment of taxes. Its guide says any tax, duty or levy declared online there can be paid online. In the last twelve months, the portal opened to all taxpayers. In February 2024 customs e-payment procedures were still being finalised. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

EGY.short: A figure for revenue paid electronically was reported in 2024.
EGY.summary: The Ministry of Finance gives EGP 2.5 trillion of e-payment and collection for July 2023 to May 2024. Electronic tax collection was EGP 613.1 billion and customs collection EGP 284.3 billion. In January 2024 it put e-payment and collection since May 2019 at EGP 8.1 trillion in 607.3 million transactions. In the last twelve months, in August 2026 Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said real-estate transaction tax can be paid by bank card through the Tax Authority's Real Estate Transactions app. In November 2026 Orange Egypt said guardians can pay family-prosecution fees through Max it and Orange Cash.

ERI.short: Nothing found names electronic payment of taxes or fees or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says how taxes and fees are paid.

ETH.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
ETH.summary: In July 2026 Ethio telecom said taxpayers can pay the federal Ministry of Revenues and twelve regional and city revenue authorities through telebirr, by app or USSD. In June 2024 Webb Fontaine said electronic payment had been introduced in the Webb Customs system. In October 2026 EthSwitch presented a Unified Government Payment Platform, a single route through the national switch for government bills. In the last twelve months, that presentation and the July 2026 telebirr arrangement are the changes found. No source found since October 2023 says the main domestic taxes are filed and paid electronically nationwide. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

GAB.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
GAB.summary: On 10 July 2025 the tax directorate and Moov Africa launched payment of taxes by Moov Money for taxpayers with turnover under FCFA 30 million. In the last twelve months, from October 2026 eTax is part of Gabon Connect, and TrésorPay takes some non-tax revenue, GabonMediaTime reports. The tax directorate says online payment of oil, mining and forestry revenue starts in October 2026, rolling out to December 2027. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

GHA.short: About GH¢1.6 billion passed through the government's payment portal from 2019 to 2024; no source found says whether the main taxes and duties are paid electronically.
GHA.summary: In May 2024 President Akufo-Addo said transactions worth some GH¢1.6 billion had passed through the Ghana.gov portal since its launch in 2019. From May 2021 the revenue authority said domestic taxpayers pay on the Ghana.gov platform. In the last twelve months, from 1 November 2026 Ghana Police say traffic fines notified by their TraffiTech-GH cameras can be paid by mobile money or card. The Bank of Ghana's fintech report for the first quarter of 2026 lists wallet payments to government as in service. The Ghana.gov figure is a running total since 2019. The open question is whether the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically.

GIN.short: Taxes could be declared and paid online in 2026; no source found says customs duties are paid electronically.
GIN.summary: On 22 December 2025 Guinea launched Tresor Pay for paying administrative fees and charges owed to the state by mobile phone. In May 2026 We are Tech reported the government had launched eTax for online declaration and payment of taxes. Tresor Pay and eTax were both launched in the last twelve months. On 14 September 2026 the territorial administration minister, Djenabou Touré, announced digital tax payment in Guinea's markets, with no date or system named. No source found since October 2023 says customs duties are paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

GMB.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
GMB.summary: In April 2026 the Accountant General said citizens and businesses can pay taxes, fees and levies through GovPay, the government payment gateway. In the last twelve months, A July 2026 agreement added SUTURA for taxes, fees and other charges. In October 2025 the revenue authority presented its new tax system to stakeholders ahead of nationwide implementation. In June 2026 the system was still being introduced ahead of full rollout. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

GNB.short: Import VAT has been payable only through the Kontaktu platform since December 2025; no source found says whether the main taxes follow.
GNB.summary: A tax directorate circular of 10 December 2025 makes import VAT payable only through Kontaktu. In July 2024 O Democrata GB reported on the tax directorate's Kontaktu platform. It lets taxpayers declare and pay taxes at any time by bank transfer, Orange Money and Mobile Money. In the last twelve months, the circular narrowed import VAT to that platform. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

GNQ.short: A 2025 order ends cash collection of some public revenues; whether any tax or fee is paid electronically is not on record.
GNQ.summary: Presidential Order 3/2025 sets the abandonment of cash collection of certain public revenues, Diario Rombe reports. In the last twelve months, on 30 September 2026 the e-money firm Muni proposed its wallet as a channel for state taxes and fees. The transport ministry said it would study the proposal. No source found says any tax or fee is paid electronically. Establishing would need electronic payment in service for some taxes or fees.

KEN.short: Sh100.8 billion was paid through the government's single payment platform in the year to June 2024; electronic payment of customs duties is not on record.
KEN.summary: In October 2024 the Treasury Cabinet Secretary gave eCitizen's collections to the Senate: Sh26.4 billion in the year to June 2023 and Sh100.8 billion in the year to June 2024. At least Sh127.2 billion had passed through it since all services were ordered paid through one number. On 27 October 2026 the Treasury's Principal Secretary told the National Assembly Finance Committee that the Treasury manages eCitizen, the government's digital payment platform. In the last twelve months, no later figure than Sh100.8 billion has been found. No source found since October 2023 says customs duties are paid electronically.

LBR.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2025; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
LBR.summary: In April 2026 the revenue authority said its LITAS system lets taxpayers register, file returns, generate payment slips and pay in real time. By August 2025 taxpayers could pay through LITAS by mobile money, phone or computer. From 1 December 2025 a central bank directive routes all government revenue collected by mobile money, taxes included, through NEPS/IIPS. In the last twelve months, the directive and the April 2026 LITAS statement are the changes found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

LBY.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
LBY.summary: On 4 December 2025 the finance ministry told customs and tax offices to take amounts over 500 dinars only by certified cheque or electronic payment. A decree by Prime Minister Aldabaiba made e-payment an approved method for collecting state revenues and public dues. Cash and cheques remain approved alongside it. The finance ministry said the Unified Tax System implements Decision No. 448 of 2025 on tax e-payment and e-collection. In the last twelve months, the instruction and the decree are the changes found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

LSO.short: The main taxes and customs duties were filed and paid electronically in 2026; the electronic share is not reported.
LSO.summary: Revenue Services Lesotho says Corporate Income Tax, PAYE, VAT and customs duties can be paid through the RSL-SLB e-payment system. In July 2024 it added EcoCash wallet payment of taxes and customs duties through its website. On 11 February 2026 it launched e-payment with Standard Lesotho Bank by USSD, internet banking and the bank's app. In the last twelve months, the February 2026 launch is the change found. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

MAR.short: In 2025, 91.4% of tax revenue was paid electronically; no source found says whether customs duties are paid electronically.
MAR.summary: The DGI says its Simpl teleservices let taxpayers declare and pay taxes electronically (telepayer). The DGI's 2025 activity report, as le360 reports it, puts the share of tax revenue paid by tele-payment at 91.4% in 2025, up from 91.2% in 2024. It counted 12,304,943 tele-payments in 2025. In the last twelve months, the 2025 figure of 91.4% is the change found. No source found since October 2023 names customs duties among the revenue filed and paid electronically.

MDG.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2025; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
MDG.summary: The Ministry of Economy and Finance says it launched SIGRNF on 9 May 2025. It lets users pay non-tax government revenues 24/7 via mobile banking, with progressive nationwide rollout. In September 2025 the finance minister said the e-Hetra online tax filing and payment system has been extended nationwide. SAFI has been in production since September 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

MLI.short: A figure for revenue paid electronically was reported in 2026.
MLI.summary: The DGI director-general says electronic receipts reached 300 billion FCFA in 2024. That was 30% of receipts, against 2% in 2022, and up 34% on 2023. The ministry reported nearly FCFA 200 million collected for local authorities through digital payment between July 2024 and May 2026. That ministry is Territorial Administration and Decentralisation. In the last twelve months, on 16 November 2026 the finance minister handed out 545 tablets to extend the TresorPay public payment platform.

MOZ.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2023; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
MOZ.summary: PwC's tax summary, reviewed in August 2026, says the Tax Authority's eDeclaração platform takes income tax and corporate tax returns. Taxes are paid through the taxpayer's bank, with a reference number from the platform. In May 2025 E&M Magazine reported online platforms for tax returns and payments. On 20 November 2026 Minister Salim Valá said taxes and fees can already be paid by mobile phone. In the last twelve months, that statement is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

MRT.short: A figure for revenue paid electronically was reported in 2026.
MRT.summary: The Direction Générale des Impôts says its STT teledeclaration and telepayment system lets taxpayers declare and pay taxes online. The finance minister said more than 500 taxpayers joined the DGI electronic platform. It contributed 36.45% of DGI revenue during 2026. The finance ministry, through the DGI, announced that from 1 November 2026 public establishments must use an electronic platform. That announcement is the change found in the last twelve months.

MUS.short: In 2025 the main taxes and customs duties were paid electronically; no source found reports the share of revenue paid electronically.
MUS.summary: The Revenue Authority says companies pay corporate tax, VAT, PAYE, APS and TDS electronically, in April 2025. Individual income tax returns are filed online, and customs duties and taxes are paid electronically through TradeNet. Foreign digital suppliers file and pay VAT electronically from January 2026. That is the change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

MWI.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
MWI.summary: In September 2024 non-tax revenue agencies were moving to e-payment, starting with the National Registration Bureau. In the last twelve months, a US government guide of June 2026 says mobile money pays public fees such as Digital ID renewals. The police set electronic payment of traffic fines through banks to start in September 2026. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

NAM.short: In 2025 domestic taxes and customs duties were paid by electronic transfer; no figure for revenue paid electronically has been found.
NAM.summary: In May 2025 NamRA said taxpayers confirm domestic tax liabilities on its ITAS portal and pay them by electronic fund transfer. Customs payments can be made by electronic fund transfer too. In October 2019 Finance Minister Schlettwein said the Integrated Tax Administration System became operational in January 2019 with online filing of tax returns. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

NER.short: Taxes are filed and paid online, and since 2026 customs duties are paid through a bank at some offices; no source found reports nationwide coverage.
NER.summary: The tax directorate says its e-sisic portal for electronic declaration and payment of taxes has operated since 13 September 2019. From 1 April 2026 customs duties and taxes on declarations are paid electronically through SONIBANK counters, payment terminals and ATMs. At first this was only at offices where SONIBANK has counters. In the last twelve months, that payment of customs duties through SONIBANK is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are both filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

NGA.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2025; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
NGA.summary: FIRS states all tax and levy collections must be processed through assessments raised on the TaxPro Max platform, in April 2025. The platform handles payment processing and receipts. The Federal Government will unveil the National Single Window, a unified payment platform bringing revenue collection agencies together, in the first quarter of 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

RWA.short: Fees for public services were paid online by mobile money in 2026; no source found says whether the main taxes and customs duties are paid electronically.
RWA.summary: In October 2026 KT Press reported on the Rwanda Governance Scorecard. It said citizens pay fees through online platforms such as Irembo, the national services portal. Payment runs through Mobile Money and Airtel Money. The report names fees for public services and not the main taxes. In the last twelve months, that report is the change found. No source since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SDN.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SDN.summary: The finance ministry says its Isali collection and payment system has been in use since early 2024, with 22 banks under contract. In April 2026 it said Isali collects all public revenue fees approved in the state budget, and that it links to the ASYCUDA customs system. The Sudan Tax Authority said in February 2025 that its e-portal takes returns, while electronic payment channels were still being activated. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, Rabak locality launched mobile electronic collection. No source found says the main taxes are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SEN.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SEN.summary: The DGID says SENTAX is its platform for online filing and payment (télépaiement) of taxes. From 1 September 2026 it is mandatory for all declarations and payments of Large Enterprise Directorate taxpayers. The DGID's communique of 27 August 2026 says SENTAX replaces ETAX for online payment (telepaiement) of taxes by these taxpayers. In the last twelve months, ETAX was replaced by SENTAX for these taxpayers. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SLE.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SLE.summary: In August 2025 the National Revenue Authority's Commissioner General said all excise taxpayers file and pay electronically. On 24 April 2025 Bo District Council launched the GovPay Sierra Leone app so property rates can be paid by mobile money. In July 2026 the NRA was rolling out its NTR Payment Mobile App for non-tax service fees. That rollout is the change found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SOM.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SOM.summary: The Central Bank of Somalia says SOMQR, launched in March 2023, lets customers pay for goods, services, taxes and fees by scanning a code. In July 2024 the finance minister said the ministry had put in place a system to collect sales tax electronically. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the central bank governor said the SIPS instant payment system supports payments to government. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SSD.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SSD.summary: The revenue authority said digital tax payments through Capital Pay will continue, in July 2026. Other tax liabilities must be deposited at designated banks. An economic reform committee told banks collecting tax to follow a policy requiring cash payment. In October 2026 Juba City Council moved all its revenue collection from manual forms to a digital payment system. In the last twelve months, that move is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

STP.short: Customs duties must be paid electronically from October 2026; no source found says whether the main taxes are filed and paid online.
STP.summary: Since February 2025 the tax directorate has taken tax payments by bank transfer. The form and proof of payment are exchanged by email. The customs authority says electronic payment of customs declarations through participating banks began on 1 September 2026. Customs declarations must be paid through electronic channels from 1 October 2026. In the last twelve months, customs payment is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SWZ.short: In 2026 income tax was filed and paid online and customs duties paid through a bank; no source found says whether VAT is filed online.
SWZ.summary: On 4 March 2024 the Eswatini Revenue Service's Tax Ease portal went live with integrated payments for taxes. On 12 June 2026 the ERS launched its Integrated Payment Solution with FNB Eswatini. It lets customs duties and import VAT be paid through the bank. In October 2026 the ERS said 2026 annual returns are filed and paid wholly online, through Tax-Ease or the TaxPAL app. Both date from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says VAT or customs declarations are filed online. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

SYC.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2024; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
SYC.summary: In March 2024 the Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) said taxpayers pay by bank transfer or at SRC offices from January 2024. They send the payment slip, return form and proof of payment by email. The SRC said it had begun migrating to a new online tax portal. In May 2024 the WTO trade facilitation database listed an electronic payment module among completed additions to the SRC's ASYCUDA World customs system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

TCD.short: Chad's main taxes are filed and paid online and customs duties paid electronically since 2024; no source found reports the electronic share of revenue.
TCD.summary: In 2024 the tax directorate said E-Tax lets taxpayers pay all the taxes and duties they owe online. Customs says all customs duties and taxes can be paid electronically since February 2024. In February 2026 the finance ministry signed a five-year convention with mobile money operators. In the last twelve months, that convention is the change found. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for revenue paid electronically. Mature would need a source from the past three years that gives a share or an amount of revenue paid electronically.

TGO.short: A figure for revenue paid electronically was reported in 2025.
TGO.summary: OTR publishes electronic declaration and payment rates by directorate for 2020 to 2025. Telepaiement was at 24% for DCIG/DOFAN/DOFR in 2025, up from 13% in 2024. Togo's justice ministry launched on 2 July 2026 online payment of fees for nearly forty services of the Tribunal de Grande Instance de Lomé. On 17 September 2026 the Ministry of Finance and Budget launched e-TPU for online filing and electronic payment of the Taxe Professionnelle Unique. Both launches came in the last twelve months.

TUN.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
TUN.summary: On 3 November 2026 the finance minister said a unified tax account for filing and remote payment would start in the first quarter of 2027. The national services portal says fines due to the Ministry of Finance can be paid online or by USSD. In November 2025 the customs spokesman said several customs offices offered electronic payment. In the last twelve months, the unified tax account was announced for 2027. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

TZA.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
TZA.summary: The Bank of Tanzania governor says electronic payments are increasingly used for government services through control numbers. The Mandatory Electronic Payments for Specified Transactions Order is in force from 1 July 2026. It requires fees, charges, levies, tolls, fares and parking to be paid electronically. Covered businesses have six months to set up compliant systems. In the last twelve months, that order is the change found. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

UGA.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
UGA.summary: MTN Mobile Money and the Uganda Revenue Authority announced an enhanced URA tax and government payment menu on 16518#, live nationwide. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the Revenue Authority said tax can be paid by EFT, RTGS, VISA, bank counter and mobile USSD. It said VAT, rental income tax and local excise duty returns are filed on the web. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

ZAF.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2026; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
ZAF.summary: In September 2023 BusinessTech reported SARS saying taxpayers pay through eFiling or EFT to public beneficiary IDs. These cover customs, excise, income tax, PAYE, provisional tax, VAT and dividends tax. SARS says Customs and Excise clients declaring goods electronically must use the SARS eFiling service to make payments. Personal Income Tax and Travellers' payments can be made on the SARS MobiApp. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

ZMB.short: In 2024 the revenue authority said about 99 percent of its payments, customs included, were made electronically.
ZMB.summary: In February 2024 the revenue authority said about 99 percent of its payments were made electronically. In December 2023 the revenue authority brought in its Integrated Payment System. The Office of the Accountant General says the government's digital payment and service platforms have collected more than K8.8 billion (US$488 million). In the last twelve months, the Government Services Bus began taking council revenue. Eight councils have taken property rates, business levies and permits electronically through the Government Services Bus since June 2026. About K21.7 million came through the Government Services Bus in the month after its June 2026 rollout to eight councils.

ZWE.short: Some taxes or fees could be paid electronically in 2025; no source found reports the main taxes and duties.
ZWE.summary: ZIMRA Public Notice 75 of 2024 says taxpayers file returns online through its Self-Service Portal. They pay VAT, PAYE and other taxes by deposit or bank transfer, posted in TaRMS. ZIMRA launched the TaRMS payment and return modules on 6 December 2023. Customs payments stay on the old platform. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 ZINARA introduced a multi-currency e-wallet on which motorists pay tolls, vehicle licences, radio licences and insurance. No source found since October 2023 says the main taxes and customs duties are filed and paid electronically. Operating would need the main taxes and customs duties filed and paid electronically.

AGO.short: In 2024, 1.3 per cent of rural people had electricity.
AGO.summary: In 2024, 1.3 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The series gives no figure for the years just before, so no source found says whether it is rising or falling. It counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 27 per cent or more has been found. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from any source.

BDI.short: In 2024, 3.6 per cent of rural people had electricity.
BDI.summary: In 2024, 3.6 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 1.6 in 2021, 1.7 in 2022 and 2.3 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 27 per cent or more has been found. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from any source.

BEN.short: In 2024, 45 per cent of rural people had electricity.
BEN.summary: In 2024, 45 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 18 in 2021, 45.5 in 2022 and 43.7 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 53 per cent or more has been found. Establishing would need 53 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity.

BFA.short: In 2024, 12.7 per cent of rural people had electricity.
BFA.summary: In 2024, 12.7 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 3.4 in 2022 and 2 in 2023. The electricity regulator, ARSE, put the rural electrification rate at 7.2 per cent in 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 27 per cent or more has been found. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, from any source.

BWA.short: In 2024, 45.9 per cent of rural people had electricity.
BWA.summary: In 2024, 45.9 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 25 in 2021, 25 in 2022 and 25 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 53 per cent or more has been found. Establishing would need 53 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity.

CAF.short: In 2024, 2 per cent of rural people had electricity.
CAF.summary: In 2024, 2 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 1.6 in 2021, 1.6 in 2022 and 2.3 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 27 per cent or more has been found. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from any source.

CIV.short: In 2024, 47.7 per cent of rural people had electricity.
CIV.summary: In 2024, 47.7 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 45.2 in 2021, 45.3 in 2022 and 48 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 53 per cent or more has been found. Establishing would need 53 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity.

CMR.short: In January 2025 the World Bank said about 25 per cent of rural Cameroonians had electricity.
CMR.summary: In January 2025 the World Bank said 75 per cent of rural Cameroonians remain without electricity, so about 25 per cent have it. Its rural electricity access series gives 42.7 per cent of rural people for 2024. The series counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure later than January 2025 has been found, and that statement names no year for its figure. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, from any source.

COD.short: In 2024, 1 per cent of rural people had electricity.
COD.summary: In 2024, 1 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The same series gives 1 in 2021, 1 in 2022 and 1 in 2023. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure of 27 per cent or more has been found. Preparing would need 27 per cent or more of rural people to have electricity, in the latest figure for 2023 or later, from any source.

AGO.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
AGO.summary: Eutelsat secured a 15-year licence for its OneWeb low-earth-orbit service in Angola in 2025. In the last twelve months, Q-KON and SISTEC opened a Luanda point of presence for Twoobii OneWeb in October 2026. In July 2026 the regulator, INACOM, licensed the startup NomaTech to sell internet access over ANGOSAT-2. No source found says services on two different satellite networks are on sale, and no sale over ANGOSAT-2 has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

BDI.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
BDI.summary: MyBroadband's table lists Burundi as 'Available' for Starlink on 17 July 2026. Connecting Africa reports that Starlink launched services in Burundi in September 2024. Le360 lists Burundi among 29 African countries where Starlink had been granted a licence as of May 2026. In the last twelve months, Community Voice named Starlink and NT Global as the satellite providers in March 2026. No source found names the network NT Global sells. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

BEN.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
BEN.summary: ARCEP Benin lists Starlink among the operators with fixed internet subscriptions, with 2,550 subscriptions at 31 March 2026. MyBroadband's Starlink status table of 17 July 2026 lists Benin as 'Available' for Starlink (SpaceX). In the last twelve months, the regulator's Starlink count rose from 2,215 at Q4 2025 to 2,550 at 31 March 2026. No source found says services on two different satellite networks are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

BFA.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
BFA.summary: MyBroadband's status table of 17 July 2026 lists Burkina Faso with estimated Starlink availability '2026', not 'Available'. The Minister of Digital Transition said negotiations with Starlink are advancing and the state hopes soon to decide whether to let it offer services, so no authorisation has yet been given. ARCEP recalled in March 2024 that Starlink held no authorisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

BWA.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on two satellite networks.
BWA.summary: ITWeb, citing Ookla data for the first quarter of 2026, reports that Starlink is in service in Botswana. Paratus Botswana, in a company press release, says it provides Eutelsat low-earth-orbit (OneWeb) satellite services combined with terrestrial links to mining operations in Botswana. MyBroadband's table lists Botswana as Available on 17 July 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

CAF.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
CAF.summary: ARCEP's half-year 2026 observatory says Starlink CAR obtained a licence to market and operate satellite fixed wireless internet, with no licence date. A table dated 17 July 2026 lists Starlink in the Central African Republic as 'Available'. In the last twelve months, a Ministry communiqué issued in Bangui in April 2026 suspended illegally imported Starlink kits operating in roaming mode. No source found says a second satellite network is on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

CIV.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on two satellite networks.
CIV.summary: Starlink, sold directly to households, and Eutelsat Konnect, sold by Orange and MTN, are both on sale in Cote d'Ivoire as of the 28 July 2026 article. ARTCI authorised Starlink, subject to the regulator's ability to interrupt network access. In the last twelve months, MTN and Eutelsat made a Konnect capacity agreement in April 2026, beside Orange's existing Orange Sat service. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

CMR.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
CMR.summary: NewsWatch reported on 27 July 2026 that Starlink's licence application in Cameroon had sat unresolved for over two years. The regulator ART declined comment and said the file is with the ministry MINPOSTEL. Cameroon is among 16 countries Starlink's availability map lists as 'Starting in 2026'. In the last twelve months, customs seized 10 Starlink modems at the Nkometou checkpoint on 12 December 2025 as unauthorised equipment. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

COD.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
COD.summary: The regulator, ARPTC, licensed Starlink as an internet provider on 2 May 2025. In March 2024 it had called the use of Starlink's network illegal. In the last twelve months, Somaf Group opened a shop selling Starlink kits in Kindu in April 2026. In July 2026 Radiocom, an authorised reseller, said Kinshasa's capacity on the residential plan was used up for four to six months. The regulator's 2026 tariff page lists Konnect Africa with no tariff, so no sale on a second network has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

Agence Ecofin reports Congo is among 16 countries Starlink marks 'Starting in 2026' on its map, and that service was still not available despite a 2025 forecast. ARPCE seized an unauthorised Starlink installation in Congo-Brazzaville in June 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated later names a provider licensed. The ban covers installing, testing, deploying or using Starlink, and no authorisation had been granted to Starlink. Agence Ecofin reports that Starlink's availability map lists Comoros among 16 African countries marked 'Starting in 2026' with no launch date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

CPV.short: Satellite broadband from one network was on sale in 2026 and the regulator counts its share; no source found reports a second network.
CPV.summary: The regulator ARME's market indicators for the second quarter of 2026 give Starlink 0.87 per cent of Cabo Verde's 500,263 internet access subscriptions. Starlink went live in Cape Verde in December 2024. In the last twelve months, its share rose from 0.64% of internet subscriptions in ARME's first-quarter 2026 report to 0.87% at the end of June 2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

DJI.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
DJI.summary: Starlink's availability table of 17 July 2026 lists Djibouti as 'No planned launch date', so it is not on sale there. Le360 says Starlink's site gives Djibouti 'service date unknown'. Djibouti is not in its list of 29 countries that had licensed Starlink as of May 2026. Another article does not say whether any licence or application exists. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

DZA.short: A satellite broadband provider licensed by 2026, with no service on sale held.
DZA.summary: State-owned Algerie Telecom Satellite (VSAT and GMPCS licences) and Djezzy (VSAT licence) are the only companies authorised to provide satellite services in Algeria. In the last twelve months, ARPCE launched a call for competition on 9 April 2026 for two licences for public satellite networks in non-geostationary orbit. Algeria is listed among about 34 countries where Starlink is in regulatory limbo, as of June 2026. No source found says households or businesses can buy satellite broadband from a licensed provider. Establishing would need households or businesses able to buy satellite broadband from a licensed provider.

EGY.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
EGY.summary: Telegraph Egypt reported on 2025-06-18 that Starlink was not yet activated in Egypt. It said selling or marketing it requires an official licence not yet held, and talks with the ministry were under way. A Starlink availability table lists Egypt as 'No planned launch date'. Egypt is placed among countries in regulatory limbo for Starlink, neither approved nor explicitly banned. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

ERI.short: Nothing found says a satellite broadband provider is licensed, or that none is, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says a satellite broadband provider is licensed, or that none is.

ETH.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
ETH.summary: The Ethiopian Communications Authority stated in a public notice that Starlink has not been granted a licence in Ethiopia. It said no discussions, past, ongoing or planned, have taken place with Starlink about one. Birr Metrics reports that the Authority denied granting Starlink a licence. TechMag lists Ethiopia among countries that continue to block or restrict Starlink to protect state-owned telecoms. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

GAB.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
GAB.summary: Gabon's regulator Arcep announced a ban on installing, using and marketing Starlink offers in Gabon, with prison and fines for offenders. Agence Ecofin reports Starlink's availability map shows Gabon as 'Starting in 2026', meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, and the service is still not available. Le360 lists Gabon among countries where Starlink is announced for 2026 with no licence granted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

GHA.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
GHA.summary: The NCA approved Starlink's application in April 2024, and in August 2024 said Starlink would start operating by the end of that month. Its November 2024 guidance says customers can buy the Starlink kit online or from four resellers. The NCA counted 15,384 satellite internet subscriptions in June 2025. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: MyBroadband listed Starlink as available in July 2026. The minister said in March 2024 that OneWeb was licensed, but no OneWeb sale has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

GIN.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
GIN.summary: Agence Ecofin reported on 31 August 2026 that Guinea is among 16 countries marked 'Starting in 2026' on Starlink's availability map. Starlink service is still not available there. MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table lists Guinea with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available'. In the last twelve months, ARPT agents were reported on 10 August 2026 to be uninstalling and confiscating Starlink equipment used by Wi-Fi resellers. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

GMB.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
GMB.summary: TechnoMag's article of 29 June 2026 lists the Gambia among 19 countries 'Scheduled for 2026', not among those where Starlink is active. MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table lists Gambia with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available'. In the last twelve months, the Minister of Digital Economy refused to approve the VSAT permit paid for in February 2026, saying Starlink needs a general satellite licence. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

GNB.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
GNB.summary: MyBroadband's table lists Guinea-Bissau as 'Available' for Starlink as of 17 July 2026. In the last twelve months, ARN-TIC, by Despacho 15/CA/ARN/2026, extended to 31 December 2026 the provisional General Authorisation held by Starlink Guiné-Bissau SARL. ARN also stated that unauthorised entities are illegally selling internet over the Starlink network and that it will intensify enforcement. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

GNQ.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
GNQ.summary: Starlink went live in Equatorial Guinea on 29 August 2026, with an order page on starlink.com, sold directly by Starlink under provisional approval. In the last twelve months, Vice-president Nguema Obiang Mangue announced on 2026-09-09 that the country officially launched Starlink, operated by SpaceX. A government session that day placed legal selling authority with ORTEL and ordered individuals' contracts outside official channels cancelled. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

KEN.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
KEN.summary: Starlink is on sale in Kenya, with a capped plan priced at $10 a month in 2026. Vodacom has a wholesale agreement with Starlink in Kenya. In the last twelve months, the Communications Authority of Kenya's count rose from 25,088 satellite internet subscriptions at 31 March 2026 to nearly 27,700 at 30 June 2026. Amazon Kuiper Kenya Limited has applied for a licence, and none is stated as granted. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

LBR.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
LBR.summary: MyBroadband's table of Starlink status in African countries, dated 17 July 2026, lists Liberia as 'Available'. Le360 lists Liberia among 29 African countries where Starlink had been granted a licence as of May 2026. The LTA Board Chairman said Starlink has entered Liberia while the LTA drafts its first satellite regulations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

LBY.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2024, on one satellite network.
LBY.summary: Eutelsat OneWeb is sold in Libya through a multi-year exclusive distribution agreement with a Libyan local partner, extended to LEO connectivity from early 2024. It serves oil and gas, telecoms, finance, government and humanitarian customers. Starlink is not licensed in Libya, and talks with the regulator GACI, open since 2024, had reached no agreement. They were on hold until further notice as of the article's date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

LSO.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
LSO.summary: MyBroadband's Starlink status table of 17 July 2026 lists Lesotho as 'Available'. In the last twelve months, Vodacom Lesotho launched its Enterprise Satellite Connectivity solution in August 2026, a fully managed satellite broadband service powered by Starlink LEO. ITWeb Africa, citing Ookla, counts Lesotho among 27 African countries where Starlink is currently licensed, with no licence date given. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

MAR.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2024, on one satellite network.
MAR.summary: The minister said customers without terrestrial broadband can get support for satellite internet under the VSAT initiative, up to 2,500 dirhams per subscription from an approved provider. In the last twelve months, on 20 April 2026 the minister said VSAT links serve zones hard to reach by land. Challenge.ma reports that no approval for Starlink has been announced by the ANRT. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

MDG.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on two satellite networks.
MDG.summary: The regulator, ARTEC, signed a five-year licence for Starlink Madagascar on 29 April 2024. Starlink has been sold through its website since late June 2024. In the last twelve months, Airtel Madagascar was reported in June 2026 to sell enterprise satellite internet over Eutelsat's OneWeb network. MyBroadband still listed Starlink as available in July 2026. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

MLI.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
MLI.summary: Agence Ecofin reported on 31 August 2026 that Starlink is not yet available in Mali, which is listed as 'Starting in 2026'. Regulatory authorisation is pending. Le360 reports that Mali is among the countries where Starlink is announced as available from 2026 but no licence has been granted. In the last twelve months, AMRTP, Mali's regulator, stated on 11 June 2026 that installing, operating, importing and selling Starlink devices without prior authorisation is a violation. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

MOZ.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2025 on two satellite networks; no source found reports a regulator's count of subscribers.
MOZ.summary: INCM, the regulator, said in February 2025 that it approved Starlink in under a year under fast-track licensing. It described a mixed market in which SATCOM, a VSAT provider since 1999 with more than 500 terminals, competes with Starlink. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: MyBroadband listed Starlink as available in Mozambique in July 2026. In mid-2026 the residential plan cost MZN 3,000 a month. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

MRT.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
MRT.summary: Starlink's Mauritanian licence application, sought for about two years, is still pending, with authorities pressing security and data-control conditions. Starlink's availability map shows Mauritania as 'Starting in 2026', meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, and the service is not yet available. Starlink and Amazon are not yet authorised for direct public service in Mauritania. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated later names a satellite broadband provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

MUS.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2025, on one satellite network; no source found reports a regulator's count of subscribers.
MUS.summary: The regulator, ICTA, ruled on 22 May 2025 that a low-orbit network may serve Mauritius only through a licensed Mauritian internet provider. Emtel launched OneWeb low-orbit internet across the country on 4 June 2025. ICTA approved Emtel's satellite internet tariffs, effective 28 May 2025. In the last twelve months, the head of ICTA said in August 2026 that OneWeb is operating through its local partner. No licence for Starlink has been found, and no second satellite network on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

MWI.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
MWI.summary: MyBroadband's Starlink status table lists Malawi as Available on 17 July 2026. Le360 lists Malawi among 29 African countries where Starlink had been granted a licence as of May 2026. Macra's director general cites the licensing of Starlink as creating competition on the market. In the last twelve months, Paratus launched Paratus Malawi in November 2026, selling Starlink connectivity to businesses in Lilongwe, Blantyre and Mzuzu. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

NAM.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
NAM.summary: Q-KON and its licensed partners launched Eutelsat OneWeb's low-orbit service on 19 June 2026, for businesses. In the last twelve months, Paratus Namibia launched OneWeb service for homes and firms across the country in October 2026. In November 2025 the regulator, CRAN, approved Paratus's Yursat Adapt satellite packages, and no network is named for them. Starlink's own map listed Namibia as starting in 2026, with authorisation still pending. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

NER.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
NER.summary: Decree 2024-728 of 21 November 2024 granted Starlink Niger a five-year licence to run a public low-orbit satellite internet network. The communications minister announced the service on sale from 13 March 2025. In the last twelve months, Airtel Niger began selling Starlink to businesses and public bodies on 16 January 2026. MyBroadband still listed Starlink as available in July 2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

NGA.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
NGA.summary: The NCC, the regulator, issued Starlink internet service and gateway licences in May 2022. Starlink began selling to households and businesses in January 2023. In the last twelve months, the NCC's count of Starlink subscribers rose from 91,991 at the end of December 2025 to 98,642 in June 2026. The NCC register lists Airtel's VSAT licence on the OneWeb network from January 2023, and no OneWeb sale has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

RWA.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
RWA.summary: Paratus Rwanda, which began operating in Rwanda about a year before this 18 August 2026 announcement, sells Starlink-powered internet to businesses. A country availability table lists Starlink as available in Rwanda. RURA counted 4,489 Starlink subscribers for the second quarter of 2025, as reported by TechCabal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SDN.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2023, on one satellite network.
SDN.summary: Canar Telecommunication procured YahClick satellite capacity under a USD 15 million six-year agreement to deliver broadband to consumers and businesses in Sudan. MyBroadband's table of Starlink availability lists Sudan as having no planned launch date. In the last twelve months, the Rapid Support Forces ordered Starlink networks disabled indefinitely in En Nahud locality, West Kordofan, from 26 August 2026. The order came from an armed group, and the regulator did not issue it. No source found says services on two different satellite networks are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SEN.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SEN.summary: Sonatel Orange launched satellite internet with Eutelsat's Konnect in January 2026, and Starlink launched commercially in February 2026. In the last twelve months, on 7 September 2026 the Supreme Court provisionally suspended Starlink's licence, on a challenge by Sonatel. The Point reported that on 3 November 2026 the court left the suspension in place pending a final ruling. No source found says both networks are on sale since the suspension. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SLE.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone licensed Starlink in June 2023, and the service went live in June 2024. In January 2025 the communications minister said three local companies provide Starlink service. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in March 2026 NatCA's director-general said Starlink had been operating for two years, and MyBroadband still listed it as available in July 2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SOM.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SOM.summary: MyBroadband's table of Starlink status in African countries as of 17 July 2026 lists Somalia as Available. AstaanConnect became Somalia's first official Starlink reseller, selling kits and subscriptions to households, businesses, schools and offices. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: TechnoMag lists Somalia among 26 countries where Starlink is active as of mid-2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SSD.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SSD.summary: The National Communication Authority signed landing-rights and provisional service licences for Starlink on 26 June 2024, and in July 2024 it approved four Starlink tariff plans. MTN South Sudan began selling Starlink kits and subscriptions nationwide in October 2025. In the last twelve months, Sudans Post said in January 2026 that satellite internet had widened access in some rural areas. It said cost puts it beyond most traders and households. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

STP.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
STP.summary: The US Embassy states that Starlink satellite internet services had recently launched in Sao Tome and Principe, as discussed with the Prime Minister during a 14-16 January 2026 visit. MyBroadband's table lists Sao Tome e Principe as Available on 17 July 2026. Le360 lists Sao Tome and Principe among 29 African countries with a Starlink licence granted. In the last twelve months, the launch was reported as above, and no earlier position has been found. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SWZ.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SWZ.summary: Starlink became available across Eswatini in December 2023, at R950 a month for the residential service. In November 2024 the managing director of Paratus Eswatini said the regulator, ESCCOM, had signed off the Starlink licence. By July 2025 Paratus Eswatini, an authorised Starlink reseller, had completed installations across the country. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: MyBroadband still listed Starlink as available in July 2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

SYC.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
SYC.summary: State House Seychelles reports that Starlink began operations in Seychelles with a soft launch at State House on 24 July 2026. Households and businesses can subscribe through Starlink's online platform, buying the hardware kit. In the last twelve months, SCRA officials confirmed that Starlink has been authorised to operate in Seychelles under the telecommunications regulations. No earlier position has been found. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

TCD.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
TCD.summary: Starlink launched in Chad at a press conference on 4 July 2025. An August 2025 order set its conditions of operation, including user identification. In the last twelve months, the minister regretted the limits of the packages on offer in June 2026. In November 2026 Russell Southwood wrote that Starlink sells through resellers such as Ilan Telecoms, with terminals delivered only to N'Djamena. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

TGO.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
TGO.summary: Techs.tg says Togo does not yet officially have Starlink service, and that ISOC-Togo began negotiations with Starlink in March 2024. Agence Ecofin says Starlink had shown Togo as planned for 2025 and now lists it for 2026, subject to approval by public authorities. Le360 lists Togo among countries where Starlink is announced as available from 2026 but no licence has been granted. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

TUN.short: A 2026 source says satellite broadband is not licensed or is banned.
TUN.summary: MyBroadband's table of 17 July 2026 lists Tunisia as '2026', not 'Available', so Starlink was not on sale there. THD states that Starlink has not obtained a commercialisation licence in Tunisia, its process reportedly paused after a feasibility study. Agence Ecofin states that Tunisia is on Starlink's map as 'Starting in 2026', with regulatory authorisation pending and no launch date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

TZA.short: In 2026 Starlink still awaited a licence and no satellite broadband provider is licensed; no source found says whether one will be.
TZA.summary: In November 2024 the regulator, TCRA, confirmed that Starlink Satellite Tanzania Limited had applied for network and application services licences. In the last twelve months, in October 2026 Starlink still had no operating licence, and its application was still under review. No other satellite broadband provider has been found licensed in Tanzania. With no provider licensed, there is no count of satellite broadband subscribers. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

UGA.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
UGA.summary: Starlink launched commercial satellite internet in Uganda on 2 September 2026 after regulatory approval. Roke Telkom and Paratus Uganda launched Starlink for Business, with Paratus Uganda the first provider to offer Starlink commercially. In the last twelve months, Roke Telkom with Paratus Uganda launched Starlink enterprise connectivity, reselling Starlink LEO capacity to businesses. No earlier position has been found. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

ZAF.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on two satellite networks.
ZAF.summary: YahClick has been sold in South Africa for years through internet service providers such as Vox Telecom. Eutelsat OneWeb operates commercially in South Africa through partners such as Paratus and Q-KON, per TechCentral commentary. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: TechCentral reported on 2026-08-23 that Starlink remains unlicensed after not meeting the 30% historically-disadvantaged ownership requirement. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

ZMB.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
ZMB.summary: Starlink's status table for African countries, dated 17 July 2026, lists Zambia as Available. Zambia is listed among markets that approved Starlink quickly, without local-ownership requirements or with them set aside. In the last twelve months, Starlink's demand outstripped allocated capacity in 2025-2026, forcing suspended new residential sign-ups in some markets. The article says similar freezes have hit Zambia. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

ZWE.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on one satellite network.
ZWE.summary: The regulator, POTRAZ, licensed Starlink on 6 September 2024, and it went live that day. In July 2025 the ICT minister said the President had approved the licensing of low-orbit satellite service himself. In the last twelve months, POTRAZ's count of VSAT subscriptions, the category that holds Starlink, rose from 23,410 at the end of 2024 to 67,057 at the end of 2025. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

AGO.summary: No stage is set. No figure for 2023 or later has been found for secondary schools with internet for teaching. BWA.summary: No stage is set. No figure for 2023 or later has been found for secondary schools with internet for teaching.
