AGO.short: A 2025 decree names a pupil data platform for recording results; no source found says whether any school uses it, so no stage is set.
AGO.summary: No stage is set. The education ministry's Sistema de Informação de Gestão Escolar (SIGE) is also called the EMIS, and is a questionnaire that schools answer, described in 2022. A June 2025 decree lists a pupil data platform among the instruments for recording assessment results. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing found says whether that platform has been built or whether any school uses it. Preparing would need an EMIS for primary schools being prepared or piloted, with staff trained, equipment delivered, an agreement signed or pilot schools using it.

BDI.short: In 2023 the yearly school count was collected on paper; no source found says whether primary schools keep per-pupil records, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: No stage is set. In 2023 Burundi's yearly school census, which it calls an EMIS, was collected on paper at the school and entered electronically at central level. The Annuaire statistique de l'éducation for 2024-2025 is dated December 2025. No other change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found describes a system with a record for each pupil that a school adds to during the year. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

BEN.short: Primary schools entered enrolments and class lists themselves in 2026; no source found says how many do, or whether any enter attendance or results.
BEN.summary: The government's progress report of December 2020 says use of Educmaster is compulsory in all public and private pre-primary, primary, secondary and technical schools. In the last twelve months, on 16 February 2026, the minister ordered every school to complete its enrolments for all nursery and primary classes by 23 February. His letter says several schools enter only their final-year examination candidates. No number or share of primary schools entering data has been published. Nothing shows them entering attendance or results. Operating would need a published share or count showing more than half of primary schools entering attendance or results.

BFA.short: A national pupil register was in pilot in 2024 and enrolment had not begun by June 2025; no source found reports the number of schools.
BFA.summary: On 25 June 2025 two ministers reviewed the national pupil file, built with WURI project support. At that date progressive enrolment of pupils was due to start at the next school year. In April 2025 the student management platform was still to be designed. In the last twelve months, KIX-SEEDS, a university-led pilot, ran in the pilot communes of Manga and Bingo in May 2026. No source found reports the pupil file past its pilot. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

BWA.short: A fund was connecting remote primary schools to broadband in 2024; no source found says how schools keep pupil records, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: No stage is set. The regulator BOCRA's 2024 annual report lists the Universal Access and Service Fund's broadband connectivity for primary schools in remote areas. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No dated statement of how primary schools keep their learners' records has been found, and no system holding a record for each learner is described. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

CAF.short: By 2026 the ministry ran a yearly school count; no source found says whether schools keep a per-pupil record, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: No stage is set. The Ministry of National Education calls its yearly school count its EMIS or its SIGE, and publishes a statistical yearbook. It also runs a teacher system, HRMIS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No system holding a record for each learner is described. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

CIV.short: A school information system launched in two regions in July 2025 after a 2024 pilot; no source found gives its coverage or who enters data.
CIV.summary: The education ministry's strategy says its DOBCONNECT project was started in January 2024 in 5 pilot establishments of the Abidjan regional directorates. Agence Ecofin reports the SIGE was launched on 10 July 2025 in the Bouaké and San Pedro regions, with a national extension to follow. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found gives either system's level, a count of schools using it, or who enters its data. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

CMR.short: No source found says how primary schools keep their pupils' records, so no stage is set.
CMR.summary: No stage is set. No source found says how primary schools in Cameroon keep their learners' records, on paper or digitally. The education systems named for the country are held by name only, with nothing on what they do in schools. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No system holding a record for each learner has been described. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

COD.short: Ministry staff, not schools, registered pupils by app in a 20-primary-school pilot in April 2026; no source found says whether it will go national.
COD.summary: SERNIE is the education ministry's service for individual learner data. Its director writes that since 1991 its staff have recorded learners in schools on paper forms. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, SERNIE completed the first test of EDUSER in schools, a three-week pilot. Its staff registered 8,634 learners in 20 primary schools of Kasai province in the three weeks by app. The director says a national rollout, which is not funded, is the next step. No primary school is shown entering its own learners' records. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

COG.short: A November 2023 decree creates a per-pupil record that schools are to fill; no source found says whether any school uses it.
COG.summary: Decree 2023-1751 of 2 November 2023 creates an education management information system, which Congo calls the SIGE. The decree assigns data entry to the schools or their inspectorates. In May 2023 a digital workspace for schools, the ENT, existed only as a specification, which proposed a trial from September 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found shows staff trained, equipment delivered or any school taking part in a trial. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

COM.short: Schools have entered marks since June 2025, and 45% of public primary schools were integrated by February 2026; no source reports the share entering marks.
COM.summary: On 2 February 2026 the ministry counted all public secondary schools and 45% of public primary schools as integrated into its e-Msomo platform. In December 2025 UNICEF Comores put more than 700 schools on e-Msomo. In the last twelve months, on 2 February 2026, the ministry gave late schools one more week. It said the platform's single report card will be the only document accepted for university enrolment. The 45% is a rate of schools integrated, and no share of primary schools entering marks has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

CPV.short: In 2025 the government said all basic schools use the system, with marks and absences entered per pupil; no source found reports the rural share.
CPV.summary: The ministry states that its school management system, SIGE, was implemented in all 395 basic education schools by February 2019. On 25 June 2025 the government said it was already used in all basic and secondary schools. The order for the 2025/2026 school year, in force from 1 September 2025, requires teachers to record pupils' assessment on SIGE's result-entry sheets. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no figure for rural schools has been found. Mature would need at least 90 per cent of primary schools entering data, with daily attendance, and a rural share.

DJI.short: In 2023 school heads registered pupils and sent absences through a national per-pupil record; no source found reports the share of primary schools doing so.
DJI.summary: All public schools transmitted their data through GOSE, the education ministry's pupil management system, as at 28 November 2023, the World Bank reported. At that date the school principal registered and transferred pupils in it, and absences went through it to central management. The project's target for primary schools transmitting on time was still unmet. On 20 November 2025 the minister said the ministry's platforms give it reliable data to detect pupils in difficulty before they drop out. No change in the number of schools using the system has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share or count showing more than half of primary schools entering attendance or results.

DZA.short: Marks for 11.7 million pupils were on the ministry's platform in 2024, level not named; no source found says how many primary schools enter them.
DZA.summary: The Ministry of National Education says it designed and built its digital platform itself, in a presentation dated 2024. The presentation says the platform manages the schooling of 11,709,830 pupils, including marks, averages, teachers' observations and orientation. In May 2025 first-year primary enrolment was done only through the system's parents' space. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how many primary schools enter data, or whether they enter attendance. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

EGY.short: The ministry signed for a nationwide attendance and results platform in August 2026; no source found says whether any school uses it.
EGY.summary: The Education Sector Plan 2023-2027 says the ministry's EMIS will be expanded to hold data down to class and student level. In the last twelve months, on 10 August 2026, the ministry signed an agreement with the Japanese company SPRIX. It is for a nationwide attendance, performance and assessment platform. The ministry said it will start in several education departments in 2026/2027 before gradual national expansion. Nothing found shows any school yet entering data on it. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot, in live use in some primary schools.

ERI.short: A digital platform for the yearly school count was built by 2026; no source says how schools keep pupils' records, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: No stage is set. The Ministry of Education's statistical yearbooks have the 2022-2023 and 2023-2024 editions published. A digital platform was developed between February 2025 and April 2026 to digitalise data collection that had been manual. Eritrea calls both EMIS. Its development period ended in April 2026, within the last twelve months. No dated statement that primary schools keep learners' records on paper has been found, and no system keeping a record for each learner is described. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

ETH.short: The ministry's web-based system, with a number for each pupil, was piloted by June 2025; no source found says whether any primary school uses it.
ETH.summary: By June 2025 the Ministry of Education developed and completed its web-based EMIS and finalised a directive for it, with World Bank support. UNICEF reports that it had been finalised and piloted, with deployment to primary schools not begun. Deployment to 4,500 primary schools in 156 weredas was planned for July 2025 to June 2026. No source dated after June 2025 reports it, so no change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing shows the system in live use in a primary school. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

GAB.short: 728 schools managed pupils' marks in a vendor's application in 2024; no source found reports the share of primary schools, as no total is given.
GAB.summary: Gabonreview reported on 27 September 2024 that Xgest is used by 728 schools. That is a count of schools of all levels together. On 24 September 2024 the ministry closed pupil enrolment on X-Gest after irregularities and ordered that no personal data pass through it. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, SOSUP, a state body, had been deploying eFormation, giving every establishment and every pupil a unique identifier. The 728 schools come with no total, so no share of primary schools has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing more than half of primary schools entering attendance or results.

GHA.short: In November 2025, 733 primary schools reported each pupil's literacy and numeracy results on a digital platform; no source reports their share of primary schools.
GHA.summary: By the World Bank's count, 733 schools were reporting on the platform at 27 November 2025. Primary schools assess and report literacy and numeracy outcomes for individual learners on it. In the last twelve months the count stood at 733 in August 2024, in June 2025 and in November 2025, so it did not change. The target is 16,000 schools by December 2028. No total of primary schools is given beside the 733, so no share has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

GIN.short: In March 2026 a nationwide registration gave primary pupils a single school number, in secondary since 2022; no source says how many schools took part.
GIN.summary: Guinea's unique pupil number, the matricule, began in 2022 at collège and lycée and was extended to primary. In the last twelve months the ministry announced the digital registration of primary pupils on 25 February 2026. Registration was launched in Matoto on 5 March 2026. Matoto's communal education director said it covered the whole national territory, public and private schools alike. No number or share of primary schools registered is given, and no source says who keys the record. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

GMB.short: Schools record each pupil in a national register, scaled up from 200 pilot schools in 2021; no source says how many primary schools enter data.
GMB.summary: The registry began as a pilot in 200 schools in 2020, and the ministry scaled it to national level in 2021. In August 2025 DHIS2 said schools record each learner's background, attendance and progression in the ministry's student registry. By August 2025 it held nearly 80% of Gambian learners, a share of learners and not of schools. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the ministry opened its Education Data Center to the public. No count or share of primary schools entering data has been published. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

GNB.short: Pupil records from one region's schools were entered at a regional office in a 2017/18 pilot; no source found says whether it continued.
GNB.summary: In 2017/18 the Gabu pilot was developed by the Gabu regional government and the NGO FEC with ministry units. That year teams from the ministry and FEC collected learner, teacher and class records school by school in Gabu and keyed them in at a regional hub. The 2018 report describes the system as a pilot for Gabu region. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the pilot continued, how many schools it covered, and any entry by the schools themselves have not been found. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year.

GNQ.short: Schools return a yearly count by questionnaire (2026); no source found says whether any keeps a per-pupil record, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: No stage is set. Equatorial Guinea runs a Censo Escolar Nacional and publishes an Anuario Estadístico de la Educación built on it. The ministry's yearbook gives the Sistema de Información y Mapa Escolar (SIME), which processes the census returns, as its EMIS. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No record for each learner that schools add to during the year has been found. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

KEN.short: Primary and secondary schools register each pupil on the national system (2026); no source says how many primary schools do so.
KEN.summary: A ministry circular dated 17 August 2026 tells schools to enter and correct each learner's record in KEMIS themselves. By 10 November 2026 KEMIS had captured about 5.06 million primary school learners. In the last twelve months KEMIS became the required platform for the 2026 Grade 10 selection. In September 2026 schools reported failed logins, slow responses and submissions that did not save. No share or count of primary schools entering data has been found for either system. Operating would need more than half of primary schools to enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, on a published share or a count with its total.

LBR.short: The Ministry said in 2026 that its school data system is paper-based and a per-pupil record planned; no source says whether any pilot has begun.
LBR.summary: In September 2025 a policy dialogue validated a costed three-year action plan whose priorities include a national unique learner and teacher ID. On 28-29 September 2026 the Ministry's planning director described the existing system as paper-based. In the last twelve months the Ministry held the two-day consultation of September 2026 to draft, review and validate an EMIS Policy. Nothing found shows staff trained, equipment delivered, an agreement signed or pilot schools chosen. Preparing would need an EMIS for primary schools being prepared or piloted, with staff trained, equipment delivered, an agreement signed or pilot schools using it.

LBY.short: A system launched in 2024 gathers school data by online survey; no source says how schools keep each pupil's record, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: Not found. Nothing found says how primary schools keep their learners' records, on paper or digitally. No system held is shown to hold a record per learner that a school adds to during the year.

LSO.short: A 2018 pilot tracked pupils in 100 schools, and in 2026 secondary schools reported through a ministry system; no source says primary schools use one.
LSO.summary: In 2018 the Ministry of Education and Training was itself implementing OpenEMIS as its new education information system, and the pilot was set in one hundred low-performance schools. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, all 365 secondary schools reported through LEMIS, the ministry's DHIS2 for Education system. A training from 30 September to 4 October 2026 covered LEMIS's individual teacher records, class management and attendance. No primary school is named, and nothing dated since 2018 shows whether the pilot still runs. Establishing would need an EMIS past its pilot, in live use in some primary schools.

MAR.short: Every school has registered its pupils in a national per-pupil record since 2014; no source found says how many primary schools enter attendance or marks.
MAR.summary: The MASSAR system was developed by the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training and launched at the end of 2013. In June 2014 each establishment registered and vetted its own pupils into a central database, and each pupil kept one number for the whole of their schooling. In the last twelve months, the ministry's letter of 7 May 2026 rolls out a new digital component for daily monitoring of pupil absence. It applies in the pioneer middle schools. No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing more than half of primary schools entering attendance or results.

MDG.short: A pilot gave 180,000 pupils in one district a permanent number in 2026; no source says whether any primary school beyond the pilot has enrolled.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's ministry piloted its Numéro Unique d'Identification Scolaire in Atsimondrano school district in March and April 2026. The pilot enrolled 180,000 learners from 792 public and private establishments of all levels. In the last twelve months, on 11 May 2026, the scale-up was launched at a public lower-secondary school in Ambatolampy district. In December 2025 the enrolment's field activities were still to be carried out. No total of establishments in the district and no count of primary schools has been found. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

MLI.short: A donor project gave families cards for heads to scan pupils' attendance on tablets in 2020; no source found says whether any school does so.
MLI.summary: In February 2020 UNICEF Mali described the PAIS project, under which each family in the target areas holds an electronic card with each child registered on it. The school principal scans the card onto a tablet as children attend. UNICEF Mali said the Kénèkolo school would digitise its attendance system that year. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated since February 2020 has been found. No count or share of schools scanning attendance has been found. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

MOZ.short: A pilot tracking individual pupils was reported in 2025; no source found says which schools, how many and whether it has gone further.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's Plano Tecnológico da Educação of May 2019 names the ministry as responsible for designing the academic information system it calls SEGI. A KIX policy brief of July 2025 recommends mandating individual student tracking "as piloted in Mozambique". No change has been found in the last twelve months. GPE KIX reported on 21 August 2026 that the collection of education data at school level is largely paper-based. No system, level, number of schools or method of entry has been found for the pilot. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

MRT.short: Pupil registration for 2026-2027 opened on a ministry platform in September 2026; no source found says who enters the records and in how many schools.
MRT.summary: Tefassil reported on 28 September 2026 that registration, transfers and corrections of pupils' status for the 2026-2027 school year go through Siraj, the ministry's pupil platform. In the last twelve months, pupil registration for 2026-2027 opened through Siraj on 28 September 2026. The ministry urged parents to register their children early. On 12 June 2026 Radio Mauritanie reported that in Trarza district inspectors and the heads of the beneficiary schools are to update data through it. No source found says whether registration is a pilot or in full use. None says who enters the records. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

MUS.short: A school records system was piloted in secondary schools by 2025; no source found says whether any primary school keeps pupils' records digitally.
MUS.summary: UNESCO IITE reported after a mission of 11-15 February 2019 that the system is the Ministry of Education's to establish, coordinated by its Director of E-Education with UNESCO technical support. A project of UNESCO IITE and the Chengdu Group, completed by August 2025, piloted an EMIS in secondary schools. In the last twelve months, the education ministry's indicative procurement plan for financial year 2026-2027, dated 17 August 2026, names an EMIS. No primary school has been found in the pilot. No count of pilot schools has been found. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

MWI.short: A digital pupil record with attendance was piloted in four schools in two districts in 2026; elsewhere records stay on paper; no rollout is known.
MWI.summary: A DHIS2-based EMIS piloted in 2026 was launched by the Unlocking Data Initiative with HISP-UNIMA at the University of Malawi. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, a cohort tracking prototype was running in four pilot schools in Machinga and Dedza, with validation due by end-June. Outside the pilot, a May 2026 policy brief says cohort tracking rests on paper records and several manual registers. No source found names the pilot schools' level or any school using the system past its pilot. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

NAM.short: In 2018, 807 of 1,848 schools were connected to the national school system and 103 piloted daily attendance entry; no source found reports anything since.
NAM.summary: The ministry's report with ADEA, published in November 2018, says 807 public schools out of 1,848 schools are connected to School-Link, at all levels together. Its attendance pilot ran from May to the end of July 2018, and 103 schools entered daily attendance. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated after 2018 has been found. The 807 schools are connected, not shown entering data, and no figure separates primary schools. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

NER.short: School heads filled printed forms for the yearly school count in 2025; no source says how schools keep pupils' records, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: No stage is set. The Ministry of National Education's recensement scolaire 2024-2025 ran on printed questionnaires, which heads of primary and secondary establishments filled in during April 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No dated statement has been found of whether primary schools keep their pupils' records on paper. No system with a record for each pupil has been found. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only, since a yearly school census does not change that.

NGA.short: A national learner number was launched in 2026 and issued first to examination candidates; no source found says whether any primary school enters learners' records.
NGA.summary: The Federal Ministry of Education launched the Learner Identification Number as its own system on 9 April 2026. In the last twelve months the number began rolling out in April 2026, with 1.9 million issued. The first phase went to candidates registered for the 2026 WAEC and NECO examinations. State officials said on 31 July 2026 that admission into Edo State's public primary and junior secondary schools is entirely manual, on forms and photocopied certificates. No source found says which levels use the number. None says who enters it, or whether any primary school fills the register. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

RWA.short: Primary schools keep a profile per pupil with exam results, and a daily attendance app is live (2026); no source reports the share of schools.
RWA.summary: HISP Rwanda, on a page of 7 May 2026, names the Ministry of Education as owner of the KARAME attendance app. In it, teachers and headteachers record each student's daily attendance at the school. The School Data Management System holds a profile for each student and captures national examination results, a World Bank study of February 2024 found. In the last twelve months, the ministry rolled out a new digital attendance tracking system, The New Times reported on 23 December 2025. No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results has been found. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

SDN.short: The ministry counts schools by survey (2026); no source found says how primary schools keep their pupils' records, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: No stage is set. The ministry's comprehensive educational statistical survey of schools, students and teachers began in Khartoum, Al-Gezira and Sennar states. In the last twelve months it was extended in phases to 7 May 2026, and a Rapid School Census Survey is planned for all 18 states. No dated statement has been found of how primary schools keep their learners' records. No system holding a record per learner has been found. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

SEN.short: A system for teachers to enter absences and report cards was launched in October 2025; no source found says how many schools use it.
SEN.summary: The ministry launched the new version on 3 October 2025, with a mobile app for pupils and parents, of its school platform PLANETE 3. Its teacher module lets teachers enter absences and produce report cards, and its coordinator said PLANETE 3 now covers elementary schools. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A December 2025 brief by APHRC lists manual, paper-based data collection and isolated digital files among Senegal's education data challenges. No school is named as using PLANETE 3, and no count has been found. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

SLE.short: In 2022-23 a rollout gave 300 primary schools tablets to enter each pupil's daily attendance; no source found says how many do so.
SLE.summary: Wi De Ya was rolled out to primary schools in academic year 2022-23. Its rollout phase covered 300 selected primary schools, each given a tablet and training. In the last twelve months, the ministry launched an initiative to build a learner-centred data system, reported in April 2026. Its Unique Learner ID system is to be piloted in four districts, in at least 20 schools in each. No source gives how many of the 300 schools enter data, or the total of primary schools. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

SOM.short: A daily per-pupil attendance app was on trial in 42 schools in Puntland State in May 2022; no source found says what has happened since.
SOM.summary: In May 2022 the Puntland education ministry proposed to expand what it calls the Digital Attendance Application. It was on trial in 42 schools in Puntland State in May 2022, after a 2019 pilot in 3 primary schools. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing is dated after May 2022. Whether the planned roll-out to about sixty schools took place has not been found, nor the level of the 42 trial schools. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

SSD.short: Teachers reported each absent pupil by text message in 2024; no source found reports the share of primary schools doing so.
SSD.summary: The attendance system SSSAMS was developed under and is supported by the Girls' Education South Sudan programme, by its site of December 2024. Its panel for academic year 2024 showed 6,650 schools of all levels as having reported attendance at least once. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, the African Union reported visits to public schools in Juba. There data moved from paper registers to state-level aggregation and national reporting. No share of primary schools reporting attendance has been found, nor a count given with its total. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

STP.short: The ministry launched a system with one enrolment per pupil in 2016, level not named; no source found says whether schools use it.
STP.summary: The Sistema Integrado de Gestão Escolar, SIGE, was launched in July 2016 by the Ministry of Education, Science and Culture, whose minister explained it at the ceremony. By the 2016 report the system gives each pupil a single enrolment, which the pupil only confirms each year. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and the latest account found is of the 2016 launch. Whether any school uses the system, at which levels and how many, has not been found. Nothing since 2016 says who runs or pays for it. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

SWZ.short: A per-pupil record has covered all 976 primary and secondary schools since March 2024; no source says how many primary schools enter attendance or results.
SWZ.summary: The Budget Speech of February 2024 describes a web-based system designed to capture data on individual learners in Grade 0, primary and high schools by their Personal Identification Numbers. It was launched nationally in March 2024 and covers all 976 primary and secondary schools, a GPE KIX blog said in October 2025. In the last twelve months, in November 2025, the software team called the system fully operational. The attendance app SEMIS was still a pilot with its roll-out to come in October 2025. No figure has been found for primary schools entering attendance or results during the year. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

SYC.short: The ministry trained school leadership teams on its pupil record platform in 2026; no source found says whether any school enters attendance or results.
SYC.summary: The EMIS helpdesk of the Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth and Information gives the procedure for recording attendance in OpenEMIS on the web, on a page of October 2025. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, a ministry team ran the schools' training for the leadership teams of primary and secondary schools across Mahé. It covered admissions, promotions and transfers, classes and subjects, and staff records. No report of a school entering attendance or results has been found. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

TCD.short: Schools filled the yearly school count on paper in 2021; no source found says how primary schools keep pupils' records, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: No stage is set. Chad's education ministry EMIS was described in 2021 as one paper questionnaire per school a year, filled by the director, carried up to the centre and keyed there. The annuaire statistique scolaire for 2024-2025 was validated at a workshop in N'Djamena on 7 October 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found states how primary schools keep their pupils' records. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

TGO.short: The ministry launched pupil numbering and designed its platform in 2023; no source found says whether any school yet uses it.
TGO.summary: The primary and secondary education ministry launched the registration of pupils with a number in 2023. The work was the design of the enrolment platform that generates the pupils' numbers. The independent panel advising the Global Partnership for Education reported on 8 April 2024 that it found no clear evidence that Togo has student identification numbers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No school is named as using the platform, and no pilot is reported. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

TUN.short: In December 2023, 92.7% of public primary schools were on the ministry's school system; no source found says how many enter attendance or results.
TUN.summary: In December 2023 the ministry's national centre for technologies in education counted 4,322 of 4,662 public primary establishments on Madrassati, or 92.7%, and put the rate of uploading primary absences at 2%. In the last twelve months, the minister said in November 2026 that the first lot of the school information system started in April 2026. Vie scolaire was launched at the end of July 2026. On 7 September 2026 the secondary teachers' federation called a boycott of the ministry's new platform until it works. No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results has been found. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

TZA.short: Heads and teachers in one council were trained on a school record system in January 2026; no source says whether any primary school enters attendance.
TZA.summary: TAMISEMI directed that the School Information System come into use when schools opened on 13 January 2026. PO-RALG's July 2025 privacy policy says the system is built for each learner's registration, attendance and assessment, entered by school staff. In the last twelve months, Handeni Town Council trained the heads of its primary and secondary schools and one teacher each on 9 January 2026. In November 2025 the government was preparing a system to follow each learner through school. No source found shows a primary school entering attendance or results, or counts the schools using the system. Establishing would need some primary schools entering attendance or results in a system past its pilot.

UGA.short: In 2025, 58.9% of all primary schools uploaded pupils' enrolment details to the national register; no source found says whether any enter attendance or results.
UGA.summary: The ministry reports that 26,597 of the country's 45,164 primary schools (58.9%) responded to the data upload for 2025. Its abstract was published in January 2026. The system collects data on each learner, issues a Learner Identification Number and tracks transfers, with 11,787,396 primary learners registered at December 2025. In the last twelve months, the ministry launched the new guidelines on 8 June 2026, with sanctions for institutions that fail their data obligations. No source found describes schools entering attendance or results. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

ZAF.short: Schools record attendance and marks digitally and a national register holds each pupil, in 2025; no source reports the share of primary schools doing so.
ZAF.summary: The Department of Basic Education's 2025/26 plan says SA-SAMS, the school administration system, is developed and maintained by the Department of Basic Education. The Department says about 99.9% of functional ordinary schools of all levels, 24,850 in 2024, had their databases uploaded to LURITS by July 2024. That figure counts schools of all levels. In the last twelve months, the Minister's reply gives learner totals from LURITS for 2020 to 2025, the 2025 dataset preliminary. No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results during the year has been found. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

ZMB.short: Schools report enrolment yearly on paper, by a 2025 account; no source found says how they keep pupil records, so no stage is set.
ZMB.summary: No stage is set. Schools send annual reports from schools yearly on paper, and the Ministry of General Education enters them into its database, for enrolment only. In the last twelve months, in September 2026, a KGS digital checklist verification tablet application for school guidance teachers was reported in 25 of 28 schools in Lavushimanda District. It is not a record of each learner. No dated statement has been found of how primary schools keep their learners' records. Absent would need a dated source stating that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only.

ZWE.short: Schools enter each pupil's absence and grades, all public schools in one province by 2026; no source found says how many primary schools nationally do so.
ZWE.summary: In June 2026 the ministry's spokesperson described its Early Warning System, now integrated into EMIS. It flags individual learners by tracking persistent absenteeism and falling grades and produces a real-time list of learners absent for extended periods. The revised EMIS has GPE funding of US$2.9 million for 2023 to 2026, with UNICEF supporting implementation. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, all 1,444 public schools in Masvingo Province used the new EMIS, and 12,324 schools nationwide had been equipped to use it. No national share of primary schools entering attendance or grades has been found. Operating would need over half of primary schools entering each learner's attendance or results, with a published share.

AGO.short: A link between social protection systems was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
AGO.summary: The ministry, MASFAMU, said it launched the modernisation and expansion phase of the Cadastro Social Único on 20 July 2026. It says the phase promotes interoperability between public institutions. A World Bank status report of 25 October 2024 said the registry was still not operational as of mid-2024. In the last twelve months, the July 2026 launch is the one dated step found. No source found since October 2023 says a registry or programme exchanges data in use. Establishing would need a system in use exchanging data with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

BDI.short: Two or more programmes shared one social registry in 2026; no source found reports links to another sector.
BDI.summary: In January 2026 a World Bank blog said the CORE-MIS of the Merankabandi (Cash for Jobs) programme connects with several payment service providers. In May 2026 the World Bank said the Merankabandi social registry is also used by the Soleil-Nyakiriza solar energy project. The project uses it to reach vulnerable households for subsidised solar kits. Both statements are from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the registry is linked to the national ID and to another sector. Mature would need the registry linked to the national ID and to civil registration, health, education or tax.

BEN.short: Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

BFA.short: A 2026 World Bank project funds linking the social registry to displaced-persons and health-insurance databases; no data exchange in use is known.
BFA.summary: On 15 June 2026 the World Bank approved US$120 million for a project in Burkina Faso that finances integration of the Registre Social Unique with the IDP, health-insurance and other key beneficiary databases. In May 2026 its appraisal document said the RSU and the data on internally displaced persons are managed separately, with coordination efforts under way. The RSU covers about a quarter of poor and vulnerable households. The funding and the appraisal are from the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a registry or programme exchanges data in use. Establishing would need a system in use that exchanges data with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

BWA.short: The single social registry served five programmes by 2025, but nothing since October 2023 names systems exchanging data, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: No stage is set. In 2022 the World Bank said the social registry is linked to OMANG, the national ID, for validation. By March 2025, 98 per cent of beneficiaries of the five main poverty-targeted social programmes had been updated in the Single Social Registry, and the World Bank's completion report set the target at 75.8 per cent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found since October 2023 names social protection systems exchanging data. Establishing would need a source after that date showing an exchange in use with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

CAF.short: A link between social protection systems was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
CAF.summary: In May 2026 the World Bank said a project's registration system will consolidate the parent project's beneficiary databases. It will cross-check the data against existing registries to reduce duplication. A World Bank appraisal says the Unified Social Registry (RSU), begun in 2018, is delayed. The Safety Nets Project will fund its management information system. In the last twelve months, the May 2026 statement is the dated step found. No source found since October 2023 says a registry or programme exchanges data in use. Establishing would need a system in use exchanging data with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

CIV.short: A link between social protection systems was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
CIV.summary: BCPFS and ONECI signed a convention on 2 April 2026 to interconnect the RSU with ONECI databases and the RNPP. In September 2025 a workshop at Grand-Bassam set out to update the RSU's interoperability framework, and the national interoperability platform began. In the last twelve months, five administrations joined that platform by July 2026, and the convention was signed. No source found since October 2023 says a registry or programme exchanges data in use. Establishing would need a system in use exchanging data with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

CMR.short: Universal health coverage enrolment and billing systems exchanged data in 2026; no registry shared by programmes is on record.
CMR.summary: In October 2025 Cameroon was assessing its ID, civil registration and disability systems for linking to the Unified Social Registry, the Digital Convergence Initiative said. In the last twelve months, Cameroon's health ministry said in November 2026 that its interoperability platform links universal health coverage enrolment and billing. A 2021 World Bank appraisal plans the registry under the social affairs ministry, to merge four existing beneficiary databases. No source found since October 2023 says two or more programmes draw on one registry. Operating would need two or more programmes drawing beneficiaries from one shared registry.

COD.short: Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COD.summary: Not found. Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

COG.short: The social registry was linked to the national ID and another sector in 2024.
COG.summary: Congo's joint arrete of 20 August 2024 states that the registre social unique is an interoperable information system. Article 8 draws its data from the civil-status information systems and the unique identification number. In the last twelve months, a workshop on 27-28 January 2026 reported survey data migrated to the PSIPJ general beneficiary register. The data came from five Talangai districts. On 10 April 2026 the social affairs minister said three programmes now have the RSU as a common source of information. They are health insurance, safety net and insertion.

COM.short: Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data, or says there is none.

CPV.short: About 16 social programmes drew on the social registry in 2024, but nothing since October 2023 names systems exchanging data, so no stage is set.
CPV.summary: No stage is set. In February 2024 the minister said about 16 social programmes draw beneficiaries from the CSU. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 the government said the Cadastro Social Único is the base of the country's social support system. A registered eligible household can access cash transfers, food security support and resilience programmes. Nothing found since October 2023 names social protection systems exchanging data. Establishing would need a source after that date showing an exchange in use with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

DJI.short: A link between social protection systems was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
DJI.summary: On 14 March 2025 the World Bank approved the US$31 million Integrated Community Resilience Project. One component scales the national Social Registry with an ANSIE interoperability upgrade. Decree 2020-137, of July 2020, makes the Registre Social the sole targeting tool for beneficiaries of social programmes. In the last twelve months, a director general said in July 2026 that an interoperability system is being built. It will let social protection bodies verify national ID cards in real time. No source found since October 2023 says a registry or programme exchanges data in use. Establishing would need a system in use exchanging data with the national ID, a payment provider or another programme.

DZA.short: Two social security funds exchanged data through the national ID in 2026; no source found says whether programmes share one registry.
DZA.summary: In April 2026 the CNAS social insurance fund and the CNR pensions fund were exchanging data instantly through the national identification number. In the last twelve months, the Ministry of National Solidarity was testing a unified digital platform in two districts in March 2026. The pilot covered the AFS allowance and the card for persons with special needs. Database links were still being checked. No source found since October 2023 says two or more programmes share one registry. Operating would need two or more programmes drawing beneficiaries from one shared registry.

EGY.short: Several programmes shared one social registry in 2026, exchanging data through the national ID; no source found reports links to health, education or tax records.
EGY.summary: Egypt's national social registry draws on 27 government databases through the national ID number, a Ministry of Social Solidarity official said in November 2026. In August 2026 the ministry said Law 12 of 2025 made the social registry the single source for every cash-transfer beneficiary database. The World Bank says cash-plus schemes run with UNFPA, UNDP and WFP target people from the Takaful and Karama registry. Both ministry statements are from the last twelve months. No source found names a link from the registry to civil registration, health, education or tax records. Mature would need the registry linked to the national ID and to civil registration, health, education or tax.

ERI.short: Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names social protection systems exchanging data, or says there is none.
