GNQ.summary: In February 2026 IDENTIC and the Bioko Chamber of Commerce stressed the need for legislation specific to startups and digital entrepreneurship. They agreed to take proposals to the Senate. That statement is the only position found in the last twelve months, and no earlier one has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy is being prepared. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

KEN.short: A startup bill was in mediation between the two houses of Parliament in 2026; none adopted is on record.
KEN.summary: The Startup Bill, 2022 was published in the Kenya Gazette in December 2022 for the Senate. In January 2025 the National Assembly passed it. The Senate rejected the Assembly's amendments on 23 July 2025. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 the bill was with a mediation committee and was not law. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under a startup law. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

LBR.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

LBY.short: A startup law or strategy was adopted by 2025; startups labelled under it are not on record.
LBY.summary: Libya's Prime Minister's Decision 23 of 2025 defines a start-up in law and took effect on issue. Decision 23 of 23 January 2025 creates the Sunduq Intilaqa fund. The fund gives startups seed finance and loan guarantees. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the decision, or that its fund has financed any. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

LSO.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

MAR.short: Over 540 startups held the state's innovative-startup label by 2025; no source found reports investments by the 2026 public startup fund.
MAR.summary: The digital development agency created its JEI label in 2019. By April 2025 it had gone to more than 540 startups from 1,303 applications. In the last twelve months, decree 2.26.576 of 3 August 2026 strengthened the rules of the Startup Catalytic Fund. The digital ministry set it up and Tamwilcom manages it, with $36 million of public money over three years. No source found since October 2023 says a public startup fund has financed startups, with investments named or counted. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act or strategy to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

MDG.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MDG.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

MLI.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2024; none adopted is on record.
MLI.summary: On 27 June 2024 Minister Alhamdou Ag Ilyene said the Startup Act's adoption was imminent. In October 2019 the Council of Ministers had adopted a start-up bill, which set the legal framework for labelling and developing start-ups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the act has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

MOZ.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MOZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

MRT.short: A startup law or strategy was adopted by 2024; startups labelled under it are not on record.
MRT.summary: The digital ministry's page lists Law No. 2024-002 P.R on technological and innovative startups, dated 2 January 2024. The Africa Capital Report says the law establishes a labelling regime. In November 2025 the digital ministry was speeding publication of the texts completing the start-up law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says startups are labelled or registered under the law. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

MUS.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

MWI.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2024; none adopted is on record.
MWI.summary: TechCabal reported in March 2024 that a startup bill was being drafted in Malawi. The bill was expected to reach parliament by the end of 2024. In the last twelve months, Tech Trends Malawi said in May 2026 that the Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship Bill, proposed in 2024, never became law. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

NAM.short: Cabinet approved a start-ups policy in 2024 and ordered a startup act finalised; no startup has been found labelled under it.
NAM.summary: On 26 November 2024 Cabinet approved the National Informal Economy, Start-ups and Entrepreneurship Development Policy (NIESED). The same decision told the trade ministry to finalise an Act to accompany the policy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. In September 2025 Cabinet authorised the ICT ministry to engage female founders as potential beneficiaries of a US$20 million venture capital fund. No startup has been found labelled under the policy, and no investment by the fund has been found. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

NER.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

NGA.short: Nigeria's 2022 Startup Act is in force and labels startups; no investment by its seed fund is reported.
NGA.summary: In July 2024 NITDA set up a Startup Labelling Committee to implement the Nigeria Startup Act. The Act was signed in October 2022, with NITDA as its secretariat. It sets up a startup label, a Startup Portal and a Startup Investment Seed Fund. About 13,000 businesses had registered as startups under NITDA's criteria by March 2025. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the Act's seed fund has invested in startups. Mature would need a public fund set up under the act to have financed startups, with investments named or counted.

RWA.short: A startup act was still being drafted in 2025, about five years after it was announced; no act or startup strategy adopted is known.
RWA.summary: In June 2025 The New Times reported that the startup act had not been enacted or tabled in Cabinet, about five years after Rwanda announced it. The ICT Chamber's chief executive said several drafts were still being validated. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The Rwanda Innovation Fund had backed 12 technology companies by 2024, KT Press reported. No fund set up under a startup law has been found, and no startup act or strategy adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

SDN.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

SEN.short: A startup law took effect with its decree in 2025; over 400 startups had registered on its platform by June 2026, but none was labelled.
SEN.summary: In January 2025 the government adopted the implementing decree for Startup Law No. 2020-01 of 6 January 2020. The decree and the Ecosysteme Startup platform were launched on 20 November 2025. In the last twelve months, by 30 June 2026 over 400 startups had registered on the Startup Act platform. None had been labelled, as no steering committee had been installed to award the label. Operating would need startups labelled or registered under the act, or its tax or other measures applied to them.

SLE.short: A startup ecosystem policy was at validation in 2026 and a startup act is expected in 2027; none adopted has been found.
SLE.summary: In March 2024 the ministry and Columbia Law School began drafting a startup bill for Parliament. In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the communications ministry and the International Trade Centre held a validation workshop on a startup ecosystem policy. On 12 September 2026 the communications minister said the Act is expected in the first quarter of 2027. No startup law or strategy adopted has been found since October 2023. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

SOM.short: Somalia had no startup law or legal definition of a startup in 2026; no bill or strategy being prepared is known.
SOM.summary: In April 2026 Ibrahim Isse Abdulle wrote that Somalia has no formal legal definition of a startup. He proposed a National Startup Act. In August 2021 the commerce ministry's director of SMEs said there was no government funding for startups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No startup bill or strategy being prepared has been found since October 2023. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

SSD.short: Nothing found names a startup law or strategy or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: Not found. Nothing found says what the state does for tech startups.

STP.short: Sao Tome and Principe adopted an entrepreneurship strategy for 2024-2030 in 2024; no startup law or strategy has been found, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: No stage is set. Resolution No. 39/2024 approves the National Strategy for Entrepreneurship in Sao Tome and Principe, 2024-2030. The strategy names no measure for startups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No startup law or strategy has been found since October 2023. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no startup law, strategy or public support for startups exists.

SWZ.short: A 2024 small-business policy with start-up measures awaits Cabinet adoption; no startup law or strategy adopted has been found.
SWZ.summary: The commerce ministry's National MSME Policy 2024-2029 provides for a start-up matching fund and a fellowship fund for entrepreneurs. It also commits to review the tax requirements for start-ups. The policy sets adoption by Cabinet as its last step. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The E45 million MSME Revolving Fund lends to start-ups. No source found says Cabinet has adopted the policy. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

SYC.short: A 2023 strategy found no startup law or act; a 2025 tax exemption for new firms is general, not a startup measure.
SYC.summary: UNCTAD's 2023 National Entrepreneurship Strategy for Seychelles found no stand-alone Entrepreneurship Policy or Act. It proposes only to consider introducing a Start-Up Act that would define innovative start-ups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy is being prepared. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

TCD.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2025; none adopted is on record.
TCD.summary: In September 2025 Finance Minister Tahir Hamid Nguilin announced reforms under way. They include a legal and regulatory framework adapted to startups. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted, or that startups are labelled under one. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

TGO.short: A startup bill approved by the cabinet in 2023 was still awaiting adoption in 2026; no startup law or strategy adopted is known.
TGO.summary: African Business reports that Togo's Council of Ministers approved startup legislation in 2023. The legislation has yet to be ratified. In October 2025 the minister, Cina Lawson, said the Togolese Startup Act was being adopted. In the last twelve months, in May 2026 the opposition deputy Brigitte Adjamagbo-Johnson wrote that the bill on the innovation ecosystem was about to be adopted. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law is adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

TUN.short: About 1,400 startups held the label in 2026 and the state fund of funds had financed 70 through its funds; no source found reports sums invested.
TUN.summary: A July 2026 report on a programme with Japan's JICA called the Startup Act the legal framework for startups. Agence Ecofin reports that about 1,400 firms held the Start-up label in 2026. In the last twelve months, in July 2026 the CDC's director-general said ANAVA had financed 10 investment funds, and through them 70 Tunisian startups were financed. In April 2026 the minister said several ministries were still working on the revised Startup Act 2.0 bill. Nothing found says how much ANAVA's funds have invested in startups.

TZA.short: Tanzania's draft startup policy went for government approval in February 2026; it was not adopted by October 2026.
TZA.summary: In 2024 the ICT ministry began drafting Tanzania's first National Startup Policy, the Tanzania Startup Association reports. In March 2025 the government opened consultations and a baseline study. In the last twelve months, in February 2026 the ministry said the draft Start-ups Policy 2026 was finalised and submitted for government approval. In October 2026 Tanzania still had no dedicated startup law or policy, and the Vice-President directed that one be finalised within six months. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

UGA.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2026; none adopted is on record.
UGA.summary: In May 2024 a ninth draft of the National Startup Policy was presented, and a private member's Startup Bill was introduced in Parliament. In the last twelve months, in June 2026 Startup Uganda said the National Startup Act was under technical review at the trade ministry. In November 2026 the Daily Monitor reported that the trade ministry was finalising a startup policy for Cabinet. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law or strategy has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

ZAF.short: A public fund backed about 96 firms by 2025, but no startup law or strategy since October 2023 is known, so no stage is set.
ZAF.summary: No stage is set. In July 2026 Business Day said South Africa had no enacted startup act, and that one was proposed. In February 2025 the science department said its public Innovation Fund had supported 12 venture capital firms and around 96 technology investments and enterprises. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a startup bill is drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy prepared or adopted. Preparing would need a startup bill drafted or tabled, or a startup strategy being written or in consultation.

ZMB.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2025; none adopted is on record.
ZMB.summary: In July 2024 Minister Felix Mutati said the government was working on a Start Up Bill to create a Venture Capital Fund for start-ups. In October 2025 he said the government had finalised the Innovation and Inventors Bill. In the last twelve months, a Smart Africa workshop in July 2026 assessed progress on the proposed Startup Bill. The ITU's 2026 digital innovation profile says the Ministry of Technology and Science is finalising a Start-up Bill after consultations. No source found since October 2023 says a startup law is adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

ZWE.short: A startup law or strategy was being prepared in 2024; none adopted is on record.
ZWE.summary: In September 2024 Zimbabwe's Cabinet adopted the principles of the Science, Technology, Innovation Start-up and Knowledge-based Economy Promotion Bill. The bill would give start-ups tax incentives, rebates and preferential procurement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. In October 2026 the telecoms regulator's director-general said its Innovation Drive Programme has given milestone-based funding to more than 100 innovations. The programme is not tied to the start-up bill. No source found since October 2023 says the bill has been adopted. Establishing would need a startup act passed or a startup strategy adopted.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 statistics law is in force; a March 2026 decree under it reset the statistics institute's statute, and a revision is in consultation.
AGO.summary: Angola's statistics law is Lei n.º 3/11 of 14 January 2011, which replaced the statistics law of 1996. In the last twelve months, Presidential Decree 43/26 of 10 March 2026 made the statistics institute the central executive body of the national statistical system under the law. It revoked its statute of 2017. The institute opened a public consultation on a proposed revision on 29 September 2026. No source found shows the statistics council meeting or a penalty under the law.

BDI.short: Burundi's statistics law, amended in 2021 and 2023, has decrees on its council and authority, and survey visas and council sessions applied it through 2026.
BDI.summary: Burundi's statistics law is Loi n°1/08 of 20 May 2021, which recast the law of 25 September 2007. Loi n°1/18 of 24 July 2023 amended it and makes every nationally representative survey subject to a statistical visa. In the last twelve months, the national statistical information committee held its 13th session on 6 November 2026, chaired by the Prime Minister. It discussed draft decrees on an enterprise classification and an order of statistics professionals. No source found shows a penalty under the law.

BEN.short: Benin's June 2022 statistics law is in force and was cited by a 2026 decree; no source found reports rules made under it.
BEN.summary: Benin's statistics law is Loi n° 2022-07 of 27 June 2022, adopted by the National Assembly on 2 June 2022. The statistics strategy of 2020 said activity then rested on a law of 12 April 2000 creating the National Statistics Council. In the last twelve months, Decree 2026-002 of 21 January 2026 cited the 2022 law among its legal bases; it was cited and not changed. No source found names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's 2021 statistics law is in force; an August 2025 decree under it reorganised the statistics council, and the statistics fund's rules are awaited.
BFA.summary: Burkina Faso's statistics law is Loi n°036-2021/AN of 6 December 2021, which repealed the law of 2007. Decree 2025-1095 of 26 August 2025 was adopted in application of it and sets up the national statistics council. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The statistics master plan of December 2025 says three application decrees are available. It says the texts on the statistics development fund were still awaited.

BWA.short: Botswana's 2009 Statistics Act is in force and its board was constituted in 2023/24; no source found names rules made under it.
BWA.summary: Botswana's statistics law is the Statistics Act, No. 15 of 2009, which establishes Statistics Botswana and commenced on 1 December 2010. Its annual report for 2023/24 says the Board was constituted in conformity with section 6 of the Act in the year to 31 March 2024, with nine members appointed by the Minister. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CAF.short: Central African Republic's 2001 statistics law is in force, and a replacement draft was validated in April 2026; no source found names rules under it.
CAF.summary: The Central African Republic's statistics law is Law No. 01.008 of 16 July 2001, which creates the national statistical system, the national statistics council and the statistics institute. In the last twelve months, a workshop in Bangui on 23 April 2026 validated a draft law to replace it. The 2001 law stays in force until the draft is adopted. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2001 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2013 statistics law, amended in 2020, is in force, and three decrees applying it were adopted in June 2025.
CIV.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's statistics law is law 2013-537 of 30 July 2013, amended by law 2020-950 of 7 December 2020. On 18 June 2025 the Council of Ministers adopted three decrees applying the statistics law. They set how the survey and census visa is granted, the conditions and prices for statistical products, and how administrative files pass to the system for statistical use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the statistics council meeting or a visa granted under the decrees.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2020 statistics law is in force with an implementing decree of December 2021; nothing done under it since is known.
CMR.summary: Cameroon's statistics law is law n°2020/010 of 20 July 2020. Decree n°2021/690 of 2 December 2021 sets the rules for applying it, and is the one rule found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

COD.short: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's first statistics law was signed as an ordonnance-loi in September 2026; no source found reports rules under it.
COD.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo made its first statistics law in 2026, after a bill drafted in December 2024 by the National Institute of Statistics. In the last twelve months, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordonnance-loi on 28 August 2026. The state news agency reported on 12 September 2026 that the President had signed it. On 21 October 2026 the Senate ratified it as ordonnance-loi n° 26/015 of 7 September 2026. No decree, regulation or order made under it has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

COG.short: Congo's 2018 law on official statistics is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
COG.summary: Congo's statistics law is law no. 36-2018 on official statistics, whose text is in the Journal officiel, issue no. 42 of 18 October 2018. In the last twelve months, INS Congo issued its advance release calendar for 2026 in October 2026, stating that it answers the requirements of law 36-2018. The calendar sets the dates on which the year's official statistics are to be released. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

COM.short: The Comoros' statistics law was adopted and promulgated in 2011 and is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
COM.summary: The Comoros' statistics law is Loi n°11-003/AU of 26 March 2011, adopted by the Assembly of the Union. A later decree records in its preamble that the law was promulgated by decree N°11-142/PR of 14 July 2011. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's 2019 statistics law is in force and its statistics institute invoked it in 2026; no source found reports rules made under it.
CPV.summary: Cabo Verde's statistics law is Lei n.º 48/IX/2019, published in the Boletim Oficial of 19 February 2019. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the board of the statistics institute said on 1 June 2026 that it asserts its technical independence under the law. In 2024 a cooperation mission of Statistics Portugal supported the revision of the law. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

DJI.short: Djibouti's 2019 statistics institute law, amended in 2021, has decrees on the institute's statutes and board; no act under it since 2023 is known.
DJI.summary: Djibouti's Loi n° 26/AN/18/8ème L of 27 February 2019 created the national statistics institute. A law of 18 February 2021 renamed it INSTAD. Decree 2023-185 named the eleven members of its board for three-year terms from 6 July 2023. No change to the law has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the board or council meeting under the law since 2023, or a standard, survey approval or penalty. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

DZA.short: Algeria's 1994 legislative decree on statistics is in force with a 1995 decree under it and is under review; no source found reports recent use.
DZA.summary: Algeria's statistics office said in a presentation of 1 July 2025 that Legislative Decree 94-01 of 15 January 1994 remains the legal basis of official statistics. It said the law is under review. Executive Decree 95-159 of 3 June 1995 restates the statutes of the office and is the one rule found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

EGY.short: Egypt's 1960 statistics and census law, amended in 1982, is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
EGY.summary: Egypt's statistics law is Law No. 35 of 1960 on statistics and censuses, issued on 9 February 1960 and amended by Law No. 28 of 1982. The statistics agency publishes it as the law that regulates statistical work. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ERI.short: Eritrea's draft statistics proclamation was awaiting issue in 2007; no source found says whether it was ever issued.
ERI.summary: A review of the statistics office's cooperation with Statistics Norway, published on 8 January 2007, says the Statistical Proclamation had been submitted to government. Its formal issue was still pending. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a statistics law is in force, or that the proclamation was issued or withdrawn after 2007. Establishing would need a statistics law in force: an act, ordinance or decree with the force of law that governs official statistics or sets up the national statistics office.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's 2005 statistics proclamation is in force; parliament approved its successor in June 2026, and no source found says whether that is published.
ETH.summary: Ethiopia's statistics law is the Central Statistics Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 442/2005, published in the Federal Negarit Gazeta on 20 April 2005. In the last twelve months, the House of People's Representatives approved the Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation unanimously on 30 June 2026, after the Council of Ministers took up the draft on 26 May 2026. No source found says the new proclamation has been published in the gazette. No decree, regulation or order made under either law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GAB.short: Gabon's statistics law, amended in 2022, is in force; an August 2024 decree under it approved the statistics institute's statutes.
GAB.summary: Gabon's statistics law is law 15/2014, amended by law 16/2022 of 6 September 2022. Decree 0314/PR/MPP of 1 August 2024 approves the statutes of the National Institute of Statistics and cites the amended law as its basis. In the last twelve months, on 22 May 2026, the planning minister presented to the Council of Ministers a bill amending ten articles of the law. The bill would bring the law into line with the Constitution of December 2024. No source found shows the statistics council meeting under the law.

GHA.short: Ghana's 2019 Statistical Service Act is in force, and a replacement bill went to consultation in July 2026; no source found names rules under it.
GHA.summary: Ghana's statistics law is the Statistical Service Act, 2019 (Act 1003), assented to on 24 September 2019. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the Service held a stakeholder engagement on a proposed Statistics Ghana Bill, 2026. On 17 November 2026 the Government Statistician said the draft bill would go to Cabinet and then Parliament. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2019 Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2014 statistics law is in force with decrees and a council appointed under it in 2015; nothing done under it since is known.
GIN.summary: Guinea's statistics law is Law L/2014/019/AN of 8 July 2014, which repealed the law of 1995. The statistics institute's compendium carries the decree of 5 August 2015 on the national statistics council, and an order naming its members with the Prime Minister as president. All of it dates from 2015. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need the law applied in the past three years: its council or board appointed or meeting, a standard, release calendar or survey approval issued under it, a rule made under it, or a penalty.

GMB.short: The Gambia's 2005 Statistics Act is in force and a 2019 replacement bill has not passed; no source found reports rules under the Act.
GMB.summary: The Gambia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2005. The bureau's strategy of September 2023 says the Act is under revision and plans a review of the 2019 Statistics Bill. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the bureau's Deputy Statistician-General called the 2005 Act outdated and asked for a revised law next year. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau's 2007 statistics law is in force and was given a regulation in March 2023; nothing done under it since is known.
GNB.summary: Guinea-Bissau's statistics law is Lei n.º 6/2007 of 10 September 2007, which sets up the national statistical system with its higher statistics council and institute. The institute's compilation also carries Decreto n.º 4/2023 of 31 March 2023, the regulation of the law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty under the law, in the past three years.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's 2020 statistics law is in force, replacing one of 2001; no decree made under it is known.
GNQ.summary: The national statistics strategy for 2022 to 2026 says Law 3/2020 of 16 October 2020 governs statistical activity in Equatorial Guinea, replacing Law 3/2001 of 17 May 2001. An African Union peer review in September 2025 credited the country with a modernised statistics law. It called for key decrees to be updated to align with it. On 10 December 2024 133 trained statisticians were appointed to the statistics units of ministries. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the 2020 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2006 Statistics Act is in force; a bill to replace the bureau went to a Senate committee in October 2026; rules not known.
KEN.summary: Kenya's statistics law is the Statistics Act (Cap. 112), assented to on 23 August 2006 and commenced on 1 February 2007, which establishes the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the Bureau and the National Treasury published the Statistics Bill, 2026. It would replace the Bureau with a Kenya Statistics Authority and repeal the Act. On 12 October 2026 the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Budget reviewed the draft bill with Bureau officials. The Act lists only two orders for a population census as subsidiary legislation. No other decree, regulation or order made under it has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2004 statistics act is in force and is cited in 2024 surveys; no source found reports rules made under it.
LBR.summary: Liberia's statistics law is the National Statistics and Geo-Information Act, approved on 22 July 2004, which sets up the statistics institute as an autonomous agency. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the institute's open data licence of June 2026 is governed by the Act. The institute's entry for the 2024 agricultural survey says the Act guarantees respondents' confidentiality. No regulation made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LBY.short: Libya's 1963 statistics and census law is listed as in force and was under review in 2024; no source found reports rules made under it.
LBY.summary: Libya's statistics law is Law No. 16 of 1963 on statistics and censuses, issued by King Idris I on 19 September 1963, which the Law Society's database lists as in force. In August 2024 the Libya Observer reported that a government meeting addressed a committee's findings on reviewing and updating the 1963 law. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2001 statistics act is in force, and a fourth replacement bill was expected to pass in 2026; no source found names rules under it.
LSO.summary: Lesotho's statistics law is the Bureau of Statistics Act, No. 8 of 2001. The African Union's peer review says the Act established the Bureau, the national statistical system and the National Statistical Council, and needs modernising. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the Bureau's director told a media workshop that the Statistics Bill is expected to be enacted before the end of 2026. The reviewers had been told in August 2025 that a fourth Statistics Bill was being drafted. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MAR.short: Morocco promulgated a new statistics law in July 2026, starting when its statistics council first meets; the 1968 decree-law applies meanwhile; rules not known.
MAR.summary: Morocco's statistics text in force is Royal Decree-Law no. 370-67 of 5 August 1968 on statistical studies. In the last twelve months, Law 046.26 on official statistics was promulgated by dahir of 28 July 2026 and published in the Bulletin officiel of 10 August 2026. The Council of Government approved the bill on 2 July 2026, and the Chamber of Councillors adopted it unanimously on 13 July 2026. It takes effect only at the first meeting of the deliberative organ of the national statistics council. No source found dates that meeting, or names a decree, regulation or order made under either law. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MDG.short: Madagascar's 2018 statistics law is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
MDG.summary: Madagascar's statistics law is Loi n° 2018-004 of 18 April 2018, adopted by the Senate on 2 March 2018 and the National Assembly on 12 March 2018. The statistics institute names the law as an institutional result achieved on its page for the 2023 to 2030 statistics strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MLI.short: Mali's 2016 statistics law is in force with decrees of 2016 and a council appointed in 2018; nothing done under it since is known.
MLI.summary: Mali's statistics law is Loi n°2016-005 of 24 February 2016, published in the Official Gazette of 18 March 2016. The master plan says the implementing decrees were taken in 2016, and that the order appointing the National Statistics Council was taken only in 2018. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. A methods manual of December 2025 cites its first article as the ground of statistical quality. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty, in the past three years.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's 1996 law creating the national statistical system is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
MOZ.summary: Mozambique's statistics law is Lei n.º 7/96 of 5 July 1996, by which the Assembly of the Republic created the National Statistical System. The text held is an excerpt of the opening chapters, which set up the system and its bodies. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to amend or replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MRT.short: Mauritania's 2005 statistics law is in force with a council decree of 2006 and members named in 2008; nothing done under it since is known.
MRT.summary: Mauritania's statistics law is law no. 2005-017 of 27 January 2005. The national statistics strategy for 2021 to 2030 lists it as the main text governing public statistical activity, and says it had not been revised. The strategy records decree no. 2006-024 of 17 April 2006 on the National Statistical Council and an order of 30 March 2008 appointing its members. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law since 2008. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty under the law, in the past three years.

MUS.short: Mauritius's Statistics Act of 2000 is in force and was amended in 2025 and August 2026; no source found reports rules made under it.
MUS.summary: Mauritius's statistics law is the Statistics Act (Act 38 of 2000), which commenced on 2 April 2001 and makes Statistics Mauritius the central statistical authority. The IMF's data review of September 2025 says most recommended amendments were made through the Finance Act 2025. In the last twelve months, Act No. 14 of 2026, assented to on 12 August 2026, amended the Act again, adding public sector debt to the statistics it covers. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MWI.short: Malawi's National Statistics Act has been in force since 2013; no source found reports rules made under it.
MWI.summary: Malawi's statistics law is the National Statistics Act (Chapter 27:01), which commenced on 19 July 2013. It establishes the National Statistical Office and the National Statistical System. The text held stops partway through, so no later section has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2011 Statistics Act is in force and a policy was made under it in 2015; nothing done under it since 2023 is known.
NAM.summary: Namibia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2011 (Act No. 9 of 2011), signed on 2 August 2011 and promulgated on 18 August 2011. The agency's census release of October 2024 says results are reported under the Act. The national spatial data policy, signed on 24 February 2015, was developed under the Act. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found since. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NER.short: Niger's 2004 statistics law is in force; cabinet adopted a replacement draft ordonnance in January 2026, and no source found says whether it is signed.
NER.summary: Niger's statistics law is Loi n° 2004-011 of 30 March 2004, which creates the National Institute of Statistics and the national statistical system. In the last twelve months, the Council of Ministers of 23 January 2026 adopted a draft ordonnance on the fundamental principles of statistical activities. It would replace the 2004 law. No source found says the ordonnance has been signed, so the 2004 law stands. No decree, regulation or order made under that law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NGA.short: Nigeria's 2007 Statistics Act is in force; the House passed a replacement bill in December 2025, and no source found reports rules under the Act.
NGA.summary: Nigeria's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2007 (Act No. 9), published in the Official Gazette of 11 June 2007. In the last twelve months, the House of Representatives passed the Statistics Bill, 2025 at third reading on 10 December 2025, to repeal the Act. A House committee held a public hearing on the bill on 8 June 2026. The report describes the 2007 Act as the current law until the bill repeals it. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2013 law on statistical activities is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
RWA.summary: Rwanda's statistics law is Law N° 45/2013 of 16 June 2013 on the organisation of statistical activities in Rwanda. The text held is the law as made, published by the national statistics institute. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to amend or replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SDN.short: Sudan's 2003 Statistics Act was in force and judged outdated in 2021; no source found reports rules made under it.
SDN.summary: Sudan's statistics law is the Statistics Act of 2003, which an assessment published in December 2021 treats as the current statistics law and calls outdated. The statistics strategy of 2012 had already listed an inadequate Statistics Act, and some of its provisions not being implemented, among the system's weaknesses. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a regulation made under the Act, or says anything of it after 2021. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2004 statistics law, amended in 2012, is in force with rules on survey visas made in 2020; nothing done under it since is known.
SEN.summary: Senegal's statistics law is law no. 2004-21 of 21 July 2004, modified and completed by law no. 2012-03 of 3 January 2012. A regional inventory lists decree n° 2248 of 23 May 2005 on the national statistics council, and two orders of 4 March 2020 on the statistical visa for censuses and surveys. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. In September 2026 a report on the IMF's data review said the authorities will revise the law. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty, in the past three years.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's 2002 Statistics Act is in force and is cited in 2023 and 2024 surveys; no source found reports rules made under it.
SLE.summary: Sierra Leone's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2002, passed in Parliament on 12 September 2002 and published in the Gazette on 7 November 2002. In February 2024 the office said it is established by the Act as the central authority for official statistics, supervised by a Statistics Council. Its entries for the agricultural surveys of 2024 and 2023 say the Act guarantees respondents' confidentiality. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2020 National Statistics Law is in force, replacing one of 1970; no source found reports rules made under it.
SOM.summary: Somalia's statistics law is Law No. 24, which the National Bureau of Statistics says mandated the Bureau's establishment and repealed Statistical Law No. 35 of 1970. The Bureau's page gives no date for the law; the record held dates it 24 February 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and the text of the law has not been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SSD.short: South Sudan's National Bureau of Statistics Act of 2024 is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
SSD.summary: South Sudan's statistics law is the National Bureau of Statistics Act, 2024, which the Bureau's page lists as the principal legislation establishing the Bureau. The Transitional National Legislative Assembly passed the bill unanimously in July 2024, replacing the 2011 statistics act. A radio report of September 2025 says the Director General raised the Act in a briefing to the Vice President's office. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe's 1998 statistics law is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
STP.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe's statistics law is Lei n.º 5/98, the framework law of the National Statistical System, passed by the National Assembly on 12 August 1998 and promulgated on 31 August 1998. Its article 18 brings it into force at once. The text held is published by the national statistics institute. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the law has been found, and no bill to amend or replace it. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SWZ.short: Eswatini's 1967 Statistics Act is in force; no source found reports rules made under it.
SWZ.summary: Eswatini's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 1967 (Act 14 of 1967), which commenced on 27 October 1967, and the text held is consolidated at 1 December 1998. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: in October 2026 the Principal Statistician said the economic census operates under the Statistics Act, which protects confidential statistical information. The Act gives a power to make regulations. No decree, regulation or order made under it has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SYC.short: Seychelles' 2010 statistics act is in force, and a 2025 peer review urged a new bill; no source found names rules under it.
SYC.summary: Seychelles' statistics law is the National Bureau of Statistics Act, 2010 (Act No. 14 of 2010), assented to on 9 July 2010, which repealed the National Statistics Bureau Act 2005. The African Union's peer review, published on 17 October 2025, recommends accelerating adoption of the new Statistics Bill. It gives no date or stage for the bill. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation made under the 2010 Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TCD.short: Chad's 2019 statistics law is in force with three decrees of July 2019 under it; nothing done under it since 2023 is known.
TCD.summary: Chad's statistics law is Loi N°026/PR/2019, dated June 2019, which makes the statistics institute the central body of the national statistical system. The institute's page of regulatory texts lists three decrees dated July 2019 on the national statistics council, the institute and the statistics development fund. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found dates an act done under the law in the last three years. Mature would need a council or board appointed or meeting, or a standard, rule or penalty under the law, in the past three years.

TGO.short: Togo's 2011 statistics law is in force with decrees of 2012 and 2015, and its statistics council met in June 2026.
TGO.summary: Togo's statistics law is law no. 2011-014 of 3 June 2011. The statistics institute says the law sets the principles and institutional frame of the national statistical system. It says a decree of 7 November 2012 made the council operational. In the last twelve months, the council held its 13th ordinary session on 30 June 2026 and adopted the national statistical activity reports for 2023 and 2024. No source found shows a penalty under the law.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 1999 statistics law is in force and the ministry is preparing a new bill; no source found reports rules made under the law.
TUN.summary: Tunisia's statistics law is Law no. 99-32 of 13 April 1999 on the national statistical system. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the acting president of the National Statistics Council said the ministry is preparing a new statistics bill as a full revision of the 1999 law. No draft of the bill has been found. No decree, regulation or order made under the 1999 law has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 2015 Statistics Act is in force and is cited in a 2025 survey; no source found reports rules made under it.
TZA.summary: Tanzania's statistics law is the Statistics Act, Chapter 351, originally Act No. 9 of 2015, which commenced on 2 November 2015. It continues the National Bureau of Statistics and sets up its Governing Board. The Bureau's dissemination policy of September 2024 says it operates as an autonomous public institution in accordance with the Act. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

UGA.short: Uganda's 1998 statistics act is in force and its board chairman invoked it in August 2026; no source found reports rules made under it.
UGA.summary: Uganda's statistics law is the Uganda Bureau of Statistics Act (Chapter 310), which commenced on 11 June 1998. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. On 7 August 2026 the finance ministry reported that the Board chairman said the Bureau was established under the Act and coordinates the National Statistical System under it. The statement names no regulation. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 1999 Statistics Act is in force and its 2024 amendment took effect in October 2025; no source found reports regulations under it.
ZAF.summary: South Africa's statistics law is the Statistics Act of 1999. An amendment act was assented to on 10 December 2024, and the amendment was proclaimed for implementation on 1 October 2025. In the last twelve months, a parliamentary committee report of 23 June 2026 lists rolling out the amendments as work in hand for Statistics South Africa. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need rules made under it.

ZMB.short: Zambia's 2018 Statistics Act is in force and its release calendar was issued in December 2025; no source found names rules made under it.
ZMB.summary: Zambia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2018 (Act No. 13 of 2018), assented to on 23 December 2018, which reconstituted the Central Statistics Office as the Zambia Statistics Agency. In the last twelve months, the Agency issued the National Statistical Release Calendar for 2026 on 1 December 2025. Section 27(1) of the Act requires it. The strategy published in July 2023 says the Act's operation began with appointing the Board and the Statistician General. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's Census and Statistics Act has been in force since 2009 and was called outdated in 2025; no source found names rules under it.
ZWE.summary: Zimbabwe's statistics law is the Census and Statistics Act (Chapter 10:29), Act 1 of 2007, which commenced on 1 July 2009. In October 2025 the agency's spokesperson said the Act is regarded as outdated and does not support an effective national statistical system. In April 2025 the SADC Secretariat sought a consultant to review the Act and draft a revised one. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No decree, regulation or order made under the Act has been found. Operating would need a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

AGO.short: A national statistics strategy was being prepared in 2026; none adopted is known to be current.
AGO.summary: In January 2026 the planning minister named the ENDE 2015-2025 as the national statistics strategy. Its period ended with 2025. In the last twelve months, the statistics institute, INE, opened a public consultation on 29 September 2026 on a new strategy. The consultation ran to 2 October. No review of progress on the ENDE 2015-2025 has been found since 2023, and no evaluation of it. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

BDI.short: The 2022-2026 statistics strategy is current, its steering group reviewed it in July 2026 and its mid-term evaluation had reported.
BDI.summary: The statistics institute, INSBU, refers to the SNDS-III as the statistics strategy in force. PARIS21's January 2026 status table lists it as adopted for 2022-2026. In the last twelve months, the statutory Groupe Sectoriel Statistique met on 28 July 2026 and discussed the recommendations of the SNDS-III mid-term evaluation. That shows the evaluation had reported. No completion date has been found for it, so the meeting date stands for it.

BEN.short: No source found shows a current statistics strategy or one in preparation, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: No stage is set. As at 30 September 2026, no national statistics strategy, current or in preparation, has been found for Benin. No source dated in the last three years says the country has none. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no current statistics strategy and none in preparation.

BFA.short: The Schema directeur de la statistique 2026-2030 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
BFA.summary: PARIS21's January 2026 status table lists the Schéma directeur de la statistique 2026-2030 as being implemented. In the last twelve months, the national statistics council examined the draft on 1 December 2025, costed at FCFA 96.689 billion. On 11 September 2026 the head of INSD, the statistics institute, called it the new framework for statistical work. No review of its progress has been found, and no evaluation of it or of the SDS 2021-2025. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

BWA.short: The BSDS 2026-2030 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
BWA.summary: Statistics Botswana and the University of Botswana launched the second Botswana Strategy for Development of Statistics, BSDS 2026-2030, a five-year national roadmap. PARIS21 states it was validated, endorsed and launched in October 2025. The first strategy, BSDS I, covered 2015-2020 and was extended to March 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No review of progress and no evaluation have been found since October 2023. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

CAF.short: The SNDS2 2024-2028 is current and its implementation was reviewed at mid-term in October 2026; no completed evaluation has been found.
CAF.summary: ICASEES, the statistics institute, says SNDS2 for 2024-2028 was adopted in August 2023. The last review found earlier was a workshop on 18 July 2024 to update it. In the last twelve months, ICASEES reviewed SNDS2's implementation at mid-term on 7-9 October 2026 with the statistical programming committee, funded by UNDP. No completed evaluation of SNDS2 has been found. Mature would need a mid-term or final evaluation of the current strategy, completed in the past three years.

CIV.short: The SNDS 2026-2030 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
CIV.summary: On 23 September 2025 the Vision et stratégies report of the SNDS 2026-2030 was adopted. A workshop validated its action plan on 10 October 2025. In the last twelve months, technical validation began on 30 April 2026, the last step before adoption. On 8 June 2026 the planning minister presented the strategy as one of the pillars of the statistical system. No review of its progress has been found, and no evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

CMR.short: The SNDS 2020-2030 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
CMR.summary: The statistics institute says Cameroon adopted its third statistics strategy, SNDS30 for 2021-2030, in 2021. In June 2024 its financing plan set a budget of FCFA 166.5 billion for 2024-2028. The institute said in June 2023 that the strategy was evaluated in 2022. In the last twelve months, the steering committee of a regional statistics project met in February 2026 to support its implementation. No review of progress on SNDS30 has been found since November 2023. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

COD.short: Nothing found says whether the country has a national statistics strategy, so no stage is set.
COD.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national statistics strategy, or says there is none.

COG.short: The SNDS 2022-2026 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
COG.summary: PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the SNDS 2022-2026 as implementing (adopted). The five-year strategy, dated January 2023, carries an action plan of 26,129.4 million FCFA. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No annual review, progress report or steering body meeting has been found since October 2023, and no mid-term or final evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

COM.short: A national statistics strategy was being prepared in 2026; none adopted is known to be current.
COM.summary: PARIS21's September 2024 table still listed the NSDS 2015-2019 as in implementation, though that period ended in 2019. In the last twelve months, PARIS21's January 2026 status table listed the SNDS 2026-2030 as being designed or awaiting adoption. No adoption has been found. No review of progress on a strategy has been found since 2023, and no evaluation of the NSDS 2015-2019. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

CPV.short: The SNDS 2022-2026 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
CPV.summary: PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the SNDS 2022-2026 as implementing (adopted). The fourth ENDE, for 2022-2026, was finalised in 2022 after a five-phase process ending in validation. In the last twelve months, a Budget Support Group mission on 20-28 November 2025 noted progress in implementing the strategy. No annual review, progress report or steering body meeting has been found. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

DJI.short: The SNDS 2025-2029 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
DJI.summary: INSTAD, the statistics institute, and its partners validated SNDS 3 for 2025-2029 at a workshop on 29 April 2025. PARIS21's January 2026 status table lists it as being implemented. In the last twelve months, the World Bank's October 2026 project report said its project supported the strategy's publication. No adoption date has been found. No review of progress on SNDS 3 has been found, and no evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

DZA.short: The National statistics strategy 2024-2028 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
DZA.summary: The ONS Director General recalled the national statistics strategy 2024-2028 on 19 November 2024 at a Finance Ministry information day. PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics 2015-2025 as implementing (adopted). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No review of progress on the strategy has been found since October 2023, and no mid-term or final evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

EGY.short: A national statistics strategy was being prepared in 2024; none adopted is known to be current.
EGY.summary: In June 2024 the planning ministry said a national strategy for the statistical system had been in preparation for nearly two years. Eighteen ministries and government and research bodies took part, and a first draft was expected the next month. PARIS21's September 2024 table lists the NSDS 2017-2021 as expired and the next one as being finalised. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No review of progress has been found since 2023, and no evaluation of the NSDS 2017-2021. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

ERI.short: The Statistical Master Plan 2023-2026 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
ERI.summary: PARIS21's September 2024 table had listed only the Statistical Master Plan for 2010-14, as expired. In the last twelve months, PARIS21's January 2026 status table listed the Statistical Master Plan 2023-2026 as the strategy being implemented. In July 2026 UNICEF named an updated Statistical Master Plan among efforts to close gaps in data on children. The 2023-2026 plan's period ends in 2026. No review of its progress has been found, and no evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

ETH.short: The NSDS 2021-2026 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
ETH.summary: On 1 February 2024 the planning ministry unveiled the Ethiopian Statistics Development Program, to run for three years. PARIS21's September 2024 table gives its period as 2023/24-2025/26 and lists the next strategy as being designed, with funding secured. PARIS21's January 2026 table lists an NSDS 2021-2026 as being implemented. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No review of progress has been found since 2023. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

GAB.short: A successor strategy for 2027-2030 was being drafted in October 2026; no current strategy is known.
GAB.summary: PARIS21's January 2026 status table lists the SNDS 2023-2025 as being implemented. Its period ended in 2025. In the last twelve months, INSTAT Gabon said in October 2026 that it had begun drafting SNDS-III for 2027-2030. An international expert's second mission on its strategic orientations was set for 1 to 13 November 2026. No adopted strategy whose period is still running has been found. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

GHA.short: NSDS III for 2026-2030 was validated in March 2026; its adoption has not been found.
GHA.summary: On 18 March 2026 the Ghana Statistical Service held a workshop to validate NSDS III for 2026-2030. PARIS21's January 2026 status table listed a successor to NSDS 2018-2022 as being designed or awaiting adoption. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the Data Forum called NSDS III finalised and asked the Service to secure its adoption by Cabinet. No source found shows NSDS III adopted. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

GIN.short: The statistics strategy for 2021-2025 ended in 2025, and no successor has been found, so no stage is set.
GIN.summary: No stage is set. Guinea's third statistics strategy, the SNDS 2021-2025, ended in 2025. As at 13 November 2026, no successor in preparation or adopted has been found, and no adoption date for the SNDS 2021-2025. No source dated in the last three years says the country has no strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a national statistics strategy being designed, drafted, validated or put to cabinet.

GMB.short: The NSDS 2024-2028 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
GMB.summary: PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the NSDS 2024-2028 as implementing (adopted). STATAFRIC says The Gambia has adopted NSDS III 2024-2028. The national statistical system technically approved it on 13 September 2023, and it went to the National Statistics Council and Cabinet. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No review of progress on NSDS III has been found since October 2023. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

GNB.short: A draft plan for the national statistical system over 2023-2028 was posted in 2023; its adoption has not been found.
GNB.summary: In 2023 the statistics institute posted a draft strategic plan for the national statistical system over 2023-2028, with a mission, values and three objectives, and no costing. PARIS21's January 2026 status table lists ENDE 2021-2024 as the strategy being implemented, though its period ended in 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the draft plan adopted. No review of progress has been found since November 2023. Establishing would need an adopted strategy whose stated period covers today.

GNQ.short: Progress on the ENDE was reviewed in 2026; no completed evaluation is known.
GNQ.summary: INEGE, the statistics institute, prepared the ENDE 2022-2026. In March 2024 the press office reported that Decree 103 approves the strategy. In February 2025 the Statistical Programmes Committee adopted the 2024 implementation report. In the last twelve months, the committee took the 2025 implementation report in April 2026. In August 2026 the national statistics council had that report on its agenda for validation. No evaluation of the ENDE 2022-2026 has been found. Mature would need a mid-term or final evaluation of the current strategy, completed in the past three years.

KEN.short: The KSDS 2023-2028 is current; no review of its progress since 2023 is known.
KEN.summary: KNBS publishes the second Kenya Strategy for Development of Statistics, KSDS II, for 2023/24-2027/28 as the national statistical system strategy. PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists it as implementing (adopted). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No annual review, progress report or steering body meeting has been found since October 2023, and no mid-term or final evaluation. Operating would need a review of progress on the current strategy in the past three years.

LBR.short: NSDS III for 2026-2030 was launched in February 2026; no review of its progress is known.
LBR.summary: NSDS III for 2026-2030 was signed at Monrovia on 15 December 2025. In the last twelve months, LISGIS, the statistics institute, launched the strategy officially on 18 February 2026.
